citation.translation: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, and Ali Bin Ibrahim, from is father, and Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, altogether from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Abu Nasr, from Jameel Bin Darraj who said, ‘I asked Abu Abdullahasws about the man who sent his dog upon the prey, so it seized it, and there did not happen to be a knife with him to slaughter it with. Can he leave it until it (the dog) kills it and (then) he eats from it?’ Heasws said: ‘There is no problem. Allahazwj Mighty and Majestic Says [5:4] so eat from what which they catch for you, and it is not befitting if you eat from what the leopard kills’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: صحيح - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (1/338)

text: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Al Hakam, from Sayf Bin Umeyra, from Abu Bakr Al Hazramy who said, ‘I asked Abu Abdullahasws about the prey of the buzzards and the falcons, and the dogs, and the leopards. So heasws said: ‘Do not eat the prey of anything from these except what you purify (slaughter), except for the hunting dog’. I said, ‘Suppose it kills it?’ Heasws said: ‘Eat, because Allahazwj Mighty and Majestic is Saying [5:4] and what you have taught the hunting animals, trained ones . . . so eat of that which they catch for you and mention the Name of Allah over it’.

citation.arabic_text: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) عَنْ صَيْدِ الْبُزَاةِ وَ الصُّقُورِ وَ الْكَلْبِ وَ الْفَهْدِ فَقَالَ لَا تَأْكُلْ صَيْدَ شَيْ‏ءٍ مِنْ هَذِهِ إِلَّا مَا ذَكَّيْتُمُوهُ إِلَّا الْكَلْبَ الْمُكَلَّبَ قُلْتُ فَإِنْ قَتَلَهُ قَالَ كُلْ لِأَنَّ اللَّهَ عَزَّ وَ جَلَّ يَقُولُ وَ ما عَلَّمْتُمْ مِنَ الْجَوارِحِ مُكَلِّبِينَ... فَكُلُوا مِمَّا أَمْسَكْنَ عَلَيْكُمْ وَ اذْكُرُوا اسْمَ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ .
citation.translation: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Al Hakam, from Sayf Bin Umeyra, from Abu Bakr Al Hazramy who said, ‘I asked Abu Abdullahasws about the prey of the buzzards and the falcons, and the dogs, and the leopards. So heasws said: ‘Do not eat the prey of anything from these except what you purify (slaughter), except for the hunting dog’. I said, ‘Suppose it kills it?’ Heasws said: ‘Eat, because Allahazwj Mighty and Majestic is Saying [5:4] and what you have taught the hunting animals, trained ones . . . so eat of that which they catch for you and mention the Name of Allah over it’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: حسن - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (21/339)

text: And from him, from Ali Bin Al Hakam, from Sayf Bin Umeyra, from Aban Bin Taghlub, from Saeed Bin Al Musayyab who said, ‘I heard Salman saying, ‘Eat from what the (hunting) dog catches, even if it has eaten two-thirds of it’.[838] (P.s. – This is not a Hadeeth) Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Al Nowfaly, from Al Sakuny, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws having said: ‘The dogs of the Kurds, when trained, so these are at the status of the Saluqiyya (Yemeni trained dogs)’.

citation.arabic_text: سَمِعْتُ سَلْمَانَ يَقُولُ كُلْ مِمَّا أَمْسَكَ الْكَلْبُ وَ إِنْ أَكَلَ ثُلُثَيْهِ . عَلِيُّ بْنُ إِبْرَاهِيمَ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنِ النَّوْفَلِيِّ عَنِ السَّكُونِيِّ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) قَالَ الْكِلَابُ الْكُرْدِيَّةُ إِذَا عُلِّمَتْ فَهِيَ بِمَنْزِلَةِ السَّلُوقِيَّةِ .

text: And from him, from Sayf Bin Umeyra, from Mansour Bin Hazim, from Salim Al Ashalli who said, ‘I asked Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> about the prey of the trained dog who has eaten from the prey. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Eat from it’.

citation.arabic_text: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) عَنْ صَيْدِ الْكَلْبِ الْمُعَلَّمِ قَدْ أَكَلَ مِنْ صَيْدِهِ قَالَ كُلْ مِنْهُ .
citation.translation: And from him, from Sayf Bin Umeyra, from Mansour Bin Hazim, from Salim Al Ashalli who said, ‘I asked Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> about the prey of the trained dog who has eaten from the prey. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Eat from it’.

text: Al Husayn Bin Muhammad, from Moala Bin Muhammad, from Al Hassan Bin Ali, from Aban Bin Usman, from Abdul Rahman Bin Abu Abdullah who said, ‘I asked Abu Abdullahasws about a man who sent his dog, so it seized a prey and ate from it. Can he eat from its remains?’ So heasws said: ‘Eat from what the dog kills when you Named (Bismillah) over it. So if had forgotten (Bismillah), so eat from it as well, and eat its remains’.

citation.arabic_text: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) عَنْ رَجُلٍ أَرْسَلَ كَلْبَهُ فَأَخَذَ صَيْداً فَأَكَلَ مِنْهُ آكُلُ مِنْ فَضْلِهِ فَقَالَ كُلْ مِمَّا قَتَلَ الْكَلْبُ إِذَا سَمَّيْتَ عَلَيْهِ فَإِنْ كُنْتَ نَاسِياً فَكُلْ مِنْهُ أَيْضاً وَ كُلْ فَضْلَهُ .
citation.translation: Al Husayn Bin Muhammad, from Moala Bin Muhammad, from Al Hassan Bin Ali, from Aban Bin Usman, from Abdul Rahman Bin Abu Abdullah who said, ‘I asked Abu Abdullahasws about a man who sent his dog, so it seized a prey and ate from it. Can he eat from its remains?’ So heasws said: ‘Eat from what the dog kills when you Named (Bismillah) over it. So if had forgotten (Bismillah), so eat from it as well, and eat its remains’.

text: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, and Ali Bin Al Hakam, from Musa Bin Bakr, from Zurara, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws having said regarding a prey of the dog, if the man sends it and Names (Bismillah), so let him eat from what it remains upon it, even if it has killed, and even if it has eaten (from it). So eat from what remains, even it was not trained (earlier on), but he trained it in that very moment, then sends it, so he eats from it, for it is trained. So as for (a hunting animal) different to the dog, from what is hunted by the leopard, and the falcon, and similar ones to that, so do not eat from its prey, except what you come to and purify (slaughter) it, because Allahazwj Mighty and Majestic is Saying ‘[5:4] trained ones. So whatever was different to the dog, so its prey is not from what can be eaten, except if you come to it, (and you) purify (slaughter) it’.

citation.arabic_text: فِي صَيْدِ الْكَلْبِ إِنْ أَرْسَلَهُ الرَّجُلُ وَ سَمَّى فَلْيَأْكُلْ مِمَّا أَمْسَكَ عَلَيْهِ وَ إِنْ قَتَلَ وَ إِنْ أَكَلَ فَكُلْ مَا بَقِيَ وَ إِنْ كَانَ غَيْرَ مُعَلَّمٍ يُعَلِّمُهُ فِي سَاعَتِهِ ثُمَّ يُرْسِلُهُ فَيَأْكُلُ مِنْهُ فَإِنَّهُ مُعَلَّمٌ فَأَمَّا خِلَافُ الْكَلْبِ مِمَّا يَصِيدُ الْفَهْدُ وَ الصَّقْرُ وَ أَشْبَاهُ ذَلِكَ فَلَا تَأْكُلْ مِنْ صَيْدِهِ إِلَّا مَا أَدْرَكْتَ ذَكَاتَهُ لِأَنَّ اللَّهَ عَزَّ وَ جَلَّ يَقُولُ مُكَلِّبِينَ فَمَا كَانَ خِلَافَ الْكَلْبِ فَلَيْسَ صَيْدُهُ مِمَّا يُؤْكَلُ إِلَّا أَنْ تُدْرِكَ ذَكَاتَهُ .

text: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al Halby, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, said, ‘He<sup>asws</sup> was asked about the falcon and the dog when they both hunt and have killed its prey and eaten from it. Can one eat from its remains or not?’ So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘As for what the bird has killed, so do not eat it, except if you purify (slaughter) it; and as for that the dog kills, and the Name of Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic is Mentioned over it, so eat, even if it has eaten from it’.

citation.arabic_text: إِنَّهُ سُئِلَ عَنْ صَيْدِ الْبَازِي وَ الْكَلْبِ إِذَا صَادَ وَ قَدْ قَتَلَ صَيْدَهُ وَ أَكَلَ مِنْهُ آكُلُ فَضْلَهُمَا أَمْ لَا فَقَالَ ( عليه السلام ) أَمَّا مَا قَتَلَتْهُ الطَّيْرُ فَلَا تَأْكُلْهُ إِلَّا أَنْ تُذَكِّيَهُ وَ أَمَّا مَا قَتَلَهُ الْكَلْبُ وَ قَدْ ذَكَرْتَ اسْمَ اللَّهِ عَزَّ وَ جَلَّ عَلَيْهِ فَكُلْ وَ إِنْ أَكَلَ مِنْهُ .

Can one eat from its remains or not?’ So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘As for what the bird has killed, so do not eat it, except if you purify (slaughter) it; and as for that the dog kills, and the Name of Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic is Mentioned over it, so eat, even if it has eaten from it’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: ضعيف - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (1/340)

text: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from AL Husayn Bin Saeed, from Al Nazar Bin Suweyd, from Al Qasim Bin Suleyman who said, ‘I asked Abu Abdullahasws about a dog which fled, and was not sent by its owner, so it hunted. Then its owner came over, and it had killed it. Can he eat from it?’ So heasws said: ‘No’. And heasws said: ‘When it hunts, and it has been Named (Bismillah), so let him eat, and if it hunts and has not been Named (Bismillah), so no; and this is from what [5:4] and what you have taught the hunting animals, trained ones’.

citation.arabic_text: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) مِنْ كَلْبٍ أَفْلَتَ وَ لَمْ يُرْسِلْهُ صَاحِبُهُ فَصَادَ فَأَدْرَكَهُ صَاحِبُهُ وَ قَدْ قَتَلَهُ أَ يَأْكُلُ مِنْهُ فَقَالَ لَا وَ قَالَ ( عليه السلام ) إِذَا صَادَ وَ قَدْ سَمَّى فَلْيَأْكُلْ وَ إِنْ صَادَ وَ لَمْ يُسَمِّ فَلَا يَأْكُلْ وَ هَذَا مِنْ ما عَلَّمْتُمْ مِنَ الْجَوارِحِ مُكَلِّبِينَ .

text: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Muawiya Bin Hukeym, form Abu Malik Al Hazramy, from Jameel Bin Darraj who said, ‘I said to Abu Abdullahasws, ‘I sent the dog (to hunt) and Named (Bismillah) over it. So it hunted, and there was nothing with me that I could purify (slaughter) it with’. Heasws said: ‘Leave it until it kills it, and eat’.

text: Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Al Hakam, from Musa Bin Bakr, from Zurara, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws having said: ‘When the man sends his dog (to hunt) and forgets to Name (Bismillah), so he is at the status of the one slaughters and forgets to Name (Bismillah), and similar to that is when he throws with the spear and forgets to Name (Bismillah)’.

citation.arabic_text: إِذَا أَرْسَلَ الرَّجُلُ كَلْبَهُ وَ نَسِيَ أَنْ يُسَمِّيَ فَهُوَ بِمَنْزِلَةِ مَنْ ذَبَحَ وَ نَسِيَ أَنْ يُسَمِّيَ وَ كَذَلِكَ إِذَا رَمَى بِالسَّهْمِ وَ نَسِيَ أَنْ يُسَمِّيَ .
citation.translation: Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Al Hakam, from Musa Bin Bakr, from Zurara, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws having said: ‘When the man sends his dog (to hunt) and forgets to Name (Bismillah), so he is at the status of the one slaughters and forgets to Name (Bismillah), and similar to that is when he throws with the spear and forgets to Name (Bismillah)’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: موثق - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (1/341)

text: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Muhammad Bin Ahmad, form one of our companions, from Al Hassan Bin Ali Bin Abu Hamza, from his father, from Abu Baseer, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws, said, ‘I asked himasws about a people who sent their dogs (to hunt) and all of these were trained, and they had Named (Bismillah) over it. So when the dogs went, so another dog included itself, one whose owner was not known. So they participated together in the hunting. So heasws said: ‘They should not be eating from it, because it is not known whether it was the trained dog which seized it (the prey) or not’.

citation.arabic_text: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنْ قَوْمٍ أَرْسَلُوا كِلَابَهُمْ وَ هِيَ مُعَلَّمَةٌ كُلُّهَا وَ قَدْ سَمَّوْا عَلَيْهَا فَلَمَّا أَنْ مَضَتِ الْكِلَابُ دَخَلَ فِيهَا كَلْبٌ غَرِيبٌ لَمْ يَعْرِفُوا لَهُ صَاحِباً فَاشْتَرَكْنَ جَمِيعاً فِي الصَّيْدِ فَقَالَ لَا يُؤْكَلُ مِنْهُ لِأَنَّكَ لَا تَدْرِي أَخَذَهُ مُعَلَّمٌ أَمْ لَا .
citation.translation: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Muhammad Bin Ahmad, form one of our companions, from Al Hassan Bin Ali Bin Abu Hamza, from his father, from Abu Baseer, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws, said, ‘I asked himasws about a people who sent their dogs (to hunt) and all of these were trained, and they had Named (Bismillah) over it. text: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Al Nowfaly, from Al Sakuny, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The black dog is the beast, do not eat from its prey because Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> ordered with its killing’.

text: قَالَ أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ ( عليه السلام ) الْكَلْبُ الْأَسْوَدُ الْبَهِيمُ لَا يُؤْكَلُ صَيْدُهُ لِأَنَّ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) أَمَرَ بِقَتْلِهِ .

text: Abu Ali Al Ashary, form Muhammad Bin Abdul Jabbar, and Muhammad Bin Ismail, from Al Fazl Bin Shazaan, altogether from Safwan Bin Yahya, from Ibn Muskan, from Al Halby who said, ‘Abu Abdullahasws said: ‘Myasws father used to pass a Verdict and heasws was fearing (the Clan of Umayya), and weasws (also) fear (the Clan of Umayya) regarding the prey of the falcons and the hawks; and as for now, so weasws are not fearing (the Clan Umayya), and weasws are not Permitting its prey, except if you were to come to it and purify (slaughter) it, for it is in the Book of Aliasws that Allahazwj Mighty and Majestic is Saying [5:4] and what you have taught the hunting animals, trained ones, is regarding the dogs’.

citation.arabic_text: قَالَ أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) كَانَ أَبِي ( عليه السلام ) يُفْتِي وَ كَانَ يَتَّقِي وَ نَحْنُ نَخَافُ فِي صَيْدِ الْبُزَاةِ وَ الصُّقُورِ وَ أَمَّا الْآنَ فَإِنَّا لَا نَخَافُ وَ لَا نُحِلُّ صَيْدَهَا إِلَّا أَنْ تُدْرَكَ ذَكَاتُهُ فَإِنَّهُ فِي كِتَابِ عَلِيٍّ ( عليه السلام ) أَنَّ اللَّهَ عَزَّ وَ جَلَّ يَقُولُ وَ ما عَلَّمْتُمْ مِنَ الْجَوارِحِ مُكَلِّبِينَ فِي الْكِلَابِ .
citation.translation: Abu Ali Al Ashary, form Muhammad Bin Abdul Jabbar, and Muhammad Bin Ismail, from Al Fazl Bin Shazaan, altogether from Safwan Bin Yahya, from Ibn Muskan, from Al Halby who said, ‘Abu Abdullahasws said: ‘Myasws father used to pass a Verdict and heasws was fearing (the Clan of Umayya), and weasws (also) fear (the Clan of Umayya) regarding the prey of the falcons and the hawks; and as for now, so weasws are not fearing (the Clan Umayya), and weasws are not Permitting its prey, except if you were to come to it and purify (slaughter) it, for it is in the Book of Aliasws that Allahazwj Mighty and Majestic is Saying [5:4] and what you have taught the hunting animals, trained ones, is regarding the dogs’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: صحيح - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (21/342)

text: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Al Hakam, from Ali Bin Abu Hamza, from Abu Baseer who said, ‘Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘When you send a falcon, or a hawk, or an eagle (to hunt), so do not eat until you come to it, so you purify (slaughter) it, and if it has killed, so do not eat’.

citation.arabic_text: قَالَ أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) إِذَا أَرْسَلْتَ بَازاً أَوْ صَقْراً أَوْ عُقَاباً فَلَا تَأْكُلْ حَتَّى تُدْرِكَهُ فَتُذَكِّيَهُ وَ إِنْ قَتَلَ فَلَا تَأْكُلْ .
citation.translation: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Al Hakam, from Ali Bin Abu Hamza, from Abu Baseer who said, ‘Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘When you send a falcon, or a hawk, or an eagle (to hunt), so do not eat until you come to it, so you purify (slaughter) it, and if it has killed, so do not eat’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: ضعيف على المشهور - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (1/342)

text: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ail Bin Al Hakam, from Aban Bin Usman, from Abdullah Bin Suleyman who said, ‘I asked Abu Abdullahasws about a man who sent his dog and his hawk (to hunt). So heasws said: ‘As for the hawk, so do not eat from its prey until you come to it, (and you) purify (slaughter) it; and as for the dog, so eat from it when you Mentioned the Name of Allahazwj (Bismillah), whether the dog has eaten from it or did not eat from it’.

citation.arabic_text: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) عَنْ رَجُلٍ أَرْسَلَ كَلْبَهُ وَ صَقْرَهُ فَقَالَ أَمَّا الصَّقْرُ فَلَا تَأْكُلْ مِنْ صَيْدِهِ حَتَّى تُدْرِكَ ذَكَاتَهُ وَ أَمَّا الْكَلْبُ فَكُلْ مِنْهُ إِذَا ذَكَرْتَ اسْمَ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ أَكَلَ الْكَلْبُ مِنْهُ أَمْ لَمْ يَأْكُلْ .
citation.translation: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ail Bin Al Hakam, from Aban Bin Usman, from Abdullah Bin Suleyman who said, ‘I asked Abu Abdullahasws about a man who sent his dog and his hawk (to hunt). So heasws said: ‘As for the hawk, so do not eat from its prey until you come to it, (and you) purify (slaughter) it; and as for the dog, so eat from it when you Mentioned the Name of Allahazwj (Bismillah), whether the dog has eaten from it or did not eat from it’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: مجهول - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (1/343)

text: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad Bin Isa, from Hareyz, from Muhammad Bin Muslim, (It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> that he<sup>asws</sup> abhorred the prey of the falcon, except what you come to and purify (slaughter) it’.

citation.arabic_text: أَنَّهُ كَرِهَ صَيْدَ الْبَازِي إِلَّا مَا أُدْرِكَتْ ذَكَاتُهُ .
citation.translation: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad Bin Isa, from Hareyz, from Muhammad Bin Muslim, (It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> that he<sup>asws</sup> abhorred the prey of the falcon, except what you come to and purify (slaughter) it’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: حسن - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (21/343)

text: Al Husayn Bin Muhammad, from Moala Bin Muhammad, from Al Hassan Bin Ali, from Aban Bin Usman, from Abdul Rahman Bin Abu Abdullah, said, ‘I asked Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> about a man who sent his falcon or his dog (to hunt), so it seized a prey, and ate from it. Can he eat from its remains?’ So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘No, whatever the falcon killed so do not eat from it except if you slaughter it’.

citation.arabic_text: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) عَنْ رَجُلٍ أَرْسَلَ بَازَهُ أَوْ كَلْبَهُ فَأَخَذَ صَيْداً وَ أَكَلَ مِنْهُ آكُلُ مِنْ فَضْلِهِمَا فَقَالَ لَا مَا قَتَلَ الْبَازِي فَلَا تَأْكُلْ مِنْهُ إِلَّا أَنْ تَذْبَحَهُ .
citation.translation: Al Husayn Bin Muhammad, from Moala Bin Muhammad, from Al Hassan Bin Ali, from Aban Bin Usman, from Abdul Rahman Bin Abu Abdullah, said, ‘I asked Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> about a man who sent his falcon or his dog (to hunt), so it seized a prey, and ate from it. Can he eat from its remains?’ So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘No, whatever the falcon killed so do not eat from it except if you slaughter it’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: ضعيف على المشهور - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (21/343)

text: Aban, from Abu Al Abbas, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, said, ‘I asked him<sup>asws</sup> about a prey of the falcon and the hawk. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Do not eat what the falcon and the hawk kill, and do not eat what the predators from the birds kill’.

citation.arabic_text: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنْ صَيْدِ الْبَازِي وَ الصَّقْرِ فَقَالَ لَا تَأْكُلْ مَا قَتَلَ الْبَازِي وَ الصَّقْرُ وَ لَا تَأْكُلْ مَا قَتَلَ سِبَاعُ الطَّيْرِ .
citation.translation: Aban, from Abu Al Abbas, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, said, ‘I asked him<sup>asws</sup> about a prey of the falcon and the hawk. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Do not eat what the falcon and the hawk kill, and do not eat what the predators from the birds kill’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: ضعيف على المشهور - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (1/343)

text: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, and Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, altogether from Ibn Mahboub, from Ibn Raib, from Abu Ubeyda Al Haza’a who said, ‘I said to Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, ‘What are you<sup>asws</sup> saying regarding the falcon, and the hawk, and the eagle?’ So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘If you come to it, purify (slaughter) it, so eat from it, and if you do not come to it (and) purify (slaughter) it, so do not eat’.

citation.arabic_text: قُلْتُ لِأَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) مَا تَقُولُ فِي الْبَازِي وَ الصَّقْرِ وَ الْعُقَابِ فَقَالَ إِنْ أَدْرَكْتَ ذَكَاتَهُ فَكُلْ مِنْهُ وَ إِنْ لَمْ تُدْرِكْ ذَكَاتَهُ فَلَا تَأْكُلْ .
citation.translation: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, and Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, altogether from Ibn Mahboub, from Ibn Raib, from Abu Ubeyda Al Haza’a who said, ‘I said to Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, ‘What are you<sup>asws</sup> saying regarding the falcon, and the hawk, and the eagle?’ So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘If you come to it, purify (slaughter) it, so eat from it, and if you do not come to it (and) purify (slaughter) it, so do not eat’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: حسن كالصحيح - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (1/343)

text: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Abu Nasr, from Al Mufazzal Bin Salih, from Aban Bin Taghlub who said, ‘I heard Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> saying: ‘My<sup>asws</sup> father<sup>asws</sup> was issuing Fatwas during the era of the Clan of Umayya that whatever the falcon and the hawk kills, so it is Permissible, and he<sup>asws</sup> was observing dissimulation from them, and I<sup>asws</sup> am not fearing them (anymore), and it is Prohibited what (they) kill’.

citation.arabic_text: سَمِعْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) يَقُولُ كَانَ أَبِي ( عليه السلام ) يُفْتِي فِي زَمَنِ بَنِي أُمَيَّةَ أَنَّ مَا قَتَلَ الْبَازِي وَ الصَّقْرُ فَهُوَ حَلَالٌ وَ كَانَ يَتَّقِيهِمْ وَ أَنَا لَا أَتَّقِيهِمْ وَ هُوَ حَرَامٌ مَا قَتَلَ .
citation.translation: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Abu Nasr, from Al Mufazzal Bin Salih, from Aban Bin Taghlub who said, ‘I heard Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> saying: ‘My<sup>asws</sup> father<sup>asws</sup> was issuing Fatwas during the era of the Clan of Umayya that whatever the falcon and the hawk kills, so it is Permissible, and he<sup>asws</sup> was observing dissimulation from them, and I<sup>asws</sup> am not fearing them (anymore), and it is Prohibited what (they) kill’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: ضعيف على المشهور - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (21/343)

text: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ismail Bin Marrar, from Yunus, from Abdullah Bin Sinan who said, ‘I asked Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> about a prey of the falcon when it hunts, and kills, and eats from it – can one eat from its remainder or not?’ So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘As for what the bird ate, so do not eat, except if you purify (slaughter) it’.

citation.arabic_text: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) عَنْ صَيْدِ الْبَازِي إِذَا صَادَ وَ قَتَلَ وَ أَكَلَ مِنْهُ آكُلُ مِنْ فَضْلِهِ أَمْ لَا فَقَالَ أَمَّا مَا أَكَلَتِ الطَّيْرُ فَلَا تَأْكُلْ إِلَّا أَنْ تُذَكِّيَهُ .
citation.translation: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ismail Bin Marrar, from Yunus, from Abdullah Bin Sinan who said, ‘I asked Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> about a prey of the falcon when it hunts, and kills, and eats from it – can one eat from its remainder or not?’ So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘As for what the bird ate, so do not eat, except if you purify (slaughter) it’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: مجهول - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (1/344)

text: Abu Ali Al Ashary, from Muhammad Bin Abdul Jabbar, from Ibn Fazzal, from Mufazzal Bin Salih, from Lays Al Murady who said, ‘I asked Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> about the hawk and the falcon, and about its prey. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Every prey which it did not kill when you came to it, so purify (slaughter) it, and the last of the purification (slaughtering) is when the eyes were fluttering and the legs were kicking and the tail was moving’. And he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘And the hawk and the falcon are not in the Quran (to justify their killings)’.

citation.arabic_text: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) عَنِ الصُّقُورِ وَ الْبُزَاةِ وَ عَنْ صَيْدِهَا فَقَالَ كُلْ مَا لَمْ يَقْتُلْنَ إِذَا أَدْرَكْتَ ذَكَاتَهُ وَ آخِرُ الذَّكَاةِ إِذَا كَانَتِ الْعَيْنُ تَطْرِفُ وَ الرِّجْلُ تَرْكُضُ وَ الذَّنَبُ تَتَحَرَّكُ وَ قَالَ ( عليه السلام ) لَيْسَتِ الصُّقُورُ وَ الْبُزَاةُ فِي الْقُرْآنِ .
citation.translation: Abu Ali Al Ashary, from Muhammad Bin Abdul Jabbar, from Ibn Fazzal, from Mufazzal Bin Salih, from Lays Al Murady who said, ‘I asked Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> about the hawk and the falcon, and about its prey. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Every prey which it did not kill when you came to it, so purify (slaughter) it, and the last of the purification (slaughtering) is when the eyes were fluttering and the legs were kicking and the tail was moving’. And he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘And the hawk and the falcon are not in the Quran (to justify their killings)’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: ضعيف - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (21/344)

text: Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Muhammad Bin Ahmad Al Nahdy, from Muhammad Bin Al Waleed, from Aban, from Al Fazl Bin Abdul Malik who said, ‘Do not eat from that the predatory birds kill’.[859] (P.s. – This is not a Hadeeth)

citation.arabic_text: لَا تَأْكُلْ مِمَّا قَتَلَتْ سِبَاعُ الطَّيْرِ .
citation.translation: Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Muhammad Bin Ahmad Al Nahdy, from Muhammad Bin Al Waleed, from Aban, from Al Fazl Bin Abdul Malik who said, ‘Do not eat from that the predatory birds kill’.[859] (P.s. – This is not a Hadeeth)
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: ضعيف - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (1/344)

text: Ali Bin Ibrahim, form his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hisham Bin Salim, from Suleyman Bin Khalid who said, ‘I asked Abu Abdullahasws about the dog of the Magians, the Muslim man takes it, so he Name (Bismillah) when he sends it (to hunt). Can he eat from what it catches upon?’ Heasws said: ‘Yes, because it is a trained hunting animal, the Name of Allahazwj has been Mentioned over it’.

citation.arabic_text: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) عَنْ كَلْبِ الْمَجُوسِيِّ يَأْخُذُهُ الرَّجُلُ الْمُسْلِمُ فَيُسَمِّي حِينَ يُرْسِلُهُ أَ يَأْكُلُ مِمَّا أَمْسَكَ عَلَيْهِ قَالَ نَعَمْ لِأَنَّهُ مُكَلَّبٌ قَدْ ذَكَرَ اسْمَ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ.
citation.translation: Ali Bin Ibrahim, form his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hisham Bin Salim, from Suleyman Bin Khalid who said, ‘I asked Abu Abdullahasws about the dog of the Magians, the Muslim man takes it, so he Name (Bismillah) when he sends it (to hunt). Can he eat from what it catches upon?’ Heasws said: ‘Yes, because it is a trained hunting animal, the Name of Allahazwj has been Mentioned over it’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: حسن - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (21/345)

text: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Al Hakam, from Mansour Bin Yunus, from Abdul Rahman Bin Sayaba who said, ‘I said to Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, ‘I borrowed a dog of the Magians, so I hunted with it. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Do not eat from its prey, except if a Muslims trains it, so it learns it’.

citation.arabic_text: قُلْتُ لِأَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) إِنِّي أَسْتَعِيرُ كَلْبَ الْمَجُوسِيِّ فَأَصِيدُ بِهِ فَقَالَ ( عليه السلام ) لَا تَأْكُلْ مِنْ صَيْدِهِ إِلَّا أَنْ يَكُونَ عَلَّمَهُ مُسْلِمٌ فَتَعَلَّمَهُ .
citation.translation: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Al Hakam, from Mansour Bin Yunus, from Abdul Rahman Bin Sayaba who said, ‘I said to Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, ‘I borrowed a dog of the Magians, so I hunted with it. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Do not eat from its prey, except if a Muslims trains it, so it learns it’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: مجهول - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (1/345)

text: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Al Nowfaly, from Al Sakuny, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws having said: ‘A dog of the Magians, do not eat its prey, except if the Muslim takes it, so he trains it and sends it (to hunt); and similar to that is the falcon, and a dog of the Ahl Al-Zimma (People under the responsibility), and their falcons are Permissible for the Muslims that they should be eating their prey’.

citation.arabic_text: كَلْبُ الْمَجُوسِيِّ لَا تَأْكُلْ صَيْدَهُ إِلَّا أَنْ يَأْخُذَهُ الْمُسْلِمُ فَيُعَلِّمَهُ وَ يُرْسِلَهُ وَ كَذَلِكَ الْبَازِي وَ كِلَابُ أَهْلِ الذِّمَّةِ وَ بُزَاتُهُمْ حَلَالٌ لِلْمُسْلِمِينَ أَنْ يَأْكُلُوا صَيْدَهَا .
citation.translation: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Al Nowfaly, from Al Sakuny, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws having said: ‘A dog of the Magians, do not eat its prey, except if the Muslim takes it, so he trains it and sends it (to hunt); and similar to that is the falcon, and a dog of the Ahl Al-Zimma (People under the responsibility), and their falcons are Permissible for the Muslims that they should be eating their prey’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: ضعيف على المشهور - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (21/345)

text: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, form Ibn Fazzal, from Sa’alba Bin Maymoun, from Bureyd Bin MUawiya Al Ijaly, from Muhammad Bin Muslim, (It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Eat from the hunt what is killed by the sword, and the arrow, and the spear’. And he<sup>asws</sup> was asked about a hunt which was hunted, so the people apportioned it before it died. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘There is no problem with it’.

citation.arabic_text: كُلْ مِنَ الصَّيْدِ مَا قَتَلَ السَّيْفُ وَ السَّهْمُ وَ الرُّمْحُ وَ سُئِلَ عَنْ صَيْدٍ صِيدَ فَتَوَزَّعَهُ الْقَوْمُ قَبْلَ أَنْ يَمُوتَ فَقَالَ لَا بَأْسَ بِهِ .
citation.translation: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, form Ibn Fazzal, from Sa’alba Bin Maymoun, from Bureyd Bin MUawiya Al Ijaly, from Muhammad Bin Muslim, (It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Eat from the hunt what is killed by the sword, and the arrow, and the spear’. And he<sup>asws</sup> was asked about a hunt which was hunted, so the people apportioned it before it died. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘There is no problem with it’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: موثق - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (21/346)

text: And from him, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Abdul Rahman Bin Abu Najran, from Aasim Bin Humeyd, from Muhammad Bin Qays, Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> has said: ‘The one who injures a hunt by a weapon, and Mentions the Name of Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic over it, then remains for a night or two nights, the predators not eating from it, and he knows that it was his weapon which killed it, so he can eat from it if he so desires to’. And he<sup>asws</sup> said regarding a mountain goat which the man hunts, but the people block him, and the man pursues it. Do you<sup>asws</sup> view it as Forbidden?’ So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘It is not with a prohibition, and there is no problem with it’.

citation.arabic_text: مَنْ جَرَحَ صَيْداً بِسِلَاحٍ وَ ذَكَرَ اسْمَ اللَّهِ عَزَّ وَ جَلَّ عَلَيْهِ ثُمَّ بَقِيَ لَيْلَةً أَوْ لَيْلَتَيْنِ لَمْ يَأْكُلْ مِنْهُ سَبُعٌ وَ قَدْ عَلِمَ أَنَّ سِلَاحَهُ هُوَ الَّذِي قَتَلَهُ فَيَأْكُلُ مِنْهُ إِنْ شَاءَ وَ قَالَ فِي إِيَّلٍ اصْطَادَهُ رَجُلٌ فَتَقَطَّعَهُ النَّاسُ وَ الرَّجُلُ يَتْبَعُهُ أَ فَتَرَاهُ نُهْبَةً فَقَالَ ( عليه السلام ) لَيْسَ بِنُهْبَةٍ وَ لَيْسَ بِهِ بَأْسٌ .
citation.translation: And from him, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Abdul Rahman Bin Abu Najran, from Aasim Bin Humeyd, from Muhammad Bin Qays, Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> has said: ‘The one who injures a hunt by a weapon, and Mentions the Name of Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic over it, then remains for a night or two nights, the predators not eating from it, and he knows that it was his weapon which killed it, so he can eat from it if he so desires to’. And he<sup>asws</sup> said regarding a mountain goat which the man hunts, but the people block him, and the man pursues it. Do you<sup>asws</sup> view it as Forbidden?’ So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘It is not with a prohibition, and there is no problem with it’.

text: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad, from Hareyz who said, ‘Abu Abdullahasws was asked about the shot at (by an arrow), so its owner finds it in the morning. Can he eat from it?’ So heasws said: ‘If he knows that it was his shooting which killed it, so let him eat from that when he had Named (Bismillah)’.

citation.arabic_text: سُئِلَ أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) عَنِ الرَّمِيَّةِ يَجِدُهَا صَاحِبُهَا فِي الْغَدِ أَ يَأْكُلُ مِنْهُ فَقَالَ إِنْ عَلِمَ أَنَّ رَمْيَتَهُ هِيَ الَّتِي قَتَلَتْهُ فَلْيَأْكُلْ مِنْ ذَلِكَ إِذَا كَانَ قَدْ سَمَّى .

text: A number of our companoins, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Khalid, from usman Bin Isa, from Sama’at who said, ‘I asked him<sup>asws</sup> about a man who shot (an arrow) at a wild donkey, or a deer, so it hit him. Then he was in search for it, so he found it in the morning, and his arrow was in it. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘If he knows that he hit it, and that it was his arrow which killed it, so let him eat from it, or else, so he should not eat from it’.

citation.arabic_text: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنْ رَجُلٍ رَمَى حِمَارَ وَحْشٍ أَوْ ظَبْياً فَأَصَابَهُ ثُمَّ كَانَ فِي طَلَبِهِ فَوَجَدَهُ مِنَ الْغَدِ وَ سَهْمُهُ فِيهِ فَقَالَ إِنْ عَلِمَ أَنَّهُ أَصَابَهُ وَ أَنَّ سَهْمَهُ هُوَ الَّذِي قَتَلَهُ فَلْيَأْكُلْ مِنْهُ وَ إِلَّا فَلَا يَأْكُلْ مِنْهُ .

text: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Abdullah Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Al Hakam, from Aban Bin Usman, from Isa Al Zummy who said, ‘I said to Abu Abdullahasws, ‘I shot my arrow and I do not know whether I Named (Bismillah) or did not Name’. So heasws said: ‘Each (of the two) is not a problem’. I said, ‘I shoot and it disappears from me, so I find my arrow in it?’ So heasws said: ‘Eat what was not eaten from it, and if it had been eaten from, so do not eat from it’.

citation.arabic_text: قُلْتُ لِأَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) أَرْمِي سَهْمِي وَ لَا أَدْرِي أَ سَمَّيْتُ أَمْ لَمْ أُسَمِّ فَقَالَ كُلْ لَا بَأْسَ قَالَ قُلْتُ أَرْمِي وَ يَغِيبُ عَنِّي فَأَجِدُ سَهْمِي فِيهِ فَقَالَ كُلْ مَا لَمْ يُؤْكَلْ مِنْهُ وَ إِنْ كَانَ قَدْ أُكِلَ مِنْهُ فَلَا تَأْكُلْ مِنْهُ .

text: Abu Ali Al Ashary, from Muhammad Bim Abdul Jabbar, and Muhammad Bin Ismail, from Al Fazl Bin Shazaan, altogether from Safwan, from Ibn Muskan, from Al Halby who said, ‘I asked Abu Abdullahasws about the hunt which the man has struck by the sword, or stabbed it with the spear, or shot at by an arrow, so he killed it, and he had Named (Bismillah) when he did that. So heasws said: ‘Eat, there is no problem with it’.

citation.arabic_text: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) عَنِ الصَّيْدِ يَضْرِبُهُ الرَّجُلُ بِالسَّيْفِ أَوْ يَطْعُنُهُ بِالرُّمْحِ أَوْ يَرْمِيهِ بِسَهْمٍ فَقَتَلَهُ وَ قَدْ سَمَّى حِينَ فَعَلَ ذَلِكَ فَقَالَ كُلْ لَا بَأْسَ بِهِ .

So heasws said: ‘Eat, there is no problem with it’.

text: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Al Husayn Bin Saeed, from Al nazar Bin Suweyd, from Hisham Bin Salim, from Suleyman Bin Khalid who said, ‘I asked Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> about the (prey) shot at, its owner finds it, can he eat it?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘If he knew that it was his shooting which killed it, so let him eat’.

text: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ibn Abu Najran, from Aasim Bin Humeyd, from Muhammad Bin Qays, (It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> said regarding a hunt in which an arrow was found, and it was dead, not known who killed it. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Do not consume it’.

citation.arabic_text: قَالَ أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ ( عليه السلام ) فِي صَيْدٍ وُجِدَ فِيهِ سَهْمٌ وَ هُوَ مَيِّتٌ لَا يُدْرَى مَنْ قَتَلَهُ قَالَ لَا تَطْعَمْهُ .

He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Do not consume it’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: صحيح - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (1/348)

text: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Abdullah Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Al Hakam, from Aban Bin Usman, from Muhammad Al Halby who said, ‘I asked him<sup>asws</sup> about the man who shoots at the hunted prey, so he knocks it down. So the people turn up and block him. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Eat it’.

citation.arabic_text: سَأَلْتُهُ ( عليه السلام ) عَنِ الرَّجُلِ يَرْمِي الصَّيْدَ فَيَصْرَعُهُ فَيَبْتَدِرُهُ الْقَوْمُ فَيُقَطِّعُونَهُ فَقَالَ كُلْهُ .

text: Abu Ali Al Ashary, from Muhammad Bin Abdul Jabbar, from Safwan, from Musa Bin Bakr, from Zurara, Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> has said: ‘When you shoot (an arrow), so you find it, and there are not traces of other than the arrow, and you see that it has not been killed by other than your arrow, so eat, whether it had disappeared from you or not disappeared from you’.

citation.arabic_text: إِذَا رَمَيْتَ فَوَجَدْتَهُ وَ لَيْسَ بِهِ أَثَرٌ غَيْرُ السَّهْمِ وَ تَرَى أَنَّهُ لَمْ يَقْتُلْهُ غَيْرُ سَهْمِكَ فَكُلْ غَابَ عَنْكَ أَوْ لَمْ يَغِبْ عَنْكَ .
citation.translation: Abu Ali Al Ashary, from Muhammad Bin Abdul Jabbar, from Safwan, from Musa Bin Bakr, from Zurara, Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> has said: ‘When you shoot (an arrow), so you find it, and there are not traces of other than the arrow, and you see that it has not been killed by other than your arrow, so eat, whether it had disappeared from you or not disappeared from you’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: ضعيف على المشهور - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (21/349)

text: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Ibn Mahboub, from Hisham Bin Salim, from Sama’at Bin Mahran who said, ‘I asked Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> about the man who shoots at the hunted prey, and he is upon the mountain, so the arrow pierces it until he exits from the other side. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Eat it, but if it had fallen into the water, or tumbles from the mountain, so it dies, so do not eat it’.

citation.arabic_text: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَنِ الرَّجُلِ يَرْمِي الصَّيْدَ وَ هُوَ عَلَى الْجَبَلِ فَيَخْرِقُهُ السَّهْمُ حَتَّى يَخْرُجَ مِنَ الْجَانِبِ الْآخَرِ قَالَ كُلْهُ قَالَ فَإِنْ وَقَعَ فِي مَاءٍ أَوْ تَدَهْدَهَ مِنَ الْجَبَلِ فَمَاتَ فَلَا تَأْكُلْهُ .
citation.translation: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Ibn Mahboub, from Hisham Bin Salim, from Sama’at Bin Mahran who said, ‘I asked Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> about the man who shoots at the hunted prey, and he is upon the mountain, so the arrow pierces it until he exits from the other side. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Eat it, but if it had fallen into the water, or tumbles from the mountain, so it dies, so do not eat it’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: موثق - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (1/349)

text: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from a man, raising it, said, ‘Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Do not shoot at the hunted prey with something which is bigger than it’.

citation.arabic_text: قَالَ أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) لَا يُرْمَى الصَّيْدُ بِشَيْ‏ءٍ هُوَ أَكْبَرُ مِنْهُ .
citation.translation: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from a man, raising it, said, ‘Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Do not shoot at the hunted prey with something which is bigger than it’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: مرفوع - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (21/349)

text: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Abdullah Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Al Hakam, from Aban, from Zurara, and Ismail Al Ju’fy, (It has been narrated) both asked Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> about what the blunt weapon kills’. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘There is no problem when it was hit by you or you made it for that’.

citation.arabic_text: لَا بَأْسَ إِذَا كَانَ هُوَ مِرْمَاتَكَ أَوْ صَنَعْتَهُ لِذَلِكَ .
citation.translation: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Abdullah Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Al Hakam, from Aban, from Zurara, and Ismail Al Ju’fy, (It has been narrated) both asked Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> about what the blunt weapon kills’. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘There is no problem when it was hit by you or you made it for that’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: مجهول - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (21/350)

text: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al Halby, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having been asked about what the blunt weapon knocks down from the hunted prey. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘If there does not happen to be an arrow for it apart from the crushing, and the Name of Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic is Mentioned over it, so let him eat what is killed’. I said, ‘Supposing there happens to be an arrow apart from it?’ So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘No’.

citation.arabic_text: إِنْ لَمْ يَكُنْ لَهُ نَبْلٌ غَيْرُ الْمِعْرَاضِ وَ ذَكَرَ اسْمَ اللَّهِ عَزَّ وَ جَلَّ عَلَيْهِ فَلْيَأْكُلْ مَا قَتَلَ قُلْتُ وَ إِنْ كَانَ لَهُ نَبْلٌ غَيْرُهُ قَالَ لَا .
citation.translation: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al Halby, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having been asked about what the blunt weapon knocks down from the hunted prey. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘If there does not happen to be an arrow for it apart from the crushing, and the Name of Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic is Mentioned over it, so let him eat what is killed’. I said, ‘Supposing there happens to be an arrow apart from it?’ So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘No’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: حسن - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (21/351)

text: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, and Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, altogether from Ibn Mahboub, from Ibn Raib, from Abu Ubeyda, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘When you shoot at it with the blunt weapon, so it pierces, so eat; and if it does not pierce, and it turns sideways, so do not eat’.

citation.arabic_text: إِذَا رَمَيْتَ بِالْمِعْرَاضِ فَخَرَقَ فَكُلْ وَ إِنْ لَمْ يَخْرِقْ وَ اعْتَرَضَ فَلَا تَأْكُلْ .
citation.translation: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, and Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, altogether from Ibn Mahboub, from Ibn Raib, from Abu Ubeyda, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘When you shoot at it with the blunt weapon, so it pierces, so eat; and if it does not pierce, and it turns sideways, so do not eat’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: صحيح - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (1/351)

text: Abu Ali Al Ashary, from Muhammad Bin Abdul Jabbar, and Muhammad Bin Ismail, from Al Fazl Bin Shazaan, altogether from Safwan Bin Yahya, from Ibn Muskan, from Al Halby who said, ‘I asked Abu Abdullahasws about the hunted prey which the man shoots at with an arrow, so he hits it sideways, and he kills it, and he had Named (Bismillah) when he shot it, and the iron (arrowhead) did not hit it. So heasws said: ‘If it was the arrow which hit it, the one which killed it, so when he sees it as such, so let him eat’.

citation.arabic_text: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) عَنِ الصَّيْدِ يَرْمِيهِ الرَّجُلُ بِسَهْمٍ فَيُصِيبُهُ مُعْتَرِضاً فَيَقْتُلُهُ وَ قَدْ كَانَ سَمَّى حِينَ رَمَى وَ لَمْ تُصِبْهُ الْحَدِيدَةُ فَقَالَ إِنْ كَانَ السَّهْمُ الَّذِي أَصَابَهُ هُوَ الَّذِي قَتَلَهُ فَإِذَا رَآهُ فَلْيَأْكُلْ .
citation.translation: Abu Ali Al Ashary, from Muhammad Bin Abdul Jabbar, and Muhammad Bin Ismail, from Al Fazl Bin Shazaan, altogether from Safwan Bin Yahya, from Ibn Muskan, from Al Halby who said, ‘I asked Abu Abdullahasws about the hunted prey which the man shoots at with an arrow, so he hits it sideways, and he kills it, and he had Named (Bismillah) when he shot it, and the iron (arrowhead) did not hit it. So heasws said: ‘If it was the arrow which hit it, the one which killed it, so when he sees it as such, so let him eat’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: صحيح - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (1/351)

text: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Al Hakam, from Abu Al Magra, from Al Halby, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws, said, ‘I asked himasws about the hunted prey hit by the arrow sideways, and it was not hit by the iron (arrowhead), and he had Named (Bismillah) when he shot it Heasws said: ‘He can eat it when he hit it, and he saw it’. And about a prey hunted by the blunt weapon, so heasws said: ‘If there does not happen to be an arrow apart from it, and he had Named (Bismillah) when he threw, so let him eat from it; and if there was an arrow apart from it, so, no’.

citation.arabic_text: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنِ الصَّيْدِ يُصِيبُهُ السَّهْمُ مُعْتَرِضاً وَ لَمْ يُصِبْهُ بِحَدِيدَةٍ وَ قَدْ سَمَّى حِينَ رَمَى قَالَ يَأْكُلُهُ إِذَا أَصَابَهُ وَ هُوَ يَرَاهُ وَ عَنْ صَيْدِ الْمِعْرَاضِ فَقَالَ إِنْ لَمْ يَكُنْ لَهُ نَبْلٌ غَيْرُهُ وَ كَانَ قَدْ سَمَّى حِينَ رَمَى فَلْيَأْكُلْ مِنْهُ وَ إِنْ كَانَ لَهُ نَبْلٌ غَيْرُهُ فَلَا .
citation.translation: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Al Hakam, from Abu Al Magra, from Al Halby, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws, said, ‘I asked himasws about the hunted prey hit by the arrow sideways, and it was not hit by the iron (arrowhead), and he had Named (Bismillah) when he shot it Heasws said: ‘He can eat it when he hit it, and he saw it’. And about a prey hunted by the blunt weapon, so heasws said: ‘If there does not happen to be an arrow apart from it, and he had Named (Bismillah) when he threw, so let him eat from it; and if there was an arrow apart from it, so, no’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: صحيح - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (21/351)

text: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al Halby, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having been asked about what is killed by the stone and the pellet, can one eat from it?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘No’.

citation.arabic_text: لَا .

citation.arabic_text: أَنَّهُ كَرِهَ الْجُلَاهِقَ .
citation.translation: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Gayas Bin Ibrahim, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws, heasws disliked (killing by) the Julahiq (a type of pellet)’.

text: Abu Ali Al Ashary, from Muhammad Bin Abdul Jabbar, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ahmad Bin Umar, from Abdullah Bin Sinan, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> regarding the man who threw the pellet, and the stone, so he killed (a hunted prey), so can he eat from it?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said:’ He cannot eat’.

citation.arabic_text: الرَّجُلِ يَرْمِي بِالْبُنْدُقِ وَ الْحَجَرِ فَيَقْتُلُ أَ فَيَأْكُلُ مِنْهُ قَالَ لَا تَأْكُلْ .

citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: موثق - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (1/353)

text: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, and Ibn Abu Najran, from Aasim Bin Humeyd, from Muhammad Bin Qays, (It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘What the snare seizes from the hunt, so a hand or a leg is cut off from it, so leave it, for it is dead, and eat from what you come to as alive, and you have mentioned the Name of Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic over it’.

citation.arabic_text: قَالَ أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ ( عليه السلام ) مَا أَخَذَتِ الْحِبَالَةُ مِنْ صَيْدٍ فَقَطَعَتْ مِنْهُ يَداً أَوْ رِجْلًا فَذَرُوهُ فَإِنَّهُ مَيِّتٌ وَ كُلُوا مَا أَدْرَكْتُمْ حَيّاً وَ ذَكَرْتُمُ اسْمَ اللَّهِ عَزَّ وَ جَلَّ عَلَيْهِ .
citation.translation: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, and Ibn Abu Najran, from Aasim Bin Humeyd, from Muhammad Bin Qays, (It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘What the snare seizes from the hunt, so a hand or a leg is cut off from it, so leave it, for it is dead, and eat from what you come to as alive, and you have mentioned the Name of Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic over it’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: حسن - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (21/353)

text: Humeyd Bin Ziyad, from Al Hassan Bin Muhammad Bin Sama’at, from someone else, from Aban Bin Usman, from Abdul Rahman Bin Abu Abdullah, Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> has said: ‘What the snare seizes, so something is cut off from it, so it is dead, and what you come to from the rest of its body as alive, so purify (slaughter) it, then eat from it’.

citation.arabic_text: مَا أَخَذَتِ الْحِبَالَةُ فَقَطَعَتْ مِنْهُ شَيْئاً فَهُوَ مَيِّتٌ وَ مَا أَدْرَكْتَ مِنْ سَائِرِ جَسَدِهِ حَيّاً فَذَكِّهِ ثُمَّ كُلْ مِنْهُ .
citation.translation: Humeyd Bin Ziyad, from Al Hassan Bin Muhammad Bin Sama’at, from someone else, from Aban Bin Usman, from Abdul Rahman Bin Abu Abdullah, Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> has said: ‘What the snare seizes, so something is cut off from it, so it is dead, and what you come to from the rest of its body as alive, so purify (slaughter) it, then eat from it’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: كالموثق - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (1/353)

text: Al Husayn Bin Muhammad, from Moala Bin Muhammad, from Al Washa, from Abdul Rahman Bin Abu Abdullah, Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> has said: ‘What the snare seizes, so something is cut off from it, so it is dead, and what you come to from the rest of its body, so purify (slaughter) it, then eat from it’.

citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: ضعيف على المشهور - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (1/354)

citation.arabic_text: مَا أَخَذَتِ الْحِبَالَةُ فَانْقَطَعَ مِنْهُ شَيْ‏ءٌ أَوْ مَاتَ فَهُوَ مَيْتَةٌ .

text: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Muhammad Bin Isa, from Hajjaj, from Khalid Bin Al Hajjaj, Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> has said: ‘Do not eat from the hunted prey which falls into the water, so it dies’.

citation.arabic_text: لَا تَأْكُلْ مِنَ الصَّيْدِ إِذَا وَقَعَ فِي الْمَاءِ فَمَاتَ .
citation.translation: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Muhammad Bin Isa, from Hajjaj, from Khalid Bin Al Hajjaj, Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> has said: ‘Do not eat from the hunted prey which falls into the water, so it dies’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: مجهول - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (1/354)

text: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Khalid, from usman Bin Isa, from Sama’at, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having been asked about a man who shot as a prey, and he was upon a mountain, or a wall, so the arrow pierced into it, so it died’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Eat from it, and if it falls into the water from it being shot, so it dies, so do not eat from it’.

citation.arabic_text: هِ السَّهْمُ فَيَمُوتُ فَقَالَ كُلْ مِنْهُ وَ إِنْ وَقَعَ فِي الْمَاءِ مِنْ رَمْيَتِكَ فَمَاتَ فَلَا تَأْكُلْ مِنْهُ .

So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Eat from it, and if it falls into the water from it being shot, so it dies, so do not eat from it’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: موثق - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (1/355)

text: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Abbad Bin Suheyb who said, ‘I asked Abu Abdullahasws about a man who Named (Bismillah) and shot at a prey, so he erred and hit another. So heasws said: ‘He can eat from it’.

citation.arabic_text: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) عَنْ رَجُلٍ سَمَّى وَ رَمَى صَيْداً فَأَخْطَأَهُ وَ أَصَابَ آخَرَ فَقَالَ يَأْكُلُ مِنْهُ .
citation.translation: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Abbad Bin Suheyb who said, ‘I asked Abu Abdullahasws about a man who Named (Bismillah) and shot at a prey, so he erred and hit another. So heasws said: ‘He can eat from it’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: موثق - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (1/355)

text: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Abu Abdullah, from Al Hassan Bin Ali, from Muhammad Bin Al Fuzayl, from Muhammad Bin Abdul Rahman, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Rasool-Allah<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Do not come to the chicks in the nests, nor the bird during their sleep until the morning’. So a man said to him<sup>saww</sup>, ‘And what is their sleep, O Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup>?’ So he<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘The night is its sleep, therefore do not hunt it during its sleep until the morning, and do not come to the chick in its nest until it has grown feathers and it flies. So when it flies, then aim with your bow at it, and set-up your net for it’.

citation.arabic_text: قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ ( صلى الله عليه وآله ) لَا تَأْتُوا الْفِرَاخَ فِي أَعْشَاشِهَا وَ لَا الطَّيْرَ فِي مَنَامِهِ حَتَّى يُصْبِحَ فَقَالَ لَهُ رَجُلٌ وَ مَا مَنَامُهُ يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ فَقَالَ اللَّيْلُ مَنَامُهُ فَلَا تَطْرُقْهُ فِي مَنَامِهِ حَتَّى يُصْبِحَ وَ لَا تَأْتُوا الْفَرْخَ فِي عُشِّهِ حَتَّى يَرِيشَ وَ يَطِيرَ فَإِذَا طَارَ فَأَوْتِرْ لَهُ قَوْسَكَ وَ انْصِبْ لَهُ فَخَّكَ .
citation.translation: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Abu Abdullah, from Al Hassan Bin Ali, from Muhammad Bin Al Fuzayl, from Muhammad Bin Abdul Rahman, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Rasool-Allah<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Do not come to the chicks in the nests, nor the bird during their sleep until the morning’. So a man said to him<sup>saww</sup>, ‘And what is their sleep, O Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup>?’ So he<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘The night is its sleep, therefore do not hunt it during its sleep until the morning, and do not come to the chick in its nest until it has grown feathers and it flies. So when it flies, then aim with your bow at it, and set-up your net for it’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: صحيح - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (21/356)

text: A number of our companions, froom Sahl Bin Ziiyad, from Muhammad Bin Al Hassan Bin Shamoun, from Abdullah Bin Abdul Rahman, from Misma’a, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> forbade from coming to the birds (for hunting) at night, and he<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘The night is a security for it’.

citation.arabic_text: نَهَى رَسُولُ اللَّهِ ( صلى الله عليه وآله ) عَنْ إِتْيَانِ الطَّيْرِ بِاللَّيْلِ وَ قَالَ ( عليه السلام ) إِنَّ اللَّيْلَ أَمَانٌ لَهَا .
citation.translation: A number of our companions, froom Sahl Bin Ziiyad, from Muhammad Bin Al Hassan Bin Shamoun, from Abdullah Bin Abdul Rahman, from Misma’a, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> forbade from coming to the birds (for hunting) at night, and he<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘The night is a security for it’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: مجهول - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (21/356)

text: نَهَى رَسُولُ اللَّهِ ( صلى الله عليه وآله ) عَنْ إِتْيَانِ الطَّيْرِ بِاللَّيْلِ وَ قَالَ ( عليه السلام ) إِنَّ اللَّيْلَ أَمَانٌ لَهَا .

citation.arabic_text: نَهَى رَسُولُ اللَّهِ ( صلى الله عليه وآله ) عَنْ إِتْيَانِ الطَّيْرِ بِاللَّيْلِ وَ قَالَ ( عليه السلام ) إِنَّ اللَّيْلَ أَمَانٌ لَهَا .

text: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al Halby, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws, said, ‘I asked himasws about hunting the fish, and if he does not Name (Bismillah) over it. So heasws said: ‘There is no problem with it’.

citation.arabic_text: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنْ صَيْدِ الْحِيتَانِ وَ إِنْ لَمْ يُسَمَّ عَلَيْهِ فَقَالَ لَا بَأْسَ بِهِ .
citation.translation: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al Halby, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws, said, ‘I asked himasws about hunting the fish, and if he does not Name (Bismillah) over it. So heasws said: ‘There is no problem with it’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: حسن - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (21/357)

text: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Amro Bin Usman, from Al Mufazzal Bin Salih, from Zayd Al Shahaam, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws having been asked about hunting the fish, and if he has not Named (Bismillah) over it. So heasws said: ‘There is no problem with it, if it was alive and he seizes it’.

citation.arabic_text: لَا بَأْسَ بِهِ إِنْ كَانَ حَيّاً أَنْ يَأْخُذَهُ .
citation.translation: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Amro Bin Usman, from Al Mufazzal Bin Salih, from Zayd Al Shahaam, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws having been asked about hunting the fish, and if he has not Named (Bismillah) over it. So heasws said: ‘There is no problem with it, if it was alive and he seizes it’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: ضعيف - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (21/357)

text: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Abdullah Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Al Hakam, from Aban, from Abdul Rahman Bin Sayaba who said, ‘I asked Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> about the fish he hunts (catches), then he makes it to be in something (e.g. a basket), then he returns it into the water, so it dies in it’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Do not eat it’.

citation.arabic_text: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) عَنِ السَّمَكِ يُصَادُ ثُمَّ يُجْعَلُ فِي شَيْ‏ءٍ ثُمَّ يُعَادُ إِلَى الْمَاءِ فَيَمُوتُ فِيهِ فَقَالَ لَا تَأْكُلْهُ .
citation.translation: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Abdullah Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Al Hakam, from Aban, from Abdul Rahman Bin Sayaba who said, ‘I asked Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> about the fish he hunts (catches), then he makes it to be in something (e.g. a basket), then he returns it into the water, so it dies in it’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Do not eat it’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: مجهول - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (1/357)

text: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Abu Ayoub, (The narrator) who asked Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> about a man who baited a fish, so he tied it with a thread, and sent it in the water, so it died. Can he eat it?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘No’.

citation.arabic_text: الْمَاءِ فَمَاتَتْ أَ تُؤْكَلُ قَالَ لَا .
citation.translation: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Abu Ayoub, (The narrator) who asked Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> about a man who baited a fish, so he tied it with a thread, and sent it in the water, so it died. Can he eat it?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘No’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: حسن - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (21/357)

text: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Khalid, from Usman Bin Isa, from Abu Baseer who said, ‘I asked Abu Abdullahasws about hunting of the Magians for the fish when they catch it by the net, and they are not Naming (Bismillah), and similar to that are the Jews. So heasws said: ‘There is no problem. But rather, hunting the fishes it seizing it’.

citation.arabic_text: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) عَنْ صَيْدِ الْمَجُوسِيِّ لِلسَّمَكِ حِينَ يَضْرِبُونَ بِالشَّبَكِ وَ لَا يُسَمُّونَ وَ كَذَلِكَ الْيَهُودِيُّ فَقَالَ لَا بَأْسَ إِنَّمَا صَيْدُ الْحِيتَانِ أَخْذُهَا .
citation.translation: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Khalid, from Usman Bin Isa, from Abu Baseer who said, ‘I asked Abu Abdullahasws about hunting of the Magians for the fish when they catch it by the net, and they are not Naming (Bismillah), and similar to that are the Jews. So heasws said: ‘There is no problem. But rather, hunting the fishes it seizing it’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: موثق - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (1/357)

text: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hisham Bin Salim, from Suleyman Bin Khalid who said, ‘I asked Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> about the fishes which the Magians are hunting. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Ali<sup>asws</sup> was saying: ‘The fishes and the grass-hoppers are pure’.

citation.arabic_text: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) عَنِ الْحِيتَانِ الَّتِي يَصِيدُهَا الْمَجُوسِيُّ فَقَالَ إِنَّ عَلِيّاً ( عليه السلام ) كَانَ يَقُولُ الْحِيتَانُ وَ الْجَرَادُ ذَكِيٌّ .
citation.translation: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hisham Bin Salim, from Suleyman Bin Khalid who said, ‘I asked Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> about the fishes which the Magians are hunting. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Ali<sup>asws</sup> was saying: ‘The fishes and the grass-hoppers are pure’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: حسن - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (21/358)

text: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Abdullah Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Al Hakam, from Aban, from Salma Abu Hafs, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Ali<sup>asws</sup> was saying regarding hunting the fish: ‘When the man comes to it and it is restless and it is restless in front of him, and is moving its tail, and flickering its eyes, so it is its purification’.

citation.arabic_text: إِنَّ عَلِيّاً ( صلوات الله عليه ) كَانَ يَقُولُ فِي صَيْدِ السَّمَكَةِ إِذَا أَدْرَكَهَا الرَّجُلُ وَ هِيَ تَضْطَرِبُ وَ تَضْرِبُ بِيَدَيْهَا وَ يَتَحَرَّكُ ذَنَبُهَا وَ تَطْرِفُ بِعَيْنِهَا فَهِيَ ذَكَاتُهَا .
citation.translation: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Abdullah Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Al Hakam, from Aban, from Salma Abu Hafs, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Ali<sup>asws</sup> was saying regarding hunting the fish: ‘When the man comes to it and it is restless and it is restless in front of him, and is moving its tail, and flickering its eyes, so it is its purification’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: مجهول - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (1/358)

text: Aban, from Isa Bin Abdullah who said, ‘I asked Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> about a hunt of the Magians. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘There is no problem with it when he gives it to you as alive, and the fish as well, or else, so their testimonies are not allowed except if you witness it for yourself’.

citation.arabic_text: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) عَنْ صَيْدِ الْمَجُوسِيِّ قَالَ لَا بَأْسَ بِهِ إِذَا أَعْطَوْكَهَا حَيّاً وَ السَّمَكَ أَيْضاً وَ إِلَّا فَلَا تُجِزْ شَهَادَتَهُمْ إِلَّا أَنْ تَشْهَدَهُ أَنْتَ .
citation.translation: Aban, from Isa Bin Abdullah who said, ‘I asked Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> about a hunt of the Magians. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘There is no problem with it when he gives it to you as alive, and the fish as well, or else, so their testimonies are not allowed except if you witness it for yourself’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: مجهول - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (21/358)

text: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al Halby, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having been asked about a hunting of the Magians for the fishes when they strike over it with the netting, and they are naming it with the Polytheism (Shirk). So he<sup>asws</sup> said; ‘There is no problem with their hunting. But rather, hunting of the fishes is their catching it’. He (the narrator) said, ‘And I asked him<sup>asws</sup> about the enclosure of canes made to be in the water for the fishes. The fishes enter into it, so some of them are dying in it. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘There is no problem with it. That enclosure, rather it was made to be for hunting with it’.

citation.arabic_text: لَا بَأْسَ بِصَيْدِهِمْ إِنَّمَا صَيْدُ الْحِيتَانِ أَخْذُهُ قَالَ وَ سَأَلْتُهُ عَنِ الْحَظِيرَةِ مِنَ الْقَصَبِ تُجْعَلُ فِي الْمَاءِ لِلْحِيتَانِ تَدْخُلُ فِيهَا الْحِيتَانُ فَيَمُوتُ بَعْضُهَا فِيهَا فَقَالَ لَا بَأْسَ بِهِ إِنَّ تِلْكَ الْحَظِيرَةَ إِنَّمَا جُعِلَتْ لِيُصَادَ بِهَا .
citation.translation: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al Halby, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having been asked about a hunting of the Magians for the fishes when they strike over it with the netting, and they are naming it with the Polytheism (Shirk). So he<sup>asws</sup> said; ‘There is no problem with their hunting. But rather, hunting of the fishes is their catching it’. He (the narrator) said, ‘And I asked him<sup>asws</sup> about the enclosure of canes made to be in the water for the fishes. The fishes enter into it, so some of them are dying in it. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘There is no problem with it. That enclosure, rather it was made to be for hunting with it’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: حسن - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (21/359)

text: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Al Husayn Bin Saeed, from Fazalat, from Al Qasim Bin Bureyd, from Muhammad Bin Muslim, (It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> regarding the man who established a net in the water, then he returned to his house, and he left it established, and he came to it after that, and a fish had fallen in it, so it had died’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘What he worked by his hands, so there is no problem with eating what falls into it’.

citation.arabic_text: الرَّجُلِ يَنْصِبُ شَبَكَةً فِي الْمَاءِ ثُمَّ يَرْجِعُ إِلَى بَيْتِهِ وَ يَتْرُكُهَا مَنْصُوبَةً وَ يَأْتِيهَا بَعْدَ ذَلِكَ وَ قَدْ وَقَعَ فِيهَا سَمَكٌ فَيَمُتْنَ فَقَالَ مَا عَمِلَتْ يَدُهُ فَلَا بَأْسَ بِأَكْلِ مَا وَقَعَ فِيهَا .
citation.translation: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Al Husayn Bin Saeed, from Fazalat, from Al Qasim Bin Bureyd, from Muhammad Bin Muslim, (It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> regarding the man who established a net in the water, then he returned to his house, and he left it established, and he came to it after that, and a fish had fallen in it, so it had died’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘What he worked by his hands, so there is no problem with eating what falls into it’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: صحيح - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (1/360)

text: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Al Amraky Bin Ali, (It has been narrated) from Ali son of Ja’far<sup>asws</sup>, from his brother<sup>asws</sup> Musa<sup>asws</sup> Bin Ja’far<sup>asws</sup>, said, ‘I asked him<sup>asws</sup> about a fish which leapt out from the river, so it falls upon the bank of the river, so it died. Is it correct to eat it?’ So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘If you seize it before it dies, then it dies, so eat it; but if it died from before you seize it, so do not eat it’.

citation.arabic_text: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنْ سَمَكَةٍ وَثَبَتْ مِنْ نَهَرٍ فَوَقَعَتْ عَلَى الْجُدِّ مِنَ النَّهَرِ فَمَاتَتْ هَلْ يَصْلُحُ أَكْلُهَا فَقَالَ إِنْ أَخَذْتَهَا قَبْلَ أَنْ تَمُوتَ ثُمَّ مَاتَتْ فَكُلْهَا وَ إِنْ مَاتَتْ مِنْ قَبْلِ أَنْ تَأْخُذَهَا فَلَا تَأْكُلْهَا .
citation.translation: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Al Amraky Bin Ali, (It has been narrated) from Ali son of Ja’far<sup>asws</sup>, from his brother<sup>asws</sup> Musa<sup>asws</sup> Bin Ja’far<sup>asws</sup>, said, ‘I asked him<sup>asws</sup> about a fish which leapt out from the river, so it falls upon the bank of the river, so it died. Is it correct to eat it?’ So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘If you seize it before it dies, then it dies, so eat it; but if it died from before you seize it, so do not eat it’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: صحيح - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (21/360)

text: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Al Nowfaly, from Al Sakuny, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> that Ali<sup>asws</sup> was asked about a fish with its belly being slit, so a fish was found inside it. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Eat both of them together’.

citation.arabic_text: هَا سَمَكَةٌ فَقَالَ كُلْهُمَا جَمِيعاً .
citation.translation: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Al Nowfaly, from Al Sakuny, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> that Ali<sup>asws</sup> was asked about a fish with its belly being slit, so a fish was found inside it. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Eat both of them together’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: ضعيف على المشهور - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (21/361)

text: Al Husayn Bin Muhammad, from Moala Bin Muhammad, from Al Washa, from Abdullah Bin Sinan who said, ‘I heard Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> saying: ‘There is no problem with the fish which the Magians hunted (fished)’.

citation.arabic_text: سَمِعْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) يَقُولُ لَا بَأْسَ بِالسَّمَكِ الَّذِي يَصِيدُهُ الْمَجُوسِيُّ .
citation.translation: Al Husayn Bin Muhammad, from Moala Bin Muhammad, from Al Washa, from Abdullah Bin Sinan who said, ‘I heard Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> saying: ‘There is no problem with the fish which the Magians hunted (fished)’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: ضعيف على المشهور - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (21/361)

text: Abu Ali Al Ashari, from Al Hassan Bin Ali Al Kufy, from Al Abbas Bin Amir, from Aban, from one of our companions, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, said, ‘I said, ‘A man entrapped a fish, so he found a fish inside of it’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘he can eat both of them together’.

citation.arabic_text: قُلْتُ رَجُلٌ اصْطَادَ سَمَكَةً فَوَجَدَ فِي جَوْفِهَا سَمَكَةً فَقَالَ يُؤْكَلَانِ جَمِيعاً .
citation.translation: Abu Ali Al Ashari, from Al Hassan Bin Ali Al Kufy, from Al Abbas Bin Amir, from Aban, from one of our companions, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, said, ‘I said, ‘A man entrapped a fish, so he found a fish inside of it’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘he can eat both of them together’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: مرسل - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (21/361)

text: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from haroun Bin Muslim, from Mas’ada Bin Sadaqa, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, having said, ‘I heard my<sup>asws</sup> father<sup>asws</sup> saying: ‘When the owner of the netting strikes with the netting, so whatever is caught in it, from live ones or dead, so it is Permissible, apart from what does not have scales for it, and he cannot eat the floating from the fishes’.

citation.arabic_text: سَمِعْتُ أَبِي ( عليه السلام ) يَقُولُ إِذَا ضَرَبَ صَاحِبُ الشَّبَكَةِ بِالشَّبَكَةِ فَمَا أَصَابَ فِيهَا مِنْ حَيٍّ أَوْ مَيِّتٍ فَهُوَ حَلَالٌ مَا خَلَا مَا لَيْسَ لَهُ قِشْرٌ وَ لَا يُؤْكَلُ الطَّافِي مِنَ السَّمَكِ .
citation.translation: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from haroun Bin Muslim, from Mas’ada Bin Sadaqa, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, having said, ‘I heard my<sup>asws</sup> father<sup>asws</sup> saying: ‘When the owner of the netting strikes with the netting, so whatever is caught in it, from live ones or dead, so it is Permissible, apart from what does not have scales for it, and he cannot eat the floating from the fishes’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: ضعيف - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (21/361)

text: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Muhammad Bin Ahmad, from Yaqoub Bin Yazeed, from Ahmad Bin Al Mubarak, from Salih Bin Ayn, from Al Washa, from Ayoub Bin Ayn, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, said, ‘I said to him<sup>asws</sup>, ‘May I be sacrificed for you<sup>asws</sup>! What are you<sup>asws</sup> saying regarding a snake which swallows a fish, then it regurgitates it, and it is alive, restless. Can I eat it?’ So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘If its scales had peeled off, so do not eat it, and if they had not peeled off, so eat it’.

citation.arabic_text: قُلْتُ لَهُ جُعِلْتُ فِدَاكَ مَا تَقُولُ فِي حَيَّةٍ ابْتَلَعَتْ سَمَكَةً ثُمَّ طَرَحَتْهَا وَ هِيَ حَيَّةٌ تَضْطَرِبُ أَ فَآكُلُهَا فَقَالَ ( عليه السلام ) إِنْ كَانَتْ فُلُوسُهَا قَدْ تَسَلَّخَتْ فَلَا تَأْكُلْهَا وَ إِنْ كَانَتْ لَمْ تَتَسَلَّخْ فَكُلْهَا .
citation.translation: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Muhammad Bin Ahmad, from Yaqoub Bin Yazeed, from Ahmad Bin Al Mubarak, from Salih Bin Ayn, from Al Washa, from Ayoub Bin Ayn, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, said, ‘I said to him<sup>asws</sup>, ‘May I be sacrificed for you<sup>asws</sup>! What are you<sup>asws</sup> saying regarding a snake which swallows a fish, then it regurgitates it, and it is alive, restless. Can I eat it?’ So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘If its scales had peeled off, so do not eat it, and if they had not peeled off, so eat it’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: مجهول - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (21/361)

text: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Muhammad Bin Musa, from Al Abbas Bin Marouf, from Marwak Bin Ubeyd, from Sama’at Bin Mahran who said, ‘Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> forbade the man from hunting on the day of Friday before the Prayer, and he<sup>asws</sup> had passed by the fishmongers on the day of Friday, so he<sup>asws</sup> forbade them from hunting for the fishes on the day of Friday before the Prayers’.

citation.arabic_text: قَالَ أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) نَهَى أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ ( عليه السلام ) أَنْ يَتَصَيَّدَ الرَّجُلُ يَوْمَ الْجُمُعَةِ قَبْلَ الصَّلَاةِ وَ كَانَ ( عليه السلام ) يَمُرُّ بِالسَّمَّاكِينَ يَوْمَ الْجُمُعَةِ فَيَنْهَاهُمْ عَنْ أَنْ يَتَصَيَّدُوا مِنَ السَّمَكِ يَوْمَ الْجُمُعَةِ قَبْلَ الصَّلَاةِ .
citation.translation: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Muhammad Bin Musa, from Al Abbas Bin Marouf, from Marwak Bin Ubeyd, from Sama’at Bin Mahran who said, ‘Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> forbade the man from hunting on the day of Friday before the Prayer, and he<sup>asws</sup> had passed by the fishmongers on the day of Friday, so he<sup>asws</sup> forbade them from hunting for the fishes on the day of Friday before the Prayers’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: مجهول - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (21/362)

text: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Abdullah Bin Al Mugheira, from the one who mentioned it, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, and the floating fish were mentioned and the people dislike from it. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘But rather, the floating from the fish are abhorred and it is what its smell has changed’.

citation.arabic_text: إِنَّمَا الطَّافِي مِنَ السَّمَكِ الْمَكْرُوهُ وَ هُوَ مَا يَتَغَيَّرُ رَائِحَتُهُ .

So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘But rather, the floating from the fish are abhorred and it is what its smell has changed’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: مرسل - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (1/362)

text: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, and Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, altogether from Ibn Mahboub, and Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Abu Nasr, altogether from Al A’ala, from Muhammad Bin Muslim who said, ‘Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> made me read something from the Book of Ali<sup>asws</sup>, so there was in it – you have been forbidden from the catfish, and the glyptothorax (mountain catfish), and the sea horse, and the floating fish (dead), and the spleen. I said, ‘O son<sup>asws</sup> of Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup>! They come to us with fish with no scales on it’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Eat from the fish what has scales for it, and what does not have scales for it, so do not eat it’.

citation.arabic_text: أَقْرَأَنِي أَبُو جَعْفَرٍ ( عليه السلام ) شَيْئاً مِنْ كِتَابِ عَلِيٍّ ( عليه السلام ) فَإِذَا فِيهِ أَنْهَاكُمْ عَنِ الْجِرِّيِّ وَ الزِّمِّيرِ وَ الْمَارْمَاهِي وَ الطَّافِي وَ الطِّحَالِ قَالَ قُلْتُ يَا ابْنَ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ يَرْحَمُكَ اللَّهُ إِنَّا نُؤْتَى بِالسَّمَكِ لَيْسَ لَهُ قِشْرٌ فَقَالَ كُلْ مَا لَهُ قِشْرٌ مِنَ السَّمَكِ وَ مَا لَيْسَ لَهُ قِشْرٌ فَلَا تَأْكُلْهُ .
citation.translation: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, and Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, altogether from Ibn Mahboub, and Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Abu Nasr, altogether from Al A’ala, from Muhammad Bin Muslim who said, ‘Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> made me read something from the Book of Ali<sup>asws</sup>, so there was in it – you have been forbidden from the catfish, and the glyptothorax (mountain catfish), and the sea horse, and the floating fish (dead), and the spleen. citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: صحيح - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (21/363)

text: Al Husayn Bin Muhammad, from Moala Bin Muhammad, from Al Hassan Bin Ali, fro Hammad Bin Usman who said, ‘I said to Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, ‘May I be sacrificed for you! The fishes, what can we eat from these?’ So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Whatever had scales for it’. I said, ‘May I be sacrificed for you<sup>asws</sup>! What are you<sup>asws</sup> saying regarding the Sea bass. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘There is no problem with eating it’. I said to him<sup>asws</sup>, ‘But it does not have scales for it’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said to me: ‘Yes, but it is a fish of evil creation. It goes beneath everything, and when you look in the roots of its ears, you will find scales on it’.

citation.arabic_text: قُلْتُ لِأَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) جُعِلْتُ فِدَاكَ الْحِيتَانُ مَا يُؤْكَلُ مِنْهَا فَقَالَ مَا كَانَ لَهُ قِشْرٌ قُلْتُ جُعِلْتُ فِدَاكَ مَا تَقُولُ فِي الْكَنْعَتِ فَقَالَ لَا بَأْسَ بِأَكْلِهِ قَالَ قُلْتُ لَهُ فَإِنَّهُ لَيْسَ لَهُ قِشْرٌ فَقَالَ لِي بَلَى وَ لَكِنَّهَا سَمَكَةٌ سَيِّئَةُ الْخُلُقِ تَحْتَكُّ بِكُلِّ شَيْ‏ءٍ وَ إِذَا نَظَرْتَ فِي أَصْلِ أُذُنِهَا وَجَدْتَ لَهَا قِشْراً .

text: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad, from Hareyz, from the one who mentioned it, (It has been narrated) from both of them<sup>asws</sup> (5<sup>th</sup> or 6<sup>th</sup> Imam<sup>asws</sup>) that Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> disliked the eel and said: ‘Do not eat from the fish except there is something upon it of the scales’, and he<sup>asws</sup> disliked the sea horse’.

citation.arabic_text: لَا تَأْكُلُوا مِنَ السَّمَكِ إِلَّا شَيْئاً عَلَيْهِ فُلُوسٌ وَ كَرِهَ الْمَارْمَاهِيَ .

text: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Usman Bin Isa, from Sama’at, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Do not eat the eels, nor the sea horse, nor the floating one, nor the spleen, because it is a house of the blood, and a morsel of Satan<sup>la</sup>’.

citation.arabic_text: لَا تَأْكُلِ الْجِرِّيثَ وَ لَا الْمَارْمَاهِيَ وَ لَا طَافِياً وَ لَا طِحَالًا لِأَنَّهُ بَيْتُ الدَّمِ وَ مُضْغَةُ الشَّيْطَانِ .
citation.translation: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Usman Bin Isa, from Sama’at, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Do not eat the eels, nor the sea horse, nor the floating one, nor the spleen, because it is a house of the blood, and a morsel of Satan<sup>la</sup>’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: موثق - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (21/364)

text: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hisham Bin Salim, from Umar Bin Hanzala who said, ‘Dried Sea bass (Rabeetha) were brought over to me in a basket. So I went over to Abu Abdullahasws, so I asked himasws about it. So heasws said: ‘Eat it, for there are scales on it’.

citation.arabic_text: حُمِلَتْ إِلَيَّ رَبِيثَا يَابِسَةٌ فِي صُرَّةٍ فَدَخَلْتُ عَلَى أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) فَسَأَلْتُهُ عَنْهَا فَقَالَ كُلْهَا فَلَهَا قِشْرٌ .

text: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Abdullah Bin Al Mugheira, from Abdullah Bin Sinan, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Amir Al-Momineen Ali<sup>asws</sup> Bin Abu Talib<sup>asws</sup> was at Al-Kufa, riding a mule of Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup>. Then he<sup>asws</sup> passed by a fish market, so he<sup>asws</sup> was saying: ‘Neither eat, nor pursue the fish which do not have scales on it’.

citation.arabic_text: كَانَ أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ عَلِيُّ بْنُ أَبِي طَالِبٍ ( عليه السلام ) بِالْكُوفَةِ يَرْكَبُ بَغْلَةَ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ ( صلى الله عليه وآله ) ثُمَّ يَمُرُّ بِسُوقِ الْحِيتَانِ فَيَقُولُ لَا تَأْكُلُوا وَ لَا تَبِيعُوا مِنَ السَّمَكِ مَا لَمْ يَكُنْ لَهُ قِشْرٌ .
