Then he<sup>asws</sup> passed by a fish market, so he<sup>asws</sup> was saying: ‘Neither eat, nor pursue the fish which do not have scales on it’.

text: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Hannan Bin Sudeyr who said, ‘Al-Aa’la Bin Kamil asked Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> and I was present, about the catfish. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘We<sup>asws</sup> found in the Book of Ali<sup>asws</sup>, Forbidden things from the fish, therefore do not go near these’. Then Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘What does not happen to have scales for it, from the fishes, so do not go near it’.

citation.arabic_text: سَأَلَ الْعَلَاءُ بْنُ كَامِلٍ أَبَا عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) وَ أَنَا حَاضِرٌ عَنِ الْجِرِّيِّ فَقَالَ وَجَدْنَا فِي كِتَابِ عَلِيٍّ ( عليه السلام ) أَشْيَاءَ مُحَرَّمَةً مِنَ السَّمَكِ فَلَا تَقْرَبْهَا ثُمَّ قَالَ أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) مَا لَمْ يَكُنْ لَهُ قِشْرٌ مِنَ السَّمَكِ فَلَا تَقْرَبَنَّهُ .
citation.translation: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Hannan Bin Sudeyr who said, ‘Al-Aa’la Bin Kamil asked Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> and I was present, about the catfish. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘We<sup>asws</sup> found in the Book of Ali<sup>asws</sup>, Forbidden things from the fish, therefore do not go near these’. Then Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘What does not happen to have scales for it, from the fishes, so do not go near it’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: حسن أو موثق - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (21/365)

text: Hanan Bin Sudeyr said, ‘Al-Fayz Bin Mukhtar gifted sea bass to Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, and went over to him<sup>asws</sup>, and I was in his<sup>asws</sup> presence. So he<sup>asws</sup> looked at it and said: ‘This has scales on it, therefore eat from it’, and we saw him<sup>asws</sup> (eating it)’.

citation.arabic_text: أَهْدَى الْفَيْضُ بْنُ الْمُخْتَارِ لِأَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) رَبِيثَا فَأَدْخَلَهَا إِلَيْهِ وَ أَنَا عِنْدَهُ فَنَظَرَ إِلَيْهَا وَ قَالَ هَذِهِ لَهَا قِشْرٌ فَأَكَلَ مِنْهُ وَ نَحْنُ نَرَاهُ .
citation.translation: Hanan Bin Sudeyr said, ‘Al-Fayz Bin Mukhtar gifted sea bass to Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, and went over to him<sup>asws</sup>, and I was in his<sup>asws</sup> presence. text: Abu Ali Al Ashary, from Al Hassan Bin Ali, from his uncle Muhammad, from Suleyman Bin Ja’far, from Is’haq, owner of the fish, who said, ‘We went out with fish to meet Abu Al-Hassan Al-Reza<sup>asws</sup> with it, and we had exited from Al-Medina, and he<sup>asws</sup> had proceeded from a journey of his<sup>asws</sup>. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Woe be unto you, O so and so! Perhaps there are fishes with you?’ So I said, ‘Yes, O my master<sup>asws</sup>, may I be sacrificed for you<sup>asws</sup>!’ So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Descend you all!’ Then he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Woe be unto you, perhaps it is Siganus?’ I said, ‘Yes’. So I showed it to him<sup>asws</sup>. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Ride! There is no need for us<sup>asws</sup> with regards to it, and the Siganus is a fish which has no scales on it’.

citation.arabic_text: حَدَّثَنِي إِسْحَاقُ صَاحِبُ الْحِيتَانِ قَالَ خَرَجْنَا بِسَمَكٍ نَتَلَقَّى بِهِ أَبَا الْحَسَنِ الرِّضَا ( عليه السلام ) وَ قَدْ خَرَجْنَا مِنَ الْمَدِينَةِ وَ قَدْ قَدِمَ هُوَ مِنْ سَفَرٍ لَهُ فَقَالَ وَيْحَكَ يَا فُلَانُ لَعَلَّ مَعَكَ سَمَكاً فَقُلْتُ نَعَمْ يَا سَيِّدِي جُعِلْتُ فِدَاكَ فَقَالَ انْزِلُوا ثُمَّ قَالَ وَيْحَكَ لَعَلَّهُ زَهْوٌ قَالَ قُلْتُ نَعَمْ فَأَرَيْتُهُ فَقَالَ ارْكَبُوا لَا حَاجَةَ لَنَا فِيهِ وَ الزَّهْوُ سَمَكٌ لَيْسَ لَهُ قِشْرٌ .

text: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Al Amraky Bin Ali, (It has been narrated) from Ali son of Ja’far<sup>asws</sup>, from his brother<sup>asws</sup> Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘It is not Permissible to eat the catfish, nor the tortoise, nor the crab’. And I asked him<sup>asws</sup> about the flesh which happens to be in the sea shells of the sea, and the Euphrates, can one eat?’ So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘That is a flesh of the frogs, it is not Permissible to eat it’.

citation.arabic_text: لَا يَحِلُّ أَكْلُ الْجِرِّيِّ وَ لَا السُّلَحْفَاةِ وَ لَا السَّرَطَانِ قَالَ وَ سَأَلْتُهُ عَنِ اللَّحْمِ الَّذِي يَكُونُ فِي أَصْدَافِ الْبَحْرِ وَ الْفُرَاتِ أَ يُؤْكَلُ فَقَالَ ذَاكَ لَحْمُ الضَّفَادِعِ لَا يَحِلُّ أَكْلُهُ .
citation.translation: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Al Amraky Bin Ali, (It has been narrated) from Ali son of Ja’far<sup>asws</sup>, from his brother<sup>asws</sup> Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘It is not Permissible to eat the catfish, nor the tortoise, nor the crab’. citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: صحيح - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (21/365)

text: Al Husayn Bin Muhammad, from Moala Bin Muhammad, from Muhammad Bin Ali Al Hamdany, from Sama’at Bin Mihran, from Al Kalby Al Nasaba who said, ‘I asked Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> about the catfish, so he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic Metamorphosed a group from the Children of Israel, so whatever of them which the ocean seized, so it is the catfish, and the glyptothorax (mountain catfish), and the sea horse, and what is besides that; and what the land seized from them, so it is the monkeys, and the pigs, and the (short-haired) rabbit, and the lizard, and what is besides that’.

citation.arabic_text: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) عَنِ الْجِرِّيِّ فَقَالَ إِنَّ اللَّهَ عَزَّ وَ جَلَّ مَسَخَ طَائِفَةً مِنْ بَنِي إِسْرَائِيلَ فَمَا أَخَذَ مِنْهُمُ الْبَحْرَ فَهُوَ الْجِرِّيُّ وَ الزِّمِّيرُ وَ الْمَارْمَاهِي وَ مَا سِوَى ذَلِكَ وَ مَا أَخَذَ مِنْهُمُ الْبَرَّ فَالْقِرَدَةُ وَ الْخَنَازِيرُ وَ الْوَبْرُ وَ الْوَرَلُ وَ مَا سِوَى ذَلِكَ .
citation.translation: Al Husayn Bin Muhammad, from Moala Bin Muhammad, from Muhammad Bin Ali Al Hamdany, from Sama’at Bin Mihran, from Al Kalby Al Nasaba who said, ‘I asked Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> about the catfish, so he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic Metamorphosed a group from the Children of Israel, so whatever of them which the ocean seized, so it is the catfish, and the glyptothorax (mountain catfish), and the sea horse, and what is besides that; and what the land seized from them, so it is the monkeys, and the pigs, and the (short-haired) rabbit, and the lizard, and what is besides that’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: ضعيف على المشهور - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (21/366)

text: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Salih Bin Al Sandy, from Yunus who said, ‘I wrote to Al-Reza<sup>asws</sup>, ‘The fish which does not happen to have scales on it, can I eat?’ So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘From the fishes which happens to have evilness for it, so it attaches with everything, so its scales go away, but when its sides are different, meaning its tail and its head, so eat it’.

citation.arabic_text: كَتَبْتُ إِلَى الرِّضَا ( عليه السلام ) السَّمَكُ لَا يَكُونُ لَهُ قِشْرٌ أَ يُؤْكَلُ فَقَالَ إِنَّ مِنَ السَّمَكِ مَا يَكُونُ لَهُ زَعَارَّةٌ فَيَحْتَكُّ بِكُلِّ شَيْ‏ءٍ فَتَذْهَبُ قُشُورُهُ وَ لَكِنْ إِذَا اخْتَلَفَ طَرَفَاهُ يَعْنِي ذَنَبَهُ وَ رَأْسَهُ فَكُلْهُ .
citation.translation: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Salih Bin Al Sandy, from Yunus who said, ‘I wrote to Al-Reza<sup>asws</sup>, ‘The fish which does not happen to have scales on it, can I eat?’ So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘From the fishes which happens to have evilness for it, so it attaches with everything, so its scales go away, but when its sides are different, meaning its tail and its head, so eat it’.

text: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Haroun Bin Muslim, from Mas’ada Bin Sadaqa who said, ‘Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> was asked about eating the locusts. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘There is no problem with eating it’. Then he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘They are emanating from the fishes of the sea (crayfish/lobsters)’. Then he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Ali<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The fish and the locusts, when they come out from the water, so it is pure, and the land is a trap for the locusts, and for the fishes it happens to be (a trap) as well’.

citation.arabic_text: سُئِلَ أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) عَنْ أَكْلِ الْجَرَادِ فَقَالَ لَا بَأْسَ بِأَكْلِهِ ثُمَّ قَالَ ( عليه السلام ) إِنَّهُ نَثْرَةٌ مِنْ حُوتٍ فِي الْبَحْرِ ثُمَّ قَالَ إِنَّ عَلِيّاً ( عليه السلام ) قَالَ إِنَّ السَّمَكَ وَ الْجَرَادَ إِذَا خَرَجَ مِنَ الْمَاءِ فَهُوَ ذَكِيٌّ وَ الْأَرْضُ لِلْجَرَادِ مَصِيدَةٌ وَ لِلسَّمَكِ قَدْ يَكُونُ أَيْضاً .

So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘There is no problem with eating it’. Then he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘They are emanating from the fishes of the sea (crayfish/lobsters)’. text: A number of our companons, from Ahmad Bin Abu Abdullah, from his father, from Awn Bin Jareer, from Amro Bin Haroun Al Saqafy, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘The locust is pure, so eat it, but as for what perishes in the sea, so do not eat it’.

citation.arabic_text: قَالَ أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ ( عليه السلام ) الْجَرَادُ ذَكِيٌّ فَكُلْهُ فَأَمَّا مَا هَلَكَ فِي الْبَحْرِ فَلَا تَأْكُلْهُ .
citation.translation: A number of our companons, from Ahmad Bin Abu Abdullah, from his father, from Awn Bin Jareer, from Amro Bin Haroun Al Saqafy, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘The locust is pure, so eat it, but as for what perishes in the sea, so do not eat it’.

text: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Al Amraky Bin Ali, (It has been narrated) from Ali son of Ja’farasws, from his brotherasws Abu Al-Hassanasws, said, ‘I asked himasws about the locust which are found dead in the desert, or in the water, can one eat?’ So heasws said: ‘Do not eat it’. He (the narrator) said, ‘And I asked himasws about Al-Dabba from the locusts, can one eat?’ Heasws said: ‘No, until it is flying around with the birds’.

citation.arabic_text: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنِ الْجَرَادِ نُصِيبُهُ مَيِّتاً فِي الصَّحْرَاءِ أَوْ فِي الْمَاءِ أَ يُؤْكَلُ فَقَالَ لَا تَأْكُلْهُ قَالَ وَ سَأَلْتُهُ ( عليه السلام ) عَنِ الدَّبَا مِنَ الْجَرَادِ أَ يُؤْكَلُ قَالَ لَا حَتَّى يَسْتَقِلَّ بِالطَّيَرَانِ .
citation.translation: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Al Amraky Bin Ali, (It has been narrated) from Ali son of Ja’farasws, from his brotherasws Abu Al-Hassanasws, said, ‘I asked himasws about the locust which are found dead in the desert, or in the water, can one eat?’ So heasws said: ‘Do not eat it’. He (the narrator) said, ‘And I asked himasws about Al-Dabba from the locusts, can one eat?’ Heasws said: ‘No, until it is flying around with the birds’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: صحيح - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (1/367)

text: A number of our companons, from Ahmad Bin Abu Abdullah, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Abu Nasr who said, ‘I asked Abu Al-Hassan Al-Reza<sup>asws</sup> about a man who hunts the birds which are worth a lot of Dirhams, and its two wings are level, and its owner is known, or he comes over, so he seeks it, one who does not accuse him (of stealing it). He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘It is not Permissible for him to keep it. He should return it to him’. So I said to him<sup>asws</sup>, ‘So if he hunts what has no control over its two wings, its seeker not known?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘It is for him’.

citation.arabic_text: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا الْحَسَنِ الرِّضَا ( عليه السلام ) عَنْ رَجُلٍ يَصِيدُ الطَّيْرَ يُسَاوِي دَرَاهِمَ كَثِيرَةً وَ هُوَ مُسْتَوِي الْجَنَاحَيْنِ وَ يَعْرِفُ صَاحِبَهُ أَوْ يَجِيئُهُ فَيَطْلُبُهُ مَنْ لَا يَتَّهِمُهُ قَالَ لَا يَحِلُّ لَهُ إِمْسَاكُهُ يَرُدُّهُ عَلَيْهِ فَقُلْتُ لَهُ فَإِنْ هُوَ صَادَ مَا هُوَ مَالِكٌ بِجَنَاحَيْهِ لَا يَعْرِفُ لَهُ طَالِباً قَالَ هُوَ لَهُ .
citation.translation: A number of our companons, from Ahmad Bin Abu Abdullah, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Abu Nasr who said, ‘I asked Abu Al-Hassan Al-Reza<sup>asws</sup> about a man who hunts the birds which are worth a lot of Dirhams, and its two wings are level, and its owner is known, or he comes over, so he seeks it, one who does not accuse him (of stealing it). He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘It is not Permissible for him to keep it. He should return it to him’. So I said to him<sup>asws</sup>, ‘So if he hunts what has no control over its two wings, its seeker not known?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘It is for him’.

text: From him, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ibn Bukeyr, from the one who reported it, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘When the birds owns its wings, so it is for the one who seizes it’.

citation.arabic_text: إِذَا مَلَكَ الطَّائِرُ جَنَاحَهُ فَهُوَ لِمَنْ أَخَذَهُ .
citation.translation: From him, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ibn Bukeyr, from the one who reported it, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘When the birds owns its wings, so it is for the one who seizes it’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: مرسل - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (21/368)

text: From him, from Ibn Fazzal, from Muhammad Bin Al Fuzayl who said, ‘I asked Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> about a hunt of the dove equating to half a Dirham, or one Dirham. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘When its owner it known, so it would be returned to him, and if its owner is not known, and its wings were levelled, flying with these two, so it is for him’.

citation.arabic_text: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا الْحَسَنِ ( عليه السلام ) عَنْ صَيْدِ الْحَمَامَةِ تُسَاوِي نِصْفَ دِرْهَمٍ أَوْ دِرْهَماً فَقَالَ إِذَا عَرَفْتَ صَاحِبَهُ فَرُدَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَ إِنْ لَمْ تَعْرِفْ صَاحِبَهُ وَ كَانَ مُسْتَوِيَ الْجَنَاحَيْنِ يَطِيرُ بِهِمَا فَهُوَ لَكَ .
citation.translation: From him, from Ibn Fazzal, from Muhammad Bin Al Fuzayl who said, ‘I asked Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> about a hunt of the dove equating to half a Dirham, or one Dirham. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘When its owner it known, so it would be returned to him, and if its owner is not known, and its wings were levelled, flying with these two, so it is for him’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: مجهول - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (1/368)

text: And from him, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ubeyd Bin Hafs Bin Qurat, from Ismail Bin Jabir, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, said, ‘I said to him<sup>asws</sup>, ‘May I be sacrificed for you<sup>asws</sup>! The bird falls upon the house, so it is seized. Is it Permissible or Prohibited, for the one who seizes it?’ So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘O Ismail! Is it complete or not complete (its wings)?’ I said, ‘May I be sacrificed for you<sup>asws</sup>! And what is complete?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The one who wings are level, in control of its wings going with them wherever it so desires to’. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘It is for the one who seizes it’.

citation.arabic_text: قُلْتُ لَهُ جُعِلْتُ فِدَاكَ الطَّيْرُ يَقَعُ عَلَى الدَّارِ فَيُؤْخَذُ أَ حَلَالٌ هُوَ أَمْ حَرَامٌ لِمَنْ أَخَذَهُ فَقَالَ يَا إِسْمَاعِيلُ عَافٍ أَمْ غَيْرُ عَافٍ قَالَ قُلْتُ جُعِلْتُ فِدَاكَ وَ مَا الْعَافِي قَالَ الْمُسْتَوِي جَنَاحَاهُ الْمَالِكُ جَنَاحَيْهِ يَذْهَبُ حَيْثُ شَاءَ قَالَ هُوَ لِمَنْ أَخَذَهُ حَلَالٌ .
citation.translation: And from him, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ubeyd Bin Hafs Bin Qurat, from Ismail Bin Jabir, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, said, ‘I said to him<sup>asws</sup>, ‘May I be sacrificed for you<sup>asws</sup>! The bird falls upon the house, so it is seized. Is it Permissible or Prohibited, for the one who seizes it?’ So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘O Ismail! And what is complete?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The one who wings are level, in control of its wings going with them wherever it so desires to’. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘It is for the one who seizes it’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: مجهول - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (21/368)

text: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Al Nowfaly, from Al Sakuny, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The bird, when it is in control of its wings, so it is a hunted prey, and it is Permissible for the one who seizes it’.

citation.arabic_text: قَالَ أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ ( عليه السلام ) إِنَّ الطَّيْرَ إِذَا مَلَكَ جَنَاحَيْهِ فَهُوَ صَيْدٌ وَ هُوَ حَلَالٌ لِمَنْ أَخَذَهُ .
citation.translation: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Al Nowfaly, from Al Sakuny, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The bird, when it is in control of its wings, so it is a hunted prey, and it is Permissible for the one who seizes it’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: ضعيف على المشهور - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (1/369)

text: And by his chain that, ‘Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> said regarding a man who saw a bird, so he pursued it until it fell upon a tree. So another man came over, so he seized it. So Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘It is for the eye what it sees, and for the hand what it seizes’.

citation.arabic_text: وَ بِإِسْنَادِهِ أَنَّ أَمِيرَ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ ( عليه السلام ) قَالَ فِي رَجُلٍ أَبْصَرَ طَائِراً فَتَبِعَهُ حَتَّى سَقَطَ عَلَى شَجَرَةٍ فَجَاءَ رَجُلٌ آخَرُ فَأَخَذَهُ فَقَالَ أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ ( عليه السلام ) لِلْعَيْنِ مَا رَأَتْ وَ لِلْيَدِ مَا أَخَذَتْ .
citation.translation: And by his chain that, ‘Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> said regarding a man who saw a bird, so he pursued it until it fell upon a tree. So another man came over, so he seized it. So Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘It is for the eye what it sees, and for the hand what it seizes’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: ضعيف على المشهور - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (1/369)

text: Ali Bin Muhammad Bin Bundar, from Ibrahim Bin Is’haq, from Ali Bin Muhammad, raising it to Dawood Al Raqqy, or someone else who said, ‘While we were seated in the presence of Abu Abdullahasws, when a man passed by in whose hand was a slaughtered swallow. So Abu Abdullahasws leapt over to him until heasws seized it from his hand, then levelled the ground with it, so heasws said: ‘Has your scholar or your jurist ordered you with this? Myasws fatherasws informed measws that myasws grandfathersaww Rasool-Allahsaww forbade from killing the six, from these was the swallow’. And heasws said: ‘It encircling in the sky is (its expression of) regret at what was done with the Peopleasws of the Household of Muhammadsaww, and its Glorification is its recitation of ‘The Praise is for Allahazwj the Lordazwj of the Worlds’. Are you not seeing it saying (chirping) ‘Wa la Zalleeen (and not those who go astray)’?’

citation.arabic_text: بَيْنَا نَحْنُ قُعُودٌ عِنْدَ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) إِذْ مَرَّ رَجُلٌ بِيَدِهِ خُطَّافٌ مَذْبُوحٌ فَوَثَبَ إِلَيْهِ أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) حَتَّى أَخَذَهُ مِنْ يَدِهِ ثُمَّ دَحَا بِهِ الْأَرْضَ فَقَالَ ( عليه السلام ) أَ عَالِمُكُمْ أَمَرَكُمْ بِهَذَا أَمْ فَقِيهُكُمْ أَخْبَرَنِي أَبِي عَنْ جَدِّي أَنَّ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ ( صلى الله عليه وآله ) نَهَى عَنْ قَتْلِ السِّتَّةِ مِنْهَا الْخُطَّافُ وَ قَالَ إِنَّ دَوَرَانَهُ فِي السَّمَاءِ أَسَفاً لِمَا فُعِلَ بِأَهْلِ بَيْتِ مُحَمَّدٍ ( صلى الله عليه وآله ) وَ تَسْبِيحَهُ قِرَاءَةُ الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ رَبِّ الْعالَمِينَ أَ لَا تَرَوْنَهُ يَقُولُ وَ لَا الضَّالِّينَ .

Are you not seeing it saying (chirping) ‘Wa la Zalleeen (and not those who go astray)’?’

text: A number of our companions, from sahl Bin Ziyad, and Ahmad Bin Abu Abdullah, altogether from Al Jamourany, from Al Hassan Bin Ali Bin Abu Hamza, from Muhammad Bin Yusuf Al Tameemy, (It has been narrated) from Muhammad son of Ja’farasws, from his fatherasws who said, ‘Rasool-Allahsaww said: ‘Treat the wagtails with goodness, meaning the swallows, for these are the friendliest of the birds of the people with the people’. Then hesaww said: ‘And are you knowing what the wagtail (swallow) is saying when it passes by and sings? She is saying, ‘In the Name of Allahazwj the Beneficent, the Merciful. The Praise is for Allahazwj Lordazwj of the Worlds’ – until hesaww recited the ‘Mother of the Book’ (Surah Al-Fatiha, Chapter 1). So when it comes the end of its singing, so she says, ‘Wa La Zalleeen’ (last Words of Surah al-Fatiha). Rasool-Allahsaww extended hissaww voice with it, ‘Wa La Zalleen’.

citation.arabic_text: قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ ( صلى الله عليه وآله ) اسْتَوْصُوا بِالصِّنِينَاتِ خَيْراً يَعْنِي الْخُطَّافَ فَإِنَّهُنَّ آنَسُ طَيْرِ النَّاسِ بِالنَّاسِ ثُمَّ قَالَ وَ تَدْرُونَ مَا تَقُولُ الصِّنِينَةُ إِذَا مَرَّتْ وَ تَرَنَّمَتْ تَقُولُ بِسْمِ اللَّهِ الرَّحْمنِ الرَّحِيمِ الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ رَبِّ الْعالَمِينَ حَتَّى قَرَأَ أُمَّ الْكِتَابِ فَإِذَا كَانَ آخِرُ تَرَنُّمِهَا قَالَتْ وَ لَا الضَّالِّينَ مَدَّ بِهَا رَسُولُ اللَّهِ ( صلى الله عليه وآله ) صَوْتَهُ وَ لَا الضَّالِّينَ .
citation.translation: A number of our companions, from sahl Bin Ziyad, and Ahmad Bin Abu Abdullah, altogether from Al Jamourany, from Al Hassan Bin Ali Bin Abu Hamza, from Muhammad Bin Yusuf Al Tameemy, (It has been narrated) from Muhammad son of Ja’farasws, from his fatherasws who said, ‘Rasool-Allahsaww said: ‘Treat the wagtails with goodness, meaning the swallows, for these are the friendliest of the birds of the people with the people’. Then hesaww said: ‘And are you knowing what the wagtail (swallow) is saying when it passes by and sings? She is saying, ‘In the Name of Allahazwj the Beneficent, the Merciful. The Praise is for Allahazwj Lordazwj of the Worlds’ – until hesaww recited the ‘Mother of the Book’ (Surah Al-Fatiha, Chapter 1). So when it comes the end of its singing, so she says, ‘Wa La Zalleeen’ (last Words of Surah al-Fatiha). Rasool-Allahsaww extended hissaww voice with it, ‘Wa La Zalleen’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: ضعيف - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (1/370)

text: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Jameel Bin Darraj who said, ‘I asked Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> about killing the swallows, or hurting them in the Sanctuary. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Do not kill them, for I<sup>asws</sup> was in the presence of Ali<sup>asws</sup> Bin Al-Husayn<sup>asws</sup>, so he<sup>asws</sup> saw me<sup>asws</sup> troubling them. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘O my<sup>asws</sup> son<sup>asws</sup>! Do not kill them and do not harm them, for they are not harming anything’.

text: A number of our companoins, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Abu Abdullah Al Barqy, from Ali Bin Muhammad Bn Suleyman, from Abu Ayoub Al Madayni, from Suleyman Bin Ja’far Al Humeyri, (It has been narrated) from Abu Al-Hassan Al-Reza<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘In each wing of the Hoopoe is inscribed in ‘Assyrian’ (an ancient language), ‘The Progeny<sup>asws</sup> of Muhammad<sup>asws</sup> are the best of Created beings’.

citation.arabic_text: فِي كُلِّ جَنَاحِ هُدْهُدٍ مَكْتُوبٌ بِالسُّرْيَانِيَّةِ آلُ مُحَمَّدٍ خَيْرُ الْبَرِيَّةِ .

text: And from him, from Yaqoub Bin Yazeed, (It has been narrated) from Ali son of Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> who said, ‘I asked my brother<sup>asws</sup> Musa<sup>asws</sup> about the Hoopoe, and killing it and slaughtering it. text: And from him, from Ali Bin Muhammad, from Abu Ayoub Al Madiny, from Suleyman Al Ja’fary, (It has been narrated) from Abu Al-Hassan Al-Reza<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> forbade from killing the Hoopoe, and the Shrike, and the Skua Gull, and the honey bees’.

citation.arabic_text: نَهَى رَسُولُ اللَّهِ ( صلى الله عليه وآله ) عَنْ قَتْلِ الْهُدْهُدِ وَ الصُّرَدِ وَ الصُّوَّامِ وَ النَّحْلَةِ .

text: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Abu Abdullah, from Ali Bin Muhammad Bin Suleyman, from Abu Ayoub Al Madainy, from Suleyman Al Ja’fary, (It has been narrated) from Abu Al-Hassan Al-Reza<sup>asws</sup>, from his<sup>asws</sup> father<sup>asws</sup>, from his<sup>asws</sup> grandfather<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Do not eat the grouse, nor insult it, nor give it to the children to play with it, for it frequents the Glorification of Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, and its Glorification is, ‘May Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Curse those who hate the Progeny<sup>asws</sup> of Muhammad<sup>saww</sup>’.

citation.arabic_text: لَا تَأْكُلُوا الْقُنْبُرَةَ وَ لَا تَسُبُّوهَا وَ لَا تُعْطُوهَا الصِّبْيَانَ يَلْعَبُونَ بِهَا فَإِنَّهَا كَثِيرَةُ التَّسْبِيحِ لِلَّهِ تَعَالَى وَ تَسْبِيحُهَا لَعَنَ اللَّهُ مُبْغِضِي آلِ مُحَمَّدٍ ( عليهم السلام ) .

text: And by his chain, said, ‘Ali<sup>asws</sup> Bin Al-Husayn<sup>asws</sup> was saying: ‘I do not farm the plantation in order to seek the Grace in it, and I<sup>asws</sup> do not farm except for the beggar to take from it, and the one with the need, and what the grouse takes from it, particularly from the birds’.

citation.arabic_text: كَانَ عَلِيُّ بْنُ الْحُسَيْنِ ( عليه السلام ) يَقُولُ مَا أَزْرَعُ الزَّرْعَ لِطَلَبِ الْفَضْلِ فِيهِ وَ مَا أَزْرَعُهُ إِلَّا لِيَنَالَهُ الْمُعْتَرُّ وَ ذُو الْحَاجَةِ وَ تَنَالَهُ الْقُنْبُرَةُ مِنْهُ خَاصَّةً مِنَ الطَّيْرِ .

text: Muhammad Bin Al Hassan, and Ali Bin Ibrahim Al Hashimy, from one of our companions, from Suleyman Bin Ja’far Al Ja’fary, (It has been narrated) from Abu Al-Hassan Al-Reza<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Ali<sup>asws</sup> Bin Al-Husayn<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The topknot on top of the heat of the grouse is from the wiping (by the hand of) Suleyman<sup>as</sup> Bin Dawood<sup>as</sup>, and that is the male grouse intended to copulate with its female, but she prevented unto him. So he said to her, ‘Do not prevent me, for I do not intend except that Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic would Extract from me a person you would be remembered by’. So she answered him to what he sought. So when it wanted to lay eggs, he said to her, ‘Where do you want to lay eggs’. So she said to him, ‘I do not know, near to the road?’ He said to her, ‘I am afraid that the passers-by would pass by you, but I see for you that you should lay eggs near the road, so the one who sees you near it would think that you are picking seeds from the road’. So she answered him to that and laid eggs, and incubated them until she oversaw the births. So while the two of them were involved in that, when there noticed Suleyman<sup>as</sup> Bin Dawood<sup>as</sup> in his<sup>as</sup> army, and the birds were shading him<sup>as</sup>. So she said to him, ‘This is Suleyman<sup>as</sup> who is coming over to us in his army, and there is no safety if he<sup>as</sup> were to trample us, and trample our eggs’. So he said to her, ‘Suleyman<sup>as</sup> would be a merciful man with us, so is there anything with you to gift to him<sup>as</sup> for (the safety of) your chicks when they are born’. She said, ‘Yes, a grass-hopper which I hid from you, awaiting for my chicks for it when they are born. So is there anything with you?’ He said, ‘Yes, I have a date with me, which I hid from you for my chicks’. She said, ‘So you take your date, and I take my grass-hopper, and we go to Suleyman<sup>as</sup>and we present these to him<sup>as</sup>, for he<sup>as</sup> is a man who loves the gifts’. So he took the date in his beak, and she took the grass-hopper in her claws, then they went to Suleyman<sup>as</sup>. So when he<sup>as</sup> saw them both, and he was upon his<sup>as</sup> throne, he<sup>as</sup> extended his<sup>as</sup> hands for them. So they went over and the male sat upon the right hand and the female sat upon the left hand, and he asked them both of their state. So they informed him<sup>as</sup>. So he<sup>as</sup> accepted both their gifts, and diverted his<sup>as</sup> army away from them and their eggs, and he<sup>as</sup> wiped (by his<sup>as</sup> hand) upon their heads, and supplicated for them both with the Blessings. So the topknot appeared on top of both their heads from the wiping of Suleyman<sup>as</sup>’.

citation.arabic_text: قَالَ عَلِيُّ بْنُ الْحُسَيْنِ ( عليه السلام ) الْقُنْزُعَةُ الَّتِي عَلَى رَأْسِ الْقُنْبُرَةِ مِنْ مَسْحَةِ سُلَيْمَانَ بْنِ دَاوُدَ وَ ذَلِكَ أَنَّ الذَّكَرَ أَرَادَ أَنْ يَسْفَدَ أُنْثَاهُ فَامْتَنَعَتْ عَلَيْهِ فَقَالَ لَهَا لَا تَمْتَنِعِي فَمَا أُرِيدُ إِلَّا أَنْ يُخْرِجَ اللَّهُ عَزَّ وَ جَلَّ مِنِّي نَسَمَةً تُذَكَّرُ بِهِ فَأَجَابَتْهُ إِلَى مَا طَلَبَ فَلَمَّا أَرَادَتْ أَنْ تَبِيضَ قَالَ لَهَا أَيْنَ تُرِيدِينَ أَنْ تَبِيضِي فَقَالَتْ لَهُ لَا أَدْرِي أُنَحِّيهِ عَنِ الطَّرِيقِ قَالَ لَهَا إِنِّي خَائِفٌ أَنْ يَمُرَّ بِكِ مَارُّ الطَّرِيقِ وَ لَكِنِّي أَرَى لَكِ أَنْ تَبِيضِي قُرْبَ الطَّرِيقِ فَمَنْ يَرَاكِ قُرْبَهُ تَوَهَّمَ أَنَّكِ تَعْرِضِينَ لِلَقْطِ الْحَبِّ مِنَ الطَّرِيقِ فَأَجَابَتْهُ إِلَى ذَلِكَ وَ بَاضَتْ وَ حَضَنَتْ حَتَّى أَشْرَفَتْ عَلَى النِّقَابِ فَبَيْنَا هُمَا كَذَلِكَ إِذْ طَلَعَ سُلَيْمَانُ بْنُ دَاوُدَ ( عليه السلام ) فِي جُنُودِهِ وَ الطَّيْرُ تُظِلُّهُ فَقَالَتْ لَهُ هَذَا سُلَيْمَانُ قَدْ طَلَعَ عَلَيْنَا فِي جُنُودِهِ وَ لَا آمَنُ أَنْ يَحْطِمَنَا وَ يَحْطِمَ بَيْضَنَا فَقَالَ لَهَا إِنَّ سُلَيْمَانَ ( عليه السلام ) لَرَجُلٌ رَحِيمٌ بِنَا فَهَلْ عِنْدَكِ شَيْ‏ءٌ هَيَّئْتِهِ لِفِرَاخِكِ إِذَا نَقَبْنَ قَالَتْ نَعَمْ جَرَادَةٌ خَبَّأْتُهَا مِنْكَ أَنْتَظِرُ بِهَا فِرَاخِي إِذَا نَقَبْنَ فَهَلْ عِنْدَ أَنْتَ شَيْ‏ءٌ قَالَ نَعَمْ عِنْدِي تَمْرَةٌ خَبَّأْتُهَا مِنْكِ لِفِرَاخِي قَالَتْ فَخُذْ أَنْتَ تَمْرَتَكَ وَ آخُذُ أَنَا جَرَادَتِي وَ نَعْرِضُ لِسُلَيْمَانَ ( عليه السلام ) فَنُهْدِيهِمَا لَهُ فَإِنَّهُ رَجُلٌ يُحِبُّ الْهَدِيَّةَ فَأَخَذَ التَّمْرَةَ فِي مِنْقَارِهِ وَ أَخَذَتْ هِيَ الْجَرَادَةَ فِي رِجْلَيْهَا ثُمَّ تَعَرَّضَا لِسُلَيْمَانَ ( عليه السلام ) فَلَمَّا رَآهُمَا وَ هُوَ عَلَى عَرْشِهِ بَسَطَ يَدَيْهِ لَهُمَا فَأَقْبَلَا فَوَقَعَ الذَّكَرُ عَلَى الْيَمِينِ وَ وَقَعَتِ الْأُنْثَى عَلَى الْيَسَارِ وَ سَأَلَهُمَا عَنْ حَالِهِمَا فَأَخْبَرَاهُ فَقَبِلَ هَدِيَّتَهُمَا وَ جَنَّبَ جُنْدَهُ عَنْهُمَا وَ عَنْ بَيْضِهِمَا وَ مَسَحَ عَلَى رَأْسِهِمَا وَ دَعَا لَهُمَا بِالْبَرَكَةِ فَحَدَثَتِ الْقُنْزُعَةُ عَلَى رَأْسِهِمَا مِنْ مَسْحَةِ سُلَيْمَانَ ( عليه السلام ) .

So he said to her, ‘Suleyman<sup>as</sup> would be a merciful man with us, so is there anything with you to gift to him<sup>as</sup> for (the safety of) your chicks when they are born’. She said, ‘Yes, a grass-hopper which I hid from you, awaiting for my chicks for it when they are born. So is there anything with you?’ He said, ‘Yes, I have a date with me, which I hid from you for my chicks’. She said, ‘So you take your date, and I take my grass-hopper, and we go to Suleyman<sup>as</sup>and we present these to him<sup>as</sup>, for he<sup>as</sup> is a man who loves the gifts’. So he took the date in his beak, and she took the grass-hopper in her claws, then they went to Suleyman<sup>as</sup>. So when he<sup>as</sup> saw them both, and he was upon his<sup>as</sup> throne, he<sup>as</sup> extended his<sup>as</sup> hands for them. So they went over and the male sat upon the right hand and the female sat upon the left hand, and he asked them both of their state. So they informed him<sup>as</sup>. So he<sup>as</sup> accepted both their gifts, and diverted his<sup>as</sup> army away from them and their eggs, and he<sup>as</sup> wiped (by his<sup>as</sup> hand) upon their heads, and supplicated for them both with the Blessings. So the topknot appeared on top of both their heads from the wiping of Suleyman<sup>as</sup>’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: مرسل - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (1/372)

text: تَمَّ كِتَابُ الصَّيْدِ مِنَ الْكَافِي وَ يَتْلُوهُ كِتَابُ الذَّبَائِحِ وَ الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ رَبِّ الْعَالَمِينَ . citation.arabic_text: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا الْحَسَنِ ( عليه السلام ) عَنْ ذَبْحِ الْبَقَرِ فِي الْمَنْحَرِ فَقَالَ لِلْبَقَرِ الذَّبْحُ وَ مَا نُحِرَ فَلَيْسَ بِذَكِيٍّ .

text: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, and Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, and Ali Bin Muhammad, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ibn Abu Nasr, from Yunus Bin Yaqoub who said, ‘I said to Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> the 1<sup>st</sup>, ‘The people of Makkah are slaughtering the cow, and rather they are slaughtering in the upper part of the chest. citation.arabic_text: قُلْتُ لِأَبِي الْحَسَنِ الْأَوَّلِ ( عليه السلام ) إِنَّ أَهْلَ مَكَّةَ لَا يَذْبَحُونَ الْبَقَرَ وَ إِنَّمَا يَنْحَرُونَ فِي اللَّبَّةِ فَمَا تَرَى فِي أَكْلِ لَحْمِهَا قَالَ فَقَالَ ( عليه السلام ) فَذَبَحُوها وَ ما كادُوا يَفْعَلُونَ لَا تَأْكُلْ إِلَّا مَا ذُبِحَ .

text: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Abu Hashim Al Ja’fary, from his father, from Humran Bin Ayn, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, said, ‘I asked him<sup>asws</sup> about the slaughter, so he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘When you slaughter it, let it hang down, and do not pause nor turn the knife in order to enter it from beneath the throat, and cut it to above, and let it hand down for the birds in particular. So if falls down a well or a hole in the ground, so do not eat it, and do not feed it (to others) for you do not know whether it was the falling (down) that killed it or the slaughter. And if it was something from the sheep, so restrain it by its wool or its hair, and do not restrain the hands or the feet; and as for the cow, so (restrain it by its) heels, but leave the tail; and as for the camel, so (restrain it by its) hooves to its armpits and leave its feet; and if something flees from the birds, and you intended to slaughter it, or escapes from you, so shoot at it with your arrow. So when it falls, so its purification is at the status of the hunted prey’.

citation.arabic_text: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنِ الذَّبْحِ فَقَالَ إِذَا ذَبَحْتَ فَأَرْسِلْ وَ لَا تَكْتِفْ وَ لَا تَقْلِبِ السِّكِّينَ لِتُدْخِلَهَا مِنْ تَحْتِ الْحُلْقُومِ وَ تَقْطَعَهُ إِلَى فَوْقُ وَ الْإِرْسَالُ لِلطَّيْرِ خَاصَّةً فَإِنْ تَرَدَّى فِي جُبٍّ أَوْ وَهْدَةٍ مِنَ الْأَرْضِ فَلَا تَأْكُلْهُ وَ لَا تُطْعِمْهُ فَإِنَّكَ لَا تَدْرِي التَّرَدِّي قَتَلَهُ أَوِ الذَّبْحُ وَ إِنْ كَانَ شَيْ‏ءٌ مِنَ الْغَنَمِ فَأَمْسِكْ صُوفَهُ أَوْ شَعْرَهُ وَ لَا تُمْسِكَنَّ يَداً وَ لَا رِجْلًا وَ أَمَّا الْبَقَرُ فَاعْقِلْهَا وَ أَطْلِقِ الذَّنَبَ وَ أَمَّا الْبَعِيرُ فَشُدَّ أَخْفَافَهُ إِلَى آبَاطِهِ وَ أَطْلِقْ رِجْلَيْهِ وَ إِنْ أَفْلَتَكَ شَيْ‏ءٌ مِنَ الطَّيْرِ وَ أَنْتَ تُرِيدُ ذَبْحَهُ أَوْ نَدَّ عَلَيْكَ فَارْمِهِ بِسَهْمِكَ فَإِذَا هُوَ سَقَطَ فَذَكِّهِ بِمَنْزِلَةِ الصَّيْدِ .

text: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Al Hassan Bin Mahboub, from Al A’ala Bin Razeyn, from Muhammad Bin Muslim, (It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup>, said, ‘I asked him<sup>asws</sup> about the slaughter, so he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Face the Qiblah by your slaughter, and do not flip it over until it dies, nor eat from a slaughter what you did not slaughter from its proper place of slaughter’.

citation.arabic_text: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنِ الذَّبِيحَةِ فَقَالَ ( عليه السلام ) اسْتَقْبِلْ بِذَبِيحَتِكَ الْقِبْلَةَ وَ لَا تَنْخَعْهَا حَتَّى تَمُوتَ وَ لَا تَأْكُلْ مِنْ ذَبِيحَةٍ مَا لَمْ تُذْبَحْ مِنْ مَذْبَحِهَا .
citation.translation: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Al Hassan Bin Mahboub, from Al A’ala Bin Razeyn, from Muhammad Bin Muslim, (It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup>, said, ‘I asked him<sup>asws</sup> about the slaughter, so he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Face the Qiblah by your slaughter, and do not flip it over until it dies, nor eat from a slaughter what you did not slaughter from its proper place of slaughter’.

text: Abu Ali Al Ashary, from Muhammad Bin Abdul Jabbar, from Safwan, from Ibn Muskan, from Muhammad Al Halby who said, ‘Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Do not flip over the slaughter until it dies. So when it is dead, so flip it over’.

citation.arabic_text: قَالَ أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) لَا تَنْخَعِ الذَّبِيحَةَ حَتَّى تَمُوتَ فَإِذَا مَاتَتْ فَانْخَعْهَا .
citation.translation: Abu Ali Al Ashary, from Muhammad Bin Abdul Jabbar, from Safwan, from Ibn Muskan, from Muhammad Al Halby who said, ‘Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Do not flip over the slaughter until it dies. So when it is dead, so flip it over’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: صحيح - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (22/9)

text: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Gayas Bin Ibrahim, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> that Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Do not slaughter the sheep in the presence of the sheep, nor a camel in the presence of the camel, and it is looking at it’.

citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: موثق - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (22/9)

text: Muhammad Bin Yahya, raising it, said, ‘Abu Al-Hassan Al-Reza<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘When you slaughter the sheep, and strip it, or strip off something from it before it dies, it is not Permissible to eat it’.

citation.arabic_text: قَالَ أَبُو الْحَسَنِ الرِّضَا ( عليه السلام ) إِذَا ذُبِحَتِ الشَّاةُ وَ سُلِخَتْ أَوْ سُلِخَ شَيْ‏ءٌ مِنْهَا قَبْلَ أَنْ تَمُوتَ لَمْ يَحِلَّ أَكْلُهَا .
citation.translation: Muhammad Bin Yahya, raising it, said, ‘Abu Al-Hassan Al-Reza<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘When you slaughter the sheep, and strip it, or strip off something from it before it dies, it is not Permissible to eat it’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: مرفوع - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (22/10)

text: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Umar Bin Azina, from Al Fazeyl Bin Yasaar who said, ‘I asked Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> about a man who slaughtered, but his knife transcended and cut off its head. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘It is a vivid slaughter. There is no problem with it, and with eating it’.

citation.arabic_text: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا جَعْفَرٍ ( عليه السلام ) عَنْ رَجُلٍ ذَبَحَ فَسَبَقَهُ السِّكِّينُ فَقَطَعَ رَأْسَهُ فَقَالَ هُوَ ذَكَاةٌ وَحِيَّةٌ لَا بَأْسَ بِهِ وَ بِأَكْلِهِ .
citation.translation: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Umar Bin Azina, from Al Fazeyl Bin Yasaar who said, ‘I asked Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> about a man who slaughtered, but his knife transcended and cut off its head. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘It is a vivid slaughter. There is no problem with it, and with eating it’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: حسن - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (2/10)

text: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad Bin Isa, from Hareyz, from Muhammad Bin Muslim who said, ‘I asked Abu Ja’farasws about a Muslim who slaughtered a sheep and Named (Bismillah), but his knife transcended by its severity, so it cut-off the head. So heasws said: ‘If the blood comes out, so eat’.

citation.arabic_text: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا جَعْفَرٍ ( عليه السلام ) عَنْ مُسْلِمٍ ذَبَحَ شَاةً وَ سَمَّى فَسَبَقَهُ السِّكِّينُ بِحِدَّتِهَا فَأَبَانَ الرَّأْسَ فَقَالَ إِنْ خَرَجَ الدَّمُ فَكُلْ .
citation.translation: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad Bin Isa, from Hareyz, from Muhammad Bin Muslim who said, ‘I asked Abu Ja’farasws about a Muslim who slaughtered a sheep and Named (Bismillah), but his knife transcended by its severity, so it cut-off the head. So heasws said: ‘If the blood comes out, so eat’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: حسن - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (22/11)

text: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Hroun Bin Muslim, from Mas’ada Bin sadaqa who said, ‘I heard Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, and he<sup>asws</sup> had been asked about the man who slaughtered, so the knife hastened and the head was cut off. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The vivid slaughter. There is no problem with eating it when it was not deliberate with that’.

citation.arabic_text: سَمِعْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) وَ قَدْ سُئِلَ عَنِ الرَّجُلِ يَذْبَحُ فَتُسْرِعُ السِّكِّينُ فَتُبِينُ الرَّأْسَ فَقَالَ الذَّكَاةُ الْوَحِيَّةُ لَا بَأْسَ بِأَكْلِهِ إِذَا لَمْ يَتَعَمَّدْ بِذَلِكَ .
citation.translation: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Hroun Bin Muslim, from Mas’ada Bin sadaqa who said, ‘I heard Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, and he<sup>asws</sup> had been asked about the man who slaughtered, so the knife hastened and the head was cut off. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The vivid slaughter. There is no problem with eating it when it was not deliberate with that’.

text: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Al Husayn Bin Saeed, from Al Qasim Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Abu Hamza, from Abu Baseer, Abu Abdullahasws has said: ‘When a camel is preventing you and you are intending to sacrifice it, so let it go away from you. So if you fear that it would precede you, so strike it with a sword, or stab it with a spear after you Name (Bismillah). So eat, except if you come to it and if it has not died afterwards, so slaughter it’.

citation.arabic_text: إِذَا امْتَنَعَ عَلَيْكَ بَعِيرٌ وَ أَنْتَ تُرِيدُ أَنْ تَنْحَرَهُ فَانْطَلَقَ مِنْكَ فَإِنْ خَشِيتَ أَنْ يَسْبِقَكَ فَضَرَبْتَهُ بِسَيْفٍ أَوْ طَعَنْتَهُ بِرُمْحٍ بَعْدَ أَنْ تُسَمِّيَ فَكُلْ إِلَّا أَنْ تُدْرِكَهُ وَ لَمْ يَمُتْ بَعْدُ فَذَكِّهِ .
citation.translation: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Al Husayn Bin Saeed, from Al Qasim Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Abu Hamza, from Abu Baseer, Abu Abdullahasws has said: ‘When a camel is preventing you and you are intending to sacrifice it, so let it go away from you. So if you fear that it would precede you, so strike it with a sword, or stab it with a spear after you Name (Bismillah). So eat, except if you come to it and if it has not died afterwards, so slaughter it’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: ضعيف - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (22/11)

text: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Safwan, from Ays Bin Al Qasim, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘A bull at Al-Kufa went on rampage, so the people followed it with their swords, so they struck it down. So they came to Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup>, and they asked him<sup>asws</sup>. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘A vivid slaughter, and its flesh is Permissible’.

citation.arabic_text: إِنَّ ثَوْراً بِالْكُوفَةِ ثَارَ فَبَادَرَ النَّاسُ إِلَيْهِ بِأَسْيَافِهِمْ فَضَرَبُوهُ فَأَتَوْا أَمِيرَ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ ( عليه السلام ) فَسَأَلُوهُ فَقَالَ ذَكَاةٌ وَحِيَّةٌ وَ لَحْمُهُ حَلَالٌ .
citation.translation: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Safwan, from Ays Bin Al Qasim, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘A bull at Al-Kufa went on rampage, so the people followed it with their swords, so they struck it down. So they came to Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup>, and they asked him<sup>asws</sup>. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘A vivid slaughter, and its flesh is Permissible’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: حسن - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (22/11)

text: Abu Ali Al Ashary, from Muhammad Bin Abdul Jabbar, and Muhammad Bin Ismail, from Al fazl Bin Shazaan, from Safwan, from Ibn Muskan, from Muhammad Al Halby who said, ‘Abu Abdullahasws said regarding a bull which disobeyed. So they pursued it with their swords, and Named (Bismillah), and they came to Aliasws. So heasws said: ‘This is a vivid slaughter, and its flesh is Permissible’.

citation.arabic_text: قَالَ أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) فِي ثَوْرٍ تَعَاصَى فَابْتَدَرُوهُ بِأَسْيَافِهِمْ وَ سَمَّوْا وَ أَتَوْا عَلِيّاً ( عليه السلام ) فَقَالَ هَذِهِ ذَكَاةٌ وَحِيَّةٌ وَ لَحْمُهُ حَلَالٌ .
citation.translation: Abu Ali Al Ashary, from Muhammad Bin Abdul Jabbar, and Muhammad Bin Ismail, from Al fazl Bin Shazaan, from Safwan, from Ibn Muskan, from Muhammad Al Halby who said, ‘Abu Abdullahasws said regarding a bull which disobeyed. So they pursued it with their swords, and Named (Bismillah), and they came to Aliasws. So heasws said: ‘This is a vivid slaughter, and its flesh is Permissible’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: صحيح - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (22/11)

text: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Abdullah Bin Muhahhad, from Ali Bin Al Hakam, from Aban Bin usman, from Al Fazl Bin Abdul Malik, and Abdul Rahman Bin Abu Abdullah, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> that a group of people came to the Prophet<sup>saww</sup>, so they said, ‘A cow of ours overcame us and became difficult over us, so we struck it with the sword’. So he<sup>saww</sup> ordered them with eating it’.

citation.arabic_text: أَنَّ قَوْماً أَتَوُا النَّبِيَّ ( صلى الله عليه وآله ) فَقَالُوا إِنَّ بَقَرَةً لَنَا غَلَبَتْنَا وَ اسْتَصْعَبَتْ عَلَيْنَا فَضَرَبْنَاهَا بِالسَّيْفِ فَأَمَرَهُمْ بِأَكْلِهَا .
citation.translation: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Abdullah Bin Muhahhad, from Ali Bin Al Hakam, from Aban Bin usman, from Al Fazl Bin Abdul Malik, and Abdul Rahman Bin Abu Abdullah, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> that a group of people came to the Prophet<sup>saww</sup>, so they said, ‘A cow of ours overcame us and became difficult over us, so we struck it with the sword’. So he<sup>saww</sup> ordered them with eating it’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: مجهول - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (22/12)

text: Humeyd Bin Ziyad, from Al Hassan Bin Muhammad Bin Sama’at, from Ahmad Bin Al Hassan Al Maysamy, from Aban, from Ismail Al Ju’fy who said, ‘I said to Abu Abdullahasws, ‘A camel fell down in a well, how can it be sacrificed?’ Heasws said: ‘Stab it with a bayonet and Name (Bismillah) and eat’.

citation.arabic_text: قُلْتُ لِأَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) بَعِيرٌ تَرَدَّى فِي بِئْرٍ كَيْفَ يُنْحَرُ قَالَ تُدْخِلُ الْحَرْبَةَ فَتَطْعُنُهُ بِهَا وَ تُسَمِّي وَ تَأْكُلُ .
citation.translation: Humeyd Bin Ziyad, from Al Hassan Bin Muhammad Bin Sama’at, from Ahmad Bin Al Hassan Al Maysamy, from Aban, from Ismail Al Ju’fy who said, ‘I said to Abu Abdullahasws, ‘A camel fell down in a well, how can it be sacrificed?’ Heasws said: ‘Stab it with a bayonet and Name (Bismillah) and eat’.

text: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al Halby, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws regarding a man who struck with his sword, a camel or a sheep, in other than its slaughtering place, and he had Named (Bismillah) when he struck. So heasws said: ‘It is not correct to slaughter an (animal) which has not been slaughter from its (proper) slaughtering place, meaning when you are deliberate for that, and his state does not happen to be a state of desperation. So as for what he is desperate towards, and it is difficult upon him, what he intends to slaughter, so there is no problem with that’.

citation.arabic_text: رَجُلٍ ضَرَبَ بِسَيْفِهِ جَزُوراً أَوْ شَاةً فِي غَيْرِ مَذْبَحِهَا وَ قَدْ سَمَّى حِينَ ضَرَبَ فَقَالَ لَا يَصْلُحُ أَكْلُ ذَبِيحَةٍ لَا تُذْبَحُ مِنْ مَذْبَحِهَا يَعْنِي إِذَا تَعَمَّدَ لِذَلِكَ وَ لَمْ تَكُنْ حَالُهُ حَالَ اضْطِرَارٍ فَأَمَّا إِذَا اضْطُرَّ إِلَيْهَا وَ اسْتَصْعَبَتْ عَلَيْهِ مَا يُرِيدُ أَنْ يَذْبَحَ فَلَا بَأْسَ بِذَلِكَ .
citation.translation: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al Halby, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws regarding a man who struck with his sword, a camel or a sheep, in other than its slaughtering place, and he had Named (Bismillah) when he struck. So heasws said: ‘It is not correct to slaughter an (animal) which has not been slaughter from its (proper) slaughtering place, meaning when you are deliberate for that, and his state does not happen to be a state of desperation. So as for what he is desperate towards, and it is difficult upon him, what he intends to slaughter, so there is no problem with that’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: حسن - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (2/12)

text: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Abdullah Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Ali Bin Al Hakam, from Aban Bin Usman, from Abdullah Bin Suleyman, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘In the Book of Ali<sup>asws</sup> (is written): ‘When the eye is blinking, or the feet are kicking, or the tail is moving, and you come over to it, so slaughter it’.

citation.arabic_text: فِي كِتَابِ عَلِيٍّ ( عليه السلام ) إِذَا طَرَفَتِ الْعَيْنُ أَوْ رَكَضَتِ الرِّجْلُ أَوْ تَحَرَّكَ الذَّنَبُ وَ أَدْرَكْتَهُ فَذَكِّهِ .
citation.translation: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Abdullah Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Ali Bin Al Hakam, from Aban Bin Usman, from Abdullah Bin Suleyman, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘In the Book of Ali<sup>asws</sup> (is written): ‘When the eye is blinking, or the feet are kicking, or the tail is moving, and you come over to it, so slaughter it’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: مجهول - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (22/13)

text: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Al Hakam, from Suleym Al Farra’a, from Al Hassan Bin Muslim who said, ‘I was in the presence of Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> when Muhammad Bin Abdul Salaam came over, so he said to him<sup>asws</sup>, ‘May I be sacrificed for you<sup>asws</sup>! My grandfather is saying to you<sup>asws</sup> that a man struck a cow with a pole-axe, so it fell. Then he slaughtered it’. But he<sup>asws</sup> did not send an answer with him, and Instead called Saeeda, a slave girl of Umm Farwa<sup>as</sup>, so he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Muhammad came to me with a message from you, but I<sup>asws</sup> disliked that I send a message with the answer with him. So if it was such that the man who slaughtered the cow, when he slaughtered it, the blood came out moderately, so eat, and feed, and if it came out with a heavy coming out, so do not go near it’.

citation.arabic_text: كُنْتُ عِنْدَ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) إِذْ جَاءَهُ مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ عَبْدِ السَّلَامِ فَقَالَ لَهُ جُعِلْتُ فِدَاكَ يَقُولُ لَكَ جَدِّي إِنَّ رَجُلًا ضَرَبَ بَقَرَةً بِفَأْسٍ فَسَقَطَتْ ثُمَّ ذَبَحَهَا فَلَمْ يُرْسِلْ مَعَهُ بِالْجَوَابِ وَ دَعَا سَعِيدَةَ مَوْلَاةَ أُمِّ فَرْوَةَ فَقَالَ لَهَا إِنَّ مُحَمَّداً أَتَانِي بِرِسَالَةٍ مِنْكِ فَكَرِهْتُ أَنْ أُرْسِلَ إِلَيْكِ بِالْجَوَابِ مَعَهُ فَإِنْ كَانَ الرَّجُلُ الَّذِي ذَبَحَ الْبَقَرَةَ حِينَ ذَبَحَ خَرَجَ الدَّمُ مُعْتَدِلًا فَكُلُوا وَ أَطْعِمُوا وَ إِنْ كَانَ خَرَجَ خُرُوجاً مُتَثَاقِلًا فَلَا تَقْرَبُوهُ .
citation.translation: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Al Hakam, from Suleym Al Farra’a, from Al Hassan Bin Muslim who said, ‘I was in the presence of Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> when Muhammad Bin Abdul Salaam came over, so he said to him<sup>asws</sup>, ‘May I be sacrificed for you<sup>asws</sup>! My grandfather is saying to you<sup>asws</sup> that a man struck a cow with a pole-axe, so it fell. Then he slaughtered it’. But he<sup>asws</sup> did not send an answer with him, and Instead called Saeeda, a slave girl of Umm Farwa<sup>as</sup>, so he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Muhammad came to me with a message from you, but I<sup>asws</sup> disliked that I send a message with the answer with him. So if it was such that the man who slaughtered the cow, when he slaughtered it, the blood came out moderately, so eat, and feed, and if it came out with a heavy coming out, so do not go near it’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: مجهول - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (2/13)

text: Al Husayn Bin Muhammad, from Moala Bin Muhammad, from Al Washa, from Aban, from Abdul Rahman Bin Abu Abdullah, Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> has said: ‘In the Book of Ali<sup>asws</sup> (it is written): ‘When the eye is blinking, or the feet are kicking, or the tail is moving, so eat from it, for you have realised its slaughter’.

citation.arabic_text: فِي كِتَابِ عَلِيٍّ ( عليه السلام ) إِذَا طَرَفَتِ الْعَيْنُ أَوْ رَكَضَتِ الرِّجْلُ أَوْ تَحَرَّكَ الذَّنَبُ فَكُلْ مِنْهُ فَقَدْ أَدْرَكْتَ ذَكَاتَهُ .
citation.translation: Al Husayn Bin Muhammad, from Moala Bin Muhammad, from Al Washa, from Aban, from Abdul Rahman Bin Abu Abdullah, Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> has said: ‘In the Book of Ali<sup>asws</sup> (it is written): ‘When the eye is blinking, or the feet are kicking, or the tail is moving, so eat from it, for you have realised its slaughter’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: ضعيف على المشهور - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (22/13)

text: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Ibn Abu Najran, from Musny Al Hannat, from Aban Bin Taghlub, Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> has said: ‘When you doubt regarding the life of a sheep, and you see it blinks its eyes, or moving its ears, or beating its tail, so slaughter it, for it is Permissible for you’.

citation.arabic_text: إِذَا شَكَكْتَ فِي حَيَاةِ شَاةٍ وَ رَأَيْتَهَا تَطْرِفُ عَيْنَهَا أَوْ تُحَرِّكُ أُذُنَيْهَا أَوْ تَمْصَعُ بِذَنَبِهَا فَاذْبَحْهَا فَإِنَّهَا لَكَ حَلَالٌ .
citation.translation: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Ibn Abu Najran, from Musny Al Hannat, from Aban Bin Taghlub, Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> has said: ‘When you doubt regarding the life of a sheep, and you see it blinks its eyes, or moving its ears, or beating its tail, so slaughter it, for it is Permissible for you’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: ضعيف على المشهور - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (2/14)

text: Abu Ali Al Ashary, from Muhammad Bin Abdul Jabbar, from Safwan Bin Yahya, from Ibn Muskan, from Muhammad Al Halby, (The narrator) says ‘I asked Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> about the slaughtered animal, so he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘When it moves the tail, or blinks, or (moves) its ears, so it is purified’.

citation.arabic_text: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنِ الذَّبِيحَةِ فَقَالَ إِذَا تَحَرَّكَ الذَّنَبُ أَوِ الطَّرْفُ أَوِ الْأُذُنُ فَهُوَ ذَكِيٌّ .
citation.translation: Abu Ali Al Ashary, from Muhammad Bin Abdul Jabbar, from Safwan Bin Yahya, from Ibn Muskan, from Muhammad Al Halby, (The narrator) says ‘I asked Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> about the slaughtered animal, so he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘When it moves the tail, or blinks, or (moves) its ears, so it is purified’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: صحيح - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (22/14)

text: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Ibn Abu Nasr, from Rafa’at, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said regarding the sheep when its blinks its eyes, or moves its tail, so it is purified’.

citation.arabic_text: فِي الشَّاةِ إِذَا طَرَفَتْ عَيْنَهَا أَوْ حَرَّكَتْ ذَنَبَهَا فَهِيَ ذَكِيَّةٌ .
citation.translation: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Ibn Abu Nasr, from Rafa’at, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said regarding the sheep when its blinks its eyes, or moves its tail, so it is purified’.

text: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Umar Bin Azina, from Muhammad Bin Muslim who said, ‘I asked Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> about a man who slaughtered an animal, so he was ignorant that he had to face towards the Qiblah. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Eat from it’. So I said to him<sup>asws</sup>, ‘So if he (intentionally) does not face it (towards the Qiblah)’. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘So do not eat from it, and do not eat from a slaughtered animal what he had not mentioned the Name of Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic upon it’. And he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘When you intend to slaughter, so face the Qibalh with your animal’.

citation.arabic_text: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا جَعْفَرٍ ( عليه السلام ) عَنْ رَجُلٍ ذَبَحَ ذَبِيحَةً فَجَهِلَ أَنْ يُوَجِّهَهَا إِلَى الْقِبْلَةِ قَالَ كُلْ مِنْهَا فَقُلْتُ لَهُ فَإِنَّهُ لَمْ يُوَجِّهْهَا قَالَ فَلَا تَأْكُلْ مِنْهَا وَ لَا تَأْكُلْ مِنْ ذَبِيحَةٍ مَا لَمْ يُذْكَرِ اسْمُ اللَّهِ عَزَّ وَ جَلَّ عَلَيْهَا وَ قَالَ ( عليه السلام ) إِذَا أَرَدْتَ أَنْ تَذْبَحَ فَاسْتَقْبِلْ بِذَبِيحَتِكَ الْقِبْلَةَ .

text: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Al Hassan Bin Mahboub, from Al A’ala Bin Razeyn, from Muhammad Bin Muslim who said, ‘I asked Abu Ja’farasws about the man who slaughters and does not Name (Bismillah). Heasws said: ‘If he had forgotten it, so there is no problem when he was a Muslim, and was good at slaughtering, and did not flip it over nor cut off the neck (until) after having slaughtered’.

citation.arabic_text: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا جَعْفَرٍ ( عليه السلام ) عَنِ الرَّجُلِ يَذْبَحُ وَ لَا يُسَمِّي قَالَ إِنْ كَانَ نَاسِياً فَلَا بَأْسَ إِذَا كَانَ مُسْلِماً وَ كَانَ يُحْسِنُ أَنْ يَذْبَحَ وَ لَا يَنْخَعُ وَ لَا يَقْطَعُ الرَّقَبَةَ بَعْدَ مَا يَذْبَحُ .
citation.translation: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Al Hassan Bin Mahboub, from Al A’ala Bin Razeyn, from Muhammad Bin Muslim who said, ‘I asked Abu Ja’farasws about the man who slaughters and does not Name (Bismillah). text: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al Halby, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws, said, ‘Heasws was asked about the slaughtered animal slaughtered towards other than the Qiblah. Heasws said: ‘There is no problem when it was not deliberate’. And about the man who slaughtered, so he forgot to Name (Bismillah), can one eat his slaughter?’ So heasws said: ‘Yes, when he was not accused, and was good at the slaughtering before that, and did not flip it over, and did not break the neck until the slaughtered animal was cold’.

citation.arabic_text: سُئِلَ عَنِ الذَّبِيحَةِ تُذْبَحُ لِغَيْرِ الْقِبْلَةِ قَالَ لَا بَأْسَ إِذَا لَمْ يَتَعَمَّدْ وَ عَنِ الرَّجُلِ يَذْبَحُ فَيَنْسَى أَنْ يُسَمِّيَ أَ تُؤْكَلُ ذَبِيحَتُهُ فَقَالَ نَعَمْ إِذَا كَانَ لَا يُتَّهَمُ وَ كَانَ يُحْسِنُ الذَّبْحَ قَبْلَ ذَلِكَ وَ لَا يَنْخَعُ وَ لَا يَكْسِرُ الرَّقَبَةَ حَتَّى تَبْرُدَ الذَّبِيحَةُ .
citation.translation: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al Halby, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws, said, ‘Heasws was asked about the slaughtered animal slaughtered towards other than the Qiblah. Heasws said: ‘There is no problem when it was not deliberate’. And about the man who slaughtered, so he forgot to Name (Bismillah), can one eat his slaughter?’ So heasws said: ‘Yes, when he was not accused, and was good at the slaughtering before that, and did not flip it over, and did not break the neck until the slaughtered animal was cold’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: حسن - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (22/15)

text: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad Bin Isa, from Hareyz, from Muhammad Bin Muslim who said, ‘I asked Abu Abdullahasws about a slaughtered animal slaughtered towards other than the Qiblah. So heasws said: ‘Eat, and there is no problem with that for as long as it was not deliberate’. He (the narrator) said, ‘And I asked himasws about a man who slaughtered and did not Name (Bismillah), so heasws said: ‘If he had forgotten, so let him Name when he remembers, and he should be saying, ‘In the Name of Allahazwj upon its beginning and upon its ending’.

citation.arabic_text: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) عَنْ ذَبِيحَةٍ ذُبِحَتْ لِغَيْرِ الْقِبْلَةِ فَقَالَ كُلْ وَ لَا بَأْسَ بِذَلِكَ مَا لَمْ يَتَعَمَّدْهُ قَالَ وَ سَأَلْتُهُ عَنْ رَجُلٍ ذَبَحَ وَ لَمْ يُسَمِّ فَقَالَ إِنْ كَانَ نَاسِياً فَلْيُسَمِّ حِينَ يَذْكُرُ وَ يَقُولُ بِسْمِ اللَّهِ عَلَى أَوَّلِهِ وَ عَلَى آخِرِهِ .
citation.translation: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad Bin Isa, from Hareyz, from Muhammad Bin Muslim who said, ‘I asked Abu Abdullahasws about a slaughtered animal slaughtered towards other than the Qiblah. text: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Al Hassan Bin Mahboub, from Al Aa’la Bin Razeyn, from Muhammad Bin Muslim who said, ‘I asked himasws about a man who slaughtered, so he Glorified (Subhanallah), or Exclaimed the Greatness (Allah-O-Akbar), or Praised Allahazwj Mighty and Majestic (Alhamdulillah). Heasws said: ‘All these are from the Names of Allahazwj Mighty and Majestic, and there is no problem with it’.

citation.arabic_text: سَأَلْتُهُ ( عليه السلام ) عَنْ رَجُلٍ ذَبَحَ فَسَبَّحَ أَوْ كَبَّرَ أَوْ هَلَّلَ أَوْ حَمِدَ اللَّهَ عَزَّ وَ جَلَّ قَالَ هَذَا كُلُّهُ مِنْ أَسْمَاءِ اللَّهِ عَزَّ وَ جَلَّ وَ لَا بَأْسَ بِهِ .
citation.translation: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Al Hassan Bin Mahboub, from Al Aa’la Bin Razeyn, from Muhammad Bin Muslim who said, ‘I asked himasws about a man who slaughtered, so he Glorified (Subhanallah), or Exclaimed the Greatness (Allah-O-Akbar), or Praised Allahazwj Mighty and Majestic (Alhamdulillah). Heasws said: ‘All these are from the Names of Allahazwj Mighty and Majestic, and there is no problem with it’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: صحيح - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (22/16)

text: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from one of his companions, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘There is no problem if the man slaughters and he was with sexual impurity’.

citation.arabic_text: لَا بَأْسَ أَنْ يَذْبَحَ الرَّجُلُ وَ هُوَ جُنُبٌ .
citation.translation: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from one of his companions, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘There is no problem if the man slaughters and he was with sexual impurity’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: حسن - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (22/16)

text: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Abu Umeyr, from Umar Bin Azina, from Muhammad Bin Muslim who said, ‘I asked one of the two (5th or 6th Imamasws) about the Words of Allahazwj Mighty and Majestic [5:1] The cattle quadrupeds are Permissible for you. So heasws said: ‘The foetus in the belly of its mother, when it grows hair and fluff, so its slaughter is the slaughter of its mother, so that is which Allahazwj Mighty and Majestic Means’.

citation.arabic_text: سَأَلْتُ أَحَدَهُمَا ( عليهما السلام ) عَنْ قَوْلِ اللَّهِ عَزَّ وَ جَلَّ أُحِلَّتْ لَكُمْ بَهِيمَةُ الْأَنْعامِ فَقَالَ الْجَنِينُ فِي بَطْنِ أُمِّهِ إِذَا أَشْعَرَ وَ أَوْبَرَ فَذَكَاتُهُ ذَكَاةُ أُمِّهِ فَذَلِكَ الَّذِي عَنَى اللَّهُ عَزَّ وَ جَلَّ .
citation.translation: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Abu Umeyr, from Umar Bin Azina, from Muhammad Bin Muslim who said, ‘I asked one of the two (5th or 6th Imamasws) about the Words of Allahazwj Mighty and Majestic [5:1] The cattle quadrupeds are Permissible for you. So heasws said: ‘The foetus in the belly of its mother, when it grows hair and fluff, so its slaughter is the slaughter of its mother, so that is which Allahazwj Mighty and Majestic Means’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: حسن - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (22/17)

text: Ali Bin Ibrahim, form his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al Halby, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘When you slaughter a slaughter, so you find a complete child in its belly, so eat, and if it does not happen to be complete, so do not eat’.

citation.arabic_text: إِذَا ذَبَحْتَ الذَّبِيحَةَ فَوَجَدْتَ فِي بَطْنِهَا وَلَداً تَامّاً فَكُلْ وَ إِنْ لَمْ يَكُنْ تَامّاً فَلَا تَأْكُلْ .
citation.translation: Ali Bin Ibrahim, form his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al Halby, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘When you slaughter a slaughter, so you find a complete child in its belly, so eat, and if it does not happen to be complete, so do not eat’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: حسن - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (22/17)

text: Abu Ali Ashary, from Muhammad Bin Abdul Jabbar Bin Ismail, from Ali Bin Al No’man, form Yaqoub Bin Shuayb who said, ‘I asked Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> about the camel foetus whose mother is slaughtered, can one eat due to her having been slaughtered?’ So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘When it was complete, and the hair has grown upon it, so eat’.

citation.arabic_text: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) عَنِ الْحُوَارِ تُذَكَّى أُمُّهُ أَ يُؤْكَلُ بِذَكَاتِهَا فَقَالَ إِذَا كَانَ تَمَاماً وَ نَبَتَ عَلَيْهِ الشَّعْرُ فَكُلْ .
citation.translation: Abu Ali Ashary, from Muhammad Bin Abdul Jabbar Bin Ismail, from Ali Bin Al No’man, form Yaqoub Bin Shuayb who said, ‘I asked Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> about the camel foetus whose mother is slaughtered, can one eat due to her having been slaughtered?’ So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘When it was complete, and the hair has grown upon it, so eat’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: صحيح - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (2/17)

text: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Abu Nasr, from Dawood Bin Al Husayn, from Yaqoub Bin Shuayb, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> – similar to it. A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Khalid, from Usman Bin Isa, from Sama’at who said, ‘I asked about the sheep which was slaughtered and inside its belly was a child, and it had grown hair. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Its slaughter is the slaughter of its mother’.

citation.arabic_text: . عِدَّةٌ مِنْ أَصْحَابِنَا عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ خَالِدٍ عَنْ عُثْمَانَ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنْ سَمَاعَةَ قَالَ سَأَلْتُهُ عَنِ الشَّاةِ يَذْبَحُهَا وَ فِي بَطْنِهَا وَلَدٌ وَ قَدْ أَشْعَرَ فَقَالَ ( عليه السلام ) ذَكَاتُهُ ذَكَاةُ أُمِّهِ .
citation.translation: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Abu Nasr, from Dawood Bin Al Husayn, from Yaqoub Bin Shuayb, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> – similar to it. citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: موثق - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (2/18)

text: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Haroun Bin Muslim, from Mas’ada Bin Sadaqa, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said regarding the foetus: ‘When it grows hair, so eat, or else, so do not eat - meaning if it has not grown hair’.

citation.arabic_text: فِي الْجَنِينِ إِذَا أَشْعَرَ فَكُلْ وَ إِلَّا فَلَا تَأْكُلْ يَعْنِي إِذَا لَمْ يُشْعِرْ .
citation.translation: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Haroun Bin Muslim, from Mas’ada Bin Sadaqa, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said regarding the foetus: ‘When it grows hair, so eat, or else, so do not eat - meaning if it has not grown hair’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: ضعيف - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (22/18)

text: Al Husayn Bin Muhammad, from Moala Bin Muhammad, from Al Washa who said, ‘I heard Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> saying: ‘The (animal) butted by the horn, and the one killed by a fall, and what the predators eat, when you come over to it, slaughter it, so eat’.

citation.arabic_text: سَمِعْتُ أَبَا الْحَسَنِ ( عليه السلام ) يَقُولُ النَّطِيحَةُ وَ الْمُتَرَدِّيَةُ وَ مَا أَكَلَ السَّبُعُ إِذَا أَدْرَكْتَ ذَكَاتَهُ فَكُلْ .
citation.translation: Al Husayn Bin Muhammad, from Moala Bin Muhammad, from Al Washa who said, ‘I heard Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> saying: ‘The (animal) butted by the horn, and the one killed by a fall, and what the predators eat, when you come over to it, slaughter it, so eat’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: ضعيف على المشهور - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (22/18)

text: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Al Hakam, from Ali Bin Abu Hamza, from Abu Baseer, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Do not eat from a prey of the predator, nor the one beaten to death, nor the one fallen to death, except if you come to it as alive, so you slaughter it’.

citation.arabic_text: لَا تَأْكُلْ مِنْ فَرِيسَةِ السَّبُعِ وَ لَا الْمَوْقُوذَةِ وَ لَا الْمُتَرَدِّيَةِ إِلَّا أَنْ تُدْرِكَهَا حَيَّةً فَتُذَكِّيَ .
citation.translation: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Al Hakam, from Ali Bin Abu Hamza, from Abu Baseer, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Do not eat from a prey of the predator, nor the one beaten to death, nor the one fallen to death, except if you come to it as alive, so you slaughter it’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: ضعيف على المشهور - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (22/19)

text: Abu Ali Al Ashary, from Muhammad Bin Abdul Jabbar, from Muhammad Bin Ismail, from Ali Bin Al Noman, from Saeed Al A’araj who said, ‘I asked Abu Abdullahasws about a cooking pot in which is a camel, and there had fallen in it an ‘Awqiya’ (A unit of measurement) of blood, can one eat?’ So heasws said: ‘Yes, because the fire consumes the blood’.

citation.arabic_text: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) عَنْ قِدْرٍ فِيهَا جَزُورٌ وَقَعَ فِيهَا مِقْدَارُ أُوقِيَّةٍ مِنْ دَمٍ أَ يُؤْكَلُ فَقَالَ ( عليه السلام ) نَعَمْ لِأَنَّ النَّارَ تَأْكُلُ الدَّمَ .
citation.translation: Abu Ali Al Ashary, from Muhammad Bin Abdul Jabbar, from Muhammad Bin Ismail, from Ali Bin Al Noman, from Saeed Al A’araj who said, ‘I asked Abu Abdullahasws about a cooking pot in which is a camel, and there had fallen in it an ‘Awqiya’ (A unit of measurement) of blood, can one eat?’ So heasws said: ‘Yes, because the fire consumes the blood’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: صحيح - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (2/19)

text: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Muhammad Bin Musa, from Al Abbas Bin Marouf, from Marouk Bin Ubeyd, from one of our companions, from Abdullah Bin Muskaan, from Muhammad Al Halby, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> used to dislike the slaughter and spilling the blood on the day of Friday before the Prayer, except out of necessity’.

citation.arabic_text: كَانَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ ( صلى الله عليه وآله ) يَكْرَهُ الذَّبْحَ وَ إِرَاقَةَ الدَّمِ يَوْمَ الْجُمُعَةِ قَبْلَ الصَّلَاةِ إِلَّا عَنْ ضَرُورَةٍ .
citation.translation: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Muhammad Bin Musa, from Al Abbas Bin Marouf, from Marouk Bin Ubeyd, from one of our companions, from Abdullah Bin Muskaan, from Muhammad Al Halby, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> used to dislike the slaughter and spilling the blood on the day of Friday before the Prayer, except out of necessity’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: مجهول - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (2/20)

text: A number of our companions, from sahl Bin Ziyad, from Muhammad Bin Ali, from Muhammad Bin Amro, from Jameel Bin Darraj, from Aban Bin Taghlub, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Ali<sup>asws</sup> Bin Al-Husayn<sup>asws</sup> used to order his<sup>asws</sup> servants that they should not slaughter until the emergence of the dawn’. – In a miscellaneous (Hadeeth) regarding the day of Friday.

citation.arabic_text: كَانَ عَلِيُّ بْنُ الْحُسَيْنِ ( عليه السلام ) يَأْمُرُ غِلْمَانَهُ أَنْ لَا يَذْبَحُوا حَتَّى يَطْلُعَ الْفَجْرُ . فِي نَوَادِرِ الْجُمُعَةِ .
citation.translation: A number of our companions, from sahl Bin Ziyad, from Muhammad Bin Ali, from Muhammad Bin Amro, from Jameel Bin Darraj, from Aban Bin Taghlub, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Ali<sup>asws</sup> Bin Al-Husayn<sup>asws</sup> used to order his<sup>asws</sup> servants that they should not slaughter until the emergence of the dawn’. – In a miscellaneous (Hadeeth) regarding the day of Friday.

text: Ali Bin Ismail, from Muhammad Bin Amro, from Jameel Bin Darraj, from Aban Bin Taghlib who said, ‘I heard Ali<sup>asws</sup> Bin Al-Husayn<sup>asws</sup> and he<sup>asws</sup> was saying to his servant: ‘Do not slaughter until the emergence of the day, for Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Made the night as a tranquility for everything’. I said, ‘May I be sacrificed for you<sup>asws</sup>! Supposing we are fearing’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘If you fear the death, so slaughter’.

text: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from Haroun Bin Muslim, from Mas’ada Bin Sadaqa who said, ‘Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> was asked about a slaughter by a boy. text: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hisham Bin Salim, from Suleyman Bin Khalid who said, ‘I asked Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> about a slaughter by the boy and the woman, can it be eaten?’ So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘When the woman was a Muslim, and she mentioned the Name of Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic upon her slaughter, her slaughter is Permissible, and similar to that is the boy, when he is strong enough upon the slaughtered animal, and mentions the Name of Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic over it, and that is when there is fear of losing the slaughtered animal, and there cannot be found one who can slaughter apart from these two’.

text: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from one of his companions who said, ‘Al-Marzabaan asked Al-Reza<sup>asws</sup> about a slaughter by the child before he attains puberty, and a slaughter by the woman. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘There is no problem with a slaughter by the eunuch, and the child, and the woman, when there is desperation to it’.

text: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Muhammad Bin Ismail, from Hanan Bin Sudeyr, from Al Husayn Bin Al Munzar who said, ‘I said to Abu Abdullahasws, ‘We are a people interchanging to the mountains, and the road is remote between us and the mountain, (many) Farsakhs (units of distance). So we buy the flock, and the two (flocks) and the three (flocks), and there happen to be in the flock one thousand five hundred sheep, and one thousand six hundred sheep, and one thousand seven hundred sheep. So one sheep, or two, or three are cut. So we ask the shepherds who come with these about their religion, so they are saying, ‘(They are) Christians’. He (the narrator) said, ‘So I said, ‘What would yourasws say regarding a slaughter by the Jews and the Christians?’ So heasws said: ‘O Husayn! The slaughtered animal by the Naming (Bismillah), and there is no reliability over it except for the People of the Oneness (Twaheed)’.

citation.arabic_text: قُلْتُ لِأَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) إِنَّا قَوْمٌ نَخْتَلِفُ إِلَى الْجَبَلِ وَ الطَّرِيقُ بَعِيدٌ بَيْنَنَا وَ بَيْنَ الْجَبَلِ فَرَاسِخُ فَنَشْتَرِي الْقَطِيعَ وَ الِاثْنَيْنِ وَ الثَّلَاثَةَ وَ يَكُونُ فِي الْقَطِيعِ أَلْفٌ وَ خَمْسُمِائَةِ شَاةٍ وَ أَلْفٌ وَ سِتُّمِائَةِ شَاةٍ وَ أَلْفٌ وَ سَبْعُمِائَةِ شَاةٍ فَتَقَعُ الشَّاةُ وَ الِاثْنَتَانِ وَ الثَّلَاثَةُ فَنَسْأَلُ الرُّعَاةَ الَّذِينَ يَجِيئُونَ بِهَا عَنْ أَدْيَانِهِمْ فَيَقُولُونَ نَصَارَى قَالَ فَقُلْتُ أَيُّ شَيْ‏ءٍ قَوْلُكَ فِي ذَبِيحَةِ الْيَهُودِ وَ النَّصَارَى فَقَالَ يَا حُسَيْنُ الذَّبِيحَةُ بِالِاسْمِ وَ لَا يُؤْمَنُ عَلَيْهَا إِلَّا أَهْلُ التَّوْحِيدِ .

text: And from him, from Hanan who said, ‘I said to Abu Abdullahasws that Al-Husayn Bin Al-Munzar reported from youasws that youasws said that the slaughter is by the Naming (Bismillah), and there is no reliability over it except for its rightful ones’. So heasws said; ‘They are narrating something in it Iasws did not desire it’. text: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Hanan Bin Sudeyr who said, ‘We went over to Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, my father and myself. So we said to him<sup>asws</sup>, ‘May Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Make us to be sacrificed for you<sup>asws</sup>! For us are a mixture of Christians, and we go to them, so they are slaughtering for us the poultry, and the chicken and the goats. Can we eat these?’ So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Do not eat these, and do not go near these, for they are saying upon their slaughters what I<sup>asws</sup> do not like for you all to eat it’. He (the narrator) said, ‘So when we proceeded to Al-Kufa, one of them invited us over, so we refused. So he said, ‘What is the matter with you? You used to come to us then you are leaving it today?’ So we said, ‘A knowledgeable one<sup>asws</sup> of ours has forbidden us, and he<sup>asws</sup> claims that you are saying upon your slaughters something that he<sup>asws</sup> does not like for us to eat it’. So he said, ‘Who is this knowledgeable one<sup>asws</sup>? By Allah<sup>azwj</sup>! He<sup>asws</sup> is the most knowledgeable of the people, and the most knowledgeable one whom Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Created. By Allah<sup>azwj</sup>! He<sup>asws</sup> spoke the truth, we are saying ‘In the name of the Messiah<sup>as</sup>’.

Can we eat these?’ So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Do not eat these, and do not go near these, for they are saying upon their slaughters what I<sup>asws</sup> do not like for you all to eat it’. He (the narrator) said, ‘So when we proceeded to Al-Kufa, one of them invited us over, so we refused. So he said, ‘What is the matter with you? You used to come to us then you are leaving it today?’ So we said, ‘A knowledgeable one<sup>asws</sup> of ours has forbidden us, and he<sup>asws</sup> claims that you are saying upon your slaughters something that he<sup>asws</sup> does not like for us to eat it’. So he said, ‘Who is this knowledgeable one<sup>asws</sup>? By Allah<sup>azwj</sup>! He<sup>asws</sup> is the most knowledgeable of the people, and the most knowledgeable one whom Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Created. By Allah<sup>azwj</sup>! He<sup>asws</sup> spoke the truth, we are saying ‘In the name of the Messiah<sup>as</sup>’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: حسن أو موثق - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (22/27)

text: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from one of our companions who said, ‘I asked Abu Abdullahasws about a slaughter by the People of the Book. So heasws said: ‘By Allahazwj! They are not eating from your slaughters, so how are you permitting yourselves that you eat their slaughters? But rather, it is the naming (Bismillah), and none can be relied over it except for a Muslim’.

citation.arabic_text: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) عَنْ ذَبِيحَةِ أَهْلِ الْكِتَابِ قَالَ فَقَالَ وَ اللَّهِ مَا يَأْكُلُونَ ذَبَائِحَكُمْ فَكَيْفَ تَسْتَحِلُّونَ أَنْ تَأْكُلُوا ذَبَائِحَهُمْ إِنَّمَا هُوَ الِاسْمُ وَ لَا يُؤْمَنُ عَلَيْهَا إِلَّا مُسْلِمٌ .
