So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘They are lying, but the one who does not eat the meat for forty days, his mannerisms would change, and his body (as well), and that is the transference of the seed in a measurement of forty days’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: مجهول - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (2/129)

text: Ali Bin Muhammad Bin Bundar, and someone else, from Ahmad Bin Abu Abdullah, from Muhammad Bin Ali, from Ibn Baqqah, from Al Hakam Bin Ayman, from Abu Asama Zayd Al Shahaam, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘The one to whom forty days come by and he does not eat the meat, so let him borrow upon Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic and let him eat it’.

text: Ali Bin Muhammad, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from one of his companions I think it was Muhammad Bin Ismail, who said, ‘One of us mentioned two (kinds of) meat in the presence of Abu Al-Hassan Al-Reza<sup>asws</sup>, so he said: ‘What meat is better than the meat of the goat?’ He (the narrator) said, ‘So Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> looked at him and said: ‘Had Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic Created a chewy morsel which is better than the lamb, so it would have been sacrificed for Ismail<sup>as</sup>’.

citation.arabic_text: ذَكَرَ بَعْضُنَا اللُّحْمَانَ عِنْدَ أَبِي الْحَسَنِ الرِّضَا ( عليه السلام ) فَقَالَ مَا لَحْمٌ بِأَطْيَبَ مِنْ لَحْمِ الْمَاعِزِ قَالَ فَنَظَرَ إِلَيْهِ أَبُو الْحَسَنِ ( عليه السلام ) وَ قَالَ لَوْ خَلَقَ اللَّهُ عَزَّ وَ جَلَّ مُضْغَةً هِيَ أَطْيَبُ مِنَ الضَّأْنِ لَفَدَى بِهَا إِسْمَاعِيلَ ( عليه السلام ) .

text: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Muhammad Bin Khalid, from Sa’ad Bin Sa’ad who said, ‘I said to Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup>, ‘My family are not eating meat of the goat’. text: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Yahya Bin Al Mubarak, reporting from Abdullah Bin Jabala, from Abu Al Sabbah Al Kinany, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘The broth of the meat of the cow does away with the whiteness (vitiligo)’.

citation.arabic_text: مَرَقُ لَحْمِ الْبَقَرِ يَذْهَبُ بِالْبَيَاضِ .
citation.translation: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Yahya Bin Al Mubarak, reporting from Abdullah Bin Jabala, from Abu Al Sabbah Al Kinany, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘The broth of the meat of the cow does away with the whiteness (vitiligo)’.

text: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Muhammad Bin Khalid, from Abdullah Bin Al Mugheira, from Ismail Bin Abu Ziyad, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘The milk of the cow is a medicine, and its butter is a healing, and its meat is an ailment’.

citation.arabic_text: أَلْبَانُ الْبَقَرِ دَوَاءٌ وَ سُمُونُهَا شِفَاءٌ وَ لُحُومُهَا دَاءٌ .

text: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, form Ali Bin Hassan, from Musa Bin Bakr who said, ‘I heard Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> saying: ‘The meat builds the meat, and the one who enters inside him a morsel of fat, throws out the likes of it from the ailments’.

citation.arabic_text: سَمِعْتُ أَبَا الْحَسَنِ ( عليه السلام ) يَقُولُ اللَّحْمُ يُنْبِتُ اللَّحْمَ وَ مَنْ أَدْخَلَ فِي جَوْفِهِ لُقْمَةَ شَحْمٍ أَخْرَجَتْ مِثْلَهَا مِنَ الدَّاءِ .
citation.translation: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, form Ali Bin Hassan, from Musa Bin Bakr who said, ‘I heard Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> saying: ‘The meat builds the meat, and the one who enters inside him a morsel of fat, throws out the likes of it from the ailments’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: ضعيف على المشهور - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (22/132)

text: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Abu Nasr, from Hammad Bin Usman, from Muhammad Bin Sowqat, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘The one who eats a morsel of fat, throws out the likes of it from the ailments’.

citation.arabic_text: مَنْ أَكَلَ لُقْمَةَ شَحْمٍ أَخْرَجَتْ مِثْلَهَا مِنَ الدَّاءِ .
citation.translation: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Abu Nasr, from Hammad Bin Usman, from Muhammad Bin Sowqat, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘The one who eats a morsel of fat, throws out the likes of it from the ailments’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: حسن - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (22/132)

text: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Abu Abdullah, from one of his companions, having delivered with it by Zurara who said, ‘I said to Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, ‘May I be sacrificed for you<sup>asws</sup>! The fat which throws out the likes of it from the ailments, which fat is it?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘It is fat of the cow, and O Zurara, no one has asked me about it before you’.

citation.arabic_text: قُلْتُ لِأَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) جُعِلْتُ فِدَاكَ الشَّحْمَةُ الَّتِي تُخْرِجُ مِثْلَهَا مِنَ الدَّاءِ أَيُّ شَحْمَةٍ هِيَ قَالَ هِيَ شَحْمَةُ الْبَقَرِ وَ مَا سَأَلَنِي يَا زُرَارَةُ عَنْهَا أَحَدٌ قَبْلَكَ .
citation.translation: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Abu Abdullah, from one of his companions, having delivered with it by Zurara who said, ‘I said to Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, ‘May I be sacrificed for you<sup>asws</sup>! The fat which throws out the likes of it from the ailments, which fat is it?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘It is fat of the cow, and O Zurara, no one has asked me about it before you’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: مرسل - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (2/132)

text: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin ZIyad, from Muhammad Bin Ismail Bin Bazie, from Yahya Bin Masour, (It has been narrated) from Abu Ibrahim<sup>asws</sup> (7th Imam<sup>asws</sup>) having said: ‘Al-Suweyq and the broth of the meat of the cow (beef soup), both do away with (remove) the vitiligo’.

citation.arabic_text: السَّوِيقُ وَ مَرَقُ لَحْمِ الْبَقَرِ يَذْهَبَانِ بِالْوَضَحِ .
citation.translation: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin ZIyad, from Muhammad Bin Ismail Bin Bazie, from Yahya Bin Masour, (It has been narrated) from Abu Ibrahim<sup>asws</sup> (7th Imam<sup>asws</sup>) having said: ‘Al-Suweyq and the broth of the meat of the cow (beef soup), both do away with (remove) the vitiligo’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: مجهول - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (2/132)

text: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Ali Bin Al Hakam, from Dawood Al Raqqy who said, ‘I wrote to Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> asking him<sup>asws</sup> about the meats of the strutting (racing) camels and their milks, so he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘There is no problem with it’.

citation.arabic_text: كَتَبْتُ إِلَى أَبِي الْحَسَنِ ( عليه السلام ) أَسْأَلُهُ عَنْ لُحُومِ الْبُخْتِ وَ أَلْبَانِهِنَّ فَقَالَ لَا بَأْسَ بِهِ .
citation.translation: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Ali Bin Al Hakam, from Dawood Al Raqqy who said, ‘I wrote to Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> asking him<sup>asws</sup> about the meats of the strutting (racing) camels and their milks, so he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘There is no problem with it’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: صحيح على الظاهر - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (22/132)

text: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Al Hassan Bin Ali, from Dawood Al Raqqy who said, ‘I said to Abu Abdullahasws, ‘May I be sacrificed for youasws! A man from the companions of Abu Al-Khattab forbade from eating the strutting (racing) camels, and from eating the meat of Al-Masroula pigeons. So Abu Abdullahasws said: ‘There is no problem with riding the strutting (racing) camels and drinking their milks, and eating the meat of Al-Masroula pigeons’.

citation.arabic_text: قُلْتُ لِأَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) جُعِلْتُ فِدَاكَ إِنَّ رَجُلًا مِنْ أَصْحَابِ أَبِي الْخَطَّابِ نَهَى عَنْ أَكْلِ الْبُخْتِ وَ عَنْ أَكْلِ لُحُومِ الْحَمَامِ الْمُسَرْوَلَةِ فَقَالَ أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) لَا بَأْسَ بِرُكُوبِ الْبُخْتِ وَ شُرْبِ أَلْبَانِهِنَّ وَ أَكْلِ لُحُومِ الْحَمَامِ الْمُسَرْوَلِ .
citation.translation: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Al Hassan Bin Ali, from Dawood Al Raqqy who said, ‘I said to Abu Abdullahasws, ‘May I be sacrificed for youasws! A man from the companions of Abu Al-Khattab forbade from eating the strutting (racing) camels, and from eating the meat of Al-Masroula pigeons. So Abu Abdullahasws said: ‘There is no problem with riding the strutting (racing) camels and drinking their milks, and eating the meat of Al-Masroula pigeons’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: صحيح - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (2/133)

text: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Khalid, from Amro Bin Usman raising it, said, ‘Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The goose is the buffalo of the birds, and the chicken is the pig of the birds, and the pheasant is the turkey of the bird, and where are you from the two rising chicks (such as) raised by a woman from Rabi’a ( a village) by the remains of her livelihood (so eat those)’.

citation.arabic_text: قَالَ أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ ( عليه السلام ) الْإِوَزُّ جَامُوسُ الطَّيْرِ وَ الدَّجَاجُ خِنْزِيرُ الطَّيْرِ وَ الدُّرَّاجُ حَبَشُ الطَّيْرِ وَ أَيْنَ أَنْتَ عَنْ فَرْخَيْنِ نَاهِضَيْنِ رَبَّتْهُمَا امْرَأَةٌ مِنْ رَبِيعَةَ بِفَضْلِ قُوتِهَا .
citation.translation: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Khalid, from Amro Bin Usman raising it, said, ‘Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The goose is the buffalo of the birds, and the chicken is the pig of the birds, and the pheasant is the turkey of the bird, and where are you from the two rising chicks (such as) raised by a woman from Rabi’a ( a village) by the remains of her livelihood (so eat those)’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: مرفوع - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (2/133)

text: From him, from al Sayyari, raising it, said, ‘The two (types of) meat were mentioned in front of Umar, so Umar said, ‘The best of the two meats is the meat of the chicken’. So Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> said; ‘Never! Those (chickens) are the pigs of the birds, but the best of the two meats is the meat of chick that has risen, or near to the rising’.

citation.arabic_text: إِنَّهُ ذُكِرَتِ اللُّحْمَانُ بَيْنَ يَدَيْ عُمَرَ فَقَالَ عُمَرُ إِنَّ أَطْيَبَ اللُّحْمَانِ لَحْمُ الدَّجَاجِ فَقَالَ أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ ( عليه السلام ) كَلَّا إِنَّ ذَلِكَ خَنَازِيرُ الطَّيْرِ وَ إِنَّ أَطْيَبَ اللُّحْمَانِ لَحْمُ فَرْخٍ قَدْ نَهَضَ أَوْ كَادَ أَنْ يَنْهَضَ .
citation.translation: From him, from al Sayyari, raising it, said, ‘The two (types of) meat were mentioned in front of Umar, so Umar said, ‘The best of the two meats is the meat of the chicken’. So Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> said; ‘Never! Those (chickens) are the pigs of the birds, but the best of the two meats is the meat of chick that has risen, or near to the rising’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: ضعيف - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (22/134)

text: Al Sayyari, from the one who reported it, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘The one who is keen to reduce his anger, so let him eat the meat of the pheasant’.

citation.arabic_text: قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ ( صلى الله عليه وآله ) مَنْ سَرَّهُ أَنْ يَقِلَّ غَيْظُهُ فَلْيَأْكُلْ لَحْمَ الدُّرَّاجِ .
citation.translation: Al Sayyari, from the one who reported it, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘The one who is keen to reduce his anger, so let him eat the meat of the pheasant’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: ضعيف - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (22/134)

text: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Muhammad Bin Musa, from Ali Bin Suleyman, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Muhammad Bin Hakeym, (It has been narrated) from Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> the 1st having said: ‘Feed the feverish the meat of الْقِبَاجِ (a type of pheasant), for it strengthens the two legs and repulses the fever with a repelling’.

citation.arabic_text: حَدَّثَنِي عَلِيُّ بْنُ سُلَيْمَانَ عَنِ ابْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ حَكِيمٍ عَنْ أَبِي الْحَسَنِ الْأَوَّلِ ( عليه السلام ) قَالَ أَطْعِمُوا الْمَحْمُومَ لَحْمَ الْقِبَاجِ فَإِنَّهُ يُقَوِّي السَّاقَيْنِ وَ يَطْرُدُ الْحُمَّى طَرْداً .
citation.translation: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Muhammad Bin Musa, from Ali Bin Suleyman, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Muhammad Bin Hakeym, (It has been narrated) from Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> the 1st having said: ‘Feed the feverish the meat of الْقِبَاجِ (a type of pheasant), for it strengthens the two legs and repulses the fever with a repelling’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: مجهول - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (22/134)

text: From him, from Muhammad Bin Isa, from Ali Bin Mahziyar who said, ‘I had lunch with Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup>, so he<sup>asws</sup> came with a sand grouse, so he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘It is Blessed and my<sup>asws</sup> father<sup>asws</sup> was fascinated by it, and he<sup>asws</sup> used to instruct the sufferer of jaundice to be fed with it, grilled for him, so he would benefit by it’.

citation.arabic_text: تَغَدَّيْتُ مَعَ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ ( عليه السلام ) فَأَتَى بِقَطَاةٍ فَقَالَ إِنَّهُ مُبَارَكٌ وَ كَانَ أَبِي ( عليه السلام ) يُعْجِبُهُ وَ كَانَ يَأْمُرُ أَنْ يُطْعَمَ صَاحِبُ الْيَرَقَانِ يُشْوَى لَهُ فَإِنَّهُ يَنْفَعُهُ .
citation.translation: From him, from Muhammad Bin Isa, from Ali Bin Mahziyar who said, ‘I had lunch with Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup>, so he<sup>asws</sup> came with a sand grouse, so he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘It is Blessed and my<sup>asws</sup> father<sup>asws</sup> was fascinated by it, and he<sup>asws</sup> used to instruct the sufferer of jaundice to be fed with it, grilled for him, so he would benefit by it’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: صحيح - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (22/134)

text: From him, from Ali Bin Suleyman, from Marwak Bin Ubeyd, from Basheyt Bin Salih who said, ‘I heard Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> the 1st saying: ‘I<sup>asws</sup> do not see a problem with eating the bustard, and it is very good for the hemorrhoids, and the back pain, and it is from what aids upon the frequency of the copulation’.

citation.arabic_text: سَمِعْتُ أَبَا الْحَسَنِ الْأَوَّلَ ( عليه السلام ) يَقُولُ لَا أَرَى بِأَكْلِ الْحُبَارَى بَأْساً وَ إِنَّهُ جَيِّدٌ لِلْبَوَاسِيرِ وَ وَجَعِ الظَّهْرِ وَ هُوَ مِمَّا يُعِينُ عَلَى كَثْرَةِ الْجِمَاعِ .
citation.translation: From him, from Ali Bin Suleyman, from Marwak Bin Ubeyd, from Basheyt Bin Salih who said, ‘I heard Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> the 1st saying: ‘I<sup>asws</sup> do not see a problem with eating the bustard, and it is very good for the hemorrhoids, and the back pain, and it is from what aids upon the frequency of the copulation’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: مجهول - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (2/135)

text: A number of our companions, form Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Nasr Bin Muhammad who said, ‘I wrote to Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> asking him<sup>asws</sup> about the meats of the wild donkeys (Zebras). So he<sup>asws</sup> wrote: ‘It is allowed to eat it, however, leaving is preferable with me<sup>asws</sup>’.

citation.arabic_text: كَتَبْتُ إِلَى أَبِي الْحَسَنِ ( عليه السلام ) أَسْأَلُهُ عَنْ لُحُومِ حُمُرِ الْوَحْشِ فَكَتَبَ ( عليه السلام ) يَجُوزُ أَكْلُهُ لِوَحْشَتِهِ وَ تَرْكُهُ عِنْدِي أَفْضَلُ .
citation.translation: A number of our companions, form Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Nasr Bin Muhammad who said, ‘I wrote to Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> asking him<sup>asws</sup> about the meats of the wild donkeys (Zebras). So he<sup>asws</sup> wrote: ‘It is allowed to eat it, however, leaving is preferable with me<sup>asws</sup>’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: ضعيف على المشهور - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (2/135)

text: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, and Ali Bin Muhammad, both together from Ali Bin Al Hassan Al Tameemy, from Ayoub Bin Nuh, from Safwan Bin Yahya, from Abdullah Bin Jundab who said, ‘I heard Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> saying: ‘There is no problem with eating the Buffalo meats and drinking their milks, and eating their butter’.

citation.arabic_text: سَمِعْتُ أَبَا الْحَسَنِ ( عليه السلام ) يَقُولُ لَا بَأْسَ بِأَكْلِ لُحُومِ الْجَوَامِيسِ وَ شُرْبِ أَلْبَانِهَا وَ أَكْلِ سُمُونِهَا.
citation.translation: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, and Ali Bin Muhammad, both together from Ali Bin Al Hassan Al Tameemy, from Ayoub Bin Nuh, from Safwan Bin Yahya, from Abdullah Bin Jundab who said, ‘I heard Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> saying: ‘There is no problem with eating the Buffalo meats and drinking their milks, and eating their butter’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: موثق - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (22/136)

text: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Muhammad Bin Al Husay, from Safwan, from Abdullah Bin Jundab who said, ‘I asked Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> about the Buffalo meats and their milks. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘There is no problem with these’.

citation.arabic_text: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا الْحَسَنِ ( عليه السلام ) عَنْ لُحُومِ الْجَوَامِيسِ وَ أَلْبَانِهَا فَقَالَ لَا بَأْسَ بِهِمَا .
citation.translation: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Muhammad Bin Al Husay, from Safwan, from Abdullah Bin Jundab who said, ‘I asked Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> about the Buffalo meats and their milks. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘There is no problem with these’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: صحيح - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (22/136)

text: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad Bin Isa, from Hareyz, from Zurara, (It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> that Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> forbade from eating the tender (raw) meat and said, ‘But rather, it is the wild animals which eat it, but (you can eat it) until after the sun has changed it, or the fire’.

citation.arabic_text: إِنَّمَا تَأْكُلُهُ السِّبَاعُ وَ لَكِنْ حَتَّى تُغَيِّرَهُ الشَّمْسُ أَوِ النَّارُ .
citation.translation: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad Bin Isa, from Hareyz, from Zurara, (It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> that Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> forbade from eating the tender (raw) meat and said, ‘But rather, it is the wild animals which eat it, but (you can eat it) until after the sun has changed it, or the fire’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: حسن - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (2/136)

text: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Al Hakam, from Hisham Bin Salim who said, ‘I asked Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> about eating the raw meat, so he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘This is a food of the wild animals’.

citation.arabic_text: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) عَنْ أَكْلِ لَحْمِ النِّي‏ءِ فَقَالَ هَذَا طَعَامُ السِّبَاعِ .
citation.translation: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Al Hakam, from Hisham Bin Salim who said, ‘I asked Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> about eating the raw meat, so he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘This is a food of the wild animals’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: صحيح - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (2/137)

text: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Biin Isa, from Al Hassan Bin Ali, from Abdul Sammad Bin Basheer, from Atiyya a brother of Abu Al Magra who said, ‘I said to Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup>, ‘The companions of Al-Mugheira are forbidding from eating the Jerk which the fire has not touched’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘There is no problem with eating it’.

citation.arabic_text: قُلْتُ لِأَبِي جَعْفَرٍ ( عليه السلام ) إِنَّ أَصْحَابَ الْمُغِيرَةِ يَنْهَوْنَ عَنْ أَكْلِ الْقَدِيدِ الَّتِي لَمْ تَمَسَّهُ النَّارُ فَقَالَ لَا بَأْسَ بِأَكْلِهِ .
citation.translation: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Biin Isa, from Al Hassan Bin Ali, from Abdul Sammad Bin Basheer, from Atiyya a brother of Abu Al Magra who said, ‘I said to Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup>, ‘The companions of Al-Mugheira are forbidding from eating the Jerk which the fire has not touched’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘There is no problem with eating it’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: مجهول - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (22/137)

text: From him, (It has been narrated) raising it from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, said, ‘I said to him<sup>asws</sup>, ‘The meat (which is) dried and the salt is sprinkled upon it, and dried in the shade’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘There is no problem with eating it because the salt has changed it’.

citation.arabic_text: قُلْتُ لَهُ إِنَّ اللَّحْمَ يُقَدَّدُ وَ يُذَرُّ عَلَيْهِ الْمِلْحُ وَ يُجَفَّفُ فِي الظِّلِّ فَقَالَ لَا بَأْسَ بِأَكْلِهِ لِأَنَّ الْمِلْحَ قَدْ غَيَّرَهُ .
citation.translation: From him, (It has been narrated) raising it from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, said, ‘I said to him<sup>asws</sup>, ‘The meat (which is) dried and the salt is sprinkled upon it, and dried in the shade’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘There is no problem with eating it because the salt has changed it’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: مرفوع - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (2/137)

text: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Musa Bin Al Hassan, from Muhammad Bin Isa, (It has been narrated) from Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> the 3rd, said, ‘He<sup>asws</sup> used to say: ‘I<sup>asws</sup> have not eaten a foodstuff which is more remaining nor more stirring for the illnesses than the dried meat, meaning the Jerk’.

citation.arabic_text: كَانَ يَقُولُ مَا أَكَلْتُ طَعَاماً أَبْقَى وَ لَا أَهْيَجَ لِلدَّاءِ مِنَ اللَّحْمِ الْيَابِسِ يَعْنِي الْقَدِيدَ .
citation.translation: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Musa Bin Al Hassan, from Muhammad Bin Isa, (It has been narrated) from Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> the 3rd, said, ‘He<sup>asws</sup> used to say: ‘I<sup>asws</sup> have not eaten a foodstuff which is more remaining nor more stirring for the illnesses than the dried meat, meaning the Jerk’.

text: From him, (It has been narrated) from Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘The Jerk is an evil meat because it relaxes in the stomach and agitates every illness, and it does no benefit anything, but it harms’.

citation.arabic_text: الْقَدِيدُ لَحْمُ سَوْءٍ لِأَنَّهُ يَسْتَرْخِي فِي الْمَعِدَةِ وَ يُهَيِّجُ كُلَّ دَاءٍ وَ لَا يَنْفَعُ مِنْ شَيْ‏ءٍ بَلْ يَضُرُّهُ .
citation.translation: From him, (It has been narrated) from Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘The Jerk is an evil meat because it relaxes in the stomach and agitates every illness, and it does no benefit anything, but it harms’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: صحيح على الظاهر - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (2/138)

text: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Khalid, from one of his companions, raising it, said, ‘Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Two things are corrective, either of which does not enter the inside at all as spoilt except that it corrects it, and two things are both spoilers, they do not enter inside at all as correct, except that they spoil it. The two correctives are the pomegranate and the luke-warm water, and the two spoilers are the cheese and the Jerk (dried meat)’.

citation.arabic_text: قَالَ أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) شَيْئَانِ صَالِحَانِ لَمْ يَدْخُلَا جَوْفَ وَاحِدٍ قَطُّ فَاسِداً إِلَّا أَصْلَحَاهُ وَ شَيْئَانِ فَاسِدَانِ لَمْ يَدْخُلَا جَوْفاً قَطُّ صَالِحاً إِلَّا أَفْسَدَاهُ فَالصَّالِحَانِ الرُّمَّانُ وَ الْمَاءُ الْفَاتِرُ وَ الْفَاسِدَانِ الْجُبُنُّ وَ الْقَدِيدُ .
citation.translation: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Khalid, from one of his companions, raising it, said, ‘Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Two things are corrective, either of which does not enter the inside at all as spoilt except that it corrects it, and two things are both spoilers, they do not enter inside at all as correct, except that they spoil it. text: He (the narrator) said, ‘ And it has been reported from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Three (things) demolish the body, and perhaps may even kill – Eating the Jerk of the forest, and entering the bathroom upon the (full) belly, and marrying the old women’. He (the narrator) said, ‘And Abu Is’haq Al-Nahawandy has increased in it: ‘And copulating with the women upon the filled (belly)’.

citation.arabic_text: ثَلَاثَةٌ يَهْدِمْنَ الْبَدَنَ وَ رُبَّمَا قَتَلْنَ أَكْلُ الْقَدِيدِ الْغَابِّ وَ دُخُولُ الْحَمَّامِ عَلَى الْبِطْنَةِ وَ نِكَاحُ الْعَجَائِزِ قَالَ وَ زَادَ فِيهِ أَبُو إِسْحَاقَ النَّهَاوَنْدِيُّ وَ غِشْيَانُ النِّسَاءِ عَلَى الِامْتِلَاءِ .
citation.translation: He (the narrator) said, ‘ And it has been reported from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Three (things) demolish the body, and perhaps may even kill – Eating the Jerk of the forest, and entering the bathroom upon the (full) belly, and marrying the old women’. He (the narrator) said, ‘And Abu Is’haq Al-Nahawandy has increased in it: ‘And copulating with the women upon the filled (belly)’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: مرسل - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (22/138)

text: From him, from one of our companions, raising it, said, ‘Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Three things which are nor eaten and these fatten, and three are eaten and these slim (the body), and two benefit from every things and do not harm from anything, and two harm from everything and do not benefit from anything. So as for those which are not eaten and these fatten are the linen, and the perfume, and the Noura (Lime-wax); and as for those which are eaten and they slim (the body), so these are the dried meat, and the cheese, and the spadix’ – and in another Hadeeth: ‘The Prairie moon (a herb), and oil-cake; and the two which benefit from everything and do not harm from anything the luke-warm water and the pomegranate; and those two which harm from everything and do not benefit from everything, so it is the dried meat, and the cheese’. I said, ‘May I be sacrificed for you<sup>asws</sup>! Then you<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘They slimmen (the body)’, and over here they are both harmful’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘But do you not know that the slimming is from the harmful?’

citation.arabic_text: قَالَ أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) ثَلَاثٌ لَا يُؤْكَلْنَ وَ هُنَّ يُسْمِنَّ وَ ثَلَاثٌ يُؤْكَلْنَ وَ هُنَّ يَهْزِلْنَ وَ اثْنَانِ يَنْفَعَانِ مِنْ كُلِّ شَيْ‏ءٍ وَ لَا يَضُرَّانِ مِنْ شَيْ‏ءٍ وَ اثْنَانِ يَضُرَّانِ مِنْ كُلِّ شَيْ‏ءٍ وَ لَا يَنْفَعَانِ مِنْ شَيْ‏ءٍ فَأَمَّا اللَّوَاتِي لَا يُؤْكَلْنَ وَ يُسْمِنَّ اسْتِشْعَارُ الْكَتَّانِ وَ الطِّيبُ وَ النُّورَةُ وَ أَمَّا اللَّوَاتِي يُؤْكَلْنَ وَ يَهْزِلْنَ فَهُوَ اللَّحْمُ الْيَابِسُ وَ الْجُبُنُّ وَ الطَّلْعُ وَ فِي حَدِيثٍ آخَرَ الْجَرَزُ وَ الْكُسْبُ وَ اللَّذَانِ يَنْفَعَانِ مِنْ كُلِّ شَيْ‏ءٍ وَ لَا يَضُرَّانِ مِنْ شَيْ‏ءٍ فَالْمَاءُ الْفَاتِرُ وَ الرُّمَّانُ وَ اللَّذَانِ يَضُرَّانِ مِنْ كُلِّ شَيْ‏ءٍ وَ لَا يَنْفَعَانِ مِنْ شَيْ‏ءٍ فَاللَّحْمُ الْيَابِسُ وَ الْجُبُنُّ قُلْتُ جُعِلْتُ فِدَاكَ ثَمَّ قُلْتَ يَهْزِلْنَ وَ قُلْتَ هَاهُنَا يَضُرَّانِ فَقَالَ أَ مَا عَلِمْتَ أَنَّ الْهُزَالَ مِنَ الْمَضَرَّةِ .
citation.translation: From him, from one of our companions, raising it, said, ‘Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Three things which are nor eaten and these fatten, and three are eaten and these slim (the body), and two benefit from every things and do not harm from anything, and two harm from everything and do not benefit from anything. So as for those which are not eaten and these fatten are the linen, and the perfume, and the Noura (Lime-wax); and as for those which are eaten and they slim (the body), so these are the dried meat, and the cheese, and the spadix’ – and in another Hadeeth: ‘The Prairie moon (a herb), and oil-cake; and the two which benefit from everything and do not harm from anything the luke-warm water and the pomegranate; and those two which harm from everything and do not benefit from everything, so it is the dried meat, and the cheese’. I said, ‘May I be sacrificed for you<sup>asws</sup>! Then you<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘They slimmen (the body)’, and over here they are both harmful’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘But do you not know that the slimming is from the harmful?’

text: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Al Rayyan, raising it, said, ‘I said to Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, ‘Why did Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> used to the love the arm more than his<sup>saww</sup> love for the rest of the body parts of the sheep?’ So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Because Adam<sup>as</sup> offered an offering on behalf of the Prophets<sup>as</sup> from his<sup>as</sup> offspring, so he<sup>as</sup> named a part for each Prophet<sup>as</sup> from his<sup>as</sup> offspring, and named the arm for Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup>. So from then, he<sup>saww</sup> used to love it, and was desiring it, and preferring it’.

citation.translation: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Al Rayyan, raising it, said, ‘I said to Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, ‘Why did Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> used to the love the arm more than his<sup>saww</sup> love for the rest of the body parts of the sheep?’ So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Because Adam<sup>as</sup> offered an offering on behalf of the Prophets<sup>as</sup> from his<sup>as</sup> offspring, so he<sup>as</sup> named a part for each Prophet<sup>as</sup> from his<sup>as</sup> offspring, and named the arm for Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup>. So from then, he<sup>saww</sup> used to love it, and was desiring it, and preferring it’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: مرفوع - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (22/139)

text: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ibn Bukeyr, from Zurara, (It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘The arm (of the sheep) was liked by Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup>’.

citation.arabic_text: كَانَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ ( صلى الله عليه وآله ) يُعْجِبُهُ الذِّرَاعُ .
citation.translation: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ibn Bukeyr, from Zurara, (It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘The arm (of the sheep) was liked by Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup>’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: موثق - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (22/139)

text: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Ja’far Bin Muhammad Al Ash’ary, from Ibn Al Qaddah, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘The Jewish woman poisoned the Prophet<sup>saww</sup> in an arm (of the sheep), and the Prophet<sup>saww</sup> used to love the arm, and the shoulder, and he<sup>saww</sup> disliked the hip due to its proximity to the urinating part’.

citation.arabic_text: سَمَّتِ الْيَهُودِيَّةُ النَّبِيَّ ( صلى الله عليه وآله ) فِي ذِرَاعٍ وَ كَانَ النَّبِيُّ ( صلى الله عليه وآله ) يُحِبُّ الذِّرَاعَ وَ الْكَتِفَ وَ يَكْرَهُ الْوَرِكَ لِقُرْبِهَا مِنَ الْمَبَالِ .
citation.translation: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Ja’far Bin Muhammad Al Ash’ary, from Ibn Al Qaddah, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘The Jewish woman poisoned the Prophet<sup>saww</sup> in an arm (of the sheep), and the Prophet<sup>saww</sup> used to love the arm, and the shoulder, and he<sup>saww</sup> disliked the hip due to its proximity to the urinating part’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: ضعيف على المشهور - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (2/139)

text: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hisham Bin Salim, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘The meat with the milk is the gravy of the Prophets<sup>as</sup>’.

citation.arabic_text: اللَّحْمُ بِاللَّبَنِ مَرَقُ الْأَنْبِيَاءِ ( عليهم السلام ) .
citation.translation: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hisham Bin Salim, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘The meat with the milk is the gravy of the Prophets<sup>as</sup>’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: حسن - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (22/139)

text: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Al Wasim Bin Yahya, from his grandfather Al Hassan Bin Rashid, from Muhammad Bin Muslim, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘When a Muslim is weak, so let him eat the meat with the milk’.

citation.arabic_text: قَالَ أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ ( عليه السلام ) إِذَا ضَعُفَ الْمُسْلِمُ فَلْيَأْكُلِ اللَّحْمَ بِاللَّبَنِ .
citation.translation: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Al Wasim Bin Yahya, from his grandfather Al Hassan Bin Rashid, from Muhammad Bin Muslim, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘When a Muslim is weak, so let him eat the meat with the milk’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: ضعيف - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (2/139)

text: Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Muhammad Bin Sinan, from Ziyad Bin Abu Al Hallal who said, ‘I had dinner with Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> by meat with milk, so he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘This is the gravy of the Prophets<sup>as</sup>’.

citation.arabic_text: تَعَشَّيْتُ مَعَ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) بِلَحْمٍ بِلَبَنٍ فَقَالَ هَذَا مَرَقُ الْأَنْبِيَاءِ ( عليهم السلام ) .
citation.translation: Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Muhammad Bin Sinan, from Ziyad Bin Abu Al Hallal who said, ‘I had dinner with Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> by meat with milk, so he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘This is the gravy of the Prophets<sup>as</sup>’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: ضعيف على المشهور - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (22/139)

text: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Abu Abdullah, from Muhammad Bin Isa, from Ubeydullah Bin Abdullah Al Dahqan, from Dorost, from Abdullah Bin Sinan, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘A Prophet<sup>as</sup> from the Prophets<sup>as</sup> complained to Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic of the weakness, so it was Said to him: “Cook the meat with the milk, for these two strengthen the body”. So I said, ‘It is Al-Muzeyra’. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘No, but the meat with the yoghurt milk’.

citation.arabic_text: شَكَا نَبِيٌّ مِنَ الْأَنْبِيَاءِ إِلَى اللَّهِ عَزَّ وَ جَلَّ الضَّعْفَ فَقِيلَ لَهُ اطْبُخِ اللَّحْمَ بِاللَّبَنِ فَإِنَّهُمَا يَشُدَّانِ الْجِسْمَ قَالَ فَقُلْتُ هِيَ الْمَضِيرَةُ قَالَ لَا وَ لَكِنِ اللَّحْمُ بِاللَّبَنِ الْحَلِيبِ .
citation.translation: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Abu Abdullah, from Muhammad Bin Isa, from Ubeydullah Bin Abdullah Al Dahqan, from Dorost, from Abdullah Bin Sinan, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘A Prophet<sup>as</sup> from the Prophets<sup>as</sup> complained to Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic of the weakness, so it was Said to him: “Cook the meat with the milk, for these two strengthen the body”. So I said, ‘It is Al-Muzeyra’. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘No, but the meat with the yoghurt milk’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: ضعيف - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (2/140)

text: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Muhammad Bin Al Waleed, from Yunus Bin Yaqoub who said, ‘The most beloved of the food to Rasool-Allahsaww was Al-Narbaja (Pomegranate gravy)’.

citation.arabic_text: إِنَّ أَحَبَّ الطَّعَامِ كَانَ إِلَى رَسُولِ اللَّهِ ( صلى الله عليه وآله ) النَّارْبَاجَةُ .
citation.translation: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Muhammad Bin Al Waleed, from Yunus Bin Yaqoub who said, ‘The most beloved of the food to Rasool-Allahsaww was Al-Narbaja (Pomegranate gravy)’.

text: Muhammad Bin Al Waleed, from Yunus Bin Yaqoub who said, ‘I sent a basket to Abu Abdullahasws and in it was Narbaja. So heasws ate from it and said: ‘Withhold the remainder of it for me, so bring it to me twice or three (times)’. Then the slave put water in it, and came up with it. So heasws said to him: ‘Woe be unto you! You have spoilt it for me’.

citation.arabic_text: أَرْسَلْتُ إِلَى أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) بِقُدَيْرَةٍ فِيهَا نَارْبَاجُ فَأَكَلَ مِنْهَا وَ قَالَ احْبِسُوا بَقِيَّتَهَا عَلَيَّ فَأُتِيَ بِهَا مَرَّتَيْنِ أَوْ ثَلَاثاً ثُمَّ إِنَّ الْغُلَامَ صَبَّ فِيهَا مَاءً فَأَتَاهُ بِهَا فَقَالَ لَهُ وَيْحَكَ أَفْسَدْتَهَا عَلَيَّ .

text: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Muhammad Bin Khalid, from Al Nazar Bin Suweyd, from Abu Baseer who said, ‘Abu Abdullahasws liked Al-Zabibiyya’ - (A sweet dish of raisins, and walnuts etc.).

citation.arabic_text: كَانَ أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) تُعْجِبُهُ الزَّبِيبِيَّةُ .

text: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Al Nowfaly, from Al Sakuny, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> the varieties (of food) enlarges the belly, and numbs the buttocks’.

citation.arabic_text: قَالَ أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ ( عليه السلام ) الْأَلْوَانُ يُعَظِّمْنَ الْبَطْنَ وَ يُخَدِّرْنَ الْأَلْيَتَيْنِ .
citation.translation: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Al Nowfaly, from Al Sakuny, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> the varieties (of food) enlarges the belly, and numbs the buttocks’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: ضعيف على المشهور - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (22/141)

text: Ali Bin Muhammad Bin Bundar, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, form Mansour Bin Al Abbas, from Suleyman Bin Rusheyd, from his father, from Al Mufazzal Bin Umar who said, ‘I ate in the presence of Abu Abdullahasws, so heasws came with a variety (of foods), so heasws said: ‘Eat from these, but as for myselfasws, so there is nothing more beloved to measws that Al-Sareyd, but it would have been good if Al-Asfanjaat (A spinach dish which tends to reduce appetite)’.

citation.arabic_text: أَكَلْتُ عِنْدَ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) فَأُتِيَ بِلَوْنٍ فَقَالَ كُلْ مِنْ هَذَا فَأَمَّا أَنَا فَمَا شَيْ‏ءٌ أَحَبَّ إِلَيَّ مِنَ الثَّرِيدِ وَ لَوَدِدْتُ أَنَّ الْإِسْفَانَاجَاتِ حُرِّمَتْ .
citation.translation: Ali Bin Muhammad Bin Bundar, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, form Mansour Bin Al Abbas, from Suleyman Bin Rusheyd, from his father, from Al Mufazzal Bin Umar who said, ‘I ate in the presence of Abu Abdullahasws, so heasws came with a variety (of foods), so heasws said: ‘Eat from these, but as for myselfasws, so there is nothing more beloved to measws that Al-Sareyd, but it would have been good if Al-Asfanjaat (A spinach dish which tends to reduce appetite)’.

text: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Al Nowfaly, from Al Sakuny, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws having said: ‘The Prophetsaww said: ‘The first one to variegate the goods was Ibrahimas, and the first one to soften Al-Sareyd was Hashimas’.

citation.arabic_text: قَالَ النَّبِيُّ ( صلى الله عليه وآله ) أَوَّلُ مَنْ لَوَّنَ إِبْرَاهِيمُ ( عليه السلام ) وَ أَوَّلُ مَنْ هَشَمَ الثَّرِيدَ هَاشِمٌ .
citation.translation: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Al Nowfaly, from Al Sakuny, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws having said: ‘The Prophetsaww said: ‘The first one to variegate the goods was Ibrahimas, and the first one to soften Al-Sareyd was Hashimas’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: ضعيف على المشهور - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (22/142)

text: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Ja’far Bin Muhammad Al Ash’ary, from Ibn Al Qaddah, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws having said: ‘The Prophetsaww said: ‘O Allahazwj! Bless for mysaww community regarding Al-Sard and Al-Sareyd’. Ja’far (the narrator) said, ‘Al-Sard is what is small, and Al-Sareyd is what is big’.

citation.arabic_text: قَالَ النَّبِيُّ ( صلى الله عليه وآله ) اللَّهُمَّ بَارِكْ لِأُمَّتِي فِي الثَّرْدِ وَ الثَّرِيدِ قَالَ جَعْفَرٌ الثَّرْدُ مَا صَغُرَ وَ الثَّرِيدُ مَا كَبُرَ .
citation.translation: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Ja’far Bin Muhammad Al Ash’ary, from Ibn Al Qaddah, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws having said: ‘The Prophetsaww said: ‘O Allahazwj! Bless for mysaww community regarding Al-Sard and Al-Sareyd’. Ja’far (the narrator) said, ‘Al-Sard is what is small, and Al-Sareyd is what is big’.

text: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Al Nowfaly, from Al Sakuny, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws having said: ‘Al-Sareyd is the food of the Arabs’.

citation.arabic_text: الثَّرِيدُ طَعَامُ الْعَرَبِ .
citation.translation: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Al Nowfaly, from Al Sakuny, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws having said: ‘Al-Sareyd is the food of the Arabs’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: ضعيف على المشهور - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (2/142)

text: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hisham Bin Salim, from Salma Bin Muhraz who said, ‘Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said to me: ‘It is upon with (eating of) Al-Sareyd, for I<sup>asws</sup> did not find anything more suitable than it’.

citation.arabic_text: قَالَ لِي أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) عَلَيْكَ بِالثَّرِيدِ فَإِنِّي لَمْ أَجِدْ شَيْئاً أَوْفَقَ مِنْهُ .
citation.translation: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hisham Bin Salim, from Salma Bin Muhraz who said, ‘Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said to me: ‘It is upon with (eating of) Al-Sareyd, for I<sup>asws</sup> did not find anything more suitable than it’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: حسن - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (22/143)

text: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Al Hakam, from Muawiya Bin Wahab, from Abu Asama Zayd Al Shahham who said, ‘I went over to my Masterasws Abu Abdullahasws, and heasws was eating Sikbaja (a rice dish with vegetables & vinegar) with the cow meat (beef)’.

citation.arabic_text: دَخَلْتُ عَلَى سَيِّدِي أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) وَ هُوَ يَأْكُلُ سِكْبَاجاً بِلَحْمِ الْبَقَرِ .
citation.translation: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Al Hakam, from Muawiya Bin Wahab, from Abu Asama Zayd Al Shahham who said, ‘I went over to my Masterasws Abu Abdullahasws, and heasws was eating Sikbaja (a rice dish with vegetables & vinegar) with the cow meat (beef)’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: صحيح - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (2/143)

text: Ali Bin Muhammad Bin Bundar, from Ahmad Bin Abu Abdullah, from his father, from Sa’adan Bin Muslim, from Ismail Bin Jabir who said, ‘I was in the presence of Abu Abdullahasws, so heasws called for the meal, so they came with Sareyd, and meat, and heasws called for oil and sprinkled it upon the meat, so I ate from it’.

citation.arabic_text: كُنْتُ عِنْدَ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) فَدَعَا بِالْمَائِدَةِ فَأُتِيَ بِثَرِيدٍ وَ لَحْمٍ وَ دَعَا بِزَيْتٍ وَ صَبَّهُ عَلَى اللَّحْمِ فَأَكَلْتُ مَعَهُ .
citation.translation: Ali Bin Muhammad Bin Bundar, from Ahmad Bin Abu Abdullah, from his father, from Sa’adan Bin Muslim, from Ismail Bin Jabir who said, ‘I was in the presence of Abu Abdullahasws, so heasws called for the meal, so they came with Sareyd, and meat, and heasws called for oil and sprinkled it upon the meat, so I ate from it’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: مجهول وآخره مرفوع - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (2/143)

text: And one of our companions reported it, raising it, said, ‘The Prophetsaww said: ‘Al-Sareyd is Blessed’.

citation.arabic_text: قَالَ النَّبِيُّ ( صلى الله عليه وآله ) الثَّرِيدُ بَرَكَةٌ .
citation.translation: And one of our companions reported it, raising it, said, ‘The Prophetsaww said: ‘Al-Sareyd is Blessed’.

text: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Gayas Bin Ibrahim, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws having said: ‘Amir Al-Momineenasws said: ‘Do not eat from the top of Al-Sareyd, and eat from its sides, for the fennel seeds are in its top’.

citation.arabic_text: قَالَ أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ ( عليه السلام ) لَا تَأْكُلُوا مِنْ رَأْسِ الثَّرِيدِ وَ كُلُوا مِنْ جَوَانِبِهِ فَإِنَّ الْبَرَكَةَ فِي رَأْسِهِ .
citation.translation: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Gayas Bin Ibrahim, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws having said: ‘Amir Al-Momineenasws said: ‘Do not eat from the top of Al-Sareyd, and eat from its sides, for the fennel seeds are in its top’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: موثق - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (2/143)

text: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Muhammad Bin Isa, from Umayya Bin Amro, from Al Shaeeri, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws having said: ‘Extinguish the fires of the grudges with the meat and Al-Sareyd’.

citation.arabic_text: أَطْفِئُوا نَائِرَةَ الضَّغَائِنِ بِاللَّحْمِ وَ الثَّرِيدِ .
citation.translation: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Muhammad Bin Isa, from Umayya Bin Amro, from Al Shaeeri, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws having said: ‘Extinguish the fires of the grudges with the meat and Al-Sareyd’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: ضعيف - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (22/143)

text: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Muhammad Bin Al Hassan, from Musa Bin Umar, from Ja’far Bin Basheer, from Ibrahim Bin Mihzam, from Abu Maryam, from Al Asbagh Bin Nubata who said, ‘I went over to Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> and in front of him<sup>asws</sup> was grill, so he<sup>asws</sup> said to me: ‘Approach, so eat’. So I said, ‘O Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup>! This is harmful to me’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said to me: ‘Approach. I<sup>asws</sup> will teach you such words that nothing would harm you with these, from what you fear. Say, ‘In the Name of Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, filling the earth and the sky, the Beneficent, the Merciful, there does not harm with His<sup>azwj</sup> Name, anything, nor an illness’. Have lunch with us<sup>asws</sup>’.

citation.arabic_text: دَخَلْتُ عَلَى أَمِيرِ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ ( عليه السلام ) وَ بَيْنَ يَدَيْهِ شِوَاءٌ فَقَالَ لِي ادْنُ فَكُلْ فَقُلْتُ يَا أَمِيرَ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ هَذَا لِي ضَارٌّ فَقَالَ لِي ادْنُ أُعَلِّمُكَ كَلِمَاتٍ لَا يَضُرُّكَ مَعَهُنَّ شَيْ‏ءٌ مِمَّا تَخَافُ قُلْ بِسْمِ اللَّهِ خَيْرِ الْأَسْمَاءِ مِلْ‏ءَ الْأَرْضِ وَ السَّمَاءِ الرَّحْمَنِ الرَّحِيمِ الَّذِي لَا يَضُرُّ مَعَ اسْمِهِ شَيْ‏ءٌ وَ لَا دَاءٌ تَغَدَّ مَعَنَا . ’بِسْمِ اللَّهِ خَيْرِ الْأَسْمَاءِ مِلْ‏ءَ الْأَرْضِ وَ السَّمَاءِ الرَّحْمَنِ الرَّحِيمِ الَّذِي لَا يَضُرُّ مَعَ اسْمِهِ شَيْ‏ءٌ وَ لَا دَاءٌ ‘
citation.translation: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Muhammad Bin Al Hassan, from Musa Bin Umar, from Ja’far Bin Basheer, from Ibrahim Bin Mihzam, from Abu Maryam, from Al Asbagh Bin Nubata who said, ‘I went over to Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> and in front of him<sup>asws</sup> was grill, so he<sup>asws</sup> said to me: ‘Approach, so eat’. So I said, ‘O Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup>! This is harmful to me’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said to me: ‘Approach. citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: مجهول - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (22/144)

text: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Ali Bin Hassan, from Musa Bin Bakr who said, ‘I complained at Al-Medina of the weakness, so I went over to Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup>. So he<sup>asws</sup> said to me: ‘I<sup>asws</sup> see you are weak’. I said, ‘Yes’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said to me: ‘Eat the Kabab (roast)’. So I ate it, and I was cured’.

citation.arabic_text: لِي أَرَاكَ ضَعِيفاً قُلْتُ نَعَمْ فَقَالَ لِي كُلِ الْكَبَابَ فَأَكَلْتُهُ فَبَرَأْتُ .
citation.translation: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Ali Bin Hassan, from Musa Bin Bakr who said, ‘I complained at Al-Medina of the weakness, so I went over to Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup>. So he<sup>asws</sup> said to me: ‘I<sup>asws</sup> see you are weak’. I said, ‘Yes’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said to me: ‘Eat the Kabab (roast)’. So I ate it, and I was cured’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: ضعيف على المشهور - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (22/144)

text: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Muhammad Bin Sinan, from Musa Bin Bakr who said, ‘Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup>, meaning the 1st, said to me: ‘What is the matter I<sup>asws</sup> see you as pale?’ So I said to him<sup>asws</sup>, ‘Pain has struck me’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said to me: ‘Eat the meat’. So I ate it. Then he<sup>asws</sup> saw me after the Friday, and I was (still) upon my pale state, so he<sup>asws</sup> said to me: ‘Did I<sup>asws</sup> not order you with eating the meat?’ I said, ‘I have not eaten anything else since you<sup>asws</sup> ordered me’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘And how did you eat it?’ I said, ‘Cooked’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘No, eat it as Kabab (roast)’. So I ate it. Then he<sup>asws</sup> sent a message to me, so he<sup>asws</sup> called me over after Friday, and the blood had returned in my face. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Now, yes!’

So he<sup>asws</sup> said to me: ‘Eat the meat’. So I ate it. Then he<sup>asws</sup> saw me after the Friday, and I was (still) upon my pale state, so he<sup>asws</sup> said to me: ‘Did I<sup>asws</sup> not order you with eating the meat?’ I said, ‘I have not eaten anything else since you<sup>asws</sup> ordered me’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘And how did you eat it?’ I said, ‘Cooked’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘No, eat it as Kabab (roast)’. So I ate it. Then he<sup>asws</sup> sent a message to me, so he<sup>asws</sup> called me over after Friday, and the blood had returned in my face. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Now, yes!’
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: ضعيف على المشهور - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (22/144)

text: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Abu Nasr, from Abdullah Bin Muhammad Al Shamy, from Husayn Bin hanzala, (It has been narrated) from one of the two (5th or 6th Imam<sup>asws</sup>) having said: ‘Eat the Kabab (roast), it does away with (removes) the fever’.

citation.arabic_text: أَكْلُ الْكَبَابِ يَذْهَبُ بِالْحُمَّى .
citation.translation: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Abu Nasr, from Abdullah Bin Muhammad Al Shamy, from Husayn Bin hanzala, (It has been narrated) from one of the two (5th or 6th Imam<sup>asws</sup>) having said: ‘Eat the Kabab (roast), it does away with (removes) the fever’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: ضعيف - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (2/144)

text: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Abu Abdullah, from Ali Bin Rayyan Bin Al Salt, from Ubeydullah Bin Abdullah Al Wasity, from Wasil Bin Suleyman, from Dorost, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘We mentioned the head from the sheep, so he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The head are a place of slaughter, and the nearest from the pasture and remote from the harm’.

citation.arabic_text: ذَكَرْنَا الرُّءُوسَ مِنَ الشَّاةِ فَقَالَ الرَّأْسُ مَوْضِعُ الذَّكَاةِ وَ أَقْرَبُ مِنَ الْمَرْعَى وَ أَبْعَدُ مِنَ الْأَذَى .
citation.translation: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Abu Abdullah, from Ali Bin Rayyan Bin Al Salt, from Ubeydullah Bin Abdullah Al Wasity, from Wasil Bin Suleyman, from Dorost, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘We mentioned the head from the sheep, so he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The head are a place of slaughter, and the nearest from the pasture and remote from the harm’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: ضعيف - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (22/145)

text: Al Husayn Bin Muhammad, from Moala Bin Muhammad, from Bistam Bin Murra Al Farsy, from Abdul Rahman Bin Yazeed al Farsy, from Muhammad Bin Marouf, from Salih Bin Razeyn, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws having said: ‘Amir Al-Momineenasws said: ‘It is upon you with (eating) Al-Hareys, for it invigorates for the worship for forty days, and it is from the foods which descended upon Rasool-Allahsaww’.

citation.arabic_text: حَدَّثَنَا عَبْدُ الرَّحْمَنِ بْنُ يَزِيدَ الْفَارِسِيُّ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ مَعْرُوفٍ عَنْ صَالِحِ بْنِ رَزِينٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) قَالَ قَالَ أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ ( عليه السلام ) عَلَيْكُمْ بِالْهَرِيسَةِ فَإِنَّهَا تُنْشِطُ لِلْعِبَادَةِ أَرْبَعِينَ يَوْماً وَ هِيَ مِنَ الْمَائِدَةِ الَّتِي أُنْزِلَتْ عَلَى رَسُولِ اللَّهِ ( صلى الله عليه وآله ) .
citation.translation: Al Husayn Bin Muhammad, from Moala Bin Muhammad, from Bistam Bin Murra Al Farsy, from Abdul Rahman Bin Yazeed al Farsy, from Muhammad Bin Marouf, from Salih Bin Razeyn, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws having said: ‘Amir Al-Momineenasws said: ‘It is upon you with (eating) Al-Hareys, for it invigorates for the worship for forty days, and it is from the foods which descended upon Rasool-Allahsaww’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: ضعيف على المشهور - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (2/145)

text: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Khalid, from Muhammad Bin Isa, from Al Dahqan, from Dorost Bin Abu Mansour, (It has been narrated) from Abdullah Bin Sinan, from Abu Abdullahasws having said: ‘A Prophetas from the Prophetsas complained to Allahazwj Mighty and Majestic of the weakness and the infrequent copulation, so Heazwj Commanded himas with the eating of Al-Hareys’.

citation.arabic_text: إِنَّ نَبِيّاً مِنَ الْأَنْبِيَاءِ شَكَا إِلَى اللَّهِ عَزَّ وَ جَلَّ الضَّعْفَ وَ قِلَّةَ الْجِمَاعِ فَأَمَرَهُ بِأَكْلِ الْهَرِيسَةِ .
citation.translation: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Khalid, from Muhammad Bin Isa, from Al Dahqan, from Dorost Bin Abu Mansour, (It has been narrated) from Abdullah Bin Sinan, from Abu Abdullahasws having said: ‘A Prophetas from the Prophetsas complained to Allahazwj Mighty and Majestic of the weakness and the infrequent copulation, so Heazwj Commanded himas with the eating of Al-Hareys’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: ضعيف وآخره مرفوع - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (22/145)

text: And in another Hadeeth, (It has been narrated) raising it to Abu Abdullahasws having said that Rasool-Allahsaww complained to hissaww Lordazwj Mighty and Majestic of the back pain, so Heazwj Commanded him with the eating of the grains with the meat, meaning Al-Hareys’.

citation.arabic_text: وَ فِي حَدِيثٍ آخَرَ رَفَعَهُ إِلَى أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) قَالَ إِنَّ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ ( صلى الله عليه وآله ) شَكَا إِلَى رَبِّهِ عَزَّ وَ جَلَّ وَجَعَ الظَّهْرِ فَأَمَرَهُ بِأَكْلِ الْحَبِّ بِاللَّحْمِ يَعْنِي الْهَرِيسَةَ .
citation.translation: And in another Hadeeth, (It has been narrated) raising it to Abu Abdullahasws having said that Rasool-Allahsaww complained to hissaww Lordazwj Mighty and Majestic of the back pain, so Heazwj Commanded him with the eating of the grains with the meat, meaning Al-Hareys’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: ضعيف على المشهور - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (2/145)

text: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Muhammad Bin Isnan, from Mansour Al Sayqal, from his father, from Abu Baseer, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws having said that Allahazwj Blessed and High Gifted Hareys to Rasool-Allahazwj from the broths of the Paradise, planted in the Gardens of the Paradise, and stirred by the Maiden Houries. So Rasool-Allahsaww ate it, so it increased in hissaww strength by some forty men, and that is something which Allahazwj Mighty and Majestic Intended that Heazwj Makes Hisazwj Prophetsaww Muhammadsaww to be joyful with’.

citation.arabic_text: إِنَّ اللَّهَ تَبَارَكَ وَ تَعَالَى أَهْدَى إِلَى رَسُولِ اللَّهِ ( صلى الله عليه وآله ) هَرِيسَةً مِنْ هَرَائِسِ الْجَنَّةِ غُرِسَتْ فِي رِيَاضِ الْجَنَّةِ وَ فَرَكَهَا الْحُورُ الْعِينُ فَأَكَلَهَا رَسُولُ اللَّهِ ( صلى الله عليه وآله ) فَزَادَ فِي قُوَّتِهِ بُضْعَ أَرْبَعِينَ رَجُلًا وَ ذَلِكَ شَيْ‏ءٌ أَرَادَ اللَّهُ عَزَّ وَ جَلَّ أَنْ يَسُرَّ بِهِ نَبِيَّهُ مُحَمَّداً ( صلى الله عليه وآله ) .
citation.translation: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Muhammad Bin Isnan, from Mansour Al Sayqal, from his father, from Abu Baseer, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws having said that Allahazwj Blessed and High Gifted Hareys to Rasool-Allahazwj from the broths of the Paradise, planted in the Gardens of the Paradise, and stirred by the Maiden Houries. So Rasool-Allahsaww ate it, so it increased in hissaww strength by some forty men, and that is something which Allahazwj Mighty and Majestic Intended that Heazwj Makes Hisazwj Prophetsaww Muhammadsaww to be joyful with’.

text: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Khalid, from Yahya Bin Ibrahim Bin Abu Al Balaad, from his father, from Al Waleed Bin Sabeeh who said, ‘Abu Abdullahasws said: ‘Which thing do you feed your family in the winter?’ I said, ‘The meat. So when there does not happen to be the meat, so the oil, and the butter’. Heasws said: ‘So what is preventing you from this ‘Karkour’, for it is one of the matters in the body, meaning the trio’. He (the narrator) said, ‘And one of our companions informed me that the trio is taken as a Qafiz (Unit of measurement) of rice, and a Qafiz of Humus, and a Qafiz of broad beans, or something else from the seeds, then mixed and cooked’.

citation.arabic_text: قَالَ أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) أَيَّ شَيْ‏ءٍ تُطْعِمُ عِيَالَكَ فِي الشِّتَاءِ قُلْتُ اللَّحْمَ فَإِذَا لَمْ يَكُنِ اللَّحْمُ فَالزَّيْتَ وَ السَّمْنَ قَالَ فَمَا يَمْنَعُكَ عَنْ هَذَا الْكَرْكُورِ فَإِنَّهُ أَمْرَأُ شَيْ‏ءٍ فِي الْجَسَدِ يَعْنِي الْمُثَلَّثَةَ قَالَ وَ أَخْبَرَنِي بَعْضُ أَصْحَابِنَا أَنَّ الْمُثَلَّثَةَ يُؤْخَذُ قَفِيزُ أَرُزٍّ وَ قَفِيزُ حِمَّصٍ وَ قَفِيزُ بَاقِلَّى أَوْ غَيْرِهِ مِنَ الْحُبُوبِ ثُمَّ يُرَضُّ جَمِيعاً وَ يُطْبَخُ .
citation.translation: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Khalid, from Yahya Bin Ibrahim Bin Abu Al Balaad, from his father, from Al Waleed Bin Sabeeh who said, ‘Abu Abdullahasws said: ‘Which thing do you feed your family in the winter?’ I said, ‘The meat. So when there does not happen to be the meat, so the oil, and the butter’. Heasws said: ‘So what is preventing you from this ‘Karkour’, for it is one of the matters in the body, meaning the trio’. He (the narrator) said, ‘And one of our companions informed me that the trio is taken as a Qafiz (Unit of measurement) of rice, and a Qafiz of Humus, and a Qafiz of broad beans, or something else from the seeds, then mixed and cooked’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: صحيح - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (22/146)

text: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Ali Bin Hadeed, from one of our companions, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws having said that Al-Talbeyn (White flour cooked with oil), clears the aggrieved heart just as the fingers clear the sweat from the forehead’.

citation.arabic_text: إِنَّ التَّلْبِينَ يَجْلُو الْقَلْبَ الْحَزِينَ كَمَا تَجْلُو الْأَصَابِعُ الْعَرَقَ مِنَ الْجَبِينِ .
citation.translation: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Ali Bin Hadeed, from one of our companions, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws having said that Al-Talbeyn (White flour cooked with oil), clears the aggrieved heart just as the fingers clear the sweat from the forehead’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: ضعيف - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (22/146)

text: And it is reported, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws having said: ‘The Prophetsaww said: ‘If anything could have sufficed you from the death, it would have been Al-Talbeyn which would have sufficed you’. So it was said, ‘O Rasool-Allahsaww! And what is Al-Talbeyn?’ Hesaww said: ‘Al Hasou (meat and vegetable soup) with the milk, Al-Hasou (meat and vegetable soup) with the milk’, and hesaww repeated it three times’.

citation.arabic_text: قَالَ النَّبِيُّ ( صلى الله عليه وآله ) لَوْ أَغْنَى عَنِ الْمَوْتِ شَيْ‏ءٌ لَأَغْنَتِ التَّلْبِينَةُ فَقِيلَ يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ وَ مَا التَّلْبِينَةُ قَالَ الْحَسْوُ بِاللَّبَنِ الْحَسْوُ بِاللَّبَنِ وَ كَرَّرَهَا ثَلَاثاً .
citation.translation: And it is reported, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws having said: ‘The Prophetsaww said: ‘If anything could have sufficed you from the death, it would have been Al-Talbeyn which would have sufficed you’. So it was said, ‘O Rasool-Allahsaww! And what is Al-Talbeyn?’ Hesaww said: ‘Al Hasou (meat and vegetable soup) with the milk, Al-Hasou (meat and vegetable soup) with the milk’, and hesaww repeated it three times’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: مرسل وآخره ضعيف على المشهور - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (22/147)

text: And Sahl Biin Ziyad reported from Muhammad Bin Al Hassan Bin Shamoun, from Al Asamma, from Misma’a Bin Abdul Malik, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> – similar to it.

citation.translation: And Sahl Biin Ziyad reported from Muhammad Bin Al Hassan Bin Shamoun, from Al Asamma, from Misma’a Bin Abdul Malik, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> – similar to it.

text: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Ahmad Bin Haroun Bin Mowafaq Al Madainy, form his father who said, ‘One day Al-Maazy<sup>asws</sup> (7th Imam<sup>asws</sup>) sent for me, so I ate in his<sup>asws</sup> presence, and most of it was sweet dishes. So I said, ‘How abundant are these sweets!’ So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘We<sup>asws</sup> and our<sup>asws</sup> Shias have both been Created from the sweetness, so we love the sweets’.

citation.arabic_text: بَعَثَ إِلَيَّ الْمَاضِي ( عليه السلام ) يَوْماً فَأَكَلْتُ عِنْدَهُ وَ أَكْثَرَ مِنَ الْحَلْوَاءِ فَقُلْتُ مَا أَكْثَرَ هَذِهِ الْحَلْوَاءَ فَقَالَ ( عليه السلام ) إِنَّا وَ شِيعَتَنَا خُلِقْنَا مِنَ الْحَلَاوَةِ فَنَحْنُ نُحِبُّ الْحَلْوَاءَ .
citation.translation: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Ahmad Bin Haroun Bin Mowafaq Al Madainy, form his father who said, ‘One day Al-Maazy<sup>asws</sup> (7th Imam<sup>asws</sup>) sent for me, so I ate in his<sup>asws</sup> presence, and most of it was sweet dishes. So I said, ‘How abundant are these sweets!’ So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘We<sup>asws</sup> and our<sup>asws</sup> Shias have both been Created from the sweetness, so we love the sweets’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: ضعيف على المشهور - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (2/147)

text: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Abu Hamza, from Abu Baseer, (It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘The one who does not want (to eat) the sweet dishes from us, wants the (sweet) drinks’.

citation.arabic_text: مَنْ لَمْ يُرِدْ مِنَّا الْحَلْوَاءَ أَرَادَ الشَّرَابَ .
citation.translation: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Abu Hamza, from Abu Baseer, (It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘The one who does not want (to eat) the sweet dishes from us, wants the (sweet) drinks’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: ضعيف على المشهور - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (22/147)

text: Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Yunus Bin Yunua Bin Yaqoub, from Abdul A’ala who said, ‘One day I ate with Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, so I was brought a stuffed grilled chicken, so we took it apart and ate it’. Ibn Fazal, from Yunus Bin Yaqoub, from Abdul A’ala who said, ‘I ate with Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>’ – like the first Hadeeth.

citation.arabic_text: أَكَلْتُ مَعَ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) يَوْماً فَأُتِيَ بِدَجَاجَةٍ مَحْشُوَّةٍ خَبِيصاً فَفَكَكْنَاهَا وَ أَكَلْنَاهَا . ابْنُ فَضَّالٍ عَنْ يُونُسَ بْنِ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ عَبْدِ الْأَعْلَى قَالَ أَكَلْتُ مَعَ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) مِثْلَ الْخَبَرِ الْأَوَّلِ .
citation.translation: Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Yunus Bin Yunua Bin Yaqoub, from Abdul A’ala who said, ‘One day I ate with Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, so I was brought a stuffed grilled chicken, so we took it apart and ate it’. Ibn Fazal, from Yunus Bin Yaqoub, from Abdul A’ala who said, ‘I ate with Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>’ – like the first Hadeeth.

text: Ibn Fazzal, from Yunus Bin Yaqoub, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws, said, ‘We were at Al-Medina, so heasws sent a message to us to make Falouzaj (a sweet drink) for himasws, and make only a little. So we sent it over to himasws in a small bowl’.

citation.arabic_text: كُنَّا بِالْمَدِينَةِ فَأَرْسَلَ إِلَيْنَا اصْنَعُوا لَنَا فَالُوذَجَ وَ أَقِلُّوا فَأَرْسَلْنَا إِلَيْهِ فِي قَصْعَةٍ صَغِيرَةٍ .
citation.translation: Ibn Fazzal, from Yunus Bin Yaqoub, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws, said, ‘We were at Al-Medina, so heasws sent a message to us to make Falouzaj (a sweet drink) for himasws, and make only a little. So we sent it over to himasws in a small bowl’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: موثق - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (22/148)

text: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Al Qasim Bin Yahya, from his grandfather Al Hassan Bin Rashid, from Muhammad Bin Muslim, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Allow the heat until it cools down, for hot food was brought near Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup>, so he<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘Allow it until it cools down, it was not for Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic to feed us the fire, and the Blessings are in the cooled (food)’.

citation.arabic_text: قَالَ أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ ( عليه السلام ) أَقِرُّوا الْحَارَّ حَتَّى يَبْرُدَ فَإِنَّ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ ( صلى الله عليه وآله ) قُرِّبَ إِلَيْهِ طَعَامٌ حَارٌّ فَقَالَ أَقِرُّوهُ حَتَّى يَبْرُدَ مَا كَانَ اللَّهُ عَزَّ وَ جَلَّ لِيُطْعِمَنَا النَّارَ وَ الْبَرَكَةُ فِي الْبَارِدِ .
citation.translation: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Al Qasim Bin Yahya, from his grandfather Al Hassan Bin Rashid, from Muhammad Bin Muslim, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Allow the heat until it cools down, for hot food was brought near Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup>, so he<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘Allow it until it cools down, it was not for Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic to feed us the fire, and the Blessings are in the cooled (food)’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: ضعيف - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (22/148)

text: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Al Nowfaly, from Al Sakuny, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said that they came to the Prophet<sup>saww</sup> with very hot food. So he<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘It was not for Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic to Feed us the fire. Allow it to cool down to enable (it to be eaten), for it (hot food) is a food with devoid of Blessings, and for the Satan<sup>la</sup> there is a share in it’.

citation.arabic_text: إِنَّ النَّبِيَّ ( صلى الله عليه وآله ) أُتِيَ بِطَعَامٍ حَارٍّ جِدّاً فَقَالَ مَا كَانَ اللَّهُ عَزَّ وَ جَلَّ لِيُطْعِمَنَا النَّارَ أَقِرُّوهُ حَتَّى يَبْرُدَ وَ يُمْكِنَ فَإِنَّهُ طَعَامٌ مَمْحُوقُ الْبَرَكَةِ وَ لِلشَّيْطَانِ فِيهِ نَصِيبٌ .
citation.translation: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Al Nowfaly, from Al Sakuny, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said that they came to the Prophet<sup>saww</sup> with very hot food. So he<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘It was not for Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic to Feed us the fire. Allow it to cool down to enable (it to be eaten), for it (hot food) is a food with devoid of Blessings, and for the Satan<sup>la</sup> there is a share in it’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: ضعيف على المشهور - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (22/148)

text: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Muhammad Bin Hakeym, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘The hot food is other than with Blessing’.

citation.arabic_text: الطَّعَامُ الْحَارُّ غَيْرُ ذِي بَرَكَةٍ .
citation.translation: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Muhammad Bin Hakeym, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘The hot food is other than with Blessing’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: حسن - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (22/149)

text: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ibn Al Qaddah, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘They came to the Prophet<sup>saww</sup> with hot food, so he<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic does not Feed us the fire. Keep it aside until it cools’. So it was left until it cooled’.

citation.arabic_text: أُتِيَ النَّبِيُّ ( صلى الله عليه وآله ) بِطَعَامٍ حَارٍّ فَقَالَ إِنَّ اللَّهَ عَزَّ وَ جَلَّ لَمْ يُطْعِمْنَا النَّارَ نَحُّوهُ حَتَّى يَبْرُدَ فَتُرِكَ حَتَّى بَرَدَ .
citation.translation: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ibn Al Qaddah, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘They came to the Prophet<sup>saww</sup> with hot food, so he<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic does not Feed us the fire. Keep it aside until it cools’. So it was left until it cooled’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: موثق - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (2/149)

text: Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Yunus Bin Yaqoub, from Suleyman Bin Khalid who said, ‘I was present at a dinner of Abu Abdullahasws in the summer, so they came with a platter upon which was bread, and they came with a bowl of Sareyd, and meat. So heasws said: ‘Come closer to me for this food’. So I approached, and heasws touched it with hisasws hand, and raised it and heasws was saying: ‘Iasws seek Protection with Allahazwj from the Fire, Iasws seek Refuge with Allahazwj from the Fire, Iasws seek Refuge with Allahazwj from the Fire. This is what we cannot be patient upon, so how (can we be patient upon) the Fire. This is what we do not have the strength upon (to bear), so how (can we bear) the Fire. This is what we cannot endure, so how (can we endure) the Fire?’ He (the narrator) said: ‘Heasws kept on repeating mentioning that until it was possible (to eat) the food, so heasws ate and I ate with himasws’.

citation.arabic_text: حَضَرْتُ عَشَاءَ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) فِي الصَّيْفِ فَأُتِيَ بِخِوَانٍ عَلَيْهِ خُبْزٌ وَ أُتِيَ بِقَصْعَةِ ثَرِيدٍ وَ لَحْمٍ فَقَالَ هَلُمَّ إِلَيَّ هَذَا الطَّعَامَ فَدَنَوْتُ فَوَضَعَ يَدَهُ فِيهِ وَ رَفَعَهَا وَ هُوَ يَقُولُ أَسْتَجِيرُ بِاللَّهِ مِنَ النَّارِ أَعُوذُ بِاللَّهِ مِنَ النَّارِ أَعُوذُ بِاللَّهِ مِنَ النَّارِ هَذَا مَا لَا نَصْبِرُ عَلَيْهِ فَكَيْفَ النَّارُ هَذَا مَا لَا نَقْوَى عَلَيْهِ فَكَيْفَ النَّارُ هَذَا مَا لَا نُطِيقُهُ فَكَيْفَ النَّارُ قَالَ وَ كَانَ ( عليه السلام ) يُكَرِّرُ ذَلِكَ حَتَّى أَمْكَنَ الطَّعَامُ فَأَكَلَ وَ أَكَلْنَا مَعَهُ .
citation.translation: Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Yunus Bin Yaqoub, from Suleyman Bin Khalid who said, ‘I was present at a dinner of Abu Abdullahasws in the summer, so they came with a platter upon which was bread, and they came with a bowl of Sareyd, and meat. So heasws said: ‘Come closer to me for this food’. So I approached, and heasws touched it with hisasws hand, and raised it and heasws was saying: ‘Iasws seek Protection with Allahazwj from the Fire, Iasws seek Refuge with Allahazwj from the Fire, Iasws seek Refuge with Allahazwj from the Fire. text: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Abu Abdullah, from Muhammad Bin Ali, from Muhammad Bin Al Haysam, from his father who said, ‘Abu Hamza made food for us and we were a group. text: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Saeed Bin Janaah, (It has been narrated) from a slave of Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> who said, ‘He<sup>asws</sup> called for dates, so he<sup>asws</sup> ate them, then said: ‘There is no desire with me<sup>asws</sup> but I<sup>asws</sup> have eaten fish’. text: Al Husayn Bin Muhammad, from Moala Bin Muhammad, from Muhammad Bin Ali Al Hamdany, from Ma’tab, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, or said, from Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> having said one day: ‘O Ma’tab! text: Muhammad Bin Yahya said, ‘One of our companions wrote to Abu Muhammad<sup>asws</sup> complaining to him<sup>asws</sup> about blood and paleness saying, ‘When I get cupping done, it leads to paleness, and when I delay the cupping, so what is your<sup>asws</sup> view regarding that?’ So he<sup>asws</sup> wrote: ‘Get cupping done and eat upon the effects of cupping, fresh grilled fish’. He (the narrator) said, ‘So I re-iterated the same question to him<sup>asws</sup>, so he<sup>asws</sup> wrote: ‘Get cupping done, and eat upon the effects of the cupping, fresh grilled fish with water and salt. He (the narrator) said, ‘So I worked upon that, so I was upon good health and it became my (regular) intake’.
