text: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Ali Bin Hassan, from Musa Bin Bakr who said, ‘I heard Abu Al Hassan<sup>asws</sup> saying: ‘Frequenting the eating of the eggs increases in the births (children)’.

citation.arabic_text: سَمِعْتُ أَبَا الْحَسَنِ ( عليه السلام ) يَقُولُ كَثْرَةُ أَكْلِ الْبَيْضِ تَزِيدُ فِي الْوَلَدِ .
citation.translation: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Ali Bin Hassan, from Musa Bin Bakr who said, ‘I heard Abu Al Hassan<sup>asws</sup> saying: ‘Frequenting the eating of the eggs increases in the births (children)’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: ضعيف على المشهور - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (2/153)

text: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Abu Abdullah, from Muhammad Bin Isa, from his father, from his grandfather, and Qays Bin Abdul Aziz, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘The yolk of the egg is light, and the albumen is heavy’.

citation.arabic_text: مُخُّ الْبَيْضِ خَفِيفٌ وَ الْبَيَاضُ ثَقِيلٌ .
citation.translation: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Abu Abdullah, from Muhammad Bin Isa, from his father, from his grandfather, and Qays Bin Abdul Aziz, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘The yolk of the egg is light, and the albumen is heavy’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: مجهول - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (22/153)

text: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Muhammad Bin Musa, from Yaqoub Bin Yazeed, from Ibn Fazzal, from one of our companions, from Ibn Abu Yafour who said, ‘I said to Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> that the chicken happens to be in the house and there is no rooster with her. She feeds upon the sweepings and other such, and she lays an egg from other than going near the rooster. So what are you<sup>asws</sup> saying regarding eating that egg?’ So he<sup>asws</sup> said to me: ‘The egg when it was from what its flesh can be eaten, so there is no problem with it and with eating it, and it is Permissible’.

citation.arabic_text: قُلْتُ لِأَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) إِنَّ الدَّجَاجَةَ تَكُونُ فِي الْمَنْزِلِ وَ لَيْسَ مَعَهَا دِيكٌ تَعْتَلِفُ مِنَ الْكُنَاسَةِ وَ غَيْرِهَا وَ تَبِيضُ مِنْ غَيْرِ أَنْ يَرْكَبَهَا الدِّيكُ فَمَا تَقُولُ فِي أَكْلِ ذَلِكَ الْبَيْضِ فَقَالَ لِي إِنَّ الْبَيْضَ إِذَا كَانَ مِمَّا يُؤْكَلُ لَحْمُهُ فَلَا بَأْسَ بِهِ وَ بِأَكْلِهِ وَ هُوَ حَلَالٌ.
citation.translation: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Muhammad Bin Musa, from Yaqoub Bin Yazeed, from Ibn Fazzal, from one of our companions, from Ibn Abu Yafour who said, ‘I said to Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> that the chicken happens to be in the house and there is no rooster with her. She feeds upon the sweepings and other such, and she lays an egg from other than going near the rooster. So what are you<sup>asws</sup> saying regarding eating that egg?’ So he<sup>asws</sup> said to me: ‘The egg when it was from what its flesh can be eaten, so there is no problem with it and with eating it, and it is Permissible’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: مجهول - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (22/153)

text: Abu Ali Al Ashary, from one of our companions, from Ibn Abu Najran, from Dawood Bin Farqad who said, ‘I asked Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> about the sheep and the cow, sometimes they give milk from other than the stallion having hit her, and the chicken laying eggs from without going near the rooster’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘All this is Permissible, good for you, everything which you can eat its flesh, so the entirety of whatever was from it, from milk, or eggs, or rennet, so eating this is Permissible, good; and sometimes this happens after the stallion having come across her and mated, and all this is Permissible’.

citation.arabic_text: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) عَنِ الشَّاةِ وَ الْبَقَرَةِ رُبَّمَا دَرَّتِ اللَّبَنَ مِنْ غَيْرِ أَنْ يَضْرِبَهَا الْفَحْلُ وَ الدَّجَاجَةُ رُبَّمَا بَاضَتْ مِنْ غَيْرِ أَنْ يَرْكَبَهَا الدِّيكُ قَالَ فَقَالَ ( عليه السلام ) كُلُّ هَذَا حَلَالٌ طَيِّبٌ لَكَ كُلُّ شَيْ‏ءٍ يُؤْكَلُ لَحْمُهُ فَجَمِيعُ مَا كَانَ مِنْهُ مِنْ لَبَنٍ أَوْ بَيْضٍ أَوْ إِنْفَحَةٍ فَكُلُّ هَذَا حَلَالٌ طَيِّبٌ وَ رُبَّمَا يَكُونُ هَذَا قَدْ ضَرَبَهُ الْفَحْلُ وَ يُبْطِئُ وَ كُلُّ هَذَا حَلَالٌ .
citation.translation: Abu Ali Al Ashary, from one of our companions, from Ibn Abu Najran, from Dawood Bin Farqad who said, ‘I asked Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> about the sheep and the cow, sometimes they give milk from other than the stallion having hit her, and the chicken laying eggs from without going near the rooster’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘All this is Permissible, good for you, everything which you can eat its flesh, so the entirety of whatever was from it, from milk, or eggs, or rennet, so eating this is Permissible, good; and sometimes this happens after the stallion having come across her and mated, and all this is Permissible’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: مرسل - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (22/153)

text: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Ali Bin Al Hakam, from Ibn Bukeyr, from Zurara, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘The Prophet<sup>saww</sup> said to Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup>: ‘O Ali<sup>asws</sup>! Start with salt in your meal, and end with the salt, for the one who starts his meal with the salt and ends it with the salt, Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Repels from him seventy types from the types of the afflictions, the easiest one being the leprosy’.

citation.arabic_text: قَالَ النَّبِيُّ ( صلى الله عليه وآله ) لِأَمِيرِ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ ( عليه السلام ) يَا عَلِيُّ افْتَتِحْ بِالْمِلْحِ فِي طَعَامِكَ وَ اخْتِمْ بِالْمِلْحِ فَإِنَّهُ مَنِ افْتَتَحَ طَعَامَهُ بِالْمِلْحِ وَ خَتَمَهُ بِالْمِلْحِ دَفَعَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ سَبْعِينَ نَوْعاً مِنْ أَنْوَاعِ الْبَلَاءِ أَيْسَرُهَا الْجُذَامُ .
citation.translation: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Ali Bin Al Hakam, from Ibn Bukeyr, from Zurara, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘The Prophet<sup>saww</sup> said to Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup>: ‘O Ali<sup>asws</sup>! Start with salt in your meal, and end with the salt, for the one who starts his meal with the salt and ends it with the salt, Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Repels from him seventy types from the types of the afflictions, the easiest one being the leprosy’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: موثق كالصحيح - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (2/154)

text: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hisham Bin Salim, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said to Ali<sup>asws</sup>! O Ali<sup>asws</sup>! Begin your meal with the salt and end with the salt, for the one who begins his meal with the salt and ends with the salt, would be cured from seventy-two types of affliction, from it being the leprosy, and the insanity, and the vitiligo’.

citation.arabic_text: قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ ( صلى الله عليه وآله ) لِعَلِيٍّ ( عليه السلام ) يَا عَلِيُّ افْتَتِحْ طَعَامَكَ بِالْمِلْحِ وَ اخْتِمْ بِالْمِلْحِ فَإِنَّ مَنِ افْتَتَحَ طَعَامَهُ بِالْمِلْحِ وَ خَتَمَ بِالْمِلْحِ عُوفِيَ مِنِ اثْنَيْنِ وَ سَبْعِينَ نَوْعاً مِنْ أَنْوَاعِ الْبَلَاءِ مِنْهُ الْجُذَامُ وَ الْجُنُونُ وَ الْبَرَصُ .
citation.translation: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hisham Bin Salim, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said to Ali<sup>asws</sup>! O Ali<sup>asws</sup>! Begin your meal with the salt and end with the salt, for the one who begins his meal with the salt and ends with the salt, would be cured from seventy-two types of affliction, from it being the leprosy, and the insanity, and the vitiligo’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: حسن - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (22/154)

text: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ismail Bin Marrar, from Yunus, from a man, from Sa’ad Al Askaf, (It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘In the salt is a healing from seventy illnesses’, or said: ‘Seventy types of the pains’. Then he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘If the people knew what is in the salt, they would not cure (illnesses) except by it’.

citation.arabic_text: إِنَّ فِي الْمِلْحِ شِفَاءً مِنْ سَبْعِينَ دَاءً أَوْ قَالَ سَبْعِينَ نَوْعاً مِنْ أَنْوَاعِ الْأَوْجَاعِ ثُمَّ قَالَ لَوْ يَعْلَمُ النَّاسُ مَا فِي الْمِلْحِ مَا تَدَاوَوْا إِلَّا بِهِ .
citation.translation: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ismail Bin Marrar, from Yunus, from a man, from Sa’ad Al Askaf, (It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘In the salt is a healing from seventy illnesses’, or said: ‘Seventy types of the pains’. Then he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘If the people knew what is in the salt, they would not cure (illnesses) except by it’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: مجهول - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (22/154)

text: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Al Qasim Bin Yahya, from his grandfather Al Hassan Bin Rashid, from Muhammad Bin Muslim, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Begin with the salt at the inception of your meal, for had the people known what is in the salt, they would choose it over the experimental antidote’.

citation.arabic_text: قَالَ أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ ( عليه السلام ) ابْدَءُوا بِالْمِلْحِ فِي أَوَّلِ طَعَامِكُمْ فَلَوْ يَعْلَمُ النَّاسُ مَا فِي الْمِلْحِ لَاخْتَارُوهُ عَلَى الدِّرْيَاقِ الْمُجَرَّبِ .
citation.translation: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Al Qasim Bin Yahya, from his grandfather Al Hassan Bin Rashid, from Muhammad Bin Muslim, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Begin with the salt at the inception of your meal, for had the people known what is in the salt, they would choose it over the experimental antidote’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: ضعيف - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (22/154)

text: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Bakr Bin Salih, from Al Ja’fary, (It has been narrated) from Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> the 1st having said: ‘It is not fruitful, a food-spread which has not salt upon it, and it is corrective for the body that one begins by it during the starting of the meal’.

citation.arabic_text: لَا يُخْصِبُ خِوَانٌ لَا مِلْحَ عَلَيْهَا وَ أَصَحُّ لِلْبَدَنِ أَنْ يُبْدَأَ بِهِ فِي أَوَّلِ الطَّعَامِ .
citation.translation: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Bakr Bin Salih, from Al Ja’fary, (It has been narrated) from Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> the 1st having said: ‘It is not fruitful, a food-spread which has not salt upon it, and it is corrective for the body that one begins by it during the starting of the meal’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: ضعيف - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (2/155)

text: Humeyd Bin Ziyad, from Al Hassan Bin Muhammad Bin Sama’at, from Ahmad Bin Al Hassan Al Maysami, from Sukeyn Bin Ammar, from Fuzayl Al Rassan, from Farwa, (It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic Revealed unto Musa<sup>as</sup> Bin Imran<sup>as</sup> that: “Order your<sup>as</sup> people they should be beginning with the salt, and ending with it, or else they should not be blaming except for themselves’.

citation.arabic_text: أَوْحَى اللَّهُ عَزَّ وَ جَلَّ إِلَى مُوسَى بْنِ عِمْرَانَ ( عليه السلام ) أَنْ مُرْ قَوْمَكَ يَفْتَتِحُوا بِالْمِلْحِ وَ يَخْتَتِمُوا بِهِ وَ إِلَّا فَلَا يَلُومُوا إِلَّا أَنْفُسَهُمْ .
citation.translation: Humeyd Bin Ziyad, from Al Hassan Bin Muhammad Bin Sama’at, from Ahmad Bin Al Hassan Al Maysami, from Sukeyn Bin Ammar, from Fuzayl Al Rassan, from Farwa, (It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic Revealed unto Musa<sup>as</sup> Bin Imran<sup>as</sup> that: “Order your<sup>as</sup> people they should be beginning with the salt, and ending with it, or else they should not be blaming except for themselves’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: مجهول - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (22/155)

text: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Ibrahim Bin Abu Mahmoud who said, ‘Al-Reza<sup>asws</sup> said to us: ‘Which food item is the worthiest?’ So one of us said, ‘The meat’, and one of us said, ‘The oil’, and one of us said, ‘The milk’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘It is naught but the salt, and we had gone out on a trip of ours and one of the slaves had forgotten the salt. So he slaughter a sheep for us from as fat as it can be, but it did not benefit us with anything until we dispersed (came back)’.

citation.arabic_text: قَالَ لَنَا الرِّضَا ( عليه السلام ) أَيُّ الْإِدَامِ أَحْرَى فَقَالَ بَعْضُنَا اللَّحْمُ وَ قَالَ بَعْضُنَا الزَّيْتُ وَ قَالَ بَعْضُنَا اللَّبَنُ فَقَالَ هُوَ ( عليه السلام ) لَا بَلِ الْمِلْحُ وَ لَقَدْ خَرَجْنَا إِلَى نُزْهَةٍ لَنَا وَ نَسِيَ بَعْضُ الْغِلْمَانِ الْمِلْحَ فَذَبَحُوا لَنَا شَاةً مِنْ أَسْمَنِ مَا يَكُونُ فَمَا انْتَفَعْنَا بِشَيْ‏ءٍ حَتَّى انْصَرَفْنَا .
citation.translation: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Ibrahim Bin Abu Mahmoud who said, ‘Al-Reza<sup>asws</sup> said to us: ‘Which food item is the worthiest?’ So one of us said, ‘The meat’, and one of us said, ‘The oil’, and one of us said, ‘The milk’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘It is naught but the salt, and we had gone out on a trip of ours and one of the slaves had forgotten the salt. So he slaughter a sheep for us from as fat as it can be, but it did not benefit us with anything until we dispersed (came back)’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: صحيح - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (22/155)

text: From him, from Yaqoub Bin Yazeed, raising it, said, ‘Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The one who sprinkles the salt upon the first morsel of his meal, the blemishes would go away from his face’.

citation.arabic_text: قَالَ أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) مَنْ ذَرَّ عَلَى أَوَّلِ لُقْمَةٍ مِنْ طَعَامِهِ الْمِلْحَ ذَهَبَ عَنْهُ بِنَمَشِ الْوَجْهِ .
citation.translation: From him, from Yaqoub Bin Yazeed, raising it, said, ‘Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The one who sprinkles the salt upon the first morsel of his meal, the blemishes would go away from his face’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: مرفوع - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (2/155)

text: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Abu Ayoub Al Khazzaz, from Muhammad Bin Muslim, ‘He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The scorpion bit Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup>, so he<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘May Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Curse you, for you (scorpions) don’t care whether it is a believer that you harm or an Infidel’. Then he<sup>saww</sup> called for the salt, so he<sup>saww</sup> rubbed it down and pressed it’. Then Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘If the people knew what was in the salt, they would not seek any other antidote with it’.

citation.arabic_text: إِنَّ الْعَقْرَبَ لَسَعَتْ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ ( صلى الله عليه وآله ) فَقَالَ لَعَنَكِ اللَّهُ فَمَا تُبَالِينَ مُؤْمِناً آذَيْتِ أَمْ كَافِراً ثُمَّ دَعَا بِالْمِلْحِ فَدَلَكَهُ فَهَدَتْ ثُمَّ قَالَ أَبُو جَعْفَرٍ ( عليه السلام ) لَوْ يَعْلَمُ النَّاسُ مَا فِي الْمِلْحِ مَا بَغَوْا مَعَهُ دِرْيَاقاً .
citation.translation: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Abu Ayoub Al Khazzaz, from Muhammad Bin Muslim, ‘He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The scorpion bit Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup>, so he<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘May Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Curse you, for you (scorpions) don’t care whether it is a believer that you harm or an Infidel’. Then he<sup>saww</sup> called for the salt, so he<sup>saww</sup> rubbed it down and pressed it’. Then Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘If the people knew what was in the salt, they would not seek any other antidote with it’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: حسن - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (22/155)

text: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Abu Abdullah, from his father, and Amro Bin Ibrahim, altogether from Khalaf Bin Hammad, from yaqoub Bin Shuayb, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘A scorpion stung Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup>, so he<sup>saww</sup> shook it off and said: ‘May Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Curse you, for neither a Believer nor an Infidel is safe from you’. Then he<sup>saww</sup> called for the salt, so he<sup>saww</sup> placed it upon the place of the bite and pressed it by his<sup>saww</sup> thumb until it melted. Then he<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘If the people knew what was in the salt, they would not be needy along with it, for any (other) antidote’.

citation.arabic_text: لَدَغَتْ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ ( صلى الله عليه وآله ) عَقْرَبٌ فَنَفَضَهَا وَ قَالَ لَعَنَكِ اللَّهُ فَمَا يَسْلَمُ مِنْكِ مُؤْمِنٌ وَ لَا كَافِرٌ ثُمَّ دَعَا بِالْمِلْحِ فَوَضَعَهُ عَلَى مَوْضِعِ اللَّدْغَةِ ثُمَّ عَصَرَهُ بِإِبْهَامِهِ حَتَّى ذَابَ ثُمَّ قَالَ لَوْ يَعْلَمُ النَّاسُ مَا فِي الْمِلْحِ مَا احْتَاجُوا مَعَهُ إِلَى دِرْيَاقٍ .
citation.translation: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Abu Abdullah, from his father, and Amro Bin Ibrahim, altogether from Khalaf Bin Hammad, from yaqoub Bin Shuayb, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘A scorpion stung Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup>, so he<sup>saww</sup> shook it off and said: ‘May Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Curse you, for neither a Believer nor an Infidel is safe from you’. Then he<sup>saww</sup> called for the salt, so he<sup>saww</sup> placed it upon the place of the bite and pressed it by his<sup>saww</sup> thumb until it melted. Then he<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘If the people knew what was in the salt, they would not be needy along with it, for any (other) antidote’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: صحيح - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (22/156)

text: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Khalid, from Usman Bin Isa, from Khalid Bin Najeeh who said, ‘I broke Fast with Abu Abdullahasws and with Abu Al-Hassanasws the 1st, during the Month of Ramazan, so the first of what was brought with was a bowl of Vinegar Sareyd and oil. So the first of what heasws took from it was three morsels, then they came with the (large) bowl’.

citation.arabic_text: كُنْتُ أُفْطِرُ مَعَ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) وَ مَعَ أَبِي الْحَسَنِ الْأَوَّلِ ( عليه السلام ) فِي شَهْرِ رَمَضَانَ فَكَانَ أَوَّلُ مَا يُؤْتَى بِهِ قَصْعَةً مِنْ ثَرِيدِ خَلٍّ وَ زَيْتٍ فَكَانَ أَوَّلُ مَا يَتَنَاوَلُ مِنْهَا ثَلَاثَ لُقَمٍ ثُمَّ يُؤْتَى بِالْجَفْنَةِ .

text: From him, from Usman Bin Isa, from Hammad Bin Usman, from Salama Al Qalanasy who said, ‘I went over to Abu Abdullahasws. So when I spoke, heasws said to me: ‘What is the matter Iasws hear your speech as weak?’ I said, ‘My mouth has fallen’. It was as if that was grievous to himasws. Then heasws said: ‘So which thing do you eat?’ I said, ‘I eat whatever was in the house’. So heasws said: ‘Upon you is with (eating the) Sareyd, for therein is a Blessing, but if there does not happen to be any meat, so the vinegar and the oil’.

citation.arabic_text: دَخَلْتُ عَلَى أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) فَلَمَّا تَكَلَّمْتُ قَالَ لِي مَا لِي أَسْمَعُ كَلَامَكَ قَدْ ضَعُفَ قُلْتُ قَدْ سَقَطَ فَمِي قَالَ فَكَأَنَّهُ شَقَّ عَلَيْهِ ذَلِكَ ثُمَّ قَالَ فَأَيَّ شَيْ‏ءٍ تَأْكُلُ قُلْتُ آكُلُ مَا كَانَ فِي الْبَيْتِ فَقَالَ عَلَيْكَ بِالثَّرِيدِ فَإِنَّ فِيهِ بَرَكَةً فَإِنْ لَمْ يَكُنْ لَحْمٌ فَالْخَلُّ وَ الزَّيْتُ .

text: From him, from Ismail Bin Mihran, from Hammad Bin Usman, from Zayd Bin Al Hassan who said, ‘I heard Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> saying: ‘Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> was the most resembling of the people with Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> in his<sup>asws</sup> meals. He<sup>asws</sup> used to eat the bread, and the vinegar, and the oil, and he<sup>asws</sup> would feed the people, the bread and the meat’.

citation.arabic_text: سَمِعْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) يَقُولُ كَانَ أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ ( عليه السلام ) أَشْبَهَ النَّاسِ طِعْمَةً بِرَسُولِ اللَّهِ ( صلى الله عليه وآله ) كَانَ يَأْكُلُ الْخُبْزَ وَ الْخَلَّ وَ الزَّيْتَ وَ يُطْعِمُ النَّاسَ الْخُبْزَ وَ اللَّحْمَ .

text: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Ubeyda Al Wasity, from Ajlan who said, ‘I had dinner with Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> after darkness, and he<sup>asws</sup> tended to have dinner after darkness. So they came with vinegar, and oil, and cold meat, so he<sup>asws</sup> went on to pluck the meat and feed it, and he<sup>asws</sup> (himself) would eat the vinegar, and the oil, and leave the meat. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘This is our<sup>asws</sup> meal, and a meal of the Prophets<sup>as</sup>’.

citation.arabic_text: تَعَشَّيْتُ مَعَ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) بَعْدَ عَتَمَةٍ وَ كَانَ يَتَعَشَّى بَعْدَ عَتَمَةٍ فَأُتِيَ بِخَلٍّ وَ زَيْتٍ وَ لَحْمٍ بَارِدٍ فَجَعَلَ يَنْتِفُ اللَّحْمَ فَيُطْعِمُنِيهِ وَ يَأْكُلُ هُوَ الْخَلَّ وَ الزَّيْتَ وَ يَدَعُ اللَّحْمَ فَقَالَ إِنَّ هَذَا طَعَامُنَا وَ طَعَامُ الْأَنْبِيَاءِ ( عليهم السلام ) .

text: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Ibn Fazzal, from Yunus Bin Yaqoub, from Abdul Al A’ala who said, ‘I ate with Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, so he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘O maid, come to us with our<sup>asws</sup> well-known meal’. So she came with a bow in which was vinegar and oil, so we ate’.

citation.arabic_text: أَكَلْتُ مَعَ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) فَقَالَ يَا جَارِيَةُ ائْتِينَا بِطَعَامِنَا الْمَعْرُوفِ فَأُتِيَ بِقَصْعَةٍ فِيهَا خَلٌّ وَ زَيْتٌ فَأَكَلْنَا .

text: And by this chain, ‘He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘They would never be poor, the family which is habitual with the vinegar, and the oil, and that is the sauce of the Prophets<sup>as</sup>’.

citation.arabic_text: وَ بِهَذَا الْإِسْنَادِ قَالَ قَالَ أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ ( عليه السلام ) مَا افْتَقَرَ أَهْلُ بَيْتٍ يَأْتَدِمُونَ بِالْخَلِّ وَ الزَّيْتِ وَ ذَلِكَ أُدْمُ الْأَنْبِيَاءِ ( عليهم السلام ) .
citation.translation: And by this chain, ‘He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘They would never be poor, the family which is habitual with the vinegar, and the oil, and that is the sauce of the Prophets<sup>as</sup>’.

text: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Al Barqy, from his father, from one of our companions, from Ayoub Bin Al Hurr, from Muhammad Bin Ali Al Halby who said, ‘I asked Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> about the meal, so he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Upon you is (eating) with the vinegar and the oil, for it is nourishing, and Ali<sup>asws</sup> used to frequently eat it, and I<sup>asws</sup> frequently eat it, and it is nourishing’.

text: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Ali Bin Asbaat, from his uncle Yaqoub Bin Salim who said, ‘I heard Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> saying: ‘Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> used eat the vinegar and the oil, and he<sup>asws</sup> kept the expenditure (for it) under his<sup>asws</sup> carpet’.

citation.arabic_text: سَمِعْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) يَقُولُ كَانَ أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ ( عليه السلام ) يَأْكُلُ الْخَلَّ وَ الزَّيْتَ وَ يَجْعَلُ نَفَقَتَهُ تَحْتَ طِنْفِسَتِهِ .

text: Al Husayn Bin Muhammad, from Moala Bin Muhammad, from Al Hassan Bin Ali Al Washa, from Abdullah Bin Sinan, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> went over to Umm Salma<sup>as</sup>, so she<sup>as</sup> forwarded a piece of bread nearer to him<sup>saww</sup> So he<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘Is there sauce with you<sup>as</sup>?’ So she<sup>as</sup> said, ‘No, O Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup>, there is nothing with me<sup>as</sup> except for vinegar’. text: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hisham Bin Salim, from Suleyman Bin Khalid, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘The vinegar strengthens the intellect’.

text: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Ali Bin Abu Hamza, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, said, ‘I heard him<sup>asws</sup> saying: ‘It would not get impoverished, a house wherein is vinegar, and Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> had said that’.

citation.arabic_text: سَمِعْتُهُ يَقُولُ مَا أَقْفَرَ بَيْتٌ فِيهِ خَلٌّ وَ قَدْ قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ ( صلى الله عليه وآله ) ذَلِكَ .

citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: ضعيف على المشهور - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (22/159)

text: Ali Bin Muhammad Bundar, from his father, from Muhammad Bin Ali Al Hamdany that, A man was in the presence of Al-Reza<sup>asws</sup> at Khurasan, so a meal was forwarded to him, upon it was vinegar and salt. So he<sup>asws</sup> began with the vinegar, and the man said, ‘May I be sacrificed for you<sup>asws</sup>, we have been instructed that we should begin with the salt’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘This is similar to this, meaning the vinegar, and the vinegar strengthens the mind, and increases in the intellect’.

citation.arabic_text: الرَّجُلُ جُعِلْتُ فِدَاكَ أَمَرْتَنَا أَنْ نَفْتَتِحَ بِالْمِلْحِ فَقَالَ هَذَا مِثْلُ هَذَا يَعْنِي الْخَلَّ وَ إِنَّ الْخَلَّ يَشُدُّ الذِّهْنَ وَ يَزِيدُ فِي الْعَقْلِ .

citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: ضعيف - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (2/159)

text: Ali, from his father, from Hannan, from his father, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, said, ‘The wine vinegar was mentioned in his<sup>asws</sup> presence, so he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘It kills the insects of the belly and strengthens the mouth’.

citation.arabic_text: ذُكِرَ عِنْدَهُ خَلُّ الْخَمْرِ فَقَالَ ( عليه السلام ) إِنَّهُ لَيَقْتُلُ دَوَابَّ الْبَطْنِ وَ يَشُدُّ الْفَمَ .
citation.translation: Ali, from his father, from Hannan, from his father, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, said, ‘The wine vinegar was mentioned in his<sup>asws</sup> presence, so he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘It kills the insects of the belly and strengthens the mouth’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: حسن أو موثق - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (2/159)

text: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Al Hakam, from Sama’at, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Vinegar of the wine strengthens the gums, and kills the insects of the belly, and strengthens the intellect’.

citation.arabic_text: خَلُّ الْخَمْرِ يَشُدُّ اللِّثَةَ وَ يَقْتُلُ دَوَابَّ الْبَطْنِ وَ يَشُدُّ الْعَقْلَ .
citation.translation: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Al Hakam, from Sama’at, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Vinegar of the wine strengthens the gums, and kills the insects of the belly, and strengthens the intellect’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: موثق - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (2/159)

text: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ali Bin Ibrahim Al Ja’fary, from Muhammad and Ahmad the two sons of Umar Bin Musa, from their father, (It has been narrated) raising it to Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘The staining (of the food) with the vinegar cuts the desire of the adultery’.

citation.arabic_text: الِاصْطِبَاغُ بِالْخَلِّ يَقْطَعُ شَهْوَةَ الزِّنَا .
citation.translation: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ali Bin Ibrahim Al Ja’fary, from Muhammad and Ahmad the two sons of Umar Bin Musa, from their father, (It has been narrated) raising it to Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘The staining (of the food) with the vinegar cuts the desire of the adultery’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: مجهول مرفوع - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (2/160)

text: Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Al Hakam, from Rabie Al Musally, form Ahmad Bin Razeyn, from Sufyan Bin Al Samt, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Upon you is with (eating) the wine vinegar, therefore immerse (bread etc.) in it, for there would not remain an insect in your inside but it would kill it’.

citation.arabic_text: عَلَيْكَ بِخَلِّ الْخَمْرِ فَاغْمِسْ فِيهِ فَإِنَّهُ لَا يَبْقَى فِي جَوْفِكَ دَابَّةٌ إِلَّا قَتَلَهَا .
citation.translation: Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Al Hakam, from Rabie Al Musally, form Ahmad Bin Razeyn, from Sufyan Bin Al Samt, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Upon you is with (eating) the wine vinegar, therefore immerse (bread etc.) in it, for there would not remain an insect in your inside but it would kill it’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: مجهول - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (22/160)

text: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from one of our companions, from Ali Bin Suleyman Bin Rusheyd, from Muhammad Bin Abdullah, from Suleyman Al Salaymi, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘The Children of Israel were beginning (their meals) with the vinegar, and they were ending with it, and we<sup>asws</sup> begin with the salt and end with the vinegar’.

citation.arabic_text: إِنَّ بَنِي إِسْرَائِيلَ كَانُوا يَسْتَفْتِحُونَ بِالْخَلِّ وَ يَخْتِمُونَ بِهِ وَ نَحْنُ نَسْتَفْتِحُ بِالْمِلْحِ وَ نَخْتِمُ بِالْخَلِّ .
citation.translation: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from one of our companions, from Ali Bin Suleyman Bin Rusheyd, from Muhammad Bin Abdullah, from Suleyman Al Salaymi, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘The Children of Israel were beginning (their meals) with the vinegar, and they were ending with it, and we<sup>asws</sup> begin with the salt and end with the vinegar’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: ضعيف - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (2/160)

text: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Musa Bin Al Hassan, from Muhammad Bin Ahmad Bin Abu Mahmoud, from his father, (It has been narrated) raising it from Abu Abdullahasws having said that when Yusufas was in the prison, heas complained to hisas Lordazwj Mighty and Majestic of eating the bread on its own, and asked for a gravy to eat it with, and with himas used to be abundance of pieces of the dry bread’. So Heazwj Commanded himas that heas should take the bread and make it to be in a pot and pour water upon it, and the salt. So it became Murayya, so heas went on to dip with it’.

citation.arabic_text: إِنَّ يُوسُفَ ( عليه السلام ) لَمَّا كَانَ فِي السِّجْنِ شَكَا إِلَى رَبِّهِ عَزَّ وَ جَلَّ أَكْلَ الْخُبْزِ وَحْدَهُ وَ سَأَلَ إِدَاماً يَأْتَدِمُ بِهِ وَ قَدْ كَانَ كَثُرَ عِنْدَهُ قِطَعُ الْخُبْزِ الْيَابِسِ فَأَمَرَهُ أَنْ يَأْخُذَ الْخُبْزَ وَ يَجْعَلَهُ فِي إِجَّانَةٍ وَ يَصُبَّ عَلَيْهِ الْمَاءَ وَ الْمِلْحَ فَصَارَ مُرِّيّاً فَجَعَلَ يَأْتَدِمُ بِهِ ( عليه السلام ) .
citation.translation: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Musa Bin Al Hassan, from Muhammad Bin Ahmad Bin Abu Mahmoud, from his father, (It has been narrated) raising it from Abu Abdullahasws having said that when Yusufas was in the prison, heas complained to hisas Lordazwj Mighty and Majestic of eating the bread on its own, and asked for a gravy to eat it with, and with himas used to be abundance of pieces of the dry bread’. So Heazwj Commanded himas that heas should take the bread and make it to be in a pot and pour water upon it, and the salt. So it became Murayya, so heas went on to dip with it’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: مجهول مرفوع - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (2/160)

text: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Ja’far Bin Muhammad, from Ibn Al Qaddah, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘Eat the (Olive) oil, and massage with the (Olive) oil, for it is from a Blessed tree’.

citation.arabic_text: قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ ( صلى الله عليه وآله ) كُلُوا الزَّيْتَ وَ ادَّهِنُوا بِالزَّيْتِ فَإِنَّهُ مِنْ شَجَرَةٍ مُبَارَكَةٍ .
citation.translation: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Ja’far Bin Muhammad, from Ibn Al Qaddah, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘Eat the (Olive) oil, and massage with the (Olive) oil, for it is from a Blessed tree’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: ضعيف على المشهور وآخره موثق - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (2/161)

text: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ibn fazzal, from Ibn Al Qaddah, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> – similar to it. Abu Ali Al Ashary, from Muhammad Bin Abdul Jabbar, from Ubeydullah Al Dahqan, from Dorost, from Ibrahim Bin Abdul Hameed, (It has been narrated) from Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘From what Adam<sup>as</sup> had bequeathed to Hibtallah<sup>as</sup>, his<sup>as</sup> son<sup>as</sup> was: ‘Eat the Olive for it is from a Blessed tree’.

citation.arabic_text: . أَبُو عَلِيٍّ الْأَشْعَرِيُّ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عَبْدِ الْجَبَّارِ عَنْ عُبَيْدِ اللَّهِ الدِّهْقَانِ عَنْ دُرُسْتَ عَنْ إِبْرَاهِيمَ بْنِ عَبْدِ الْحَمِيدِ عَنْ أَبِي الْحَسَنِ ( عليه السلام ) قَالَ كَانَ مِمَّا أَوْصَى بِهِ آدَمُ ( عليه السلام ) إِلَى هِبَةِ اللَّهِ ابْنِهِ أَنْ كُلِ الزَّيْتُونَ فَإِنَّهُ مِنْ شَجَرَةٍ مُبَارَكَةٍ .
citation.translation: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ibn fazzal, from Ibn Al Qaddah, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> – similar to it. Abu Ali Al Ashary, from Muhammad Bin Abdul Jabbar, from Ubeydullah Al Dahqan, from Dorost, from Ibrahim Bin Abdul Hameed, (It has been narrated) from Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘From what Adam<sup>as</sup> had bequeathed to Hibtallah<sup>as</sup>, his<sup>as</sup> son<sup>as</sup> was: ‘Eat the Olive for it is from a Blessed tree’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: مجهول - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (2/161)

text: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Abu Abdullah, from yaqoub Bin Yazeed, from Yahya Bin Al Mubarak, from Abdullah Bin Jabala, from Is’haq Bin Ammar, or someone else who said, ‘I said to Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, ‘They (the people) are saying the Olives stimulates the wind’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The Olives dispels the wind’.

citation.arabic_text: قُلْتُ لِأَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) إِنَّهُمْ يَقُولُونَ الزَّيْتُونُ يُهَيِّجُ الرِّيَاحَ فَقَالَ إِنَّ الزَّيْتُونَ يَطْرُدُ الرِّيَاحَ .
citation.translation: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Abu Abdullah, from yaqoub Bin Yazeed, from Yahya Bin Al Mubarak, from Abdullah Bin Jabala, from Is’haq Bin Ammar, or someone else who said, ‘I said to Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, ‘They (the people) are saying the Olives stimulates the wind’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The Olives dispels the wind’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: ساقط - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (22/161)

text: From him, from Mansour Bin Al Abbas, from Muhammad Bin Abdullah Bin Wasi’a, from Is’haq Bin Ismail, from Muhammad Bin Yazeed, from Abu Dawood Al Nkhai’e, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Massage with the oil, and use it as a sauce for it is a massager of the best ones and a sauce of the Chosen ones. It has been wiped with the Holiness twice, Blessed coming and Blessed returning, an illness does not harm with it’.

citation.arabic_text: قَالَ أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ ( عليه السلام ) ادَّهِنُوا بِالزَّيْتِ وَ أْتَدِمُوا بِهِ فَإِنَّهُ دُهْنَةُ الْأَخْيَارِ وَ إِدَامُ الْمُصْطَفَيْنَ مُسِحَتْ بِالْقُدْسِ مَرَّتَيْنِ بُورِكَتْ مُقْبِلَةً وَ بُورِكَتْ مُدْبِرَةً لَا يَضُرُّ مَعَهَا دَاءٌ .
citation.translation: From him, from Mansour Bin Al Abbas, from Muhammad Bin Abdullah Bin Wasi’a, from Is’haq Bin Ismail, from Muhammad Bin Yazeed, from Abu Dawood Al Nkhai’e, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Massage with the oil, and use it as a sauce for it is a massager of the best ones and a sauce of the Chosen ones. It has been wiped with the Holiness twice, Blessed coming and Blessed returning, an illness does not harm with it’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: ضعيف - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (22/161)

text: Mansour Bin Al Abbas, from Ibrahim Bin Muhammad al Zara’a Al Basry, from a man, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, said, ‘We mentioned the Olives in his<sup>asws</sup> presence, so the man said, ‘It brings the wind’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘No, but it dispels the wind’.

citation.arabic_text: ذَكَرْنَا عِنْدَهُ الزَّيْتُونَ فَقَالَ الرَّجُلُ يَجْلِبُ الرِّيَاحَ فَقَالَ لَا بَلْ يَطْرُدُ الرِّيَاحَ .
citation.translation: Mansour Bin Al Abbas, from Ibrahim Bin Muhammad al Zara’a Al Basry, from a man, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, said, ‘We mentioned the Olives in his<sup>asws</sup> presence, so the man said, ‘It brings the wind’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘No, but it dispels the wind’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: ضعيف - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (22/162)

text: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Al Nowfaly, from Al Jareery, from Abdul Momin Al Ansary, (It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘The oil is a massager of the righteous, and a sauce of the best ones. There is Blessing in it coming, and a Blessing in it returning, immersed in the Holiness twice’.

citation.arabic_text: قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ ( صلى الله عليه وآله ) الزَّيْتُ دُهْنُ الْأَبْرَارِ وَ إِدَامُ الْأَخْيَارِ بُورِكَ فِيهِ مُقْبِلًا وَ بُورِكَ فِيهِ مُدْبِراً انْغَمَسَ بِالْقُدْسِ مَرَّتَيْنِ .
citation.translation: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Al Nowfaly, from Al Jareery, from Abdul Momin Al Ansary, (It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘The oil is a massager of the righteous, and a sauce of the best ones. There is Blessing in it coming, and a Blessing in it returning, immersed in the Holiness twice’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: ضعيف على المشهور - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (2/162)

text: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Abdullah Bin Ja’far, raising it, said, ‘Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The Olives increase in the water’.

citation.arabic_text: قَالَ أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) الزَّيْتُونُ يَزِيدُ فِي الْمَاءِ .
citation.translation: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Abdullah Bin Ja’far, raising it, said, ‘Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The Olives increase in the water’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: مرفوع - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (22/162)

text: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Abu Nasr, from Hammad Bin Usman, from Muhammad Bin Sowqa, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘The people are not healed with the likes of (healing with) the honey’.

citation.arabic_text: مَا اسْتَشْفَى النَّاسُ بِمِثْلِ الْعَسَلِ .
citation.translation: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Abu Nasr, from Hammad Bin Usman, from Muhammad Bin Sowqa, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘The people are not healed with the likes of (healing with) the honey’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: ضعيف على المشهور - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (2/162)

text: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Al Qasim Bin Yahya, from his grandfather Al Hassan Bin Rashid, from Muhammad Bin Muslim, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws having said: ‘Amir Al-Momineenasws said: ‘Licking the honey is a healing from every illness. Allahazwj Mighty and Majestic Says [16:69] There comes forth from its belly a beverage of many colours, in which there is healing for the people, and it is with the recitation of the Quran and chewing frankincense[1478] melts the phlegm’.

citation.arabic_text: قَالَ أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ ( عليه السلام ) لَعْقُ الْعَسَلِ شِفَاءٌ مِنْ كُلِّ دَاءٍ قَالَ اللَّهُ عَزَّ وَ جَلَّ يَخْرُجُ مِنْ بُطُونِها شَرابٌ مُخْتَلِفٌ أَلْوانُهُ فِيهِ شِفاءٌ لِلنَّاسِ وَ هُوَ مَعَ قِرَاءَةِ الْقُرْآنِ وَ مَضْغِ اللُّبَانِ يُذِيبُ الْبَلْغَمَ .
citation.translation: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Al Qasim Bin Yahya, from his grandfather Al Hassan Bin Rashid, from Muhammad Bin Muslim, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws having said: ‘Amir Al-Momineenasws said: ‘Licking the honey is a healing from every illness. Allahazwj Mighty and Majestic Says [16:69] There comes forth from its belly a beverage of many colours, in which there is healing for the people, and it is with the recitation of the Quran and chewing frankincense[1478] melts the phlegm’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: ضعيف - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (22/162)

text: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hisham Bin Salim, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> liked the honey’.

citation.arabic_text: كَانَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ ( صلى الله عليه وآله ) يُعْجِبُهُ الْعَسَلُ .
citation.translation: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hisham Bin Salim, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> liked the honey’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: حسن - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (22/163)

text: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Abdullah Bin Ja’far, from Muhammad Bin Isa, from Ibrahim Bin Abdul Hameed, from Sukeyn, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘The Prophet<sup>saww</sup> used to eat the honey and he<sup>saww</sup> was saying: ‘A Verse from the Quran and chewing the frankincense melts the phlegm’.

citation.arabic_text: كَانَ النَّبِيُّ ( صلى الله عليه وآله ) يَأْكُلُ الْعَسَلَ وَ يَقُولُ آيَاتٌ مِنَ الْقُرْآنِ وَ مَضْغُ اللُّبَانِ يُذِيبُ الْبَلْغَمَ .
citation.translation: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Abdullah Bin Ja’far, from Muhammad Bin Isa, from Ibrahim Bin Abdul Hameed, from Sukeyn, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘The Prophet<sup>saww</sup> used to eat the honey and he<sup>saww</sup> was saying: ‘A Verse from the Quran and chewing the frankincense melts the phlegm’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: مجهول - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (22/163)

text: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Ali Bin Hassan, from Musa Bin Bakr, (It has been narrated) from Abu Al Hassan<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘A patient cannot be healed like (he can) with the likes of honey’.

citation.arabic_text: مَا اسْتَشْفَى مَرِيضٌ بِمِثْلِ الْعَسَلِ .
citation.translation: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Ali Bin Hassan, from Musa Bin Bakr, (It has been narrated) from Abu Al Hassan<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘A patient cannot be healed like (he can) with the likes of honey’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: ضعيف على المشهور - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (2/163)

text: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Ali Bin Hassan, from Musa Bin Bakr who said, ‘Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> the 1st used to frequently eat the sugar at sleep time’.

citation.arabic_text: كَثِيراً مَا يَأْكُلُ السُّكَّرَ عِنْدَ النَّوْمِ .
citation.translation: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Ali Bin Hassan, from Musa Bin Bakr who said, ‘Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> the 1st used to frequently eat the sugar at sleep time’.

text: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Abdul Aziz Al abdy who said, ‘Abu Abdullahasws said: ‘While it was that the cheese harms from everything and does not benefit, so the sugar benefits from everything and does not harm from anything’ (it is the Suleymaniyya sugar, see the Hadeeth below).

citation.arabic_text: قَالَ أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) لَئِنْ كَانَ الْجُبُنُّ يَضُرُّ مِنْ كُلِّ شَيْ‏ءٍ وَ لَا يَنْفَعُ فَإِنَّ السُّكَّرَ يَنْفَعُ مِنْ كُلِّ شَيْ‏ءٍ وَ لَا يَضُرُّ مِنْ شَيْ‏ءٍ .

citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: ضعيف - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (22/163)

text: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhamad, from Muhammad Bin Ahmad Al Azdy, from one of our companions, raising it, said, ‘A man complained to Abu Abdullahasws, so he said, ‘I am a complaining man’. So heasws said: ‘Where is it from the Blessed?’ So I said, ‘May I be sacrificed for youasws! And what is the Blessed?’ Heasws said: ‘The sugar’. I said, ‘Which sugar, may I be sacrificed for youasws?’ Heasws said: ‘Your Suleymaniyya, this’.

citation.arabic_text: شَكَا رَجُلٌ إِلَى أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) فَقَالَ إِنِّي رَجُلٌ شَاكِي فَقَالَ أَيْنَ هُوَ عَنِ الْمُبَارَكِ فَقُلْتُ جُعِلْتُ فِدَاكَ وَ مَا الْمُبَارَكُ قَالَ السُّكَّرُ قُلْتُ أَيُّ السُّكَّرِ جُعِلْتُ فِدَاكَ قَالَ سُلَيْمَانِيُّكُمْ هَذَا .
citation.translation: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhamad, from Muhammad Bin Ahmad Al Azdy, from one of our companions, raising it, said, ‘A man complained to Abu Abdullahasws, so he said, ‘I am a complaining man’. So heasws said: ‘Where is it from the Blessed?’ So I said, ‘May I be sacrificed for youasws! And what is the Blessed?’ Heasws said: ‘The sugar’. I said, ‘Which sugar, may I be sacrificed for youasws?’ Heasws said: ‘Your Suleymaniyya, this’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: مرفوع - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (22/163)

text: Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Muhammad Bin Sahl, (It has been narrated) from al-Rezaasws, or said, ‘one of our companions from Al-Rezaasws, having said: ‘The Al-Tabarzad sugar eats up the phlegm with a devouring’.

citation.arabic_text: بَعْضُ أَصْحَابِنَا عَنِ الرِّضَا ( عليه السلام ) قَالَ السُّكَّرُ الطَّبَرْزَدُ يَأْكُلُ الْبَلْغَمَ أَكْلًا .
citation.translation: Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Muhammad Bin Sahl, (It has been narrated) from al-Rezaasws, or said, ‘one of our companions from Al-Rezaasws, having said: ‘The Al-Tabarzad sugar eats up the phlegm with a devouring’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: مجهول - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (22/164)

text: Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Al Hassan Bin Ali Bin Al no’man, from one of our companions who said, ‘I complained to Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> of the pain. So he<sup>asws</sup> said to me: ‘When you go to your bed so eat two (lumps of) sugar’. He said, ‘So I did that, and I was cured. So I informed one of the physicians and he was the most splendid of the people of our city, so he said, ‘From where did Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> recognise this. This is from the treasures of our knowledge. However, he<sup>asws</sup> is the owner of Books, so it is befitting that he<sup>asws</sup> happened to have found it in one of his<sup>asws</sup> Books’.

citation.arabic_text: شَكَوْتُ إِلَى أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) الْوَجَعَ فَقَالَ لِي إِذَا أَوَيْتَ إِلَى فِرَاشِكَ فَكُلْ سُكَّرَتَيْنِ قَالَ فَفَعَلْتُ ذَلِكَ فَبَرَأْتُ فَخَبَّرْتُ بَعْضَ الْمُتَطَبِّبِينَ وَ كَانَ أَفْرَهَ أَهْلِ بِلَادِنَا فَقَالَ مِنْ أَيْنَ عَرَفَ أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) هَذَا هَذَا مِنْ مَخْزُونِ عِلْمِنَا أَمَا إِنَّهُ صَاحِبُ كُتُبٍ فَيَنْبَغِي أَنْ يَكُونَ أَصَابَهُ فِي بَعْضِ كُتُبِهِ .
citation.translation: Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Al Hassan Bin Ali Bin Al no’man, from one of our companions who said, ‘I complained to Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> of the pain. So I informed one of the physicians and he was the most splendid of the people of our city, so he said, ‘From where did Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> recognise this. This is from the treasures of our knowledge. However, he<sup>asws</sup> is the owner of Books, so it is befitting that he<sup>asws</sup> happened to have found it in one of his<sup>asws</sup> Books’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: مرسل - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (2/164)

text: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Abu Abdullah, from his father, from Sa’dan Bin Muslim, from Mo’tab who said, ‘When I had dinner with Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, he<sup>asws</sup> said to me: ‘When you enter the storage so seek out for me<sup>asws</sup>, two (lumps of) sugar’. So I said, ‘May I be sacrificed for you<sup>asws</sup>! There is nothing there’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said, ‘Enter, woe be unto you!’ So I entered and found two (lumps of) sugar, so came with these to him<sup>asws</sup>’.

citation.arabic_text: لَمَّا تَعَشَّى أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) قَالَ لِي إِذَا دَخَلْتَ الْخِزَانَةَ فَاطْلُبْ لِي سُكَّرَتَيْنِ فَقُلْتُ جُعِلْتُ فِدَاكَ لَيْسَ ثَمَّ شَيْ‏ءٌ فَقَالَ ادْخُلْ وَيْحَكَ قَالَ فَدَخَلْتُ فَوَجَدْتُ سُكَّرَتَيْنِ فَأَتَيْتُهُ بِهِمَا .

text: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, raising it, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws, said, ‘A man complained to himasws of the epidemic, so heasws said to him: ‘And where are you from the good, the Blessed?’ He said, ‘I said, ‘And what is the good, the Blessed?’ So heasws said: ‘Your Suleymaniyya (a type of sugar), this’. Abu Abdullahasws said: ‘The first one to take the sugar was Suleymanas Bin Dawoodas’.

citation.arabic_text: شَكَا إِلَيْهِ رَجُلٌ الْوَبَاءَ فَقَالَ لَهُ وَ أَيْنَ أَنْتَ عَنِ الطَّيِّبِ الْمُبَارَكِ قَالَ قُلْتُ وَ مَا الطَّيِّبُ الْمُبَارَكُ فَقَالَ سُلَيْمَانِيُّكُمْ هَذَا قَالَ فَقَالَ أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) إِنَّ أَوَّلَ مَنِ اتَّخَذَ السُّكَّرَ سُلَيْمَانُ بْنُ دَاوُدَ ( عليه السلام ) .
citation.translation: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, raising it, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws, said, ‘A man complained to himasws of the epidemic, so heasws said to him: ‘And where are you from the good, the Blessed?’ He said, ‘I said, ‘And what is the good, the Blessed?’ So heasws said: ‘Your Suleymaniyya (a type of sugar), this’. Abu Abdullahasws said: ‘The first one to take the sugar was Suleymanas Bin Dawoodas’.

text: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Musa Bin Al Hassan, from Ubeyd Al Khayyat, from Abdul Aziz, from Ibn Sinan, from A man, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘If a man has a thousand Dirhams with him, not having with him other than it, then he buys sugar with (all of) it, he would not have been extravagant’.

citation.arabic_text: لَوْ أَنَّ رَجُلًا عِنْدَهُ أَلْفُ دِرْهَمٍ لَيْسَ عِنْدَهُ غَيْرُهَا ثُمَّ اشْتَرَى بِهَا سُكَّراً لَمْ يَكُنْ مُسْرِفاً .
citation.translation: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Musa Bin Al Hassan, from Ubeyd Al Khayyat, from Abdul Aziz, from Ibn Sinan, from A man, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘If a man has a thousand Dirhams with him, not having with him other than it, then he buys sugar with (all of) it, he would not have been extravagant’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: ضعيف على المشهور - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (22/164)

text: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Abu Abdullah, from a number of our companions, from Ali Bin Asbaat, from Yahya Bin Bashir Al Nabbal who said, ‘Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> to my father: ‘A Bashir! By which thing are you curing your sick ones?’ So he said, ‘By these bitter medicines’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said to him: ‘No. When one of you is sick, so take the white sugar, pound it and pour the cold water over it, make him drink it, for the One Who<sup>azwj</sup> Made the healing to be in the bitter is Able to Make it to be in the sweet’.

citation.arabic_text: قَالَ أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) لِأَبِي يَا بَشِيرُ بِأَيِّ شَيْ‏ءٍ تُدَاوُونَ مَرْضَاكُمْ فَقَالَ بِهَذِهِ الْأَدْوِيَةِ الْمِرَارِ فَقَالَ لَهُ لَا إِذَا مَرِضَ أَحَدُكُمْ فَخُذِ السُّكَّرَ الْأَبْيَضَ فَدُقَّهُ وَ صُبَّ عَلَيْهِ الْمَاءَ الْبَارِدَ وَ اسْقِهِ إِيَّاهُ فَإِنَّ الَّذِي جَعَلَ الشِّفَاءَ فِي الْمَرَارَةِ قَادِرٌ أَنْ يَجْعَلَهُ فِي الْحَلَاوَةِ .
citation.translation: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Abu Abdullah, from a number of our companions, from Ali Bin Asbaat, from Yahya Bin Bashir Al Nabbal who said, ‘Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> to my father: ‘A Bashir! By which thing are you curing your sick ones?’ So he said, ‘By these bitter medicines’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said to him: ‘No. When one of you is sick, so take the white sugar, pound it and pour the cold water over it, make him drink it, for the One Who<sup>azwj</sup> Made the healing to be in the bitter is Able to Make it to be in the sweet’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: مرسل مجهول - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (22/165)

citation.arabic_text: السُّكَّرُ الطَّبَرْزَدُ يَأْكُلُ الْبَلْغَمَ أَكْلًا .

text: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Ahmad Bin Asheym, from one of our companions who said, ‘One of our family members had fever, so the physicians prescribed Al-Ghafis (a herb) for him. So we made him drink it, but he did not benefit from it. So I complained of that to Abu Abdullahasws, so heasws said: ‘Allahazwj has not Made a healing in anything from the bitter. Take a (lump of) sugar and a half, so grind it in a vessel and pour water over it until it melts in it, and place iron over it, and apportion it from the beginning of the night. So when it becomes (a solution), so take it with your hand and make him drink it. So when it is the second night, so make it with two (lumps of) sugar and a half, and apportion it just as you had done beforehand, and make him drink it. And when it was the third night, so take three (lumps of) sugar and a half, and apportion it like that’. He (the narrator) said, ‘So I did, and Allahazwj Mighty and Majestic Healed our sick’.

citation.arabic_text: حُمَّ بَعْضُ أَهْلِنَا فَوَصَفَ لَهُ الْمُتَطَبِّبُونَ الْغَافِثَ فَسَقَيْنَاهُ فَلَمْ يَنْتَفِعْ بِهِ فَشَكَوْتُ ذَلِكَ إِلَى أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) فَقَالَ مَا جَعَلَ اللَّهُ فِي شَيْ‏ءٍ مِنَ الْمُرِّ شِفَاءً خُذْ سُكَّرَةً وَ نِصْفاً فَصَيِّرْهَا فِي إِنَاءٍ وَ صُبَّ عَلَيْهَا الْمَاءَ حَتَّى يَغْمُرَهَا وَ ضَعْ عَلَيْهَا حَدِيدَةً وَ نَجِّمْهَا مِنْ أَوَّلِ اللَّيْلِ فَإِذَا أَصْبَحْتَ فَأَمْرِسْهَا بِيَدِكَ وَ اسْقِهِ فَإِذَا كَانَتِ اللَّيْلَةُ الثَّانِيَةُ فَصَيِّرْهَا سُكَّرَتَيْنِ وَ نِصْفاً وَ نَجِّمْهَا كَمَا فَعَلْتَ وَ اسْقِهِ وَ إِذَا كَانَتِ اللَّيْلَةُ الثَّالِثَةُ فَخُذْ ثَلَاثَ سُكَّرَاتٍ وَ نِصْفاً وَ نَجِّمْهُنَّ مِثْلَ ذَلِكَ قَالَ فَفَعَلْتُ فَشَفَى اللَّهُ عَزَّ وَ جَلَّ مَرِيضَنَا .
citation.translation: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Ahmad Bin Asheym, from one of our companions who said, ‘One of our family members had fever, so the physicians prescribed Al-Ghafis (a herb) for him. So we made him drink it, but he did not benefit from it. So I complained of that to Abu Abdullahasws, so heasws said: ‘Allahazwj has not Made a healing in anything from the bitter. Take a (lump of) sugar and a half, so grind it in a vessel and pour water over it until it melts in it, and place iron over it, and apportion it from the beginning of the night. So when it becomes (a solution), so take it with your hand and make him drink it. So when it is the second night, so make it with two (lumps of) sugar and a half, and apportion it just as you had done beforehand, and make him drink it. And when it was the third night, so take three (lumps of) sugar and a half, and apportion it like that’. He (the narrator) said, ‘So I did, and Allahazwj Mighty and Majestic Healed our sick’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: مجهول - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (22/165)

text: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Al Nowfaly, from Al Sakuny, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The margarine of the cow is a healing’.

citation.arabic_text: قَالَ أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ ( عليه السلام ) سُمُونُ الْبَقَرِ شِفَاءٌ .
citation.translation: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Al Nowfaly, from Al Sakuny, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The margarine of the cow is a healing’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: ضعيف على المشهور - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (2/166)

text: From him, from his father, from Al Nowfaly, from Al Sakuny, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The margarine is a medicine, and it is better in the summer than it is in the winter, and none enters the inside, the likes of it’.

citation.arabic_text: قَالَ أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ ( عليه السلام ) السَّمْنُ دَوَاءٌ وَ هُوَ فِي الصَّيْفِ خَيْرٌ مِنْهُ فِي الشِّتَاءِ وَ مَا دَخَلَ جَوْفاً مِثْلُهُ .

citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: ضعيف على المشهور - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (2/166)

text: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Abu Abdullah, from his father, from Al Muttalib Bin Ziyad, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘The best of the sauces is the margarine’.

citation.arabic_text: نِعْمَ الْإِدَامُ السَّمْنُ .
citation.translation: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Abu Abdullah, from his father, from Al Muttalib Bin Ziyad, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘The best of the sauces is the margarine’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: صحيح - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (22/166)

text: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hammad Bin Usman, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘When the man reaches fifty years, so he should not go to sleep and inside him is something from the margarine’.

citation.arabic_text: إِذَا بَلَغَ الرَّجُلُ خَمْسِينَ سَنَةً فَلَا يَبِيتَنَّ وَ فِي جَوْفِهِ شَيْ‏ءٌ مِنَ السَّمْنِ .
citation.translation: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hammad Bin Usman, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘When the man reaches fifty years, so he should not go to sleep and inside him is something from the margarine’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: حسن - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (22/166)

text: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Al Washa, from Hammad Bin Usman who said, ‘I was in the presence of Abu Abdullahasws, so an old man from the people of Al-Iraq spoke to himasws, so heasws said to him: ‘What is the matter Iasws your speech as having changed?’ So he said to himasws, ‘The front (teeth) of my mouth have fallen off so my speech is deficient’. So Abu Abdullahasws said to him: ‘And Iasws as well, some of myasws teeth have fallen off to the extent that the Satanla whispers unto measws so hela is saying to measws, ‘When the remaining (teeth) go away, so which what thing would youasws be eating?’ So Iasws am saying: ‘There is not Strength except by Allahazwj’. Then heasws said to me: ‘It is upon you with (eating) Al-Sareyd, for it is corrective, and keep away from the margarine, for it is not compatible with the old man’.

citation.arabic_text: كُنْتُ عِنْدَ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) فَكَلَّمَهُ شَيْخٌ مِنْ أَهْلِ الْعِرَاقِ فَقَالَ لَهُ مَا لِي أَرَى كَلَامَكَ مُتَغَيِّراً فَقَالَ لَهُ سَقَطَتْ مَقَادِيمُ فَمِي فَنَقَصَ كَلَامِي فَقَالَ لَهُ أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) وَ أَنَا أَيْضاً قَدْ سَقَطَ بَعْضُ أَسْنَانِي حَتَّى إِنَّهُ لَيُوَسْوِسُ إِلَيَّ الشَّيْطَانُ فَيَقُولُ لِي إِذَا ذَهَبَتِ الْبَقِيَّةُ فَبِأَيِّ شَيْ‏ءٍ تَأْكُلُ فَأَقُولُ لَا حَوْلَ وَ لَا قُوَّةَ إِلَّا بِاللَّهِ ثُمَّ قَالَ لِي عَلَيْكَ بِالثَّرِيدِ فَإِنَّهُ صَالِحٌ وَ اجْتَنِبِ السَّمْنَ فَإِنَّهُ لَا يُلَائِمُ الشَّيْخَ .
citation.translation: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Al Washa, from Hammad Bin Usman who said, ‘I was in the presence of Abu Abdullahasws, so an old man from the people of Al-Iraq spoke to himasws, so heasws said to him: ‘What is the matter Iasws your speech as having changed?’ So he said to himasws, ‘The front (teeth) of my mouth have fallen off so my speech is deficient’. So Abu Abdullahasws said to him: ‘And Iasws as well, some of myasws teeth have fallen off to the extent that the Satanla whispers unto measws so hela is saying to measws, ‘When the remaining (teeth) go away, so which what thing would youasws be eating?’ So Iasws am saying: ‘There is not Strength except by Allahazwj’. Then heasws said to me: ‘It is upon you with (eating) Al-Sareyd, for it is corrective, and keep away from the margarine, for it is not compatible with the old man’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: صحيح - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (22/166)

text: Ali Bin Muhammad Bin Bundar, from Ahmad Bin Abu Abdullah, from his father, from the one who mentioned it, from Abu Hafs Al Abbar, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘The margarine, nothing like it enters the inside, and I<sup>asws</sup> dislike it for the old man’.

citation.arabic_text: السَّمْنُ مَا دَخَلَ جَوْفاً مِثْلُهُ وَ إِنَّنِي لَأَكْرَهُهُ لِلشَّيْخِ .
citation.translation: Ali Bin Muhammad Bin Bundar, from Ahmad Bin Abu Abdullah, from his father, from the one who mentioned it, from Abu Hafs Al Abbar, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘The margarine, nothing like it enters the inside, and I<sup>asws</sup> dislike it for the old man’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: مجهول - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (22/167)

text: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Al Hakam, from Al Rabie Bin Muhammad al Musly, from Abdullah Bin Suleyman, (It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘It never happened that Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> would eat food nor drink a drink except that he<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘O Allah<sup>azwj</sup>! Bless for us in it, and Change it for that which is better than it’, except for the milk, for he<sup>saww</sup> was saying: ‘O Allah<sup>azwj</sup>! Bless for us in it, and Increase it for us from it’.

citation.arabic_text: لَمْ يَكُنْ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ ( صلى الله عليه وآله ) يَأْكُلُ طَعَاماً وَ لَا يَشْرَبُ شَرَاباً إِلَّا قَالَ اللَّهُمَّ بَارِكْ لَنَا فِيهِ وَ أَبْدِلْنَا بِهِ خَيْراً مِنْهُ إِلَّا اللَّبَنَ فَإِنَّهُ كَانَ يَقُولُ اللَّهُمَّ بَارِكْ لَنَا فِيهِ وَ زِدْنَا مِنْهُ .
citation.translation: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Al Hakam, from Al Rabie Bin Muhammad al Musly, from Abdullah Bin Suleyman, (It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘It never happened that Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> would eat food nor drink a drink except that he<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘O Allah<sup>azwj</sup>! Bless for us in it, and Change it for that which is better than it’, except for the milk, for he<sup>saww</sup> was saying: ‘O Allah<sup>azwj</sup>! Bless for us in it, and Increase it for us from it’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: مجهول - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (2/167)

text: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Salma Bin Al Khattab, from Abbad Bin Yaqoub, from Ubeyd Bin Muhammad, from Muhamad Bin Qays, (It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Milk of the black sheep is better than milk of the red ones; and milk of the red cow is better than the milk of the black ones’.

citation.arabic_text: لَبَنُ الشَّاةِ السَّوْدَاءِ خَيْرٌ مِنْ لَبَنِ حَمْرَاوَيْنِ وَ لَبَنُ الْبَقَرِ الْحَمْرَاءِ خَيْرٌ مِنْ لَبَنِ سَوْدَاوَيْنِ .
citation.translation: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Salma Bin Al Khattab, from Abbad Bin Yaqoub, from Ubeyd Bin Muhammad, from Muhamad Bin Qays, (It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Milk of the black sheep is better than milk of the red ones; and milk of the red cow is better than the milk of the black ones’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: ضعيف - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (22/167)

text: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Ja’far Bin Muhammad Al Ash’ary, from Ibn Al Qaddah, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Whenever the Prophet<sup>saww</sup> drank the milk, said: ‘O Allah<sup>azwj</sup>! Bless for us in it, and Increase for us from it’.

citation.arabic_text: كَانَ النَّبِيُّ ( صلى الله عليه وآله ) إِذَا شَرِبَ اللَّبَنَ قَالَ اللَّهُمَّ بَارِكْ لَنَا فِيهِ وَ زِدْنَا مِنْهُ .
citation.translation: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Ja’far Bin Muhammad Al Ash’ary, from Ibn Al Qaddah, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Whenever the Prophet<sup>saww</sup> drank the milk, said: ‘O Allah<sup>azwj</sup>! Bless for us in it, and Increase for us from it’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: ضعيف على المشهور - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (22/167)

text: Al Husayn Bin Muhammad, from Al Sayyari, from Ubeydullah Bin abu Abdullah Al Farsy, from the one who mentioned it, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, said, ‘A man said to him<sup>asws</sup>, ‘I drank milk so it harmed me’. So Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said to him: ‘No, by Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, the milk does not harm at all, but you have eaten something else with it, so it harmed you, that which you ate, so you thought that, that (harm) is from the milk’.

citation.arabic_text: قَالَ لَهُ رَجُلٌ إِنِّي أَكَلْتُ لَبَناً فَضَرَّنِي قَالَ فَقَالَ لَهُ أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) لَا وَ اللَّهِ مَا يَضُرُّ لَبَنٌ قَطُّ وَ لَكِنَّكَ أَكَلْتَهُ مَعَ غَيْرِهِ فَضَرَّكَ الَّذِي أَكَلْتَهُ فَظَنَنْتَ أَنَّ ذَلِكَ مِنَ اللَّبَنِ .
citation.translation: Al Husayn Bin Muhammad, from Al Sayyari, from Ubeydullah Bin abu Abdullah Al Farsy, from the one who mentioned it, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, said, ‘A man said to him<sup>asws</sup>, ‘I drank milk so it harmed me’. So Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said to him: ‘No, by Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, the milk does not harm at all, but you have eaten something else with it, so it harmed you, that which you ate, so you thought that, that (harm) is from the milk’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: ضعيف على المشهور - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (2/167)

text: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Al Nowfaly, from Al Sakuny, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws having said: ‘Rasool-Allahsaww said: ‘There is no one who chokes by drinking the milk because Allahazwj Mighty and Majestic is Saying [16:66] pure milk, palatable for the drinkers’.

citation.arabic_text: قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ ( صلى الله عليه وآله ) لَيْسَ أَحَدٌ يَغَصُّ بِشُرْبِ اللَّبَنِ لِأَنَّ اللَّهَ عَزَّ وَ جَلَّ يَقُولُ لَبَناً خالِصاً سائِغاً لِلشَّارِبِينَ .
citation.translation: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Al Nowfaly, from Al Sakuny, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws having said: ‘Rasool-Allahsaww said: ‘There is no one who chokes by drinking the milk because Allahazwj Mighty and Majestic is Saying [16:66] pure milk, palatable for the drinkers’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: ضعيف على المشهور - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (2/168)

text: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, form Usman Bin Isa, from Khalid Bin Najeeh, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws having said: ‘The milk is a meal of the Mursil Prophetsas’.

citation.arabic_text: اللَّبَنُ طَعَامُ الْمُرْسَلِينَ .
citation.translation: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, form Usman Bin Isa, from Khalid Bin Najeeh, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws having said: ‘The milk is a meal of the Mursil Prophetsas’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: مجهول - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (22/168)

text: Ali Bin Muhammad Bin Bundar, and someone else, from Ahmad Bin Abu Abdullah, from his father, from Al Qasim Bin Muhammad Al Jowhary, from Abu Al Hassan Al Asbahany who said, ‘I was in the presence of Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, so a man said to him<sup>asws</sup> and I was listening, ‘May I be sacrificed for you<sup>asws</sup>! I find the weakness in my body’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘It is upon you with (drinking) the milk, for it builds the flesh and strengthens the bones’.

citation.arabic_text: كُنْتُ عِنْدَ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) فَقَالَ لَهُ رَجُلٌ وَ أَنَا أَسْمَعُ جُعِلْتُ فِدَاكَ إِنِّي أَجِدُ الضَّعْفَ فِي بَدَنِي فَقَالَ لَهُ عَلَيْكَ بِاللَّبَنِ فَإِنَّهُ يُنْبِتُ اللَّحْمَ وَ يَشُدُّ الْعَظْمَ .
citation.translation: Ali Bin Muhammad Bin Bundar, and someone else, from Ahmad Bin Abu Abdullah, from his father, from Al Qasim Bin Muhammad Al Jowhary, from Abu Al Hassan Al Asbahany who said, ‘I was in the presence of Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, so a man said to him<sup>asws</sup> and I was listening, ‘May I be sacrificed for you<sup>asws</sup>! I find the weakness in my body’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘It is upon you with (drinking) the milk, for it builds the flesh and strengthens the bones’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: ضعيف - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (22/168)

text: From him, from Nuh Bin Shuayb, from the one who mentioned it, (It has been narrated) from Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> the 1st having said: ‘The one to whom the water of the back changes, so it would be beneficial for him, the milk and the honey’.

citation.arabic_text: مَنْ تَغَيَّرَ عَلَيْهِ مَاءُ الظَّهْرِ فَإِنَّهُ يَنْفَعُ لَهُ اللَّبَنُ الْحَلِيبُ وَ الْعَسَلُ .
citation.translation: From him, from Nuh Bin Shuayb, from the one who mentioned it, (It has been narrated) from Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> the 1st having said: ‘The one to whom the water of the back changes, so it would be beneficial for him, the milk and the honey’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: مرسل - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (22/168)

text: From him, from Muhammad Bin Ali, from Abdul Rahman Bin Abu Hashim, from Muhammad Bin Ali Bin Abu Hamza, from Abu Baseer who said, ‘We ate with Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, so they came with camel meat. So we thought it is from his<sup>asws</sup> house. So we ate, then they came with bowl of milk. So we drank from it. Then he<sup>asws</sup> said to me: ‘Drink, O Abu Muhammad!’ So I tasted it, and I said, ‘May I be sacrificed for you<sup>asws</sup>, milk!’ So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘It is the nature’. Then they came to us with dates, so we ate it’.

citation.arabic_text: أَكَلْنَا مَعَ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) فَأُتِينَا بِلَحْمِ جَزُورٍ فَظَنَنْتُ أَنَّهُ مِنْ بَيْتِهِ فَأَكَلْنَا ثُمَّ أُتِينَا بِعُسٍّ مِنْ لَبَنٍ فَشَرِبَ مِنْهُ ثُمَّ قَالَ لِي اشْرَبْ يَا أَبَا مُحَمَّدٍ فَذُقْتُهُ فَقُلْتُ جُعِلْتُ فِدَاكَ لَبَنٌ فَقَالَ إِنَّهَا الْفِطْرَةُ ثُمَّ أُتِينَا بِتَمْرٍ فَأَكَلْنَاهُ .
citation.translation: From him, from Muhammad Bin Ali, from Abdul Rahman Bin Abu Hashim, from Muhammad Bin Ali Bin Abu Hamza, from Abu Baseer who said, ‘We ate with Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, so they came with camel meat. So we thought it is from his<sup>asws</sup> house. So we ate, then they came with bowl of milk. So we drank from it. Then he<sup>asws</sup> said to me: ‘Drink, O Abu Muhammad!’ So I tasted it, and I said, ‘May I be sacrificed for you<sup>asws</sup>, milk!’ So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘It is the nature’. Then they came to us with dates, so we ate it’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: ضعيف على المشهور - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (22/168)

text: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Al Nowfaly, from Al Sakuny, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The cow milk is a medication’.

citation.arabic_text: قَالَ أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ ( عليه السلام ) أَلْبَانُ الْبَقَرِ دَوَاءٌ .
citation.translation: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Al Nowfaly, from Al Sakuny, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The cow milk is a medication’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: ضعيف على المشهور - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (22/169)

text: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Khalid, from Yahya Bin Ibrahim Bin Abu Al Balaad, from his father, from his grandfather who said, ‘I complained to Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> of stomach pain, so he<sup>asws</sup> said to me:’ What prevents you from drinking the cow milk? Do you drink it at all?’ So I said to him<sup>asws</sup>, ‘Yes, repeatedly’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘How do you find it as?’ So I said, ‘I find it as repairing for the stomach, and a covering for fat of the two kidneys, and making me desirous for the food’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘If it was its days, I<sup>asws</sup> and you would have gone out to Yanba’a until we drink it’.

citation.arabic_text: شَكَوْتُ إِلَى أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ ( عليه السلام ) ذِرْباً وَجَدْتُهُ فَقَالَ لِي مَا يَمْنَعُكَ مِنْ شُرْبِ أَلْبَانِ الْبَقَرِ فَقَالَ لِي أَ شَرِبْتَهَا قَطُّ فَقُلْتُ لَهُ نَعَمْ مِرَاراً فَقَالَ كَيْفَ وَجَدْتَهَا فَقُلْتُ وَجَدْتُهَا تَدْبُغُ الْمَعِدَةَ وَ تَكْسُو الْكُلْيَتَيْنِ الشَّحْمَ وَ تُشَهِّي الطَّعَامَ فَقَالَ لِي لَوْ كَانَتْ أَيَّامُهُ لَخَرَجْتُ أَنَا وَ أَنْتَ إِلَى يَنْبُعَ حَتَّى نَشْرَبَهُ .
citation.translation: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Khalid, from Yahya Bin Ibrahim Bin Abu Al Balaad, from his father, from his grandfather who said, ‘I complained to Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> of stomach pain, so he<sup>asws</sup> said to me:’ What prevents you from drinking the cow milk? Do you drink it at all?’ So I said to him<sup>asws</sup>, ‘Yes, repeatedly’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘How do you find it as?’ So I said, ‘I find it as repairing for the stomach, and a covering for fat of the two kidneys, and making me desirous for the food’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘If it was its days, I<sup>asws</sup> and you would have gone out to Yanba’a until we drink it’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: مجهول - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (2/170)

text: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bnin Abu Nasr, from Aban Bin Usman, from Zurara, (It has been narrated) from one of the two (5<sup>th</sup> or 6<sup>th</sup> Imam<sup>asws</sup>) having said: ‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘It is upon you with (drinking) the cow milk, for it mingles with every tree’.

citation.arabic_text: قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ ( صلى الله عليه وآله ) عَلَيْكُمْ بِأَلْبَانِ الْبَقَرِ فَإِنَّهَا تُخْلَطُ مَعَ كُلِّ الشَّجَرِ .
citation.translation: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bnin Abu Nasr, from Aban Bin Usman, from Zurara, (It has been narrated) from one of the two (5<sup>th</sup> or 6<sup>th</sup> Imam<sup>asws</sup>) having said: ‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘It is upon you with (drinking) the cow milk, for it mingles with every tree’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: موثق كالصحيح - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (22/170)

text: Muhammad Bin Yahya, (It has been narrated) raising it to Abu Al-Hassanasws having said: ‘The one who intends to eat the yoghurt and for it not to harm him, so let him pour the digestive (الْهَاضُومَ) over it’. I said to himasws, ‘And what is the digestive?’ Heasws said: ‘Al-Nankhwah (A herb)’.

citation.arabic_text: مَنْ أَرَادَ أَكْلَ الْمَاسْتِ وَ لَا يَضُرُّهُ فَلْيَصُبَّ عَلَيْهِ الْهَاضُومَ قُلْتُ لَهُ وَ مَا الْهَاضُومُ قَالَ النَّانْخَواهُ .
citation.translation: Muhammad Bin Yahya, (It has been narrated) raising it to Abu Al-Hassanasws having said: ‘The one who intends to eat the yoghurt and for it not to harm him, so let him pour the digestive (الْهَاضُومَ) over it’. I said to himasws, ‘And what is the digestive?’ Heasws said: ‘Al-Nankhwah (A herb)’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: مرفوع - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (22/170)

text: محمد بن يحيى، عن أحمد بن محمد بن عيسى، عن بكر بن صالح، عن الجعفري قال: سمعت أبا الحسن موسى عليه السلام يقول: أبوال الابل خير من ألبانها، ويجعل الله عزوجل الشفاء في ألبانها.

citation.arabic_text: محمد بن يحيى، عن أحمد بن محمد بن عيسى، عن بكر بن صالح، عن الجعفري قال: سمعت أبا الحسن موسى عليه السلام يقول: أبوال الابل خير من ألبانها، ويجعل الله عزوجل الشفاء في ألبانها.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: ضعيف - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (2/171)

text: عدة من أصحابنا، عن أحمد بن أبي عبدالله، عن نوح بن شعيب، عن بعض أصحابنا، عن موسى بن عبدالله بن الحسين قال: سمعت أشياخنا يقولون: ألبان اللقاح شفاء من كل داء وعاهة، ولصاحب البطن أبوالها.

citation.arabic_text: عدة من أصحابنا، عن أحمد بن أبي عبدالله، عن نوح بن شعيب، عن بعض أصحابنا، عن موسى بن عبدالله بن الحسين قال: سمعت أشياخنا يقولون: ألبان اللقاح شفاء من كل داء وعاهة، ولصاحب البطن أبوالها.

text: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Safwan Bin Yahya, from Ays Bin Al Qasim who said, ‘I asked Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> about drinking the yoghurt milk. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Drink it’.

citation.arabic_text: عَلِيُّ بْنُ إِبْرَاهِيمَ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ صَفْوَانَ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنْ عِيصِ بْنِ الْقَاسِمِ قَالَ سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) عَنْ شُرْبِ أَلْبَانِ الْأُتُنِ فَقَالَ اشْرَبْهَا .
citation.translation: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Safwan Bin Yahya, from Ays Bin Al Qasim who said, ‘I asked Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> about drinking the yoghurt milk. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Drink it’.

text: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Abu Abdullah, from his father, from Al Husayn Bin Al Mubarak, from Abu Maryam Al Ansary, (It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup>, said, ‘I asked him<sup>asws</sup> about drinking the yoghurt milk, so he<sup>asws</sup> said to me: ‘There is no problem with it’.

citation.arabic_text: عِدَّةٌ مِنْ أَصْحَابِنَا عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنِ الْحُسَيْنِ بْنِ الْمُبَارَكِ عَنْ أَبِي مَرْيَمَ الْأَنْصَارِيِّ عَنْ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ ( عليه السلام ) قَالَ سَأَلْتُهُ عَنْ شُرْبِ أَلْبَانِ الْأُتُنِ فَقَالَ لِي لَا بَأْسَ بِهَا .
citation.translation: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Abu Abdullah, from his father, from Al Husayn Bin Al Mubarak, from Abu Maryam Al Ansary, (It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup>, said, ‘I asked him<sup>asws</sup> about drinking the yoghurt milk, so he<sup>asws</sup> said to me: ‘There is no problem with it’.

text: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Abdul Rahma Bin Abu Najran, from Safwan Bin Yahya, from l Ays Bin Al Qasim, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws, said, ‘I had lunch with himasws, so heasws said to me: ‘Do you know what this is?’ I said, ‘No’. Heasws said: ‘Sheyraz Al-Atun. Weasws take it for ourasws sick, so Iasws would love it if you would eat from it’. So I ate’.

citation.arabic_text: تَغَدَّيْتُ مَعَهُ فَقَالَ لِي أَ تَدْرِي مَا هَذَا قُلْتُ لَا قَالَ هَذَا شِيرَازُ الْأُتُنِ اتَّخَذْنَاهُ لِمَرِيضٍ لَنَا فَإِنْ أَحْبَبْتَ أَنْ تَأْكُلَ مِنْهُ فَكُلْ .
citation.translation: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Abdul Rahma Bin Abu Najran, from Safwan Bin Yahya, from l Ays Bin Al Qasim, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws, said, ‘I had lunch with himasws, so heasws said to me: ‘Do you know what this is?’ I said, ‘No’. Heasws said: ‘Sheyraz Al-Atun. Weasws take it for ourasws sick, so Iasws would love it if you would eat from it’. So I ate’.
