text: Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Muhammad Bin Khalid, from Khalaf Bin Hammad, from Yahya Bin Abdullah who said, ‘I was in the presence of Abu Abdullahasws, and they came to us with small dishes. So heasws pointed with hisasws hand to one of them and said: ‘This is Sheyraz Al-Utun. Weasws take it for the sick ones with usasws, and the one who so desires to so let him eat, and the one who so desires to, so let him leave it’.

citation.arabic_text: كُنْتُ عِنْدَ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) فَأُتِينَا بِسُكُرُّجَاتٍ فَأَشَارَ بِيَدِهِ نَحْوَ وَاحِدَةٍ مِنْهُنَّ وَ قَالَ هَذَا شِيرَازُ الْأُتُنِ اتَّخَذْنَاهُ لِعَلِيلٍ عِنْدَنَا وَ مَنْ شَاءَ فَلْيَأْكُلْ وَ مَنْ شَاءَ فَلْيَدَعْ .

text: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Ibn Mahboub, from Abdullah Bin Sinan, from Abdullah Bin Suleyman who said, ‘I asked Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> about the cheese, so he<sup>asws</sup> said to me: ‘You have asked me<sup>asws</sup> about a food which I<sup>asws</sup> love’. Then he<sup>asws</sup> gave one Dirham to the slave, so he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘O slave! Buy some cheese for us and call for the lunch’. So we had lunch with him<sup>asws</sup>, and they came with the cheese. So he<sup>asws</sup> ate and we ate with him<sup>asws</sup>. So when we were free from the lunch, I said to him<sup>asws</sup>, ‘What are you<sup>asws</sup> saying regarding the cheese?’ So he<sup>asws</sup> said to me: ‘Or did you not see me<sup>asws</sup> eating it?’ I said, ‘Yes, but I would love to hear it from you<sup>asws</sup>’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘I shall inform you about the cheese and other such, everything what was Permissible regarding it, and Prohibited. So it is Permissible for you until you recognise the Prohibition with exactly it, so leave it’.

citation.arabic_text: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا جَعْفَرٍ ( عليه السلام ) عَنِ الْجُبُنِّ فَقَالَ لِي لَقَدْ سَأَلْتَنِي عَنْ طَعَامٍ يُعْجِبُنِي ثُمَّ أَعْطَى الْغُلَامَ دِرْهَماً فَقَالَ يَا غُلَامُ ابْتَعْ لَنَا جُبُنّاً وَ دَعَا بِالْغَدَاءِ فَتَغَدَّيْنَا مَعَهُ وَ أُتِيَ بِالْجُبُنِّ فَأَكَلَ وَ أَكَلْنَا مَعَهُ فَلَمَّا فَرَغْنَا مِنَ الْغَدَاءِ قُلْتُ لَهُ مَا تَقُولُ فِي الْجُبُنِّ فَقَالَ لِي أَ وَ لَمْ تَرَنِي أَكَلْتُهُ قُلْتُ بَلَى وَ لَكِنِّي أُحِبُّ أَنْ أَسْمَعَهُ مِنْكَ فَقَالَ سَأُخْبِرُكَ عَنِ الْجُبُنِّ وَ غَيْرِهِ كُلُّ مَا كَانَ فِيهِ حَلَالٌ وَ حَرَامٌ فَهُوَ لَكَ حَلَالٌ حَتَّى تَعْرِفَ الْحَرَامَ بِعَيْنِهِ فَتَدَعَهُ.

text: Ahmad Bin Muhammad Al Kufy, from Muhammad Bin Ahmad Al Nahdy, from Muhammad Bin Al Waleed, from Aban Bin Abdul Rahman, from Abdullah Bin Suleyman, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> regarding the cheese. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Everything is Permissible for you until two witnesses come to you with two testimonies in your presence that in it is a dead (animal thing)’.

citation.arabic_text: الْجُبُنِّ قَالَ كُلُّ شَيْ‏ءٍ لَكَ حَلَالٌ حَتَّى يَجِيئَكَ شَاهِدَانِ يَشْهَدَانِ عِنْدَكَ أَنَّ فِيهِ مَيْتَةً .

He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Everything is Permissible for you until two witnesses come to you with two testimonies in your presence that in it is a dead (animal thing)’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: ضعيف على المشهور - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (2/173)

text: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ali Bin Ibrahim Al Hashimy, from his father, from Muhammad Bin Al Fazal Al Neyshapouri, from one of his men, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, said, ‘A man asked him<sup>asws</sup> about the cheese, so he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘An illness, there is no cure in it’. So when it was the evening, the man came over to Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, so he looked at the cheese upon the table-spread, so he said, ‘May I be sacrificed for you<sup>asws</sup>! I asked you<sup>asws</sup> at lunch about the cheese, so you<sup>asws</sup> said to me: ‘It is an illness, there is no cure for it, and at this time I see it upon the food-spread?’ So he<sup>asws</sup> said to me: ‘It is harmful with the lunch and beneficial with the dinner, increasing in the water of the back’. And it is reported that: ‘The harmfulness of the cheese is in its crust’.

citation.arabic_text: سَأَلَهُ رَجُلٌ عَنِ الْجُبُنِّ فَقَالَ دَاءٌ لَا دَوَاءَ فِيهِ فَلَمَّا كَانَ بِالْعَشِيِّ دَخَلَ الرَّجُلُ عَلَى أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) فَنَظَرَ إِلَى الْجُبُنِّ عَلَى الْخِوَانِ فَقَالَ جُعِلْتُ فِدَاكَ سَأَلْتُكَ بِالْغَدَاةِ عَنِ الْجُبُنِّ فَقُلْتَ لِي إِنَّهُ هُوَ الدَّاءُ الَّذِي لَا دَوَاءَ لَهُ وَ السَّاعَةَ أَرَاهُ عَلَى الْخِوَانِ قَالَ فَقَالَ لِي هُوَ ضَارٌّ بِالْغَدَاةِ نَافِعٌ بِالْعَشِيِّ وَ يَزِيدُ فِي مَاءِ الظَّهْرِ . وَ رُوِيَ أَنَّ مَضَرَّةَ الْجُبُنِّ فِي قِشْرِهِ .

text: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Al Nowfaly, from Al Sakuny, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Eating the walnuts during the intense heat agitates the heat in the inside and agitates the blisters upon the body, and eating it in the winter warms the kidneys and dispels the cold’.

citation.arabic_text: قَالَ أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ ( عليه السلام ) أَكْلُ الْجَوْزِ فِي شِدَّةِ الْحَرِّ يُهَيِّجُ الْحَرَّ فِي الْجَوْفِ وَ يُهَيِّجُ الْقُرُوحَ عَلَى الْجَسَدِ وَ أَكْلُهُ فِي الشِّتَاءِ يُسَخِّنُ الْكُلْيَتَيْنِ وَ يَدْفَعُ الْبَرْدَ .
citation.translation: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Al Nowfaly, from Al Sakuny, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Eating the walnuts during the intense heat agitates the heat in the inside and agitates the blisters upon the body, and eating it in the winter warms the kidneys and dispels the cold’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: ضعيف على المشهور - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (2/173)

text: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Abdul Aziz Al Abdy who said, ‘Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The cheese and the walnuts, when they gather together, in each one of them is a healing, and if these are separated, in each one of these is an illness’.

citation.arabic_text: قَالَ أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) الْجُبُنُّ وَ الْجَوْزُ إِذَا اجْتَمَعَا فِي كُلِّ وَاحِدٍ مِنْهُمَا شِفَاءٌ وَ إِنِ افْتَرَقَا كَانَ فِي كُلِّ وَاحِدٍ مِنْهُمَا دَاءٌ .
citation.translation: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Abdul Aziz Al Abdy who said, ‘Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The cheese and the walnuts, when they gather together, in each one of them is a healing, and if these are separated, in each one of these is an illness’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: ضعيف - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (2/174)

text: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Idrees Bin Al Hassan, from Ubeyd Bin Zurara, from his father, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> that the walnuts and the cheese, when they gather together would be a cure, and when these two are separated, they would be an illness’.

citation.arabic_text: إِنَّ الْجَوْزَ وَ الْجُبُنَّ إِذَا اجْتَمَعَا كَانَا دَوَاءً وَ إِذَا افْتَرَقَا كَانَا دَاءً .
citation.translation: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Idrees Bin Al Hassan, from Ubeyd Bin Zurara, from his father, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> that the walnuts and the cheese, when they gather together would be a cure, and when these two are separated, they would be an illness’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: مجهول - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (22/174)

text: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Khalid, from Usman Bin Isa, from the one who informed him, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘The best of the foods is the rice, and we<sup>asws</sup> preserve it for our<sup>asws</sup> sick ones’.

citation.arabic_text: عِدَّةٌ مِنْ أَصْحَابِنَا عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ خَالِدٍ عَنْ عُثْمَانَ بْنِ عِيسَى عَمَّنْ أَخْبَرَهُ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) قَالَ نِعْمَ الطَّعَامُ الْأَرُزُّ وَ إِنَّا لَنَدَّخِرُهُ لِمَرْضَانَا .
citation.translation: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Khalid, from Usman Bin Isa, from the one who informed him, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘The best of the foods is the rice, and we<sup>asws</sup> preserve it for our<sup>asws</sup> sick ones’.

text: From him, from Yahya Bin Isa, from the one who informed him, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘The best of the foods is the rice, and we<sup>asws</sup> cure our<sup>asws</sup> sick ones with it’.

citation.arabic_text: عَنْهُ عَنْ يَحْيَى بْنِ عِيسَى عَمَّنْ أَخْبَرَهُ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) قَالَ قَالَ نِعْمَ الطَّعَامُ الْأَرُزُّ وَ إِنَّا لَنُدَاوِي بِهِ مَرْضَانَا.
citation.translation: From him, from Yahya Bin Isa, from the one who informed him, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘The best of the foods is the rice, and we<sup>asws</sup> cure our<sup>asws</sup> sick ones with it’.

text: From him, from Usman Bin Isa, from Khalid Bin Najeeh who said, ‘I complained to Abu Abdullahasws of stomach pains, so heasws said to me: ‘Take the rice, wash it, then dry it in the shade, then powder it, and take from it during every morning as per your convenience’. And Is’haq Al Jareery increased in it, ‘(Heasws said): ‘Fry it a little, the weight of one Awqiya (Unit of measurement), and drink it’.

citation.arabic_text: عَنْهُ عَنْ عُثْمَانَ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنْ خَالِدِ بْنِ نَجِيحٍ قَالَ شَكَوْتُ إِلَى أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) وَجَعَ بَطْنِي فَقَالَ لِي خُذِ الْأَرُزَّ فَاغْسِلْهُ ثُمَّ جَفِّفْهُ فِي الظِّلِّ ثُمَّ رُضَّهُ وَ خُذْ مِنْهُ فِي كُلِّ غَدَاةٍ مِلْ‏ءَ رَاحَتِكَ وَ زَادَ فِيهِ إِسْحَاقُ الْجَرِيرِيُّ تَقْلِيهِ قَلِيلًا وَزْنَ أُوقِيَّةٍ وَ اشْرَبْهُ .

text: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Sa’alba Bin Maymoun, from Humran who said, ‘Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> was with stomach pain, so he<sup>asws</sup> instructed that the rice be cooked for him<sup>asws</sup>, and the Sumac (a kind of pepper) sprinkled upon it. So he<sup>asws</sup> ate and was cured’.

citation.arabic_text: عِدَّةٌ مِنْ أَصْحَابِنَا عَنْ سَهْلِ بْنِ زِيَادٍ عَنِ ابْنِ فَضَّالٍ عَنْ ثَعْلَبَةَ بْنِ مَيْمُونٍ عَنْ حُمْرَانَ قَالَ كَانَ بِأَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) وَجَعُ الْبَطْنِ فَأَمَرَ أَنْ يُطْبَخَ لَهُ الْأَرُزُّ وَ يُجْعَلَ عَلَيْهِ السُّمَّاقُ فَأَكَلَهُ فَبَرَأَ .

text: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Al Hakam, and Al Hassan Bin Ali Bin Fazzal, from Yunus Bin Yaqoub who said, ‘Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘There has not been brought to us<sup>asws</sup> from your areas anything more beloved to me<sup>asws</sup> than the rice, and the viola. I<sup>asws</sup> complained of intense pain, so I<sup>asws</sup> was inspired to eat the rice. So I<sup>asws</sup> ordered with it, so it was washed and dried. Then it was fried, and ground, so it was made from me<sup>asws</sup> as an oiled powder, and cooked, so I<sup>asws</sup> took it, so Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic Made that pain to go away from me<sup>asws</sup>’.

citation.arabic_text: قَالَ أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) مَا يَأْتِينَا مِنْ نَاحِيَتِكُمْ شَيْ‏ءٌ أَحَبُّ إِلَيَّ مِنَ الْأَرُزِّ وَ الْبَنَفْسَجِ إِنِّي اشْتَكَيْتُ وَجَعِي ذَلِكَ الشَّدِيدَ فَأُلْهِمْتُ أَكْلَ الْأَرُزِّ فَأَمَرْتُ بِهِ فَغُسِلَ وَ جُفِّفَ ثُمَّ قُلِيَ وَ طُحِنَ فَجُعِلَ لِي مِنْهُ سَفُوفٌ بِزَيْتٍ وَ طَبِيخٌ أَتَحَسَّاهُ فَأَذْهَبَ اللَّهُ عَزَّ وَ جَلَّ عَنِّي بِذَلِكَ الْوَجَعَ.

text: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ismail Bin Marrar, and someone else, from Hisham Bin Al Hakam, from Zurara who said, ‘I saw a nurse-maid of Abu Al-Hassan Musa<sup>asws</sup> being fed the rice, and she threw it upon him<sup>asws</sup>. So it grieved me, what I saw. So I went over to Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, so he<sup>asws</sup> said to me: ‘I<sup>asws</sup> reckon your grief is due to what you saw from a nursemaid of Abu Al-Hassan Musa<sup>asws</sup>’. I said, ‘Yes, may I be sacrificed for you<sup>asws</sup>’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said to me: ‘The best of the foods is the rice, it expands the intestine, and cuts off the hemorrhoids, and we envy the people of Al-Iraq with their eating of the rice, and partially-ripened dates, for these two expand the intestine and cut off the hemorrhoids’.

text: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Abu Abdullah, from Abu Suleyman Sl Haza’a, from Muhammad Bin Al Fayz who said, ‘I was in the presence of Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, so a man came over, so he said to him<sup>asws</sup>, ‘My daughter has withered and with her is the belly (pregnancy)’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘What prevents you from the rice with the fat? Take four or five stones, so place these by the side of the fire and make the rice to be in the pot and cook it until it is done, and take the fat of fresh kidneys. So when the rice reaches (is cooked), so place the fat in a bowl along with the stones, and cover over it with another bowl. Then stir it with a new stirring, and set it such that no steam comes out. So when the fat has melted, so make it to be in the rice, then she can eat it’.

citation.arabic_text: كُنْتُ عِنْدَ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) فَجَاءَهُ رَجُلٌ فَقَالَ لَهُ إِنَّ ابْنَتِي قَدْ ذَبَلَتْ وَ بِهَا الْبَطَنُ فَقَالَ مَا يَمْنَعُكَ مِنَ الْأَرُزِّ بِالشَّحْمِ خُذْ حِجَاراً أَرْبَعاً أَوْ خَمْساً فَاطْرَحْهَا بِجَنْبِ النَّارِ وَ اجْعَلِ الْأَرُزَّ فِي الْقِدْرِ وَ اطْبُخْهُ حَتَّى يُدْرِكَ وَ خُذْ شَحْمَ كُلًى طَرِيّاً فَإِذَا بَلَغَ الْأَرُزُّ فَاطْرَحِ الشَّحْمَ فِي قَصْعَةٍ مَعَ الْحِجَارَةِ وَ كُبَّ عَلَيْهَا قَصْعَةً أُخْرَى ثُمَّ حَرِّكْهَا تَحْرِيكاً جَيِّداً وَ اضْبِطْهَا كَيْ لَا يَخْرُجَ بُخَارُهُ فَإِذَا ذَابَ الشَّحْمُ فَاجْعَلْهُ فِي الْأَرُزِّ ثُمَّ تَحَسَّاهُ .

text: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from MUawiya Bin Ammar who said, ‘I said to Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> that the people are reporting that the Prophet<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘The Lentils, seventy Prophets<sup>as</sup> have Blessed upon it’’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘It is that which is named with you as the chick-peas, and we<sup>asws</sup> called it the lentils’.

text: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Khalid, from his father, from Fazalat, from Rafa’at who said, ‘I heard Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> saying: ‘When Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Blessed and High Restored the health of Ayoub<sup>as</sup>, he<sup>as</sup> looked at (the affairs of) the Children of Israel who had farmed, so he<sup>as</sup> raised his<sup>as</sup> eyes towards the sky and said: ‘My<sup>as</sup> God, and my<sup>as</sup> Master! Your<sup>azwj</sup> servant Ayoub<sup>as</sup> was afflicted and You<sup>azwj</sup> Granted him<sup>as</sup> health, and he<sup>as</sup> has nowhere to plant anything, and this is a plantation of the Children of Israel’. So Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic Revealed unto him<sup>as</sup>: “O Ayoub<sup>as</sup>! Take a handful from your<sup>as</sup> rosary, so plant it”; and his<sup>as</sup> rosary had salt in it. So Ayoub<sup>as</sup> took a handful from it, so he<sup>as</sup> planted it, and there came out this lentil, and you all are calling is as chick-peas, and we<sup>asws</sup> are calling it as lentils’.

citation.arabic_text: سَمِعْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) يَقُولُ إِنَّ اللَّهَ تَبَارَكَ وَ تَعَالَى لَمَّا عَافَى أَيُّوبَ ( عليه السلام ) نَظَرَ إِلَى بَنِي إِسْرَائِيلَ قَدِ ازْدَرَعَتْ فَرَفَعَ طَرْفَهُ إِلَى السَّمَاءِ وَ قَالَ إِلَهِي وَ سَيِّدِي عَبْدُكَ أَيُّوبُ الْمُبْتَلَى عَافَيْتَهُ وَ لَمْ يَزْدَرِعْ شَيْئاً وَ هَذَا لِبَنِي إِسْرَائِيلَ زَرْعٌ فَأَوْحَى اللَّهُ عَزَّ وَ جَلَّ إِلَيْهِ يَا أَيُّوبُ خُذْ مِنْ سُبْحَتِكَ كَفّاً فَابْذُرْهُ وَ كَانَتْ سُبْحَتُهُ فِيهَا مِلْحٌ فَأَخَذَ أَيُّوبُ ( عليه السلام ) كَفّاً مِنْهَا فَبَذَرَهُ فَخَرَجَ هَذَا الْعَدَسُ وَ أَنْتُمْ تُسَمُّونَهُ الْحِمِّصَ وَ نَحْنُ نُسَمِّيهِ الْعَدَسَ .
citation.translation: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Khalid, from his father, from Fazalat, from Rafa’at who said, ‘I heard Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> saying: ‘When Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Blessed and High Restored the health of Ayoub<sup>as</sup>, he<sup>as</sup> looked at (the affairs of) the Children of Israel who had farmed, so he<sup>as</sup> raised his<sup>as</sup> eyes towards the sky and said: ‘My<sup>as</sup> God, and my<sup>as</sup> Master! Your<sup>azwj</sup> servant Ayoub<sup>as</sup> was afflicted and You<sup>azwj</sup> Granted him<sup>as</sup> health, and he<sup>as</sup> has nowhere to plant anything, and this is a plantation of the Children of Israel’. So Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic Revealed unto him<sup>as</sup>: “O Ayoub<sup>as</sup>! Take a handful from your<sup>as</sup> rosary, so plant it”; and his<sup>as</sup> rosary had salt in it. So Ayoub<sup>as</sup> took a handful from it, so he<sup>as</sup> planted it, and there came out this lentil, and you all are calling is as chick-peas, and we<sup>asws</sup> are calling it as lentils’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: صحيح - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (2/177)

text: From him, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Abu Nasr, (It has been narrated) from Al-Reza<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘The chick-peas is good for the back pain’, and he<sup>asws</sup> used to call for it before the meal and after it’.

citation.arabic_text: الْحِمِّصُ جَيِّدٌ لِوَجَعِ الظَّهْرِ وَ كَانَ يَدْعُو بِهِ قَبْلَ الطَّعَامِ وَ بَعْدَهُ .
citation.translation: From him, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Abu Nasr, (It has been narrated) from Al-Reza<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘The chick-peas is good for the back pain’, and he<sup>asws</sup> used to call for it before the meal and after it’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: صحيح - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (22/178)

text: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Al Nowfaly, from Al Sakuny, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Eating the lentils softens the heat and frequents the tears’.

citation.arabic_text: قَالَ أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ ( عليه السلام ) أَكْلُ الْعَدَسِ يُرِقُّ الْقَلْبَ وَ يُكْثِرُ الدَّمْعَةَ .
citation.translation: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Al Nowfaly, from Al Sakuny, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Eating the lentils softens the heat and frequents the tears’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: ضعيف على المشهور - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (2/178)

text: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Khalid, from Furaat Bin Ahnaf that one of the Children of Israel complained to Allahazwj Mighty and Majestic of the hardness of the heart and the scarcity of the tears. So Allahazwj Mighty and Majestic Revealed unto him: “Eat the lentils”. So he ate the lentils, and the heart softened and the tears flowed’.[1535] (P.s. – This is no a Hadeeth) From him, from Muhammad Bin Ali, from Muhammad Bin Al Fuzayl, from Abdul Rahman Bin Zayd, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws having said: ‘A man complained to the Prophetsaww of Allahazwj of the hardness of the heart. So hesaww said to him: ‘It is upon you with (eating) the lentils, for it softens the heart and accelerates the tears’.

citation.arabic_text: عِدَّةٌ مِنْ أَصْحَابِنَا عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ خَالِدٍ عَنْ فُرَاتِ بْنِ أَحْنَفَ أَنَّ بَعْضَ بَنِي إِسْرَائِيلَ شَكَا إِلَى اللَّهِ عَزَّ وَ جَلَّ قَسْوَةَ الْقَلْبِ وَ قِلَّةَ الدَّمْعَةِ فَأَوْحَى اللَّهُ عَزَّ وَ جَلَّ إِلَيْهِ أَنْ كُلِ الْعَدَسَ فَأَكَلَ الْعَدَسَ فَرَقَّ قَلْبُهُ وَ جَرَتْ دَمْعَتُهُ . عَنْهُ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عَلِيٍّ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ الْفُضَيْلِ عَنْ عَبْدِ الرَّحْمَنِ بْنِ زَيْدٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) قَالَ شَكَا رَجُلٌ إِلَى نَبِيِّ اللَّهِ ( صلى الله عليه وآله ) قَسَاوَةَ الْقَلْبِ فَقَالَ لَهُ عَلَيْكَ بِالْعَدَسِ فَإِنَّهُ يُرِقُّ الْقَلْبَ وَ يُسْرِعُ الدَّمْعَةَ .

text: From him, from Dawood Bin Is’haq Al Haza’a, from Muhammad Bin Al Qayz who said, ‘I ate lentil broth in the presence of Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, so I said, ‘May I be sacrificed for you<sup>asws</sup>! They (people) are saying that seventy Prophets<sup>as</sup> have sanctified upon the lentils’. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘They are lying! No, by Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, not even twenty Prophets<sup>as</sup>’. And it is reported that it softens the heart and accelerates the tears’.

citation.arabic_text: أَكَلْتُ عِنْدَ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ع مَرَقَةً بِعَدَسٍ فَقُلْتُ جُعِلْتُ فِدَاكَ إِنَّ هَؤُلَاءِ يَقُولُونَ إِنَّ الْعَدَسَ قَدَّسَ عَلَيْهِ ثَمَانُونَ نَبِيّاً قَالَ كَذَبُوا لَا وَ اللَّهِ وَ لَا عِشْرُونَ نَبِيّاً . وَ رُوِيَ أَنَّهُ يُرِقُّ الْقَلْبَ وَ يُسْرِعُ الدَّمْعَةَ .

text: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Muhammad Bin Ahmad, from Musa Bin Ja’far, from Muhammad Bin Al Hassan, from Umar Bin Salma, from Muhammad Bin Abdullah, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Eating the Broad-beans enhances the two thighs, and increases in the brain, and gives birth to fresh blood’.

citation.arabic_text: أَكْلُ الْبَاقِلَّى يُمَخِّخُ السَّاقَيْنِ وَ يَزِيدُ فِي الدِّمَاغِ وَ يُوَلِّدُ الدَّمَ الطَّرِيَّ .
citation.translation: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Muhammad Bin Ahmad, from Musa Bin Ja’far, from Muhammad Bin Al Hassan, from Umar Bin Salma, from Muhammad Bin Abdullah, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Eating the Broad-beans enhances the two thighs, and increases in the brain, and gives birth to fresh blood’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: مجهول - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (22/179)

text: From him, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Abu Nasr, (It has been narrated) from Al-Reza<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Eating the broad-beans enhances the two thighs, and gives birth to the fresh blood’.

text: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Abu Abdullah, from one of his companions, from Salih Bin Uqba who said, ‘I heard Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> saying: ‘Eat the Broad-beans with its skin for it repairs the stomach’.

citation.arabic_text: سَمِعْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) يَقُولُ كُلُوا الْبَاقِلَّى بِقِشْرِهِ فَإِنَّهُ يَدْبُغُ الْمَعِدَةَ .
citation.translation: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Abu Abdullah, from one of his companions, from Salih Bin Uqba who said, ‘I heard Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> saying: ‘Eat the Broad-beans with its skin for it repairs the stomach’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: ضعيف - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (2/179)

text: Ali Bin Muhammad, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Ibn Abu Najran, from the one who mentioned it, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘The Kidney-beans expel the underlying wind’.

citation.arabic_text: اللُّوبِيَاءِ يَطْرُدُ الرِّيَاحَ الْمُسْتَبْطِنَةَ .
citation.translation: Ali Bin Muhammad, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Ibn Abu Najran, from the one who mentioned it, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘The Kidney-beans expel the underlying wind’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: ضعيف على المشهور - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (22/179)

text: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Muhammad Bin Musa, from Ahmad Bin Al Hassan Al Jallab, from one of his companions who said, ‘A man complained to Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> of vitiligo, so he<sup>asws</sup> ordered him that he should cook the Mung-beans, and apportion it and make it to be in his meal’.

citation.arabic_text: شَكَا رَجُلٌ إِلَى أَبِي الْحَسَنِ ( عليه السلام ) الْبَهَقَ فَأَمَرَهُ أَنْ يَطْبُخَ الْمَاشَ وَ يَتَحَسَّاهُ وَ يَجْعَلَهُ فِي طَعَامِهِ .

citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: مجهول - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (2/179)

text: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from one of our companions, from Ali Bin Hassan, from Abdul Rahman Bin Kaseer who said, ‘I fell sick at Al-Medina, so my stomach went (diarrhoea), so Abu Abdullahasws prescribed for me Al-Suweyq of the finger-millet and instructed me that I should take Al-Suweyq of the finger-millet and drink it with water of cumin. So I did it and my belly retained, and I regained health’.

citation.arabic_text: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَحْيَى عَنْ بَعْضِ أَصْحَابِنَا عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ حَسَّانَ عَنْ عَبْدِ الرَّحْمَنِ بْنِ كَثِيرٍ قَالَ مَرِضْتُ بِالْمَدِينَةِ فَانْطَلَقَ بَطْنِي فَوَصَفَ لِي أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) سَوِيقَ الْجَاوَرْسِ وَ أَمَرَنِي أَنْ آخُذَ سَوِيقَ الْجَاوَرْسِ وَ أَشْرَبَهُ بِمَاءِ الْكَمُّونِ فَفَعَلْتُ فَأَمْسَكَ بَطْنِي وَ عُوفِيتُ .
citation.translation: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from one of our companions, from Ali Bin Hassan, from Abdul Rahman Bin Kaseer who said, ‘I fell sick at Al-Medina, so my stomach went (diarrhoea), so Abu Abdullahasws prescribed for me Al-Suweyq of the finger-millet and instructed me that I should take Al-Suweyq of the finger-millet and drink it with water of cumin. So I did it and my belly retained, and I regained health’.

text: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Ayoub Bin Nuh who said, ‘The one who ate Hareys with Abu Al-Hassanasws the 1st, (has) narrated to me with the Finger-millet and (heasws) said, ‘But, it is a food in which there is no heaviness, nor is there any painful suffering for it, and Iasws like it, therefore Iasws instructed that it should be taken for measws and it is beneficial with the milk, and soft in the stomach’.

citation.arabic_text: حَدَّثَنِي مَنْ أَكَلَ مَعَ أَبِي الْحَسَنِ الْأَوَّلِ ( عليه السلام ) هَرِيسَةً بِالْجَاوَرْسِ وَ قَالَ أَمَا إِنَّهُ طَعَامٌ لَيْسَ فِيهِ ثِقَلٌ وَ لَا لَهُ غَائِلَةٌ وَ إِنَّهُ أَعْجَبَنِي فَأَمَرْتُ أَنْ يُتَّخَذَ لِي وَ هُوَ بِاللَّبَنِ أَنْفَعُ وَ أَلْيَنُ فِي الْمَعِدَةِ .
citation.translation: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Ayoub Bin Nuh who said, ‘The one who ate Hareys with Abu Al-Hassanasws the 1st, (has) narrated to me with the Finger-millet and (heasws) said, ‘But, it is a food in which there is no heaviness, nor is there any painful suffering for it, and Iasws like it, therefore Iasws instructed that it should be taken for measws and it is beneficial with the milk, and soft in the stomach’.

text: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Hanaan Bin Sudeyr, from his father who said, ‘Ali<sup>asws</sup> Bin Al-Husayn<sup>asws</sup> loved to see a date-loving person due to the love of Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> for the dates’.

citation.arabic_text: عَلِيُّ بْنُ إِبْرَاهِيمَ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ حَنَانِ بْنِ سَدِيرٍ عَنْ أَبِيهِ قَالَ كَانَ عَلِيُّ بْنُ الْحُسَيْنِ ( عليه السلام ) يُحِبُّ أَنْ يَرَى الرَّجُلَ تَمْرِيّاً لِحُبِّ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ ( صلى الله عليه وآله ) التَّمْرَ .
citation.translation: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Hanaan Bin Sudeyr, from his father who said, ‘Ali<sup>asws</sup> Bin Al-Husayn<sup>asws</sup> loved to see a date-loving person due to the love of Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> for the dates’.

text: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Abu Al Magra, from one of his companions, from Uqba Bin Bashir, (It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup>, said, ‘We went over to him<sup>asws</sup>, so he<sup>asws</sup> called for the dates, and we ate them. Then he<sup>asws</sup> increased it for us from it, then said: ‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘I<sup>saww</sup> love the man’, or said: ‘I<sup>saww</sup> like the man who loves to (eat) the date’.

citation.arabic_text: عَلِيُّ بْنُ إِبْرَاهِيمَ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنِ ابْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ عَنْ أَبِي الْمَغْرَاءِ عَنْ بَعْضِ أَصْحَابِهِ عَنْ عُقْبَةَ بْنِ بَشِيرٍ عَنْ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ ( عليه السلام ) قَالَ دَخَلْنَا عَلَيْهِ فَاسْتَدْعَى بِتَمْرٍ فَأَكَلْنَا ثُمَّ ازْدَدْنَا مِنْهُ ثُمَّ قَالَ قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ ( صلى الله عليه وآله ) إِنِّي أُحِبُّ الرَّجُلَ أَوْ قَالَ يُعْجِبُنِي الرَّجُلُ إِذَا كَانَ تَمْرِيّاً .

text: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Amro Bin Usman, from Abu Amro, from a man, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws having said: ‘The best of your dates is Al-Barny, it does away with the illnesses, and there is no illness in it, and it does away with the fatigue and there is no harmfulness for it, and it does away with the phlegm; and with every date is a Reward’. citation.arabic_text: عَلِيُّ بْنُ إِبْرَاهِيمَ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ عَمْرِو بْنِ عُثْمَانَ عَنْ أَبِي عَمْرٍو عَنْ رَجُلٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) قَالَ خَيْرُ تُمُورِكُمُ الْبَرْنِيُّ يَذْهَبُ بِالدَّاءِ وَ لَا دَاءَ فِيهِ وَ يَذْهَبُ بِالْإِعْيَاءِ وَ لَا ضَرَرَ لَهُ وَ يَذْهَبُ بِالْبَلْغَمِ وَ مَعَ كُلِّ تَمْرَةٍ حَسَنَةٌ وَ فِي رِوَايَةٍ أُخْرَى يَهْنَأُ وَ يَمْرَأُ وَ يَذْهَبُ بِالْإِعْيَاءِ وَ يُشْبِعُ .

text: A number of our companions, from sahl Bin Ziyad, from Muhammad Bin Ismail Al Razy, from Suleyman Bin Ja’far Al Ja’fary who said, ‘I went over to Abu Al-Hassan Al-Rezaasws and in front of himasws were Barny dates heasws was constant in eating it, eating it with desire. So heasws said to me: ‘O Suleyman! Approach and eat’. So I approached himasws and ate with himasws, and I said to himasws, ‘May I be sacrificed for youasws! I see youasws eating this date with desire’. So heasws said: ‘Yes, Iasws love it’. He (the narrator) said, ‘I said, ‘And why is that so?’ Heasws said: ‘Because Rasool-Allahsaww was a date-lover, and Aliasws was a date-lover, and Al-Hassanasws was a date-lover, and Abu Abdullah Al-Husaynasws was a date-lover, and Zayn Al-Abideenasws was a date-lover, and Abu Ja’farasws was a date-lover, and Abu Abdullahasws was a date-lover, and myasws fatherasws was a date-lover, and ourasws Shias are loving the dates because they have been Created from ourasws clay, and ourasws enemies, O Sulayman, are loving the intoxicants because they have been Created from the [55:15] smokeless fire’.

citation.arabic_text: عِدَّةٌ مِنْ أَصْحَابِنَا عَنْ سَهْلِ بْنِ زِيَادٍ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ إِسْمَاعِيلَ الرَّازِيِّ عَنْ سُلَيْمَانَ بْنِ جَعْفَرٍ الْجَعْفَرِيِّ قَالَ دَخَلْتُ عَلَى أَبِي الْحَسَنِ الرِّضَا ( عليه السلام ) وَ بَيْنَ يَدَيْهِ تَمْرٌ بَرْنِيٌّ وَ هُوَ مُجِدٌّ فِي أَكْلِهِ يَأْكُلُهُ بِشَهْوَةٍ فَقَالَ لِي يَا سُلَيْمَانُ ادْنُ فَكُلْ قَالَ فَدَنَوْتُ مِنْهُ فَأَكَلْتُ مَعَهُ وَ أَنَا أَقُولُ لَهُ جُعِلْتُ فِدَاكَ إِنِّي أَرَاكَ تَأْكُلُ هَذَا التَّمْرَ بِشَهْوَةٍ فَقَالَ نَعَمْ إِنِّي لَأُحِبُّهُ قَالَ قُلْتُ وَ لِمَ ذَاكَ قَالَ لِأَنَّ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ ( صلى الله عليه وآله ) كَانَ تَمْرِيّاً وَ كَانَ عَلِيٌّ ( عليه السلام ) تَمْرِيّاً وَ كَانَ الْحَسَنُ ( عليه السلام ) تَمْرِيّاً وَ كَانَ أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ الْحُسَيْنُ ( عليه السلام ) تَمْرِيّاً وَ كَانَ زَيْنُ الْعَابِدِينَ ( عليه السلام ) تَمْرِيّاً وَ كَانَ أَبُو جَعْفَرٍ ( عليه السلام ) تَمْرِيّاً وَ كَانَ أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) تَمْرِيّاً وَ كَانَ أَبِي ( عليه السلام ) تَمْرِيّاً وَ أَنَا تَمْرِيٌّ وَ شِيعَتُنَا يُحِبُّونَ التَّمْرَ لِأَنَّهُمْ خُلِقُوا مِنْ طِينَتِنَا وَ أَعْدَاؤُنَا يَا سُلَيْمَانُ يُحِبُّونَ الْمُسْكِرَ لِأَنَّهُمْ خُلِقُوا مِنْ مَارِجٍ مِنْ نَارٍ .

text: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Abu Abdullah, from Muhammad Bin Ali, from Ali Bin Khattab Al Hallal, from A’ala Bin Razeyn who said, ‘Abu Abdullahasws said to me: ‘O A’ala! Heasws said: ‘It is Al-Ajwa. So whatever is pure so it is Al-Ajwa, and whatever was other than that, so rather it is from its resemblances’.

text: Al Husayn Bin Muhammad, from Ahmad Bin Is’haq, and Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Muhammad Bin Ismail, altogether from Sa’dan Bin Muslim, from one of our companions who said, ‘ When Abu Abdullahasws proceeded to Al-Hira, heasws rode hisasws animal, and went to Al-Khowrank. So heasws descended and took shade with the shadow of hisasws animal, and with himasws was a black slave of hisasws. So heasws a man from the people of Al-Kufa who had bought a palm tree said to the slave: ‘Who is this one?’ So he said to him, ‘This is Ja’farasws Bin Muhammadasws’. So he came with a huge platter (of various dates) and placed it in front of himasws. So heasws said to the man: ‘What is this?’ He said, ‘This is Al-Barny (dates)’. So heasws said: ‘Therein is a healing’, and heasws looked at Al-Sabiriyya (dates), so heasws said: ‘What is this?’ So he said, ‘Al-Sabiriyya’. So heasws said: ‘With us this is (called) Al-Bayz’. An heasws said for Al-Mushan (dates): ‘What is this?’ So the man said, ‘Al-Mushan (dates)’. So heasws said: ‘This, with us is (called) Umm Jirzan’. And heasws looked at Al-Safran, so heasws said: ‘What is this?’ So the man said, ‘Al-Sarfan’. So heasws said: ‘With us it is (called) Al-Ajwa and therein is a healing’.

citation.arabic_text: الْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ إِسْحَاقَ وَ مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَحْيَى عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ إِسْمَاعِيلَ جَمِيعاً عَنْ سَعْدَانَ بْنِ مُسْلِمٍ عَنْ بَعْضِ أَصْحَابِنَا قَالَ لَمَّا قَدِمَ أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) الْحِيرَةَ رَكِبَ دَابَّتَهُ وَ مَضَى إِلَى الْخَوَرْنَقِ فَنَزَلَ فَاسْتَظَلَّ بِظِلِّ دَابَّتِهِ وَ مَعَهُ غُلَامٌ لَهُ أَسْوَدُ فَرَأَى رَجُلًا مِنْ أَهْلِ الْكُوفَةِ قَدِ اشْتَرَى نَخْلًا فَقَالَ لِلْغُلَامِ مَنْ هَذَا فَقَالَ لَهُ هَذَا جَعْفَرُ بْنُ مُحَمَّدٍ ( عليه السلام ) فَجَاءَ بِطَبَقٍ ضَخْمٍ فَوَضَعَهُ بَيْنَ يَدَيْهِ فَقَالَ لِلرَّجُلِ مَا هَذَا فَقَالَ هَذَا الْبَرْنِيُّ فَقَالَ فِيهِ شِفَاءٌ وَ نَظَرَ إِلَى السَّابِرِيِّ فَقَالَ مَا هَذَا فَقَالَ السَّابِرِيُّ فَقَالَ هَذَا عِنْدَنَا الْبِيضُ وَ قَالَ لِلْمُشَانِ مَا هَذَا فَقَالَ الرَّجُلُ الْمُشَانُ فَقَالَ ( عليه السلام ) هَذَا عِنْدَنَا أُمُّ جِرْذَانَ وَ نَظَرَ إِلَى الصَّرَفَانِ فَقَالَ مَا هَذَا فَقَالَ الرَّجُلُ الصَّرَفَانُ فَقَالَ هُوَ عِنْدَنَا الْعَجْوَةُ وَ فِيهِ شِفَاءٌ .
citation.translation: Al Husayn Bin Muhammad, from Ahmad Bin Is’haq, and Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Muhammad Bin Ismail, altogether from Sa’dan Bin Muslim, from one of our companions who said, ‘ When Abu Abdullahasws proceeded to Al-Hira, heasws rode hisasws animal, and went to Al-Khowrank. So heasws descended and took shade with the shadow of hisasws animal, and with himasws was a black slave of hisasws. So heasws a man from the people of Al-Kufa who had bought a palm tree said to the slave: ‘Who is this one?’ So he said to him, ‘This is Ja’farasws Bin Muhammadasws’. So he came with a huge platter (of various dates) and placed it in front of himasws. So heasws said to the man: ‘What is this?’ He said, ‘This is Al-Barny (dates)’. So heasws said: ‘Therein is a healing’, and heasws looked at Al-Sabiriyya (dates), so heasws said: ‘What is this?’ So he said, ‘Al-Sabiriyya’. So heasws said: ‘With us this is (called) Al-Bayz’. An heasws said for Al-Mushan (dates): ‘What is this?’ So the man said, ‘Al-Mushan (dates)’. So heasws said: ‘This, with us is (called) Umm Jirzan’. And heasws looked at Al-Safran, so heasws said: ‘What is this?’ So the man said, ‘Al-Sarfan’. So heasws said: ‘With us it is (called) Al-Ajwa and therein is a healing’.

text: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hisham Bin Al Hakam, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, said, ‘The dates were mentioned in his<sup>asws</sup> presence, so he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The one (type) with you is better than one (type) with us, and the entirety of what is with us is better than the entirety of what is with you all’.

citation.arabic_text: عَلِيُّ بْنُ إِبْرَاهِيمَ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنِ ابْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ عَنْ هِشَامِ بْنِ الْحَكَمِ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) قَالَ ذُكِرَتِ التُّمُورُ عِنْدَهُ فَقَالَ الْوَاحِدُ عِنْدَكُمْ أَطْيَبُ مِنَ الْوَاحِدِ عِنْدَنَا وَ الْجَمِيعُ عِنْدَنَا أَطْيَبُ مِنَ الْجَمِيعِ عِنْدَكُمْ .
citation.translation: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hisham Bin Al Hakam, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, said, ‘The dates were mentioned in his<sup>asws</sup> presence, so he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The one (type) with you is better than one (type) with us, and the entirety of what is with us is better than the entirety of what is with you all’.

text: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Abdullah Bin Muhammad Al Hajjal, from Abu Suleyman Al Hammar who said, ‘We were in the presence of Abu Abdullahasws, so they came to us with Mazeyra (a sauce), and food after it. Then we were given a basket of dates upon which were a variety of these. So heasws went on to take with hisasws hand one after the other, and heasws was saying: ‘Which thing do you call this one?’ So we said such and such, until heasws he took (another) one, so heasws said: ‘So what are you calling this one?’ So we said, ‘Al-Mushan’. So heasws said: ‘We call it Umm Jirzan, and that Rasool-Allahsaww was given something from it, so hesaww ate from it, and supplicated for it, therefore there is nothing from the palm trees which is more fruit-bearing than it’.

citation.arabic_text: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَحْيَى عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنْ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ الْحَجَّالِ عَنْ أَبِي سُلَيْمَانَ الْحَمَّارِ قَالَ كُنَّا عِنْدَ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) فَجَاءَنَا بِمَضِيرَةٍ وَ طَعَامٍ بَعْدَهَا ثُمَّ أَتَى بِقِنَاعٍ مِنْ رُطَبٍ عَلَيْهِ أَلْوَانٌ فَجَعَلَ ( عليه السلام ) يَأْخُذُ بِيَدِهِ الْوَاحِدَةَ بَعْدَ الْوَاحِدَةِ فَيَقُولُ أَيَّ شَيْ‏ءٍ تُسَمُّونَ هَذَا فَنَقُولُ كَذَا وَ كَذَا حَتَّى أَخَذَ وَاحِدَةً فَقَالَ مَا تُسَمُّونَ هَذِهِ فَقُلْنَا الْمُشَانَ فَقَالَ نَحْنُ نُسَمِّيهَا أُمَّ جِرْذَانَ إِنَّ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ ( صلى الله عليه وآله ) أُتِيَ بِشَيْ‏ءٍ مِنْهَا فَأَكَلَ مِنْهَا وَ دَعَا لَهَا فَلَيْسَ شَيْ‏ءٌ مِنْ نَخْلٍ أَحْمَلَ مِنْهَا .
citation.translation: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Abdullah Bin Muhammad Al Hajjal, from Abu Suleyman Al Hammar who said, ‘We were in the presence of Abu Abdullahasws, so they came to us with Mazeyra (a sauce), and food after it. Then we were given a basket of dates upon which were a variety of these. So heasws went on to take with hisasws hand one after the other, and heasws was saying: ‘Which thing do you call this one?’ So we said such and such, until heasws he took (another) one, so heasws said: ‘So what are you calling this one?’ So we said, ‘Al-Mushan’. So heasws said: ‘We call it Umm Jirzan, and that Rasool-Allahsaww was given something from it, so hesaww ate from it, and supplicated for it, therefore there is nothing from the palm trees which is more fruit-bearing than it’.

text: Abu Ali Al Ashary, from Muhammad Bin Abdul Jabbar, from Ibn Fazzal, from Sa’alba Bin Maymoun, from Ammar Al Sabaty who said, ‘I was with Abu Abdullahasws, so heasws brought me some dates, and heasws went on to eat from it, and drank the water, and heasws gave me the bowl. So I disliked to return it, so I drank until I had done that repeatedly. So I said, ‘I was with excess phlegm so I complained about it to Ahran the physician of Al-Hajjaj’. So heasws said to me: ‘Is there a palm tree for you in the orchard?’ I said, ‘Yes’. Heasws said: ‘Therein are palm trees?’ I said, ‘Yes’. So heasws said to me: ‘Count to measws whatever its therein’. So I counted until I reached Al-Heyroun (a type of date). So heasws said to me: ‘Eat seven dates from it whenever you intend to sleep, and do not drink the water’. So I did it, and I wanted to spit but I did not have the ability upon that. So I complained to himasws of that, so heasws said to me: ‘Drink the water, a little, and wait until your condition is moderate’. So I did it. So Abu Abdullahasws said: ‘As for myselfasws, so had it not been for the water, I would not care if Iasws do not taste it’.

citation.arabic_text: أَبُو عَلِيٍّ الْأَشْعَرِيُّ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عَبْدِ الْجَبَّارِ عَنِ ابْنِ فَضَّالٍ عَنْ ثَعْلَبَةَ بْنِ مَيْمُونٍ عَنْ عَمَّارٍ السَّابَاطِيِّ قَالَ كُنْتُ مَعَ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) فَأُتِيَ بِرُطَبٍ فَجَعَلَ يَأْكُلُ مِنْهُ وَ يَشْرَبُ الْمَاءَ وَ يُنَاوِلُنِي الْإِنَاءَ فَأَكْرَهُ أَنْ أَرُدَّهُ فَأَشْرَبُ حَتَّى فَعَلَ ذَلِكَ مِرَاراً قَالَ فَقُلْتُ إِنِّي كُنْتُ صَاحِبَ بَلْغَمٍ فَشَكَوْتُ إِلَى أَهْرَنَ طَبِيبِ الْحَجَّاجِ فَقَالَ لِي أَ لَكَ نَخْلٌ فِي بُسْتَانٍ قُلْتُ نَعَمْ قَالَ فِيهِ نَخْلٌ قُلْتُ نَعَمْ فَقَالَ لِي عُدَّ عَلَيَّ مَا فِيهِ فَعَدَدْتُ حَتَّى بَلَغْتُ الْهِيرُونَ فَقَالَ لِي كُلْ مِنْهُ سَبْعَ تَمَرَاتٍ حِينَ تُرِيدُ أَنْ تَنَامَ وَ لَا تَشْرَبِ الْمَاءَ فَفَعَلْتُ وَ كُنْتُ أُرِيدُ أَنْ أَبْصُقَ فَلَا أَقْدِرُ عَلَى ذَلِكَ فَشَكَوْتُ إِلَيْهِ ذَلِكَ فَقَالَ لِي اشْرَبِ الْمَاءَ قَلِيلًا وَ أَمْسِكْ حَتَّى يَعْتَدِلَ طَبْعُكَ فَفَعَلْتُ فَقَالَ أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) أَمَّا أَنَا فَلَوْ لَا الْمَاءُ مَا بَالَيْتُ أَلَّا أَذُوقَهُ .

text: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Abu Abdullah, from Muhammad Bin Isa, from Dahqan, from Dorost Bin Abu Mansour, from Abdullah Bin Sinan, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws having said: ‘The one who eats seven Ajwa dates during every day upon the empty stomach from the dates of Al-Aaliya (A place in Al-Medina), neither would poison harm him, nor sorcery, nor Satanla’.

citation.arabic_text: عِدَّةٌ مِنْ أَصْحَابِنَا عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنِ الدِّهْقَانِ عَنْ دُرُسْتَ بْنِ أَبِي مَنْصُورٍ عَنْ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ بْنِ سِنَانٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) قَالَ مَنْ أَكَلَ فِي كُلِّ يَوْمٍ سَبْعَ تَمَرَاتٍ عَجْوَةٍ عَلَى الرِّيقِ مِنْ تَمْرِ الْعَالِيَةِ لَمْ يَضُرَّهُ سَمٌّ وَ لَا سِحْرٌ وَ لَا شَيْطَانٌ .

text: From him, from Yaqoub Bin Yazeed, from Ziyad Bin Marwan Al Qindy, from Abdullah Bin Sinan, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws having said: ‘The one who eats seven Ajwa dates at his sleep time, would kill the insects in his belly’.

citation.arabic_text: عَنْهُ عَنْ يَعْقُوبَ بْنِ يَزِيدَ عَنْ زِيَادِ بْنِ مَرْوَانَ الْقَنْدِيِّ عَنْ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ بْنِ سِنَانٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) قَالَ مَنْ أَكَلَ سَبْعَ تَمَرَاتٍ عَجْوَةٍ عِنْدَ مَنَامِهِ قَتَلْنَ الدِّيدَانَ مِنْ بَطْنِهِ .
citation.translation: From him, from Yaqoub Bin Yazeed, from Ziyad Bin Marwan Al Qindy, from Abdullah Bin Sinan, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws having said: ‘The one who eats seven Ajwa dates at his sleep time, would kill the insects in his belly’.

text: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Khalid, from Ibrahim Bin Uqba, from Muyassar, from Muhammad Bin Abdul Aziz, from his father, (It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’farasws or Abu Abdullahasws regarding the Words of Allahazwj Mighty and Majestic [18:19] then let him see which of them has purest food, so let him bring you provision from it’.

citation.arabic_text: اللَّهِ عَزَّ وَ جَلَّ فَلْيَنْظُرْ أَيُّها أَزْكى طَعاماً فَلْيَأْتِكُمْ بِرِزْقٍ مِنْهُ قَالَ أَزْكَى طَعَاماً التَّمْرُ .

text: From him, from his father, from Ibn Sinan, from Ibrahim Bin Mihzam, from Anbasa Bin Bajad, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Never was a meal presented to Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> in which were dates, except that he<sup>saww</sup> began with the dates’.

citation.arabic_text: مَا قُدِّمَ إِلَى رَسُولِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) طَعَامٌ فِيهِ تَمْرٌ إِلَّا بَدَأَ بِالتَّمْرِ .

text: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Hanaan Bin Sudeyr, from his father who said, ‘Ali<sup>asws</sup> Bin Al-Husayn<sup>asws</sup> loved to see a date-loving person due to the love of Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> for the dates’.

citation.arabic_text: كَانَ عَلِيُّ بْنُ الْحُسَيْنِ ( عليه السلام ) يُحِبُّ أَنْ يَرَى الرَّجُلَ تَمْرِيّاً لِحُبِّ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ ( صلى الله عليه وآله ) التَّمْرَ .
citation.translation: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Hanaan Bin Sudeyr, from his father who said, ‘Ali<sup>asws</sup> Bin Al-Husayn<sup>asws</sup> loved to see a date-loving person due to the love of Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> for the dates’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: حسن أو موثق - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (22/181)

text: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Abu Al Magra, from one of his companions, from Uqba Bin Bashir, (It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup>, said, ‘We went over to him<sup>asws</sup>, so he<sup>asws</sup> called for the dates, and we ate them. citation.arabic_text: دَخَلْنَا عَلَيْهِ فَاسْتَدْعَى بِتَمْرٍ فَأَكَلْنَا ثُمَّ ازْدَدْنَا مِنْهُ ثُمَّ قَالَ قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ ( صلى الله عليه وآله ) إِنِّي أُحِبُّ الرَّجُلَ أَوْ قَالَ يُعْجِبُنِي الرَّجُلُ إِذَا كَانَ تَمْرِيّاً .

citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: مرسل مجهول - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (22/181)

text: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Amro Bin Usman, from Abu Amro, from a man, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws having said: ‘The best of your dates is Al-Barny, it does away with the illnesses, and there is no illness in it, and it does away with the fatigue and there is no harmfulness for it, and it does away with the phlegm; and with every date is a Reward’. And in another report, ‘It is palatable, and it is wholesome (nourishing), and it does away with the fatigue, and it satiates’.

citation.arabic_text: خَيْرُ تُمُورِكُمُ الْبَرْنِيُّ يَذْهَبُ بِالدَّاءِ وَ لَا دَاءَ فِيهِ وَ يَذْهَبُ بِالْإِعْيَاءِ وَ لَا ضَرَرَ لَهُ وَ يَذْهَبُ بِالْبَلْغَمِ وَ مَعَ كُلِّ تَمْرَةٍ حَسَنَةٌ وَ فِي رِوَايَةٍ أُخْرَى يَهْنَأُ وَ يَمْرَأُ وَ يَذْهَبُ بِالْإِعْيَاءِ وَ يُشْبِعُ .

text: A number of our companions, from sahl Bin Ziyad, from Muhammad Bin Ismail Al Razy, from Suleyman Bin Ja’far Al Ja’fary who said, ‘I went over to Abu Al-Hassan Al-Rezaasws and in front of himasws were Barny dates heasws was constant in eating it, eating it with desire. So heasws said to me: ‘O Suleyman! Approach and eat’. So I approached himasws and ate with himasws, and I said to himasws, ‘May I be sacrificed for youasws! I see youasws eating this date with desire’. So heasws said: ‘Yes, Iasws love it’. He (the narrator) said, ‘I said, ‘And why is that so?’ Heasws said: ‘Because Rasool-Allahsaww was a date-lover, and Aliasws was a date-lover, and Al-Hassanasws was a date-lover, and Abu Abdullah Al-Husaynasws was a date-lover, and Zayn Al-Abideenasws was a date-lover, and Abu Ja’farasws was a date-lover, and Abu Abdullahasws was a date-lover, and myasws fatherasws was a date-lover, and ourasws Shias are loving the dates because they have been Created from ourasws clay, and ourasws enemies, O Sulayman, are loving the intoxicants because they have been Created from the [55:15] smokeless fire’.

citation.arabic_text: دَخَلْتُ عَلَى أَبِي الْحَسَنِ الرِّضَا ( عليه السلام ) وَ بَيْنَ يَدَيْهِ تَمْرٌ بَرْنِيٌّ وَ هُوَ مُجِدٌّ فِي أَكْلِهِ يَأْكُلُهُ بِشَهْوَةٍ فَقَالَ لِي يَا سُلَيْمَانُ ادْنُ فَكُلْ قَالَ فَدَنَوْتُ مِنْهُ فَأَكَلْتُ مَعَهُ وَ أَنَا أَقُولُ لَهُ جُعِلْتُ فِدَاكَ إِنِّي أَرَاكَ تَأْكُلُ هَذَا التَّمْرَ بِشَهْوَةٍ فَقَالَ نَعَمْ إِنِّي لَأُحِبُّهُ قَالَ قُلْتُ وَ لِمَ ذَاكَ قَالَ لِأَنَّ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ ( صلى الله عليه وآله ) كَانَ تَمْرِيّاً وَ كَانَ عَلِيٌّ ( عليه السلام ) تَمْرِيّاً وَ كَانَ الْحَسَنُ ( عليه السلام ) تَمْرِيّاً وَ كَانَ أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ الْحُسَيْنُ ( عليه السلام ) تَمْرِيّاً وَ كَانَ زَيْنُ الْعَابِدِينَ ( عليه السلام ) تَمْرِيّاً وَ كَانَ أَبُو جَعْفَرٍ ( عليه السلام ) تَمْرِيّاً وَ كَانَ أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) تَمْرِيّاً وَ كَانَ أَبِي ( عليه السلام ) تَمْرِيّاً وَ أَنَا تَمْرِيٌّ وَ شِيعَتُنَا يُحِبُّونَ التَّمْرَ لِأَنَّهُمْ خُلِقُوا مِنْ طِينَتِنَا وَ أَعْدَاؤُنَا يَا سُلَيْمَانُ يُحِبُّونَ الْمُسْكِرَ لِأَنَّهُمْ خُلِقُوا مِنْ مَارِجٍ مِنْ نَارٍ .

text: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ismail Bin Marrar, from Yunus, from Hisham Bin Al Hakam, from Zurrar, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws having said: ‘Al-Barny dates satiate, and it is palatable, and it is nourishing, and it is the cure and there is no illness for it. It does away with the fatigue, and with every date is a Reward’.

citation.arabic_text: التَّمْرُ الْبَرْنِيُّ يُشْبِعُ وَ يَهْنَأُ وَ يَمْرَأُ وَ هُوَ الدَّوَاءُ وَ لَا دَاءَ لَهُ يَذْهَبُ بِالْعَيَاءِ وَ مَعَ كُلِّ تَمْرَةٍ حَسَنَةٌ .

text: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Abu Abdullah, from Muhammad Bin Ali, from Ali Bin Khattab Al Hallal, from A’ala Bin Razeyn who said, ‘Abu Abdullahasws said to me: ‘O A’ala! Do you know what is the first tree planted upon the surface of the earth?’ I said, ‘Allahazwj and Hisazwj Rasoolsaww and a sonasws of Hisazwj Rasoolsaww are most knowing’. Heasws said: ‘It is Al-Ajwa. So whatever is pure so it is Al-Ajwa, and whatever was other than that, so rather it is from its resemblances’.

citation.arabic_text: قَالَ لِي أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) يَا عَلَاءُ هَلْ تَدْرِي مَا أَوَّلُ شَجَرَةٍ نَبَتَتْ عَلَى وَجْهِ الْأَرْضِ قُلْتُ اللَّهُ وَ رَسُولُهُ وَ ابْنُ رَسُولِهِ أَعْلَمُ قَالَ إِنَّهَا الْعَجْوَةُ فَمَا خَلَصَ فَهُوَ الْعَجْوَةُ وَ مَا كَانَ غَيْرَ ذَلِكَ فَإِنَّمَا هُوَ مِنَ الْأَشْبَاهِ .
citation.translation: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Abu Abdullah, from Muhammad Bin Ali, from Ali Bin Khattab Al Hallal, from A’ala Bin Razeyn who said, ‘Abu Abdullahasws said to me: ‘O A’ala! text: From him, from his father, form Hammad Bin Isa, from Rabie Bin Abdullah, from Al Fuzayl, (It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’farasws having said: ‘Allahazwj Mighty and Majestic Sent down Al-Ajwa and Al-Ateeq from the sky’. I said, ‘And what is Al-Ateeq?’ Heasws said: ‘The stallion’.

citation.arabic_text: أَنْزَلَ اللَّهُ عَزَّ وَ جَلَّ الْعَجْوَةَ وَ الْعَتِيقَ مِنَ السَّمَاءِ قُلْتُ وَ مَا الْعَتِيقُ قَالَ الْفَحْلُ .
citation.translation: From him, from his father, form Hammad Bin Isa, from Rabie Bin Abdullah, from Al Fuzayl, (It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’farasws having said: ‘Allahazwj Mighty and Majestic Sent down Al-Ajwa and Al-Ateeq from the sky’. I said, ‘And what is Al-Ateeq?’ Heasws said: ‘The stallion’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: حسن - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (22/182)

text: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Muhammad Bin Al Husayn, from Abdul Rahman Bin Abu Hashim, from Abu Khadeeja, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws having said: ‘Al-Ajwa, it is the mother of the dates which Allahazwj Mighty and Majestic Sent down to Adamas, from the Paradise’.

citation.arabic_text: الْعَجْوَةُ هِيَ أُمُّ التَّمْرِ الَّتِي أَنْزَلَهَا اللَّهُ عَزَّ وَ جَلَّ لآِدَمَ ( عليه السلام ) مِنَ الْجَنَّةِ .
citation.translation: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Muhammad Bin Al Husayn, from Abdul Rahman Bin Abu Hashim, from Abu Khadeeja, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws having said: ‘Al-Ajwa, it is the mother of the dates which Allahazwj Mighty and Majestic Sent down to Adamas, from the Paradise’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: مختلف فيه - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (2/183)

text: Al Husayn Bin Muhammad, from Moala Bin Muhammad, from Al Washa, from Ahmad Bin A’iz, from Abu Khadeeja, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws having said: ‘Al-Ajwa is the mother of the dates and it is which Allahazwj Mighty and Majestic Sent down from the Paradise to Adamas, and these are the Words of Allahazwj Mighty and Majestic [59:5] Whatever palm-tree you cut down or leave standing upon its roots – it Means Al-Ajwa’.

citation.arabic_text: الْعَجْوَةُ أُمُّ التَّمْرِ وَ هِيَ الَّتِي أَنْزَلَهَا اللَّهُ عَزَّ وَ جَلَّ مِنَ الْجَنَّةِ لآِدَمَ ( عليه السلام ) وَ هُوَ قَوْلُ اللَّهِ عَزَّ وَ جَلَّ ما قَطَعْتُمْ مِنْ لِينَةٍ أَوْ تَرَكْتُمُوها قائِمَةً عَلى أُصُولِها قَالَ يَعْنِي الْعَجْوَةَ .
citation.translation: Al Husayn Bin Muhammad, from Moala Bin Muhammad, from Al Washa, from Ahmad Bin A’iz, from Abu Khadeeja, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws having said: ‘Al-Ajwa is the mother of the dates and it is which Allahazwj Mighty and Majestic Sent down from the Paradise to Adamas, and these are the Words of Allahazwj Mighty and Majestic [59:5] Whatever palm-tree you cut down or leave standing upon its roots – it Means Al-Ajwa’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: ضعيف على المشهور - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (2/183)

text: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Moamar Bin Khallad, (It has been narrated) from Abu Al-Hassan Al-Rezaasws having said: ‘The palm tree of Maryamas was Al-Ajwa, and it was Sent down in December/January, and Al-Ajwa and Al-Ateeq were Sent down with Adamas, and from it the variety of the palm trees disseminated’.

citation.arabic_text: كَانَتْ نَخْلَةُ مَرْيَمَ ( عليها السلام ) الْعَجْوَةَ وَ نَزَلَتْ فِي كَانُونَ وَ نَزَلَ مَعَ آدَمَ ( عليه السلام ) الْعَتِيقُ وَ الْعَجْوَةُ وَ مِنْهَا تَفَرَّقَ أَنْوَاعُ النَّخْلِ .
citation.translation: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Moamar Bin Khallad, (It has been narrated) from Abu Al-Hassan Al-Rezaasws having said: ‘The palm tree of Maryamas was Al-Ajwa, and it was Sent down in December/January, and Al-Ajwa and Al-Ateeq were Sent down with Adamas, and from it the variety of the palm trees disseminated’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: صحيح - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (22/183)

text: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Muhammad Bin Al Husayn, from Abdul Rahman Bin Abu Hashim, from Abu Khadeeja who said, ‘We took a variety of dates from Al-Medina, so a companion of our planted it in an orchard. So there came out from it, Al-Sakkar, and Al-Heyroun, and Al-Shahreyz, and Al-Sarfan, and every type of date’.

citation.arabic_text: أَخَذْنَا مِنَ الْمَدِينَةِ نَوَى الْعَجْوَةِ فَغَرَسَهُ صَاحِبٌ لَنَا فِي بُسْتَانٍ فَخَرَجَ مِنْهُ السُّكَّرُ وَ الْهِيرُونُ وَ الشِّهْرِيزُ وَ الصَّرَفَانُ وَ كُلُّ ضَرْبٍ مِنَ التَّمْرِ .
citation.translation: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Muhammad Bin Al Husayn, from Abdul Rahman Bin Abu Hashim, from Abu Khadeeja who said, ‘We took a variety of dates from Al-Medina, so a companion of our planted it in an orchard. So there came out from it, Al-Sakkar, and Al-Heyroun, and Al-Shahreyz, and Al-Sarfan, and every type of date’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: مختلف فيه - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (2/183)

text: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hisham Bin Al Hakam, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws having said: ‘Al-Sarfan is the chief of your dates’.

citation.arabic_text: الصَّرَفَانُ سَيِّدُ تُمُورِكُمْ .
citation.translation: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hisham Bin Al Hakam, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws having said: ‘Al-Sarfan is the chief of your dates’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: حسن - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (2/184)

text: Al Husayn Bin Muhammad, from Ahmad Bin Is’haq, and Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Muhammad Bin Ismail, altogether from Sa’dan Bin Muslim, from one of our companions who said, ‘ When Abu Abdullahasws proceeded to Al-Hira, heasws rode hisasws animal, and went to Al-Khowrank. So heasws descended and took shade with the shadow of hisasws animal, and with himasws was a black slave of hisasws. So heasws a man from the people of Al-Kufa who had bought a palm tree said to the slave: ‘Who is this one?’ So he said to him, ‘This is Ja’farasws Bin Muhammadasws’. So he came with a huge platter (of various dates) and placed it in front of himasws. So heasws said to the man: ‘What is this?’ He said, ‘This is Al-Barny (dates)’. So heasws said: ‘Therein is a healing’, and heasws looked at Al-Sabiriyya (dates), so heasws said: ‘What is this?’ So he said, ‘Al-Sabiriyya’. So heasws said: ‘With us this is (called) Al-Bayz’. An heasws said for Al-Mushan (dates): ‘What is this?’ So the man said, ‘Al-Mushan (dates)’. So heasws said: ‘This, with us is (called) Umm Jirzan’. And heasws looked at Al-Safran, so heasws said: ‘What is this?’ So the man said, ‘Al-Sarfan’. So heasws said: ‘With us it is (called) Al-Ajwa and therein is a healing’.

citation.arabic_text: لَمَّا قَدِمَ أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) الْحِيرَةَ رَكِبَ دَابَّتَهُ وَ مَضَى إِلَى الْخَوَرْنَقِ فَنَزَلَ فَاسْتَظَلَّ بِظِلِّ دَابَّتِهِ وَ مَعَهُ غُلَامٌ لَهُ أَسْوَدُ فَرَأَى رَجُلًا مِنْ أَهْلِ الْكُوفَةِ قَدِ اشْتَرَى نَخْلًا فَقَالَ لِلْغُلَامِ مَنْ هَذَا فَقَالَ لَهُ هَذَا جَعْفَرُ بْنُ مُحَمَّدٍ ( عليه السلام ) فَجَاءَ بِطَبَقٍ ضَخْمٍ فَوَضَعَهُ بَيْنَ يَدَيْهِ فَقَالَ لِلرَّجُلِ مَا هَذَا فَقَالَ هَذَا الْبَرْنِيُّ فَقَالَ فِيهِ شِفَاءٌ وَ نَظَرَ إِلَى السَّابِرِيِّ فَقَالَ مَا هَذَا فَقَالَ السَّابِرِيُّ فَقَالَ هَذَا عِنْدَنَا الْبِيضُ وَ قَالَ لِلْمُشَانِ مَا هَذَا فَقَالَ الرَّجُلُ الْمُشَانُ فَقَالَ ( عليه السلام ) هَذَا عِنْدَنَا أُمُّ جِرْذَانَ وَ نَظَرَ إِلَى الصَّرَفَانِ فَقَالَ مَا هَذَا فَقَالَ الرَّجُلُ الصَّرَفَانُ فَقَالَ هُوَ عِنْدَنَا الْعَجْوَةُ وَ فِيهِ شِفَاءٌ .

text: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hisham Bin Al Hakam, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, said, ‘The dates were mentioned in his<sup>asws</sup> presence, so he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The one (type) with you is better than one (type) with us, and the entirety of what is with us is better than the entirety of what is with you all’.

citation.arabic_text: ذُكِرَتِ التُّمُورُ عِنْدَهُ فَقَالَ الْوَاحِدُ عِنْدَكُمْ أَطْيَبُ مِنَ الْوَاحِدِ عِنْدَنَا وَ الْجَمِيعُ عِنْدَنَا أَطْيَبُ مِنَ الْجَمِيعِ عِنْدَكُمْ .
citation.translation: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hisham Bin Al Hakam, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, said, ‘The dates were mentioned in his<sup>asws</sup> presence, so he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The one (type) with you is better than one (type) with us, and the entirety of what is with us is better than the entirety of what is with you all’.

text: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Abdullah Bin Muhammad Al Hajjal, from Abu Suleyman Al Hammar who said, ‘We were in the presence of Abu Abdullahasws, so they came to us with Mazeyra (a sauce), and food after it. Then we were given a basket of dates upon which were a variety of these. So heasws went on to take with hisasws hand one after the other, and heasws was saying: ‘Which thing do you call this one?’ So we said such and such, until heasws he took (another) one, so heasws said: ‘So what are you calling this one?’ So we said, ‘Al-Mushan’. So heasws said: ‘We call it Umm Jirzan, and that Rasool-Allahsaww was given something from it, so hesaww ate from it, and supplicated for it, therefore there is nothing from the palm trees which is more fruit-bearing than it’.

citation.arabic_text: كُنَّا عِنْدَ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) فَجَاءَنَا بِمَضِيرَةٍ وَ طَعَامٍ بَعْدَهَا ثُمَّ أَتَى بِقِنَاعٍ مِنْ رُطَبٍ عَلَيْهِ أَلْوَانٌ فَجَعَلَ ( عليه السلام ) يَأْخُذُ بِيَدِهِ الْوَاحِدَةَ بَعْدَ الْوَاحِدَةِ فَيَقُولُ أَيَّ شَيْ‏ءٍ تُسَمُّونَ هَذَا فَنَقُولُ كَذَا وَ كَذَا حَتَّى أَخَذَ وَاحِدَةً فَقَالَ مَا تُسَمُّونَ هَذِهِ فَقُلْنَا الْمُشَانَ فَقَالَ نَحْنُ نُسَمِّيهَا أُمَّ جِرْذَانَ إِنَّ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ ( صلى الله عليه وآله ) أُتِيَ بِشَيْ‏ءٍ مِنْهَا فَأَكَلَ مِنْهَا وَ دَعَا لَهَا فَلَيْسَ شَيْ‏ءٌ مِنْ نَخْلٍ أَحْمَلَ مِنْهَا .

text: Abu Ali Al Ashary, from Muhammad Bin Abdul Jabbar, from Ibn Fazzal, from Sa’alba Bin Maymoun, from Ammar Al Sabaty who said, ‘I was with Abu Abdullahasws, so heasws brought me some dates, and heasws went on to eat from it, and drank the water, and heasws gave me the bowl. So I disliked to return it, so I drank until I had done that repeatedly. So I said, ‘I was with excess phlegm so I complained about it to Ahran the physician of Al-Hajjaj’. So heasws said to me: ‘Is there a palm tree for you in the orchard?’ I said, ‘Yes’. Heasws said: ‘Therein are palm trees?’ I said, ‘Yes’. So heasws said to me: ‘Count to measws whatever its therein’. So I counted until I reached Al-Heyroun (a type of date). So heasws said to me: ‘Eat seven dates from it whenever you intend to sleep, and do not drink the water’. So I did it, and I wanted to spit but I did not have the ability upon that. So I complained to himasws of that, so heasws said to me: ‘Drink the water, a little, and wait until your condition is moderate’. So I did it. So Abu Abdullahasws said: ‘As for myselfasws, so had it not been for the water, I would not care if Iasws do not taste it’.

citation.arabic_text: كُنْتُ مَعَ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) فَأُتِيَ بِرُطَبٍ فَجَعَلَ يَأْكُلُ مِنْهُ وَ يَشْرَبُ الْمَاءَ وَ يُنَاوِلُنِي الْإِنَاءَ فَأَكْرَهُ أَنْ أَرُدَّهُ فَأَشْرَبُ حَتَّى فَعَلَ ذَلِكَ مِرَاراً قَالَ فَقُلْتُ إِنِّي كُنْتُ صَاحِبَ بَلْغَمٍ فَشَكَوْتُ إِلَى أَهْرَنَ طَبِيبِ الْحَجَّاجِ فَقَالَ لِي أَ لَكَ نَخْلٌ فِي بُسْتَانٍ قُلْتُ نَعَمْ قَالَ فِيهِ نَخْلٌ قُلْتُ نَعَمْ فَقَالَ لِي عُدَّ عَلَيَّ مَا فِيهِ فَعَدَدْتُ حَتَّى بَلَغْتُ الْهِيرُونَ فَقَالَ لِي كُلْ مِنْهُ سَبْعَ تَمَرَاتٍ حِينَ تُرِيدُ أَنْ تَنَامَ وَ لَا تَشْرَبِ الْمَاءَ فَفَعَلْتُ وَ كُنْتُ أُرِيدُ أَنْ أَبْصُقَ فَلَا أَقْدِرُ عَلَى ذَلِكَ فَشَكَوْتُ إِلَيْهِ ذَلِكَ فَقَالَ لِي اشْرَبِ الْمَاءَ قَلِيلًا وَ أَمْسِكْ حَتَّى يَعْتَدِلَ طَبْعُكَ فَفَعَلْتُ فَقَالَ أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) أَمَّا أَنَا فَلَوْ لَا الْمَاءُ مَا بَالَيْتُ أَلَّا أَذُوقَهُ .

text: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Abu Abdullah, from Muhammad Bin Isa, from Dahqan, from Dorost Bin Abu Mansour, from Abdullah Bin Sinan, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws having said: ‘The one who eats seven Ajwa dates during every day upon the empty stomach from the dates of Al-Aaliya (A place in Al-Medina), neither would poison harm him, nor sorcery, nor Satanla’.

citation.arabic_text: مَنْ أَكَلَ فِي كُلِّ يَوْمٍ سَبْعَ تَمَرَاتٍ عَجْوَةٍ عَلَى الرِّيقِ مِنْ تَمْرِ الْعَالِيَةِ لَمْ يَضُرَّهُ سَمٌّ وَ لَا سِحْرٌ وَ لَا شَيْطَانٌ .
citation.translation: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Abu Abdullah, from Muhammad Bin Isa, from Dahqan, from Dorost Bin Abu Mansour, from Abdullah Bin Sinan, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws having said: ‘The one who eats seven Ajwa dates during every day upon the empty stomach from the dates of Al-Aaliya (A place in Al-Medina), neither would poison harm him, nor sorcery, nor Satanla’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: ضعيف - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (2/186)

text: From him, from Yaqoub Bin Yazeed, from Ziyad Bin Marwan Al Qindy, from Abdullah Bin Sinan, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws having said: ‘The one who eats seven Ajwa dates at his sleep time, would kill the insects in his belly’.

citation.arabic_text: مَنْ أَكَلَ سَبْعَ تَمَرَاتٍ عَجْوَةٍ عِنْدَ مَنَامِهِ قَتَلْنَ الدِّيدَانَ مِنْ بَطْنِهِ .
citation.translation: From him, from Yaqoub Bin Yazeed, from Ziyad Bin Marwan Al Qindy, from Abdullah Bin Sinan, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws having said: ‘The one who eats seven Ajwa dates at his sleep time, would kill the insects in his belly’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: موثق - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (2/187)

text: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Abu Abdullah, from his father, from Ahmad Bin Suleyman, from Ahmad Bin Yahya Al Tahhan, from the one who narrated it, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abullahasws having said: ‘Five are from the fruits of the Paradise in the world – the Al-Amleysi Pomegranate, and Al-Sheysqan apple, and the Quince, and the Al-Raziqy grapes, and Al-Mushan dates’.

citation.arabic_text: خَمْسٌ مِنْ فَوَاكِهِ الْجَنَّةِ فِي الدُّنْيَا الرُّمَّانُ الْإِمْلِيسِيُّ وَ التُّفَّاحُ الشَّيْسَقَانُ وَ السَّفَرْجَلُ وَ الْعِنَبُ الرَّازِقِيُّ وَ الرُّطَبُ الْمُشَانُ .
citation.translation: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Abu Abdullah, from his father, from Ahmad Bin Suleyman, from Ahmad Bin Yahya Al Tahhan, from the one who narrated it, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abullahasws having said: ‘Five are from the fruits of the Paradise in the world – the Al-Amleysi Pomegranate, and Al-Sheysqan apple, and the Quince, and the Al-Raziqy grapes, and Al-Mushan dates’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: مجهول مرسل - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (2/187)

text: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Abdullah Bin Ja’far, from Abdul Aziz Bin Zakariyya Al Lu’lui, from Suleyman Bin Al Mufazzal who said, ‘I heard Abu Al-Jaroud narrating Abou Abu Ja’farasws having said: ‘Four descended from the Paradise – Al-Raziqy grape, and Al-Mushan date, and Al-Amleysi pomegranate, and Al-Sheysqan apple’.

citation.arabic_text: سَمِعْتُ أَبَا الْجَارُودِ يُحَدِّثُ عَنْ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ ( عليه السلام ) قَالَ أَرْبَعَةٌ نَزَلَتْ مِنَ الْجَنَّةِ الْعِنَبُ الرَّازِقِيُّ وَ الرُّطَبُ الْمُشَانُ وَ الرُّمَّانُ الْإِمْلِيسِيُّ وَ التُّفَّاحُ الشَّيْسَقَانُ .
citation.translation: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Abdullah Bin Ja’far, from Abdul Aziz Bin Zakariyya Al Lu’lui, from Suleyman Bin Al Mufazzal who said, ‘I heard Abu Al-Jaroud narrating Abou Abu Ja’farasws having said: ‘Four descended from the Paradise – Al-Raziqy grape, and Al-Mushan date, and Al-Amleysi pomegranate, and Al-Sheysqan apple’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: ضعيف - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (22/187)

text: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Ja’far Bin Muhammad, from Ibn Al Qaddah, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> him<sup>asws</sup> having disliked peeling the fruits’.

citation.arabic_text: أَنَّهُ كَانَ يَكْرَهُ تَقْشِيرَ الثَّمَرَةِ .
citation.translation: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Ja’far Bin Muhammad, from Ibn Al Qaddah, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> him<sup>asws</sup> having disliked peeling the fruits’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: ضعيف على المشهور - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (22/188)

text: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Abu Abdullah, from Al Husayn Bin Al Munzar, from the one who mentioned it, from Furat Bin Ahnaf who said, ‘Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘For every fruit there is poison, so whenever you are given it, so wipe it with the water, or immerse it in the water, meaning wash it’.

citation.arabic_text: قَالَ أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) إِنَّ لِكُلِّ ثَمَرَةٍ سَمّاً فَإِذَا أَتَيْتُمْ بِهَا فَمَسُّوهَا بِالْمَاءِ أَوِ اغْمِسُوهَا فِي الْمَاءِ يَعْنِي اغْسِلُوهَا .
citation.translation: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Abu Abdullah, from Al Husayn Bin Al Munzar, from the one who mentioned it, from Furat Bin Ahnaf who said, ‘Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘For every fruit there is poison, so whenever you are given it, so wipe it with the water, or immerse it in the water, meaning wash it’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: ضعيف - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (2/188)

text: Muhammad Bin yahya, from Musa Bin Al Hassan, from one of his companions, from Ibn Baqqah, from Haroun Bin Al Khattab, from Abu Al Hassan Al Rassan who said, ‘I was grazing my sheep in a road of Al-Khowrnak, so I saw a group of people walking over. So I inclined towards one who was with them and I said, ‘Who are they?’ So he said, ‘Ja’farasws Bin Muhammadasws and Abdullah Bin Al-Hassan. They are both being taken to Al-Mansour’. He (the narrator) said, ‘So, I asked about them afterwards, and it was said to me, ‘They have lodged at Al-Hira. So, I rose early in order to greet them. So, I went over and there were baskets in front of them in which were dates which had been gifted to them from Al-Kufa and were uncovered in front of them. So, Ja’farasws Bin Muhammadasws extended hisasws hand, so heasws ate and said to me: ‘Eat’. Then heasws said to Abdullah Bin Al-Hassan: ‘O Abu Muhammad! What is your view, how good are these dates?’ Then Ja’farasws Bin Muhammadasws turned around towards me, so heasws said to me: ‘O people of Al-Kufa! You have been preferred over the people in the foods with three – Your fishes, this Al-Bunany; and your grapes, this Al-Raziqy; and your dates, this Al-Mushan’.

citation.arabic_text: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَحْيَى عَنْ مُوسَى بْنِ الْحَسَنِ عَنْ بَعْضِ أَصْحَابِهِ عَنِ ابْنِ بَقَّاحٍ عَنْ هَارُونَ بْنِ الْخَطَّابِ عَنْ أَبِي الْحَسَنِ الرَّسَّانِ قَالَ كُنْتُ أَرْعَى جِمَالِي فِي طَرِيقِ الْخَوَرْنَقِ فَبَصُرْتُ بِقَوْمٍ قَادِمِينَ فَمِلْتُ إِلَى بَعْضِ مَنْ مَعَهُمْ فَقُلْتُ مَنْ هَؤُلَاءِ فَقَالَ جَعْفَرُ بْنُ مُحَمَّدٍ ( عليه السلام ) وَ عَبْدُ اللَّهِ بْنُ الْحَسَنِ قُدِّمَ بِهِمَا عَلَى الْمَنْصُورِ قَالَ فَسَأَلْتُ عَنْهُمْ مِنْ بَعْدُ فَقِيلَ لِي إِنَّهُمْ نَزَلُوا بِالْحِيرَةِ فَبَكَّرْتُ لِأُسَلِّمَ عَلَيْهِمْ فَدَخَلْتُ فَإِذَا قُدَّامَهُمْ سِلَالٌ فِيهَا رُطَبٌ قَدْ أُهْدِيَتْ إِلَيْهِمْ مِنَ الْكُوفَةِ فَكُشِفَتْ قُدَّامَهُمْ فَمَدَّ يَدَهُ جَعْفَرُ بْنُ مُحَمَّدٍ ( عليه السلام ) فَأَكَلَ وَ قَالَ لِي كُلْ ثُمَّ قَالَ لِعَبْدِ اللَّهِ بْنِ الْحَسَنِ يَا أَبَا مُحَمَّدٍ مَا تَرَى مَا أَحْسَنَ هَذَا الرُّطَبَ ثُمَّ الْتَفَتَ إِلَيَّ جَعْفَرُ بْنُ مُحَمَّدٍ ( عليه السلام ) فَقَالَ لِي يَا أَهْلَ الْكُوفَةِ فُضِّلْتُمْ عَلَى النَّاسِ فِي المَطْعَمِ بِثَلَاثٍ سَمَكِكُمْ هَذَا الْبُنَانِيِّ وَ عِنَبِكُمْ هَذَا الرَّازِقِيِّ وَ رُطَبِكُمْ هَذَا الْمُشَانِ .

text: Al Husayn Bin Muhammad, from Moala Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Al Sandy, from Isa Bin Abdul Rahman, from his father, from his grandfather who said, ‘Abu Akasha Bin Mihsan Al-Asady came over to Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup>, so he<sup>asws</sup> forwarded some grapes to him and said to him: ‘One, one (at a time) is how the old man and the young children eat, and three or four (at a time) is how he eats, the one who things he is not satiated, and you eat two (at a time), for it is preferable’.

citation.arabic_text: الْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنْ مُعَلَّى بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ السِّنْدِيِّ قَالَ حَدَّثَنِي عِيسَى بْنُ عَبْدِ الرَّحْمَنِ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ جَدِّهِ قَالَ دَخَلَ أَبُو عُكَّاشَةَ بْنُ مِحْصَنٍ الْأَسَدِيُّ عَلَى أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ ( عليه السلام ) فَقَدَّمَ إِلَيْهِ عِنَباً وَ قَالَ لَهُ حَبَّةً حَبَّةً يَأْكُلُ الشَّيْخُ الْكَبِيرُ وَ الصَّبِيُّ الصَّغِيرُ وَ ثَلَاثَةً وَ أَرْبَعَةً يَأْكُلُ مَنْ يَظُنُّ أَنَّهُ لَا يَشْبَعُ وَ كُلْهُ حَبَّتَيْنِ حَبَّتَيْنِ فَإِنَّهُ مُسْتَحَبٌّ .

citation.arabic_text: يَأْكُلُ الْخُبْزَ بِالْعِنَبِ .

text: From him, from Al Qasin Al Zayyat, from Aban Bin Usman, from Musa Bin Al A’ala, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘When the water laid bare the bones of the dead, so Noah<sup>as</sup> saw that and panicked with an intense panic, and was aggrieved due to that. So Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic Revealed unto him<sup>as</sup>: “This is your doing, you<sup>as</sup> supplicated against them”. So he<sup>as</sup> said: ‘O Lord<sup>azwj</sup>! I<sup>as</sup> seek Forgiveness from You<sup>azwj</sup> and I<sup>as</sup> repent to You<sup>azwj</sup>’. So Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic Revealed unto him<sup>as</sup>: “If you<sup>as</sup> were to eat the black grapes, it would do away with (remove) your grief’.

citation.arabic_text: لَمَّا حَسَرَ الْمَاءُ عَنْ عِظَامِ الْمَوْتَى فَرَأَى ذَلِكَ نُوحٌ ( عليه السلام ) جَزِعَ جَزَعاً شَدِيداً وَ اغْتَمَّ لِذَلِكَ فَأَوْحَى اللَّهُ عَزَّ وَ جَلَّ إِلَيْهِ هَذَا عَمَلُكَ بِنَفْسِكَ أَنْتَ دَعَوْتَ عَلَيْهِمْ فَقَالَ يَا رَبِّ إِنِّي أَسْتَغْفِرُكَ وَ أَتُوبُ إِلَيْكَ فَأَوْحَى اللَّهُ عَزَّ وَ جَلَّ إِلَيْهِ أَنْ كُلِ الْعِنَبَ الْأَسْوَدَ لِيَذْهَبَ غَمُّكَ .

text: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hisham Bin Salim who said, ‘Ali<sup>asws</sup> Bin Al-Husayn<sup>asws</sup> liked the grapes. So one day he<sup>as</sup> was Fasting, and when he<sup>as</sup> broke Fast the first of what came were the grapes, given to him<sup>asws</sup> by a mother of his<sup>as</sup> child, a cluster of grapes. So she placed these in front of him<sup>asws</sup>, and a beggar came over. So he<sup>asws</sup> handed these over to him, and the mother of his<sup>as</sup> child went to the beggar and bought them off from him. Then she came with it and placed it in front of him<sup>asws</sup>. So another beggar came over, and he<sup>asws</sup> gave these to him. So the mother of his<sup>as</sup> child did the like of that. Then she came with these and placed them in front of him<sup>as</sup>. So there came another beggar, and he<sup>asws</sup> gave these to him. So the mother of his<sup>asws</sup> child did the like of that. So when it was during the fourth time, he<sup>asws</sup> ate it (as no other beggar came over)’.

citation.arabic_text: كَانَ عَلِيُّ بْنُ الْحُسَيْنِ ( عليه السلام ) يُعْجِبُهُ الْعِنَبُ فَكَانَ يَوْماً صَائِماً فَلَمَّا أَفْطَرَ كَانَ أَوَّلُ مَا جَاءَ الْعِنَبُ أَتَتْهُ أُمُّ وَلَدٍ لَهُ بِعُنْقُودِ عِنَبٍ فَوَضَعَتْهُ بَيْنَ يَدَيْهِ فَجَاءَ سَائِلٌ فَدَفَعَهُ إِلَيْهِ فَدَسَّتْ أُمُّ وَلَدِهِ إِلَى السَّائِلِ فَاشْتَرَتْهُ مِنْهُ ثُمَّ أَتَتْهُ بِهِ فَوَضَعَتْهُ بَيْنَ يَدَيْهِ فَجَاءَ سَائِلٌ آخَرُ فَأَعْطَاهُ إِيَّاهُ فَفَعَلَتْ أُمُّ الْوَلَدِ كَذَلِكَ ثُمَّ أَتَتْهُ بِهِ فَوَضَعَتْهُ بَيْنَ يَدَيْهِ فَجَاءَ سَائِلٌ آخَرُ فَأَعْطَاهُ فَفَعَلَتْ أُمُّ الْوَلَدِ مِثْلَ ذَلِكَ فَلَمَّا كَانَ فِي الْمَرَّةِ الرَّابِعَةِ أَكَلَهُ ( عليه السلام ).

text: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Bakr Bin Salih, (It has been narrated) raising it from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘A Prophet<sup>as</sup> from the Prophets<sup>as</sup> complained to Allah<sup>as</sup> Mighty and Majestic of the gloom, so Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic Commanded him<sup>as</sup> with eating the grapes’.

citation.arabic_text: شَكَا نَبِيٌّ مِنَ الْأَنْبِيَاءِ إِلَى اللَّهِ عَزَّ وَ جَلَّ الْغَمَّ فَأَمَرَهُ اللَّهُ عَزَّ وَ جَلَّ بِأَكْلِ الْعِنَبِ .

text: Muhammad Bin yahya, from Musa Bin Al Hassan, from one of his companions, from Ibn Baqqah, from Haroun Bin Al Khattab, from Abu Al Hassan Al Rassan who said, ‘I was grazing my sheep in a road of Al-Khowrnak, so I saw a group of people walking over. So I inclined towards one who was with them and I said, ‘Who are they?’ So he said, ‘Ja’farasws Bin Muhammadasws and Abdullah Bin Al-Hassan. They are both being taken to Al-Mansour’. He (the narrator) said, ‘So, I asked about them afterwards, and it was said to me, ‘They have lodged at Al-Hira. So, I rose early in order to greet them. So, I went over and there were baskets in front of them in which were dates which had been gifted to them from Al-Kufa and were uncovered in front of them. So, Ja’farasws Bin Muhammadasws extended hisasws hand, so heasws ate and said to me: ‘Eat’. Then heasws said to Abdullah Bin Al-Hassan: ‘O Abu Muhammad! What is your view, how good are these dates?’ Then Ja’farasws Bin Muhammadasws turned around towards me, so heasws said to me: ‘O people of Al-Kufa! You have been preferred over the people in the foods with three – Your fishes, this Al-Bunany; and your grapes, this Al-Raziqy; and your dates, this Al-Mushan’.

citation.arabic_text: كُنْتُ أَرْعَى جِمَالِي فِي طَرِيقِ الْخَوَرْنَقِ فَبَصُرْتُ بِقَوْمٍ قَادِمِينَ فَمِلْتُ إِلَى بَعْضِ مَنْ مَعَهُمْ فَقُلْتُ مَنْ هَؤُلَاءِ فَقَالَ جَعْفَرُ بْنُ مُحَمَّدٍ ( عليه السلام ) وَ عَبْدُ اللَّهِ بْنُ الْحَسَنِ قُدِّمَ بِهِمَا عَلَى الْمَنْصُورِ قَالَ فَسَأَلْتُ عَنْهُمْ مِنْ بَعْدُ فَقِيلَ لِي إِنَّهُمْ نَزَلُوا بِالْحِيرَةِ فَبَكَّرْتُ لِأُسَلِّمَ عَلَيْهِمْ فَدَخَلْتُ فَإِذَا قُدَّامَهُمْ سِلَالٌ فِيهَا رُطَبٌ قَدْ أُهْدِيَتْ إِلَيْهِمْ مِنَ الْكُوفَةِ فَكُشِفَتْ قُدَّامَهُمْ فَمَدَّ يَدَهُ جَعْفَرُ بْنُ مُحَمَّدٍ ( عليه السلام ) فَأَكَلَ وَ قَالَ لِي كُلْ ثُمَّ قَالَ لِعَبْدِ اللَّهِ بْنِ الْحَسَنِ يَا أَبَا مُحَمَّدٍ مَا تَرَى مَا أَحْسَنَ هَذَا الرُّطَبَ ثُمَّ الْتَفَتَ إِلَيَّ جَعْفَرُ بْنُ مُحَمَّدٍ ( عليه السلام ) فَقَالَ لِي يَا أَهْلَ الْكُوفَةِ فُضِّلْتُمْ عَلَى النَّاسِ فِي المَطْعَمِ بِثَلَاثٍ سَمَكِكُمْ هَذَا الْبُنَانِيِّ وَ عِنَبِكُمْ هَذَا الرَّازِقِيِّ وَ رُطَبِكُمْ هَذَا الْمُشَانِ .

text: Al Husayn Bin Muhammad, from Moala Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Al Sandy, from Isa Bin Abdul Rahman, from his father, from his grandfather who said, ‘Abu Akasha Bin Mihsan Al-Asady came over to Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup>, so he<sup>asws</sup> forwarded some grapes to him and said to him: ‘One, one (at a time) is how the old man and the young children eat, and three or four (at a time) is how he eats, the one who things he is not satiated, and you eat two (at a time), for it is preferable’.

citation.arabic_text: حَدَّثَنِي عِيسَى بْنُ عَبْدِ الرَّحْمَنِ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ جَدِّهِ قَالَ دَخَلَ أَبُو عُكَّاشَةَ بْنُ مِحْصَنٍ الْأَسَدِيُّ عَلَى أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ ( عليه السلام ) فَقَدَّمَ إِلَيْهِ عِنَباً وَ قَالَ لَهُ حَبَّةً حَبَّةً يَأْكُلُ الشَّيْخُ الْكَبِيرُ وَ الصَّبِيُّ الصَّغِيرُ وَ ثَلَاثَةً وَ أَرْبَعَةً يَأْكُلُ مَنْ يَظُنُّ أَنَّهُ لَا يَشْبَعُ وَ كُلْهُ حَبَّتَيْنِ حَبَّتَيْنِ فَإِنَّهُ مُسْتَحَبٌّ .

text: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Al Nowfaly, from Al Sakuny, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The one starts his morning with (eating) twenty one red raisins would not fall sick except for the sickness of death, Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Willing’.

citation.arabic_text: قَالَ أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ ( عليه السلام ) مَنِ اصْطَبَحَ بِإِحْدَى وَ عِشْرِينَ زَبِيبَةً حَمْرَاءَ لَمْ يَمْرَضْ إِلَّا مَرَضَ الْمَوْتِ إِنْ شَاءَ اللَّهُ .

text: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Al Qasim Bin Yahya, from his grandfather Al Hassan Bin Rashid, from Abu Baseer, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘(Eating) twenty one raisins every day upon the empty stomach dispels the entirety of the diseases except for the disease of death’.

citation.arabic_text: قَالَ أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ ( عليه السلام ) إِحْدَى وَ عِشْرُونَ زَبِيبَةً حَمْرَاءَ فِي كُلِّ يَوْمٍ عَلَى الرِّيقِ تَدْفَعُ جَمِيعَ الْأَمْرَاضِ إِلَّا مَرَضَ الْمَوْتِ .

text: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Abu Abdullah, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Abu Nasr, from a man from the people of Egypt, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘The raisins tighten the nerves, and do away with the exhaustion, and aromatise the breath’.

citation.arabic_text: حَدَّثَنِي رَجُلٌ مِنْ أَهْلِ مِصْرَ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) قَالَ الزَّبِيبُ يَشُدُّ الْعَصَبَ وَ يَذْهَبُ بِالنَّصَبِ وَ يُطَيِّبُ النَّفَسَ .

text: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hammad Bin Usman, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘There is none from the things the participation (of others) in it is more hateful for me than in (eating of) the Pomegranate, and there is none from the Pomegranates except that inside it is a seed from the Paradise. So when the Infidel eats it, Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic Sends an Angels to him, so he removes from it’.

citation.arabic_text: عَلِيُّ بْنُ إِبْرَاهِيمَ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنِ ابْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ عَنْ حَمَّادِ بْنِ عُثْمَانَ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) قَالَ مَا مِنْ شَيْ‏ءٍ أُشَارَكُ فِيهِ أَبْغَضَ إِلَيَّ مِنَ الرُّمَّانِ وَ مَا مِنْ رُمَّانَةٍ إِلَّا وَ فِيهَا حَبَّةٌ مِنَ الْجَنَّةِ فَإِذَا أَكَلَهَا الْكَافِرُ بَعَثَ اللَّهُ عَزَّ وَ جَلَّ إِلَيْهِ مَلَكاً فَانْتَزَعَهَا مِنْهُ .
citation.translation: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hammad Bin Usman, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘There is none from the things the participation (of others) in it is more hateful for me than in (eating of) the Pomegranate, and there is none from the Pomegranates except that inside it is a seed from the Paradise.
