citation.arabic_text: عَنْهُ عَنِ النَّهِيكِيِّ عَنْ عُبَيْدِ اللَّهِ بْنِ أَحْمَدَ عَنْ زِيَادِ بْنِ مَرْوَانَ الْقَنْدِيِّ قَالَ سَمِعْتُ أَبَا الْحَسَنِ ( عليه السلام ) يَعْنِي الْأَوَّلَ يَقُولُ مَنْ أَكَلَ رُمَّانَةً يَوْمَ الْجُمُعَةِ عَلَى الرِّيقِ نَوَّرَتْ قَلْبَهُ أَرْبَعِينَ صَبَاحاً فَإِنْ أَكَلَ رُمَّانَتَيْنِ فَثَمَانِينَ يَوْماً فَإِنْ أَكَلَ ثَلَاثاً فَمِائَةً وَ عِشْرِينَ يَوْماً وَ طُرِدَتْ عَنْهُ وَسْوَسَةُ الشَّيْطَانِ وَ مَنْ طُرِدَتْ عَنْهُ وَسْوَسَةُ الشَّيْطَانِ لَمْ يَعْصِ اللَّهَ عَزَّ وَ جَلَّ وَ مَنْ لَمْ يَعْصِ اللَّهَ أَدْخَلَهُ اللَّهُ الْجَنَّةَ .

text: From him, from Al Husayn Bin Saeed, from Amro Bin Ibrahim, from Al Khurasany who said, ‘Eating the sweet Pomegranate increases in the water of the man, and improves the childbirths’. (P.s. – This is not a Hadeeth)’.

citation.arabic_text: عَنْهُ عَنِ الْحُسَيْنِ بْنِ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ عَمْرِو بْنِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ عَنِ الْخُرَاسَانِيِّ قَالَ أَكْلُ الرُّمَّانِ الْحُلْوِ يَزِيدُ فِي مَاءِ الرَّجُلِ وَ يُحَسِّنُ الْوَلَدَ.

text: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Ibrahim Bin Abul Rahman, from Ziyad, (It has been narrated) from Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Smoke of the Pomegranate negates the vermin’.

citation.arabic_text: عِدَّةٌ مِنْ أَصْحَابِنَا عَنْ سَهْلِ بْنِ زِيَادٍ عَنْ إِبْرَاهِيمَ بْنِ عَبْدِ الرَّحْمَنِ عَنْ زِيَادٍ عَنْ أَبِي الْحَسَنِ ( عليه السلام ) قَالَ دُخَانُ شَجَرِ الرُّمَّانِ يَنْفِي الْهَوَامَّ .

text: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad Bin Ismail, from Al fazl Bin Shazaan, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Ibrahim Bin Abdul Hameed who said, ‘I heard Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> saying: ‘It is upon you with (eating) the Pomegranate, for it would not be eaten by a hungry one except that it would suffice him, nor by a satiated one except that it would be order him (for more food)’.

citation.arabic_text: الْفَاكِهَةُ مِائَةٌ وَ عِشْرُونَ لَوْناً سَيِّدُهَا الرُّمَّانُ .

text: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Abu Abdullah, from his father, from Fazalat Bin Ayoub, from Umar Bin Aban Al Kalby who said, ‘I heard Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> and Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> both<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘There is no fruit upon the surface of the earth more beloved to Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> than the Pomegranate, and, by Allah<sup>azwj</sup> whenever I<sup>asws</sup> have eat it I<sup>asws</sup> love it that no one else should participate in it with me’.

citation.arabic_text: سَمِعْتُ أَبَا جَعْفَرٍ وَ أَبَا عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) يَقُولَانِ مَا عَلَى وَجْهِ الْأَرْضِ ثَمَرَةٌ كَانَتْ أَحَبَّ إِلَى رَسُولِ اللَّهِ ( صلى الله عليه وآله ) مِنَ الرُّمَّانِ وَ كَانَ وَ اللَّهِ إِذَا أَكَلَهَا أَحَبَّ أَنْ لَا يَشْرَكَهُ فِيهَا أَحَدٌ .

text: From him, from Muhammad Bin Isa, from Al Dahqan, from Dorost, from Ibrahim Bin Abdul Hameed, (It has been narrated) from Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘From what Adam<sup>as</sup> bequeathed with to Hibtullah<sup>as</sup> was that he<sup>as</sup> said to him<sup>as</sup>: ‘It is upon you with (eating) the Pomegranate, for if you<sup>as</sup> were to eat it and you<sup>as</sup> are hungry so it would suffice you<sup>as</sup>, and if you<sup>as</sup> were to eat it and you<sup>as</sup> are satiated, it would order you (for more food)’.

citation.arabic_text: مِمَّا أَوْصَى بِهِ آدَمُ ( عليه السلام ) هِبَةَ اللَّهِ أَنْ قَالَ لَهُ عَلَيْكَ بِالرُّمَّانِ فَإِنَّكَ إِنْ أَكَلْتَهُ وَ أَنْتَ جَائِعٌ أَجْزَأَكَ وَ إِنْ أَكَلْتَهُ وَ أَنْتَ شَبْعَانُ أَمْرَأَكَ .

text: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hammad Bin Usman, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘There is none from the things the participation (of others) in it is more hateful for me than in (eating of) the Pomegranate, and there is none from the Pomegranates except that inside it is a seed from the Paradise. So when the Infidel eats it, Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic Sends an Angels to him, so he removes from it’.

citation.arabic_text: مَا مِنْ شَيْ‏ءٍ أُشَارَكُ فِيهِ أَبْغَضَ إِلَيَّ مِنَ الرُّمَّانِ وَ مَا مِنْ رُمَّانَةٍ إِلَّا وَ فِيهَا حَبَّةٌ مِنَ الْجَنَّةِ فَإِذَا أَكَلَهَا الْكَافِرُ بَعَثَ اللَّهُ عَزَّ وَ جَلَّ إِلَيْهِ مَلَكاً فَانْتَزَعَهَا مِنْهُ .

text: Abu Ali Al Ashary, from Muhammad Bin Abdul Jabbar, from Muhammad Bin Salim, from Ahmad Bin Nazar, from Mufazzal who said, ‘I heard Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> saying: ‘There is none from the foods that I<sup>asws</sup> eat except that I<sup>asws</sup> am desirous of a human to participate in it except for the Pomegranate, for there is none from the Pomegranates except inside it is a seed from the Paradise’.

citation.arabic_text: سَمِعْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) يَقُولُ مَا مِنْ طَعَامٍ آكُلُهُ إِلَّا وَ أَنَا أَشْتَهِي أَنْ أُشَارَكَ فِيهِ أَوْ قَالَ يَشْرَكَنِي فِيهِ إِنْسَانٌ إِلَّا الرُّمَّانَ فَإِنَّهُ لَيْسَ مِنْ رُمَّانَةٍ إِلَّا وَ فِيهَا حَبَّةٌ مِنَ الْجَنَّةِ .

text: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Usman Bin Isa, from Sama’at, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Whenever Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> ate the Pomegranate placed a towel underneath it. So he<sup>asws</sup> was asked about that, so he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Therein are seeds from the Paradise’. So it was said to him<sup>asws</sup>, ‘The Jews, and the Christians, and the ones besides them are eating it’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘When it was like that, Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic Sends an Angel to him, so he removes (that seed) from it, perhaps he might eat it’.

citation.arabic_text: كَانَ أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ ( عليه السلام ) إِذَا أَكَلَ الرُّمَّانَ بَسَطَ تَحْتَهُ مِنْدِيلًا فَسُئِلَ عَنْ ذَلِكَ فَقَالَ إِنَّ فِيهِ حَبَّاتٍ مِنَ الْجَنَّةِ. فَقِيلَ لَهُ إِنَّ الْيَهُودَ وَ النَّصَارَى وَ مَنْ سِوَاهُمْ يَأْكُلُونَهُ فَقَالَ إِذَا كَانَ ذَلِكَ بَعَثَ اللَّهُ عَزَّ وَ جَلَّ إِلَيْهِ مَلَكاً فَانْتَزَعَهَا مِنْهُ لِكَيْلَا يَأْكُلَهَا

text: Abu Ali Al Ashary, from Muhammad Bin Abdul Jabbar, from Safwan Bin Yahya, from Mansour Bin Hazim, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘The one who eats a seed from a Pomegranate sickens the whisperings of the Satan<sup>la</sup> for forty days’.

citation.arabic_text: مَنْ أَكَلَ حَبَّةً مِنْ رُمَّانٍ أَمْرَضَتْ شَيْطَانَ الْوَسْوَسَةِ أَرْبَعِينَ يَوْماً .
citation.translation: Abu Ali Al Ashary, from Muhammad Bin Abdul Jabbar, from Safwan Bin Yahya, from Mansour Bin Hazim, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘The one who eats a seed from a Pomegranate sickens the whisperings of the Satan<sup>la</sup> for forty days’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: صحيح - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (22/192)

text: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, and Muhammad Bin Al Husayn, altogether from Muhammad Bin Ismail Bin Bazie, from Salih Bin Uqba, from Yazeed Bin Abdul Malik Al Nowfaly who said, ‘I went over to Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> and in his<sup>asws</sup> hand was a Pomegranate, so he<sup>asws</sup> said to me: ‘O Mo’tab! Give him a Pomegranate, for there is nothing more hateful to me<sup>asws</sup> in letting someone participating in something than letting him participate in a Pomegranate’. Then he<sup>asws</sup> had cupping done and ordered me that I should get cupping done. So I had cupping done. Then he<sup>asws</sup> called for another Pomegranate, then said: ‘O Yazeed! But rather, a Believer eats a Pomegranate until he completes eating it, Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic Sends the Satan<sup>la</sup> away from the illumination of his heart for forty mornings; and the one who eats two, Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic Sends the Satan<sup>la</sup> away from the illumination of his heart for a hundred days; and the one who eats three until he completes these, Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic Sends the Satan<sup>la</sup> away from the illumination of his heart for a year; and the one from whom Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Sends the Satan<sup>la</sup> away from his heart for a year, would not sin, and the one who does not sin would enter the Paradise’.

citation.arabic_text: دَخَلْتُ عَلَى أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) وَ فِي يَدِهِ رُمَّانَةٌ فَقَالَ يَا مُعَتِّبُ أَعْطِهِ رُمَّانَةً فَإِنِّي لَمْ أُشْرَكْ فِي شَيْ‏ءٍ أَبْغَضَ إِلَيَّ مِنْ أَنْ أُشْرَكَ فِي رُمَّانَةٍ ثُمَّ احْتَجَمَ وَ أَمَرَنِي أَنْ أَحْتَجِمَ فَاحْتَجَمْتُ ثُمَّ دَعَا بِرُمَّانَةٍ أُخْرَى ثُمَّ قَالَ يَا يَزِيدُ أَيُّمَا مُؤْمِنٍ أَكَلَ رُمَّانَةً حَتَّى يَسْتَوْفِيَهَا أَذْهَبَ اللَّهُ عَزَّ وَ جَلَّ الشَّيْطَانَ عَنْ إِنَارَةِ قَلْبِهِ أَرْبَعِينَ صَبَاحاً وَ مَنْ أَكَلَ اثْنَتَيْنِ أَذْهَبَ اللَّهُ عَزَّ وَ جَلَّ الشَّيْطَانَ عَنْ إِنَارَةِ قَلْبِهِ مِائَةَ يَوْمٍ وَ مَنْ أَكَلَ ثَلَاثاً حَتَّى يَسْتَوْفِيَهَا أَذْهَبَ اللَّهُ عَزَّ وَ جَلَّ الشَّيْطَانَ عَنْ إِنَارَةِ قَلْبِهِ سَنَةً وَ مَنْ أَذْهَبَ اللَّهُ الشَّيْطَانَ عَنْ إِنَارَةِ قَلْبِهِ سَنَةً لَمْ يُذْنِبْ وَ مَنْ لَمْ يُذْنِبْ دَخَلَ الْجَنَّةَ .

text: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Abdullah Bin Sinan who said, ‘I heard Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> saying: ‘It is upon you with (eating) the sweet Pomegranate for there is none from a seed which falls in a stomach of a Believer except that it annihilates an illness and extinguishes the whispering of the Satan<sup>la</sup> from him’.

citation.arabic_text: سَمِعْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) يَقُولُ عَلَيْكُمْ بِالرُّمَّانِ الْحُلْوِ فَكُلُوهُ فَإِنَّهُ لَيْسَتْ مِنْ حَبَّةٍ تَقَعُ فِي مَعِدَةِ مُؤْمِنٍ إِلَّا أَبَادَتْ دَاءً وَ أَطْفَأَتْ شَيْطَانَ الْوَسْوَسَةِ عَنْهُ .
citation.translation: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Abdullah Bin Sinan who said, ‘I heard Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> saying: ‘It is upon you with (eating) the sweet Pomegranate for there is none from a seed which falls in a stomach of a Believer except that it annihilates an illness and extinguishes the whispering of the Satan<sup>la</sup> from him’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: صحيح - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (22/193)

text: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hisham Bin Salim, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said, ‘I heard him<sup>asws</sup> saying: ‘The one who eats a Pomegranate upon the empty stomach, illuminates his heart for forty days’.

citation.arabic_text: سَمِعْتُهُ يَقُولُ مَنْ أَكَلَ رُمَّانَةً عَلَى الرِّيقِ أَنَارَتْ قَلْبَهُ أَرْبَعِينَ يَوْماً .
citation.translation: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hisham Bin Salim, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said, ‘I heard him<sup>asws</sup> saying: ‘The one who eats a Pomegranate upon the empty stomach, illuminates his heart for forty days’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: حسن - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (2/193)

text: Ali Bin Muhammad Bin Bundar, from his father, from Muhammad Bin Ali Al Hamdany, from Abu Saeed Al Raqqan, from Salih Bin Uqba who said, ‘I heard Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> saying: ‘Eat the Pomegranate with its dividing lining, for it repairs the stomach and increased in the intellect’.

citation.arabic_text: سَمِعْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) يَقُولُ كُلُوا الرُّمَّانَ بِشَحْمِهِ فَإِنَّهُ يَدْبُغُ الْمَعِدَةَ وَ يَزِيدُ فِي الذِّهْنِ .
citation.translation: Ali Bin Muhammad Bin Bundar, from his father, from Muhammad Bin Ali Al Hamdany, from Abu Saeed Al Raqqan, from Salih Bin Uqba who said, ‘I heard Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> saying: ‘Eat the Pomegranate with its dividing lining, for it repairs the stomach and increased in the intellect’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: ضعيف - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (2/193)

text: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Ja’far Bin Muhammad Al Ashary, from Ibn Al Qaddah, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws having said: ‘Eat the Al-Muzz Promegranate with its dividing lining, for it repairs the stomach’.

citation.arabic_text: كُلُوا الرُّمَّانَ الْمُزَّ بِشَحْمِهِ فَإِنَّهُ دِبَاغٌ لِلْمَعِدَةِ .
citation.translation: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Ja’far Bin Muhammad Al Ashary, from Ibn Al Qaddah, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws having said: ‘Eat the Al-Muzz Promegranate with its dividing lining, for it repairs the stomach’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: ضعيف - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (22/193)

text: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Ibrahim Bin Abdul Hameed, from Al Waleed Bin Sabeeh, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws, said, ‘The sweet Pomegranate was mentioned, so heasws said: ‘Al-Muzz (a type of Pomegranate) is corrective in the belly’.

citation.arabic_text: ذُكِرَ الرُّمَّانُ الْحُلْوُ فَقَالَ الْمُزُّ أَصْلَحُ فِي الْبَطْنِ .
citation.translation: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Ibrahim Bin Abdul Hameed, from Al Waleed Bin Sabeeh, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws, said, ‘The sweet Pomegranate was mentioned, so heasws said: ‘Al-Muzz (a type of Pomegranate) is corrective in the belly’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: حسن أو موثق - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (2/193)

text: Muhammad Bin Ismail, from Al Fazl Bin Shazaan, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Ibrahim Bin Abdul Hameed, from Al Waleed Bin Sabeeh, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws – similar to it. A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Khalid, from Ibn Baqqah, from Salih Bin Uqba Al Khayyat, or Al Qammat, from Yazeed Bin Abdul Malik who said, ‘I heard Abu Abdullahasws saying: ‘The one who eats a Pomegranate illuminates his heart, and the one whose heart Allahazwj Illuminates, the Satanla would be remote from him’. I said, ‘Which Pomegranate, may I be sacrificed for youasws?’ So heasws said: ‘Your Sowraniyya, this one’.

citation.arabic_text: . عِدَّةٌ مِنْ أَصْحَابِنَا عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ خَالِدٍ عَنِ ابْنِ بَقَّاحٍ عَنْ صَالِحِ بْنِ عُقْبَةَ الْخَيَّاطِ أَوِ الْقَمَّاطِ عَنْ يَزِيدَ بْنِ عَبْدِ الْمَلِكِ قَالَ سَمِعْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) يَقُولُ مَنْ أَكَلَ رُمَّانَةً أَنَارَتْ قَلْبَهُ وَ مَنْ أَنَارَ اللَّهُ قَلْبَهُ بَعُدَ الشَّيْطَانُ عَنْهُ قُلْتُ أَيَّ الرُّمَّانِ جُعِلْتُ فِدَاكَ فَقَالَ سُورَانِيَّكُمْ هَذَا .
citation.translation: Muhammad Bin Ismail, from Al Fazl Bin Shazaan, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Ibrahim Bin Abdul Hameed, from Al Waleed Bin Sabeeh, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws – similar to it. A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Khalid, from Ibn Baqqah, from Salih Bin Uqba Al Khayyat, or Al Qammat, from Yazeed Bin Abdul Malik who said, ‘I heard Abu Abdullahasws saying: ‘The one who eats a Pomegranate illuminates his heart, and the one whose heart Allahazwj Illuminates, the Satanla would be remote from him’. I said, ‘Which Pomegranate, may I be sacrificed for youasws?’ So heasws said: ‘Your Sowraniyya, this one’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: ضعيف - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (22/193)

text: From him, from Al Naheyki, from Ubeydullah Bin Ahmad, from Ziyad Bin Marwan Al Qindy who said, ‘I heard Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup>, meaning the 1<sup>st</sup>. saying: ‘The one who eats a Pomegranate on the day of Friday upon the empty stomach, would enlighten his heart for forty mornings; and if he were to eat two Pomegranates so it would be for eighty days; and so if he were to eat three, so one hundred and twenty days; and the whisperings of the Satan<sup>la</sup> would be dispelled from him, and the one from whom the whisperings of the Satan<sup>la</sup> are dispelled would not disobey Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic, and the one who does not disobey Allah<sup>asws</sup>, Allah<sup>azwj</sup> would Enter him into the Paradise’.

citation.arabic_text: سَمِعْتُ أَبَا الْحَسَنِ ( عليه السلام ) يَعْنِي الْأَوَّلَ يَقُولُ مَنْ أَكَلَ رُمَّانَةً يَوْمَ الْجُمُعَةِ عَلَى الرِّيقِ نَوَّرَتْ قَلْبَهُ أَرْبَعِينَ صَبَاحاً فَإِنْ أَكَلَ رُمَّانَتَيْنِ فَثَمَانِينَ يَوْماً فَإِنْ أَكَلَ ثَلَاثاً فَمِائَةً وَ عِشْرِينَ يَوْماً وَ طُرِدَتْ عَنْهُ وَسْوَسَةُ الشَّيْطَانِ وَ مَنْ طُرِدَتْ عَنْهُ وَسْوَسَةُ الشَّيْطَانِ لَمْ يَعْصِ اللَّهَ عَزَّ وَ جَلَّ وَ مَنْ لَمْ يَعْصِ اللَّهَ أَدْخَلَهُ اللَّهُ الْجَنَّةَ .
citation.translation: From him, from Al Naheyki, from Ubeydullah Bin Ahmad, from Ziyad Bin Marwan Al Qindy who said, ‘I heard Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup>, meaning the 1<sup>st</sup>. saying: ‘The one who eats a Pomegranate on the day of Friday upon the empty stomach, would enlighten his heart for forty mornings; and if he were to eat two Pomegranates so it would be for eighty days; and so if he were to eat three, so one hundred and twenty days; and the whisperings of the Satan<sup>la</sup> would be dispelled from him, and the one from whom the whisperings of the Satan<sup>la</sup> are dispelled would not disobey Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic, and the one who does not disobey Allah<sup>asws</sup>, Allah<sup>azwj</sup> would Enter him into the Paradise’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: موثق - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (22/194)

text: From him, from Al Husayn Bin Saeed, from Amro Bin Ibrahim, from Al Khurasany who said, ‘Eating the sweet Pomegranate increases in the water of the man, and improves the childbirths’. (P.s. – This is not a Hadeeth)’.

citation.arabic_text: أَكْلُ الرُّمَّانِ الْحُلْوِ يَزِيدُ فِي مَاءِ الرَّجُلِ وَ يُحَسِّنُ الْوَلَدَ.
citation.translation: From him, from Al Husayn Bin Saeed, from Amro Bin Ibrahim, from Al Khurasany who said, ‘Eating the sweet Pomegranate increases in the water of the man, and improves the childbirths’. (P.s. – This is not a Hadeeth)’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: صحيح على الظاهر - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (22/194)

text: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Ibrahim Bin Abul Rahman, from Ziyad, (It has been narrated) from Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Smoke of the Pomegranate negates the vermin’.

citation.arabic_text: دُخَانُ شَجَرِ الرُّمَّانِ يَنْفِي الْهَوَامَّ .
citation.translation: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Ibrahim Bin Abul Rahman, from Ziyad, (It has been narrated) from Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Smoke of the Pomegranate negates the vermin’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: ضعيف على المشهور - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (22/194)

text: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Muhammad Bin Sinan, from Ismail Bin Jabir who said, ‘I heard Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> saying: ‘The apple radiates the stomach’.

citation.arabic_text: سَمِعْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) يَقُولُ التُّفَّاحُ نَضُوحُ الْمَعِدَةِ .
citation.translation: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Muhammad Bin Sinan, from Ismail Bin Jabir who said, ‘I heard Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> saying: ‘The apple radiates the stomach’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: ضعيف على المشهور - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (22/195)

text: Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Bakr Bin Salih, from Al Ja’fary who said, ‘Abu Al-Hassan Musa<sup>asws</sup> saying: ‘The apple benefits from the effects from a number of toxins, and the sorcery, and the small faults presented from the people of the earth, and the overwhelming phlegm, and there is nothing quicker than it in benefitting’.

citation.arabic_text: سَمِعْتُ أَبَا الْحَسَنِ مُوسَى ( عليه السلام ) يَقُولُ التُّفَّاحُ يَنْفَعُ مِنْ خِصَالٍ عِدَّةٍ مِنَ السَّمِّ وَ السِّحْرِ وَ اللَّمَمِ يَعْرِضُ مِنْ أَهْلِ الْأَرْضِ وَ الْبَلْغَمِ الْغَالِبِ وَ لَيْسَ شَيْ‏ءٌ أَسْرَعَ مِنْهُ مَنْفَعَةً .
citation.translation: Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Bakr Bin Salih, from Al Ja’fary who said, ‘Abu Al-Hassan Musa<sup>asws</sup> saying: ‘The apple benefits from the effects from a number of toxins, and the sorcery, and the small faults presented from the people of the earth, and the overwhelming phlegm, and there is nothing quicker than it in benefitting’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: ضعيف - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (22/195)

text: Ali Bin Muhammad Bin Bundar, from his father, from Muhammad Bin Ali Al Hamdany, from Abdullah Bin Sinna, from Dorost Bin Abu Mansour who said, ‘Al-Mufazzal Bin Umar sent me to Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> as a courtesy. So I went over to him<sup>asws</sup> on a scorching hot day, and facing him<sup>asws</sup> was a tray in which there were green apples, so by Allah<sup>azwj</sup> I could not be patient and I said to him<sup>asws</sup>, ‘May I be sacrificed for you<sup>asws</sup>! You<sup>asws</sup> are eating from this and the people are abhorring it?’ So he<sup>asws</sup> said to me as if he<sup>asws</sup> had not ceased to recognise me: ‘I<sup>asws</sup> woke up in this night of mine<sup>asws</sup>, so I<sup>asws</sup> sent for it and they came with it, So I<sup>asws</sup> ate it and it takes off the fever and settles the temperature’. So I proceeded (home) and I found my family with fever, so I fed them (apples), and the fever was lifted from them’.

citation.arabic_text: بَعَثَنِي الْمُفَضَّلُ بْنُ عُمَرَ إِلَى أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) بِلَطَفٍ فَدَخَلْتُ عَلَيْهِ فِي يَوْمٍ صَائِفٍ وَ قُدَّامَهُ طَبَقٌ فِيهِ تُفَّاحٌ أَخْضَرُ فَوَ اللَّهِ إِنْ صَبَرْتُ أَنْ قُلْتُ لَهُ جُعِلْتُ فِدَاكَ أَ تَأْكُلُ مِنْ هَذَا وَ النَّاسُ يَكْرَهُونَهُ فَقَالَ لِي كَأَنَّهُ لَمْ يَزَلْ يَعْرِفُنِي وُعِكْتُ فِي لَيْلَتِي هَذِهِ فَبَعَثْتُ فَأُتِيتُ بِهِ فَأَكَلْتُهُ وَ هُوَ يَقْلَعُ الْحُمَّى وَ يُسَكِّنُ الْحَرَارَةَ فَقَدِمْتُ فَأَصَبْتُ أَهْلِي مَحْمُومِينَ فَأَطْعَمْتُهُمْ فَأَقْلَعَتِ الْحُمَّى عَنْهُمْ .
citation.translation: Ali Bin Muhammad Bin Bundar, from his father, from Muhammad Bin Ali Al Hamdany, from Abdullah Bin Sinna, from Dorost Bin Abu Mansour who said, ‘Al-Mufazzal Bin Umar sent me to Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> as a courtesy. So I went over to him<sup>asws</sup> on a scorching hot day, and facing him<sup>asws</sup> was a tray in which there were green apples, so by Allah<sup>azwj</sup> I could not be patient and I said to him<sup>asws</sup>, ‘May I be sacrificed for you<sup>asws</sup>! So I proceeded (home) and I found my family with fever, so I fed them (apples), and the fever was lifted from them’.

text: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Yaqoub Bin Yazeed, from Ziyad Al Qindy who said, ‘I entered Al-Medina and with me was my brother Sayf and the people had been struck with nose-bleed, and it was so that when the man had nose-bleed for two days, he died. So I returned to the house and Sayf had nose-bleed with intense bleeding. So I went over to Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, so he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘O Ziyad! Feed Sayf the apple’. So I fed it to him, so he was cured’.

citation.arabic_text: دَخَلْتُ الْمَدِينَةَ وَ مَعِي أَخِي سَيْفٌ فَأَصَابَ النَّاسُ بِرُعَافٍ فَكَانَ الرَّجُلُ إِذَا رَعَفَ يَوْمَيْنِ مَاتَ فَرَجَعْتُ إِلَى الْمَنْزِلِ فَإِذَا سَيْفٌ يَرْعُفُ رُعَافاً شَدِيداً فَدَخَلْتُ عَلَى أَبِي الْحَسَنِ ( عليه السلام ) فَقَالَ يَا زِيَادُ أَطْعِمْ سَيْفاً التُّفَّاحَ فَأَطْعَمْتُهُ إِيَّاهُ فَبَرَأَ .
citation.translation: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Yaqoub Bin Yazeed, from Ziyad Al Qindy who said, ‘I entered Al-Medina and with me was my brother Sayf and the people had been struck with nose-bleed, and it was so that when the man had nose-bleed for two days, he died. So I returned to the house and Sayf had nose-bleed with intense bleeding. So I went over to Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, so he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘O Ziyad! Feed Sayf the apple’. So I fed it to him, so he was cured’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: ضعيف على المشهور - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (22/196)

text: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Al Hakam, from Ziyad Bin Marwan who said, ‘The people were struck with plague at Makkah, so I wrote to Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup>. So he<sup>asws</sup> wrote to me: ‘Eat the apple’.

citation.arabic_text: أَصَابَ النَّاسَ وَبَاءٌ بِمَكَّةَ فَكَتَبْتُ إِلَى أَبِي الْحَسَنِ ( عليه السلام ) فَكَتَبَ إِلَيَّ كُلِ التُّفَّاحَ .
citation.translation: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Al Hakam, from Ziyad Bin Marwan who said, ‘The people were struck with plague at Makkah, so I wrote to Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup>. So he<sup>asws</sup> wrote to me: ‘Eat the apple’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: موثق - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (2/196)

text: Abu Ali Al Ashary, from Muhammad Bin Abdul Jabbar, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ibn Bukeyr who said, ‘I had nose-bleed for a year at Al-Medina. So our companions asked Abu Abdullahasws about something which could stop the nose-bleed, so heasws said to them: ‘Make him drink Suweyq of the apples’. So they made me drink it, and the nose-bleed cut-off from me’.

citation.arabic_text: رَعَفْتُ سَنَةً بِالْمَدِينَةِ فَسَأَلَ أَصْحَابُنَا أَبَا عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) عَنْ شَيْ‏ءٍ يُمْسِكُ الرُّعَافَ فَقَالَ لَهُمُ اسْقُوهُ سَوِيقَ التُّفَّاحِ فَسَقَوْنِي فَانْقَطَعَ عَنِّي الرُّعَافُ .
citation.translation: Abu Ali Al Ashary, from Muhammad Bin Abdul Jabbar, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ibn Bukeyr who said, ‘I had nose-bleed for a year at Al-Medina. So our companions asked Abu Abdullahasws about something which could stop the nose-bleed, so heasws said to them: ‘Make him drink Suweyq of the apples’. So they made me drink it, and the nose-bleed cut-off from me’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: موثق كالصحيح - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (2/196)

text: Muhammad Bin yahya, from Muhammad Bin Musa, from one of our companions, (It has been narrated) raising it to Abu Abdullahasws having said: ‘Iasws do not know for the toxins, any cure more beneficial that a Suweyq of the apples’.

citation.arabic_text: مَا أَعْرِفُ لِلسُّمُومِ دَوَاءً أَنْفَعَ مِنْ سَوِيقِ التُّفَّاحِ .
citation.translation: Muhammad Bin yahya, from Muhammad Bin Musa, from one of our companions, (It has been narrated) raising it to Abu Abdullahasws having said: ‘Iasws do not know for the toxins, any cure more beneficial that a Suweyq of the apples’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: مرفوع - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (2/196)

text: From him, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Al Husayn Bin Saeed, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Yazeed who said, ‘Whenever if a person from the household is stung by a snake or a scorpion, heasws said: ‘Make him drink Suweyq of the apples’.

citation.arabic_text: كَانَ إِذَا لَسَعَ إِنْسَاناً مِنْ أَهْلِ الدَّارِ حَيَّةٌ أَوْ عَقْرَبٌ قَالَ اسْقُوهُ سَوِيقَ التُّفَّاحِ .
citation.translation: From him, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Al Husayn Bin Saeed, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Yazeed who said, ‘Whenever if a person from the household is stung by a snake or a scorpion, heasws said: ‘Make him drink Suweyq of the apples’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: مجهول - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (22/196)

text: A number of our companioins, from Ahmad Bin Abu Abdullah, from Yaqoub Bin Yazeed, from Al Qindy, from Al Mufazzal Bin Umar, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, said, ‘The fever was mentioned to him<sup>asws</sup>, so he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘We<sup>asws</sup> the People<sup>asws</sup> of the Household do not cure it except by the pouring of the cold water upon us (for cooling the external heat) and eating the apple (for cooling the internal heat)’.

citation.arabic_text: ذُكِرَ لَهُ الْحُمَّى فَقَالَ ( عليه السلام ) إِنَّا أَهْلُ بَيْتٍ لَا نَتَدَاوَى إِلَّا بِإِفَاضَةِ الْمَاءِ الْبَارِدِ يُصَبُّ عَلَيْنَا وَ أَكْلِ التُّفَّاحِ.
citation.translation: A number of our companioins, from Ahmad Bin Abu Abdullah, from Yaqoub Bin Yazeed, from Al Qindy, from Al Mufazzal Bin Umar, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, said, ‘The fever was mentioned to him<sup>asws</sup>, so he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘We<sup>asws</sup> the People<sup>asws</sup> of the Household do not cure it except by the pouring of the cold water upon us (for cooling the external heat) and eating the apple (for cooling the internal heat)’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: مختلف فيه - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (22/197)

text: From him, from his father, from Yunus, from the one who mentioned it, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘If the people knew what was in the apple, they would not cure their sick ones except by it’. He (the narrator) said, ‘And some of them have reported from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Feed the apple to your feverish ones, for there is none from the things more beneficial than the apple’.

citation.arabic_text: لَوْ يَعْلَمُ النَّاسُ مَا فِي التُّفَّاحِ مَا دَاوَوْا مَرْضَاهُمْ إِلَّا بِهِ. قَالَ وَ رَوَى بَعْضُهُمْ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) قَالَ أَطْعِمُوا مَحْمُومِيكُمُ التُّفَّاحَ فَمَا مِنْ شَيْ‏ءٍ أَنْفَعَ مِنَ التُّفَّاحِ .
citation.translation: From him, from his father, from Yunus, from the one who mentioned it, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘If the people knew what was in the apple, they would not cure their sick ones except by it’. He (the narrator) said, ‘And some of them have reported from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Feed the apple to your feverish ones, for there is none from the things more beneficial than the apple’.

text: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Muhammad Bin Al Hassan Bin Shamoun, from Abdullah Bin Abdul Rahman, from Misma’a Bin Abdul Malik, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Eat the apple for it repairs the stomach’.

citation.arabic_text: إِنَّ أَمِيرَ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ ( عليه السلام ) قَالَ كُلُوا التُّفَّاحَ فَإِنَّهُ يَدْبُغُ الْمَعِدَةَ .
citation.translation: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Muhammad Bin Al Hassan Bin Shamoun, from Abdullah Bin Abdul Rahman, from Misma’a Bin Abdul Malik, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Eat the apple for it repairs the stomach’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: ضعيف على المشهور - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (22/197)

text: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Al Qasim Bin Yahya, from his grandfather Al Hassan Bin Rashid, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Eating the Quince is strengthening for the weak heart and aromatises the stomach, and purifies the heart, and emboldens the timid’.

citation.arabic_text: قَالَ أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ ( عليه السلام ) أَكْلُ السَّفَرْجَلِ قُوَّةٌ لِلْقَلْبِ الضَّعِيفِ وَ يُطَيِّبُ الْمَعِدَةَ وَ يُذَكِّي الْفُؤَادَ وَ يُشَجِّعُ الْجَبَانَ .
citation.translation: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Al Qasim Bin Yahya, from his grandfather Al Hassan Bin Rashid, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Eating the Quince is strengthening for the weak heart and aromatises the stomach, and purifies the heart, and emboldens the timid’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: ضعيف - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (2/197)

text: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Al Nowfaly, from Al Sakuny, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> Bin Abu Talib<sup>as</sup> was in the presence of the Prophet<sup>saww</sup> and he<sup>as</sup> gifted a Quince to the Prophet<sup>saww</sup>. So the Prophet<sup>saww</sup> cut off a piece from it and gave it to Ja’far<sup>as</sup>, but he<sup>as</sup> refused to eat it (out of respect). So he<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘Take it, and eat it, for it purifies the heart, and emboldens the timid’. And in another report: ‘(He<sup>saww</sup> said): ‘Eat, for it clears the colour and improves the child birth’.

citation.arabic_text: كَانَ جَعْفَرُ بْنُ أَبِي طَالِبٍ عِنْدَ النَّبِيِّ ( صلى الله عليه وآله ) فَأُهْدِيَ إِلَى النَّبِيِّ ( صلى الله عليه وآله ) سَفَرْجَلٌ فَقَطَعَ مِنْهُ النَّبِيُّ ( صلى الله عليه وآله ) قِطْعَةً وَ نَاوَلَهَا جَعْفَراً فَأَبَى أَنْ يَأْكُلَهَا فَقَالَ خُذْهَا وَ كُلْهَا فَإِنَّهَا تُذَكِّي الْقَلْبَ وَ تُشَجِّعُ الْجَبَانَ وَ فِي رِوَايَةٍ أُخْرَى كُلْ فَإِنَّهُ يُصَفِّي اللَّوْنَ وَ يُحَسِّنُ الْوَلَدَ .
citation.translation: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Al Nowfaly, from Al Sakuny, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> Bin Abu Talib<sup>as</sup> was in the presence of the Prophet<sup>saww</sup> and he<sup>as</sup> gifted a Quince to the Prophet<sup>saww</sup>. So the Prophet<sup>saww</sup> cut off a piece from it and gave it to Ja’far<sup>as</sup>, but he<sup>as</sup> refused to eat it (out of respect). So he<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘Take it, and eat it, for it purifies the heart, and emboldens the timid’. And in another report: ‘(He<sup>saww</sup> said): ‘Eat, for it clears the colour and improves the child birth’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: ضعيف على المشهور - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (2/197)

text: Al Husayn Bin Muhammad, from Moala Bin Muhammad, raising it, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘The one who eats a Quince upon the empty stomach would make good his water and improve the child birth’.

citation.arabic_text: مَنْ أَكَلَ سَفَرْجَلَةً عَلَى الرِّيقِ طَابَ مَاؤُهُ وَ حَسُنَ وَلَدُهُ .
citation.translation: Al Husayn Bin Muhammad, from Moala Bin Muhammad, raising it, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘The one who eats a Quince upon the empty stomach would make good his water and improve the child birth’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: ضعيف على المشهور - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (2/198)

text: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Muhammad Bin Ismail Bin Baie, from his uncle Hamza Bin Bazie, (It has been narrated) from Abu Ibrahim<sup>as</sup> (7th Imam<sup>asws</sup>) having said: ‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said to Ja’far<sup>as</sup>: ‘Eat the Quince, for it strengthens the heart and emboldens the timid’.

citation.arabic_text: قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ ( صلى الله عليه وآله ) لِجَعْفَرٍ يَا جَعْفَرُ كُلِ السَّفَرْجَلَ فَإِنَّهُ يُقَوِّي الْقَلْبَ وَ يُشَجِّعُ الْجَبَانَ .
citation.translation: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Muhammad Bin Ismail Bin Baie, from his uncle Hamza Bin Bazie, (It has been narrated) from Abu Ibrahim<sup>as</sup> (7th Imam<sup>asws</sup>) having said: ‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said to Ja’far<sup>as</sup>: ‘Eat the Quince, for it strengthens the heart and emboldens the timid’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: صحيح على الظاهر - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (22/198)

text: Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Al Hassan Bin Ali, from Jameel Bin Darraj, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘The one who eats a Quince Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic would Make his tongue speak wisdom for forty mornings’.

citation.arabic_text: مَنْ أَكَلَ سَفَرْجَلَةً أَنْطَقَ اللَّهُ عَزَّ وَ جَلَّ الْحِكْمَةَ عَلَى لِسَانِهِ أَرْبَعِينَ صَبَاحاً .
citation.translation: Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Al Hassan Bin Ali, from Jameel Bin Darraj, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘The one who eats a Quince Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic would Make his tongue speak wisdom for forty mornings’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: موثق كالصحيح - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (2/198)

text: Muhammad Bin Abdullah Bin Ja’far, from his father, from Ali Bin Suleyman Bin Rusheyd, from Marwak Bin Ubeyd, from the one who mentioned it, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic did not Send a Prophet<sup>saww</sup> except that his<sup>as</sup> fragrance was that of a Quince’.

citation.arabic_text: مَا بَعَثَ اللَّهُ عَزَّ وَ جَلَّ نَبِيّاً إِلَّا وَ مَعَهُ رَائِحَةُ السَّفَرْجَلِ .
citation.translation: Muhammad Bin Abdullah Bin Ja’far, from his father, from Ali Bin Suleyman Bin Rusheyd, from Marwak Bin Ubeyd, from the one who mentioned it, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic did not Send a Prophet<sup>saww</sup> except that his<sup>as</sup> fragrance was that of a Quince’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: مجهول - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (2/198)

text: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Abu Abdullah, from a number of his companions, from Ali Bin Asbaat, from Abu Muhammad Al Jowhary, from Sufyan Bin Uyayna who said, ‘I heard Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> Bin Muhammad<sup>asws</sup> saying: ‘The Quince removes the distress of the grief just as the hand removes the sweat from the forehead’.

citation.arabic_text: سَمِعْتُ جَعْفَرَ بْنَ مُحَمَّدٍ ( عليه السلام ) يَقُولُ السَّفَرْجَلُ يَذْهَبُ بِهَمِّ الْحَزِينِ كَمَا تَذْهَبُ الْيَدُ بِعَرَقِ الْجَبِينِ .
citation.translation: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Abu Abdullah, from a number of his companions, from Ali Bin Asbaat, from Abu Muhammad Al Jowhary, from Sufyan Bin Uyayna who said, ‘I heard Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> Bin Muhammad<sup>asws</sup> saying: ‘The Quince removes the distress of the grief just as the hand removes the sweat from the forehead’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: مجهول - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (22/198)

text: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Abu Nasr, (It has been narrated) from Abu Al-Hassan Al-Reza<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘The Fig removes the bad breath, and strengthens the gums and the bones, and builds the hair, and eliminates the illnesses and with it you would not be in need for a medicine’. And he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The Fig is something with the vegetation of the Paradise’.

citation.arabic_text: التِّينُ يَذْهَبُ بِالْبَخَرِ وَ يَشُدُّ الْفَمَ وَ الْعَظْمَ وَ يُنْبِتُ الشَّعْرَ وَ يَذْهَبُ بِالدَّاءِ وَ لَا يُحْتَاجُ مَعَهُ إِلَى دَوَاءٍ وَ قَالَ ( عليه السلام ) التِّينُ أَشْبَهُ شَيْ‏ءٍ بِنَبَاتِ الْجَنَّةِ.
citation.translation: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Abu Nasr, (It has been narrated) from Abu Al-Hassan Al-Reza<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘The Fig removes the bad breath, and strengthens the gums and the bones, and builds the hair, and eliminates the illnesses and with it you would not be in need for a medicine’. And he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The Fig is something with the vegetation of the Paradise’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: حسن وآخره ضعيف على المشهور - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (2/199)

text: And Sahl Bin Ziyad reported from Ahmad Bin Al Ash’as, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Abu Nasr as well – similar to it.

citation.translation: And Sahl Bin Ziyad reported from Ahmad Bin Al Ash’as, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Abu Nasr as well – similar to it.

text: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Al Qasim Bin yahya, from his grandfather Al Hassan Bin Rashid, from Abu Baseer, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Eat the pears for it galvanises the heart and settles the interior pains by the Permission of Allah<sup>azwj</sup> the High’.

citation.arabic_text: كُلُوا الْكُمَّثْرَى فَإِنَّهُ يَجْلُو الْقَلْبَ وَ يُسَكِّنُ أَوْجَاعَ الْجَوْفِ بِإِذْنِ اللَّهِ تَعَالَى .
citation.translation: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Al Qasim Bin yahya, from his grandfather Al Hassan Bin Rashid, from Abu Baseer, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Eat the pears for it galvanises the heart and settles the interior pains by the Permission of Allah<sup>azwj</sup> the High’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: ضعيف - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (22/199)

text: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Abdullah Bin Ja’far, from Muhammad Bin Isa, from Al Washa, from one of our companions, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘The pears repair the stomach and strengthens it, it and the Quince are the same, and it is more beneficial upon the full stomach than upon the empty, and the one who is hit by overwhelming stress so let him eat it, meaning upon the food’.

citation.arabic_text: الْكُمَّثْرَى يَدْبُغُ الْمَعِدَةَ وَ يُقَوِّيهَا هُوَ وَ السَّفَرْجَلُ سَوَاءٌ وَ هُوَ عَلَى الشِّبَعِ أَنْفَعُ مِنْهُ عَلَى الرِّيقِ وَ مَنْ أَصَابَهُ طَخَاءٌ فَلْيَأْكُلْهُ يَعْنِي عَلَى الطَّعَامِ .
citation.translation: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Abdullah Bin Ja’far, from Muhammad Bin Isa, from Al Washa, from one of our companions, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘The pears repair the stomach and strengthens it, it and the Quince are the same, and it is more beneficial upon the full stomach than upon the empty, and the one who is hit by overwhelming stress so let him eat it, meaning upon the food’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: مرسل - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (22/199)

text: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Abdullah Bin Ja’far, from yaqoub Bin Yazeed, from Ziyad who said, ‘I went over to Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> the 1st and in front of him<sup>asws</sup> was a bowl of water in which were black plums during its season. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘There was a fever with me and the soft plums extinguish the heat, and settle the paleness, and the dried from it settles the blood and takes away the illness of the rumbling’.

citation.arabic_text: دَخَلْتُ عَلَى أَبِي الْحَسَنِ الْأَوَّلِ ( عليه السلام ) وَ بَيْنَ يَدَيْهِ تَوْرُ مَاءٍ فِيهِ إِجَّاصٌ أَسْوَدُ فِي إِبَّانِهِ فَقَالَ إِنَّهُ هَاجَتْ بِي حَرَارَةٌ وَ إِنَّ الْإِجَّاصَ الطَّرِيَّ يُطْفِئُ الْحَرَارَةَ وَ يُسَكِّنُ الصَّفْرَاءَ وَ إِنَّ الْيَابِسَ مِنْهُ يُسَكِّنُ الدَّمَ وَ يَسُلُّ الدَّاءَ الدَّوِيَّ .
citation.translation: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Abdullah Bin Ja’far, from yaqoub Bin Yazeed, from Ziyad who said, ‘I went over to Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> the 1st and in front of him<sup>asws</sup> was a bowl of water in which were black plums during its season. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘There was a fever with me and the soft plums extinguish the heat, and settle the paleness, and the dried from it settles the blood and takes away the illness of the rumbling’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: موثق - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (2/200)

text: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Bakr Bin Salih, from Abdullah Bin Ibrahim Al Ja’fary, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘What are your physicians instructing you with regarding the Citron?’ So I said, ‘They are instructing us that we eat it before the meal’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘I<sup>asws</sup> am ordering you all with it after the meal’.

citation.arabic_text: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَحْيَى عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنْ بَكْرِ بْنِ صَالِحٍ عَنْ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ بْنِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ الْجَعْفَرِيِّ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) قَالَ بِأَيِّ شَيْ‏ءٍ يَأْمُرُكُمْ أَطِبَّاؤُكُمْ فِي الْأُتْرُجِّ فَقُلْتُ يَأْمُرُونَنَا أَنْ نَأْكُلَهُ قَبْلَ الطَّعَامِ فَقَالَ إِنِّي آمُرُكُمْ بِهِ بَعْدَ الطَّعَامِ .
citation.translation: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Bakr Bin Salih, from Abdullah Bin Ibrahim Al Ja’fary, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘What are your physicians instructing you with regarding the Citron?’ So I said, ‘They are instructing us that we eat it before the meal’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘I<sup>asws</sup> am ordering you all with it after the meal’.

text: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Khalid, from Al Qasim, from Al Qasim Bin Yahya, from his grandfather Al Hassan Bin Rashid, from Abu Baseer, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Eat the Citron after the meal, for the Progeny<sup>asws</sup> of Muhammad<sup>saww</sup> are doing that’.

text: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Al Hakam and Al Washa altogether from Ali Bin Abu Hamza, from Abu Baseer who said, ‘I had a guest with me, so he desired to eat the Citron with honey, so I fed it to him, and I ate with him. Then I went to Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> and there was a meal on the table in front of him<sup>asws</sup>. So he<sup>asws</sup> said to me: ‘Approach, and eat’. So I said, ‘I have eaten before coming to you<sup>asws</sup>, Citron with honey, and I still find its heaviness as I ate a lot from it’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘O slave, go to the maid and say to her to send to us the dry pieces of bread from the ones she dries in the oven’. So he came with it, and he<sup>asws</sup> said to me: ‘Eat this dry bread for it would digest the Citron’. So I ate it. Then I arose, and it was as if I had not eaten anything’.

text: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Ahmad Bin Haroun, from Mowfaq Al Madainy, from his father, from his grandfather who said, ‘Al-Maazy<sup>asws</sup> (7th Imam<sup>asws</sup>) sent for me one day, so he<sup>asws</sup> made me sit for the lunch. So when they came with the meal, there were no vegetables upon it. So he<sup>asws</sup> restrained his<sup>asws</sup> hand, then said to the slave: ‘Do you no know that I<sup>asws</sup> do not eat upon a food-spread in which there is no greenery? So bring me the greens’. So the slave went and came with the vegetables and placed it upon the food-spread. So he<sup>asws</sup> extended his<sup>asws</sup> hand at that time and ate’.

citation.arabic_text: بَعَثَ إِلَيَّ الْمَاضِي ( عليه السلام ) يَوْماً فَأَجْلَسَنِي لِلْغَدَاءِ فَلَمَّا جَاءُوا بِالْمَائِدَةِ لَمْ يَكُنْ عَلَيْهَا بَقْلٌ فَأَمْسَكَ يَدَهُ ثُمَّ قَالَ لِلْغُلَامِ أَ مَا عَلِمْتَ أَنِّي لَا آكُلُ عَلَى مَائِدَةٍ لَيْسَ فِيهَا خُضْرَةٌ فَأْتِنِي بِالْخُضْرَةِ قَالَ فَذَهَبَ الْغُلَامُ فَجَاءَ بِالْبَقْلِ فَأَلْقَاهُ عَلَى الْمَائِدَةِ فَمَدَّ يَدَهُ ( عليه السلام ) حِينَئِذٍ وَ أَكَلَ .

text: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Hannan who said, ‘I was with Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> upon the food-spread, so he<sup>asws</sup> inclined upon the vegetables and I abstained from it due to an illness which was with me. So he<sup>asws</sup> turned towards me and said, ‘O Hanaan! Do you not know that Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> was never brought a platter except that upon it were vegetables?’ I said, ‘And why, may I be sacrificed for you<sup>asws</sup>?’ So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Because the hearts of the Believers are green, and it yearns for its forms’.

citation.arabic_text: كُنْتُ مَعَ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) عَلَى الْمَائِدَةِ فَمَالَ عَلَى الْبَقْلِ وَ امْتَنَعْتُ أَنَا مِنْهُ لِعِلَّةٍ كَانَتْ بِي فَالْتَفَتَ إِلَيَّ فَقَالَ يَا حَنَانُ أَ مَا عَلِمْتَ أَنَّ أَمِيرَ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ ( عليه السلام ) لَمْ يُؤْتَ بِطَبَقٍ إِلَّا وَ عَلَيْهِ بَقْلٌ قُلْتُ وَ لِمَ جُعِلْتُ فِدَاكَ فَقَالَ لِأَنَّ قُلُوبَ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ خَضِرَةٌ وَ هِيَ تَحِنُّ إِلَى أَشْكَالِهَا .

text: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Al Nowfaly, from Al Sakuny, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘The one who loves that his water and his children be abundant, so let him frequent in eating the endive’.

text: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Al Nowfaly, from Al Sakuny, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘The best of the vegetables is the endive, and there is none from a leaf except that upon it is a drop (dew) from the Paradise. text: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Haroun Bin Muslim, from Mas’ada Bin sadaqa, from Ziyad, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘The endive is the chief of the vegetables’.

citation.arabic_text: عَلِيُّ بْنُ إِبْرَاهِيمَ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ هَارُونَ بْنِ مُسْلِمٍ عَنْ مَسْعَدَةَ بْنِ صَدَقَةَ عَنْ زِيَادٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) قَالَ الْهِنْدَبَاءُ سَيِّدُ الْبُقُولِ .

text: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad and Ali Al Ashary, from Muhammad Bin Abdul Jabbar altogether from Al Hajjal, from Sa’alba, from a man, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘It is upon you with (eating) the endive, for it increased in the water, and improves the child birth, and it is hot, soft, increasing in the male children’.

citation.arabic_text: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَحْيَى عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ وَ أَبُو عَلِيٍّ الْأَشْعَرِيُّ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عَبْدِ الْجَبَّارِ جَمِيعاً عَنِ الْحَجَّالِ عَنْ ثَعْلَبَةَ عَنْ رَجُلٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) قَالَ عَلَيْكَ بِالْهِنْدَبَاءِ فَإِنَّهُ يَزِيدُ فِي الْمَاءِ وَ يُحَسِّنُ الْوَلَدَ وَ هُوَ حَارٌّ لَيِّنٌ يَزِيدُ فِي الْوَلَدِ الذُّكُورَةَ .
citation.translation: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad and Ali Al Ashary, from Muhammad Bin Abdul Jabbar altogether from Al Hajjal, from Sa’alba, from a man, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘It is upon you with (eating) the endive, for it increased in the water, and improves the child birth, and it is hot, soft, increasing in the male children’.

text: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Abu Abdullah, from Abu Suleyman Al Haza’a, from Muhammad Bin Al Fayz who said, ‘I had lunch with Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> and upon the food-spread were vegetables, and with us was an old man who avoided the endive. So Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘But you all are thinking that the endive is cold, and it is not like that, but it is moderate, and its merits upon the vegetables is like our<sup>asws</sup> merits upon the people’.

citation.arabic_text: عِدَّةٌ مِنْ أَصْحَابِنَا عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَنْ أَبِي سُلَيْمَانَ الْحَذَّاءِ الْجَبَلِيِّ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ الْفَيْضِ قَالَ تَغَدَّيْتُ مَعَ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) وَ عَلَى الْخِوَانِ بَقْلٌ وَ مَعَنَا شَيْخٌ فَجَعَلَ يَتَنَكَّبُ الْهِنْدَبَاءَ فَقَالَ أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) أَمَّا أَنْتُمْ فَتَزْعُمُونَ أَنَّ الْهِنْدَبَاءَ بَارِدَةٌ وَ لَيْسَتْ كَذَلِكَ وَ لَكِنَّهَا مُعْتَدِلَةٌ وَ فَضْلُهَا عَلَى الْبُقُولِ كَفَضْلِنَا عَلَى النَّاسِ .
citation.translation: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Abu Abdullah, from Abu Suleyman Al Haza’a, from Muhammad Bin Al Fayz who said, ‘I had lunch with Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> and upon the food-spread were vegetables, and with us was an old man who avoided the endive. So Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘But you all are thinking that the endive is cold, and it is not like that, but it is moderate, and its merits upon the vegetables is like our<sup>asws</sup> merits upon the people’.

text: From him, from one of our companions, from Al Samma, from Shuayb, from Abu Baseer, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Eat the endive, for there is none from the mornings except that there descends upon it a drop from the Paradise. So when we were free from the lunch, he<sup>asws</sup> called for it again, and I saw him<sup>asws</sup> pursuing its leaves upon the food-spread and eating it, and he<sup>asws</sup> gave me from it, and he<sup>asws</sup> was saying: ‘Finish your meal with it, for it makes agreeable what was before just as it makes you desirous for what is after it, and does away with the heaviness, and aromatises the burps and the smell of the breath’.

text: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Muhammad Bin Musa, from Ashkeyb Bin Abdat Al Hamdany, by a chain of his, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘The sweet basil is a vegetable of the Prophets<sup>as</sup>, therein are eight qualities – It is palatable, and it opens the blockages, and it aromatises the burps, and aromatises the breath, and makes one desirous of the food, and it removes illnesses, and it is a security from the leprosy when it settles in the inside of the human being, it suppresses the illnesses, all of them’.

citation.arabic_text: الْحَوْكُ بَقْلَةُ الْأَنْبِيَاءِ أَمَا إِنَّ فِيهِ ثَمَانَ خِصَالٍ يُمْرِئُ وَ يَفْتَحُ السُّدَدَ وَ يُطَيِّبُ الْجُشَاءَ وَ يُطَيِّبُ النَّكْهَةَ وَ يُشَهِّي الطَّعَامَ وَ يَسُلُّ الدَّاءَ وَ هُوَ أَمَانٌ مِنَ الْجُذَامِ إِذَا اسْتَقَرَّ فِي جَوْفِ الْإِنْسَانِ قَمَعَ الدَّاءَ كُلَّهُ .

text: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Abdullah, from Muhammad Bin Isa, or someone else, from Abdul Rahman, from Hammad Bin Zakariyya, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘The vegetables were mentioned in the presence of Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup>, so he<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘Eat the leek, for its example among the vegetables is like the example of the bread in the rest of the foods’, or said, ‘Sauces’.

citation.arabic_text: عِدَّةٌ مِنْ أَصْحَابِنَا عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عِيسَى أَوْ غَيْرِهِ عَنْ عَبْدِ الرَّحْمَنِ عَنْ حَمَّادِ بْنِ زَكَرِيَّا عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) قَالَ ذُكِرَتِ الْبُقُولُ عِنْدَ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ ( صلى الله عليه وآله ) فَقَالَ كُلُوا الْكُرَّاثَ فَإِنَّ مَثَلَهُ فِي الْبُقُولِ كَمَثَلِ الْخُبْزِ فِي سَائِرِ الطَّعَامِ أَوْ قَالَ الْإِدَامِ.

text: From him, from Dawood Bin Abu Dawood, (It has been narrated) from a man who saw Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> at Khurasan eating the leek from the orchards just as it was. So it was said to him<sup>asws</sup>, ‘There is compost in it’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Nothing from it attaches to it, and it is good for the hemorrhoids’.

citation.arabic_text: عَنْهُ عَنْ دَاوُدَ بْنِ أَبِي دَاوُدَ عَنْ رَجُلٍ رَأَى أَبَا الْحَسَنِ ( عليه السلام ) بِخُرَاسَانَ يَأْكُلُ الْكُرَّاثَ مِنَ الْبُسْتَانِ كَمَا هُوَ فَقِيلَ لَهُ إِنَّ فِيهِ السَّمَادَ فَقَالَ ( عليه السلام ) لَا تَعَلَّقُ بِهِ مِنْهُ شَيْ‏ءٌ وَ هُوَ جَيِّدٌ لِلْبَوَاسِيرِ .
citation.translation: From him, from Dawood Bin Abu Dawood, (It has been narrated) from a man who saw Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> at Khurasan eating the leek from the orchards just as it was. text: From him, from one of his companions, from Hanaan Bin Sudeyr who said, ‘I was with Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> upon the food-spread, so I inclined towards the endive, so he<sup>asws</sup> said to me: ‘O Hanaan! Why are you not eating the leek?’ I said, ‘Due to what has come from you<sup>asws</sup> from the reports regarding the endive’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘And what is that which has come from us<sup>asws</sup>?’ I said, ‘It is said from you<sup>asws</sup> that you<sup>asws</sup> said that a drop from the Paradise falls upon it, every day one drop’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘So upon the leek then, seven drops’. I said, ‘So how should I eat it?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Cut off its root and throw away its head’.

citation.arabic_text: عَنْهُ عَنْ بَعْضِ أَصْحَابِهِ عَنْ حَنَانِ بْنِ سَدِيرٍ قَالَ كُنْتُ مَعَ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) عَلَى الْمَائِدَةِ فَمِلْتُ عَلَى الْهِنْدَبَاءِ فَقَالَ لِي يَا حَنَانُ لِمَ لَا تَأْكُلُ الْكُرَّاثَ قُلْتُ لِمَا جَاءَ عَنْكُمْ مِنَ الرِّوَايَةِ فِي الْهِنْدَبَاءِ فَقَالَ وَ مَا الَّذِي جَاءَ عَنَّا قُلْتُ إِنَّهُ قِيلَ عَنْكُمْ إِنَّكُمْ قُلْتُمْ إِنَّهُ يُقَطَّرُ عَلَيْهِ مِنَ الْجَنَّةِ فِي كُلِّ يَوْمٍ قَطْرَةٌ قَالَ فَقَالَ ( عليه السلام ) فَعَلَى الْكُرَّاثِ إِذَنْ سَبْعُ قَطَرَاتٍ قُلْتُ فَكَيْفَ آكُلُهُ قَالَ اقْطَعْ أُصُولَهُ وَ اقْذِفْ بِرُءُوسِهِ .

citation.translation: From him, from one of his companions, from Hanaan Bin Sudeyr who said, ‘I was with Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> upon the food-spread, so I inclined towards the endive, so he<sup>asws</sup> said to me: ‘O Hanaan! Why are you not eating the leek?’ I said, ‘Due to what has come from you<sup>asws</sup> from the reports regarding the endive’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘And what is that which has come from us<sup>asws</sup>?’ I said, ‘It is said from you<sup>asws</sup> that you<sup>asws</sup> said that a drop from the Paradise falls upon it, every day one drop’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘So upon the leek then, seven drops’. I said, ‘So how should I eat it?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Cut off its root and throw away its head’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: مرسل - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (2/208)

text: From him, from one of his companions, raising it, said, ‘Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Eat the leak with the grained salt’.

citation.arabic_text: كَانَ أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ ( عليه السلام ) يَأْكُلُ الْكُرَّاثَ بِالْمِلْحِ الْجَرِيشِ .
citation.translation: From him, from one of his companions, raising it, said, ‘Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Eat the leak with the grained salt’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: مرفوع - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (2/209)

text: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Abu Abdullah, from Muhammad Bin Isa, or someone else, from Quteyba Bin Mihran, from Hammad Bin Zakariyya, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘It is upon you with (eating) the celery, for it is a food of Ilyas<sup>as</sup>, and Al-Yas’a<sup>as</sup>, and Yoshua<sup>as</sup> Bin Noun<sup>as</sup>’.

citation.arabic_text: قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ ( صلى الله عليه وآله ) عَلَيْكُمْ بِالْكَرَفْسِ فَإِنَّهُ طَعَامُ إِلْيَاسَ وَ الْيَسَعِ وَ يُوشَعَ بْنِ نُونٍ.

text: From him, from Nuh Bin Shuayb Al Neyshapouri, from Muhammad Bin Al Hassan Bin Ali Bin Yaqteen regarding what is known from Nadir the servant who said, ‘Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> mentioned the celery, so he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘You all are desiring it and there is none from an animal except that it has rubbed with it’.

citation.arabic_text: مَا أَعْلَمُ عَنْ نَادِرٍ الْخَادِمِ قَالَ ذَكَرَ أَبُو الْحَسَنِ ( عليه السلام ) الْكَرَفْسَ فَقَالَ أَنْتُمْ تَشْتَهُونَهُ وَ لَيْسَ مِنْ دَابَّةٍ إِلَّا وَ هِيَ تَحْتَكُّ بِهِ .

text: Muhammad Bin yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Muhammad Bin Isa, from Al Dahqan, from Dorost, from Ibrahim Bin Abdul Hameed, (It has been narrated) from Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Eating the apple and the coriander inherits the forgetfulness’.

citation.arabic_text: أَكْلُ التُّفَّاحِ وَ الْكُزْبُرَةِ يُورِثُ النِّسْيَانَ .

citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: ضعيف - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (22/210)

text: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from one of our companions, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> trod upon the scorching ground, so it burned him<sup>saww</sup>. So he<sup>saww</sup> trod upon the purslane, and it is referred to as the ‘vegetable of the idiots’, so it settled from him<sup>saww</sup> the heat of the scorching ground. So he<sup>saww</sup> supplicated for it, and he<sup>saww</sup> used to love it, and he<sup>saww</sup> was saying: ‘From the vegetables, there is none more Blessed’.

citation.arabic_text: عَلِيُّ بْنُ إِبْرَاهِيمَ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنِ ابْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ عَنْ بَعْضِ أَصْحَابِنَا عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ قَالَ وَطِئَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ ( صلى الله عليه وآله ) الرَّمْضَاءَ فَأَحْرَقَتْهُ فَوَطِئَ عَلَى الرِّجْلَةِ وَ هِيَ الْبَقْلَةُ الْحَمْقَاءُ فَسَكَنَ عَنْهُ حَرُّ الرَّمْضَاءِ فَدَعَا لَهَا وَ كَانَ يُحِبُّهَا ( صلى الله عليه وآله ) وَ يَقُولُ مِنْ بَقْلَةٍ مَا أَبْرَكَهَا .

text: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Usman Bin Isa, from Furat Bin Ahnaf who said, ‘I heard Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> saying: ‘There is no vegetable upon the surface of the earth more noble, nor any more beneficial than the Purslane, and it is a vegetable of Fatima<sup>asws</sup>’. Then he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘May Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Curse the Clan of Umayya! They named it as the ‘vegetable of the idiots’ due to their hatred and enmity to Fatima<sup>asws</sup>’.

citation.arabic_text: سَمِعْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) يَقُولُ لَيْسَ عَلَى وَجْهِ الْأَرْضِ بَقْلَةٌ أَشْرَفُ وَ لَا أَنْفَعُ مِنَ الْفَرْفَخِ وَ هُوَ بَقْلَةُ فَاطِمَةَ ( عليها السلام ) ثُمَّ قَالَ لَعَنَ اللَّهُ بَنِي أُمَيَّةَ هُمْ سَمَّوْهَا بَقْلَةَ الْحَمْقَاءِ بُغْضاً لَنَا وَ عَدَاوَةً لِفَاطِمَةَ ( عليها السلام ) .

citation.arabic_text: عَلَيْكُمْ بِالْخَسِّ فَإِنَّهُ يُصَفِّي الدَّمَ .

text: From him, from Muhammad Bin Musa, from Ali Bin Al Hassan Al Hamdany, from Muhammad Bin Amro Bin Ibrahim, (It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> or Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> – the uncertainty being from Muhammad Bin Musa who said, ‘The rue was mentioned, so he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘But there are benefits therein – it increases the intellect, and augments the brain, apart from it that it decays the water of the back’. citation.arabic_text: عَنْهُ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ مُوسَى عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ الْحَسَنِ الْهَمْدَانِيِّ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عَمْرِو بْنِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ عَنْ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ أَوْ أَبِي الْحَسَنِ ( عليه السلام ) الْوَهْمُ مِنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ مُوسَى قَالَ ذُكِرَ السَّدَابُ فَقَالَ أَمَا إِنَّ فِيهِ مَنَافِعَ زِيَادَةٌ فِي الْعَقْلِ وَ تَوْفِيرٌ فِي الدِّمَاغِ غَيْرَ أَنَّهُ يُنَتِّنُ مَاءَ الظَّهْرِ . وَ رُوِيَ أَنَّهُ جَيِّدٌ لِوَجَعِ الْأُذُنِ .

text: Muhammad Bin yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from yaqoub Bin aamir, from a man, (It has been narrated) from Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘The rue increases in the intellect’.

So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The endive and the sweet basil is for us<sup>asws</sup> and the watercress is for the Clan of Umayya’.

text: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Abu Abdullah, form Muhammad Bin Isa, and someone else, from Quteyba Al A’ashy, or said Quteyba Bin Mihran, from Hammad Bin Zakariyya, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘The man would not fill himself up with the watercress after he has Prayed al-Isha the last, so he sleeps during that night, except that his soul would pull him towards the leprosy’.

citation.arabic_text: قُتَيْبَةَ بْنِ مِهْرَانَ عَنْ حَمَّادِ بْنِ زَكَرِيَّا عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) قَالَ مَا تَضْلَعُ الرَّجُلُ مِنَ الْجِرْجِيرِ بَعْدَ أَنْ يُصَلِّيَ الْعِشَاءَ الْآخِرَةَ فَبَاتَ تِلْكَ اللَّيْلَةَ إِلَّا وَ نَفْسُهُ تُنَازِعُهُ إِلَى الْجُذَامِ .

text: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Al Nowfaly, from Al Sakuny, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘The one who eats the watercress at night, the vein of leprosy would hit him from his nose, and he would sleep with blood flowing’.

citation.arabic_text: مَنْ أَكَلَ الْجِرْجِيرَ بِاللَّيْلِ ضَرَبَ عَلَيْهِ عِرْقُ الْجُذَامِ مِنْ أَنْفِهِ وَ بَاتَ يُنْزَفُ الدَّمُ .

So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The endive and the sweet basil is for us<sup>asws</sup> and the watercress is for the Clan of Umayya’.

citation.arabic_text: سَأَلَ رَجُلٌ أَبَا عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) عَنِ الْبَقْلِ الْهِنْدَبَاءِ وَ الْبَاذَرُوجِ وَ الْجِرْجِيرِ فَقَالَ الْهِنْدَبَاءُ وَ وَ الْبَاذَرُوجُ لَنَا وَ الْجِرْجِيرُ لِبَنِي أُمَيَّةَ .
citation.translation: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Musa Bin Al Hassan, from Ahmad Bin Suleyman, from his father, from Abu Baseer who said, ‘A man asked Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> about the vegetable, the endive and the sweet basil and the watercress. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The endive and the sweet basil is for us<sup>asws</sup> and the watercress is for the Clan of Umayya’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: مجهول - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (22/212)

text: عدة من أصحابنا، عن أحمد بن أبي عبد الله، عن محمد بن عيسى، عن الحسين بن سعيد، عن نصير مولى أبي عبد الله عليه السلام، عن موفق مولى أبي الحسن عليه السلام قال: كان مولاي أبو الحسن عليه السلام إذا أمر بشراء البقل يأمر بالاكثار منه ومن الجرجير فيشترى له وكان يقول عليه السلام: ما أحمق بعض الناس يقولون إنه ينبت في واد في جهنم والله عز وجل يقول:وقودها الناس والحجارة فكيف تنبت البقل.

citation.arabic_text: عدة من أصحابنا، عن أحمد بن أبي عبد الله، عن محمد بن عيسى، عن الحسين بن سعيد، عن نصير مولى أبي عبد الله عليه السلام، عن موفق مولى أبي الحسن عليه السلام قال: كان مولاي أبو الحسن عليه السلام إذا أمر بشراء البقل يأمر بالاكثار منه ومن الجرجير فيشترى له وكان يقول عليه السلام: ما أحمق بعض الناس يقولون إنه ينبت في واد في جهنم والله عز وجل يقول:وقودها الناس والحجارة فكيف تنبت البقل.

text: From him, from Muhammad Bin Isa, from one of the Husayniyayn, (It has been narrated) from Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> that the Chard suppresses the vein of the leprosy, and there does not enter the inside of the sufferer of the vitiligo like a leaf of the Chard’.

citation.arabic_text: عَنْهُ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنْ بَعْضِ الْحُصَيْنِيِّينَ عَنْ أَبِي الْحَسَنِ ( عليه السلام ) أَنَّ السِّلْقَ يَقْمَعُ عِرْقَ الْجُذَامِ وَ مَا دَخَلَ جَوْفَ الْمُبَرْسَمِ مِثْلُ وَرَقِ السِّلْقِ .
citation.translation: From him, from Muhammad Bin Isa, from one of the Husayniyayn, (It has been narrated) from Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> that the Chard suppresses the vein of the leprosy, and there does not enter the inside of the sufferer of the vitiligo like a leaf of the Chard’.

text: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Abu Abdullah, from Al Hassan Bin Ali, from Abu Usman, (It has been narrated) raising it to Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic Raised the leprosy from the Jews by their eating the Chard, and their gouging out the veils’.

citation.arabic_text: إِنَّ اللَّهَ عَزَّ وَ جَلَّ رَفَعَ عَنِ الْيَهُودِ الْجُذَامَ بِأَكْلِهِمُ السِّلْقَ وَ قَلْعِهِمُ الْعُرُوقَ .
citation.translation: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Abu Abdullah, from Al Hassan Bin Ali, from Abu Usman, (It has been narrated) raising it to Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic Raised the leprosy from the Jews by their eating the Chard, and their gouging out the veils’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: مرفوع - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (22/213)

text: From him, from Muhammad Bin Abdul Hameed, from Safwan Bin Yahya, (It has been narrated) from Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘The best of the vegetables is the Chard’.

citation.arabic_text: نِعْمَ الْبَقْلَةُ السِّلْقُ .
citation.translation: From him, from Muhammad Bin Abdul Hameed, from Safwan Bin Yahya, (It has been narrated) from Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘The best of the vegetables is the Chard’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: صحيح - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (22/213)

text: From him, from Ali Bin Al Hassan Al Taymi, from Suleyman Bin Abbad, from Isa Bin Abu Al Ward, from Muhammad Bin Qays, (It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> that the Children of Israel complained to Musa<sup>asws</sup> of what they were facing from the whiteness (Vitiligo), so he<sup>as</sup> took that complaint to Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Glorious and High. So Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Revealed unto him<sup>as</sup> that: “Order them with eating the cow meat with the Chard’.

citation.arabic_text: أَنَّ بَنِي إِسْرَائِيلَ شَكَوْا إِلَى مُوسَى ( عليه السلام ) مَا يَلْقَوْنَ مِنَ الْبَيَاضِ فَشَكَا ذَلِكَ إِلَى اللَّهِ سُبْحَانَهُ وَ تَعَالَى فَأَوْحَى اللَّهُ إِلَيْهِ أَنْ مُرْهُمْ بِأَكْلِ لَحْمِ الْبَقَرِ بِالسِّلْقِ .
citation.translation: From him, from Ali Bin Al Hassan Al Taymi, from Suleyman Bin Abbad, from Isa Bin Abu Al Ward, from Muhammad Bin Qays, (It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> that the Children of Israel complained to Musa<sup>asws</sup> of what they were facing from the whiteness (Vitiligo), so he<sup>as</sup> took that complaint to Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Glorious and High. So Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Revealed unto him<sup>as</sup> that: “Order them with eating the cow meat with the Chard’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: مجهول - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (22/213)

text: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Abdullah Bin Ja’far, from Muhammad Bin Isa, (It has been narrated) from Abu Al-Hassan Al-Reza<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Feed the Chard to your sick ones, meaning a leaf of it, for therein is a healing, and there is no cure with it, nor is there a suffering for it, and gifts the sleep to the patient, and keep away from its root for it agitates the black bile’.

citation.arabic_text: أَطْعِمُوا مَرْضَاكُمُ السِّلْقَ يَعْنِي وَرَقَهُ فَإِنَّ فِيهِ شِفَاءً وَ لَا دَاءَ مَعَهُ وَ لَا غَائِلَةَ لَهُ وَ يُهْدِئُ نَوْمَ الْمَرِيضِ وَ اجْتَنِبُوا أَصْلَهُ فَإِنَّهُ يُهَيِّجُ السَّوْدَاءَ .
citation.translation: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Abdullah Bin Ja’far, from Muhammad Bin Isa, (It has been narrated) from Abu Al-Hassan Al-Reza<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Feed the Chard to your sick ones, meaning a leaf of it, for therein is a healing, and there is no cure with it, nor is there a suffering for it, and gifts the sleep to the patient, and keep away from its root for it agitates the black bile’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: صحيح - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (2/213)

text: From him, from Muhammad Bin Isa, from one of the Husayniyayn, (It has been narrated) from Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> that the Chard suppresses the vein of the leprosy, and there does not enter the inside of the sufferer of the vitiligo like a leaf of the Chard’.

text: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Abdullah Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Ali Bin Al Hakam, from Aban Bin Usman, from Abu Baseer, (It has been narrated) from Fatima<sup>as</sup> daughter of Ali<sup>asws</sup>, from Amamat daughter of Abu Al A’as, from Al Rabie and her mother Zaynab daughter of Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup>, said, ‘Amir Al Momineen<sup>asws</sup> came over to me in a Month of Ramazan, so he<sup>asws</sup> came for dinner, and dates, and truffles. So he<sup>asws</sup> ate, and he was loving the truffles’.

citation.arabic_text: تْ أَتَانِي أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ عَلِيٌّ ( عليه السلام ) فِي شَهْرِ رَمَضَانَ فَأُتِيَ بِعَشَاءٍ وَ تَمْرٍ وَ كَمْأَةٍ فَأَكَلَ ( عليه السلام ) وَ كَانَ يُحِبُّ الْكَمْأَةَ .
citation.translation: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Abdullah Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Ali Bin Al Hakam, from Aban Bin Usman, from Abu Baseer, (It has been narrated) from Fatima<sup>as</sup> daughter of Ali<sup>asws</sup>, from Amamat daughter of Abu Al A’as, from Al Rabie and her mother Zaynab daughter of Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup>, said, ‘Amir Al Momineen<sup>asws</sup> came over to me in a Month of Ramazan, so he<sup>asws</sup> came for dinner, and dates, and truffles. So he<sup>asws</sup> ate, and he was loving the truffles’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: مجهول - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (2/214)

text: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Abu Abdullah, from Muhammad Bin Ali, from Muhammad Bin Al Fuzayl, from Abdul Rahman Bin Zayd, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘The truffle is from the Manna, and the Manna is from the Paradise, and its water is a healing for the eyes’.

citation.arabic_text: قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ ( صلى الله عليه وآله ) الْكَمْأَةُ مِنَ الْمَنِّ وَ الْمَنُّ مِنَ الْجَنَّةِ وَ مَاؤُهَا شِفَاءٌ لِلْعَيْنِ .
citation.translation: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Abu Abdullah, from Muhammad Bin Ali, from Muhammad Bin Al Fuzayl, from Abdul Rahman Bin Zayd, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘The truffle is from the Manna, and the Manna is from the Paradise, and its water is a healing for the eyes’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: ضعيف - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (22/214)

text: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Ibn Fazzal, from Abdullah Bin Maymoun Al qaddah, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘The Prophet<sup>saww</sup> liked the gourd, and he<sup>asws</sup> used to pick it up from the platter’.

citation.arabic_text: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَحْيَى عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنِ ابْنِ فَضَّالٍ عَنْ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ بْنِ مَيْمُونٍ الْقَدَّاحِ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) قَالَ كَانَ النَّبِيُّ ( صلى الله عليه وآله ) يُعْجِبُهُ الدُّبَّاءُ وَ يَلْتَقِطُهُ مِنَ الصَّحْفَةِ .
citation.translation: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Ibn Fazzal, from Abdullah Bin Maymoun Al qaddah, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘The Prophet<sup>saww</sup> liked the gourd, and he<sup>asws</sup> used to pick it up from the platter’.

text: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad,f rom Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Abu Nasr, from Abdullah Bin Muhammad Al Shamy, from Al Husayn Bin Hanzala, from one of the two (5th or 6th Imamasws) having said: ‘The gourd increases the mind’.

citation.arabic_text: عِدَّةٌ مِنْ أَصْحَابِنَا عَنْ سَهْلِ بْنِ زِيَادٍ عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ أَبِي نَصْرٍ عَنْ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ الشَّامِيِّ عَنِ الْحُسَيْنِ بْنِ حَنْظَلَةَ عَنْ أَحَدِهِمَا ( عليهما السلام ) قَالَ الدُّبَّاءُ يَزِيدُ فِي الدِّمَاغِ .
citation.translation: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad,f rom Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Abu Nasr, from Abdullah Bin Muhammad Al Shamy, from Al Husayn Bin Hanzala, from one of the two (5th or 6th Imamasws) having said: ‘The gourd increases the mind’.

text: From him, from Ali Bin Hassan, from Musa Bin Bakr who said, ‘I heard Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> saying: ‘The gourd increases the intellect’.

citation.arabic_text: عَنْهُ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ حَسَّانَ عَنْ مُوسَى بْنِ بَكْرٍ قَالَ سَمِعْتُ أَبَا الْحَسَنِ ( عليه السلام ) يَقُولُ الدُّبَّاءُ يَزِيدُ فِي الْعَقْلِ .
citation.translation: From him, from Ali Bin Hassan, from Musa Bin Bakr who said, ‘I heard Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> saying: ‘The gourd increases the intellect’.

text: Al Husayn Bin Muhammad, from Al Sayyari, raising it, said, ‘The Prophet<sup>saww</sup> liked the gourd, and he<sup>saww</sup> would order his<sup>saww</sup> wives, when they cooked a pot, so they should be frequenting from the gourd, and it is the pumpkin’.

citation.arabic_text: الْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنِ السَّيَّارِيِّ رَفَعَهُ قَالَ كَانَ النَّبِيُّ ( صلى الله عليه وآله ) يُعْجِبُهُ الدُّبَّاءُ وَ كَانَ يَأْمُرُ نِسَاءَهُ إِذَا طَبَخْنَ قِدْراً يُكْثِرْنَ مِنَ الدُّبَّاءِ وَ هُوَ الْقَرْعُ .

It is upon you<sup>asws</sup> with (eating) the gourd. Therefore eat it, for it increases the mind and the intellect’.

citation.arabic_text: عِدَّةٌ مِنْ أَصْحَابِنَا عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ بَعْضِ أَصْحَابِنَا عَنْ أَبِي الْحَسَنِ مُوسَى ( عليه السلام ) قَالَ كَانَ فِيمَا أَوْصَى بِهِ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ ( صلى الله عليه وآله ) عَلِيّاً ( عليه السلام ) أَنَّهُ قَالَ لَهُ يَا عَلِيُّ عَلَيْكَ بِالدُّبَّاءِ فَكُلْهُ فَإِنَّهُ يَزِيدُ فِي الدِّمَاغِ وَ الْعَقْلِ .

It is upon you<sup>asws</sup> with (eating) the gourd. Therefore eat it, for it increases the mind and the intellect’.

text: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Al Nowfaly, from Al Sakuny, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> that Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> was asked about the pumpkin to be slaughtered. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The pumpkin is not to be slaughtered. So eat it, and do not slaughter it, do not let the Satan<sup>la</sup> tempt you all, may Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Curse him<sup>la</sup>’.

citation.arabic_text: الْقَرْعُ لَيْسَ يُذَكَّى فَكُلُوهُ وَ لَا تَذْبَحُوهُ وَ لَا يَسْتَهْوِيَنَّكُمُ الشَّيْطَانُ لَعَنَهُ اللَّهُ .

text: And by his chain, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘The Prophet<sup>saww</sup> fascinated by the gourd in the pots, and it is the pumpkin’.
