citation.arabic_text: سَمِعْتُ أَبَا الْحَسَنِ ( عليه السلام ) يَقُولُ الدُّبَّاءُ يَزِيدُ فِي الْعَقْلِ .
citation.translation: From him, from Ali Bin Hassan, from Musa Bin Bakr who said, ‘I heard Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> saying: ‘The gourd increases the intellect’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: ضعيف على المشهور - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (2/216)

text: Al Husayn Bin Muhammad, from Al Sayyari, raising it, said, ‘The Prophet<sup>saww</sup> liked the gourd, and he<sup>saww</sup> would order his<sup>saww</sup> wives, when they cooked a pot, so they should be frequenting from the gourd, and it is the pumpkin’.

citation.arabic_text: كَانَ النَّبِيُّ ( صلى الله عليه وآله ) يُعْجِبُهُ الدُّبَّاءُ وَ كَانَ يَأْمُرُ نِسَاءَهُ إِذَا طَبَخْنَ قِدْراً يُكْثِرْنَ مِنَ الدُّبَّاءِ وَ هُوَ الْقَرْعُ .
citation.translation: Al Husayn Bin Muhammad, from Al Sayyari, raising it, said, ‘The Prophet<sup>saww</sup> liked the gourd, and he<sup>saww</sup> would order his<sup>saww</sup> wives, when they cooked a pot, so they should be frequenting from the gourd, and it is the pumpkin’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: ضعيف - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (22/216)

text: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Abu Abdullah, from his father, from oe of our companions, (It has been narrated) from Abu Al-Hassan Musa<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Among what Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> bequeathed to Ali<sup>asws</sup> with was that he<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘O Ali<sup>asws</sup>! It is upon you<sup>asws</sup> with (eating) the gourd. Therefore eat it, for it increases the mind and the intellect’.

citation.arabic_text: كَانَ فِيمَا أَوْصَى بِهِ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ ( صلى الله عليه وآله ) عَلِيّاً ( عليه السلام ) أَنَّهُ قَالَ لَهُ يَا عَلِيُّ عَلَيْكَ بِالدُّبَّاءِ فَكُلْهُ فَإِنَّهُ يَزِيدُ فِي الدِّمَاغِ وَ الْعَقْلِ .
citation.translation: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Abu Abdullah, from his father, from oe of our companions, (It has been narrated) from Abu Al-Hassan Musa<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Among what Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> bequeathed to Ali<sup>asws</sup> with was that he<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘O Ali<sup>asws</sup>! It is upon you<sup>asws</sup> with (eating) the gourd. Therefore eat it, for it increases the mind and the intellect’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: مرسل - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (22/217)

text: Ali Bin Muhammad Bin Bundar, from his father, from Muhammad Bin Ali Al Hamdany, from Hanaan who said, ‘I heard Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, and I was with him<sup>asws</sup> upon the food-spread, so he<sup>asws</sup> gave me a radish and said: ‘O Hanaan! Eat the radish for therein are three qualities – its leaf dispels the wind, and its core eases the flow of urine, and its root cuts the phlegm’. And in another report: ‘And its leaf nourishes’.

citation.arabic_text: سَمِعْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) وَ كُنْتُ مَعَهُ عَلَى الْمَائِدَةِ فَنَاوَلَنِي فُجْلَةً وَ قَالَ يَا حَنَانُ كُلِ الْفُجْلَ فَإِنَّ فِيهِ ثَلَاثَ خِصَالٍ وَرَقُهُ يَطْرُدُ الرِّيَاحَ وَ لُبُّهُ يُسَرْبِلُ الْبَوْلَ وَ أَصْلُهُ يَقْطَعُ الْبَلْغَمَ . وَ فِي رِوَايَةٍ أُخْرَى وَرَقُهُ يُمْرِئُ .
citation.translation: Ali Bin Muhammad Bin Bundar, from his father, from Muhammad Bin Ali Al Hamdany, from Hanaan who said, ‘I heard Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, and I was with him<sup>asws</sup> upon the food-spread, so he<sup>asws</sup> gave me a radish and said: ‘O Hanaan! Eat the radish for therein are three qualities – its leaf dispels the wind, and its core eases the flow of urine, and its root cuts the phlegm’. And in another report: ‘And its leaf nourishes’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: ضعيف - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (22/217)

text: From him, from Al Sayyari, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Khalid, from Ahmad Bin Al Mubarak, from Abu Usman, from Dorost, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘The radish, its root cuts the phlegm, and its core digests, and its leaf flows the urine with a flowing’.

citation.arabic_text: الْفُجْلُ أَصْلُهُ يَقْطَعُ الْبَلْغَمَ وَ لُبُّهُ يَهْضِمُ وَ وَرَقُهُ يَحْدِرُ الْبَوْلَ حَدْراً .
citation.translation: From him, from Al Sayyari, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Khalid, from Ahmad Bin Al Mubarak, from Abu Usman, from Dorost, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘The radish, its root cuts the phlegm, and its core digests, and its leaf flows the urine with a flowing’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: ضعيف - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (2/217)

text: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Ibrahim Bin Abdul Rahman, from his father, from Dawood Bin Farqad who said, ‘I heard Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> saying: ‘Eating the carrots warms the kidneys, and establishes the manhood’. I said to him<sup>asws</sup>, ‘May I be sacrificed for you<sup>asws</sup>! How can I eat it and there are no teeth for me’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said to me: ‘Instruct the maid to boil it, and eat it’.

citation.arabic_text: عِدَّةٌ مِنْ أَصْحَابِنَا عَنْ سَهْلِ بْنِ زِيَادٍ عَنْ إِبْرَاهِيمَ بْنِ عَبْدِ الرَّحْمَنِ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ دَاوُدَ بْنِ فَرْقَدٍ قَالَ سَمِعْتُ أَبَا الْحَسَنِ ( عليه السلام ) يَقُولُ أَكْلُ الْجَزَرِ يُسَخِّنُ الْكُلْيَتَيْنِ وَ يَنْصِبُ الذَّكَرَ قَالَ فَقُلْتُ لَهُ جُعِلْتُ فِدَاكَ كَيْفَ آكُلُهُ وَ لَيْسَ لِي أَسْنَانٌ قَالَ فَقَالَ لِي مُرِ الْجَارِيَةَ تَسْلُقُهُ وَ كُلْهُ .
citation.translation: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Ibrahim Bin Abdul Rahman, from his father, from Dawood Bin Farqad who said, ‘I heard Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> saying: ‘Eating the carrots warms the kidneys, and establishes the manhood’. I said to him<sup>asws</sup>, ‘May I be sacrificed for you<sup>asws</sup>! How can I eat it and there are no teeth for me’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said to me: ‘Instruct the maid to boil it, and eat it’.

text: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Al Hassan Bin Ali, or someone else, from Dawood Bin Farqad, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Eating the carrots warms the kidneys and stirs the manhood’.

citation.arabic_text: أَكْلُ الْجَزَرِ يُسَخِّنُ الْكُلْيَتَيْنِ وَ يُقِيمُ الذَّكَرَ .
citation.translation: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Al Hassan Bin Ali, or someone else, from Dawood Bin Farqad, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Eating the carrots warms the kidneys and stirs the manhood’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: مجهول - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (22/217)

text: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Muhammad Bin Musa, from Ahmad Bin Al Hassan Al Jallab, from Musa Bin Ismail, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from one of our companions who said, ‘Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The carrots are a security from the colitis, and the hemorrhoids, and it aids upon the copulation’.

citation.arabic_text: قَالَ أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) الْجَزَرُ أَمَانٌ مِنَ الْقُولَنْجِ وَ الْبَوَاسِيرِ وَ يُعِينُ عَلَى الْجِمَاعِ .
citation.translation: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Muhammad Bin Musa, from Ahmad Bin Al Hassan Al Jallab, from Musa Bin Ismail, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from one of our companions who said, ‘Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The carrots are a security from the colitis, and the hemorrhoids, and it aids upon the copulation’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: ضعيف - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (22/217)

text: From him, from Al Hassan Bin Al Husayn, from Muhamad Bin Sinan, from the one who mentioned it, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘It is upon you with (eating) the turnips, so eat these and be habitual in eating it, and conceal it except from its deserving one, for there is no one except with him is a vein of the leprosy, therefore melt it by eating it’.

citation.arabic_text: عَنْهُ عَنِ الْحَسَنِ بْنِ الْحُسَيْنِ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ سِنَانٍ عَمَّنْ ذَكَرَهُ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) قَالَ عَلَيْكُمْ بِالسَّلْجَمِ فَكُلُوهُ وَ أَدِيمُوا أَكْلَهُ وَ اكْتُمُوهُ إِلَّا عَنْ أَهْلِهِ فَمَا مِنْ أَحَدٍ إِلَّا وَ بِهِ عِرْقٌ مِنَ الْجُذَامِ فَأَذِيبُوهُ بِأَكْلِهِ .
citation.translation: From him, from Al Hassan Bin Al Husayn, from Muhamad Bin Sinan, from the one who mentioned it, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘It is upon you with (eating) the turnips, so eat these and be habitual in eating it, and conceal it except from its deserving one, for there is no one except with him is a vein of the leprosy, therefore melt it by eating it’.

text: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Abdullah Bin Ja’far, from Muhammad Bin Isa, from Ali Bin Al Musayyab who said, ‘Al-Abd Al-Salihasws (7th Imamasws) said: ‘It is upon you with (eating) Al-Lafti (a turnip dish), so eat it, meaning the turnip, for there is no one except for him is a vein for the leprosy, and Al-Lafti removes it’.

citation.arabic_text: قَالَ الْعَبْدُ الصَّالِحُ ( عليه السلام ) عَلَيْكَ بِاللِّفْتِ فَكُلْهُ يَعْنِي السَّلْجَمَ فَإِنَّهُ لَيْسَ مِنْ أَحَدٍ إِلَّا وَ لَهُ عِرْقٌ مِنَ الْجُذَامِ وَ اللِّفْتُ يُذِيبُهُ .
citation.translation: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Abdullah Bin Ja’far, from Muhammad Bin Isa, from Ali Bin Al Musayyab who said, ‘Al-Abd Al-Salihasws (7th Imamasws) said: ‘It is upon you with (eating) Al-Lafti (a turnip dish), so eat it, meaning the turnip, for there is no one except for him is a vein for the leprosy, and Al-Lafti removes it’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: صحيح - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (22/218)

text: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Abu Abdullah, from Abdul Aziz Al Muhtady, (It has been narrated) raising it to Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘There is no one except inside of him is a vein of the leprosy, so melt it by the turnip’.

citation.arabic_text: مَا مِنْ أَحَدٍ إِلَّا وَ فِيهِ عِرْقٌ مِنَ الْجُذَامِ فَأَذِيبُوهُ بِالسَّلْجَمِ .
citation.translation: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Abu Abdullah, from Abdul Aziz Al Muhtady, (It has been narrated) raising it to Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘There is no one except inside of him is a vein of the leprosy, so melt it by the turnip’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: مرفوع - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (22/218)

text: From him, from Yaqoub Bin Yazeed, from Yahya Bin Al Mubarak, from Abdullah Bin Al Mubarak, from Abduall Bin Jabala, from Ali Bin Abu Hamza, (It has been narrated) from Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup>, or said, from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘There is no one except with him is a vein of the leprosy, therefore melt it by eating the turnip’.

citation.arabic_text: عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) قَالَ مَا مِنْ أَحَدٍ إِلَّا وَ بِهِ عِرْقٌ مِنَ الْجُذَامِ فَأَذِيبُوهُ بِأَكْلِ السَّلْجَمِ .
citation.translation: From him, from Yaqoub Bin Yazeed, from Yahya Bin Al Mubarak, from Abdullah Bin Al Mubarak, from Abduall Bin Jabala, from Ali Bin Abu Hamza, (It has been narrated) from Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup>, or said, from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘There is no one except with him is a vein of the leprosy, therefore melt it by eating the turnip’.

citation.arabic_text: عَلَيْكُمْ بِالسَّلْجَمِ فَكُلُوهُ وَ أَدِيمُوا أَكْلَهُ وَ اكْتُمُوهُ إِلَّا عَنْ أَهْلِهِ فَمَا مِنْ أَحَدٍ إِلَّا وَ بِهِ عِرْقٌ مِنَ الْجُذَامِ فَأَذِيبُوهُ بِأَكْلِهِ .

text: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Al Hajjal, from the one who mentioned it, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> used to eat the cucumbers with the salt’.

citation.arabic_text: كَانَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ ( صلى الله عليه وآله ) يَأْكُلُ الْقِثَّاءَ بِالْمِلْحِ .
citation.translation: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Al Hajjal, from the one who mentioned it, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> used to eat the cucumbers with the salt’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: مرسل - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (22/219)

text: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Abdullah Bin Ja’far, from Muhammad Bin Isa, from Ubeydullah Al Dahqan, from dorost Al Wasity, from Abdullah Bin Sinan who said, ‘Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘When you eat the cucumbers, so eat it from its lower part, for it is greater in its Blessing’.

citation.arabic_text: قَالَ أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) إِذَا أَكَلْتُمُ الْقِثَّاءَ فَكُلُوهُ مِنْ أَسْفَلِهِ فَإِنَّهُ أَعْظَمُ لِبَرَكَتِهِ .
citation.translation: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Abdullah Bin Ja’far, from Muhammad Bin Isa, from Ubeydullah Al Dahqan, from dorost Al Wasity, from Abdullah Bin Sinan who said, ‘Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘When you eat the cucumbers, so eat it from its lower part, for it is greater in its Blessing’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: ضعيف - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (22/219)

text: Al Husayn Bin Muhammad, from Moalla Bin Muhammad, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, and Abdullah Bin Al Qasim, from Abdul Rahman Al Hashimy who said, ‘He<sup>asws</sup> said to one of his slaves: ‘Be (buy) less for us<sup>asws</sup> from the onions, and more for us<sup>asws</sup> from the aubergines’. So he said to him<sup>asws</sup> for his understanding, ‘The aubergines?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Yes, the aubergines, in all its tastes is beneficial for the illnesses, corrective for the health, balanced in its states, corrective for the old man and the youth, being moderate in its heat and its coolness, being hot in hot places and cool in cold places’.

citation.arabic_text: الْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنْ مُعَلَّى بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ وَ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ بْنِ الْقَاسِمِ عَنْ عَبْدِ الرَّحْمَنِ الْهَاشِمِيِّ قَالَ قَالَ لِبَعْضِ مَوَالِيهِ أَقْلِلْ لَنَا مِنَ الْبَصَلِ وَ أَكْثِرْ لَنَا مِنَ الْبَاذَنْجَانِ فَقَالَ لَهُ مُسْتَفْهِماً الْبَاذَنْجَانِ قَالَ نَعَمْ الْبَاذَنْجَانُ جَامِعُ الطَّعْمِ مَنْفِيُّ الدَّاءِ صَالِحٌ لِلطَّبِيعَةِ مُنْصِفٌ فِي أَحْوَالِهِ صَالِحٌ لِلشَّيْخِ وَ الشَّابِّ مُعْتَدِلٌ فِي حَرَارَتِهِ وَ بُرُودَتِهِ حَارٌّ فِي مَكَانِ الْحَرَارَةِ وَ بَارِدٌ فِي مَكَانِ الْبُرُودَةِ .
citation.translation: Al Husayn Bin Muhammad, from Moalla Bin Muhammad, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, and Abdullah Bin Al Qasim, from Abdul Rahman Al Hashimy who said, ‘He<sup>asws</sup> said to one of his slaves: ‘Be (buy) less for us<sup>asws</sup> from the onions, and more for us<sup>asws</sup> from the aubergines’. So he said to him<sup>asws</sup> for his understanding, ‘The aubergines?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Yes, the aubergines, in all its tastes is beneficial for the illnesses, corrective for the health, balanced in its states, corrective for the old man and the youth, being moderate in its heat and its coolness, being hot in hot places and cool in cold places’.

text: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Abdullah Bin Ali Bin Aamir, from Ibrahim Bin Al Fazl, from Ja’far Bin Yahya, from his father, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Eat the aubergine for it removes the illness and there is no disease in it’.

citation.arabic_text: كُلُوا الْبَاذَنْجَانَ فَإِنَّهُ يُذْهِبُ الدَّاءَ وَ لَا دَاءَ لَهُ .
citation.translation: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Abdullah Bin Ali Bin Aamir, from Ibrahim Bin Al Fazl, from Ja’far Bin Yahya, from his father, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Eat the aubergine for it removes the illness and there is no disease in it’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: مجهول - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (22/219)

text: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from one of our companions who said, ‘Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> the 3rd said to one of his<sup>asws</sup> workers: ‘Frequent for us from the aubergines, for it is hot during the time of heat, and cool in the times of coldness, being moderate in all of the times, good upon every state’.

citation.arabic_text: قَالَ أَبُو الْحَسَنِ الثَّالِثِ ( عليه السلام ) لِبَعْضِ قَهَارِمَتِهِ اسْتَكْثِرُوا لَنَا مِنَ الْبَاذَنْجَانِ فَإِنَّهُ حَارٌّ فِي وَقْتِ الْحَرَارَةِ وَ بَارِدٌ فِي وَقْتِ الْبُرُودَةِ مُعْتَدِلٌ فِي الْأَوْقَاتِ كُلِّهَا جَيِّدٌ عَلَى كُلِّ حَالٍ.
citation.translation: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from one of our companions who said, ‘Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> the 3rd said to one of his<sup>asws</sup> workers: ‘Frequent for us from the aubergines, for it is hot during the time of heat, and cool in the times of coldness, being moderate in all of the times, good upon every state’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: ضعيف على المشهور - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (2/219)

text: Al Husayn Bin Muhammad, from Moalla Bin Muhammad, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, and Abdullah Bin Al Qasim, from Abdul Rahman Al Hashimy who said, ‘He<sup>asws</sup> said to one of his slaves: ‘Be (buy) less for us<sup>asws</sup> from the onions, and more for us<sup>asws</sup> from the aubergines’. So he said to him<sup>asws</sup> for his understanding, ‘The aubergines?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Yes, the aubergines, in all its tastes is beneficial for the illnesses, corrective for the health, balanced in its states, corrective for the old man and the youth, being moderate in its heat and its coolness, being hot in hot places and cool in cold places’.

citation.arabic_text: قَالَ لِبَعْضِ مَوَالِيهِ أَقْلِلْ لَنَا مِنَ الْبَصَلِ وَ أَكْثِرْ لَنَا مِنَ الْبَاذَنْجَانِ فَقَالَ لَهُ مُسْتَفْهِماً الْبَاذَنْجَانِ قَالَ نَعَمْ الْبَاذَنْجَانُ جَامِعُ الطَّعْمِ مَنْفِيُّ الدَّاءِ صَالِحٌ لِلطَّبِيعَةِ مُنْصِفٌ فِي أَحْوَالِهِ صَالِحٌ لِلشَّيْخِ وَ الشَّابِّ مُعْتَدِلٌ فِي حَرَارَتِهِ وَ بُرُودَتِهِ حَارٌّ فِي مَكَانِ الْحَرَارَةِ وَ بَارِدٌ فِي مَكَانِ الْبُرُودَةِ .
citation.translation: Al Husayn Bin Muhammad, from Moalla Bin Muhammad, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, and Abdullah Bin Al Qasim, from Abdul Rahman Al Hashimy who said, ‘He<sup>asws</sup> said to one of his slaves: ‘Be (buy) less for us<sup>asws</sup> from the onions, and more for us<sup>asws</sup> from the aubergines’. So he said to him<sup>asws</sup> for his understanding, ‘The aubergines?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Yes, the aubergines, in all its tastes is beneficial for the illnesses, corrective for the health, balanced in its states, corrective for the old man and the youth, being moderate in its heat and its coolness, being hot in hot places and cool in cold places’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: ضعيف على المشهور - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (22/220)

text: From him, from Al Sayyari, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Khalid, from Ahmad Bin Al Mubarak Al Deynaoury, from Abu Usman, from Dorost, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said; ‘The onion aromatises the breath, and strengthens the back, and softens the skin’.

citation.arabic_text: عَنْهُ عَنِ السَّيَّارِيِّ عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ خَالِدٍ عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ الْمُبَارَكِ الدِّينَوَرِيِّ عَنْ أَبِي عُثْمَانَ عَنْ دُرُسْتَ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) قَالَ الْبَصَلُ يُطَيِّبُ النَّكْهَةَ وَ يَشُدُّ الظَّهْرَ وَ يُرِقُّ الْبَشَرَةَ .
citation.translation: From him, from Al Sayyari, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Khalid, from Ahmad Bin Al Mubarak Al Deynaoury, from Abu Usman, from Dorost, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said; ‘The onion aromatises the breath, and strengthens the back, and softens the skin’.

text: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Khalid, from Muhammad Bin Ali, from Abdul Rahman Bin Zayd Bin Aslam, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘When you enter a city, so eat from its onions, it would dispel from you its plague’.

citation.arabic_text: عِدَّةٌ مِنْ أَصْحَابِنَا عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ خَالِدٍ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عَلِيٍّ عَنْ عَبْدِ الرَّحْمَنِ بْنِ زَيْدِ بْنِ أَسْلَمَ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) قَالَ قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ ( صلى الله عليه وآله ) إِذَا دَخَلْتُمْ بِلَاداً فَكُلُوا مِنْ بَصَلِهَا يَطْرُدْ عَنْكُمْ وَبَاءَهَا .
citation.translation: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Khalid, from Muhammad Bin Ali, from Abdul Rahman Bin Zayd Bin Aslam, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘When you enter a city, so eat from its onions, it would dispel from you its plague’.

text: A number of our companions, from sahl Bin Ziyad, from Mansour Bin Al Abbas, from Abdul Aziz bin Hassan Al Baghdady, from Salih Bin Uqba, from Abdullah Bin Muhammad Al Ju’fy who said, ‘Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> mentioned the onions, so he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘It aromatises the breath, and does away with the phlegm, and increases in the copulation’.

citation.arabic_text: ذَكَرَ أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) الْبَصَلَ فَقَالَ يُطَيِّبُ النَّكْهَةَ وَ يَذْهَبُ بِالْبَلْغَمِ وَ يَزِيدُ فِي الْجِمَاعِ .
citation.translation: A number of our companions, from sahl Bin Ziyad, from Mansour Bin Al Abbas, from Abdul Aziz bin Hassan Al Baghdady, from Salih Bin Uqba, from Abdullah Bin Muhammad Al Ju’fy who said, ‘Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> mentioned the onions, so he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘It aromatises the breath, and does away with the phlegm, and increases in the copulation’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: ضعيف على المشهور - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (2/220)

text: Abu Ali Al Ashary, from Muhammad Bin Salim, from Ahmad Bin Al Nazar, from Amro Bin Shimr, from Jabir who said, ‘Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The onion removes the mental breakdown and strengthens the nerves, and increases in the walking ability, and increases in the water, and does away with the fever’.

citation.arabic_text: قَالَ أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) الْبَصَلُ يَذْهَبُ بِالنَّصَبِ وَ يَشُدُّ الْعَصَبَ وَ يَزِيدُ فِي الْخُطَى وَ يَزِيدُ فِي الْمَاءِ وَ يَذْهَبُ بِالْحُمَّى .
citation.translation: Abu Ali Al Ashary, from Muhammad Bin Salim, from Ahmad Bin Al Nazar, from Amro Bin Shimr, from Jabir who said, ‘Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The onion removes the mental breakdown and strengthens the nerves, and increases in the walking ability, and increases in the water, and does away with the fever’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: ضعيف - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (22/220)

text: Ali Bin Muhammad Bin Bundar, from his father, from Muhammad Bin Ali Al hamdany, from Al Hassan Bin Ali Al Kaslaan, from Maysar Baya’a the Zaty, and he was his maternal uncle who said, ‘I heard Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> saying: ‘Eat the onion for therein are three qualities – It aromatises the breath, and strengthens the gums, and increases in the water and the copulation’.

citation.arabic_text: سَمِعْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) يَقُولُ كُلُوا الْبَصَلَ فَإِنَّ فِيهِ ثَلَاثَ خِصَالٍ يُطَيِّبُ النَّكْهَةَ وَ يَشُدُّ اللِّثَةَ وَ يَزِيدُ فِي الْمَاءِ وَ الْجِمَاعِ .
citation.translation: Ali Bin Muhammad Bin Bundar, from his father, from Muhammad Bin Ali Al hamdany, from Al Hassan Bin Ali Al Kaslaan, from Maysar Baya’a the Zaty, and he was his maternal uncle who said, ‘I heard Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> saying: ‘Eat the onion for therein are three qualities – It aromatises the breath, and strengthens the gums, and increases in the water and the copulation’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: ضعيف - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (22/221)

text: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Umar Bin Azina, from Muhammad Bin Muslim, (It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup>, said, ‘I asked him<sup>asws</sup> about eating the garlic, so he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘But rather Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> forbade from it due to its smell, so he<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘The one who eats this bad vegetable, so he should not go near our Masjids. So as for the one who eats it and does not come to the Masjid, so there is no problem’.

citation.arabic_text: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنْ أَكْلِ الثُّومِ فَقَالَ إِنَّمَا نَهَى رَسُولُ اللَّهِ ( صلى الله عليه وآله ) عَنْهُ لِرِيحِهِ فَقَالَ مَنْ أَكَلَ هَذِهِ الْبَقْلَةَ الْخَبِيثَةَ فَلَا يَقْرَبْ مَسْجِدَنَا فَأَمَّا مَنْ أَكَلَهُ وَ لَمْ يَأْتِ الْمَسْجِدَ فَلَا بَأْسَ .
citation.translation: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Umar Bin Azina, from Muhammad Bin Muslim, (It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup>, said, ‘I asked him<sup>asws</sup> about eating the garlic, so he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘But rather Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> forbade from it due to its smell, so he<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘The one who eats this bad vegetable, so he should not go near our Masjids. So as for the one who eats it and does not come to the Masjid, so there is no problem’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: حسن - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (2/221)

text: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Al husayn Bin Saeed, from Hammad, from Shuayb, from Abu Baseer, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, said, ‘He<sup>asws</sup> was asked about eating the garlic, and the onion, and the leek, so he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘There is no problem in eating it remotely, and in the pots, and there is no problem in curing (illnesses) with the leek, but when one of you eats that (garlic), so he should not go out to the Masjid’.

citation.arabic_text: سُئِلَ عَنْ أَكْلِ الثُّومِ وَ الْبَصَلِ وَ الْكُرَّاثِ فَقَالَ لَا بَأْسَ بِأَكْلِهِ نِيّاً وَ فِي الْقُدُورِ وَ لَا بَأْسَ بِأَنْ يُتَدَاوَى بِالثُّومِ وَ لَكِنْ إِذَا أَكَلَ ذَلِكَ أَحَدُكُمْ فَلَا يَخْرُجْ إِلَى الْمَسْجِدِ .
citation.translation: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Al husayn Bin Saeed, from Hammad, from Shuayb, from Abu Baseer, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, said, ‘He<sup>asws</sup> was asked about eating the garlic, and the onion, and the leek, so he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘There is no problem in eating it remotely, and in the pots, and there is no problem in curing (illnesses) with the leek, but when one of you eats that (garlic), so he should not go out to the Masjid’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: صحيح - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (22/221)

text: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Khalid, from usman Bin Isa, from Abdullah Bin Muskan, from Al Hassan Al Zayyat who said, ‘When I had fulfilled my rituals, I passed by Al-Medina. So I asked about Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup>, and was told that he<sup>asws</sup> is at Al-Yanba’a. So I went to Yanba’a. So he<sup>asws</sup> said to me: ‘O Hassan! You have walked to over here?’ I said, ‘Yes, may I be sacrificed for you<sup>asws</sup>, as I disliked going out and I have not seen you<sup>asws</sup>’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘I<sup>asws</sup> ate from this vegetable, meaning the garlic, so I<sup>asws</sup> wanted to keep away from the Masjid of Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup>’.

citation.arabic_text: لَمَّا أَنْ قَضَيْتُ نُسُكِي مَرَرْتُ بِالْمَدِينَةِ فَسَأَلْتُ عَنْ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ ( عليه السلام ) فَقَالَ هُوَ بِيَنْبُعَ فَأَتَيْتُ يَنْبُعَ فَقَالَ لِي يَا حَسَنُ مَشَيْتَ إِلَى هَاهُنَا قُلْتُ نَعَمْ جُعِلْتُ فِدَاكَ كَرِهْتُ أَنْ أَخْرُجَ وَ لَا أَرَاكَ فَقَالَ ( عليه السلام ) إِنِّي أَكَلْتُ مِنْ هَذِهِ الْبَقْلَةِ يَعْنِي الثُّومَ فَأَرَدْتُ أَنْ أَتَنَحَّى عَنْ مَسْجِدِ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ ( صلى الله عليه وآله ) .

So I asked about Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup>, and was told that he<sup>asws</sup> is at Al-Yanba’a. So I went to Yanba’a. So he<sup>asws</sup> said to me: ‘O Hassan! You have walked to over here?’ I said, ‘Yes, may I be sacrificed for you<sup>asws</sup>, as I disliked going out and I have not seen you<sup>asws</sup>’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘I<sup>asws</sup> ate from this vegetable, meaning the garlic, so I<sup>asws</sup> wanted to keep away from the Masjid of Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup>’.

text: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Ziyad Al Qandy, (It has been narrated) from Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> the 1st having said: ‘The medicine of Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> was the thyme, and he<sup>asws</sup> was saying: ‘It comes to the stomach as velvet like the plush brocade’.

citation.arabic_text: كَانَ دَوَاءُ أَمِيرِ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ ( عليه السلام ) السَّعْتَرَ وَ كَانَ يَقُولُ إِنَّهُ يَصِيرُ لِلْمَعِدَةِ خَمْلًا كَخَمْلِ الْقَطِيفَةِ .
citation.translation: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Ziyad Al Qandy, (It has been narrated) from Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> the 1st having said: ‘The medicine of Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> was the thyme, and he<sup>asws</sup> was saying: ‘It comes to the stomach as velvet like the plush brocade’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: موثق - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (22/222)

text: From him, from Musa Bin Al Hassan, from Ali Bin Suleyman, from one of the middle-men, (It has been narrated) from Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup>, that he complained to him<sup>asws</sup> of moisture (acidity), so he<sup>asws</sup> ordered him that he should eat the thyme upon the empty stomach’.

citation.arabic_text: أَنَّهُ شَكَا إِلَيْهِ رُطُوبَةً فَأَمَرَهُ أَنْ يَسْتَفَّ السَّعْتَرَ عَلَى الرِّيقِ .
citation.translation: From him, from Musa Bin Al Hassan, from Ali Bin Suleyman, from one of the middle-men, (It has been narrated) from Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup>, that he complained to him<sup>asws</sup> of moisture (acidity), so he<sup>asws</sup> ordered him that he should eat the thyme upon the empty stomach’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: مجهول - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (22/222)

text: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Ibn Mahboub, from Wahab Bin Abd Rabbihi who said, ‘I saw Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> picking teeth, so I looked at him<sup>asws</sup>. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> used to pick teeth and he<sup>asws</sup> was of the aromatic mouth’.

citation.arabic_text: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَحْيَى عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنِ ابْنِ مَحْبُوبٍ عَنْ وَهْبِ بْنِ عَبْدِ رَبِّهِ قَالَ رَأَيْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) يَتَخَلَّلُ فَنَظَرْتُ إِلَيْهِ فَقَالَ إِنَّ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ ( صلى الله عليه وآله ) كَانَ يَتَخَلَّلُ وَ هُوَ يُطَيِّبُ الْفَمَ .

citation.translation: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Al Nowfaly, from Al Sakuny, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> forbade picking teeth with the reed and the basil stem’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: ضعيف على المشهور - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (2/224)

text: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Abu Abdullah, from Muhammad Bin Isa, from Al Dahqan, from Dorost, from Abdullah Bin Sinan, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘The Prophet<sup>saww</sup> used to pick teeth with everything he<sup>saww</sup> came across except for the palm leaves and the reeds’.

citation.arabic_text: كَانَ النَّبِيُّ ( صلى الله عليه وآله ) يَتَخَلَّلُ بِكُلِّ مَا أَصَابَ مَا خَلَا الْخُوصَ وَ الْقَصَبَ .
citation.translation: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Abu Abdullah, from Muhammad Bin Isa, from Al Dahqan, from Dorost, from Abdullah Bin Sinan, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘The Prophet<sup>saww</sup> used to pick teeth with everything he<sup>saww</sup> came across except for the palm leaves and the reeds’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: ضعيف - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (22/224)

text: From him, from the one who reported it, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> forbade from picking teeth with the pomegranate (stem) and the myrtle (leaf), and the reeds, and said: ‘These stir the vein of the ulcers’.

citation.arabic_text: نَهَى رَسُولُ اللَّهِ ( صلى الله عليه وآله ) عَنِ التَّخَلُّلِ بِالرُّمَّانِ وَ الْآسِ وَ الْقَصَبِ وَ قَالَ ( صلى الله عليه وآله ) إِنَّهُنَّ يُحَرِّكْنَ عِرْقَ الْآكِلَةِ .
citation.translation: From him, from the one who reported it, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> forbade from picking teeth with the pomegranate (stem) and the myrtle (leaf), and the reeds, and said: ‘These stir the vein of the ulcers’.

text: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Khalid, from Usman Bin Isa, from Is’haq Bin Jareer who said, ‘I asked Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> about the meat which happens (to be stuck) in the teeth. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘As for what is in the front of the mouth, so swallow it, and whatever was in the molars, so toss it’.

citation.arabic_text: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) عَنِ اللَّحْمِ الَّذِي يَكُونُ فِي الْأَسْنَانِ فَقَالَ أَمَّا مَا كَانَ فِي مُقَدَّمِ الْفَمِ فَكُلْهُ وَ مَا كَانَ فِي الْأَضْرَاسِ فَاطْرَحْهُ .
citation.translation: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Khalid, from Usman Bin Isa, from Is’haq Bin Jareer who said, ‘I asked Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> about the meat which happens (to be stuck) in the teeth. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘As for what is in the front of the mouth, so swallow it, and whatever was in the molars, so toss it’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: موثق - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (2/225)

text: From him, from Ibn Mahboub, from Ibn Sinana, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘As for what happens to be upon the gums, so swallow it and gobble it, and whatever was in between the teeth, so throw it’.

citation.arabic_text: أَمَّا مَا يَكُونُ عَلَى اللِّثَةِ فَكُلْهُ وَ ازْدَرِدْهُ وَ مَا كَانَ بَيْنَ الْأَسْنَانِ فَارْمِ بِهِ .
citation.translation: From him, from Ibn Mahboub, from Ibn Sinana, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘As for what happens to be upon the gums, so swallow it and gobble it, and whatever was in between the teeth, so throw it’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: صحيح - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (2/225)

text: From him, from his father, from Abdullah Bin Al Fazl Al Nowfaly, from Al Fazl Bin Yunus who said, ‘Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> had lunch with me. So when he<sup>asws</sup> was free from the meal, they came with the toothpicks. So I said, ‘May I be sacrificed for you<sup>asws</sup>! What is a limit of this toothpick?’ So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘O Fazl! Eat what remains in your mouth. So whatever your tongue can get around to, so eat it, and whatever is settled, so extract it with the tooth pick. So you are in the choice with regards to it, if you so desire to, eat, and if you so desire to, toss it’.

citation.arabic_text: تَغَدَّى عِنْدِي أَبُو الْحَسَنِ ( عليه السلام ) فَلَمَّا فَرَغَ مِنَ الطَّعَامِ أُتِيَ بِالْخِلَالِ فَقُلْتُ جُعِلْتُ فِدَاكَ مَا حَدُّ هَذَا الْخِلَالِ فَقَالَ يَا فَضْلُ كُلُّ مَا بَقِيَ فِي فَمِكَ فَمَا أَدَرْتَ عَلَيْهِ لِسَانَكَ فَكُلْهُ وَ مَا اسْتَكَنَّ فَأَخْرِجْهُ بِالْخِلَالِ فَأَنْتَ فِيهِ بِالْخِيَارِ إِنْ شِئْتَ أَكَلْتَهُ وَ إِنْ شِئْتَ طَرَحْتَهُ .
citation.translation: From him, from his father, from Abdullah Bin Al Fazl Al Nowfaly, from Al Fazl Bin Yunus who said, ‘Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> had lunch with me. So when he<sup>asws</sup> was free from the meal, they came with the toothpicks. So I said, ‘May I be sacrificed for you<sup>asws</sup>! What is a limit of this toothpick?’ So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘O Fazl! Eat what remains in your mouth. So whatever your tongue can get around to, so eat it, and whatever is settled, so extract it with the tooth pick. So you are in the choice with regards to it, if you so desire to, eat, and if you so desire to, toss it’.

text: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, (It has been narrated) raising it to Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Not one of you should swallow what he picks teeth with, for the pus can happen from it’.

citation.arabic_text: قَالَ لَا يَزْدَرِدَنَّ أَحَدُكُمْ مَا يَتَخَلَّلُ بِهِ فَإِنَّهُ يَكُونُ مِنْهُ الدُّبَيْلَةُ .
citation.translation: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, (It has been narrated) raising it to Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Not one of you should swallow what he picks teeth with, for the pus can happen from it’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: مرفوع - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (2/225)

text: From him, from Ibn Mahboub, from Abu Wallad who said, ‘I saw Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> the 1<sup>st</sup> in Al Hijr (at the Kabah), and he<sup>asws</sup> was seated, and with him<sup>asws</sup> were a number of his<sup>asws</sup> family members, so I hear him<sup>asws</sup> saying: ‘My teeth hurt, so I took the cyperus and rubbed it down by my teeth, and that benefitted me, and settled down from it’.

citation.arabic_text: عَنْهُ عَنِ ابْنِ مَحْبُوبٍ عَنْ أَبِي وَلَّادٍ قَالَ رَأَيْتُ أَبَا الْحَسَنِ الْأَوَّلَ ( عليه السلام ) فِي الْحِجْرِ وَ هُوَ قَاعِدٌ وَ مَعَهُ عِدَّةٌ مِنْ أَهْلِ بَيْتِهِ فَسَمِعْتُهُ يَقُولُ ضُرِبَتْ عَلَيَّ أَسْنَانِي فَأَخَذْتُ السُّعْدَ فَدَلَكْتُ بِهِ أَسْنَانِي فَنَفَعَنِي ذَلِكَ وَ سَكَنَتْ عَنِّي .
citation.translation: From him, from Ibn Mahboub, from Abu Wallad who said, ‘I saw Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> the 1<sup>st</sup> in Al Hijr (at the Kabah), and he<sup>asws</sup> was seated, and with him<sup>asws</sup> were a number of his<sup>asws</sup> family members, so I hear him<sup>asws</sup> saying: ‘My teeth hurt, so I took the cyperus and rubbed it down by my teeth, and that benefitted me, and settled down from it’.

text: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Al Husayn Bin Saeed, from Ahmad Bin Yazeed, (It has been narrated) from Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> the 1st having said: ‘Eating the saltwort disinfects the mouth’.

citation.arabic_text: أَكْلُ الْأُشْنَانِ يُبْخِرُ الْفَمَ .
citation.translation: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Al Husayn Bin Saeed, from Ahmad Bin Yazeed, (It has been narrated) from Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> the 1st having said: ‘Eating the saltwort disinfects the mouth’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: مجهول - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (2/226)

text: One of our companions, from Ja’far Bin Ibrahim Al Hazramy, from Sa’ad who said, ‘I said to Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup>, ‘I eat the saltwort’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup>, when he<sup>asws</sup> performed ablution (with saltwort), closed his<sup>asws</sup> lips, and in it is an abhorrent quality, it inherits the tuberculosis, and does away with the water of the back, and weakens the knees’. So I said, ‘So (what about) the clay?’ So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Every clay is Prohibited (to eat), like the dead, and the blood, and the flesh of the swine, except for the clay of the grave of Al-Husayn<sup>asws</sup>, for therein is a healing from every illness, but do not frequent from it, and in it is a security from every fear’.

citation.arabic_text: قُلْتُ لِأَبِي الْحَسَنِ ( عليه السلام ) إِنَّا نَأْكُلُ الْأُشْنَانَ فَقَالَ كَانَ أَبُو الْحَسَنِ ( عليه السلام ) إِذَا تَوَضَّأَ ضَمَّ شَفَتَيْهِ وَ فِيهِ خِصَالٌ تُكْرَهُ إِنَّهُ يُورِثُ السِّلَّ وَ يَذْهَبُ بِمَاءِ الظَّهْرِ وَ يُوهِي الرُّكْبَتَيْنِ فَقُلْتُ فَالطِّينُ فَقَالَ كُلُّ طِينٍ حَرَامٌ مِثْلُ الْمَيْتَةِ وَ الدَّمِ وَ لَحْمِ الْخِنْزِيرِ إِلَّا طِينَ قَبْرِ الْحُسَيْنِ ( عليه السلام ) فَإِنَّ فِيهِ شِفَاءً مِنْ كُلِّ دَاءٍ وَ لَكِنْ لَا يُكْثَرُ مِنْهُ وَ فِيهِ أَمَانٌ مِنْ كُلِّ خَوْفٍ .
citation.translation: One of our companions, from Ja’far Bin Ibrahim Al Hazramy, from Sa’ad who said, ‘I said to Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup>, ‘I eat the saltwort’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup>, when he<sup>asws</sup> performed ablution (with saltwort), closed his<sup>asws</sup> lips, and in it is an abhorrent quality, it inherits the tuberculosis, and does away with the water of the back, and weakens the knees’. So I said, ‘So (what about) the clay?’ So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Every clay is Prohibited (to eat), like the dead, and the blood, and the flesh of the swine, except for the clay of the grave of Al-Husayn<sup>asws</sup>, for therein is a healing from every illness, but do not frequent from it, and in it is a security from every fear’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: مجهول - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (22/226)

text: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ali Bin Al Hassan Bin Ali, from Ahmad Bin Al Husayn Bin Umar, from his uncle Muhammad Bin Umar, from a man, (It has been narrated) from Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> the 1st having said: ‘The one who cleans himself with the cyperus after defecation, and washes his mouth with it after the food would not be hit by an illness in his mouth, and would not fear anything from the winds of hemorrhoids’.

citation.arabic_text: مَنِ اسْتَنْجَى بِالسُّعْدِ بَعْدَ الْغَائِطِ وَ غَسَلَ بِهِ فَمَهُ بَعْدَ الطَّعَامِ لَمْ تُصِبْهُ عِلَّةٌ فِي فَمِهِ وَ لَمْ يَخَفْ شَيْئاً مِنْ أَرْيَاحِ الْبَوَاسِيرِ .
citation.translation: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ali Bin Al Hassan Bin Ali, from Ahmad Bin Al Husayn Bin Umar, from his uncle Muhammad Bin Umar, from a man, (It has been narrated) from Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> the 1st having said: ‘The one who cleans himself with the cyperus after defecation, and washes his mouth with it after the food would not be hit by an illness in his mouth, and would not fear anything from the winds of hemorrhoids’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: مجهول - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (2/226)

text: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Abdu Abdullah, from Abu Al Khazraj Al Hassan Bin Al Zabarqan Al Ansary, from Al Fazl Bin Usman, from Abu Aziz Al Murady who said, and he is a maternal uncle of my mother, ‘I heard Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> saying: ‘Take the cyperus to be in your teeth for it aromatises the mouth, and increases in the copulations’.

citation.arabic_text: وَ هُوَ خَالُ أُمِّي قَالَ سَمِعْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) يَقُولُ اتَّخِذُوا فِي أَسْنَانِكُمُ السُّعْدَ فَإِنَّهُ يُطَيِّبُ الْفَمَ وَ يَزِيدُ فِي الْجِمَاعِ .
citation.translation: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Abdu Abdullah, from Abu Al Khazraj Al Hassan Bin Al Zabarqan Al Ansary, from Al Fazl Bin Usman, from Abu Aziz Al Murady who said, and he is a maternal uncle of my mother, ‘I heard Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> saying: ‘Take the cyperus to be in your teeth for it aromatises the mouth, and increases in the copulations’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: مجهول - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (2/226)

text: : أَخَذَنِي الْعَبَّاسُ بْنُ مُوسَى فَأَمَرَ فَوُجِئَ فَمِي «1» فَتَزَعْزَعَتْ أَسْنَانِي فَلَا أَقْدِرُ أَنْ أَمْضَغَ الطَّعَامَ فَرَأَيْتُ أَبِي فِي الْمَنَامِ وَ مَعَهُ شَيْخٌ لَا أَعْرِفُهُ فَقَالَ أَبِي رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ سَلِّمْ عَلَيْهِ فَقُلْتُ يَا أَبَهْ مَنْ هُوَ فَقَالَ هَذَا أَبُو شَيْبَةَ الْخُرَاسَانِيُّ «2» قَالَ فَسَلَّمْتُ عَلَيْهِ فَقَالَ مَا لِي أَرَاكَ هَكَذَا قَالَ قُلْتُ إِنَّ الْفَاسِقَ الْعَبَّاسَ بْنَ مُوسَى أَمَرَنِي فَوُجِئَ فَمِي فَتَزَعْزَعَتْ أَسْنَانِي فَقَالَ لِي شُدَّهَا بِالسُّعْدِ فَأَصْبَحْتُ فَتَمَضْمَضْتُ بِالسُّعْدِ فَسَكَنَتْ أَسْنَانِي.

text: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Bakr Bin Salih, from Isa Bin Abdullah Bin Muhammad Bin Umar Bin Ali, from his father, from his grandfather who said, ‘Amir Al-Momineenasws said: ‘الْمَاءُ سَيِّدُ الشَّرَابِ’ The water is the chief of the drinks, in the world and the Hereafter’. A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Abu Abdullah Al Barqy, from Muhammad Bin Ali, from Isa Bin Abdullah, by his chain – similar to it.

citation.arabic_text: قَالَ أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ ( صلوات الله عليه ) الْمَاءُ سَيِّدُ الشَّرَابِ فِي الدُّنْيَا وَ الْآخِرَةِ . عِدَّةٌ مِنْ أَصْحَابِنَا عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ الْبَرْقِيِّ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عَلِيٍّ عَنْ عِيسَى بْنِ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ بِإِسْنَادِهِ مِثْلَهُ .
citation.translation: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Bakr Bin Salih, from Isa Bin Abdullah Bin Muhammad Bin Umar Bin Ali, from his father, from his grandfather who said, ‘Amir Al-Momineenasws said: ‘الْمَاءُ سَيِّدُ الشَّرَابِ’ The water is the chief of the drinks, in the world and the Hereafter’. A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Abu Abdullah Al Barqy, from Muhammad Bin Ali, from Isa Bin Abdullah, by his chain – similar to it.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: ضعيف - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (2/229)

text: Abu Ali Al Ashary, from Muhammad Bin Abdul Jabbar and Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, altogether from Ibn Fazal, from Sa’alba Bin Maymoun, from Ubeyd Bin Zurara who said, ‘I heard Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> saying, and he<sup>asws</sup> mentioned Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup>, so he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘O Allah<sup>azwj</sup>! You<sup>azwj</sup> Know that he<sup>saww</sup> is more beloved to us<sup>asws</sup> than the fathers and the mothers, and ‘الْمَاءِ الْبَارِدِ’ the cold water’.

citation.arabic_text: سَمِعْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) يَقُولُ وَ ذَكَرَ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ ( صلى الله عليه وآله ) فَقَالَ اللَّهُمَّ إِنَّكَ تَعْلَمُ أَنَّهُ أَحَبُّ إِلَيْنَا مِنَ الْآبَاءِ وَ الْأُمَّهَاتِ وَ الْمَاءِ الْبَارِدِ .
citation.translation: Abu Ali Al Ashary, from Muhammad Bin Abdul Jabbar and Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, altogether from Ibn Fazal, from Sa’alba Bin Maymoun, from Ubeyd Bin Zurara who said, ‘I heard Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> saying, and he<sup>asws</sup> mentioned Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup>, so he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘O Allah<sup>azwj</sup>! You<sup>azwj</sup> Know that he<sup>saww</sup> is more beloved to us<sup>asws</sup> than the fathers and the mothers, and ‘الْمَاءِ الْبَارِدِ’ the cold water’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: موثق - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (2/229)

text: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from someone else, from Al Abbas Bin Marouf, from Sa’dan Bin Muslim, from Abul Rahman Bin Al Hajjaj, Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> has said: ‘The first of what Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, would Question the servant is that He<sup>azwj</sup> would be Saying to him: “Did I<sup>azwj</sup> not Quench you from the fresh waters of the Euphrates?”’.

citation.arabic_text: أَوَّلُ مَا يَسْأَلُ اللَّهُ جَلَّ ذِكْرُهُ الْعَبْدَ أَنْ يَقُولَ لَهُ أَ وَ لَمْ أُرْوِكَ مِنْ عَذْبِ الْفُرَاتِ .
citation.translation: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from someone else, from Al Abbas Bin Marouf, from Sa’dan Bin Muslim, from Abul Rahman Bin Al Hajjaj, Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> has said: ‘The first of what Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, would Question the servant is that He<sup>azwj</sup> would be Saying to him: “Did I<sup>azwj</sup> not Quench you from the fresh waters of the Euphrates?”’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: مجهول - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (22/229)

text: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Abu Abdullah, from Ali Bin Al Rayyan Bin Al Salt, raising it, said, ‘Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘The chief of the drink of the Paradise, is the water’.

citation.arabic_text: قَالَ أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ ( صلى الله عليه وآله ) سَيِّدُ شَرَابِ الْجَنَّةِ الْمَاءُ .
citation.translation: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Abu Abdullah, from Ali Bin Al Rayyan Bin Al Salt, raising it, said, ‘Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘The chief of the drink of the Paradise, is the water’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: مرفوع - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (22/229)

text: From him, from Muhammad Bin Ali, from Isa Bin Abdullah Bin Muhammad Bin Umar Bin Ali, from his father, from his grandfather who said, ‘Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The water is the chief of the drinks in the world and the Hereafter’.

citation.arabic_text: قَالَ أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ ( عليه السلام ) الْمَاءُ سَيِّدُ الشَّرَابِ فِي الدُّنْيَا وَ الْآخِرَةِ .
citation.translation: From him, from Muhammad Bin Ali, from Isa Bin Abdullah Bin Muhammad Bin Umar Bin Ali, from his father, from his grandfather who said, ‘Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The water is the chief of the drinks in the world and the Hereafter’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: ضعيف - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (2/229)

text: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Muhammad Bin Ahmad, from Yaqoub Bin Yazeed, from Ibn Fazzal, from the one who informed him, Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> has said: ‘The one who enjoys with the water in the world, Allah<sup>azwj</sup> would Make him enjoy from the drinks of the Paradise’.

citation.arabic_text: مَنْ تَلَذَّذَ بِالْمَاءِ فِي الدُّنْيَا لَذَّذَهُ اللَّهُ عَزَّ وَ جَلَّ مِنْ أَشْرِبَةِ الْجَنَّةِ .
citation.translation: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Muhammad Bin Ahmad, from Yaqoub Bin Yazeed, from Ibn Fazzal, from the one who informed him, Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> has said: ‘The one who enjoys with the water in the world, Allah<sup>azwj</sup> would Make him enjoy from the drinks of the Paradise’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: مرسل - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (2/229)

text: Ahmad Bin Muhammad Al Kufy, from Ali Bin Al Hassan Maysami, from Ali Bin Asbaat, from Abdul Samad Bin Bundar, from Al Husayn Bin Alwan who said, ‘A man asked Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> about the taste of water, so he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Ask to understand it and do not ask to irritate. The taste of water is the taste of life’.

citation.arabic_text: سَأَلَ رَجُلٌ أَبَا عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) عَنْ طَعْمِ الْمَاءِ فَقَالَ سَلْ تَفَقُّهاً وَ لَا تَسْأَلْ تَعَنُّتاً طَعْمُ الْمَاءِ طَعْمُ الْحَيَاةِ .
citation.translation: Ahmad Bin Muhammad Al Kufy, from Ali Bin Al Hassan Maysami, from Ali Bin Asbaat, from Abdul Samad Bin Bundar, from Al Husayn Bin Alwan who said, ‘A man asked Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> about the taste of water, so he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Ask to understand it and do not ask to irritate. The taste of water is the taste of life’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: مجهول - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (22/229)

text: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Ja’far Bin Muhammad Al Ashary, from Ibn Al Qaddah, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘Sip the water with a sipping and do not gulp it down with a gulping, for you would find the liver (trouble) from it’.

citation.arabic_text: قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ ( صلى الله عليه وآله ) مَصُّوا الْمَاءَ مَصّاً وَ لَا تَعُبُّوهُ عَبّاً فَإِنَّهُ يُوجَدُ مِنْهُ الْكُبَادُ .
citation.translation: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Ja’far Bin Muhammad Al Ashary, from Ibn Al Qaddah, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘Sip the water with a sipping and do not gulp it down with a gulping, for you would find the liver (trouble) from it’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: ضعيف على المشهور - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (22/230)

text: Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Muhammad Bin Al Hassan Bin Shamoun Al Basry, from Abu Tayfour Al Mutattab who said, ‘I went over to Abu Al-Hassan Al-Maazy<sup>asws</sup> (7th Imam<sup>asws</sup>), so I said something negative about drinking the water, so he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘And what is the problem with the water and it revolves the food in the stomach, and it settles the anger, and increases in the understanding ability, and extinguishes the bitterness’.

citation.arabic_text: دَخَلْتُ عَلَى أَبِي الْحَسَنِ الْمَاضِي ( عليه السلام ) فَنَهَيْتُهُ عَنْ شُرْبِ الْمَاءِ فَقَالَ ( عليه السلام ) وَ مَا بَأْسٌ بِالْمَاءِ وَ هُوَ يُدِيرُ الطَّعَامَ فِي الْمَعِدَةِ وَ يُسَكِّنُ الْغَضَبَ وَ يَزِيدُ فِي اللُّبِّ وَ يُطْفِئُ الْمِرَارَ .
citation.translation: Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Muhammad Bin Al Hassan Bin Shamoun Al Basry, from Abu Tayfour Al Mutattab who said, ‘I went over to Abu Al-Hassan Al-Maazy<sup>asws</sup> (7th Imam<sup>asws</sup>), so I said something negative about drinking the water, so he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘And what is the problem with the water and it revolves the food in the stomach, and it settles the anger, and increases in the understanding ability, and extinguishes the bitterness’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: ضعيف على المشهور - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (22/230)

text: Al Husayn Bin Muhammad, from Moala Bin Muhammad Al Basry, from Abu Dawood Al Mustaraq, from the one who narrated it who said, ‘I was in the presence of Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, so he<sup>asws</sup> called for the dates. So he<sup>asws</sup> ate and went on to drink water over it. So I said, ‘May I be sacrificed for you<sup>asws</sup>! If you could wait from the water’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘But rather, I<sup>asws</sup> eat the dates in order to aromatise the water over it’.

citation.arabic_text: كُنْتُ عِنْدَ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) فَدَعَا بِتَمْرٍ فَأَكَلَ وَ أَقْبَلَ يَشْرَبُ عَلَيْهِ الْمَاءَ فَقُلْتُ لَهُ جُعِلْتُ فِدَاكَ لَوْ أَمْسَكْتَ عَنِ الْمَاءِ فَقَالَ إِنَّمَا آكُلُ التَّمْرَ لِأَسْتَطِيبَ عَلَيْهِ الْمَاءَ.
citation.translation: Al Husayn Bin Muhammad, from Moala Bin Muhammad Al Basry, from Abu Dawood Al Mustaraq, from the one who narrated it who said, ‘I was in the presence of Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, so he<sup>asws</sup> called for the dates. So he<sup>asws</sup> ate and went on to drink water over it. So I said, ‘May I be sacrificed for you<sup>asws</sup>! If you could wait from the water’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘But rather, I<sup>asws</sup> eat the dates in order to aromatise the water over it’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: ضعيف على المشهور - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (2/230)

text: Ali Bin Muhammad, from one of his companions, from Yasser who said, ‘Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘I<sup>asws</sup> wonder at the one who eats the like of that’ – and he<sup>asws</sup> gestured by his<sup>asws</sup> hand (eats a lot) – ‘and he does not drink water over it, how come his stomach does not burst’.

citation.arabic_text: قَالَ أَبُو الْحَسَنِ ( عليه السلام ) عَجَباً لِمَنْ أَكَلَ مِثْلَ ذَا وَ أَشَارَ بِيَدِهِ وَ لَمْ يَشْرَبْ عَلَيْهِ الْمَاءَ كَيْفَ لَا تَنْشَقُّ مَعِدَتُهُ .
citation.translation: Ali Bin Muhammad, from one of his companions, from Yasser who said, ‘Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘I<sup>asws</sup> wonder at the one who eats the like of that’ – and he<sup>asws</sup> gestured by his<sup>asws</sup> hand (eats a lot) – ‘and he does not drink water over it, how come his stomach does not burst’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: مرسل - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (22/230)

text: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hisham Bin Al Hakam who said, ‘Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Drinking the cold water is abundant enjoyment’.

citation.arabic_text: قَالَ أَبُو الْحَسَنِ ( عليه السلام ) إِنَّ شُرْبَ الْمَاءِ الْبَارِدِ أَكْثَرُ تَلَذُّذاً .
citation.translation: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hisham Bin Al Hakam who said, ‘Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Drinking the cold water is abundant enjoyment’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: حسن - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (2/231)

text: A number or our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Saeed Bin Janah Bin Umar Al Halby who said, ‘Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said, and he<sup>asws</sup> was advising a man saying to him: ‘Reduce from drinking the water, for it extends every illness, and avoid the medication for as long as your body can bear the illness’.

citation.arabic_text: قَالَ أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) وَ هُوَ يُوصِي رَجُلًا فَقَالَ لَهُ أَقْلِلْ مِنْ شُرْبِ الْمَاءِ فَإِنَّهُ يَمُدُّ كُلَّ دَاءٍ وَ اجْتَنِبِ الدَّوَاءَ مَا احْتَمَلَ بَدَنُكَ الدَّاءَ .
citation.translation: A number or our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Saeed Bin Janah Bin Umar Al Halby who said, ‘Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said, and he<sup>asws</sup> was advising a man saying to him: ‘Reduce from drinking the water, for it extends every illness, and avoid the medication for as long as your body can bear the illness’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: ضعيف على المشهور - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (22/231)

text: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Yasser the servant, Al-Reza<sup>asws</sup> has said: ‘There is no problem with drinking the water abundantly upon the meal, but do not frequent from it upon apart from it’. And he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Do you not see that if a man were to eat the likes of this’ – and he<sup>asws</sup> gathered his<sup>asws</sup> both of his<sup>asws</sup> hands such that he<sup>asws</sup> neither joined them nor separated them – ‘then he does not drink the water over it, his stomach could burst?’

citation.arabic_text: لَا بَأْسَ بِكَثْرَةِ شُرْبِ الْمَاءِ عَلَى الطَّعَامِ وَ لَا تُكْثِرْ مِنْهُ عَلَى غَيْرِهِ وَ قَالَ أَ رَأَيْتَ لَوْ أَنَّ رَجُلًا أَكَلَ مِثْلَ ذَا وَ جَمَعَ يَدَيْهِ كِلْتَيْهِمَا لَمْ يَضُمَّهُمَا وَ لَمْ يُفَرِّقْهُمَا ثُمَّ لَمْ يَشْرَبْ عَلَيْهِ الْمَاءَ كَانَ يَنْشَقُّ مَعِدَتُهُ .
citation.translation: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Yasser the servant, Al-Reza<sup>asws</sup> has said: ‘There is no problem with drinking the water abundantly upon the meal, but do not frequent from it upon apart from it’. And he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Do you not see that if a man were to eat the likes of this’ – and he<sup>asws</sup> gathered his<sup>asws</sup> both of his<sup>asws</sup> hands such that he<sup>asws</sup> neither joined them nor separated them – ‘then he does not drink the water over it, his stomach could burst?’
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: مجهول - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (22/231)

text: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Ali Bin Hassan, from Musa Bin Bakr, from one of our companions, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Do not frequent from drinking the water for it extends every illness’.

citation.arabic_text: لَا تُكْثِرْ مِنْ شُرْبِ الْمَاءِ فَإِنَّهُ مَادَّةٌ لِكُلِّ دَاءٍ .
citation.translation: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Ali Bin Hassan, from Musa Bin Bakr, from one of our companions, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Do not frequent from drinking the water for it extends every illness’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: ضعيف على المشهور - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (2/232)

text: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Al Nowfaly, from Al Sakuny, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Drinking the water whilst standing at daytime is strengthening and corrective for the body’.

citation.arabic_text: شُرْبُ الْمَاءِ مِنْ قِيَامٍ بِالنَّهَارِ أَقْوَى وَ أَصَحُّ لِلْبَدَنِ .
citation.translation: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Al Nowfaly, from Al Sakuny, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Drinking the water whilst standing at daytime is strengthening and corrective for the body’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: ضعيف على المشهور - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (22/232)

text: Ali Bin Muhammad, from Muhammad Bin Ahmad Bin Abu Mahmoud, (It has been narrated) raising it to Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Drinking the water whilst standing at daytime nourishes the food, and drinking the water whilst standing at night time inherits the yellow water’.

citation.arabic_text: شُرْبُ الْمَاءِ مِنْ قِيَامٍ بِالنَّهَارِ يُمْرِئُ الطَّعَامَ وَ شُرْبُ الْمَاءِ مِنْ قِيَامٍ بِاللَّيْلِ يُورِثُ الْمَاءَ الْأَصْفَرَ .
citation.translation: Ali Bin Muhammad, from Muhammad Bin Ahmad Bin Abu Mahmoud, (It has been narrated) raising it to Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Drinking the water whilst standing at daytime nourishes the food, and drinking the water whilst standing at night time inherits the yellow water’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: مرفوع - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (2/232)

text: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Muhammad Bin Ali, from Abdul Rahman Bin Abu Hashim, from Abu Hashim Bin Yahya Al Madainy, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> had a water container, so he<sup>asws</sup> drank from it and he<sup>asws</sup> was standing’.

citation.arabic_text: قَامَ أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ ( عليه السلام ) إِلَى إِدَاوَةٍ فَشَرِبَ مِنْهَا وَ هُوَ قَائِمٌ .
citation.translation: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Muhammad Bin Ali, from Abdul Rahman Bin Abu Hashim, from Abu Hashim Bin Yahya Al Madainy, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> had a water container, so he<sup>asws</sup> drank from it and he<sup>asws</sup> was standing’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: ضعيف - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (22/232)

text: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad Bin Ismail, from Al Fazl Bin Shazaan, altogether from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Abdul Rahman Bin Al Hajjaj who said, ‘I was in the presence of Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> when Abdul Malik Al-Qummy came over to him<sup>asws</sup>, so he said to him<sup>asws</sup>, ‘May Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Keep you well! Can I drink the water and I am standing?’ So he<sup>asws</sup> said to him: ‘If you so desire to’. He said, ‘Shall I drink in one breath until I am quenched?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘If you so desire to’. He said, ‘Supposing I were to prostrate and my hands were inside my clothes?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘If you so desire to’. Then Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘I<sup>asws</sup>, by Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, am not from this, and the likes of it. I<sup>asws</sup> fear over you’.

citation.arabic_text: كُنْتُ عِنْدَ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) إِذْ دَخَلَ عَلَيْهِ عَبْدُ الْمَلِكِ الْقُمِّيُّ فَقَالَ لَهُ أَصْلَحَكَ اللَّهُ أَشْرَبُ الْمَاءَ وَ أَنَا قَائِمٌ فَقَالَ لَهُ إِنْ شِئْتَ قَالَ أَ فَأَشْرَبُ بِنَفَسٍ وَاحِدٍ حَتَّى أَرْوَى قَالَ إِنْ شِئْتَ قَالَ فَأَسْجُدُ وَ يَدِي فِي ثَوْبِي قَالَ إِنْ شِئْتَ ثُمَّ قَالَ أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) إِنِّي وَ اللَّهِ مَا مِنْ هَذَا وَ شِبْهِهِ أَخَافُ عَلَيْكُمْ .
citation.translation: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad Bin Ismail, from Al Fazl Bin Shazaan, altogether from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Abdul Rahman Bin Al Hajjaj who said, ‘I was in the presence of Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> when Abdul Malik Al-Qummy came over to him<sup>asws</sup>, so he said to him<sup>asws</sup>, ‘May Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Keep you well! Can I drink the water and I am standing?’ So he<sup>asws</sup> said to him: ‘If you so desire to’. He said, ‘Shall I drink in one breath until I am quenched?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘If you so desire to’. He said, ‘Supposing I were to prostrate and my hands were inside my clothes?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘If you so desire to’. Then Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘I<sup>asws</sup>, by Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, am not from this, and the likes of it. I<sup>asws</sup> fear over you’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: حسن كالصحيح - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (2/232)

text: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Abu Abdullah, from his father, from his grandfather, from Abdullah Bin Al Mugheira, from Amro Bin Abu Al Miqdam who said, ‘I was in the presence of Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup>, I and my father, so they came to us with a clay vessel in which was water. So he<sup>asws</sup> drank standing, then gave it to my father. So he drank from it, and he was standing. Then he gave it to me, so I drank from it, and I was standing’.

citation.arabic_text: كُنْتُ عِنْدَ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ ( عليه السلام ) أَنَا وَ أَبِي فَأُتِيَ بِقَدَحٍ مِنْ خَزَفٍ فِيهِ مَاءٌ فَشَرِبَ وَ هُوَ قَائِمٌ ثُمَّ نَاوَلَهُ أَبِي فَشَرِبَ مِنْهُ وَ هُوَ قَائِمٌ ثُمَّ نَاوَلَنِيهِ فَشَرِبْتُ مِنْهُ وَ أَنَا قَائِمٌ .
citation.translation: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Abu Abdullah, from his father, from his grandfather, from Abdullah Bin Al Mugheira, from Amro Bin Abu Al Miqdam who said, ‘I was in the presence of Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup>, I and my father, so they came to us with a clay vessel in which was water. text: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Abu Abdullah, from Ibn Al Azramy, from Hatim Bin Ismail Al Madainy, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> that Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> drank the water and he<sup>asws</sup> was standing, then drank from the remainder of his<sup>asws</sup> ablution, standing. text: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al Halby, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Three breaths during the drink is better than one breath’.

citation.arabic_text: ثَلَاثَةُ أَنْفَاسٍ فِي الشُّرْبِ أَفْضَلُ مِنْ نَفَسٍ وَاحِدٍ .

text: Abu Ali Al Ashary, from Muhammad Bin Abdul Jabbar, from Safwan Bin Yahya, from Moala Abu Usman, from Moala Bin Khunays, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Three breaths are better than one breath (whilst drinking)’.

text: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from one of his companions, from Usman Bin Isa, from an old man from the people of Al Medina who said, ‘I asked Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> about the man who drinks the water, so he does not cut off his breath until he is quenched’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘And is the enjoyment except for that?’ I said, ‘But they (people) are saying that it is the drinking of the thirsty camel’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘They are lying! But rather the drinking of the thirsty camel is what the Name of Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic is not mentioned upon’.

citation.arabic_text: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) عَنِ الرَّجُلِ يَشْرَبُ الْمَاءَ فَلَا يَقْطَعُ نَفَسَهُ حَتَّى يَرْوَى قَالَ فَقَالَ ( عليه السلام ) وَ هَلِ اللَّذَّةُ إِلَّا ذَاكَ قُلْتُ فَإِنَّهُمْ يَقُولُونَ إِنَّهُ شُرْبُ الْهِيمِ قَالَ فَقَالَ كَذَبُوا إِنَّمَا شُرْبُ الْهِيمِ مَا لَمْ يُذْكَرِ اسْمُ اللَّهِ عَزَّ وَ جَلَّ عَلَيْهِ .
citation.translation: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from one of his companions, from Usman Bin Isa, from an old man from the people of Al Medina who said, ‘I asked Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> about the man who drinks the water, so he does not cut off his breath until he is quenched’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘And is the enjoyment except for that?’ I said, ‘But they (people) are saying that it is the drinking of the thirsty camel’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘They are lying! text: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Abdullah Bin Sinan who said, ‘I heard Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> saying that the man drinks the drink from the water, so Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic Enters him into the Paradise by it’. I said, ‘How is that, O son<sup>asws</sup> of Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup>?’ The man drinks the water, so he cuts it off, then takes pulls away the container although he desires it, so he Praises Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic. Then he repeats it, and he drinks, then he pulls it away although he desires it, so he Praises Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic, then returns to drinking it. Thus, Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic Obligates for him due to that, the Paradise’.

citation.arabic_text: سَمِعْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) يَقُولُ إِنَّ الرَّجُلَ يَشْرَبُ الشَّرْبَةَ مِنَ الْمَاءِ فَيُدْخِلُهُ اللَّهُ عَزَّ وَ جَلَّ بِهَا الْجَنَّةَ قُلْتُ وَ كَيْفَ ذَاكَ يَا ابْنَ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ قَالَ إِنَّ الرَّجُلَ يَشْرَبُ الْمَاءَ فَيَقْطَعُهُ ثُمَّ يُنَحِّي الْإِنَاءَ وَ هُوَ يَشْتَهِيهِ فَيَحْمَدُ اللَّهَ عَزَّ وَ جَلَّ ثُمَّ يَعُودُ فِيهِ وَ يَشْرَبُ ثُمَّ يُنَحِّيهِ وَ هُوَ يَشْتَهِيهِ فَيَحْمَدُ اللَّهَ عَزَّ وَ جَلَّ ثُمَّ يَعُودُ فَيَشْرَبُ فَيُوجِبُ اللَّهُ عَزَّ وَ جَلَّ لَهُ بِذَلِكَ الْجَنَّةَ .
citation.translation: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Abdullah Bin Sinan who said, ‘I heard Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> saying that the man drinks the drink from the water, so Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic Enters him into the Paradise by it’. I said, ‘How is that, O son<sup>asws</sup> of Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup>?’ The man drinks the water, so he cuts it off, then takes pulls away the container although he desires it, so he Praises Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic. Then he repeats it, and he drinks, then he pulls it away although he desires it, so he Praises Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic, then returns to drinking it. Thus, Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic Obligates for him due to that, the Paradise’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: صحيح - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (2/234)

text: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Ja’far Bin Muhammad Al Ashary, from Ibn Al Qaddah, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Whenever Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> drank the water, said: ‘The Praise is for Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Who Quenched us with sweet and fresh, and did not Quench us with salty, bitter, and did not Seize us for our sins’.

citation.arabic_text: كَانَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ ( صلى الله عليه وآله ) إِذَا شَرِبَ الْمَاءَ قَالَ الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ الَّذِي سَقَانَا عَذْباً زُلَالًا وَ لَمْ يَسْقِنَا مِلْحاً أُجَاجاً وَ لَمْ يُؤَاخِذْنَا بِذُنُوبِنَا .
citation.translation: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Ja’far Bin Muhammad Al Ashary, from Ibn Al Qaddah, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Whenever Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> drank the water, said: ‘The Praise is for Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Who Quenched us with sweet and fresh, and did not Quench us with salty, bitter, and did not Seize us for our sins’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: ضعيف على المشهور - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (2/234)

text: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Abu Abdullah, from Yaqoub Bin Yazeed, from a cousin of Umar Bin Yazeed, from a daughter of Umar Bin Yazeed, from her father, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Whenever one of you drinks the water, so he says, ‘بِسْمِ اللَّهِ’ ‘In the Name of Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, then drinks, then cuts it and says, ‘الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ’ ‘The Praise is for Allah<sup>azwj</sup>’, then drinks, so he says, بِسْمِ اللَّهِ ‘In the Name of Allah<sup>azwj</sup>’, then cuts it, so he says, الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ ‘The Praise is for Allah<sup>azwj</sup>’, then drinks, so he says, بِسْمِ اللَّهِ ‘In the Name of Allah<sup>azwj</sup>’, then cuts it and says, الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ ‘ The Praise is for Allah<sup>azwj</sup>’ – that water would Glorify for him for as long as it is in his belly up to the times it exits’.

citation.arabic_text: إِذَا شَرِبَ أَحَدُكُمُ الْمَاءَ فَقَالَ بِسْمِ اللَّهِ ثُمَّ شَرِبَ ثُمَّ قَطَعَهُ فَقَالَ الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ ثُمَّ شَرِبَ فَقَالَ بِسْمِ اللَّهِ ثُمَّ قَطَعَهُ فَقَالَ الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ ثُمَّ شَرِبَ فَقَالَ بِسْمِ اللَّهِ ثُمَّ قَطَعَهُ فَقَالَ الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ سَبَّحَ ذَلِكَ الْمَاءُ لَهُ مَا دَامَ فِي بَطْنِهِ إِلَى أَنْ يَخْرُجَ .
citation.translation: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Abu Abdullah, from Yaqoub Bin Yazeed, from a cousin of Umar Bin Yazeed, from a daughter of Umar Bin Yazeed, from her father, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Whenever one of you drinks the water, so he says, ‘بِسْمِ اللَّهِ’ ‘In the Name of Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, then drinks, then cuts it and says, ‘الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ’ ‘The Praise is for Allah<sup>azwj</sup>’, then drinks, so he says, بِسْمِ اللَّهِ ‘In the Name of Allah<sup>azwj</sup>’, then cuts it, so he says, الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ ‘The Praise is for Allah<sup>azwj</sup>’, then drinks, so he says, بِسْمِ اللَّهِ ‘In the Name of Allah<sup>azwj</sup>’, then cuts it and says, الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ ‘ The Praise is for Allah<sup>azwj</sup>’ – that water would Glorify for him for as long as it is in his belly up to the times it exits’.

text: Ali Bin Muhammad, raising it, said, ‘Abu Abdullahasws said: ‘Whenever you want to drink the water at night, so stir the water and say, ‘ O water’, water of Zamzam and water of Euphrates, I express greetings to both you’.

citation.arabic_text: قَالَ أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) إِذَا أَرَدْتَ أَنْ تَشْرَبَ الْمَاءَ بِاللَّيْلِ فَحَرِّكِ الْمَاءَ وَ قُلْ يَا مَاءُ مَاءُ زَمْزَمَ وَ مَاءُ فُرَاتٍ يُقْرِءَانِكَ السَّلَامَ .

text: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Ibrahim Al Karkhy, from Talha Bin Zayd, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> used to drink in the Syrian cup which they came with from Syria and was gifted unto him<sup>saww</sup>’.

citation.translation: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Ibrahim Al Karkhy, from Talha Bin Zayd, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> used to drink in the Syrian cup which they came with from Syria and was gifted unto him<sup>saww</sup>’.

citation.arabic_text: رَأَيْتُ أَبَا جَعْفَرٍ ( عليه السلام ) وَ هُوَ يَشْرَبُ فِي قَدَحٍ مِنْ خَزَفٍ .

text: A number of our companion, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Usman Bin Isa, from Sama’at Bin Mihran, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘It is not befitting, drinking in a vessel of the gold and the silver’.

citation.arabic_text: لَا يَنْبَغِي الشُّرْبُ فِي آنِيَةِ الذَّهَبِ وَ لَا الْفِضَّةِ .

text: From him, from Muhammad Bin Ali, from Yunus Bin Yaqoub, from his brother Yusuf who said, ‘I was with Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> at Al-Hajar (the Black Stone), so he<sup>asws</sup> asked for water. citation.arabic_text: كُنْتُ مَعَ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) بِالْحِجْرِ فَاسْتَسْقَى مَاءً فَأُتِيَ بِقَدَحٍ مِنْ صُفْرٍ فَقَالَ رَجُلٌ إِنَّ عَبَّادَ بْنَ كَثِيرٍ يَكْرَهُ الشُّرْبَ فِي الصُّفْرِ فَقَالَ لَا بَأْسَ وَ قَالَ ( عليه السلام ) لِلرَّجُلِ أَلَّا سَأَلْتَهُ أَ ذَهَبٌ هُوَ أَمْ فِضَّةٌ .
citation.translation: From him, from Muhammad Bin Ali, from Yunus Bin Yaqoub, from his brother Yusuf who said, ‘I was with Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> at Al-Hajar (the Black Stone), so he<sup>asws</sup> asked for water. So they came with a yellow cup. So a man said, ‘Abbad Bin Kaseer dislikes drinking in the yellow cup’.
