citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: ضعيف - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (2/307)

text: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Ibn Abu Najran, from Musny Al Hannat, from Abu Baseer, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The chess and the dice, are both (classified as) the gambling’.

citation.arabic_text: قَالَ أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ ( عليه السلام ) الشِّطْرَنْجُ وَ النَّرْدُ هُمَا الْمَيْسِرُ .
citation.translation: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Ibn Abu Najran, from Musny Al Hannat, from Abu Baseer, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The chess and the dice, are both (classified as) the gambling’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: ضعيف على المشهور - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (2/308)

text: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hafs Bin Al Bakhtary, from the one who mentioned it, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘The chess is from the falsehood’.

citation.arabic_text: الشِّطْرَنْجُ مِنَ الْبَاطِلِ .
citation.translation: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hafs Bin Al Bakhtary, from the one who mentioned it, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘The chess is from the falsehood’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: مرسل - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (22/308)

text: Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Muhammad Bin Al Hakam, a brother of Hisham Bin Al Hakam, from Umar Bin Yazeed, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said : ‘Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Emancipates (liberate) people during every night of the Month of Ramazan, Emancipating (liberating) them from the Fire, except the one who breaks Fast upon an intoxicant, or a bickerer, or an owner of the two kings’. I said, ‘And which thing is the ‘owner of the two kings’?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The chess’.

citation.arabic_text: إِنَّ لِلَّهِ فِي كُلِّ لَيْلَةٍ مِنْ شَهْرِ رَمَضَانَ عُتَقَاءَ مِنَ النَّارِ إِلَّا مَنْ أَفْطَرَ عَلَى مُسْكِرٍ أَوْ مُشَاحِنٍ أَوْ صَاحِبَ شَاهَيْنِ قَالَ قُلْتُ وَ أَيُّ شَيْ‏ءٍ صَاحِبُ شَاهَيْنِ قَالَ الشِّطْرَنْجُ .
citation.translation: Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Muhammad Bin Al Hakam, a brother of Hisham Bin Al Hakam, from Umar Bin Yazeed, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said : ‘Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Emancipates (liberate) people during every night of the Month of Ramazan, Emancipating (liberating) them from the Fire, except the one who breaks Fast upon an intoxicant, or a bickerer, or an owner of the two kings’. I said, ‘And which thing is the ‘owner of the two kings’?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The chess’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: مجهول - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (2/308)

text: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ali Bin Iqba, from Ibn Bukeyr, from Zurara, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having been asked about the chess, and about a game of youths which is called ‘The game of the Emir’, and about a game of the three. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘What is your view, if the truth were to be differentiated from the falsehood, with which of these two would these all be?’ I said, ‘With the falsehood’. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Therefore, there is no goodness in it’.

citation.arabic_text: أَ رَأَيْتَكَ إِذَا مُيِّزَ الْحَقُّ مِنَ الْبَاطِلِ مَعَ أَيِّهِمَا يَكُونُ قَالَ قُلْتُ مَعَ الْبَاطِلِ قَالَ فَلَا خَيْرَ فِيهِ .
citation.translation: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ali Bin Iqba, from Ibn Bukeyr, from Zurara, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having been asked about the chess, and about a game of youths which is called ‘The game of the Emir’, and about a game of the three. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘What is your view, if the truth were to be differentiated from the falsehood, with which of these two would these all be?’ I said, ‘With the falsehood’. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Therefore, there is no goodness in it’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: موثق - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (2/308)

text: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umery, from one of his companions, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws regarding the Words of Allahazwj Blessed and High [22:30] therefore avoid the uncleanness of the idols and avoid false words. Heasws said: ‘The uncleanness of the idols it is the chess, and the false words is the singing (music)’.

citation.arabic_text: اللَّهِ تَبَارَكَ وَ تَعَالَى فَاجْتَنِبُوا الرِّجْسَ مِنَ الْأَوْثانِ وَ اجْتَنِبُوا قَوْلَ الزُّورِ قَالَ الرِّجْسُ مِنَ الْأَوْثَانِ هُوَ الشِّطْرَنْجُ وَ قَوْلُ الزُّورِ الْغِنَاءُ .
citation.translation: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umery, from one of his companions, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws regarding the Words of Allahazwj Blessed and High [22:30] therefore avoid the uncleanness of the idols and avoid false words. Heasws said: ‘The uncleanness of the idols it is the chess, and the false words is the singing (music)’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: حسن - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (2/308)

text: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Muhammad Bin Sinan, from Abdul Malik Al Qummy who said, ‘I and my brother Idrees were in the presence of Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, so Idrees said, ‘May we be sacrificed for you<sup>asws</sup>! What is the gambling?’ So Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘It is the chess’. He said, ‘So I said, ‘But they (people) are saying that it is the dice?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘And the dice, as well’.

citation.arabic_text: كُنْتُ أَنَا وَ إِدْرِيسُ أَخِي عِنْدَ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) فَقَالَ إِدْرِيسُ جَعَلَنَا اللَّهُ فِدَاكَ مَا الْمَيْسِرُ فَقَالَ أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) هِيَ الشِّطْرَنْجُ قَالَ فَقُلْتُ أَمَا إِنَّهُمْ يَقُولُونَ إِنَّهَا النَّرْدُ قَالَ وَ النَّرْدُ أَيْضاً .
citation.translation: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Muhammad Bin Sinan, from Abdul Malik Al Qummy who said, ‘I and my brother Idrees were in the presence of Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, so Idrees said, ‘May we be sacrificed for you<sup>asws</sup>! What is the gambling?’ So Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘It is the chess’. He said, ‘So I said, ‘But they (people) are saying that it is the dice?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘And the dice, as well’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: ضعيف على المشهور - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (22/309)

text: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Muhammad Bin Isa, from Abdullah Bin Aasim, from Ali Bin Ismail Al Maysami, from Rabie Bin Abdullah, from Al Fuzayl who said, ‘I asked Abu Ja’farasws about these things which the people play with, the dice and the chess, until I ended up to (mentioning) Al-Suddary (a game). So heasws said: ‘If Allahazwj were to Differentiate between the truth and the falsehood, in which of these two (categories) would (these games) fall into’. I said, ‘With the falsehood’. Heasws said: ‘So what is it to you with the falsehood’.

citation.arabic_text: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا جَعْفَرٍ ( عليه السلام ) عَنْ هَذِهِ الْأَشْيَاءِ الَّتِي يَلْعَبُ بِهَا النَّاسُ النَّرْدِ وَ الشِّطْرَنْجِ حَتَّى انْتَهَيْتُ إِلَى السُّدَّرِ فَقَالَ إِذَا مَيَّزَ اللَّهُ بَيْنَ الْحَقِّ وَ الْبَاطِلِ فِي أَيِّهِمَا يَكُونُ قُلْتُ مَعَ الْبَاطِلِ قَالَ فَمَا لَكَ وَ لِلْبَاطِلِ .
citation.translation: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Muhammad Bin Isa, from Abdullah Bin Aasim, from Ali Bin Ismail Al Maysami, from Rabie Bin Abdullah, from Al Fuzayl who said, ‘I asked Abu Ja’farasws about these things which the people play with, the dice and the chess, until I ended up to (mentioning) Al-Suddary (a game). So heasws said: ‘If Allahazwj were to Differentiate between the truth and the falsehood, in which of these two (categories) would (these games) fall into’. I said, ‘With the falsehood’. Heasws said: ‘So what is it to you with the falsehood’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: ضعيف على المشهور - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (22/309)

text: Sahl, from Muhammad Bin Isa, from Yunus, from Al Husayn Bin Umar Bin Yazeed, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Forgives during the Month of Ramazan (every one) except for three – the partaken of an intoxicant, or a player of the two kings (Chess), or a bickerer’.

citation.arabic_text: يَغْفِرُ اللَّهُ فِي شَهْرِ رَمَضَانَ إِلَّا لِثَلَاثَةٍ صَاحِبِ مُسْكِرٍ أَوْ صَاحِبِ شَاهَيْنِ أَوْ مُشَاحِنٍ .
citation.translation: Sahl, from Muhammad Bin Isa, from Yunus, from Al Husayn Bin Umar Bin Yazeed, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Forgives during the Month of Ramazan (every one) except for three – the partaken of an intoxicant, or a player of the two kings (Chess), or a bickerer’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: ضعيف على المشهور - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (22/309)

text: From him, from Muhammad Bin Isa, from Yunus, from Abu Ayoub, from Abdullah Bin Jundab, from the one who informed him, Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> has said: ‘The chess is gambling, and the dice is gambling’.

citation.arabic_text: الشِّطْرَنْجُ مَيْسِرٌ وَ النَّرْدُ مَيْسِرٌ .
citation.translation: From him, from Muhammad Bin Isa, from Yunus, from Abu Ayoub, from Abdullah Bin Jundab, from the one who informed him, Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> has said: ‘The chess is gambling, and the dice is gambling’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: ضعيف - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (22/309)

text: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad Bin Isa who said, ‘A man from the (people of) Al-Basra came over to Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> the 1st so he said to him<sup>asws</sup>, ‘May I be sacrificed for you<sup>asws</sup>! I sit with a people who are playing with the chess, and I do not play with it, but I (just) look’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘What is it to you and a gathering which Allah<sup>azwj</sup> does not Look at its people?’

citation.arabic_text: دَخَلَ رَجُلٌ مِنَ الْبَصْرِيِّينَ عَلَى أَبِي الْحَسَنِ الْأَوَّلِ ( عليه السلام ) فَقَالَ لَهُ جُعِلْتُ فِدَاكَ إِنِّي أَقْعُدُ مَعَ قَوْمٍ يَلْعَبُونَ بِالشِّطْرَنْجِ وَ لَسْتُ أَلْعَبُ بِهَا وَ لَكِنْ أَنْظُرُ فَقَالَ مَا لَكَ وَ لِمَجْلِسٍ لَا يَنْظُرُ اللَّهُ إِلَى أَهْلِهِ .
citation.translation: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad Bin Isa who said, ‘A man from the (people of) Al-Basra came over to Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> the 1st so he said to him<sup>asws</sup>, ‘May I be sacrificed for you<sup>asws</sup>! I sit with a people who are playing with the chess, and I do not play with it, but I (just) look’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘What is it to you and a gathering which Allah<sup>azwj</sup> does not Look at its people?’
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: حسن - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (22/309)

text: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from Haroun Bin Muslim, from Mas’ada Bin Ziyad, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having been asked about the chess, so he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Leave the Magian thing to its people, may Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Curse it’.

citation.arabic_text: دَعُوا الْمَجُوسِيَّةَ لِأَهْلِهَا لَعَنَهَا اللَّهُ .
citation.translation: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from Haroun Bin Muslim, from Mas’ada Bin Ziyad, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having been asked about the chess, so he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Leave the Magian thing to its people, may Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Curse it’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: صحيح على الظاهر - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (22/310)

text: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Musa Bin Al Qasim, from Muhammad Bin Ali Bin Ja’far, (It has been narrated) from Al-Reza<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘A man came over to Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup>, so he said, ‘O Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup>! What are you<sup>asws</sup> saying regarding the chess which the people are playing with?’ So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘My<sup>asws</sup> father<sup>asws</sup> Ali<sup>asws</sup> Bin Al-Husayn<sup>asws</sup> informed me<sup>asws</sup> from Al-Husayn<sup>asws</sup> Bin Ali<sup>asws</sup>, from Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘The one who spoke and his speech was for other than the Mention of Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic, it would be vain, and the one who was silent, so his silence was for other than remembering Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, is would be forgetfulness’. Then he<sup>asws</sup> was silent, so the man stood up and left’.

citation.arabic_text: جَاءَ رَجُلٌ إِلَى أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ ( عليه السلام ) فَقَالَ يَا أَبَا جَعْفَرٍ مَا تَقُولُ فِي الشِّطْرَنْجِ الَّتِي يَلْعَبُ بِهَا النَّاسُ فَقَالَ أَخْبَرَنِي أَبِي عَلِيُّ بْنُ الْحُسَيْنِ عَنِ الْحُسَيْنِ بْنِ عَلِيٍّ عَنْ أَمِيرِ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ ( عليه السلام ) قَالَ قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ ( صلى الله عليه وآله ) مَنْ كَانَ نَاطِقاً فَكَانَ مَنْطِقُهُ لِغَيْرِ ذِكْرِ اللَّهِ عَزَّ وَ جَلَّ كَانَ لَاغِياً وَ مَنْ كَانَ صَامِتاً فَكَانَ صَمْتُهُ لِغَيْرِ ذِكْرِ اللَّهِ كَانَ سَاهِياً ثُمَّ سَكَتَ فَقَامَ الرَّجُلُ وَ انْصَرَفَ .
citation.translation: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Musa Bin Al Qasim, from Muhammad Bin Ali Bin Ja’far, (It has been narrated) from Al-Reza<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘A man came over to Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup>, so he said, ‘O Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup>! What are you<sup>asws</sup> saying regarding the chess which the people are playing with?’ So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘My<sup>asws</sup> father<sup>asws</sup> Ali<sup>asws</sup> Bin Al-Husayn<sup>asws</sup> informed me<sup>asws</sup> from Al-Husayn<sup>asws</sup> Bin Ali<sup>asws</sup>, from Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘The one who spoke and his speech was for other than the Mention of Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic, it would be vain, and the one who was silent, so his silence was for other than remembering Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, is would be forgetfulness’. Then he<sup>asws</sup> was silent, so the man stood up and left’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: صحيح - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (2/310)

text: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Ibn Raib who said, ‘I went over to Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, so I said, ‘May I be sacrificed for you<sup>asws</sup>! What are you<sup>asws</sup> saying regarding the chess?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The mover of it is like a mover of the flesh of swine’. So I said, ‘And what is upon the one who moves the flesh of swine?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘He should wash his hand’.

citation.arabic_text: دَخَلْتُ عَلَى أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) فَقُلْتُ جُعِلْتُ فِدَاكَ مَا تَقُولُ فِي الشِّطْرَنْجِ قَالَ الْمُقَلِّبُ لَهَا كَالْمُقَلِّبِ لَحْمَ الْخِنْزِيرِ فَقُلْتُ مَا عَلَى مَنْ قَلَّبَ لَحْمَ الْخِنْزِيرِ قَالَ يَغْسِلُ يَدَهُ .
citation.translation: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Ibn Raib who said, ‘I went over to Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, so I said, ‘May I be sacrificed for you<sup>asws</sup>! What are you<sup>asws</sup> saying regarding the chess?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The mover of it is like a mover of the flesh of swine’. So I said, ‘And what is upon the one who moves the flesh of swine?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘He should wash his hand’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: ضعيف على المشهور - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (2/310)

text: Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Ali Bin Saeed, from Suleyman Al Ja’fary, (It has been narrated) from Abu Al-Hassan Al-Reza<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘The one familiar regarding the chess is like the one familiar regarding the Fire’.

citation.arabic_text: الْمُطَّلِعُ فِي الشِّطْرَنْجِ كَالْمُطَّلِعِ فِي النَّارِ .
citation.translation: Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Ali Bin Saeed, from Suleyman Al Ja’fary, (It has been narrated) from Abu Al-Hassan Al-Reza<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘The one familiar regarding the chess is like the one familiar regarding the Fire’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: ضعيف على المشهور - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (2/310)

text: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Al Nowfaly, from Al Sakuny, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> forbade from the playing with the chess, and the dice’.

citation.arabic_text: نَهَى رَسُولُ اللَّهِ ( صلى الله عليه وآله ) عَنِ اللَّعِبِ بِالشِّطْرَنْجِ وَ النَّرْدِ .
citation.translation: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Al Nowfaly, from Al Sakuny, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> forbade from the playing with the chess, and the dice’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: ضعيف على المشهور - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (2/310)

text: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Al Qasim Bin Yahya, form his grandfather Al Hassan Bin Rashid, from Abu Baseer , (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Allah<sup>azwj</sup> is Beautiful and Loves the beauty, and He<sup>azwj</sup> Loves that He<sup>azwj</sup> Sees the effects of the Bounties upon His<sup>azwj</sup> servants’.

citation.chapter: The Book of Outfits and the Beautification and the Magnanimity (al-Kafi, vol 6), 8:1
citation.arabic_text: قَالَ أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ ( عليه السلام ) إِنَّ اللَّهَ جَمِيلٌ يُحِبُّ الْجَمَالَ وَ يُحِبُّ أَنْ يَرَى أَثَرَ النِّعْمَةِ عَلَى عَبْدِهِ .
citation.translation: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Al Qasim Bin Yahya, form his grandfather Al Hassan Bin Rashid, from Abu Baseer , (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Allah<sup>azwj</sup> is Beautiful and Loves the beauty, and He<sup>azwj</sup> Loves that He<sup>azwj</sup> Sees the effects of the Bounties upon His<sup>azwj</sup> servants’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: ضعيف - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (2/311)

text: Ali Bin Muhammad raising it, Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> has said: ‘When Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Favours upon His<sup>azwj</sup> servant with a Bounty, and he displays it (with thanks), he is named as a Beloved of Allah<sup>azwj</sup> narrating with a Bounty of Allah<sup>azwj</sup>; and when Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Favours upon a servant with a Bounty, so he does not display it (with thanks), he is named as the one being angry with Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, a denier in a Bounty of Allah<sup>azwj</sup>’.

citation.chapter: The Book of Outfits and the Beautification and the Magnanimity (al-Kafi, vol 6), 8:1
citation.arabic_text: إِذَا أَنْعَمَ اللَّهُ عَلَى عَبْدِهِ بِنِعْمَةٍ فَظَهَرَتْ عَلَيْهِ سُمِّيَ حَبِيبَ اللَّهِ مُحَدِّثاً بِنِعْمَةِ اللَّهِ وَ إِذَا أَنْعَمَ اللَّهُ عَلَى عَبْدٍ بِنِعْمَةٍ فَلَمْ تَظْهَرْ عَلَيْهِ سُمِّيَ بَغِيضَ اللَّهِ مُكَذِّباً بِنِعْمَةِ اللَّهِ .
citation.translation: Ali Bin Muhammad raising it, Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> has said: ‘When Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Favours upon His<sup>azwj</sup> servant with a Bounty, and he displays it (with thanks), he is named as a Beloved of Allah<sup>azwj</sup> narrating with a Bounty of Allah<sup>azwj</sup>; and when Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Favours upon a servant with a Bounty, so he does not display it (with thanks), he is named as the one being angry with Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, a denier in a Bounty of Allah<sup>azwj</sup>’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: مرفوع - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (22/310)

text: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Muhammad Bin Sinan, from Uqba Bin Muhammad, from Salma Bin Muhammad Baya’a Al Qalanasy who said, ‘Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> passed by a man who had raised his voiced upon a man requiring something small from him. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘With how much are you seeking it?’ He said, ‘With such and such’. So Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Has it nor reached you that it has been said that there is no Religion for the one who has no magnanimity (generosity) for him’.

citation.chapter: The Book of Outfits and the Beautification and the Magnanimity (al-Kafi, vol 6), 8:1
citation.arabic_text: مَرَّ أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) عَلَى رَجُلٍ قَدِ ارْتَفَعَ صَوْتُهُ عَلَى رَجُلٍ يَقْتَضِيهِ شَيْئاً يَسِيراً فَقَالَ بِكَمْ تُطَالِبُهُ قَالَ بِكَذَا وَ كَذَا فَقَالَ أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) أَ مَا بَلَغَكَ أَنَّهُ كَانَ يُقَالُ لَا دِينَ لِمَنْ لَا مُرُوءَةَ لَهُ .
citation.translation: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Muhammad Bin Sinan, from Uqba Bin Muhammad, from Salma Bin Muhammad Baya’a Al Qalanasy who said, ‘Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> passed by a man who had raised his voiced upon a man requiring something small from him. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘With how much are you seeking it?’ He said, ‘With such and such’. So Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Has it nor reached you that it has been said that there is no Religion for the one who has no magnanimity (generosity) for him’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: ضعيف على المشهور - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (2/312)

text: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Ali Bin Asbaat, from the one who reported, Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> has said: ‘When Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Favours upon His<sup>azwj</sup> servant with a Bounty He<sup>azwj</sup> Loves to See it upon him, because He<sup>azwj</sup> is Beautiful and Loves the beauty’.

citation.chapter: The Book of Outfits and the Beautification and the Magnanimity (al-Kafi, vol 6), 8:1
citation.arabic_text: إِذَا أَنْعَمَ اللَّهُ عَلَى عَبْدِهِ بِنِعْمَةٍ أَحَبَّ أَنْ يَرَاهَا عَلَيْهِ لِأَنَّهُ جَمِيلٌ يُحِبُّ الْجَمَالَ .
citation.translation: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Ali Bin Asbaat, from the one who reported, Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> has said: ‘When Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Favours upon His<sup>azwj</sup> servant with a Bounty He<sup>azwj</sup> Loves to See it upon him, because He<sup>azwj</sup> is Beautiful and Loves the beauty’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: ضعيف على المشهور - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (22/312)

text: Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Muhamad Bin Al Hassan Bin Shamoun, from Abdullah Bin Abdul Rahman, from Misma’a Bin Abdul Malik, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> saw a man with dishevelled (untidy) hair of his head, and dirty clothes and in a bad state. So Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘From the Religion is the enjoyment and the manifestation of the Bounty’.

citation.chapter: The Book of Outfits and the Beautification and the Magnanimity (al-Kafi, vol 6), 8:1
citation.arabic_text: أَبْصَرَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ ( صلى الله عليه وآله ) رَجُلًا شَعِثاً شَعْرُ رَأْسِهِ وَسِخَةً ثِيَابُهُ سَيِّئَةً حَالُهُ فَقَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ ( صلى الله عليه وآله ) مِنَ الدِّينِ الْمُتْعَةُ وَ إِظْهَارُ النِّعْمَةِ .
citation.translation: Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Muhamad Bin Al Hassan Bin Shamoun, from Abdullah Bin Abdul Rahman, from Misma’a Bin Abdul Malik, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> saw a man with dishevelled (untidy) hair of his head, and dirty clothes and in a bad state. So Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘From the Religion is the enjoyment and the manifestation of the Bounty’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: ضعيف على المشهور - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (22/312)

text: And by this chain, (Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>) said: ‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘The most evil servant is the filthy one’.

citation.chapter: The Book of Outfits and the Beautification and the Magnanimity (al-Kafi, vol 6), 8:1
citation.arabic_text: وَ بِهَذَا الْإِسْنَادِ قَالَ قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ ( صلى الله عليه وآله ) بِئْسَ الْعَبْدُ الْقَاذُورَةُ .
citation.translation: And by this chain, (Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>) said: ‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘The most evil servant is the filthy one’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: ضعيف على المشهور - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (2/312)

text: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from one of his companions, from Muawiya Bin Wahab who said, ‘Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> saw me and I was carrying grass. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘It is disliked for the man of magnanimity that he should be carrying the lowly thing so they (people) would be audacious (disrespectful) towards him’.

citation.chapter: The Book of Outfits and the Beautification and the Magnanimity (al-Kafi, vol 6), 8:1
citation.arabic_text: رَآنِي أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) وَ أَنَا أَحْمِلُ بَقْلًا فَقَالَ يُكْرَهُ لِلرَّجُلِ السَّرِيِّ أَنْ يَحْمِلَ الشَّيْ‏ءَ الدَّنِيَّ فَيُجْتَرَأَ عَلَيْهِ .

text: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Hadeed, from Murazam Bin Hakeym, from Abdul A’ala, a slave of the progeny of Saam who said, ‘I said to Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> that, the people are reporting that for you<sup>asws</sup> is a lot of wealth’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘That does not bother me<sup>asws</sup>. One day Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> passed by some people from Qureysh, and upon him<sup>asws</sup> was a torn shirt. So they said, ‘The morning has come to Ali<sup>asws</sup> and there is no wealth for him<sup>asws</sup>’. So Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> heard that and he<sup>asws</sup> ordered the one who was in charge of his<sup>asws</sup> charities that he should gather his<sup>asws</sup> dates and do not send anything from these to the people and that these should be kept aside. Then he<sup>asws</sup> said to him: ‘Firstly sell these to the first one (buyer) and make these to be Dirhams. Then keep these where the dates were kept, and compress with it where it cannot be seen. He<sup>asws</sup> then said to the person in charge: ‘When I<sup>asws</sup> call you with the dates, so climb and look at the wealth, so strike it with you leg as if you have no intention for the Dirhams until you scatter these’. Then he sent for a man from them, calling them over. Then he called for the dates. So when he climbed to descend with the dates, he struck with his leg and the Dirhams were scattered. So they said, ‘What is this O Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup>!’ So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘This is wealth of the one who has no wealth for him<sup>asws</sup>’. Then he ordered with that wealth, so he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Look at the deserving ones of every house which I<sup>asws</sup> used to send to them’. So they looked at his wealth, and he<sup>asws</sup> sent it (to them)’.

citation.chapter: The Book of Outfits and the Beautification and the Magnanimity (al-Kafi, vol 6), 8:1
citation.arabic_text: قُلْتُ لِأَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) إِنَّ النَّاسَ يَرْوُونَ أَنَّ لَكَ مَالًا كَثِيراً فَقَالَ مَا يَسُوؤُنِي ذَاكَ إِنَّ أَمِيرَ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ ( عليه السلام ) مَرَّ ذَاتَ يَوْمٍ عَلَى نَاسٍ شَتَّى مِنْ قُرَيْشٍ وَ عَلَيْهِ قَمِيصٌ مُخَرَّقٌ فَقَالُوا أَصْبَحَ عَلِيٌّ لَا مَالَ لَهُ فَسَمِعَهَا أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ ( عليه السلام ) فَأَمَرَ الَّذِي يَلِي صَدَقَتَهُ أَنْ يَجْمَعَ تَمْرَهُ وَ لَا يَبْعَثَ إِلَى إِنْسَانٍ شَيْئاً وَ أَنْ يُوَفِّرَهُ ثُمَّ قَالَ لَهُ بِعْهُ الْأَوَّلَ فَالْأَوَّلَ وَ اجْعَلْهَا دَرَاهِمَ ثُمَّ اجْعَلْهَا حَيْثُ تَجْعَلُ التَّمْرَ فَاكْبِسْهُ مَعَهُ حَيْثُ لَا يُرَى وَ قَالَ لِلَّذِي يَقُومُ عَلَيْهِ إِذَا دَعَوْتُ بِالتَّمْرِ فَاصْعَدْ وَ انْظُرِ الْمَالَ فَاضْرِبْهُ بِرِجْلِكَ كَأَنَّكَ لَا تَعْمِدُ الدَّرَاهِمَ حَتَّى تَنْثُرَهَا ثُمَّ بَعَثَ إِلَى رَجُلٍ مِنْهُمْ يَدْعُوهُمْ ثُمَّ دَعَا بِالتَّمْرِ فَلَمَّا صَعِدَ يَنْزِلُ بِالتَّمْرِ ضَرَبَ بِرِجْلِهِ فَنُثِرَتِ الدَّرَاهِمُ فَقَالُوا مَا هَذَا يَا أَبَا الْحَسَنِ فَقَالَ هَذَا مَالُ مَنْ لَا مَالَ لَهُ ثُمَّ أَمَرَ بِذَلِكَ الْمَالِ فَقَالَ انْظُرُوا أَهْلَ كُلِّ بَيْتٍ كُنْتُ أَبْعَثُ إِلَيْهِمْ فَانْظُرُوا مَالَهُ وَ ابْعَثُوا إِلَيْهِ .

text: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, form Ibn Abu Umeyr, raising it, said, ‘Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘I<sup>asws</sup> dislike it for the man that a Bounty happens to be upon him from Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, so he does not manifest it’.

citation.chapter: The Book of Outfits and the Beautification and the Magnanimity (al-Kafi, vol 6), 8:1
citation.arabic_text: قَالَ أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) إِنِّي لَأَكْرَهُ لِلرَّجُلِ أَنْ يَكُونَ عَلَيْهِ نِعْمَةٌ مِنَ اللَّهِ فَلَا يُظْهِرَهَا .

citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: حسن - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (2/313)

text: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Al Qasim Bin Yahya, from his grandfather Al Hassan Bin Rashid, from Abu Baseer, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Let one of you outfit for your Muslim brother just as he outfits himself for the stranger whom he loves that he should see him in a good state’.

citation.chapter: The Book of Outfits and the Beautification and the Magnanimity (al-Kafi, vol 6), 8:1
citation.arabic_text: قَالَ أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ ( عليه السلام ) لِيَتَزَيَّنْ أَحَدُكُمْ لِأَخِيهِ الْمُسْلِمِ كَمَا يَتَزَيَّنُ لِلْغَرِيبِ الَّذِي يُحِبُّ أَنْ يَرَاهُ فِي أَحْسَنِ الْهَيْئَةِ .
citation.translation: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Al Qasim Bin Yahya, from his grandfather Al Hassan Bin Rashid, from Abu Baseer, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Let one of you outfit for your Muslim brother just as he outfits himself for the stranger whom he loves that he should see him in a good state’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: ضعيف - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (2/313)

text: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Ibn Fazzal, altogether from Yunus Bin Yaqoub, from Abu Baseer who said, ‘It (news) reached Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> that Talha and Al-Zubeyr were both saying, ‘There is not for Ali<sup>asws</sup>, any wealth’. He (the narrator) said, ‘So that was grievous upon him<sup>asws</sup>, so he<sup>asws</sup> ordered his<sup>asws</sup> representatives that they should gather his<sup>asws</sup> harvest until when a year passes by, to bring it to him<sup>asws</sup>, and there had gathered from the price of the harvest, one hundred thousand Dirhams. So he<sup>asws</sup> had it displayed in front of him<sup>asws</sup> and sent a messenger to Talha and Al-Zubayr. So he brought both of them to him<sup>asws</sup>. So he<sup>asws</sup> said to them both: ‘This wealth, by Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, is for me<sup>asws</sup>, there not being a share for anyone else in it’, and they had both verified it’. So they both left from his<sup>asws</sup> presence, and they were both saying, ‘He<sup>asws</sup> does have wealth for him<sup>asws</sup>’.

citation.chapter: The Book of Outfits and the Beautification and the Magnanimity (al-Kafi, vol 6), 8:1

text: From him, from Ibn Fazzal, and Ibn Mahboub, from Yunus Bin Yaqoub, from Abu Baseer, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘The people in Al-Medina were saying, ‘There is no wealth for Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup>’. So Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> sent for a man of Al-Medina and borrowed a thousand Dirhams from him, and sent with it to the governor and said: ‘This is a charity of our<sup>asws</sup> wealth’. So they said, ‘Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> would not have sent this from himself<sup>asws</sup> except that there was indeed wealth for him<sup>asws</sup>’.

citation.chapter: The Book of Outfits and the Beautification and the Magnanimity (al-Kafi, vol 6), 8:1
citation.arabic_text: إِنَّ أُنَاساً بِالْمَدِينَةِ قَالُوا لَيْسَ لِلْحَسَنِ ( عليه السلام ) مَالٌ فَبَعَثَ الْحَسَنُ ( عليه السلام ) إِلَى رَجُلٍ بِالْمَدِينَةِ فَاسْتَقْرَضَ مِنْهُ أَلْفَ دِرْهَمٍ وَ أَرْسَلَ بِهَا إِلَى الْمُصَدِّقِ وَ قَالَ هَذِهِ صَدَقَةُ مَالِنَا فَقَالُوا مَا بَعَثَ الْحَسَنُ ( عليه السلام ) بِهَذِهِ مِنْ تِلْقَاءِ نَفْسِهِ إِلَّا وَ لَهُ مَالٌ .

text: From him, from Ali Bin Jadeed, from Murazam Bin Hakeym, from Abdul A’ala, a slave of the progeny of Saam who said, ‘The state of Ali<sup>asws</sup> Bin Al-Husayn<sup>asws</sup> was extremely difficult until the people of Al-Medina were discussing it. text: From him, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Abu Shuayb Al Mahamily, from Abu Hashim, from one of our companions, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic Loves the beauty, and the beautification, and Hates the misery and the wretchedness’.

citation.chapter: The Book of Outfits and the Beautification and the Magnanimity (al-Kafi, vol 6), 8:1

text: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Muhammad Bin Al Husayn, from Muhammad Bin Aslam, from Haroun Bin Muslim, from Bureyd Bin Muawiya who said, ‘Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said to Ubeyd Bin Ziiyad: ‘Manifestation of the Bounty is more beloved to Allah<sup>azwj</sup> than its maintenance, so beware that you should not be outfitting except in the best of outfits of your people’. He (the narrator) said, ‘So Ubdeyd was not seen except in the best of outfits of his people until he died’.

citation.chapter: The Book of Outfits and the Beautification and the Magnanimity (al-Kafi, vol 6), 8:1
citation.arabic_text: قَالَ أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) لِعُبَيْدِ بْنِ زِيَادٍ إِظْهَارُ النِّعْمَةِ أَحَبُّ إِلَى اللَّهِ مِنْ صِيَانَتِهَا فَإِيَّاكَ أَنْ تَتَزَيَّنَ إِلَّا فِي أَحْسَنِ زِيِّ قَوْمِكَ قَالَ فَمَا رُئِيَ عُبَيْدٌ إِلَّا فِي أَحْسَنِ زِيِّ قَوْمِهِ حَتَّى مَاتَ .

text: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Ali bin Al Hakam, from Abdullah Bin Jundab, from Sufyan Bin Al Samt who said, ‘I heard Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> saying: ‘The clean clothes suppress the enemy’.

text: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Abdullah Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Al Hakam, from Aban Bin Usman, from Yahya Bin Abu Al A’ala, from Abu Abdullahasws having said: ‘Amir Al-Momineenasws sent Abdullah Bin Al-Abbas to Ibn Al-Kawwa and his companions, and upon him was a thin shirt and a garment. So when they looked at him, they said, ‘O Ibn Abbas! You are the best of us amongst ourselves and you are wearing these clothes?’ So he said, ‘[7:32] Say: Who has prohibited the adornments of Allah which He has Brought forth for His servants and the good provisions? [7:31] Take to your adornments at every Masjid’.

citation.arabic_text: بَعَثَ أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ ( عليه السلام ) عَبْدَ اللَّهِ بْنَ الْعَبَّاسِ إِلَى ابْنِ الْكَوَّاءِ وَ أَصْحَابِهِ وَ عَلَيْهِ قَمِيصٌ رَقِيقٌ وَ حُلَّةٌ فَلَمَّا نَظَرُوا إِلَيْهِ قَالُوا يَا ابْنَ عَبَّاسٍ أَنْتَ خَيْرُنَا فِي أَنْفُسِنَا وَ أَنْتَ تَلْبَسُ هَذَا اللِّبَاسَ فَقَالَ وَ هَذَا أَوَّلُ مَا أُخَاصِمُكُمْ فِيهِ قُلْ مَنْ حَرَّمَ زِينَةَ اللَّهِ الَّتِي أَخْرَجَ لِعِبادِهِ وَ الطَّيِّباتِ مِنَ الرِّزْقِ وَ قَالَ خُذُوا زِينَتَكُمْ عِنْدَ كُلِّ مَسْجِدٍ .

text: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Muhammad Bin Isa, from Safwan, from Yusuf Bin Ibrahim who said, ‘I went over to Abu Abdullahasws and upon me was Al-Khazz coat and a Al-Khazz pallium. So heasws looked at me, so I said, ‘May I be sacrificed for youasws! Upon me is an Al Khazz coat and an Al Khazz pallium, so what are youasws saying with regards to it?’ So heasws said: ‘And what is the problem with Al-Khazz?’ I said, ‘And its wrapping is embroidered’. Heasws said: ‘And there is no problem with embroidery, for Al-Husaynasws was hit and upon him was an Al-Khazz coat’. Then heasws said: ‘Abdullah Bin Abbas, when Amir Al-Momineenasws sent him to the Khawarijites, so he paused to them wearing the best of his clothes, and perfumed himself with the best of his perfumes, and rode the best of his rides. So he went and paused to them. So they said, ‘O Ibn Abbas! Between us, you are the best of the people, but you have come to us in the clothes of the tyrants and their rides’. So he recited to them this Verse [7:32] Say: Who has prohibited the adornments of Allah which He has Brought forth for His servants and the good provisions? Therefore, wear (nice clothes) and beautify, for Allahazwj is Beautiful, Heazwj Loves the beauty, but it should be from the Permissibles (means)’.

citation.chapter: The Book of Outfits and the Beautification and the Magnanimity (al-Kafi, vol 6), 8:2
citation.arabic_text: دَخَلْتُ عَلَى أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) وَ عَلَيَّ جُبَّةُ خَزٍّ وَ طَيْلَسَانُ خَزٍّ فَنَظَرَ إِلَيَّ فَقُلْتُ جُعِلْتُ فِدَاكَ عَلَيَّ جُبَّةُ خَزٍّ وَ طَيْلَسَانُ خَزٍّ فَمَا تَقُولُ فِيهِ فَقَالَ وَ مَا بَأْسٌ بِالْخَزِّ قُلْتُ وَ سَدَاهُ إِبْرِيسَمٌ قَالَ وَ مَا بَأْسٌ بِإِبْرِيسَمٍ فَقَدْ أُصِيبَ الْحُسَيْنُ ( عليه السلام ) وَ عَلَيْهِ جُبَّةُ خَزٍّ ثُمَّ قَالَ إِنَّ عَبْدَ اللَّهِ بْنَ عَبَّاسٍ لَمَّا بَعَثَهُ أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ ( عليه السلام ) إِلَى الْخَوَارِجِ فَوَاقَفَهُمْ لَبِسَ أَفْضَلَ ثِيَابِهِ وَ تَطَيَّبَ بِأَفْضَلِ طِيبِهِ وَ رَكِبَ أَفْضَلَ مَرَاكِبِهِ فَخَرَجَ فَوَاقَفَهُمْ فَقَالُوا يَا ابْنَ عَبَّاسٍ بَيْنَا أَنْتَ أَفْضَلُ النَّاسِ إِذَا أَتَيْتَنَا فِي لِبَاسِ الْجَبَابِرَةِ وَ مَرَاكِبِهِمْ فَتَلَا عَلَيْهِمْ هَذِهِ الْآيَةَ قُلْ مَنْ حَرَّمَ زِينَةَ اللَّهِ الَّتِي أَخْرَجَ لِعِبادِهِ وَ الطَّيِّباتِ مِنَ الرِّزْقِ فَالْبَسْ وَ تَجَمَّلْ فَإِنَّ اللَّهَ جَمِيلٌ يُحِبُّ الْجَمَالَ وَ لْيَكُنْ مِنْ حَلَالٍ .

text: Ali Bin Muhammad Bin Bundar, from Ahmad Bin Abu Abdullah, from Muhammad Bin Ali, raising it, said, ‘Sufyan Al-Sowry passed by in the Sacred Masjid, so he saw Abu Abdullahasws and upon himasws were a lot of clothes of goodly price. So he said, ‘By Allahazwj! I will go to himasws and rebuke himasws’. So he approached himasws. So heasws said, ‘O sonasws of Rasool-Allahsaww! Rasool-Allahsaww did not wear the likes of these clothes, nor did Aliasws, nor did anyone (else) from yourasws forefathers’. So Abu Abdullahasws said to him: ‘Rasool-Allahsaww was in an era of scarcity and financial straitness, and hesaww used to take in accordance with hissaww straitness and hissaww ability, and the world after that has long gone past it, thus the most deserving of its people with it are its righteous ones’. Then heasws recited [7:32] Say: Who has prohibited the adornments of Allah which He has Brought forth for His servants and the good provisions? And weasws are the most rightful of taking from it what Allahazwj has Granted it, besides Iasws, O Sowry, what you see upon measws from the clothes, rather Iasws wear it for the people’. Then heasws drew the hand of Sufyan, so heasws brought it towards himselfasws. Then heasws raised his upper garment, and there was a cloth beneath that, upon hisasws skin, which was rough. So heasws said: ‘This, Iasws wear it for myselfasws, and what you see is for the people’. Then heasws drew the upper clothing of Sufyan which was rough, coarse, and inside that was a smooth cloth. So heasws said: ‘You wear this outer garment for the people, and you wear this for yourself, delighting in it’.

citation.chapter: The Book of Outfits and the Beautification and the Magnanimity (al-Kafi, vol 6), 8:2
citation.arabic_text: مَرَّ سُفْيَانُ الثَّوْرِيُّ فِي الْمَسْجِدِ الْحَرَامِ فَرَأَى أَبَا عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) وَ عَلَيْهِ ثِيَابٌ كَثِيرَةُ الْقِيمَةِ حِسَانٌ فَقَالَ وَ اللَّهِ لآَتِيَنَّهُ وَ لَأُوَبِّخَنَّهُ فَدَنَا مِنْهُ فَقَالَ يَا ابْنَ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ مَا لَبِسَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ ( صلى الله عليه وآله ) مِثْلَ هَذَا اللِّبَاسِ وَ لَا عَلِيٌّ ( عليه السلام ) وَ لَا أَحَدٌ مِنْ آبَائِكَ فَقَالَ لَهُ أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) كَانَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ ( صلى الله عليه وآله ) فِي زَمَانِ قَتْرٍ مُقْتِرٍ وَ كَانَ يَأْخُذُ لِقَتْرِهِ وَ اقْتِدَارِهِ وَ إِنَّ الدُّنْيَا بَعْدَ ذَلِكَ أَرْخَتْ عَزَالِيَهَا فَأَحَقُّ أَهْلِهَا بِهَا أَبْرَارُهَا ثُمَّ تَلَا قُلْ مَنْ حَرَّمَ زِينَةَ اللَّهِ الَّتِي أَخْرَجَ لِعِبادِهِ وَ الطَّيِّباتِ مِنَ الرِّزْقِ وَ نَحْنُ أَحَقُّ مَنْ أَخَذَ مِنْهَا مَا أَعْطَاهُ اللَّهُ غَيْرَ أَنِّي يَا ثَوْرِيُّ مَا تَرَى عَلَيَّ مِنْ ثَوْبٍ إِنَّمَا أَلْبَسُهُ لِلنَّاسِ ثُمَّ اجْتَذَبَ يَدَ سُفْيَانَ فَجَرَّهَا إِلَيْهِ ثُمَّ رَفَعَ الثَّوْبَ الْأَعْلَى وَ أَخْرَجَ ثَوْباً تَحْتَ ذَلِكَ عَلَى جِلْدِهِ غَلِيظاً فَقَالَ هَذَا أَلْبَسُهُ لِنَفْسِي وَ مَا رَأَيْتَهُ لِلنَّاسِ ثُمَّ جَذَبَ ثَوْباً عَلَى سُفْيَانَ أَعْلَاهُ غَلِيظٌ خَشِنٌ وَ دَاخِلُ ذَلِكَ ثَوْبٌ لَيِّنٌ فَقَالَ لَبِسْتَ هَذَا الْأَعْلَى لِلنَّاسِ وَ لَبِسْتَ هَذَا لِنَفْسِكَ تَسُرُّهَا.

text: Al Husayn Bin Muhammad, from Moala Bin Muhammad, from Al Washa, from Abdullah Bin Sinan who said, ‘I heard Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> saying: ‘Whilst I<sup>asws</sup> was in the circumambulation (of the Kaaba) when a man grabbed hold of my<sup>asws</sup> clothes, and he was Abbad Bin Kaseer Al-Basry. So he said, ‘O Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> Bin Muhammad<sup>asws</sup>! You<sup>asws</sup> are wearing the likes of these clothes, and you<sup>asws</sup> are in this place along with the status which you<sup>asws</sup> are in from Ali<sup>asws</sup>?’ So I<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘It is a Furqaby (Egyptian) cloth, which I<sup>asws</sup> bought with one Dinar, and Ali<sup>asws</sup> was in an era in which it was correct for him<sup>asws</sup> what he<sup>asws</sup> wore in it, and if I<sup>asws</sup> were to wear the likes of that in our<sup>asws</sup> era, the people would say, ‘This is a show-off like Abbad’.

citation.arabic_text: سَمِعْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) يَقُولُ بَيْنَا أَنَا فِي الطَّوَافِ وَ إِذَا بِرَجُلٍ يَجْذِبُ ثَوْبِي وَ إِذَا هُوَ عَبَّادُ بْنُ كَثِيرٍ الْبَصْرِيُّ فَقَالَ يَا جَعْفَرَ بْنَ مُحَمَّدٍ تَلْبَسُ مِثْلَ هَذِهِ الثِّيَابِ وَ أَنْتَ فِي هَذَا الْمَوْضِعِ مَعَ الْمَكَانِ الَّذِي أَنْتَ فِيهِ مِنْ عَلِيٍّ ( عليه السلام ) فَقُلْتُ ثَوْبٌ فُرْقُبِيٌّ اشْتَرَيْتُهُ بِدِينَارٍ وَ كَانَ عَلِيٌّ ( عليه السلام ) فِي زَمَانٍ يَسْتَقِيمُ لَهُ مَا لَبِسَ فِيهِ وَ لَوْ لَبِسْتُ مِثْلَ ذَلِكَ اللِّبَاسِ فِي زَمَانِنَا لَقَالَ النَّاسُ هَذَا مُرَاءٍ مِثْلُ عَبَّادٍ .
citation.translation: Al Husayn Bin Muhammad, from Moala Bin Muhammad, from Al Washa, from Abdullah Bin Sinan who said, ‘I heard Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> saying: ‘Whilst I<sup>asws</sup> was in the circumambulation (of the Kaaba) when a man grabbed hold of my<sup>asws</sup> clothes, and he was Abbad Bin Kaseer Al-Basry. So he said, ‘O Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> Bin Muhammad<sup>asws</sup>! You<sup>asws</sup> are wearing the likes of these clothes, and you<sup>asws</sup> are in this place along with the status which you<sup>asws</sup> are in from Ali<sup>asws</sup>?’ So I<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘It is a Furqaby (Egyptian) cloth, which I<sup>asws</sup> bought with one Dinar, and Ali<sup>asws</sup> was in an era in which it was correct for him<sup>asws</sup> what he<sup>asws</sup> wore in it, and if I<sup>asws</sup> were to wear the likes of that in our<sup>asws</sup> era, the people would say, ‘This is a show-off like Abbad’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: ضعيف على المشهور - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (2/318)

text: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Khalid, from Usman Bin Isa, from Is’haq Bin Ammar who said, ‘I asked Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> about the man who happened to have ten shirts for him, rotating between these. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘There is no problem’.

citation.chapter: The Book of Outfits and the Beautification and the Magnanimity (al-Kafi, vol 6), 8:2
citation.arabic_text: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) عَنِ الرَّجُلِ يَكُونُ لَهُ عَشَرَةُ أَقْمِصَةٍ يُرَاوِحُ بَيْنَهَا قَالَ لَا بَأْسَ .
citation.translation: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Khalid, from Usman Bin Isa, from Is’haq Bin Ammar who said, ‘I asked Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> about the man who happened to have ten shirts for him, rotating between these. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘There is no problem’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: موثق - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (2/318)

text: And by this chain, from Is’haq Bin Ammar who said, ‘I said to Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, ‘There happen to be three shirts for me’. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘There is no problem’. So he did not cease (numbering) until it reached ten. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Do they not make each other last longer?’ I said, ‘Yes, and were I to wear one, it would last for a little (while)’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘There is no problem’.

citation.chapter: The Book of Outfits and the Beautification and the Magnanimity (al-Kafi, vol 6), 8:2
citation.arabic_text: قُلْتُ لِأَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) يَكُونُ لِي ثَلَاثَةُ أَقْمِصَةٍ قَالَ لَا بَأْسَ قَالَ فَلَمْ أَزَلْ حَتَّى بَلَغْتُ عَشَرَةً فَقَالَ أَ لَيْسَ يُوَدِّعُ بَعْضُهَا بَعْضاً قُلْتُ بَلَى وَ لَوْ كُنْتُ إِنَّمَا أَلْبَسُ وَاحِداً لَكَانَ أَقَلَّ بَقَاءً قَالَ لَا بَأْسَ .
citation.translation: And by this chain, from Is’haq Bin Ammar who said, ‘I said to Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, ‘There happen to be three shirts for me’. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘There is no problem’. So he did not cease (numbering) until it reached ten. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Do they not make each other last longer?’ I said, ‘Yes, and were I to wear one, it would last for a little (while)’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘There is no problem’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: موثق - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (22/318)

text: From him, from Nuh Bin Shuayb, from one of his companions, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws, said, ‘I asked himasws about the man affluent man taking many clothes, new ones, and the pallium, and an abundance of shirts making each other last longer, beautifying by these, would he happen to be an extravagant?’ Heasws said: ‘No, because Allahazwj Mighty and Majestic Saying [65:7] Let him who has abundance spend out of his abundance’.

citation.chapter: The Book of Outfits and the Beautification and the Magnanimity (al-Kafi, vol 6), 8:2
citation.arabic_text: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنِ الرَّجُلِ الْمُوسِرِ يَتَّخِذُ الثِّيَابَ الْكَثِيرَةَ الْجِيَادَ وَ الطَّيَالِسَةَ وَ الْقُمُصَ الْكَثِيرَةَ يَصُونُ بَعْضُهَا بَعْضاً يَتَجَمَّلُ بِهَا أَ يَكُونُ مُسْرِفاً قَالَ لَا لِأَنَّ اللَّهَ عَزَّ وَ جَلَّ يَقُولُ لِيُنْفِقْ ذُو سَعَةٍ مِنْ سَعَتِهِ .
citation.translation: From him, from Nuh Bin Shuayb, from one of his companions, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws, said, ‘I asked himasws about the man affluent man taking many clothes, new ones, and the pallium, and an abundance of shirts making each other last longer, beautifying by these, would he happen to be an extravagant?’ Heasws said: ‘No, because Allahazwj Mighty and Majestic Saying [65:7] Let him who has abundance spend out of his abundance’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: مرسل - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (2/319)

text: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Ja’far Bin Muhammad Al Ashary, from Ibn Al Qadah who said, ‘Abu Abdullahasws was leaning upon me’, or said, ‘Upon my father’, so Abbad Bin Kaseer Al Basry came over and upon himasws were clothes of Merv (a city), so he said, ‘O Abu Abdullahasws! Youasws are from the Peopleasws of the Household of the Prophet-hood, and yourasws fatherasws was what heasws was, so what are these Mervian clothes upon youasws? If only youasws would wear besides these clothes’. So Abu Abdullahasws said to him: ‘Woe be unto you, O Abbad! [7:32] Say: Who has prohibited the adornments of Allah which He has Brought forth for His servants and the good provisions? When Allahazwj Mighty and Majestic Favours upon Hisazwj servant with a Bounty Loves that Heazwj Sees it upon him. There is no problem with it. Woe be unto you, O Abbad! But rather, Iasws am a part of Rasool-Allahsaww, therefore do not hurt measws’. And it was so that Abbad had worn two Qatary (a city) clothes’.

citation.chapter: The Book of Outfits and the Beautification and the Magnanimity (al-Kafi, vol 6), 8:2
citation.arabic_text: كَانَ أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) مُتَّكِئاً عَلَيَّ أَوْ قَالَ عَلَى أَبِي فَلَقِيَهُ عَبَّادُ بْنُ كَثِيرٍ الْبَصْرِيُّ وَ عَلَيْهِ ثِيَابٌ مَرْوِيَّةٌ حِسَانٌ فَقَالَ يَا أَبَا عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) إِنَّكَ مِنْ أَهْلِ بَيْتِ النُّبُوَّةِ وَ كَانَ أَبُوكَ وَ كَانَ فَمَا هَذِهِ الثِّيَابُ الْمَرْوِيَّةُ عَلَيْكَ فَلَوْ لَبِسْتَ دُونَ هَذِهِ الثِّيَابِ فَقَالَ لَهُ أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) وَيْلَكَ يَا عَبَّادُ مَنْ حَرَّمَ زِينَةَ اللَّهِ الَّتِي أَخْرَجَ لِعِبَادِهِ وَ الطَّيِّبَاتِ مِنَ الرِّزْقِ إِنَّ اللَّهَ عَزَّ وَ جَلَّ إِذَا أَنْعَمَ عَلَى عَبْدِهِ نِعْمَةً أَحَبَّ أَنْ يَرَاهَا عَلَيْهِ لَيْسَ بِهَا بَأْسٌ وَيْلَكَ يَا عَبَّادُ إِنَّمَا أَنَا بَضْعَةٌ مِنْ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ ( صلى الله عليه وآله ) فَلَا تُؤْذِنِي وَ كَانَ عَبَّادٌ يَلْبَسُ ثَوْبَيْنِ قِطْرِيَّيْنِ .

text: Muhammad Bin yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Al Qasim Bin Yahya, from his grandfather Al Hassan Bin Rashid, from Abu Baseer, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The clean clothes remove the stress and the grief, and it is a cleanliness for the Salat (Prayer)’.

citation.chapter: The Book of Outfits and the Beautification and the Magnanimity (al-Kafi, vol 6), 8:2
citation.arabic_text: قَالَ أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ ( عليه السلام ) النَّظِيفُ مِنَ الثِّيَابِ يُذْهِبُ الْهَمَّ وَ الْحَزَنَ وَ هُوَ طَهُورٌ لِلصَّلَاةِ .
citation.translation: Muhammad Bin yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Al Qasim Bin Yahya, from his grandfather Al Hassan Bin Rashid, from Abu Baseer, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The clean clothes remove the stress and the grief, and it is a cleanliness for the Salat (Prayer)’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: ضعيف - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (2/320)

text: Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Hammad Bin Usman who said, ‘I was there in the presence of Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> when a man said to him<sup>asws</sup>, ‘May Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Keep you<sup>asws</sup> well! You<sup>asws</sup> mentioned that Ali<sup>asws</sup> Bin Abu Talib<sup>asws</sup> was wearing the coarse (clothes), wearing the shirt of four Dirhams, and what resembles that, and we see upon you<sup>asws</sup> the new clothes?’ So he<sup>asws</sup> said to him: ‘Ali<sup>asws</sup> Bin Abu Talib<sup>asws</sup> was wearing that during an era undeniably, and were he<sup>asws</sup> to wear the likes of that today he<sup>asws</sup> would have been defamed by it. So the best of the clothes during every era are clothes of its people, besides that when our<sup>asws</sup> Qaim<sup>asws</sup> rises, he<sup>asws</sup> would wear the clothes of Ali<sup>asws</sup>, and walk upon his<sup>asws</sup> way’.

citation.chapter: The Book of Outfits and the Beautification and the Magnanimity (al-Kafi, vol 6), 8:2
citation.arabic_text: كُنْتُ حَاضِراً عِنْدَ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) إِذْ قَالَ لَهُ رَجُلٌ أَصْلَحَكَ اللَّهُ ذَكَرْتَ أَنَّ عَلِيَّ بْنَ أَبِي طَالِبٍ ( عليه السلام ) كَانَ يَلْبَسُ الْخَشِنَ يَلْبَسُ الْقَمِيصَ بِأَرْبَعَةِ دَرَاهِمَ وَ مَا أَشْبَهَ ذَلِكَ وَ نَرَى عَلَيْكَ اللِّبَاسَ الْجَيِّدَ قَالَ فَقَالَ لَهُ إِنَّ عَلِيَّ بْنَ أَبِي طَالِبٍ ( عليه السلام ) كَانَ يَلْبَسُ ذَلِكَ فِي زَمَانٍ لَا يُنْكَرُ وَ لَوْ لَبِسَ مِثْلَ ذَلِكَ الْيَوْمَ لَشُهِرَ بِهِ فَخَيْرُ لِبَاسِ كُلِّ زَمَانٍ لِبَاسُ أَهْلِهِ غَيْرَ أَنَّ قَائِمَنَا إِذَا قَامَ لَبِسَ لِبَاسَ عَلِيٍّ ( عليه السلام ) وَ سَارَ بِسِيرَتِهِ .

You<sup>asws</sup> mentioned that Ali<sup>asws</sup> Bin Abu Talib<sup>asws</sup> was wearing the coarse (clothes), wearing the shirt of four Dirhams, and what resembles that, and we see upon you<sup>asws</sup> the new clothes?’ So he<sup>asws</sup> said to him: ‘Ali<sup>asws</sup> Bin Abu Talib<sup>asws</sup> was wearing that during an era undeniably, and were he<sup>asws</sup> to wear the likes of that today he<sup>asws</sup> would have been defamed by it. text: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Ali Bin Asbaat, from the one who reported it, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘There is no problem if there happen to be twenty shirts for the man’.

citation.chapter: The Book of Outfits and the Beautification and the Magnanimity (al-Kafi, vol 6), 8:2
citation.arabic_text: لَا بَأْسَ أَنْ يَكُونَ لِلرَّجُلِ عِشْرُونَ قَمِيصاً .
citation.translation: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Ali Bin Asbaat, from the one who reported it, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘There is no problem if there happen to be twenty shirts for the man’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: ضعيف على المشهور - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (22/320)

text: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Abu Ayoub Al Khazzaz, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Blessed and High Hates the clothes which defame’.

citation.chapter: The Book of Outfits and the Beautification and the Magnanimity (al-Kafi, vol 6), 8:3
citation.arabic_text: إِنَّ اللَّهَ تَبَارَكَ وَ تَعَالَى يُبْغِضُ شُهْرَةَ اللِّبَاسِ .
citation.translation: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Abu Ayoub Al Khazzaz, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Blessed and High Hates the clothes which defame’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: حسن - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (2/320)

text: Muhammad Bin Yahya, form Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Muhammad Bin Ismail, from Abu Ismail Al Sarraj, from Ibn Muskan, from a man, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘It is sufficient disgrace for the man that he wears clothes by which he is defamed, or rides an animal which defames him’.

citation.chapter: The Book of Outfits and the Beautification and the Magnanimity (al-Kafi, vol 6), 8:3
citation.arabic_text: كَفَى بِالْمَرْءِ خِزْياً أَنْ يَلْبَسَ ثَوْباً يَشْهَرُهُ أَوْ يَرْكَبَ دَابَّةً تَشْهَرُهُ .
citation.translation: Muhammad Bin Yahya, form Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Muhammad Bin Ismail, from Abu Ismail Al Sarraj, from Ibn Muskan, from a man, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘It is sufficient disgrace for the man that he wears clothes by which he is defamed, or rides an animal which defames him’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: مرسل - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (22/321)

text: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Khalid, from Usman Bin Isa, from the one who mentioned it, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘The fame (seeker), the good of it and the evil of it, are in the Fire’.

citation.chapter: The Book of Outfits and the Beautification and the Magnanimity (al-Kafi, vol 6), 8:3
citation.arabic_text: الشُّهْرَةُ خَيْرُهَا وَ شَرُّهَا فِي النَّارِ .
citation.translation: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Khalid, from Usman Bin Isa, from the one who mentioned it, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘The fame (seeker), the good of it and the evil of it, are in the Fire’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: مرسل - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (2/321)

text: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Muhammad Bin Sinan, from Abu Al Jaroud, from Abu Saeed, (It has been narrated) from Al-Husayn<sup>asws</sup> having said: ’The one who wears clothes which defame him, Allah<sup>azwj</sup> would Clothe him on the Day of Judgement in a garment from the Fire’.

citation.chapter: The Book of Outfits and the Beautification and the Magnanimity (al-Kafi, vol 6), 8:3
citation.arabic_text: مَنْ لَبِسَ ثَوْباً يَشْهَرُهُ كَسَاهُ اللَّهُ يَوْمَ الْقِيَامَةِ ثَوْباً مِنَ النَّارِ .
citation.translation: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Muhammad Bin Sinan, from Abu Al Jaroud, from Abu Saeed, (It has been narrated) from Al-Husayn<sup>asws</sup> having said: ’The one who wears clothes which defame him, Allah<sup>azwj</sup> would Clothe him on the Day of Judgement in a garment from the Fire’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: ضعيف على المشهور - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (2/321)

text: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ibn Al Qaddah, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘Wear the white for it is better and purer, and enshroud your deceased in it’.

citation.chapter: The Book of Outfits and the Beautification and the Magnanimity (al-Kafi, vol 6), 8:4
citation.arabic_text: قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ ( صلى الله عليه وآله ) الْبَسُوا الْبَيَاضَ فَإِنَّهُ أَطْيَبُ وَ أَطْهَرُ وَ كَفِّنُوا فِيهِ مَوْتَاكُمْ .
citation.translation: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ibn Al Qaddah, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘Wear the white for it is better and purer, and enshroud your deceased in it’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: موثق - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (22/322)

text: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Abu Abdullah, from one of his companions, from Safwan Al Jammal who said, ‘I transported Abu Abdullahasws for the second time to Al-Kufa and Abu Ja’far Al-Mansour was with it. When we arrived at Al-Hashimiyya, a city of Abu Ja’far, heasws extracted hisasws leg from the stirrups, then descended and called for a young mule, and wore white clothes and a white headgear. So when heasws went over to him, Abu Ja’far said to himasws, ‘Youasws have resembled yourselfasws with the Prophetsas’. So Abu Abdullahasws said: ‘And it means you are distancing measws from the sonsasws of the Prophetsas’. So he said, ‘I was thinking that I would send to Al-Medina, the ones who would uproot its palm trees and make captives of its offspring’. So heasws said: ‘And why is that, O commander of the faithful?’ So he said, ‘It has been raised to me that yourasws slave Al-Moala Bin Khunays is calling (people) to youasws and is gathering the wealth for youasws’. So heasws said: ‘By Allahazwj that is not so’. So he said, ‘I would not agree with youasws except with (matters of) the divorce, and the emancipation, and the sacrifice, and the walking (to the Kabah)’. So heasws said: ‘Is it with the rivals from besides Allahazwj that you are instructing me that Iasws should be swearing? The one who is not pleased with Allahazwj, so he has nothing to do with Allahazwj, regarding anything’. So he said, ‘Are you using jurisprudence (Fiqh) upon me?’ So heasws said: ‘Iasws distance myselfasws from the jurisprudence (Fiqh), and Iasws am a sonasws of Rasool-Allahsaww’. So he said, ‘So I shall gather between youasws and the one who informed with you’. So he did it. So the man who had informed of it, came over. So Abu Abdullahasws said to him: ‘O you! So he said, ‘Yes, by Allahazwj besides Whom there is no god except for Himazwj, the Knower of the unseen and the seen, the Beneficent, the Merciful, I did do it’. So Abu Abdullahasws said to him: ‘Woe be unto you! You Glorify Allahazwj thinking Heazwj would be too Embarrassed from Punishing you? But say, ‘I disavow from the Might and Strength of Allahazwj and I come to my own might and strength’. So the man swore by it, and he had not completed it and he fell down dead’. So Abu Ja’far said to himasws, ‘I will not ratify against you after it, ever, and I would make good yourasws allowing and yourasws refuting’.

citation.chapter: The Book of Outfits and the Beautification and the Magnanimity (al-Kafi, vol 6), 8:4
citation.arabic_text: حَمَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) الْحَمْلَةَ الثَّانِيَةَ إِلَى الْكُوفَةِ وَ أَبُو جَعْفَرٍ الْمَنْصُورُ بِهَا فَلَمَّا أَشْرَفَ عَلَى الْهَاشِمِيَّةِ مَدِينَةِ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ أَخْرَجَ رِجْلَهُ مِنْ غَرْزِ الرِّجْلِ ثُمَّ نَزَلَ وَ دَعَا بِبَغْلَةٍ شَهْبَاءَ وَ لَبِسَ ثِيَابَ بِيضٍ وَ كُمَّةً بَيْضَاءَ فَلَمَّا دَخَلَ عَلَيْهِ قَالَ لَهُ أَبُو جَعْفَرٍ لَقَدْ تَشَبَّهْتَ بِالْأَنْبِيَاءِ فَقَالَ أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) وَ أَنَّى تُبَعِّدُنِي مِنْ أَبْنَاءِ الْأَنْبِيَاءِ فَقَالَ لَقَدْ هَمَمْتُ أَنْ أَبْعَثَ إِلَى الْمَدِينَةِ مَنْ يَعْقِرُ نَخْلَهَا وَ يَسْبِي ذُرِّيَّتَهَا فَقَالَ وَ لِمَ ذَلِكَ يَا أَمِيرَ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ فَقَالَ رُفِعَ إِلَيَّ أَنَّ مَوْلَاكَ الْمُعَلَّى بْنَ خُنَيْسٍ يَدْعُو إِلَيْكَ وَ يَجْمَعُ لَكَ الْأَمْوَالَ فَقَالَ وَ اللَّهِ مَا كَانَ فَقَالَ لَسْتُ أَرْضَى مِنْكَ إِلَّا بِالطَّلَاقِ وَ الْعَتَاقِ وَ الْهَدْيِ وَ الْمَشْيِ فَقَالَ أَ بِالْأَنْدَادِ مِنْ دُونِ اللَّهِ تَأْمُرُنِي أَنْ أَحْلِفَ إِنَّهُ مَنْ لَمْ يَرْضَ بِاللَّهِ فَلَيْسَ مِنَ اللَّهِ فِي شَيْ‏ءٍ فَقَالَ أَ تَتَفَقَّهُ عَلَيَّ فَقَالَ وَ أَنَّى تُبَعِّدُنِي مِنَ الْفِقْهِ وَ أَنَا ابْنُ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ ( صلى الله عليه وآله ) فَقَالَ فَإِنِّي أَجْمَعُ بَيْنَكَ وَ بَيْنَ مَنْ سَعَى بِكَ قَالَ فَافْعَلْ فَجَاءَ الرَّجُلُ الَّذِي سَعَى بِهِ فَقَالَ لَهُ أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ يَا هَذَا فَقَالَ نَعَمْ وَ اللَّهِ الَّذِي لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا هُوَ عَالِمِ الْغَيْبِ وَ الشَّهَادَةِ الرَّحْمَنِ الرَّحِيمِ لَقَدْ فَعَلْتَ فَقَالَ لَهُ أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) وَيْلَكَ تُمَجِّدُ اللَّهَ فَيَسْتَحْيِي مِنْ تَعْذِيبِكَ وَ لَكِنْ قُلْ بَرِئْتُ مِنْ حَوْلِ اللَّهِ وَ قُوَّتِهِ وَ أَلْجَأْتُ إِلَى حَوْلِي وَ قُوَّتِي فَحَلَفَ بِهَا الرَّجُلُ فَلَمْ يَسْتَتِمَّهَا حَتَّى وَقَعَ مَيِّتاً فَقَالَ لَهُ أَبُو جَعْفَرٍ لَا أُصَدِّقُ بَعْدَهَا عَلَيْكَ أَبَداً وَ أَحْسَنَ جَائِزَتَهُ وَ رَدَّهُ .

text: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Al Hakam, from Muawiya Bin Mayassar, from Al Hakam Bin Uteyba who said, ‘I went over to Abu Ja’farasws and heasws was in a recently furbished room, and upon himasws was a dyed shirt and a dyed sheet, the effects of the dye being upon his shoulders. So heasws went on to look at the room and looking at its furnishings, so heasws said: ‘O Hakam! What are you saying regarding this?’ So I said, ‘And what I was about to say, and I saw it upon youasws, and as for with us, so it is rather the worn-out youth who are doing it’. So heasws said to me: ‘O Hakam! [7:32] Say: Who has prohibited the adornments of Allah which He has Brought forth for His servants and the good provisions? And this is from what Allahazwj has Brought forth for Hisazwj servants. So As for this room which you see, so it is the ladies chamber, and Iasws am very close to the time of the wedding, and myasws room is the room which you know’.

citation.chapter: The Book of Outfits and the Beautification and the Magnanimity (al-Kafi, vol 6), 8:5
citation.arabic_text: دَخَلْتُ عَلَى أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ ( عليه السلام ) وَ هُوَ فِي بَيْتٍ مُنَجَّدٍ وَ عَلَيْهِ قَمِيصٌ رَطْبٌ وَ مِلْحَفَةٌ مَصْبُوغَةٌ قَدْ أَثَّرَ الصِّبْغُ عَلَى عَاتِقِهِ فَجَعَلْتُ أَنْظُرُ إِلَى الْبَيْتِ وَ أَنْظُرُ إِلَى هَيْئَتِهِ فَقَالَ يَا حَكَمُ مَا تَقُولُ فِي هَذَا فَقُلْتُ وَ مَا عَسَيْتَ أَنْ أَقُولَ وَ أَنَا أَرَاهُ عَلَيْكَ وَ أَمَّا عِنْدَنَا فَإِنَّمَا يَفْعَلُهُ الشَّابُّ الْمُرَهَّقُ فَقَالَ لِي يَا حَكَمُ مَنْ حَرَّمَ زِينَةَ اللَّهِ الَّتِي أَخْرَجَ لِعِبَادِهِ وَ الطَّيِّبَاتِ مِنَ الرِّزْقِ وَ هَذَا مِمَّا أَخْرَجَ اللَّهُ لِعِبَادِهِ فَأَمَّا هَذَا الْبَيْتُ الَّذِي تَرَى فَهُوَ بَيْتُ الْمَرْأَةِ وَ أَنَا قَرِيبُ الْعَهْدِ بِالْعُرْسِ وَ بَيْتِي الْبَيْتُ الَّذِي تَعْرِفُ .

text: Abu Ali Al Ashary, form Muhammad Bin Abdul Jabbar, from Safwan, from Bureyd, from Malik Bin Ayn who said, ‘I went over to Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> and upon him<sup>asws</sup> was a red sheet, new, intensely red. So I smiled when I entered, so he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘It is as if I<sup>asws</sup> know why you are laughing. You are laughing at this cloth, which is upon me<sup>asws</sup>. It was the Saqafiyya woman who compelled me<sup>asws</sup> over it, and I<sup>asws</sup> love her, so she compelled me<sup>asws</sup> upon wearing it’. Then he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘We<sup>asws</sup> do not Pray in this nor do we<sup>asws</sup> Pray in vibrant colours’. He (the narrator) said, ‘Then I went over to him<sup>asws</sup>, and he<sup>asws</sup> had divorced her, so he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘I<sup>asws</sup> heard her disavowing from Ali<sup>asws</sup>, so there was no leeway for me<sup>asws</sup> that I<sup>asws</sup> should keep her and she disavowed from him<sup>asws</sup>’.

citation.chapter: The Book of Outfits and the Beautification and the Magnanimity (al-Kafi, vol 6), 8:5

citation.translation: Abu Ali Al Ashary, form Muhammad Bin Abdul Jabbar, from Safwan, from Bureyd, from Malik Bin Ayn who said, ‘I went over to Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> and upon him<sup>asws</sup> was a red sheet, new, intensely red. So I smiled when I entered, so he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘It is as if I<sup>asws</sup> know why you are laughing. You are laughing at this cloth, which is upon me<sup>asws</sup>. text: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Khalid, from Usman Bin Isa, from Abdullah Bin Muskan, from Al Hassan Al Zayyat Al Basry who said, ‘I and a companion of mine went to Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup>, and he<sup>asws</sup> was is a recently refurbished room, and upon him<sup>asws</sup> was a pink sheet, and had trimmed his<sup>asws</sup> beard and applied kohl. So we asked him<sup>asws</sup> certain questions. So when we arose, he<sup>asws</sup> said to me: ‘O Hassan!’ I said, ‘At your<sup>asws</sup> service!’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘When it is the morning, so come to me, you and your companion’. So I said, ‘Yes, may I be sacrificed for you<sup>asws</sup>’. So when it was the morning, we went over to him<sup>asws</sup>, and he<sup>asws</sup> was in a room in which there was nothing except for a mat and upon him<sup>asws</sup> was a coarse shirt. Then he<sup>asws</sup> faced towards my companions, so he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘O brother of the people of Al-Basra! You came over to me<sup>asws</sup> yesterday and I<sup>asws</sup> was in the wife’s chamber, and yesterday was her day, and the room was her room, and the chattels were her chattels. So she adorned for me<sup>asws</sup> upon (the condition) that I<sup>asws</sup> would adorn for her just as she had adorned for me<sup>asws</sup>, therefore do not let anything enter your heart’. So my companion said to him<sup>asws</sup>, ‘May I be sacrificed for you<sup>asws</sup>! By Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, there had entered something into my heart, so as for now, so by Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, Allah<sup>azwj</sup> has Removed what was (in my heart), and I know that the truth is in what you<sup>asws</sup> say’.

citation.chapter: The Book of Outfits and the Beautification and the Magnanimity (al-Kafi, vol 6), 8:5

citation.arabic_text: قُلْتُ لِأَبِي جَعْفَرٍ الثَّانِي ( عليه السلام ) إِنَّ بِلَادَنَا بِلَادٌ بَارِدَةٌ فَمَا تَقُولُ فِي لُبْسِ هَذَا الْوَبَرِ قَالَ الْبَسْ مِنْهَا مَا أُكِلَ وَ ضُمِنَ .
citation.translation: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad from Muhammad Bin Isa, from Usman Bin Saeed, from Abdul Kareem Al Hamdany, from Abu Tamama who said, ‘I said to Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> the 2<sup>nd</sup> that our city is a cold city, so what are you<sup>asws</sup> saying regarding wearing of these furs’. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Wear from it what can be eaten (Permissible animals), and responsibly’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: ضعيف على المشهور - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (2/328)

text: Abu Ali Al Ashary, from Muhammad in Abdul Jabbar, from Ibn Fazzal, from Muhammad Bin Al Husayn Bin Kaseer Al Khazzaz, from his father who said, ‘I saw Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, and upon him<sup>asws</sup> was a coarse, rough shirt underneath his<sup>asws</sup> clothes, and above it was a woolen coat, and above it was a coarse shirt. So I touched it and said, ‘May I be sacrificed for you<sup>asws</sup>! The people are disliking the woolen dress’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Never! My<sup>asws</sup> father<sup>asws</sup> Muhammad<sup>asws</sup> Bin Ali<sup>asws</sup> wore it, and Ali<sup>asws</sup> Bin Al-Husayn<sup>asws</sup> wore it, and they<sup>asws</sup> used to wear the roughest of their clothes whenever they<sup>asws</sup> stood for the Prayer, and we<sup>asws</sup> do that (as well)’.

citation.chapter: The Book of Outfits and the Beautification and the Magnanimity (al-Kafi, vol 6), 8:8
citation.arabic_text: رَأَيْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) وَ عَلَيْهِ قَمِيصٌ غَلِيظٌ خَشِنٌ تَحْتَ ثِيَابِهِ وَ فَوْقَهَا جُبَّةُ صُوفٍ وَ فَوْقَهَا قَمِيصٌ غَلِيظٌ فَمَسِسْتُهَا فَقُلْتُ جُعِلْتُ فِدَاكَ إِنَّ النَّاسَ يَكْرَهُونَ لِبَاسَ الصُّوفِ فَقَالَ كَلَّا كَانَ أَبِي مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ عَلِيٍّ ( عليه السلام ) يَلْبَسُهَا وَ كَانَ عَلِيُّ بْنُ الْحُسَيْنِ ( عليه السلام ) يَلْبَسُهَا وَ كَانُوا ( عليهم السلام ) يَلْبَسُونَ أَغْلَظَ ثِيَابِهِمْ إِذَا قَامُوا إِلَى الصَّلَاةِ وَ نَحْنُ نَفْعَلُ ذَلِكَ .

text: Ali Bin Muhammad Bin Bundar, from Ahmad Bin Abu Abdullah, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Abu Nasr, from Abu Jareer Al Qummy who said, ‘I asked Al-Reza<sup>asws</sup> about the feather, is it pure?’ So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘My<sup>asws</sup> father<sup>asws</sup> used to stuff the pillow with the feathers’.

citation.chapter: The Book of Outfits and the Beautification and the Magnanimity (al-Kafi, vol 6), 8:8
citation.arabic_text: سَأَلْتُ الرِّضَا ( عليه السلام ) عَنِ الرِّيشِ أَ ذَكِيٌّ هُوَ فَقَالَ كَانَ أَبِي ( عليه السلام ) يَتَوَسَّدُ الرِّيشَ .

text: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad Bin Isa, from Hareyz, from Zurara who said, ‘Abu Ja’farasws Prayed upon one of hisasws children, and upon himasws was a yellow Al-Khazz coat and a yellow Al-Khazz shawl’.

citation.chapter: The Book of Outfits and the Beautification and the Magnanimity (al-Kafi, vol 6), 8:9
citation.arabic_text: خَرَجَ أَبُو جَعْفَرٍ ( عليه السلام ) يُصَلِّي عَلَى بَعْضِ أَطْفَالِهِمْ وَ عَلَيْهِ جُبَّةُ خَزٍّ صَفْرَاءُ وَ مِطْرَفُ خَزٍّ أَصْفَرُ .
citation.translation: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad Bin Isa, from Hareyz, from Zurara who said, ‘Abu Ja’farasws Prayed upon one of hisasws children, and upon himasws was a yellow Al-Khazz coat and a yellow Al-Khazz shawl’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: حسن - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (2/329)

text: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Abu Nasr, (It has been narrated) from Abu Al-Hassan Al-Rezaasws having said: ‘Aliasws Bin Al-Husaynasws used to wear Al-Khazz coat of fifty Dinars, and Al-Khazz shawl of fifty Dinars’.

citation.chapter: The Book of Outfits and the Beautification and the Magnanimity (al-Kafi, vol 6), 8:9
citation.arabic_text: كَانَ عَلِيُّ بْنُ الْحُسَيْنِ ( عليه السلام ) يَلْبَسُ الْجُبَّةَ الْخَزَّ بِخَمْسِينَ دِينَاراً وَ الْمِطْرَفَ الْخَزَّ بِخَمْسِينَ دِينَاراً .
citation.translation: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Abu Nasr, (It has been narrated) from Abu Al-Hassan Al-Rezaasws having said: ‘Aliasws Bin Al-Husaynasws used to wear Al-Khazz coat of fifty Dinars, and Al-Khazz shawl of fifty Dinars’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: ضعيف على المشهور - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (2/330)

text: Abu Ali Al Ashary, from Muhammad Bin Abdul Jabbar, from Safwan Bin Yahya, from Abdul Rahman Bin Al Hajjaj who said, ‘A man asked Abu Abdullahasws and I was in hisasws presence, about Al-Khazz (Otter-skin?) dress. So heasws said: ‘There is no problem with it’. So the man said, ‘May I be sacrificed for youasws! These are dogs coming out from the water’. So Abu Abdullahasws said: ‘When it comes out from the water, does it live outside the water?’ So the man said, ‘No’. Heasws said, ‘So there is no problem’.

citation.chapter: The Book of Outfits and the Beautification and the Magnanimity (al-Kafi, vol 6), 8:9
citation.arabic_text: سَأَلَ أَبَا عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) رَجُلٌ وَ أَنَا عِنْدَهُ عَنْ جُلُودِ الْخَزِّ فَقَالَ لَيْسَ بِهَا بَأْسٌ فَقَالَ الرَّجُلُ جُعِلْتُ فِدَاكَ إِنَّهَا فِي بِلَادِي وَ إِنَّمَا هِيَ كِلَابٌ تَخْرُجُ مِنَ الْمَاءِ فَقَالَ أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) إِذَا خَرَجَتْ مِنَ الْمَاءِ تَعِيشُ خَارِجَةً مِنَ الْمَاءِ فَقَالَ الرَّجُلُ لَا قَالَ فَلَا بَأْسَ.
citation.translation: Abu Ali Al Ashary, from Muhammad Bin Abdul Jabbar, from Safwan Bin Yahya, from Abdul Rahman Bin Al Hajjaj who said, ‘A man asked Abu Abdullahasws and I was in hisasws presence, about Al-Khazz (Otter-skin?) dress. So heasws said: ‘There is no problem with it’. So the man said, ‘May I be sacrificed for youasws! These are dogs coming out from the water’. So Abu Abdullahasws said: ‘When it comes out from the water, does it live outside the water?’ So the man said, ‘No’. Heasws said, ‘So there is no problem’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: صحيح - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (2/330)

text: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Al Hassan Bin Ali Al Washa, (It has been narrated) from Abu Al-Hassan Al-Rezaasws, said, ‘I heard himasws saying: ‘Aliasws Bin Al-Husaynasws used to wear Al-Khazz in the winter, and Al-Khazz shawl, and a hood of Al-Khazz. So heasws would be wearing it in the winter, and sell the shawl in the summer and give charity with its price. Then heasws was saying [7:32] Say: Who has prohibited the adornments of Allah which He has Brought forth for His servants and the good provisions?’.

citation.chapter: The Book of Outfits and the Beautification and the Magnanimity (al-Kafi, vol 6), 8:9
citation.arabic_text: سَمِعْتُهُ يَقُولُ كَانَ عَلِيُّ بْنُ الْحُسَيْنِ ( عليه السلام ) يَلْبَسُ فِي الشِّتَاءِ الْخَزَّ وَ الْمِطْرَفَ الْخَزَّ وَ الْقَلَنْسُوَةَ الْخَزَّ فَيَشْتُو فِيهِ وَ يَبِيعُ الْمِطْرَفَ فِي الصَّيْفِ وَ يَتَصَدَّقُ بِثَمَنِهِ ثُمَّ يَقُولُ مَنْ حَرَّمَ زِينَةَ اللَّهِ الَّتِي أَخْرَجَ لِعِبادِهِ وَ الطَّيِّباتِ مِنَ الرِّزْقِ .
citation.translation: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Al Hassan Bin Ali Al Washa, (It has been narrated) from Abu Al-Hassan Al-Rezaasws, said, ‘I heard himasws saying: ‘Aliasws Bin Al-Husaynasws used to wear Al-Khazz in the winter, and Al-Khazz shawl, and a hood of Al-Khazz. So heasws would be wearing it in the winter, and sell the shawl in the summer and give charity with its price. Then heasws was saying [7:32] Say: Who has prohibited the adornments of Allah which He has Brought forth for His servants and the good provisions?’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: ضعيف على المشهور - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (22/330)

text: Abu Ali Al Ashary, from Muhammad Bin Abdul Jabbar, from Safwan Bin Yahya, from Al Ays Bin Al Qasim, from Abu Dawood Yusuf Bin Ibrahim who said, ‘I went over to Abu Abdullahasws and upon me was an Al-Khazz cloak, and its lining was of Khazz, and a pallium of Khazz, of high quality. So I said, ‘Upon me are clothes which I dislike to wear’. So heasws said: ‘And what is it?’ I said, ‘This pallium of mine’. Heasws said: ‘And what is the matter with the pallium?’ I said, ‘It is of Khazz’. Heasws said: ‘And what is the matter with Al-Khazz?’ I said, ‘Its lining is of silk’. Heasws said: ‘And what is the matter with the silk?’ Heasws said: ‘Do not dislike it if the lining of the cloth happens to be of silk, nor its buttons, nor its emblem. But rather it is disliked, the entirety of it from the silk, for the men and it is not disliked for the women’.

citation.chapter: The Book of Outfits and the Beautification and the Magnanimity (al-Kafi, vol 6), 8:9
citation.arabic_text: دَخَلْتُ عَلَى أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) وَ عَلَيَّ قَبَاءُ خَزٍّ وَ بِطَانَتُهُ خَزٌّ وَ طَيْلَسَانُ خَزٍّ مُرْتَفِعٌ فَقُلْتُ إِنَّ عَلَيَّ ثَوْباً أَكْرَهُ لُبْسَهُ فَقَالَ وَ مَا هُوَ قُلْتُ طَيْلَسَانِي هَذَا قَالَ وَ مَا بَالُ الطَّيْلَسَانِ قُلْتُ هُوَ خَزٌّ قَالَ وَ مَا بَالُ الْخَزِّ قُلْتُ سَدَاهُ إِبْرِيسَمٌ قَالَ وَ مَا بَالُ الْإِبْرِيسَمِ قَالَ لَا يُكْرَهُ أَنْ يَكُونَ سَدَى الثَّوْبِ إِبْرِيسَماً وَ لَا زِرُّهُ وَ لَا عَلَمُهُ إِنَّمَا يُكْرَهُ الْمُصْمَتُ مِنَ الْإِبْرِيسَمِ لِلرِّجَالِ وَ لَا يُكْرَهُ لِلنِّسَاءِ .

So I said, ‘Upon me are clothes which I dislike to wear’. So heasws said: ‘And what is it?’ I said, ‘This pallium of mine’. Heasws said: ‘And what is the matter with the pallium?’ I said, ‘It is of Khazz’. Heasws said: ‘And what is the matter with Al-Khazz?’ I said, ‘Its lining is of silk’. citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: مجهول - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (2/330)

text: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Abu Abdullah, from Musa Bin Al Qasim, from Amro Bin Usman, form Abu Jameela, from a man, (It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’farasws having said: ‘The group of the Progenyasws of Muhammadsaww, weasws wear Al-Khazz and the Yemeni (clothes)’.

citation.chapter: The Book of Outfits and the Beautification and the Magnanimity (al-Kafi, vol 6), 8:9
citation.arabic_text: إِنَّا مَعَاشِرَ آلِ مُحَمَّدٍ نَلْبَسُ الْخَزَّ وَ الْيُمْنَةَ .
citation.translation: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Abu Abdullah, from Musa Bin Al Qasim, from Amro Bin Usman, form Abu Jameela, from a man, (It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’farasws having said: ‘The group of the Progenyasws of Muhammadsaww, weasws wear Al-Khazz and the Yemeni (clothes)’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: ضعيف - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (22/331)

text: From him, from his father, from Sa’ad Bin Sa’ad who said, ‘I asked Al-Rezaasws about the skin of Al-Khazz (Otter?), so heasws said: ‘It is that Al-Khazz which weasws wear’. So I said, ‘May I be sacrificed for youasws! That is the fur?’ So heasws said: ‘When its fur is Permissible, so its skin is Permissible (to wear)’.

citation.chapter: The Book of Outfits and the Beautification and the Magnanimity (al-Kafi, vol 6), 8:9
citation.arabic_text: سَأَلْتُ الرِّضَا ( عليه السلام ) عَنْ جُلُودِ الْخَزِّ فَقَالَ هُوَ ذَا نَلْبَسُ الْخَزَّ فَقُلْتُ جُعِلْتُ فِدَاكَ ذَاكَ الْوَبَرُ فَقَالَ إِذَا حَلَّ وَبَرُهُ حَلَّ جِلْدُهُ .
citation.translation: From him, from his father, from Sa’ad Bin Sa’ad who said, ‘I asked Al-Rezaasws about the skin of Al-Khazz (Otter?), so heasws said: ‘It is that Al-Khazz which weasws wear’. citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: صحيح - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (22/331)

text: From him, from Ja’far Bin Isa who said, ‘I wrote to Abu Al-Hassan Al-Rezaasws asking himasws about the animals from which Al-Khazz is made, from their fur, is it a predator?’ So heasws wrote: ‘Al-Husaynasws Bin Aliasws wore Al-Khazz, and from after himasws, myasws grandfatherasws’.

citation.chapter: The Book of Outfits and the Beautification and the Magnanimity (al-Kafi, vol 6), 8:9
citation.arabic_text: كَتَبْتُ إِلَى أَبِي الْحَسَنِ الرِّضَا ( عليه السلام ) أَسْأَلُهُ عَنِ الدَّوَابِّ الَّتِي يُعْمَلُ الْخَزُّ مِنْ وَبَرِهَا أَ سِبَاعٌ هِيَ فَكَتَبَ ( عليه السلام ) لَبِسَ الْخَزَّ الْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ عَلِيٍّ وَ مِنْ بَعْدِهِ جَدِّي ( عليهما السلام ) .
