citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: حسن - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (2/331)

text: Abu Ali Al Ashary, from Muhammad Bin Salim, from Ahmad Bin Al Nazar, from Amro Bin Shimr, from Jabir, (It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’farasws having said: ‘Al-Husaynasws Bin Aliasws was killed and upon himasws was a coat of dark Khazz, so they found therein sixty three tears from the strikes with the sword, and the stabbings with the spear, or the shootings with the arrow’.

citation.chapter: The Book of Outfits and the Beautification and the Magnanimity (al-Kafi, vol 6), 8:9
citation.arabic_text: قُتِلَ الْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ عَلِيٍّ ( عليه السلام ) وَ عَلَيْهِ جُبَّةُ خَزٍّ دَكْنَاءُ فَوَجَدُوا فِيهَا ثَلَاثَةً وَ سِتِّينَ مِنْ بَيْنِ ضَرْبَةٍ بِالسَّيْفِ وَ طَعْنَةٍ بِالرُّمْحِ أَوْ رَمْيَةٍ بِالسَّهْمِ .
citation.translation: Abu Ali Al Ashary, from Muhammad Bin Salim, from Ahmad Bin Al Nazar, from Amro Bin Shimr, from Jabir, (It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’farasws having said: ‘Al-Husaynasws Bin Aliasws was killed and upon himasws was a coat of dark Khazz, so they found therein sixty three tears from the strikes with the sword, and the stabbings with the spear, or the shootings with the arrow’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: ضعيف - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (22/331)

text: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Muhammad Bin Isa, from Hafs Bin Amro Abu Muhammad the announcer of Ali Bin Yaqteen who said, ‘I saw upon Abu Abdullahasws, and heasws was Praying in the garden, a quince-coloured Khazz cloak’.

citation.chapter: The Book of Outfits and the Beautification and the Magnanimity (al-Kafi, vol 6), 8:9
citation.arabic_text: رَأَيْتُ عَلَى أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) وَ هُوَ يُصَلِّي فِي الرَّوْضَةِ جُبَّةَ خَزٍّ سَفَرْجَلِيَّةً .
citation.translation: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Muhammad Bin Isa, from Hafs Bin Amro Abu Muhammad the announcer of Ali Bin Yaqteen who said, ‘I saw upon Abu Abdullahasws, and heasws was Praying in the garden, a quince-coloured Khazz cloak’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: ضعيف على المشهور - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (22/331)

text: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Ibn Fazzal, and Sahl Bin Ziyad, form Muhammad Bin Isa, from Yasser who said, ‘Abu Al-Hassanasws said to me: ‘Buy Khazz for yourself, and if you so desire to, so Washy’. So I said, ‘They are all Al-Washy’. So heasws said: ‘And what is Al-Washy?’ I said, ‘What does not happen to have cotton in it. They (people) are saying, it is Prohibited’. Heasws said: ‘Wear what has cotton in it’.

citation.chapter: The Book of Outfits and the Beautification and the Magnanimity (al-Kafi, vol 6), 8:10
citation.arabic_text: قَالَ لِي أَبُو الْحَسَنِ ( عليه السلام ) اشْتَرِ لِنَفْسِكَ خَزّاً وَ إِنْ شِئْتَ فَوَشْياً فَقُلْتُ كُلَّ الْوَشْيِ فَقَالَ وَ مَا الْوَشْيُ قُلْتُ مَا لَمْ يَكُنْ فِيهِ قُطْنٌ يَقُولُونَ إِنَّهُ حَرَامٌ قَالَ الْبَسْ مَا فِيهِ قُطْنٌ .
citation.translation: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Ibn Fazzal, and Sahl Bin Ziyad, form Muhammad Bin Isa, from Yasser who said, ‘Abu Al-Hassanasws said to me: ‘Buy Khazz for yourself, and if you so desire to, so Washy’. So I said, ‘They are all Al-Washy’. So heasws said: ‘And what is Al-Washy?’ I said, ‘What does not happen to have cotton in it. They (people) are saying, it is Prohibited’. Heasws said: ‘Wear what has cotton in it’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: ضعيف على المشهور - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (2/332)

text: Humeyd Bin Ziyad, from Muhammad Bin Isa, from Al Abbas Bin Hilal Al Shamy, A slave of Abu Al-Hassanasws, from himasws, said, ‘I said to himasws, ‘May I be sacrificed for youasws! How fascinating to the people is the one who eats tasteless food and wears rough clothes and is humble’. So heasws said: ‘But do you not know that Yusufas, a Prophetas son of a Prophetas was wearing gowns of embroidered brocade and buttons of gold, and heas would sit in the gathering of the progeny of Pharaohla, giving judgements. So the people were not needy to hisas clothes, but rather they were needy to hisas equitable decisions. And rather what is needed from the Imam (leader) is that he should speak the truth, and when he makes a promise, fulfils it, and when he gives a judgement, does justice. Allahazwj did not Prohibit food nor drinks from the Permissible, but rather Heazwj Prohibited from the Prohibitions, be it little or a lot, and Allahazwj Mighty and Majestic has Said [7:32] Say: Who has prohibited the adornments of Allah which He has Brought forth for His servants and the good provisions?’.

citation.chapter: The Book of Outfits and the Beautification and the Magnanimity (al-Kafi, vol 6), 8:11
citation.arabic_text: قُلْتُ لَهُ جُعِلْتُ فِدَاكَ مَا أَعْجَبَ إِلَى النَّاسِ مَنْ يَأْكُلُ الْجَشِبَ وَ يَلْبَسُ الْخَشِنَ وَ يَتَخَشَّعُ فَقَالَ أَ مَا عَلِمْتَ أَنَّ يُوسُفَ ( عليه السلام ) نَبِيٌّ ابْنُ نَبِيٍّ كَانَ يَلْبَسُ أَقْبِيَةَ الدِّيبَاجِ مَزْرُورَةً بِالذَّهَبِ وَ يَجْلِسُ فِي مَجَالِسِ آلِ فِرْعَوْنَ يَحْكُمُ فَلَمْ يَحْتَجِ النَّاسُ إِلَى لِبَاسِهِ وَ إِنَّمَا احْتَاجُوا إِلَى قِسْطِهِ وَ إِنَّمَا يُحْتَاجُ مِنَ الْإِمَامِ فِي أَنَّ إِذَا قَالَ صَدَقَ وَ إِذَا وَعَدَ أَنْجَزَ وَ إِذَا حَكَمَ عَدَلَ إِنَّ اللَّهَ لَا يُحَرِّمُ طَعَاماً وَ لَا شَرَاباً مِنْ حَلَالٍ وَ إِنَّمَا حَرَّمَ الْحَرَامَ قَلَّ أَوْ كَثُرَ وَ قَدْ قَالَ اللَّهُ عَزَّ وَ جَلَّ قُلْ مَنْ حَرَّمَ زِينَةَ اللَّهِ الَّتِي أَخْرَجَ لِعِبادِهِ وَ الطَّيِّباتِ مِنَ الرِّزْقِ .

text: Muhammad Bin Yahya, and someone else, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Al Husayn Bin Saeed, from al Nazar Bin Suweyd, from Al Qasim Bin Suleyman, form Jarrah Al Madainy, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> that he<sup>asws</sup> disliked wearing the shirt hemmed with the brocade, and disliked the silk clothes, and the embroidered clothes, and disliked red cushion covers, for these are the cushions of Iblees<sup>la</sup>’.

text: From him, from his father, from Al Qasim Bin Urwa, from Ubeyd Bin Zurara, Abu Abdullahasws has said: ‘There is no problem with Al-Qazz (silk) clothes when it was either seamed or united with the cotton or flax’.

text: From him, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Abu Nasr who said, ‘Al-Hassan Bin Qiyama asked Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> about the clothes seamed with the Al-Qazz (silk), and the cotton, and Al-Qazz (silk) is more than the half, can one Pray in it?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘There is no problem’. - and Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> used to have gowns from it like that’.

citation.arabic_text: سَأَلَ الْحَسَنُ بْنُ قِيَامَا أَبَا الْحَسَنِ ( عليه السلام ) عَنِ الثَّوْبِ الْمُلْحَمِ بِالْقَزِّ وَ الْقُطْنِ وَ الْقَزُّ أَكْثَرُ مِنَ النِّصْفِ أَ يُصَلَّى فِيهِ قَالَ لَا بَأْسَ وَ قَدْ كَانَ لِأَبِي الْحَسَنِ ( عليه السلام ) مِنْهُ جِبَابٌ كَذَلِكَ .

text: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Abu Ayoub, from Sama’at, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws having said: ‘It is not befitting for the woman that she should wear the pure silk and she is in Ihraam (for Hajj), and as for during the heat and the cold, so there is no problem’.

citation.arabic_text: لَا يَنْبَغِي لِلْمَرْأَةِ أَنْ تَلْبَسَ الْحَرِيرَ الْمَحْضَ وَ هِيَ مُحْرِمَةٌ وَ أَمَّا فِي الْحَرِّ وَ الْبَرْدِ فَلَا بَأْسَ .

text: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from Salih Bin Al Sandy, from Ja’far Bin Basheer, from Abu Al Hassan Al Ahmasy, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Abu Saeed asked him<sup>asws</sup> about the gown, and I was in his<sup>asws</sup> presence, its hemming being of silk, can one wear it and he was feeling cold?’ So he<sup>asws</sup> instructed him that he can wear it’.

text: Al Husayn Bin Muhammad, from Moala Bin Muhammad, from Al Hassan Bin Ali Al Washa, from Ahmad Bin Aiz, from Abu Khadeeja, from Moala Bin Khunays, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws having said: ‘Aliasws was among you all, so heasws went over to the Clan of Deywan and bought three garments with one Dinar – the shirt which was up to above the heel, and the trouser up to the half of the leg, and the cloak from hisasws front was up to his chest, and from behind himasws was up to hisasws lower back. Then heasws raised hisasws hands towards the sky, and heasws did not cease to Praise Allahazwj what Heazwj has Clothed himasws with until heasws entered hisasws house. Then heasws said: ‘This is the dress which is befitting for the Muslims that they should be wearing it’. Abu Abdullahasws said: ‘But weasws are not able to wear it today, and were weasws to do it, they would say, ‘Insane’, and they would say, ‘Show-off’, and Allahazwj the High is Saying [74:4] And your garments do purify’. Heasws said: ‘And your clothes, raise these and do not let it flow (upon the ground), and when ourasws Qaimasws rises, this would be the clothing’.

citation.chapter: The Book of Outfits and the Beautification and the Magnanimity (al-Kafi, vol 6), 8:12

text: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Muhammad Bin Isa, from Yunus Bin Yaqoub, from Abdullah Bin Yaqoub, from Abdullah Bin Hilal who said, ‘Abu Abdullahasws ordered me that I should buy a trouser for himasws. So I said to himasws, ‘I could not find except for the extensive ones’. Heasws said: ‘Cut off from it and hem it’. He (the narrator) said, ‘Then heasws said: ‘Myasws fatherasws said: ‘And whatever exceeds the two heels, so it is in the Fire’. Muhammad Bin yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from yunus Bin Yaqoub – similar to it’.

text: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Al Hakam, from Abdul Rahman Bin Usman, (It has been narrated) from a man from the people of Al-Yamama who was with Abu Al-Hassanasws (7th Imamasws) was imprisoned at Baghdad, said, ‘Abu Al-Hassanasws said to me: ‘Allahazwj the High Said to Hisazwj Prophetsaww [74:4] And your garments do purify, and hissaww garment was clean, but rather hesaww was Commanded with the rolling-up’.

citation.arabic_text: قَالَ لِي أَبُو الْحَسَنِ ( عليه السلام ) إِنَّ اللَّهَ تَعَالَى قَالَ لِنَبِيِّهِ ( صلى الله عليه وآله ) وَ ثِيابَكَ فَطَهِّرْ وَ كَانَتْ ثِيَابُهُ طَاهِرَةً وَ إِنَّمَا أَمَرَهُ بِالتَّشْمِيرِ .

text: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, form Ibn Mahboub, from Hisham Bin Salim, from Abu Baseer, (It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> that the Prophet<sup>saww</sup> advised a man from the Clan of Tameem so he<sup>saww</sup> said to him: ‘Beware of letting the trousers and the shirt to drag, for that is from the fancifulness and Allah<sup>azwj</sup> does not Love the fanciful’.

citation.arabic_text: لَهُ إِيَّاكَ وَ إِسْبَالَ الْإِزَارِ وَ الْقَمِيصِ فَإِنَّ ذَلِكَ مِنَ الْمَخِيلَةِ وَ اللَّهُ لَا يُحِبُّ الْمَخِيلَةَ .

text: Abu Ali Al Ashary, from Al Hassan Bin Ali Al Kufy, from Ubeys Bin Hisham, from Aban, from Abu Hamza, raising it, said, ‘Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> looked at a youth who had relaxed his trouser. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘O my<sup>asws</sup> son! Raise your trouser, for it is more lasting for your clothes, and more cleansing for your heart (from fancifulness)’.

citation.chapter: The Book of Outfits and the Beautification and the Magnanimity (al-Kafi, vol 6), 8:12

text: A number of our copanions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Khalid, from his father, from Muhammad Bin Sinan, from Al Hassan Al Sayqal who said, ‘Abu Abdullahasws said to me: ‘Would you like measws to show you the shirt of Aliasws in which heasws was struck, or Iasws show youasws hisasws blood?’ I said, ‘Yes’. So heasws called for it, and it was in a basket. So heasws extracted it and displayed it. It was a cotton-like shirt resembling Al-Sunbulany (made in), and there was in the spot of the pocket up to the ground a stain of blood whiter than the milk, resembling a stroke of the sword. Heasws said: ‘This is the shirt of Aliasws in which heasws was struck, and these are the traces of hisasws blood’. So I measured its body by the open palm (Shibr), so it was three open-palm’s width and I measured its bottom by the open palm (Shibr), so it was twelve open-palm’s length’.

citation.chapter: The Book of Outfits and the Beautification and the Magnanimity (al-Kafi, vol 6), 8:12

text: Abu Ali Al Ashary, from Muhammad Bin Abdul Jabbar, and Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, altogether from Al Hajjal, from Sa’alba Bin Maymoun, form Zurara Bin Ayn who said, ‘I saw the shirt of Aliasws in which heasws was killed, in the presence of Abu Ja’farasws, so its bottom was of twelve Shibr (open-palm’s width), and its width was of three Shibr (open-palm’s width), and I saw blood stains in it’.

Then heasws measured out its display by six Shibr (open-palm’s width). Then heasws tore it and said, ‘Stitch its borders and trim its edges’.

text: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Al Nowfaly, from Al Sakuny, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> let me<sup>asws</sup> know: ‘Whenever you<sup>asws</sup> wear new clothes, you<sup>asws</sup> should be saying: ‘The Praise is for Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Who Clothed me<sup>asws</sup> from the clothes what I<sup>asws</sup> beautify with among the people. O Allah<sup>azwj</sup>! Make these to be clothes of Blessings, working in these according to Your<sup>azwj</sup> Pleasure and build Your<sup>azwj</sup> Masjids in these’. He<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘O Ali<sup>asws</sup>! The one who says that would not have worn his shirt but Allah<sup>azwj</sup> would have Forgiven him’. And in another copy: ‘He would not be hit by anything he dislikes’.

citation.chapter: The Book of Outfits and the Beautification and the Magnanimity (al-Kafi, vol 6), 8:13

text: Al Husayn Bin Muhammad, from Moala Bin Muhammad, from Muhammad Bin Ali Al Hamdany, from Al Husayn Bin Abu Usman, from Khalid Al Jawwad who said, ‘I heard Abu Al-Hassan Musa<sup>asws</sup> saying: ‘It would have been more befitting for one of you whenever he wore new clothes, that he should pass his hand over it and he should be saying, ‘The Praise is for Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Who Clothed me what I cover my nakedness with, and beautify with among the people, and adorn with between them’.

citation.chapter: The Book of Outfits and the Beautification and the Magnanimity (al-Kafi, vol 6), 8:13
citation.arabic_text: سَمِعْتُ أَبَا الْحَسَنِ مُوسَى ( عليه السلام ) يَقُولُ قَدْ يَنْبَغِي لِأَحَدِكُمْ إِذَا لَبِسَ الثَّوْبَ الْجَدِيدَ أَنْ يُمِرَّ يَدَهُ عَلَيْهِ وَ يَقُولَ الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ الَّذِي كَسَانِي مَا أُوَارِي بِهِ عَوْرَتِي وَ أَتَجَمَّلُ بِهِ فِي النَّاسِ وَ أَتَزَيَّنُ بِهِ بَيْنَهُمْ .

text: Ali Bin Muhammad, from Salih Bin Abu Hammad, from someone else, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws having said: ‘The one who recites [97:1] We have indeed revealed this thirty two times in a new utensil, and sprinkle his new clothes with it when he wears it, he would be eating in ease (plentifully) for as long as a thread from it remains’.

citation.chapter: The Book of Outfits and the Beautification and the Magnanimity (al-Kafi, vol 6), 8:13
citation.arabic_text: مَنْ قَرَأَ إِنَّا أَنْزَلْنَاهُ ثِنْتَيْنِ وَ ثَلَاثِينَ مَرَّةً فِي إِنَاءٍ جَدِيدٍ وَ رَشَّ بِهِ ثَوْبَهُ الْجَدِيدَ إِذَا لَبِسَهُ لَمْ يَزَلْ يَأْكُلُ فِي سَعَةٍ مَا بَقِيَ مِنْهُ سِلْكٌ .
citation.translation: Ali Bin Muhammad, from Salih Bin Abu Hammad, from someone else, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws having said: ‘The one who recites [97:1] We have indeed revealed this thirty two times in a new utensil, and sprinkle his new clothes with it when he wears it, he would be eating in ease (plentifully) for as long as a thread from it remains’.

text: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Al Qasim Bin Yahya, from his grandfather Al Hassan Bin Rashid, from Muhammad Bin Muslim, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws having said: ‘Amir Al-Momineenasws said: ‘Whenever Allahazwj Clothes a Believer with new clothes, so let him perform ablution, and let him Pray two cycles reciting in both of these the Mother of the Book (Chapter 1 – Surah Al-Fatiha), and The Verse of the Chair (Chapter 2:255 Ayat Al-Kursy), and [112:1] Say: He Allah is One (Surah Al-Ikhlaas), and [97:1] We have indeed revealed this (Chapter 97). Then let him Praise Allahazwj Who Veiled his nakedness, and Adorned him among the people, and let him frequently say, ‘There is no Might or power except with Allahazwj’, so he would not disobey Allahazwj in it, and for him would be an Angel for every thread in it, Sanctifying Allahazwj for him, and seeking Forgiveness for him, and beseeching for Mercy to be upon him’.

citation.chapter: The Book of Outfits and the Beautification and the Magnanimity (al-Kafi, vol 6), 8:13
citation.arabic_text: قَالَ أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ ( عليه السلام ) إِذَا كَسَا اللَّهُ تَعَالَى الْمُؤْمِنَ ثَوْباً جَدِيداً فَلْيَتَوَضَّأْ وَ لْيُصَلِّ رَكْعَتَيْنِ يَقْرَأُ فِيهِمَا أُمَّ الْكِتَابِ وَ آيَةَ الْكُرْسِيِّ وَ قُلْ هُوَ اللَّهُ أَحَدٌ وَ إِنَّا أَنْزَلْنَاهُ ثُمَّ لْيَحْمَدِ اللَّهَ الَّذِي سَتَرَ عَوْرَتَهُ وَ زَيَّنَهُ فِي النَّاسِ وَ لْيُكْثِرْ مِنْ قَوْلِ لَا حَوْلَ وَ لَا قُوَّةَ إِلَّا بِاللَّهِ فَإِنَّهُ لَا يَعْصِي اللَّهَ فِيهِ وَ لَهُ بِكُلِّ سِلْكٍ فِيهِ مَلَكٌ يُقَدِّسُ لَهُ وَ يَسْتَغْفِرُ لَهُ وَ يَتَرَحَّمُ عَلَيْهِ .
citation.translation: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Al Qasim Bin Yahya, from his grandfather Al Hassan Bin Rashid, from Muhammad Bin Muslim, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws having said: ‘Amir Al-Momineenasws said: ‘Whenever Allahazwj Clothes a Believer with new clothes, so let him perform ablution, and let him Pray two cycles reciting in both of these the Mother of the Book (Chapter 1 – Surah Al-Fatiha), and The Verse of the Chair (Chapter 2:255 Ayat Al-Kursy), and [112:1] Say: He Allah is One (Surah Al-Ikhlaas), and [97:1] We have indeed revealed this (Chapter 97). text: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ali Bin Al Husayn Al Neyshapouri, form Abdullah Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Al Rayyan, from Yunus, from Umar Bin Yazeed who said, ‘I wanted to go over to Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, so I wore my clothes and displayed my new pallium which I was fascinated with. So a camel squeezed me in one of the streets, so it ruptured from every direction. Thus I was gloomy due to that. So I came over to Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, and he<sup>asws</sup> looked at my pallium, so he<sup>asws</sup> said to me: ‘What is the matter I<sup>asws</sup> see you with torn clothes?’ So I informed him with the story. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘O Umar! Whenever you wear new clothes, so say, ‘There is no god except for Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, Muhammad<sup>saww</sup> is His<sup>azwj</sup> Rasool<sup>saww</sup>’, you would be free from the misfortunes; and whenever you love something so do not mention it frequently, for that is from what crushes you; and whenever there is a need for you to a man, so do not insult him from his behind, for Allah<sup>azwj</sup> would Make that to occur in his heart’.

citation.chapter: The Book of Outfits and the Beautification and the Magnanimity (al-Kafi, vol 6), 8:13

text: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Al Hassan Bin Ali, from Ali Bin Iqba, from Is’haq Bin Ammar, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘The lowest form of extravagance is discarding the remnants of the vessel, and the routine of wearing the protective clothing, and throwing away cores’.

citation.chapter: The Book of Outfits and the Beautification and the Magnanimity (al-Kafi, vol 6), 8:14
citation.arabic_text: أَدْنَى الْإِسْرَافِ هِرَاقَةُ فَضْلِ الْإِنَاءِ وَ ابْتِذَالُ ثَوْبِ الصَّوْنِ وَ إِلْقَاءُ النَّوَى .
citation.translation: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Al Hassan Bin Ali, from Ali Bin Iqba, from Is’haq Bin Ammar, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘The lowest form of extravagance is discarding the remnants of the vessel, and the routine of wearing the protective clothing, and throwing away cores’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: موثق - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (22/342)

text: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Muhammad Bin Al Husayn, from Muhammad Bin Ismail, from Salih Bin Uqba, from Suleyman Bin Salih who said, ‘I said to Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, ‘What is the lowest of the extravagance?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Your routinely wearing of your protective clothing, and your discarding the remnants of your utensil, and your eating the dates and your throwing with the core over here and over there’.

citation.chapter: The Book of Outfits and the Beautification and the Magnanimity (al-Kafi, vol 6), 8:14
citation.arabic_text: قُلْتُ لِأَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) مَا أَدْنَى مَا يَجِي‏ءُ مِنَ الْإِسْرَافِ قَالَ ابْتِذَالُكَ ثَوْبَ صَوْنِكَ وَ إِهْرَاقُكَ فَضْلَ إِنَائِكَ وَ أَكْلُكَ التَّمْرَ وَ رَمْيَكَ بِالنَّوَى هَاهُنَا وَ هَاهُنَا .
citation.translation: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Muhammad Bin Al Husayn, from Muhammad Bin Ismail, from Salih Bin Uqba, from Suleyman Bin Salih who said, ‘I said to Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, ‘What is the lowest of the extravagance?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Your routinely wearing of your protective clothing, and your discarding the remnants of your utensil, and your eating the dates and your throwing with the core over here and over there’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: ضعيف - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (2/342)

text: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Muhammad Bin Isa, from Al Hassan Bin Ali Bin Yaqteen, from Al Fazl Bin Kaseer Al Madainy, from the one who mentioned it, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, said, ‘One of his companions went over to him<sup>asws</sup>, so he saw upon him<sup>asws</sup> a shirt in which was a patch. So he went on staring at it, so Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘What is the matter with you, staring?’ So he said, ‘A patch attached in your<sup>asws</sup> shirt’. He<sup>asws</sup> said to me: ‘Strike you hand to this book and read what is in it’; and in front of him<sup>asws</sup> was a book, or near to him<sup>asws</sup>. So the man looked in it, and there was (written) in it: ‘There is no faith for the one who has no shame for him, nor any wealth for the one who has no esteem for him, nor anything new for the one who does not have (anything) old for him’.

citation.chapter: The Book of Outfits and the Beautification and the Magnanimity (al-Kafi, vol 6), 8:14
citation.arabic_text: دَخَلَ عَلَيْهِ بَعْضُ أَصْحَابِهِ فَرَأَى عَلَيْهِ قَمِيصاً فِيهِ قَبٌّ قَدْ رَقَعَهُ فَجَعَلَ يَنْظُرُ إِلَيْهِ فَقَالَ لَهُ أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) مَا لَكَ تَنْظُرُ فَقَالَ قَبٌّ مُلْقًى فِي قَمِيصِكَ قَالَ فَقَالَ لِيَ اضْرِبْ يَدَكَ إِلَى هَذَا الْكِتَابِ فَاقْرَأْ مَا فِيهِ وَ كَانَ بَيْنَ يَدَيْهِ كِتَابٌ أَوْ قَرِيبٌ مِنْهُ فَنَظَرَ الرَّجُلُ فِيهِ فَإِذَا فِيهِ لَا إِيمَانَ لِمَنْ لَا حَيَاءَ لَهُ وَ لَا مَالَ لِمَنْ لَا تَقْدِيرَ لَهُ وَ لَا جَدِيدَ لِمَنْ لَا خَلَقَ لَهُ .
citation.translation: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Muhammad Bin Isa, from Al Hassan Bin Ali Bin Yaqteen, from Al Fazl Bin Kaseer Al Madainy, from the one who mentioned it, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, said, ‘One of his companions went over to him<sup>asws</sup>, so he saw upon him<sup>asws</sup> a shirt in which was a patch. So he went on staring at it, so Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘What is the matter with you, staring?’ So he said, ‘A patch attached in your<sup>asws</sup> shirt’. He<sup>asws</sup> said to me: ‘Strike you hand to this book and read what is in it’; and in front of him<sup>asws</sup> was a book, or near to him<sup>asws</sup>. So the man looked in it, and there was (written) in it: ‘There is no faith for the one who has no shame for him, nor any wealth for the one who has no esteem for him, nor anything new for the one who does not have (anything) old for him’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: ضعيف على المشهور - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (2/342)

text: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from the one who mentioned it, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws having said: ‘The one who wears a turban and does not Tahannak it (lets one end hang in front and the other at the back), so an illness strikes him and there is no cure for it, so he should not blame anyone except for himself’.

citation.chapter: The Book of Outfits and the Beautification and the Magnanimity (al-Kafi, vol 6), 8:15
citation.arabic_text: مَنْ تَعَمَّمَ وَ لَمْ يَتَحَنَّكْ فَأَصَابَهُ دَاءٌ لَا دَوَاءَ لَهُ فَلَا يَلُومَنَّ إِلَّا نَفْسَهُ .
citation.translation: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from the one who mentioned it, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws having said: ‘The one who wears a turban and does not Tahannak it (lets one end hang in front and the other at the back), so an illness strikes him and there is no cure for it, so he should not blame anyone except for himself’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: حسن - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (2/343)

text: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, form Abu Hamman, (It has been narrated) from Abu Al-Hassanasws regarding the Words of Allahazwj Mighty and Majestic [3:125] marked Angels. Heasws said: ‘The turbans which Rasool-Allahsaww wore, so hesaww let it loose from in front of himsaww, and from behind himsaww, and Jibraeelas wore it letting it loose from in front of himas and from behind himas’.

citation.chapter: The Book of Outfits and the Beautification and the Magnanimity (al-Kafi, vol 6), 8:15
citation.arabic_text: اللَّهِ عَزَّ وَ جَلَّ مُسَوِّمِينَ قَالَ الْعَمَائِمُ اعْتَمَّ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ ( صلى الله عليه وآله ) فَسَدَلَهَا مِنْ بَيْنِ يَدَيْهِ وَ مِنْ خَلْفِهِ وَ اعْتَمَّ جَبْرَئِيلُ فَسَدَلَهَا مِنْ بَيْنِ يَدَيْهِ وَ مِنْ خَلْفِهِ .
citation.translation: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, form Abu Hamman, (It has been narrated) from Abu Al-Hassanasws regarding the Words of Allahazwj Mighty and Majestic [3:125] marked Angels. Heasws said: ‘The turbans which Rasool-Allahsaww wore, so hesaww let it loose from in front of himsaww, and from behind himsaww, and Jibraeelas wore it letting it loose from in front of himas and from behind himas’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: صحيح - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (2/343)

text: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Abu Jameela, from Jabir, (It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘There were white turbans upon the Angels Sent on the Day of Badr’.

citation.chapter: The Book of Outfits and the Beautification and the Magnanimity (al-Kafi, vol 6), 8:15
citation.arabic_text: كَانَتْ عَلَى الْمَلَائِكَةِ الْعَمَائِمُ الْبِيضُ الْمُرْسَلَةُ يَوْمَ بَدْرٍ .
citation.translation: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Abu Jameela, from Jabir, (It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘There were white turbans upon the Angels Sent on the Day of Badr’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: ضعيف - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (22/343)

text: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Abu Abdullah, from Al Husayn Bin Ali Al Uqayli, from Ali Bin Abdu Ali Al Lahby, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> put on the turban on Ali<sup>asws</sup> by his<sup>saww</sup> hand, so he<sup>saww</sup> let it hang from in front of him, and shortened it from behind him of the measurement of four fingers, then said: ‘Turn around’. So he<sup>asws</sup> turned. Then he<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘Face me<sup>saww</sup>’. So he<sup>asws</sup> faced. Then he<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘This is how the Angels are crowned’.

citation.chapter: The Book of Outfits and the Beautification and the Magnanimity (al-Kafi, vol 6), 8:15
citation.arabic_text: عَمَّمَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ ( صلى الله عليه وآله ) عَلِيّاً ( عليه السلام ) بِيَدِهِ فَسَدَلَهَا مِنْ بَيْنِ يَدَيْهِ وَ قَصَّرَهَا مِنْ خَلْفِهِ قَدْرَ أَرْبَعِ أَصَابِعَ ثُمَّ قَالَ أَدْبِرْ فَأَدْبَرَ ثُمَّ قَالَ أَقْبِلْ فَأَقْبَلَ ثُمَّ قَالَ هَكَذَا تِيجَانُ الْمَلَائِكَةِ .
citation.translation: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Abu Abdullah, from Al Husayn Bin Ali Al Uqayli, from Ali Bin Abdu Ali Al Lahby, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> put on the turban on Ali<sup>asws</sup> by his<sup>saww</sup> hand, so he<sup>saww</sup> let it hang from in front of him, and shortened it from behind him of the measurement of four fingers, then said: ‘Turn around’. So he<sup>asws</sup> turned. Then he<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘Face me<sup>saww</sup>’. So he<sup>asws</sup> faced. Then he<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘This is how the Angels are crowned’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: مجهول - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (22/343)

text: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Al Nowfaly, from Al Sakuny, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘The turbans are the crowns of the Arabs’. And it is reported that layering (without letting one end hang in front and the other hang at the back) is a turban of Iblees<sup>la</sup>, may Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Curse him<sup>la</sup>’.

citation.chapter: The Book of Outfits and the Beautification and the Magnanimity (al-Kafi, vol 6), 8:15
citation.arabic_text: قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ ( صلى الله عليه وآله ) الْعَمَائِمُ تِيجَانُ الْعَرَبِ . وَ رُوِيَ أَنَّ الطَّابِقِيَّةَ عِمَّةُ إِبْلِيسَ لَعَنَهُ اللَّهُ .
citation.translation: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Al Nowfaly, from Al Sakuny, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘The turbans are the crowns of the Arabs’. And it is reported that layering (without letting one end hang in front and the other hang at the back) is a turban of Iblees<sup>la</sup>, may Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Curse him<sup>la</sup>’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: ضعيف على المشهور - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (22/343)

text: Abu Ali Al Ashary, from one of his companions, from Ali Bin Al Hakam, (It has been narrated) raising it to Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘The one who goes out from his house wearing a turban (passing) beneath his chin, intending a journey, would neither be hit during his journey by theft, nor by burning, nor by abhorrence’.

citation.chapter: The Book of Outfits and the Beautification and the Magnanimity (al-Kafi, vol 6), 8:15
citation.arabic_text: مَنْ خَرَجَ مِنْ مَنْزِلِهِ مُعْتَمّاً تَحْتَ حَنَكِهِ يُرِيدُ سَفَراً لَمْ يُصِبْهُ فِي سَفَرِهِ سَرَقٌ وَ لَا حَرَقٌ وَ لَا مَكْرُوهٌ .
citation.translation: Abu Ali Al Ashary, from one of his companions, from Ali Bin Al Hakam, (It has been narrated) raising it to Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘The one who goes out from his house wearing a turban (passing) beneath his chin, intending a journey, would neither be hit during his journey by theft, nor by burning, nor by abhorrence’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: مرسل - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (2/344)

text: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Musa Bin Ja’far Al Baghdady, from Amro Bin Saeed, from Isa Bin Hamza, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘The one who wears a turban, so he does not circle it beneath his chin, and a sickness hits him for which there is no cure for it, so he should not blame anyone except for himself’.

citation.chapter: The Book of Outfits and the Beautification and the Magnanimity (al-Kafi, vol 6), 8:15
citation.arabic_text: مَنِ اعْتَمَّ فَلَمْ يُدِرِ الْعِمَامَةَ تَحْتَ حَنَكِهِ فَأَصَابَهُ أَلَمٌ لَا دَوَاءَ لَهُ فَلَا يَلُومَنَّ إِلَّا نَفْسَهُ .
citation.translation: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Musa Bin Ja’far Al Baghdady, from Amro Bin Saeed, from Isa Bin Hamza, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘The one who wears a turban, so he does not circle it beneath his chin, and a sickness hits him for which there is no cure for it, so he should not blame anyone except for himself’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: ضعيف على المشهور - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (2/344)

text: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Al Nowfaly, from Al Sakuny, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> wore Al-Yemeni cap, and the white, and the quilted one, and the one with the two ear-covers during the battle, and his<sup>saww</sup> turban was the fastening one and it had a hood for it to cover by’.

citation.chapter: The Book of Outfits and the Beautification and the Magnanimity (al-Kafi, vol 6), 8:16
citation.arabic_text: كَانَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ ( صلى الله عليه وآله ) يَلْبَسُ الْقَلَانِسَ الْيَمَنِيَّةَ وَ الْبَيْضَاءَ وَ الْمُضَرَّبَةَ وَ ذَاتَ الْأُذُنَيْنِ فِي الْحَرْبِ وَ كَانَتْ عِمَامَتُهُ السَّحَابَ وَ كَانَ لَهُ بُرْنُسٌ يَتَبَرْنَسُ بِهِ .
citation.translation: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Al Nowfaly, from Al Sakuny, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> wore Al-Yemeni cap, and the white, and the quilted one, and the one with the two ear-covers during the battle, and his<sup>saww</sup> turban was the fastening one and it had a hood for it to cover by’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: ضعيف على المشهور - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (22/344)

text: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from one of his companions, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> used to wear a white quilted cap, and he<sup>saww</sup> was wearing it during the battle, a cape which had two ear-coverings for it’.

citation.chapter: The Book of Outfits and the Beautification and the Magnanimity (al-Kafi, vol 6), 8:16
citation.arabic_text: كَانَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ ( صلى الله عليه وآله ) يَلْبَسُ قَلَنْسُوَةً بَيْضَاءَ مُضَرَّبَةً وَ كَانَ يَلْبَسُ فِي الْحَرْبِ قَلَنْسُوَةً لَهَا أُذُنَانِ .
citation.translation: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from one of his companions, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> used to wear a white quilted cap, and he<sup>saww</sup> was wearing it during the battle, a cape which had two ear-coverings for it’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: حسن - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (22/344)

text: Humeyd Bin Ziyad, from Al Hassan Bin Muhammad Bin Sama’at, from Ahmad Bin Al Hassan Al Maysami, from Al Husayn Bin Mukhtar who said, ‘Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Make a white cap for me and do not break it (more than one piece), for the Master<sup>asws</sup> like me<sup>asws</sup> does not wear the broken one’.

citation.chapter: The Book of Outfits and the Beautification and the Magnanimity (al-Kafi, vol 6), 8:16
citation.arabic_text: قَالَ أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) اعْمَلْ لِي قَلَانِسَ بَيْضَاءَ وَ لَا تُكَسِّرْهَا فَإِنَّ السَّيِّدَ مِثْلِي لَا يَلْبَسُ الْمُكَسَّرَ .
citation.translation: Humeyd Bin Ziyad, from Al Hassan Bin Muhammad Bin Sama’at, from Ahmad Bin Al Hassan Al Maysami, from Al Husayn Bin Mukhtar who said, ‘Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Make a white cap for me and do not break it (more than one piece), for the Master<sup>asws</sup> like me<sup>asws</sup> does not wear the broken one’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: موثق - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (22/345)

text: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Abu Abdullah, from Yahya Bin Ibrahim Bin Abu Al Balaad, form his father, from Al Husayn Bin Mukhtar who said, ‘Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Take a cap for me and do not make any colouring to be in it, for the Master<sup>asws</sup> like me<sup>asws</sup> does not wear it, meaning do not break it (more than one piece)’.

citation.chapter: The Book of Outfits and the Beautification and the Magnanimity (al-Kafi, vol 6), 8:16
citation.arabic_text: قَالَ أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) اتَّخِذْ لِي قَلَنْسُوَةً وَ لَا تَجْعَلْهَا مُصَبَّغَةً فَإِنَّ السَّيِّدَ مِثْلِي لَا يَلْبَسُهَا يَعْنِي لَا تُكَسِّرْهَا .
citation.translation: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Abu Abdullah, from Yahya Bin Ibrahim Bin Abu Al Balaad, form his father, from Al Husayn Bin Mukhtar who said, ‘Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Take a cap for me and do not make any colouring to be in it, for the Master<sup>asws</sup> like me<sup>asws</sup> does not wear it, meaning do not break it (more than one piece)’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: موثق - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (22/345)

text: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Muhammad Bin Isa, from Abdullah Bin Abdul Rahman, from Shuayb, from Abu Baseer, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Good shoes are a protection for the body and assists upon the Prayer and the cleanliness’.

citation.chapter: The Book of Outfits and the Beautification and the Magnanimity (al-Kafi, vol 6), 8:17
citation.arabic_text: قَالَ أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ ( عليه السلام ) اسْتِجَادَةُ الْحِذَاءِ وِقَايَةٌ لِلْبَدَنِ وَ عَوْنٌ عَلَى الصَّلَاةِ وَ الطَّهُورِ.
citation.translation: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Muhammad Bin Isa, from Abdullah Bin Abdul Rahman, from Shuayb, from Abu Baseer, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Good shoes are a protection for the body and assists upon the Prayer and the cleanliness’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: ضعيف على المشهور - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (2/345)

text: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Al Nowfaly, from Al Sakuny, Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> has said: ‘The first one to take to the sandals was Ibrahim<sup>asws</sup>’.

citation.chapter: The Book of Outfits and the Beautification and the Magnanimity (al-Kafi, vol 6), 8:17
citation.arabic_text: أَوَّلُ مَنِ اتَّخَذَ النَّعْلَيْنِ إِبْرَاهِيمُ ( عليه السلام ) .
citation.translation: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Al Nowfaly, from Al Sakuny, Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> has said: ‘The first one to take to the sandals was Ibrahim<sup>asws</sup>’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: ضعيف على المشهور - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (22/345)

text: And by this chain who said, ‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘The one who takes to a sandal, so let it be a good one’.

citation.chapter: The Book of Outfits and the Beautification and the Magnanimity (al-Kafi, vol 6), 8:17
citation.arabic_text: وَ بِهَذَا الْإِسْنَادِ قَالَ قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ ( صلى الله عليه وآله ) مَنِ اتَّخَذَ نَعْلًا فَلْيَسْتَجِدْهَا .
citation.translation: And by this chain who said, ‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘The one who takes to a sandal, so let it be a good one’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: ضعيف على المشهور - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (2/346)

text: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, form Al Qasim Bin Yahya, from his grandfather Al Hassan Bin Rashid, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Do not wear the flat (shoes) for these are the shoes of Pharaoh<sup>la</sup>, and he<sup>la</sup> was the first one to take to the flat (shoes without heal curve)’.

citation.chapter: The Book of Outfits and the Beautification and the Magnanimity (al-Kafi, vol 6), 8:17
citation.arabic_text: قَالَ أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ ( عليه السلام ) لَا تَحْتَذُوا الْمَلْسَ فَإِنَّهَا حِذَاءُ فِرْعَوْنَ وَ هُوَ أَوَّلُ مَنِ اتَّخَذَ الْمَلْسَ .
citation.translation: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, form Al Qasim Bin Yahya, from his grandfather Al Hassan Bin Rashid, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Do not wear the flat (shoes) for these are the shoes of Pharaoh<sup>la</sup>, and he<sup>la</sup> was the first one to take to the flat (shoes without heal curve)’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: ضعيف - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (2/346)

text: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, form Ibn Mahboub, from Al A’ala Bin Razeyn, from Muhammad Bin Muslim, (It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘I<sup>asws</sup> detest the man if I<sup>asws</sup> do not see a heel-covering on the sandals’.

citation.chapter: The Book of Outfits and the Beautification and the Magnanimity (al-Kafi, vol 6), 8:17
citation.arabic_text: إِنِّي لَأَمْقُتُ الرَّجُلَ لَا أَرَاهُ مُعَقَّبَ النَّعْلَيْنِ .
citation.translation: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, form Ibn Mahboub, from Al A’ala Bin Razeyn, from Muhammad Bin Muslim, (It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘I<sup>asws</sup> detest the man if I<sup>asws</sup> do not see a heel-covering on the sandals’.

Heasws, ‘So there is no problem’.

text: Al Husayn Bin Muhammad, from Moala Bin Muhammad, form Ali Bin Hassan, form Abdul Rahman Bin Kaseer who said, ‘I was walking along with Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, so the strap of his<sup>asws</sup> sandal got cut (broke). text: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Yaqoub Al Sarraj who said, ‘We were walking along with Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> and he<sup>asws</sup> wanted to condole his<sup>asws</sup> relatives due to there being death of a child, so the strap of a sandal of Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> snapped. So he<sup>asws</sup> grabbed his<sup>asws</sup> sandal from his<sup>asws</sup> feet, then walk bare-footed. So Ibn Abu Yafour looked at him<sup>asws</sup>, so he took off his own sandal from his feet, and untied the strap from it and gave it to Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>. So he<sup>asws</sup> turned away from it as if he<sup>asws</sup> was not happy, then refused to accept it, then said: ‘Indeed! The one in the difficulties is the foremost with the patience over it’. So he<sup>asws</sup> walked bare-footed until he<sup>asws</sup> came up to a man whom he gave his<sup>asws</sup> condolences’.

text: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Muhammad Bin Isa, from Muhammad Bin Ali Al Hamdany, from Hanan Bin Sudeyr who said, ‘I went over to Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> and in my leg was a black sandal, so he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘O Hanaan! What is it to you and the black. Do you not know that in it are three characteristics? text: A number or our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Ja’far Bin Muhammad Al Ashary, from Ibn Al Qaddah, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, said, ‘He<sup>asws</sup> was saying: ‘Whenever one of you wears his sandals, so let him wear the right before the left, and when he takes them off, so let him take-off the left before the right’.

citation.arabic_text: كَانَ يَقُولُ إِذَا لَبِسَ أَحَدُكُمْ نَعْلَهُ فَلْيَلْبَسِ الْيَمِينَ قَبْلَ الْيَسَارِ وَ إِذَا خَلَعَهَا فَلْيَخْلَعِ الْيُسْرَى قَبْلَ الْيُمْنَى .
citation.translation: A number or our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Ja’far Bin Muhammad Al Ashary, from Ibn Al Qaddah, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, said, ‘He<sup>asws</sup> was saying: ‘Whenever one of you wears his sandals, so let him wear the right before the left, and when he takes them off, so let him take-off the left before the right’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: ضعيف على المشهور - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (2/353)

text: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Al Hakam, from Aban, from Al Halby, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Do not walk in one shoe’. I said, ‘And why?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Because if you are hit by the touch of the Satan<sup>la</sup>, it would barely separate from you (the injury) except what Allah<sup>azwj</sup> so Desires’.

citation.chapter: The Book of Outfits and the Beautification and the Magnanimity (al-Kafi, vol 6), 8:20
citation.arabic_text: لَا تَمْشِ فِي حِذَاءٍ وَاحِدٍ قُلْتُ وَ لِمَ قَالَ لِأَنَّهُ إِنْ أَصَابَكَ مَسٌّ مِنَ الشَّيْطَانِ لَمْ يَكَدْ يُفَارِقُكَ إِلَّا مَا شَاءَ اللَّهُ .
citation.translation: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Al Hakam, from Aban, from Al Halby, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Do not walk in one shoe’. I said, ‘And why?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Because if you are hit by the touch of the Satan<sup>la</sup>, it would barely separate from you (the injury) except what Allah<sup>azwj</sup> so Desires’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: موثق كالصحيح - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (2/353)

text: From him, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Al A’ala, from Muhammad Bin Muslim, (It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘The one who walks in one shoe, so a touch of the Satan<sup>la</sup> hits him, it would not leave him (the injury) except what Allah<sup>azwj</sup> so Desires’.

citation.chapter: The Book of Outfits and the Beautification and the Magnanimity (al-Kafi, vol 6), 8:20
citation.arabic_text: مَنْ مَشَى فِي حِذَاءٍ وَاحِدٍ فَأَصَابَهُ مَسٌّ مِنَ الشَّيْطَانِ لَمْ يَدَعْهُ إِلَّا مَا شَاءَ اللَّهُ .
citation.translation: From him, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Al A’ala, from Muhammad Bin Muslim, (It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘The one who walks in one shoe, so a touch of the Satan<sup>la</sup> hits him, it would not leave him (the injury) except what Allah<sup>azwj</sup> so Desires’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: موثق كالصحيح - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (22/353)

text: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Al Nowfaly, from Al Sakuny, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, from Ali<sup>asws</sup>, if one were to walk in one shoe and repair the other, he<sup>asws</sup> did not see any problem with that’.

citation.chapter: The Book of Outfits and the Beautification and the Magnanimity (al-Kafi, vol 6), 8:20
citation.arabic_text: نَعْلٍ وَاحِدَةٍ وَ يُصْلِحُ الْأُخْرَى لَا يَرَى بِذَلِكَ بَأْساً .
citation.translation: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Al Nowfaly, from Al Sakuny, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, from Ali<sup>asws</sup>, if one were to walk in one shoe and repair the other, he<sup>asws</sup> did not see any problem with that’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: ضعيف على المشهور - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (2/353)

text: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hisham Bin Salim, Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> has said: ‘The ring of Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> was of ‘leaf’ (silver)’.

citation.chapter: The Book of Outfits and the Beautification and the Magnanimity (al-Kafi, vol 6), 8:21
citation.arabic_text: كَانَ خَاتَمُ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ ( صلى الله عليه وآله ) مِنْ وَرِقٍ .
citation.translation: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hisham Bin Salim, Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> has said: ‘The ring of Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> was of ‘leaf’ (silver)’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: حسن - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (2/354)

text: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Abdullah Bin Sinan and Muawiya Bin Wahab, Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> has said: ‘The ring of Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> was of leaf (silver)’. I said to him<sup>asws</sup>, ‘Was there a stone in it?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘No’.

citation.chapter: The Book of Outfits and the Beautification and the Magnanimity (al-Kafi, vol 6), 8:21
citation.arabic_text: كَانَ خَاتَمُ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ ( صلى الله عليه وآله ) مِنْ وَرِقٍ قَالَ قُلْتُ لَهُ كَانَ فِيهِ فَصٌّ قَالَ لَا .
citation.translation: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Abdullah Bin Sinan and Muawiya Bin Wahab, Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> has said: ‘The ring of Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> was of leaf (silver)’. I said to him<sup>asws</sup>, ‘Was there a stone in it?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘No’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: صحيح - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (22/354)

text: Abu Ali Al Ashary, from Al Hassan Bin Ali Al Kufy, from Ubeys Bin Hisham, form Husayn Bin Ahmad Al Minqary, from Yunus Bin Zabyan, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘From the Sunnah, is wearing of the ring’.

citation.chapter: The Book of Outfits and the Beautification and the Magnanimity (al-Kafi, vol 6), 8:21
citation.arabic_text: مِنَ السُّنَّةِ لُبْسُ الْخَاتَمِ .
citation.translation: Abu Ali Al Ashary, from Al Hassan Bin Ali Al Kufy, from Ubeys Bin Hisham, form Husayn Bin Ahmad Al Minqary, from Yunus Bin Zabyan, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘From the Sunnah, is wearing of the ring’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: ضعيف - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (22/354)

text: Muhammad Bin Yahya, form Muhammad Bin Al Husayn, from Abdul Rahman Bin Abu Hashim, from Abu Khadeeja who said, ‘The stone (in the ring) should be circular’. And he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘This is how the ring of Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> used to be’.

citation.chapter: The Book of Outfits and the Beautification and the Magnanimity (al-Kafi, vol 6), 8:21
citation.arabic_text: الْفَصُّ مُدَوَّرٌ وَ قَالَ هَكَذَا كَانَ خَاتَمُ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ ( صلى الله عليه وآله ) .
citation.translation: Muhammad Bin Yahya, form Muhammad Bin Al Husayn, from Abdul Rahman Bin Abu Hashim, from Abu Khadeeja who said, ‘The stone (in the ring) should be circular’. And he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘This is how the ring of Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> used to be’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: مختلف فيه - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (2/354)

text: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ghalib Bin Usman, from Rawh Bin Abdul Raheem, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said to Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup>: ‘Do not wear the ring of gold, for it is your<sup>asws</sup> adornment in the Hereafter’.

citation.chapter: The Book of Outfits and the Beautification and the Magnanimity (al-Kafi, vol 6), 8:21
citation.arabic_text: قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ ( صلى الله عليه وآله ) لِأَمِيرِ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ ( عليه السلام ) لَا تَخَتَّمْ بِالذَّهَبِ فَإِنَّهُ زِينَتُكَ فِي الْآخِرَةِ.
citation.translation: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ghalib Bin Usman, from Rawh Bin Abdul Raheem, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said to Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup>: ‘Do not wear the ring of gold, for it is your<sup>asws</sup> adornment in the Hereafter’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: موثق - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (22/354)

text: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Al Qasim Bin Yahya, from his grandfather Al Hassan Bin Rashid, from Abu Baseer, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Do not wear a ring without the silver, for Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘The palm is not purified wherein is a ring of iron’.

citation.chapter: The Book of Outfits and the Beautification and the Magnanimity (al-Kafi, vol 6), 8:21
citation.arabic_text: قَالَ أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ ( عليه السلام ) لَا تَخَتَّمُوا بِغَيْرِ الْفِضَّةِ فَإِنَّ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ ( صلى الله عليه وآله ) قَالَ مَا طَهُرَتْ كَفٌّ فِيهَا خَاتَمُ حَدِيدٍ .
citation.translation: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Al Qasim Bin Yahya, from his grandfather Al Hassan Bin Rashid, from Abu Baseer, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Do not wear a ring without the silver, for Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘The palm is not purified wherein is a ring of iron’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: ضعيف - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (2/355)

text: Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Al Husayn Bin Saeed, from Al Nazar Bin Suweyd, from Al Qasim Bin Suleyman, from Jarrah Al Madainy, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Do not make (wear) a ring of gold to be in your hand’.

citation.chapter: The Book of Outfits and the Beautification and the Magnanimity (al-Kafi, vol 6), 8:21
citation.arabic_text: لَا تَجْعَلْ فِي يَدِكَ خَاتَماً مِنْ ذَهَبٍ .
citation.translation: Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Al Husayn Bin Saeed, from Al Nazar Bin Suweyd, from Al Qasim Bin Suleyman, from Jarrah Al Madainy, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Do not make (wear) a ring of gold to be in your hand’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: مجهول - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (2/355)

text: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Khalid, from Ali Bin Al Hakam, from Aban, from Yahya Bin Abu Al A’ala, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having been asked about wearing the ring in the right hand, and I said, ‘I saw the Clan of Hashim wearing rings in their right hands’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘My<sup>asws</sup> father<sup>asws</sup> wore rings in his<sup>asws</sup> left, and he<sup>asws</sup> was higher than them, and of more understanding’.

citation.chapter: The Book of Outfits and the Beautification and the Magnanimity (al-Kafi, vol 6), 8:21
citation.arabic_text: الْيَمِينِ وَ قُلْتُ إِنِّي رَأَيْتُ بَنِي هَاشِمٍ يَتَخَتَّمُونَ فِي أَيْمَانِهِمْ فَقَالَ كَانَ أَبِي يَتَخَتَّمُ فِي يَسَارِهِ وَ كَانَ أَفْضَلَهُمْ وَ أَفْقَهَهُمْ .
citation.translation: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Khalid, from Ali Bin Al Hakam, from Aban, from Yahya Bin Abu Al A’ala, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having been asked about wearing the ring in the right hand, and I said, ‘I saw the Clan of Hashim wearing rings in their right hands’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘My<sup>asws</sup> father<sup>asws</sup> wore rings in his<sup>asws</sup> left, and he<sup>asws</sup> was higher than them, and of more understanding’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: مجهول - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (22/355)

text: From him, from Muhammad Bin Ali, from Ali Bin Asbaat, from Ali son of Ja’farasws who said, ‘I asked my brotherasws Musaasws about the ring to be worn in the right hand. So heasws said: ‘If you so desire to, wear it in the right hand, and if you so desire to, in the left’.

citation.chapter: The Book of Outfits and the Beautification and the Magnanimity (al-Kafi, vol 6), 8:21
citation.arabic_text: سَأَلْتُ أَخِي مُوسَى ( عليه السلام ) عَنِ الْخَاتَمِ يُلْبَسُ فِي الْيَمِينِ فَقَالَ إِنْ شِئْتَ فِي الْيَمِينِ وَ إِنْ شِئْتَ فِي الْيَسَارِ .
citation.translation: From him, from Muhammad Bin Ali, from Ali Bin Asbaat, from Ali son of Ja’farasws who said, ‘I asked my brotherasws Musaasws about the ring to be worn in the right hand. So heasws said: ‘If you so desire to, wear it in the right hand, and if you so desire to, in the left’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: ضعيف - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (22/356)

text: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Ali Bin Atiyya, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> did not wear a ring except for a little while, until he<sup>saww</sup> left it’.

citation.chapter: The Book of Outfits and the Beautification and the Magnanimity (al-Kafi, vol 6), 8:21
citation.arabic_text: مَا تَخَتَّمَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ ( صلى الله عليه وآله ) إِلَّا يَسِيراً حَتَّى تَرَكَهُ .
citation.translation: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Ali Bin Atiyya, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> did not wear a ring except for a little while, until he<sup>saww</sup> left it’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: حسن - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (22/356)

text: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Ja’far Bin Muhammad Al Ashary, from Ibn Al Qaddah, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> that the Prophet<sup>saww</sup> was wearing rings in his<sup>saww</sup> right hand’.

citation.chapter: The Book of Outfits and the Beautification and the Magnanimity (al-Kafi, vol 6), 8:21
citation.arabic_text: يَمِينِهِ .
citation.translation: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Ja’far Bin Muhammad Al Ashary, from Ibn Al Qaddah, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> that the Prophet<sup>saww</sup> was wearing rings in his<sup>saww</sup> right hand’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: ضعيف على المشهور - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (22/356)

text: And by this chain, (He<sup>asws</sup>) said: ‘Ali<sup>asws</sup>, and Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup>, and Al-Husayn<sup>asws</sup> were wearing rings in their<sup>asws</sup> left hands’.

citation.chapter: The Book of Outfits and the Beautification and the Magnanimity (al-Kafi, vol 6), 8:21
citation.arabic_text: وَ بِهَذَا الْإِسْنَادِ قَالَ كَانَ عَلِيٌّ وَ الْحَسَنُ وَ الْحُسَيْنُ ( صلوات الله عليهم ) يَتَخَتَّمُونَ فِي أَيْسَارِهِمْ .
citation.translation: And by this chain, (He<sup>asws</sup>) said: ‘Ali<sup>asws</sup>, and Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup>, and Al-Husayn<sup>asws</sup> were wearing rings in their<sup>asws</sup> left hands’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: ضعيف على المشهور - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (2/356)

text: Al Husayn Bin Muhammad, from Moala Bin Muhammad, from Al Washa, from Musny Al Hannat, from Hatim Bin Ismail, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> and Al-Husayn<sup>asws</sup> were wearing rings in their<sup>asws</sup> left hands’.

citation.chapter: The Book of Outfits and the Beautification and the Magnanimity (al-Kafi, vol 6), 8:21
citation.arabic_text: كَانَ الْحَسَنُ وَ الْحُسَيْنُ ( عليهما السلام ) يَتَخَتَّمَانِ فِي يَسَارِهِمَا .
citation.translation: Al Husayn Bin Muhammad, from Moala Bin Muhammad, from Al Washa, from Musny Al Hannat, from Hatim Bin Ismail, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> and Al-Husayn<sup>asws</sup> were wearing rings in their<sup>asws</sup> left hands’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: ضعيف على المشهور - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (22/356)

text: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Khalid, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Abu Nasr, from Aban, from Yahya Bin Abu Al a’ala, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> and Al-Husayn<sup>asws</sup> were both wearing rings in their<sup>asws</sup> left hands’.

citation.chapter: The Book of Outfits and the Beautification and the Magnanimity (al-Kafi, vol 6), 8:21
citation.arabic_text: كَانَ الْحَسَنُ وَ الْحُسَيْنُ ( عليهما السلام ) يَتَخَتَّمَانِ فِي يَسَارِهِمَا .
citation.translation: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Khalid, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Abu Nasr, from Aban, from Yahya Bin Abu Al a’ala, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> and Al-Husayn<sup>asws</sup> were both wearing rings in their<sup>asws</sup> left hands’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: مجهول - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (2/357)

citation.chapter: The Book of Outfits and the Beautification and the Magnanimity (al-Kafi, vol 6), 8:21

citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: مجهول - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (22/357)

text: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Khalid, from Muhammad Bin Ali, from Al Azramy, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:’ Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> was wearing rings in his<sup>asws</sup> right hand’.

citation.chapter: The Book of Outfits and the Beautification and the Magnanimity (al-Kafi, vol 6), 8:21
citation.arabic_text: كَانَ أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ ( عليه السلام ) يَتَخَتَّمُ فِي يَمِينِهِ .
citation.translation: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Khalid, from Muhammad Bin Ali, from Al Azramy, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:’ Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> was wearing rings in his<sup>asws</sup> right hand’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: ضعيف - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (22/357)

text: Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Muhammad Bin Isa, from Safwan, (It has been narrated) from Abu Al-Hassan Al-Reza<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘A ring of Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> was evaluated, so my<sup>asws</sup> father<sup>asws</sup> took from it for seven’. I said, ‘Seven Dirhams?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Seven Dinars’.

citation.chapter: The Book of Outfits and the Beautification and the Magnanimity (al-Kafi, vol 6), 8:21
citation.arabic_text: قَوَّمُوا خَاتَمَ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) فَأَخَذَهُ أَبِي مِنْهُمْ بِسَبْعَةٍ قَالَ قُلْتُ بِسَبْعَةِ دَرَاهِمَ قَالَ بِسَبْعَةِ دَنَانِيرَ .
citation.translation: Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Muhammad Bin Isa, from Safwan, (It has been narrated) from Abu Al-Hassan Al-Reza<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘A ring of Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> was evaluated, so my<sup>asws</sup> father<sup>asws</sup> took from it for seven’. I said, ‘Seven Dirhams?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Seven Dinars’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: ضعيف على المشهور - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (22/357)

text: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Khalid, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Abu Nasr, (It has been narrated) from Al-Reza<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘The carnelian negates the poverty, and wearing the carnelian negates the hypocrisy’.

citation.arabic_text: الْعَقِيقُ يَنْفِي الْفَقْرَ وَ لُبْسُ الْعَقِيقِ يَنْفِي النِّفَاقَ .

citation.chapter: The Book of Outfits and the Beautification and the Magnanimity (al-Kafi, vol 6), 8:22

text: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ali Bin Ma’bad, from Al Husayn Bin Khalid, (It has been narrated) from Al Reza<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> was saying: ‘The one who takes a ring the stone of which is carnelian, would not be impoverished and would not be judged for him except with that which is better’.

citation.chapter: The Book of Outfits and the Beautification and the Magnanimity (al-Kafi, vol 6), 8:22
citation.arabic_text: كَانَ أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) يَقُولُ مَنِ اتَّخَذَ خَاتَماً فَصُّهُ عَقِيقٌ لَمْ يَفْتَقِرْ وَ لَمْ يُقْضَ لَهُ إِلَّا بِالَّتِي هِيَ أَحْسَنُ .

citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: مجهول - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (22/358)

text: Muhammad Bin yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Yaqoub Bin Yazeed, from Ibrahim Bin Uqba, from Sayaba Bin Ayoub, from Muhammad Bin Al Fazl, from Abdul Raheem Al Qaseyr who said, ‘The governor sent a summoner to a man from the progeny of Abu Talib<sup>as</sup> regarding a felony, so he passed by Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Follow him with a carnelian ring’. So they brought it (to him) and he did not see any abhorrence’.

citation.chapter: The Book of Outfits and the Beautification and the Magnanimity (al-Kafi, vol 6), 8:22
citation.arabic_text: بَعَثَ الْوَالِي إِلَى رَجُلٍ مِنْ آلِ أَبِي طَالِبٍ فِي جِنَايَةٍ فَمَرَّ بِأَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) فَقَالَ أَتْبِعُوهُ بِخَاتَمِ عَقِيقٍ فَأُتِيَ بِخَاتَمِ عَقِيقٍ فَلَمْ يَرَ مَكْرُوهاً .
citation.translation: Muhammad Bin yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Yaqoub Bin Yazeed, from Ibrahim Bin Uqba, from Sayaba Bin Ayoub, from Muhammad Bin Al Fazl, from Abdul Raheem Al Qaseyr who said, ‘The governor sent a summoner to a man from the progeny of Abu Talib<sup>as</sup> regarding a felony, so he passed by Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Follow him with a carnelian ring’. citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: مجهول - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (22/358)

text: From him, from Muhammad Bin Ahmad, raising it, said, ‘A man complained to the Prophet<sup>saww</sup> that his way had been cut-off (by the bandits), so he<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘Why did you not wear a ring with the carnelian, for it is a protection from every evil’.

citation.chapter: The Book of Outfits and the Beautification and the Magnanimity (al-Kafi, vol 6), 8:22
citation.arabic_text: شَكَا رَجُلٌ إِلَى النَّبِيِّ ( صلى الله عليه وآله ) أَنَّهُ قُطِعَ عَلَيْهِ الطَّرِيقُ فَقَالَ ( صلى الله عليه وآله ) هَلَّا تَخَتَّمْتَ بِالْعَقِيقِ فَإِنَّهُ يَحْرُسُ مِنْ كُلِّ سُوءٍ .
citation.translation: From him, from Muhammad Bin Ahmad, raising it, said, ‘A man complained to the Prophet<sup>saww</sup> that his way had been cut-off (by the bandits), so he<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘Why did you not wear a ring with the carnelian, for it is a protection from every evil’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: مرفوع - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (2/358)

text: Ali Bin Ibrahim, form his father, from Ali Bin Ma’bad, from Al Husayn Bin Khalid, (It has been narrated) from Al-Reza<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> was saying: ‘You should be wearing rings with the rubies for these negate the poverty’.

text: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Haroun Bin Muslim, from a man from our companions and he was Al Hassan Bin Ali Bin Fazl, and he had the epitaph of Sikbaj, (It has been narrated) from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Abu Nasr the owner of the hostels, and he used to stand for one of the affairs of Al-Maazy<sup>asws</sup> (7<sup>th</sup> Imam<sup>asws</sup>) who said, ‘One day he<sup>asws</sup> said to me and dictated to me from a book: ‘Wear a ring of the emerald, there is ease, and there is no difficulties in it’.

citation.chapter: The Book of Outfits and the Beautification and the Magnanimity (al-Kafi, vol 6), 8:23
citation.arabic_text: قَالَ لِي يَوْماً وَ أَمْلَى عَلَيَّ مِنْ كِتَابٍ التَّخَتُّمُ بِالزُّمُرُّدِ يُسْرٌ لَا عُسْرَ فِيهِ .
citation.translation: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Haroun Bin Muslim, from a man from our companions and he was Al Hassan Bin Ali Bin Fazl, and he had the epitaph of Sikbaj, (It has been narrated) from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Abu Nasr the owner of the hostels, and he used to stand for one of the affairs of Al-Maazy<sup>asws</sup> (7<sup>th</sup> Imam<sup>asws</sup>) who said, ‘One day he<sup>asws</sup> said to me and dictated to me from a book: ‘Wear a ring of the emerald, there is ease, and there is no difficulties in it’.

citation.chapter: The Book of Outfits and the Beautification and the Magnanimity (al-Kafi, vol 6), 8:24

text: Ali Bin Muhammad Bin Bundar, from Ibrahim Bin Is’haq Al Ahmar, from Al Hassan Bin Sahl, from Al Hassan Bin Ali Bin Mihran who said, ‘I went over to Abu Al-Hassan Musa<sup>asws</sup> and in his<sup>asws</sup> finger was a ring with a stone of turquoise with an engraving: ‘اللَّهُ الْمَلِكُ’ “Allah<sup>azwj</sup> the King”. So I deliberated looking at it, so he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘What is the matter with you, deliberately looking at it?’ So I said, ‘It has reached me that there was for Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> a ring with a stone of turquoise with an engraving: “Allah<sup>azwj</sup> the King”’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Do you recognise it?’ I said, ‘No’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘This is it. Do you know what is the reason for it?’ I said, ‘No’. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘This is a stone gifted by Jibraeel<sup>as</sup> to Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup>, so Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> gifted it to Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup>. Do you know what it’s name is?’ I said, ‘Turquoise’. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘This is in Persian. So what is its name in Arabic?’ I said, ‘I do not know’. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Its name is Al-Zafar’.

citation.chapter: The Book of Outfits and the Beautification and the Magnanimity (al-Kafi, vol 6), 8:24
citation.arabic_text: دَخَلْتُ عَلَى أَبِي الْحَسَنِ مُوسَى ( عليه السلام ) وَ فِي إِصْبَعِهِ خَاتَمٌ فَصُّهُ فَيْرُوزَجٌ نَقْشُهُ اللَّهُ الْمَلِكُ فَأَدَمْتُ النَّظَرَ إِلَيْهِ فَقَالَ مَا لَكَ تُدِيمُ النَّظَرَ إِلَيْهِ فَقُلْتُ بَلَغَنِي أَنَّهُ كَانَ لِعَلِيٍّ أَمِيرِ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ ( عليه السلام ) خَاتَمٌ فَصُّهُ فَيْرُوزَجٌ نَقْشُهُ اللَّهُ الْمَلِكُ فَقَالَ أَ تَعْرِفُهُ قُلْتُ لَا فَقَالَ هَذَا هُوَ تَدْرِي مَا سَبَبُهُ قُلْتُ لَا قَالَ هَذَا حَجَرٌ أَهْدَاهُ جَبْرَئِيلُ ( عليه السلام ) إِلَى رَسُولِ اللَّهِ ( صلى الله عليه وآله ) فَوَهَبَهُ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ ( صلى الله عليه وآله ) لِأَمِيرِ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ ( عليه السلام ) أَ تَدْرِي مَا اسْمُهُ قُلْتُ فَيْرُوزَجٌ قَالَ هَذَا بِالْفَارِسِيَّةِ فَمَا اسْمُهُ بِالْعَرَبِيَّةِ قُلْتُ لَا أَدْرِي قَالَ اسْمُهُ الظَّفَرُ .

citation.translation: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Muhammad Bin Ahmad, from Ali Bin Al Rayyan, from Ali Bin Muhammad well known as Ibn Wahba Al Abdasy, and it is a town from the towns of Wasit, (It has been narrated) raising it to Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said, The best of the stones (for rings) is the crystal’.

text: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Al Hassan Bin Mahboub, from Abdullah Bin Sinan, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘The engraving of the ring of Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> was – “Muhammad<sup>saww</sup>, Rasool, Allah<sup>azwj</sup>”, and the engraving of the ring of Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> was – “Allah<sup>azwj</sup> the King”, and the engraving of the ring of my<sup>asws</sup> father<sup>asws</sup> was – ‘الْعِزَّةُ لِلَّهِ’ “The Honour is for Allah<sup>azwj</sup>”’.

text: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Jameel Bin Darraj, from Yunus Bin Zabyan and Hafs Bin Giyas, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> both having said, May we be sacrificed for you<sup>asws</sup>! Is it disliked that the man should inscribe in his ring, other than his own name and the name of his father?’ So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘In my<sup>asws</sup> ring it is inscribed – ‘اللَّهُ خَالِقُ كُلِّ شَيْ‏ءٍ’ “Allah<sup>azwj</sup> the Creator of everything”; and in the ring of my<sup>asws</sup> father<sup>asws</sup> Muhammad<sup>asws</sup> Bin Ali<sup>asws</sup>, and he<sup>asws</sup> was the best of the Muhammads<sup>asws</sup> I<sup>asws</sup> have ever seen with my<sup>asws</sup> eyes (was inscribed) – “The Honour is for Allah<sup>azwj</sup>”; and in the ring of Ali<sup>asws</sup> Bin Al-Husayn<sup>asws</sup> (was inscribed) – “The Praise is for Allah<sup>azwj</sup> the Exalted the Magnificent; and in the ring of Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> and Al-Husayn<sup>asws</sup> (was inscribed) – Allah<sup>azwj</sup> is Sufficient for me”; and in the ring of Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> (was inscribed) – “Allah<sup>azwj</sup> the King”’.

text: A number of our companions, form Ahmad Bin Abu Abdullah, from Abdullah Bin Muhammad Al Naheyki, from Ibrahim Bin Abdul Hameed who said, ‘Mo’tab passed by me and with him was a ring, so I said to him, ‘Which thing is this?’ So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘A ring of Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>’. So I took it to read what was (inscribed) in it, so there was in it – ‘اللَّهُمَّ أَنْتَ ثِقَتِي فَقِنِي شَرَّ خَلْقِكَ’ “O Allah<sup>azwj</sup>! You<sup>azwj</sup> are my<sup>asws</sup> Trusted One, so Protect me<sup>asws</sup> from the evil of Your<sup>azwj</sup> creatures”’.

text: From him, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Abu Nasr who said, ‘I was in the presence of Abu Al-Hassan Al-Reza<sup>asws</sup>, so he<sup>asws</sup> brought out to us a ring of Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, and a ring of Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup>, and it was (inscribed) upon the ring of Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>: ‘أَنْتَ ثِقَتِي فَاعْصِمْنِي مِنَ النَّاسِ’ “You<sup>azwj</sup> are my<sup>asws</sup> Trusted, so Protect me<sup>asws</sup> from the people”; and the engraving of the ring of Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> was: ‘حَسْبِيَ اللَّهُ’ ‘Allah<sup>azwj</sup> is sufficient for me<sup>asws</sup>”, and in it was a rose and a crescent in its upper part’.

citation.arabic_text: كُنْتُ عِنْدَ أَبِي الْحَسَنِ الرِّضَا ( عليه السلام ) فَأَخْرَجَ إِلَيْنَا خَاتَمَ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) وَ خَاتَمَ أَبِي الْحَسَنِ ( عليه السلام ) وَ كَانَ عَلَى خَاتَمِ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) أَنْتَ ثِقَتِي فَاعْصِمْنِي مِنَ النَّاسِ وَ نَقْشُ خَاتَمِ أَبِي الْحَسَنِ ( عليه السلام ) حَسْبِيَ اللَّهُ وَ فِيهِ وَرْدَةٌ وَ هِلَالٌ فِي أَعْلَاهُ .

text: From him, form his father, from Yunus Bin Abdul Rahman who said, ‘I asked Abu Al-Hassan Al-Reza<sup>asws</sup> about the engraving on his<sup>asws</sup> ring and the ring of his<sup>asws</sup> father<sup>asws</sup>. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The engraving on my<sup>asws</sup> ring is: “Whatever Allah<sup>azwj</sup> so Desires. There is no Strength except by Allah<sup>azwj</sup>”; and the engraving of the ring of my father<sup>asws</sup> is: “Allah<sup>azwj</sup> is Sufficient”, and it is which I (the narrator) used to wear with’.

text: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ali Bin Ma’bad, from Al Husayn Bin Khalid, (It has been narrated) from Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘It was (inscribed) upon a ring of Ali<sup>asws</sup> Bin Al-Husayn<sup>asws</sup> – ‘خَزِيَ وَ شَقِيَ قَاتِلُ الْحُسَيْنِ بْنِ عَلِيٍّ ( عليه السلام )’ “Disgraceful and wretched is the murderer of Al-Husayn<sup>asws</sup> Bin Ali<sup>asws</sup>”’.

citation.arabic_text: كَانَ عَلَى خَاتَمِ عَلِيِّ بْنِ الْحُسَيْنِ ( عليه السلام ) خَزِيَ وَ شَقِيَ قَاتِلُ الْحُسَيْنِ بْنِ عَلِيٍّ ( عليه السلام ) .

text: Sahl Bin Ziyad, from one of his companions, from Wasil Bin Suleyman, from Abdullah Bin Sinan who said, ‘We mentioned the ring of Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup>, so he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Would you love it if I<sup>asws</sup> were to show it to you?’ So I said, ‘Yes’. So he<sup>asws</sup> called for a sealed covering, so he<sup>asws</sup> opened it and brought out a cotton sheet, so there was a silver ring and in it was embedded a black stone, and upon it was inscribed in two lines – “Muhammad<sup>saww</sup>, Rasool<sup>saww</sup>, Allah<sup>azwj</sup>”’. Then he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The stone of the Prophet<sup>saww</sup> was black’.

text: Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Muhammad Bin Isa, from Al Husayn Bin Khalid, (It has been narrated) from Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> the 2<sup>nd</sup>, said, ‘I said to him<sup>asws</sup>, ‘We are reporting in the Hadeeth that Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> was cleaning himself<sup>saww</sup> and his<sup>saww</sup> ring was in his<sup>saww</sup> finger, and similar to that is what Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> did, and the engraving of a ring of Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> was – “Muhammad<sup>saww</sup> Rasool<sup>saww</sup> Allah<sup>azwj</sup>”’. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘They spoke the truth’. I said, ‘So would it befit us that we do it’. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘They (people) are wearing rings in the right hand and you all are wearing rings in the left hand’. He (the narrator) said, ‘So I was silent, so he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Do you know what was the engraving in the ring of Adam<sup>as</sup>?’ So I said, ‘No’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘There is no god except for Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, Muhammad<sup>saww</sup> is Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup>’, and the engraving in the ring of the Prophet<sup>saww</sup> was “Muhammad<sup>saww</sup> Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup>”; and the ring of Amir Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> was “Allah<sup>azwj</sup> the King”; and the ring of Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> was “The Honour is for Allah<sup>azwj</sup>”, and the ring of Al-Husayn<sup>asws</sup> was “Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Fulfils His<sup>azwj</sup> Command”, and Ali<sup>asws</sup> Bin Al-Husayn<sup>asws</sup> wore the ring of his<sup>asws</sup> father<sup>asws</sup>, and Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> the great wore the ring of his<sup>asws</sup> grandfather Al-Husayn<sup>asws</sup>, and the ring of Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> was “Allah<sup>azwj</sup> is my<sup>asws</sup> Guardian and Protects me<sup>asws</sup> from His<sup>azwj</sup> creatures; and Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> the 1<sup>st</sup> “Allah<sup>azwj</sup> is Sufficient”; and Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> the 2<sup>nd</sup> “Whatever Allah<sup>azwj</sup> so Desires, there is no Strength except with Allah<sup>azwj</sup>”’. And Al-Husayn Bin Khalid (the narrator) said, ‘And he<sup>asws</sup> extended his<sup>asws</sup> hand towards me and said: ‘My<sup>asws</sup> ring is the ring of my<sup>asws</sup> father<sup>asws</sup> as well’.
