citation.arabic_text: قُلْتُ لَهُ إِنَّا رُوِّينَا فِي الْحَدِيثِ أَنَّ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ ( صلى الله عليه وآله ) كَانَ يَسْتَنْجِي وَ خَاتَمُهُ فِي إِصْبَعِهِ وَ كَذَلِكَ كَانَ يَفْعَلُ أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ ( عليه السلام ) وَ كَانَ نَقْشُ خَاتَمِ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ ( صلى الله عليه وآله ) مُحَمَّدٌ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ قَالَ صَدَقُوا قُلْتُ فَيَنْبَغِي لَنَا أَنْ نَفْعَلَ قَالَ إِنَّ أُولَئِكَ كَانُوا يَتَخَتَّمُونَ فِي الْيَدِ الْيُمْنَى وَ إِنَّكُمْ أَنْتُمْ تَتَخَتَّمُونَ فِي الْيُسْرَى قَالَ فَسَكَتَ فَقَالَ أَ تَدْرِي مَا كَانَ نَقْشُ خَاتَمِ آدَمَ ( عليه السلام ) فَقُلْتُ لَا فَقَالَ لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا اللَّهُ مُحَمَّدٌ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ وَ كَانَ نَقْشُ خَاتَمِ النَّبِيِّ ( صلى الله عليه وآله ) مُحَمَّدٌ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ وَ خَاتَمِ أَمِيرِ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ ( عليه السلام ) اللَّهُ الْمَلِكُ وَ خَاتَمِ الْحَسَنِ ( عليه السلام ) الْعِزَّةُ لِلَّهِ وَ خَاتَمِ الْحُسَيْنِ ( عليه السلام ) إِنَّ اللَّهَ بَالِغُ أَمْرِهِ وَ عَلِيُّ بْنُ الْحُسَيْنِ ( عليه السلام ) خَاتَمُ أَبِيهِ وَ أَبُو جَعْفَرٍ الْأَكْبَرُ خَاتَمُ جَدِّهِ الْحُسَيْنِ ( عليه السلام ) وَ خَاتَمُ جَعْفَرٍ ( عليه السلام ) اللَّهُ وَلِيِّي وَ عِصْمَتِي مِنْ خَلْقِهِ وَ أَبُو الْحَسَنِ الْأَوَّلُ ( عليه السلام ) حَسْبِيَ اللَّهُ وَ أَبُو الْحَسَنِ الثَّانِي مَا شَاءَ اللَّهُ لَا قُوَّةَ إِلَّا بِاللَّهِ وَ قَالَ الْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ خَالِدٍ وَ مَدَّ يَدَهُ إِلَيَّ وَ قَالَ خَاتَمِي خَاتَمُ أَبِي ( عليه السلام ) أَيْضاً .
citation.translation: Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Muhammad Bin Isa, from Al Husayn Bin Khalid, (It has been narrated) from Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> the 2<sup>nd</sup>, said, ‘I said to him<sup>asws</sup>, ‘We are reporting in the Hadeeth that Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> was cleaning himself<sup>saww</sup> and his<sup>saww</sup> ring was in his<sup>saww</sup> finger, and similar to that is what Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> did, and the engraving of a ring of Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> was – “Muhammad<sup>saww</sup> Rasool<sup>saww</sup> Allah<sup>azwj</sup>”’. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘They spoke the truth’. I said, ‘So would it befit us that we do it’. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘They (people) are wearing rings in the right hand and you all are wearing rings in the left hand’. He (the narrator) said, ‘So I was silent, so he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Do you know what was the engraving in the ring of Adam<sup>as</sup>?’ So I said, ‘No’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘There is no god except for Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, Muhammad<sup>saww</sup> is Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup>’, and the engraving in the ring of the Prophet<sup>saww</sup> was “Muhammad<sup>saww</sup> Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup>”; and the ring of Amir Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> was “Allah<sup>azwj</sup> the King”; and the ring of Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> was “The Honour is for Allah<sup>azwj</sup>”, and the ring of Al-Husayn<sup>asws</sup> was “Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Fulfils His<sup>azwj</sup> Command”, and Ali<sup>asws</sup> Bin Al-Husayn<sup>asws</sup> wore the ring of his<sup>asws</sup> father<sup>asws</sup>, and Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> the great wore the ring of his<sup>asws</sup> grandfather Al-Husayn<sup>asws</sup>, and the ring of Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> was “Allah<sup>azwj</sup> is my<sup>asws</sup> Guardian and Protects me<sup>asws</sup> from His<sup>azwj</sup> creatures; and Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> the 1<sup>st</sup> “Allah<sup>azwj</sup> is Sufficient”; and Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> the 2<sup>nd</sup> “Whatever Allah<sup>azwj</sup> so Desires, there is no Strength except with Allah<sup>azwj</sup>”’. And Al-Husayn Bin Khalid (the narrator) said, ‘And he<sup>asws</sup> extended his<sup>asws</sup> hand towards me and said: ‘My<sup>asws</sup> ring is the ring of my<sup>asws</sup> father<sup>asws</sup> as well’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: ضعيف على المشهور - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (2/363)

text: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Al Qasim Bin Yahya, from his grandfather Al Hassan Bin Rashid, from Abu Baseer, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The one who engraves upon his ring the Name of Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, so let him withdraw it from the hand with which he cleans himself during the ablution’.

So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘We<sup>asws</sup> marry women, so we<sup>asws</sup> give them their dowries, and they buy whatever they so desire to. There is nothing for us<sup>asws</sup> from it’.

citation.arabic_text: دَخَلَ قَوْمٌ عَلَى الْحُسَيْنِ بْنِ عَلِيٍّ ( عليه السلام ) فَقَالُوا يَا ابْنَ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ نَرَى فِي مَنْزِلِكَ أَشْيَاءَ نَكْرَهُهَا وَ إِذَا فِي مَنْزِلِهِ بُسُطٌ وَ نَمَارِقُ فَقَالَ ( عليه السلام ) إِنَّا نَتَزَوَّجُ النِّسَاءَ فَنُعْطِيهِنَّ مُهُورَهُنَّ فَيَشْتَرِينَ مَا شِئْنَ لَيْسَ لَنَا مِنْهُ شَيْ‏ءٌ .
citation.translation: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Mansour Bin Al Abbas, from saeed Bin Janaah, from Abu Khalid Al Zaydi, from Jabir, (It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘A group of people came over to Al-Husayn<sup>asws</sup> Bin Ali<sup>asws</sup>, so they said, ‘O son<sup>asws</sup> of Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup>! We see such things in your<sup>asws</sup> dwelling which we dislike’, and in his<sup>asws</sup> house were rugs and cushions. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘We<sup>asws</sup> marry women, so we<sup>asws</sup> give them their dowries, and they buy whatever they so desire to. There is nothing for us<sup>asws</sup> from it’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: ضعيف - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (2/366)

text: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Khalid, from his father, from Abdullah Bin Al Mugheira, from Abu Malik Al Juhuny, from Abdullah Bin Ata’a who said, ‘I went over to Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup>, so I saw in his<sup>asws</sup> house, rugs, and pillows, and patterns, and amenities’. text: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Abu Abdullah, from Usman Bin Isa, from Abdullah Bin Muskan, from Al Hassan Al Zayyat who said, ‘I went over to Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> in a refurbished room. citation.arabic_text: دَخَلْتُ عَلَى أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ ( عليه السلام ) فِي بَيْتٍ مُنَجَّدٍ ثُمَّ عُدْتُ إِلَيْهِ مِنَ الْغَدِ وَ هُوَ فِي بَيْتٍ لَيْسَ فِيهِ إِلَّا حَصِيرٌ وَ عَلَيْهِ قَمِيصٌ غَلِيظٌ فَقَالَ الْبَيْتُ الَّذِي رَأَيْتَهُ لَيْسَ بَيْتِي إِنَّمَا هُوَ بَيْتُ الْمَرْأَةِ وَ كَانَ أَمْسِ يَوْمُهَا .

text: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from one of his companions, from Ali Bin Ismail Al Maysami, from Abu Al Jaroud who said, ‘I went over to Abu Ja’farasws and heasws was seated upon a chattel, so I went on to touch the chattel with my hand, so heasws said: ‘This which you are touching with your hand, is Armany (Armenian)’. So I said to himasws, ‘And what have youasws to do with Al-Armany?’. So heasws said: ‘This is a chattel which the mother of Ali came with’, a wife of hisasws’. So when it was another time, I went over to himasws, so I went on to touch what was beneath me, so heasws said: ‘It is as if you want to see what is beneath you’. So I said, ‘No, but the blind tend to tamper’. So heasws said to me: ‘That chattel was for the mother of Ali, and she used to view by the opinions of the Khawarijites, so Iasws respited her for a night up to the morning that she might retract from her opinion, and accept the Wilayah of Amir Al-Momineenasws, but she refrained to measws. So when it was the morning, Iasws divorced her’.

citation.chapter: The Book of Outfits and the Beautification and the Magnanimity (al-Kafi, vol 6), 8:28
citation.arabic_text: دَخَلْتُ عَلَى أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ ( عليه السلام ) وَ هُوَ جَالِسٌ عَلَى مَتَاعٍ فَجَعَلْتُ أَلْمِسُ الْمَتَاعَ بِيَدِي فَقَالَ هَذَا الَّذِي تَلْمِسُهُ بِيَدِكَ أَرْمَنِيٌّ فَقُلْتُ لَهُ وَ مَا أَنْتَ وَ الْأَرْمَنِيَّ فَقَالَ هَذَا مَتَاعٌ جَاءَتْ بِهِ أُمُّ عَلِيٍّ امْرَأَةٌ لَهُ فَلَمَّا كَانَ مِنْ قَابِلٍ دَخَلْتُ عَلَيْهِ فَجَعَلْتُ أَلْمِسُ مَا تَحْتِي فَقَالَ كَأَنَّكَ تُرِيدُ أَنْ تَنْظُرَ مَا تَحْتَكَ فَقُلْتُ لَا وَ لَكِنَّ الْأَعْمَى يَعْبَثُ فَقَالَ لِي إِنَّ ذَلِكَ الْمَتَاعَ كَانَ لِأُمِّ عَلِيٍّ وَ كَانَتْ تَرَى رَأْيَ الْخَوَارِجِ فَأَدَرْتُهَا لَيْلَةً إِلَى الصُّبْحِ أَنْ تَرْجِعَ عَنْ رَأْيِهَا وَ تَتَوَلَّى أَمِيرَ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ ( عليه السلام ) فَامْتَنَعَتْ عَلَيَّ فَلَمَّا أَصْبَحْتُ طَلَّقْتُهَا .

text: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Al Amraky Bin Ali, (It has been narrated) from Ali son of Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> who said, ‘I asked Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> about the silk mattresses, and the likes of it from the brocade, and the silk Prayer mat and the likes of it from the brocade, is it correct for the man to sleep over it, and recline upon, and the Prayer?’ So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Furnish it, and stand upon it, but do not Prostrate upon it’.

citation.arabic_text: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا الْحَسَنِ ( صلوات الله عليه ) عَنِ الْفِرَاشِ الْحَرِيرِ وَ مِثْلِهِ مِنَ الدِّيبَاجِ وَ الْمُصَلَّى الْحَرِيرِ وَ مِثْلِهِ مِنَ الدِّيبَاجِ هَلْ يَصْلُحُ لِلرَّجُلِ النَّوْمُ عَلَيْهِ وَ التُّكَأَةُ وَ الصَّلَاةُ فَقَالَ يَفْرِشُهُ وَ يَقُومُ عَلَيْهِ وَ لَا يَسْجُدُ عَلَيْهِ .

text: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, and a number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, altogether from Ibn Mahboub, from Al Abbas Bin Al Waleed Bin Sabeeh who said, ‘Shihab Bin Abd Rabih asked me that I should seek permission for him to (see) Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>. So I let Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> know about that, so he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Tell him he can come to us<sup>asws</sup> whenever he so desires to’. So I took him over to him<sup>asws</sup> one night, and Shihab wore a covering of the head. I placed a cushion for him, so he sat over it and Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said to him: ‘Remove you veil O Shihab, for the veil casts a doubt during the night and is a disgrace during the day’.

citation.chapter: The Book of Outfits and the Beautification and the Magnanimity (al-Kafi, vol 6), 8:29
citation.arabic_text: سَأَلَنِي شِهَابُ بْنُ عَبْدِ رَبِّهِ أَنْ أَسْتَأْذِنَ لَهُ عَلَى أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) فَأَعْلَمْتُ ذَلِكَ أَبَا عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) فَقَالَ قُلْ لَهُ يَأْتِينَا إِذَا شَاءَ فَأَدْخَلْتُهُ عَلَيْهِ لَيْلًا وَ شِهَابٌ مُقَنَّعُ الرَّأْسِ فَطُرِحَتْ لَهُ وِسَادَةٌ فَجَلَسَ عَلَيْهَا فَقَالَ لَهُ أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) أَلْقِ قِنَاعَكَ يَا شِهَابُ فَإِنَّ الْقِنَاعَ رِيبَةٌ بِاللَّيْلِ مَذَلَّةٌ بِالنَّهَارِ .

text: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Al Nowfaly, from Al Sakuny, Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> has said: ‘Amir Al Momineen<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘When the hoods appear as legacy, the adultery would appear’.

citation.arabic_text: قَالَ أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ ( صلوات الله عليه ) إِذَا ظَهَرَتِ الْقَلَانِسُ الْمُتَرِّكَةُ ظَهَرَ الزِّنَا .

text: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Muhammad Bin Isa, from Ubeydullah Bin Abdullah Al Dagqan, from Dorost Bin Abu Mansour, from Ibrahim Bin Abdul Hameed, (It has been narrated) from Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> that he<sup>asws</sup> was saying: ‘Folding the clothes is its resting, and it is more lasting for it’.

text: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Moamar Bin Khallad, (It has been narrated) from Abu Al-Hassan Al-Reza<sup>asws</sup>, said, ‘I<sup>asws</sup> went out and I<sup>asws</sup> wanted to see Dawood Bin Isa Bin Ali, and he was lodged at the well of Maymoun, and upon me<sup>asws</sup> were two coarse clothes. So I<sup>asws</sup> saw an old woman and with her were two slave girls, so I<sup>asws</sup> said, ‘O old woman! Would you like to sell these two slave girls?’ So she said, ‘Yes, but the likes of you<sup>asws</sup> cannot buy these two’. I<sup>asws</sup> said, ‘And why do you say so?’ She said, ‘Because one of them is a singer and the other one is a musician’. So I<sup>asws</sup> went over to Dawood Bin Isa, so he stood up for me<sup>asws</sup> and made me<sup>asws</sup> to sit in his seat. So when I<sup>asws</sup> went out from his presence, he said to his companions, ‘Do you know who this is? This is Ali<sup>asws</sup> Bin Musa<sup>asws</sup> whom the people of Al-Iraq are alleging that obedience to him<sup>asws</sup> is an Obligation’.

citation.chapter: The Book of Outfits and the Beautification and the Magnanimity (al-Kafi, vol 6), 8:29
citation.arabic_text: خَرَجْتُ وَ أَنَا أُرِيدُ دَاوُدَ بْنَ عِيسَى بْنِ عَلِيٍّ وَ كَانَ يَنْزِلُ بِئْرَ مَيْمُونٍ وَ عَلَيَّ ثَوْبَانِ غَلِيظَانِ فَرَأَيْتُ امْرَأَةً عَجُوزاً وَ مَعَهَا جَارِيَتَانِ فَقُلْتُ يَا عَجُوزُ أَ تُبَاعُ هَاتَانِ الْجَارِيَتَانِ فَقَالَتْ نَعَمْ وَ لَكِنْ لَا يَشْتَرِيهِمَا مِثْلُكَ قُلْتُ وَ لِمَ قَالَتْ لِأَنَّ إِحْدَاهُمَا مُغَنِّيَةٌ وَ الْأُخْرَى زَامِرَةٌ فَدَخَلْتُ عَلَى دَاوُدَ بْنِ عِيسَى فَرَفَعَنِي وَ أَجْلَسَنِي فِي مَجْلِسِي فَلَمَّا خَرَجْتُ مِنْ عِنْدِهِ قَالَ لِأَصْحَابِهِ تَعْلَمُونَ مَنْ هَذَا هَذَا عَلِيُّ بْنُ مُوسَى الَّذِي يَزْعُمُ أَهْلُ الْعِرَاقِ أَنَّهُ مَفْرُوضُ الطَّاعَةِ .
citation.translation: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Moamar Bin Khallad, (It has been narrated) from Abu Al-Hassan Al-Reza<sup>asws</sup>, said, ‘I<sup>asws</sup> went out and I<sup>asws</sup> wanted to see Dawood Bin Isa Bin Ali, and he was lodged at the well of Maymoun, and upon me<sup>asws</sup> were two coarse clothes. So I<sup>asws</sup> saw an old woman and with her were two slave girls, so I<sup>asws</sup> said, ‘O old woman! Would you like to sell these two slave girls?’ So she said, ‘Yes, but the likes of you<sup>asws</sup> cannot buy these two’. I<sup>asws</sup> said, ‘And why do you say so?’ She said, ‘Because one of them is a singer and the other one is a musician’. So I<sup>asws</sup> went over to Dawood Bin Isa, so he stood up for me<sup>asws</sup> and made me<sup>asws</sup> to sit in his seat. So when I<sup>asws</sup> went out from his presence, he said to his companions, ‘Do you know who this is? This is Ali<sup>asws</sup> Bin Musa<sup>asws</sup> whom the people of Al-Iraq are alleging that obedience to him<sup>asws</sup> is an Obligation’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: صحيح - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (22/370)

text: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, form Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hisham Bin Al Hakam, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws having dislike wearing Al-Burtala (a deep cape)’.

text: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ali Bin Muhammad Al Qasany, from Al Qasim Bin Muhammad, from Suleyman Bin dawood Al Minqary, from Hammad Bin Isa who said, ‘Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> looked at a mattress in a house of a man, so he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘There is a mattress for the man, and a mattress for his family, and a mattress for his guest, and a mattress for the Satan<sup>la</sup>’.

citation.chapter: The Book of Outfits and the Beautification and the Magnanimity (al-Kafi, vol 6), 8:29
citation.arabic_text: مَنْ لَبِسَ السَّرَاوِيلَ مِنْ قُعُودٍ وُقِيَ وَجَعَ الْخَاصِرَةِ .
citation.translation: Abu Ali Al Ashary, from one of his companions, from Muhammad Bin Khalid Al Tayalisy, from Ali Bin Abu Hamza, from Abu Baseer, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘The one who wears trousers whilst seated would not get groin pain’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: مرسل مجهول - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (2/371)

text: Al Husayn Bin Muhammad, from Moala Bin Muhammad, from Mansour Bin Al Abbas, from Al Hassan Bin Ali Bin Yaqteen, from Amro Bin Ibrahim, from Khalaf Bin Hammad, from Ali Al Qummy, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Expansive shirting and the (cutting) the hair growth of the hair in the nose is a safety from the leprosy’. Then he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Have you not heard the words of the poet – ‘And you will not see my shirt except as wide of the collar and the sleeves’’.

citation.arabic_text: سَعَةُ الْجُرُبَّانِ وَ نَبَاتُ الشَّعْرِ فِي الْأَنْفِ أَمَانٌ مِنَ الْجُذَامِ ثُمَّ قَالَ أَ مَا سَمِعْتَ قَوْلَ الشَّاعِرِ وَ لَا تَرَى قَمِيصِي إِلَّا وَاسِعَ الْجَيْبِ وَ الْيَدِ

citation.arabic_text: قَالَ أَبُو الْحَسَنِ ( عليه السلام ) مِنْ مُرُوءَةِ الرَّجُلِ أَنْ يَكُونَ دَوَابُّهُ سِمَاناً قَالَ وَ سَمِعْتُهُ يَقُولُ ثَلَاثَةٌ مِنَ الْمُرُوءَةِ فَرَاهَةُ الدَّابَّةِ وَ حُسْنُ وَجْهِ الْمَمْلُوكِ وَ الْفَرْشُ السَّرِيُّ .

text: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Muhammad Bin Al Hassan Bin Shamoun, from Abdullah Bin Abdul Rahman, from Misma’a, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘Not one of you should touch the clothes of the one who has not worn them yet’.

citation.chapter: The Book of Outfits and the Beautification and the Magnanimity (al-Kafi, vol 6), 8:29
citation.arabic_text: قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ ( صلى الله عليه وآله ) لَا يَمْسَحْ أَحَدُكُمْ بِثَوْبِ مَنْ لَمْ يَكْسَهُ .
citation.translation: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Muhammad Bin Al Hassan Bin Shamoun, from Abdullah Bin Abdul Rahman, from Misma’a, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘Not one of you should touch the clothes of the one who has not worn them yet’.

text: Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Muhammad Bin Bakr, from Zakariyya Al Momin, from the one who narrated it, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Fold your clothes at night, for when these are displayed, the Satan<sup>la</sup> wears it at night’.

citation.chapter: The Book of Outfits and the Beautification and the Magnanimity (al-Kafi, vol 6), 8:29

text: Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Yahya Bin Al Mubarak, from Abdullah Jabala Al Kinany who said, ‘Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> met me and I was dangling a fish in my hand, so he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Throw it away! I<sup>asws</sup> dislike for the eminent man that he should be carrying the abject thing by himself’. Then he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The group of your enemies are numerous. The people are your enemies, O group of Shiah, people hold grudges against you. Therefore adorn yourselves to them with your ability over it’.

citation.chapter: The Book of Outfits and the Beautification and the Magnanimity (al-Kafi, vol 6), 8:29
citation.arabic_text: اسْتَقْبَلَنِي أَبُو الْحَسَنِ ( عليه السلام ) وَ قَدْ عَلَّقْتُ سَمَكَةً فِي يَدِي فَقَالَ اقْذِفْهَا إِنَّنِي لَأَكْرَهُ لِلرَّجُلِ السَّرِيِّ أَنْ يَحْمِلَ الشَّيْ‏ءَ الدَّنِيَّ بِنَفْسِهِ ثُمَّ قَالَ إِنَّكُمْ قَوْمٌ أَعْدَاؤُكُمْ كَثِيرَةٌ عَادَاكُمُ الْخَلْقُ يَا مَعْشَرَ الشِّيعَةِ إِنَّكُمْ قَدْ عَادَاكُمُ الْخَلْقُ فَتَزَيَّنُوا لَهُمْ بِمَا قَدَرْتُمْ عَلَيْهِ .

text: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Al Hassan Bin Al Jaham who said, ‘I went over to Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> and he<sup>asws</sup> had dyed (hair) with the black. So I said, ‘I see you<sup>asws</sup> have dyed (hair) with the black’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘And in the dyeing there is Recompense, and the dye and the henna are from what Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic Increases in the chastity of the women, and the women have neglected the chastity due to the neglecting of the henna by their husbands’. I said, ‘It has reached us that henna tends to increase in the greying?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Which thing increase in the greying? The greying increases during every day’.

citation.chapter: The Book of Outfits and the Beautification and the Magnanimity (al-Kafi, vol 6), 8:30
citation.arabic_text: دَخَلْتُ عَلَى أَبِي الْحَسَنِ ( عليه السلام ) وَ قَدِ اخْتَضَبَ بِالسَّوَادِ فَقُلْتُ أَرَاكَ قَدِ اخْتَضَبْتَ بِالسَّوَادِ فَقَالَ إِنَّ فِي الْخِضَابِ أَجْراً وَ الْخِضَابُ وَ التَّهْيِئَةُ مِمَّا يَزِيدُ اللَّهُ عَزَّ وَ جَلَّ فِي عِفَّةِ النِّسَاءِ وَ لَقَدْ تَرَكَ النِّسَاءُ الْعِفَّةَ بِتَرْكِ أَزْوَاجِهِنَّ لَهُنَّ التَّهْيِئَةَ قَالَ قُلْتُ بَلَغَنَا أَنَّ الْحِنَّاءَ يَزِيدُ فِي الشَّيْبِ قَالَ أَيُّ شَيْ‏ءٍ يَزِيدُ فِي الشَّيْبِ الشَّيْبُ يَزِيدُ فِي كُلِّ يَوْمٍ .
citation.translation: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Al Hassan Bin Al Jaham who said, ‘I went over to Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> and he<sup>asws</sup> had dyed (hair) with the black. So I said, ‘I see you<sup>asws</sup> have dyed (hair) with the black’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘And in the dyeing there is Recompense, and the dye and the henna are from what Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic Increases in the chastity of the women, and the women have neglected the chastity due to the neglecting of the henna by their husbands’. I said, ‘It has reached us that henna tends to increase in the greying?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Which thing increase in the greying? The greying increases during every day’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: موثق كالصحيح - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (2/372)

text: Muhammad Bin Yaha, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Al Hakam, from Miskeen Bin Abu Al Hakam, from a man, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘A man came over to the Prophet<sup>saww</sup>, so he<sup>saww</sup> saw the greying in his beard. So the Prophet<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘A radiance’. Then he<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘The one who gets old and grey in Al-Islam, there would be a radiance for him on the Day of Judgement’. He (the narrator) said, ‘So the man dyed with the henna, then he came over to the Prophet<sup>saww</sup>. So when he<sup>saww</sup> saw the dyeing, he<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘A radiance and Islam’. So the man dyed with the black. So the Prophet<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘A radiance, and Islam, and faith, and a love for your wives, and an awe in the hearts of your enemies’.

citation.chapter: The Book of Outfits and the Beautification and the Magnanimity (al-Kafi, vol 6), 8:30
citation.arabic_text: جَاءَ رَجُلٌ إِلَى النَّبِيِّ ( صلى الله عليه وآله ) فَنَظَرَ إِلَى الشَّيْبِ فِي لِحْيَتِهِ فَقَالَ النَّبِيُّ ( صلى الله عليه وآله ) نُورٌ ثُمَّ قَالَ مَنْ شَابَ شَيْبَةً فِي الْإِسْلَامِ كَانَتْ لَهُ نُوراً يَوْمَ الْقِيَامَةِ قَالَ فَخَضَبَ الرَّجُلُ بِالْحِنَّاءِ ثُمَّ جَاءَ إِلَى النَّبِيِّ ( صلى الله عليه وآله ) فَلَمَّا رَأَى الْخِضَابَ قَالَ نُورٌ وَ إِسْلَامٌ فَخَضَبَ الرَّجُلُ بِالسَّوَادِ فَقَالَ النَّبِيُّ ( صلى الله عليه وآله ) نُورٌ وَ إِسْلَامٌ وَ إِيمَانٌ وَ مَحَبَّةٌ إِلَى نِسَائِكُمْ وَ رَهْبَةٌ فِي قُلُوبِ عَدُوِّكُمْ .

text: Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Al Abbas Bin Musa Al Warraq, (It has been narrated) from Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘A group of people came over to Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup>, so they saw him<sup>asws</sup> as having dyed (hair) with the black. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘I<sup>asws</sup> am a man who loves the women, and I<sup>asws</sup> do it for them’.

citation.arabic_text: دَخَلَ قَوْمٌ عَلَى أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ ( عليه السلام ) فَرَأَوْهُ مُخْتَضِباً بِالسَّوَادِ فَسَأَلُوهُ فَقَالَ إِنِّي رَجُلٌ أُحِبُّ النِّسَاءَ وَ أَنَا أَتَصَنَّعُ لَهُنَّ .

text: Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Saeed Bin Janah, from Abu Khalid Al Zaydi, from Jabir, (It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘A group of people came over to Al-Husayn<sup>asws</sup> Bin Ali<sup>asws</sup>, so they saw him<sup>asws</sup> as having dyed (hair) with the black. So they asked him<sup>asws</sup> about that. text: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Abu Abdullah, from Muhammad Bin Ismail, from Muhammad Bin Uzafar, from umar Bin Yazeed who said, ‘Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Beware of the discolouration of the dyeing, for in that is despair’.

citation.translation: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Abu Abdullah, from Muhammad Bin Ismail, from Muhammad Bin Uzafar, from umar Bin Yazeed who said, ‘Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Beware of the discolouration of the dyeing, for in that is despair’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: صحيح - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (2/375)

text: Ali Bin Muhammad Bin Bundar, and Muhammad Bin Al Hassan, from Ibrahim Bin Is’haq Al Ahmar, from Muhammad Bin Abdullah Bin Mihran, from his father, raising it, said, ‘The Prophet<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘Spending a Dirham in the dye is better than spending a Dirham in the Way of Allah<sup>azwj</sup>. Therein are fourteen qualities – It dispels the wind from the ears, and it refines the vision, and softens the nose-ducts, and aromatises the breath, and strengthens the gums, and removes the fainting, and reduces the whisperings of the Satan<sup>la</sup>, and the Angels are happy by it, and the believers get glad tidings by it, and the Infidels are disappointed by it, and it is an adornment, and it is a perfume, and a freedom in his grave, and Munkar and Nakeer (two questioning Angels) are too embarrassed from it (the questioning)’.

citation.chapter: The Book of Outfits and the Beautification and the Magnanimity (al-Kafi, vol 6), 8:30
citation.arabic_text: قَالَ النَّبِيُّ ( صلى الله عليه وآله ) نَفَقَةُ دِرْهَمٍ فِي الْخِضَابِ أَفْضَلُ مِنْ نَفَقَةِ دِرْهَمٍ فِي سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ إِنَّ فِيهِ أَرْبَعَ عَشْرَةَ خَصْلَةً يَطْرُدُ الرِّيحَ مِنَ الْأُذُنَيْنِ وَ يَجْلُو الْغِشَاءَ عَنِ الْبَصَرِ وَ يُلَيِّنُ الْخَيَاشِيمَ وَ يُطَيِّبُ النَّكْهَةَ وَ يَشُدُّ اللِّثَةَ وَ يَذْهَبُ بِالْغَشَيَانِ وَ يُقِلُّ وَسْوَسَةَ الشَّيْطَانِ وَ تَفْرَحُ بِهِ الْمَلَائِكَةُ وَ يَسْتَبْشِرُ بِهِ الْمُؤْمِنُ وَ يَغِيظُ بِهِ الْكَافِرُ وَ هُوَ زِينَةٌ وَ هُوَ طِيبٌ وَ بَرَاءَةٌ فِي قَبْرِهِ وَ يَسْتَحْيِي مِنْهُ مُنْكَرٌ وَ نَكِيرٌ .
citation.translation: Ali Bin Muhammad Bin Bundar, and Muhammad Bin Al Hassan, from Ibrahim Bin Is’haq Al Ahmar, from Muhammad Bin Abdullah Bin Mihran, from his father, raising it, said, ‘The Prophet<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘Spending a Dirham in the dye is better than spending a Dirham in the Way of Allah<sup>azwj</sup>. Therein are fourteen qualities – It dispels the wind from the ears, and it refines the vision, and softens the nose-ducts, and aromatises the breath, and strengthens the gums, and removes the fainting, and reduces the whisperings of the Satan<sup>la</sup>, and the Angels are happy by it, and the believers get glad tidings by it, and the Infidels are disappointed by it, and it is an adornment, and it is a perfume, and a freedom in his grave, and Munkar and Nakeer (two questioning Angels) are too embarrassed from it (the questioning)’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: ضعيف - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (22/375)

text: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Al Hakam, from Sayf Bin Ameyra, from Abu Bakr Al Hazramy who said, ‘I was with Abu Alqama and Al-Haris Bin Al-Mugheira, and Abu Hassan in the presence of Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, and Alqama had dyed with the henna, and Al-Haris had dyed with the black (dye), and Abu Hassan had not dyed. Al-Husayn<sup>asws</sup> was killed and he<sup>asws</sup> dyed with the woad (a dyeing plant)’.

citation.arabic_text: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) عَنِ الْخِضَابِ بِالْوَسْمَةِ فَقَالَ لَا بَأْسَ قَدْ قُتِلَ الْحُسَيْنُ ( عليه السلام ) وَ هُوَ مُخْتَضِبٌ بِالْوَسْمَةِ .
citation.translation: From him, from his father, from Yunus, from Abu Bakr Al Hazramy who said, ‘I asked Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> about the dyeing with the woad (a dyeing plant), so he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘There is no problem. Al-Husayn<sup>asws</sup> was killed and he<sup>asws</sup> dyed with the woad (a dyeing plant)’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: حسن - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (2/377)

text: From him, from his father, from Al Qasim Bin Muhammad Al Jowhary, from Al Husayn Bin Umar Bin Yazeed, from his father who said, ‘I heard Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> saying: ‘The dyeing with the black (dye) is amusing for the women, and an awe to the enemy’.

citation.chapter: The Book of Outfits and the Beautification and the Magnanimity (al-Kafi, vol 6), 8:31
citation.arabic_text: سَمِعْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) يَقُولُ الْخِضَابُ بِالسَّوَادِ أُنْسٌ لِلنِّسَاءِ وَ مَهَابَةٌ لِلْعَدُوِّ .
citation.translation: From him, from his father, from Al Qasim Bin Muhammad Al Jowhary, from Al Husayn Bin Umar Bin Yazeed, from his father who said, ‘I heard Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> saying: ‘The dyeing with the black (dye) is amusing for the women, and an awe to the enemy’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: ضعيف - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (2/377)

text: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hisham Bin Al Hakam, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘The (application of) henna increase in the water of the face, and frequents the greying’.

citation.chapter: The Book of Outfits and the Beautification and the Magnanimity (al-Kafi, vol 6), 8:32
citation.arabic_text: الْحِنَّاءُ يَزِيدُ فِي مَاءِ الْوَجْهِ وَ يُكْثِرُ الشَّيْبَ .
citation.translation: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hisham Bin Al Hakam, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘The (application of) henna increase in the water of the face, and frequents the greying’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: حسن - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (2/377)

text: Abu Ali Al Ashary, from Muhammad Bin Abdul Jabbar, from Safwan, from Al A’ala, from Muhammad Bin Muslim who said, ‘Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The henna ignites the greying’.

citation.chapter: The Book of Outfits and the Beautification and the Magnanimity (al-Kafi, vol 6), 8:32
citation.arabic_text: قَالَ أَبُو جَعْفَرٍ ( عليه السلام ) الْحِنَّاءُ يَشْعَلُ الشَّيْبَ .
citation.translation: Abu Ali Al Ashary, from Muhammad Bin Abdul Jabbar, from Safwan, from Al A’ala, from Muhammad Bin Muslim who said, ‘Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The henna ignites the greying’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: صحيح - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (2/377)

text: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Muawiya Bin Ammar who said, ‘I saw Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having dyed with the henna’.

citation.chapter: The Book of Outfits and the Beautification and the Magnanimity (al-Kafi, vol 6), 8:32
citation.arabic_text: رَأَيْتُ أَبَا جَعْفَرٍ ( عليه السلام ) مَخْضُوباً بِالْحِنَّاءِ .
citation.translation: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Muawiya Bin Ammar who said, ‘I saw Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having dyed with the henna’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: حسن - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (22/377)

text: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Abu Abdullah, from his father, from Fazala Bin Ayoub, from Hareyz, (It has been narrated) from a slave of Ali<sup>asws</sup> Bin Al-Husayn<sup>asws</sup> who said, ‘I heard Ali<sup>asws</sup> Bin Al-Husayn<sup>asws</sup> saying: ‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘Dye with the henna for it refines the vision, and builds the hair, and aromatises the wind, and gives tranquillity to the wife’.

citation.chapter: The Book of Outfits and the Beautification and the Magnanimity (al-Kafi, vol 6), 8:32
citation.arabic_text: سَمِعْتُ عَلِيَّ بْنَ الْحُسَيْنِ ( صلوات الله عليه ) يَقُولُ قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ ( صلى الله عليه وآله ) اخْتَضِبُوا بِالْحِنَّاءِ فَإِنَّهُ يَجْلُو الْبَصَرَ وَ يُنْبِتُ الشَّعْرَ وَ يُطَيِّبُ الرِّيحَ وَ يُسَكِّنُ الزَّوْجَةَ .
citation.translation: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Abu Abdullah, from his father, from Fazala Bin Ayoub, from Hareyz, (It has been narrated) from a slave of Ali<sup>asws</sup> Bin Al-Husayn<sup>asws</sup> who said, ‘I heard Ali<sup>asws</sup> Bin Al-Husayn<sup>asws</sup> saying: ‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘Dye with the henna for it refines the vision, and builds the hair, and aromatises the wind, and gives tranquillity to the wife’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: مجهول - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (22/378)

text: From him, from Ubdous Bin Ibrahim al Baghdady, (It has been narrated) raising it to Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘The henna removes the odour, and increases in the water of the face, and aromatises the breath, and improves the birth’.

citation.chapter: The Book of Outfits and the Beautification and the Magnanimity (al-Kafi, vol 6), 8:32
citation.arabic_text: الْحِنَّاءُ يَذْهَبُ بِالسَّهَكِ وَ يَزِيدُ فِي مَاءِ الْوَجْهِ وَ يُطَيِّبُ النَّكْهَةَ وَ يُحَسِّنُ الْوَلَدَ .
citation.translation: From him, from Ubdous Bin Ibrahim al Baghdady, (It has been narrated) raising it to Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘The henna removes the odour, and increases in the water of the face, and aromatises the breath, and improves the birth’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: مجهول مرفوع - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (2/378)

text: From him, from Ali Bin Suleyman Bin Rusheyd, from Malik Bin Asheym, from Ismail Bin Yazi’e who said, ‘I said to Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup>, ‘For me there is a young daughter whose regularity (of menstruation) is lifted’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Dye her head with the henna so the menstruation would be returning to her’. He (the narrator) said, ‘So I did that, so the menstruation returned to her’.

citation.chapter: The Book of Outfits and the Beautification and the Magnanimity (al-Kafi, vol 6), 8:32
citation.arabic_text: قُلْتُ لِأَبِي الْحَسَنِ ( عليه السلام ) إِنَّ لِي فَتَاةً قَدِ ارْتَفَعَتْ عِلَّتُهَا فَقَالَ اخْضِبْ رَأْسَهَا بِالْحِنَّاءِ فَإِنَّ الْحَيْضَ سَيَعُودُ إِلَيْهَا قَالَ فَفَعَلْتُ ذَلِكَ فَعَادَ إِلَيْهَا الْحَيْضُ .
citation.translation: From him, from Ali Bin Suleyman Bin Rusheyd, from Malik Bin Asheym, from Ismail Bin Yazi’e who said, ‘I said to Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup>, ‘For me there is a young daughter whose regularity (of menstruation) is lifted’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Dye her head with the henna so the menstruation would be returning to her’. He (the narrator) said, ‘So I did that, so the menstruation returned to her’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: مجهول - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (2/378)

text: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Moamar Bin Khallad, (It has been narrated) from Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Three (things), one who recognises these would not leave them – Cutting the hair, and rolling up of the clothes, and copulating with the slave-girls’.

citation.chapter: The Book of Outfits and the Beautification and the Magnanimity (al-Kafi, vol 6), 8:33
citation.arabic_text: ثَلَاثٌ مَنْ عَرَفَهُنَّ لَمْ يَدَعْهُنَّ جَزُّ الشَّعْرِ وَ تَشْمِيرُ الثِّيَابِ وَ نِكَاحُ الْإِمَاءِ .
citation.translation: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Moamar Bin Khallad, (It has been narrated) from Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Three (things), one who recognises these would not leave them – Cutting the hair, and rolling up of the clothes, and copulating with the slave-girls’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: صحيح - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (2/378)

text: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Muhammad Bin Abu Hamza, from Is’haq Bin Ammar, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, said, ‘He<sup>asws</sup> said to me: ‘Cut your hair to reduce its smell, and its insects (lice etc.), and its dirt, and it thickens your neck, and it refines your vision’. And in another report, (He<sup>asws</sup> said): ‘And its rests your body’.

citation.chapter: The Book of Outfits and the Beautification and the Magnanimity (al-Kafi, vol 6), 8:33
citation.arabic_text: قَالَ لِي اسْتَأْصِلْ شَعْرَكَ يَقِلُّ دَرَنُهُ وَ دَوَابُّهُ وَ وَسَخُهُ وَ تَغْلُظُ رَقَبَتُكَ وَ يَجْلُو بَصَرُكَ وَ فِي رِوَايَةٍ أُخْرَى وَ يَسْتَرِيحُ بَدَنُكَ .
citation.translation: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Muhammad Bin Abu Hamza, from Is’haq Bin Ammar, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, said, ‘He<sup>asws</sup> said to me: ‘Cut your hair to reduce its smell, and its insects (lice etc.), and its dirt, and it thickens your neck, and it refines your vision’. And in another report, (He<sup>asws</sup> said): ‘And its rests your body’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: حسن أو موثق - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (2/378)

text: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Abu Nasr who said, ‘I said to Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> that our companions are reporting that shaving the head regarding other than Hajj or Umrah is a mutilation’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Whenever Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> used to fulfil his rituals, would go to a town called Sayah and shave (his<sup>asws</sup> head)’.

citation.chapter: The Book of Outfits and the Beautification and the Magnanimity (al-Kafi, vol 6), 8:33
citation.arabic_text: قُلْتُ لِأَبِي الْحَسَنِ ( عليه السلام ) إِنَّ أَصْحَابَنَا يَرْوُونَ أَنَّ حَلْقَ الرَّأْسِ فِي غَيْرِ حَجٍّ وَ لَا عُمْرَةٍ مُثْلَةٌ فَقَالَ كَانَ أَبُو الْحَسَنِ ( عليه السلام ) إِذَا قَضَى مَنَاسِكَهُ عَدَلَ إِلَى قَرْيَةٍ يُقَالُ لَهَا سَايَةُ فَحَلَقَ .
citation.translation: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Abu Nasr who said, ‘I said to Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> that our companions are reporting that shaving the head regarding other than Hajj or Umrah is a mutilation’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Whenever Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> used to fulfil his rituals, would go to a town called Sayah and shave (his<sup>asws</sup> head)’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: ضعيف على المشهور - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (2/379)

text: Ali Bin Muhammad, raising it, said, ‘I said to Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> that the people are saying that shaving-off the head is a mutilation. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘It is an Umrah for us<sup>asws</sup> and a mutilation for our<sup>asws</sup> enemies’.

citation.chapter: The Book of Outfits and the Beautification and the Magnanimity (al-Kafi, vol 6), 8:33
citation.arabic_text: قُلْتُ لِأَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) إِنَّ النَّاسَ يَقُولُونَ إِنَّ حَلْقَ الرَّأْسِ مُثْلَةٌ فَقَالَ عُمْرَةٌ لَنَا وَ مُثْلَةٌ لِأَعْدَائِنَا .
citation.translation: Ali Bin Muhammad, raising it, said, ‘I said to Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> that the people are saying that shaving-off the head is a mutilation. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘It is an Umrah for us<sup>asws</sup> and a mutilation for our<sup>asws</sup> enemies’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: مرفوع - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (22/379)

text: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, and Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, altogether from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Abdul Rahman Bin Umar Bin Aslam who said, ‘The cupper performed cupping on me in the fovea, so Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> saw me, so he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Which thing is this? Go and shave-off your head!’ He (the narrator) said, ‘So I went and shaved-off my head’.

citation.chapter: The Book of Outfits and the Beautification and the Magnanimity (al-Kafi, vol 6), 8:33
citation.arabic_text: حَجَمَنِي الْحَجَّامُ فَحَلَقَ مِنْ مَوْضِعِ النُّقْرَةِ فَرَآنِي أَبُو الْحَسَنِ ( عليه السلام ) فَقَالَ أَيُّ شَيْ‏ءٍ هَذَا اذْهَبْ فَاحْلِقْ رَأْسَكَ قَالَ فَذَهَبْتُ وَ حَلَقْتُ رَأْسِي .
citation.translation: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, and Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, altogether from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Abdul Rahman Bin Umar Bin Aslam who said, ‘The cupper performed cupping on me in the fovea, so Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> saw me, so he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Which thing is this? Go and shave-off your head!’ He (the narrator) said, ‘So I went and shaved-off my head’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: مجهول - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (2/379)

text: Abu Ali Al Ashary, from Muhammad Bin Abdul Jabbar, from Safwan, from Ibn Sinan who said, ‘I said to Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, ‘What are you<sup>asws</sup> saying regarding lengthening of the hair?’ So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The companions of Muhammad<sup>saww</sup> were hairy, meaning the trimming’.

citation.chapter: The Book of Outfits and the Beautification and the Magnanimity (al-Kafi, vol 6), 8:33
citation.arabic_text: قُلْتُ لِأَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) مَا تَقُولُ فِي إِطَالَةِ الشَّعْرِ فَقَالَ كَانَ أَصْحَابُ مُحَمَّدٍ ( صلى الله عليه وآله ) مُشْعِرِينَ يَعْنِي الطَّمَّ .
citation.translation: Abu Ali Al Ashary, from Muhammad Bin Abdul Jabbar, from Safwan, from Ibn Sinan who said, ‘I said to Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, ‘What are you<sup>asws</sup> saying regarding lengthening of the hair?’ So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The companions of Muhammad<sup>saww</sup> were hairy, meaning the trimming’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: صحيح - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (22/380)

text: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Al Hakam, from Sa’dan, from Abu Baseer, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Every Friday is what is between the trimming to the trimming’.

citation.chapter: The Book of Outfits and the Beautification and the Magnanimity (al-Kafi, vol 6), 8:33
citation.arabic_text: إِنِّي لَأَحْلِقُ كُلَّ جُمُعَةٍ فِيمَا بَيْنَ الطَّلْيَةِ إِلَى الطَّلْيَةِ .
citation.translation: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Al Hakam, from Sa’dan, from Abu Baseer, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Every Friday is what is between the trimming to the trimming’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: مجهول - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (2/380)

text: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Yahya Bin Al Mubarak, from Abdullah Bin Jabala, from Is’haq Bin Ammar, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, said, ‘I said, ‘May I be sacrificed for you<sup>asws</sup>! Sometimes there are a lot of hairs in my back, so it grieves me with an intense grief’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘O Is’haq! But, do you not know that shaving the back removes the grief?’

citation.chapter: The Book of Outfits and the Beautification and the Magnanimity (al-Kafi, vol 6), 8:33
citation.arabic_text: قُلْتُ جُعِلْتُ فِدَاكَ رُبَّمَا كَثُرَ الشَّعْرُ فِي قَفَايَ فَيَغُمُّنِي غَمّاً شَدِيداً فَقَالَ لِي يَا إِسْحَاقُ أَ مَا عَلِمْتَ أَنَّ حَلْقَ الْقَفَا يَذْهَبُ بِالْغَمِّ .
citation.translation: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Yahya Bin Al Mubarak, from Abdullah Bin Jabala, from Is’haq Bin Ammar, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, said, ‘I said, ‘May I be sacrificed for you<sup>asws</sup>! Sometimes there are a lot of hairs in my back, so it grieves me with an intense grief’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘O Is’haq! But, do you not know that shaving the back removes the grief?’
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: ضعيف على المشهور - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (22/380)

text: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Abu Nasr, from Dawood Bin Al Husayn, from Abu Al Abbas Al Baqbaaq who said, ‘I asked Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> about the man who happens to have abundance (of hair), shall he part (style) it or leave it?’ So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘He should part (style) it’.

citation.chapter: The Book of Outfits and the Beautification and the Magnanimity (al-Kafi, vol 6), 8:34
citation.arabic_text: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) عَنِ الرَّجُلِ يَكُونُ لَهُ وَفْرَةٌ أَ يَفْرُقُهَا أَوْ يَدَعُهَا فَقَالَ يَفْرُقُهَا .
citation.translation: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Abu Nasr, from Dawood Bin Al Husayn, from Abu Al Abbas Al Baqbaaq who said, ‘I asked Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> about the man who happens to have abundance (of hair), shall he part (style) it or leave it?’ So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘He should part (style) it’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: ضعيف على المشهور - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (2/381)

text: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Al Nowfaly, from Al Sakuny, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘The one who takes (grows) hair, so let him make it good and take care of it or trim it’.

citation.chapter: The Book of Outfits and the Beautification and the Magnanimity (al-Kafi, vol 6), 8:34
citation.arabic_text: قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ ( صلى الله عليه وآله ) مَنِ اتَّخَذَ شَعْراً فَلْيُحْسِنْ وِلَايَتَهُ أَوْ لِيَجُزَّهُ .
citation.translation: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Al Nowfaly, from Al Sakuny, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘The one who takes (grows) hair, so let him make it good and take care of it or trim it’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: ضعيف على المشهور - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (2/381)

text: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Hammad, from Ayoub Bin Haroun, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, said, ‘I said to him<sup>asws</sup>, ‘Did Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> used to part (style) his<sup>saww</sup> hair?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘No. Whenever Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> lengthened his<sup>saww</sup> hair, it would be to the lobe of his<sup>saww</sup> ear’.

citation.chapter: The Book of Outfits and the Beautification and the Magnanimity (al-Kafi, vol 6), 8:34

text: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Muhammad Bin Isa, from Amro Bin Ibrahim, from Khalaf Bin Hammad, from Amro Bin Sabit, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, said, ‘I said, ‘They (people) are reporting that the parting (styling) is from the Sunnah’. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The Prophet<sup>saww</sup> did not part, nor did the Prophets<sup>as</sup> beforehand keep (long) hair’.

citation.chapter: The Book of Outfits and the Beautification and the Magnanimity (al-Kafi, vol 6), 8:34
citation.arabic_text: قُلْتُ إِنَّهُمْ يَرْوُونَ أَنَّ الْفَرْقَ مِنَ السُّنَّةِ قَالَ مِنَ السُّنَّةِ قُلْتُ يَزْعُمُونَ أَنَّ النَّبِيِّ ( صلى الله عليه وآله ) فَرَقَ قَالَ مَا فَرَقَ النَّبِيُّ ( صلى الله عليه وآله ) وَ لَا كَانَ الْأَنْبِيَاءُ ( عليهم السلام ) تُمْسِكُ الشَّعْرَ .
citation.translation: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Muhammad Bin Isa, from Amro Bin Ibrahim, from Khalaf Bin Hammad, from Amro Bin Sabit, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, said, ‘I said, ‘They (people) are reporting that the parting (styling) is from the Sunnah’. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘From the Sunnah?’ I said, ‘They are alleging that the Prophet<sup>saww</sup> parted’. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The Prophet<sup>saww</sup> did not part, nor did the Prophets<sup>as</sup> beforehand keep (long) hair’.

text: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Ibn Abu Nasr, from Ali Bin Abu Hamza, from Abu Baseer who said, ‘I said to Abu Abdullahasws, ‘The parting (of the hair) is from the Sunnah?’ Heasws said: ‘No’. I said, ‘So did Rasool-Allahsaww part (the hair)?’ Heasws said: ‘Yes’. I said, ‘How is it that Rasool-Allahsaww parted and it is not from the Sunnah?’ Heasws said: ‘The one who is hit by what Rasool-Allahsaww was hit by would be parting just as Rasool-Allahsaww parted, so he would have abided by the Sunnah, or else, so no’. I said to himasws, ‘How is that?’ Heasws said: ‘Rasool-Allahsaww, when hesaww was turned away from the House (Kabah), and hesaww had ushered the sacrificial animal, and wore the Ihraam, Allahazwj Showed himsaww the vision in which Allahazwj Informed himsaww of it in Hisazwj Book [48:27] Certainly Allah had Endorsed to His Rasool the vision with the truth: you shall enter the Sacred Masjid, if Allah Pleases, in security, (some) having their heads shaved and (others) having their hair cut, you shall not be fearing. Thus, Rasool-Allahsaww knew that Allahazwj would be Fulfilling for him with what Heazwj had Shown himsaww. So from then onwards, hesaww preserved the hair which was upon hissaww head when hesaww was in Ihraam, awaiting to shave it off in the Sanctuary, since Allahazwj Mighty and Majestic has Promised himsaww. So when hesaww did shave it off, did not repeat the preservation of the hair, nor was that from hissaww own self’.

citation.chapter: The Book of Outfits and the Beautification and the Magnanimity (al-Kafi, vol 6), 8:34
citation.arabic_text: قُلْتُ لِأَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) الْفَرْقُ مِنَ السُّنَّةِ قَالَ لَا قُلْتُ فَهَلْ فَرَقَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ ( صلى الله عليه وآله ) قَالَ نَعَمْ قُلْتُ كَيْفَ فَرَقَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ ( صلى الله عليه وآله ) وَ لَيْسَ مِنَ السُّنَّةِ قَالَ مَنْ أَصَابَهُ مَا أَصَابَ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ ( صلى الله عليه وآله ) يَفْرُقُ كَمَا فَرَقَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ ( صلى الله عليه وآله ) فَقَدْ أَصَابَ سُنَّةَ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ ( صلى الله عليه وآله ) وَ إِلَّا فَلَا قُلْتُ لَهُ كَيْفَ ذَلِكَ قَالَ إِنَّ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ ( صلى الله عليه وآله ) حِينَ صُدَّ عَنِ الْبَيْتِ وَ قَدْ كَانَ سَاقَ الْهَدْيَ وَ أَحْرَمَ أَرَاهُ اللَّهُ الرُّؤْيَا الَّتِي أَخْبَرَهُ اللَّهُ بِهَا فِي كِتَابِهِ إِذْ يَقُولُ لَقَدْ صَدَقَ اللَّهُ رَسُولَهُ الرُّؤْيا بِالْحَقِّ لَتَدْخُلُنَّ الْمَسْجِدَ الْحَرامَ إِنْ شاءَ اللَّهُ آمِنِينَ مُحَلِّقِينَ رُؤُسَكُمْ وَ مُقَصِّرِينَ لا تَخافُونَ فَعَلِمَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ ( صلى الله عليه وآله ) أَنَّ اللَّهَ سَيَفِي لَهُ بِمَا أَرَاهُ فَمِنْ ثَمَّ وَفَّرَ ذَلِكَ الشَّعْرَ الَّذِي كَانَ عَلَى رَأْسِهِ حِينَ أَحْرَمَ انْتِظَاراً لِحَلْقِهِ فِي الْحَرَمِ حَيْثُ وَعَدَهُ اللَّهُ عَزَّ وَ جَلَّ فَلَمَّا حَلَقَهُ لَمْ يُعِدْ فِي تَوْفِيرِ الشَّعْرِ وَ لَا كَانَ ذَلِكَ مِنْ قَبْلِهِ ( صلى الله عليه وآله ) .

text: Al Husayn Bin Muhammad, from Moala Bin Muhammad, and Ali Bin Muhammad, from Salih Bin Abu Hammad, altogether from Al Washa, from Ahmad Bin A’aiz, from Abu Khadeeja, from Moala Bin Khunays, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Whatever exceeds from the beard from the fist, so it is in the Fire’.

citation.chapter: The Book of Outfits and the Beautification and the Magnanimity (al-Kafi, vol 6), 8:35
citation.arabic_text: مَا زَادَ مِنَ اللِّحْيَةِ عَنِ الْقَبْضَةِ فَهُوَ فِي النَّارِ .

citation.arabic_text: قَدْرِ اللِّحْيَةِ قَالَ تَقْبِضُ بِيَدِكَ عَلَى اللِّحْيَةِ وَ تَجُزُّ مَا فَضَلَ .

citation.translation: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Al Nowfaly, from Al Sakuny, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘It is from the Sunnah that you pluck from the moustache until it reaches the verge’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: ضعيف على المشهور - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (2/383)

citation.arabic_text: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنْ قَصِّ الشَّارِبِ أَ مِنَ السُّنَّةِ قَالَ نَعَمْ .

citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: مرسل - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (22/383)

So when he<sup>saww</sup> saw him, he<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘Like this, so keep doing it’.
