citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: ضعيف على المشهور - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (22/384)

text: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Muhammad Bin Hamza Al Ashary, raising it, said, ‘Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Plucking the hair from the nose beautifies the face’.

citation.chapter: The Book of Outfits and the Beautification and the Magnanimity (al-Kafi, vol 6), 8:36
citation.arabic_text: قَالَ أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) أَخْذُ الشَّعْرِ مِنَ الْأَنْفِ يُحَسِّنُ الْوَجْهَ .
citation.translation: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Muhammad Bin Hamza Al Ashary, raising it, said, ‘Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Plucking the hair from the nose beautifies the face’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: مرفوع - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (2/384)

text: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Al Hakam, from Abdullah Bin Jundab, from Sufyan Bin Al Samt who said, ‘Abu Abdullahasws said to me: ‘The clean clothes suppress the enemy, and the oiling removes the anguish, and the combing for the head removes Al-Waba (illness)’. I said, ‘And what is Al-Waba?’ Heasws said: ‘The fever. And combing the beard strengthens the teeth’.

citation.chapter: The Book of Outfits and the Beautification and the Magnanimity (al-Kafi, vol 6), 8:37
citation.arabic_text: قَالَ لِي أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) الثَّوْبُ النَّقِيُّ يَكْبِتُ الْعَدُوَّ وَ الدُّهْنُ يَذْهَبُ بِالْبُؤْسِ وَ الْمَشْطُ لِلرَّأْسِ يَذْهَبُ بِالْوَبَاءِ قَالَ قُلْتُ وَ مَا الْوَبَاءُ قَالَ الْحُمَّى وَ الْمَشْطُ لِلِّحْيَةِ يَشُدُّ الْأَضْرَاسَ .
citation.translation: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Al Hakam, from Abdullah Bin Jundab, from Sufyan Bin Al Samt who said, ‘Abu Abdullahasws said to me: ‘The clean clothes suppress the enemy, and the oiling removes the anguish, and the combing for the head removes Al-Waba (illness)’. I said, ‘And what is Al-Waba?’ Heasws said: ‘The fever. And combing the beard strengthens the teeth’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: مجهول - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (22/385)

text: Humeyd Bin Ziyad, from Al Hassan Bin Muhammad Bin Sama’at, from Ahmad Bin Al Hassan Al Maysami, form Muhammad Bin Is’haq, from Ammar Al Nowfaly, from his father who said, ‘I heard Abu Al-Hassanasws saying: ‘The combing removes the Al-Waba (fever), and for Abu Abdullahasws was a comb in the Masjid, combing with it whenever heasws was free from the Prayer’.

citation.chapter: The Book of Outfits and the Beautification and the Magnanimity (al-Kafi, vol 6), 8:37
citation.arabic_text: سَمِعْتُ أَبَا الْحَسَنِ ( عليه السلام ) يَقُولُ الْمَشْطُ يَذْهَبُ بِالْوَبَاءِ وَ كَانَ لِأَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) مُشْطٌ فِي الْمَسْجِدِ يَتَمَشَّطُ بِهِ إِذَا فَرَغَ مِنْ صَلَاتِهِ .
citation.translation: Humeyd Bin Ziyad, from Al Hassan Bin Muhammad Bin Sama’at, from Ahmad Bin Al Hassan Al Maysami, form Muhammad Bin Is’haq, from Ammar Al Nowfaly, from his father who said, ‘I heard Abu Al-Hassanasws saying: ‘The combing removes the Al-Waba (fever), and for Abu Abdullahasws was a comb in the Masjid, combing with it whenever heasws was free from the Prayer’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: مجهول - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (22/385)

text: Ali Bin Ibrhim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Al Husayn Bin Al Hassan Bin Aasim, from his father who said, ‘I went over to Abu Ibrahim<sup>asws</sup> (7<sup>th</sup> Imam<sup>asws</sup>), and in his<sup>asws</sup> hand was an ivory comb to comb with. So I said to him<sup>asws</sup>, ‘May I be sacrificed for you<sup>asws</sup>! There ones with us in al-Iraq who are alleging that it is not Permissible to be combing with the ivory’. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘And why, for there used to be, from my<sup>asws</sup> father<sup>asws</sup>, one or two ivory combs’. Then he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘You should be combing with the ivory, for the ivory removed the illness (fever)’.

citation.chapter: The Book of Outfits and the Beautification and the Magnanimity (al-Kafi, vol 6), 8:37
citation.arabic_text: دَخَلْتُ عَلَى أَبِي إِبْرَاهِيمَ ( عليه السلام ) وَ فِي يَدِهِ مُشْطُ عَاجٍ يَتَمَشَّطُ بِهِ فَقُلْتُ لَهُ جُعِلْتُ فِدَاكَ إِنَّ عِنْدَنَا بِالْعِرَاقِ مَنْ يَزْعُمُ أَنَّهُ لَا يَحِلُّ التَّمَشُّطُ بِالْعَاجِ قَالَ وَ لِمَ فَقَدْ كَانَ لِأَبِي ( عليه السلام ) مِنْهَا مُشْطٌ أَوْ مُشْطَانِ ثُمَّ قَالَ تَمَشَّطُوا بِالْعَاجِ فَإِنَّ الْعَاجَ يَذْهَبُ بِالْوَبَاءِ .
citation.translation: Ali Bin Ibrhim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Al Husayn Bin Al Hassan Bin Aasim, from his father who said, ‘I went over to Abu Ibrahim<sup>asws</sup> (7<sup>th</sup> Imam<sup>asws</sup>), and in his<sup>asws</sup> hand was an ivory comb to comb with. So I said to him<sup>asws</sup>, ‘May I be sacrificed for you<sup>asws</sup>! There ones with us in al-Iraq who are alleging that it is not Permissible to be combing with the ivory’. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘And why, for there used to be, from my<sup>asws</sup> father<sup>asws</sup>, one or two ivory combs’. Then he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘You should be combing with the ivory, for the ivory removed the illness (fever)’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: مجهول - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (2/385)

text: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from Salih Bin Al Sandy, from Ja’far Bin Basheer, from Musa Bin Bakr who said, ‘I saw Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> combing with an ivory comb, and I had bought it for him<sup>asws</sup>’.

citation.chapter: The Book of Outfits and the Beautification and the Magnanimity (al-Kafi, vol 6), 8:37
citation.arabic_text: رَأَيْتُ أَبَا الْحَسَنِ ( عليه السلام ) يَتَمَشَّطُ بِمُشْطِ عَاجٍ وَ اشْتَرَيْتُهُ لَهُ .
citation.translation: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from Salih Bin Al Sandy, from Ja’far Bin Basheer, from Musa Bin Bakr who said, ‘I saw Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> combing with an ivory comb, and I had bought it for him<sup>asws</sup>’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: ضعيف - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (22/385)

text: Al Husayn Bin Muhammad, from Moala Bin Muhammad, from Al Washa, from Abdullah Bin Suleyman who said, ‘I asked Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> about the ivory, so he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘There is no problem with it, and there is a comb for me<sup>asws</sup>, from it (ivory)’.

citation.chapter: The Book of Outfits and the Beautification and the Magnanimity (al-Kafi, vol 6), 8:37
citation.arabic_text: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا جَعْفَرٍ ( عليه السلام ) عَنِ الْعَاجِ فَقَالَ لَا بَأْسَ بِهِ وَ إِنَّ لِي مِنْهُ لَمُشْطاً .
citation.translation: Al Husayn Bin Muhammad, from Moala Bin Muhammad, from Al Washa, from Abdullah Bin Suleyman who said, ‘I asked Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> about the ivory, so he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘There is no problem with it, and there is a comb for me<sup>asws</sup>, from it (ivory)’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: ضعيف على المشهور - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (22/385)

text: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Ibn Mahboub, from Nazar Bin Is’haq, from Anbasa Bin Saeed, (It has been narrated) raising the Hadeeth to the Prophet<sup>saww</sup> having said: ‘Frequent combing of the head removes the illness (fever), and brings the livelihood, and increases in the copulation’.

citation.chapter: The Book of Outfits and the Beautification and the Magnanimity (al-Kafi, vol 6), 8:37
citation.arabic_text: كَثْرَةُ تَسْرِيحِ الرَّأْسِ تَذْهَبُ بِالْوَبَاءِ وَ تَجْلِبُ الرِّزْقَ وَ تَزِيدُ فِي الْجِمَاعِ .
citation.translation: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Ibn Mahboub, from Nazar Bin Is’haq, from Anbasa Bin Saeed, (It has been narrated) raising the Hadeeth to the Prophet<sup>saww</sup> having said: ‘Frequent combing of the head removes the illness (fever), and brings the livelihood, and increases in the copulation’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: مجهول - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (22/386)

text: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Abdullah Bin Al Mugheira, (It has been narrated) from Abu Al-Hassanasws regarding the Words of Allahazwj Mighty and Majestic [7:31] O Children of Adam! Take to your adornments at every Masjid. Heasws said: ‘From that is the combing at every Prayer’.

citation.chapter: The Book of Outfits and the Beautification and the Magnanimity (al-Kafi, vol 6), 8:37
citation.arabic_text: اللَّهِ عَزَّ وَ جَلَّ خُذُوا زِينَتَكُمْ عِنْدَ كُلِّ مَسْجِدٍ قَالَ مِنْ ذَلِكَ التَّمَشُّطُ عِنْدَ كُلِّ صَلَاةٍ .
citation.translation: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Abdullah Bin Al Mugheira, (It has been narrated) from Abu Al-Hassanasws regarding the Words of Allahazwj Mighty and Majestic [7:31] O Children of Adam! Take to your adornments at every Masjid. Heasws said: ‘From that is the combing at every Prayer’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: حسن - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (2/386)

text: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Khalid, from Nuh Bin Shuayb, from Ibn Mayyah, from Yunus, from the one who informed him, (It has been narrated) from Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Whenever you comb your head and your beard, then wipe the comb upon your chest for it removes the worries and the illness (fever)’.

citation.chapter: The Book of Outfits and the Beautification and the Magnanimity (al-Kafi, vol 6), 8:37
citation.arabic_text: إِذَا سَرَّحْتَ رَأْسَكَ وَ لِحْيَتَكَ فَأَمِرَّ الْمُشْطَ عَلَى صَدْرِكَ فَإِنَّهُ يَذْهَبُ بِالْهَمِّ وَ الْوَبَاءِ .
citation.translation: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Khalid, from Nuh Bin Shuayb, from Ibn Mayyah, from Yunus, from the one who informed him, (It has been narrated) from Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Whenever you comb your head and your beard, then wipe the comb upon your chest for it removes the worries and the illness (fever)’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: ضعيف - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (22/386)

text: From him, from his father, ‘He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Frequent combing reduces the phlegm’.

citation.chapter: The Book of Outfits and the Beautification and the Magnanimity (al-Kafi, vol 6), 8:37
citation.arabic_text: كَثْرَةُ التَّمَشُّطِ تُقَلِّلُ الْبَلْغَمَ .
citation.translation: From him, from his father, ‘He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Frequent combing reduces the phlegm’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: مرسل - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (22/386)

text: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Al Hassan Bin Atiyya, from Ismail Bin Jabir, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘The one who combs his beard seventy times, and enumerates it one by one, the Satan<sup>la</sup> would not come near him for forty days’.

citation.chapter: The Book of Outfits and the Beautification and the Magnanimity (al-Kafi, vol 6), 8:37
citation.arabic_text: مَنْ سَرَّحَ لِحْيَتَهُ سَبْعِينَ مَرَّةً وَ عَدَّهَا مَرَّةً مَرَّةً لَمْ يَقْرَبْهُ الشَّيْطَانُ أَرْبَعِينَ يَوْماً .
citation.translation: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Al Hassan Bin Atiyya, from Ismail Bin Jabir, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘The one who combs his beard seventy times, and enumerates it one by one, the Satan<sup>la</sup> would not come near him for forty days’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: ضعيف على المشهور - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (2/386)

text: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Ibrahim Bin Mihzam, from Al Qasim Bin Al Waleed who said, ‘I asked Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> about the bones of the elephants, and their oils, and their combs. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘There is no problem with it’.

citation.chapter: The Book of Outfits and the Beautification and the Magnanimity (al-Kafi, vol 6), 8:37
citation.arabic_text: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) عَنْ عِظَامِ الْفِيلِ مَدَاهِنِهَا وَ أَمْشَاطِهَا قَالَ لَا بَأْسَ بِهَا .
citation.translation: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Ibrahim Bin Mihzam, from Al Qasim Bin Al Waleed who said, ‘I asked Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> about the bones of the elephants, and their oils, and their combs. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘There is no problem with it’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: مجهول - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (2/386)

text: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Al Qasim Bin Yahya, from his grandfather Al Hassan Bin Rashid who said, ‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘Trimming the nails prevents the grievous illness and bring the livelihood’.

citation.chapter: The Book of Outfits and the Beautification and the Magnanimity (al-Kafi, vol 6), 8:38
citation.arabic_text: قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ ( صلى الله عليه وآله ) تَقْلِيمُ الْأَظْفَارِ يَمْنَعُ الدَّاءَ الْأَعْظَمَ وَ يُدِرُّ الرِّزْقَ .
citation.translation: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Al Qasim Bin Yahya, from his grandfather Al Hassan Bin Rashid who said, ‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘Trimming the nails prevents the grievous illness and bring the livelihood’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: ضعيف - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (2/387)

text: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hisham Bin Salim, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Trimming the nails on the day of Friday is a safety from the leprosy, and the vitiligo, and the blindness, and if you do not need to, so file it’.

citation.chapter: The Book of Outfits and the Beautification and the Magnanimity (al-Kafi, vol 6), 8:38
citation.arabic_text: تَقْلِيمُ الْأَظْفَارِ يَوْمَ الْجُمُعَةِ يُؤَمِّنُ مِنَ الْجُذَامِ وَ الْبَرَصِ وَ الْعَمَى وَ إِنْ لَمْ تَحْتَجْ فَحُكَّهَا .
citation.translation: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hisham Bin Salim, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Trimming the nails on the day of Friday is a safety from the leprosy, and the vitiligo, and the blindness, and if you do not need to, so file it’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: حسن - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (2/387)

text: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Al Hassan Bin Ali, from Al Hassan Bin Suleyman, from his uncle Abdullah Bin Hilal who said, ‘Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said to me: ‘Take (pluck) from your moustache and (cut) your nails during every Friday, so if there does not happen to be anything in these, so file it, and neither will insanity hit you, nor leprosy, nor vitiligo’.

citation.chapter: The Book of Outfits and the Beautification and the Magnanimity (al-Kafi, vol 6), 8:38
citation.arabic_text: قَالَ لِي أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) خُذْ مِنْ شَارِبِكَ وَ أَظْفَارِكَ فِي كُلِّ جُمُعَةٍ فَإِنْ لَمْ يَكُنْ فِيهَا شَيْ‏ءٌ فَحُكَّهَا لَا يُصِيبُكَ جُنُونٌ وَ لَا جُذَامٌ وَ لَا بَرَصٌ .
citation.translation: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Al Hassan Bin Ali, from Al Hassan Bin Suleyman, from his uncle Abdullah Bin Hilal who said, ‘Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said to me: ‘Take (pluck) from your moustache and (cut) your nails during every Friday, so if there does not happen to be anything in these, so file it, and neither will insanity hit you, nor leprosy, nor vitiligo’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: مجهول - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (2/387)

text: From him, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ibn Bukeyr, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Trimming the nails, and taking (plucking) the moustache during every Friday is a safety from the vitiligo and the insanity’.

citation.chapter: The Book of Outfits and the Beautification and the Magnanimity (al-Kafi, vol 6), 8:38
citation.arabic_text: تَقْلِيمُ الْأَظْفَارِ وَ أَخْذُ الشَّارِبِ فِي كُلِّ جُمُعَةٍ أَمَانٌ مِنَ الْبَرَصِ وَ الْجُنُونِ .
citation.translation: From him, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ibn Bukeyr, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Trimming the nails, and taking (plucking) the moustache during every Friday is a safety from the vitiligo and the insanity’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: موثق - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (2/387)

text: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Abu Nasr, from Ibn Uqba, from his father, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘From the Sunnah is the trimming of the nails’.

citation.chapter: The Book of Outfits and the Beautification and the Magnanimity (al-Kafi, vol 6), 8:38
citation.arabic_text: مِنَ السُّنَّةِ تَقْلِيمُ الْأَظْفَارِ .
citation.translation: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Abu Nasr, from Ibn Uqba, from his father, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘From the Sunnah is the trimming of the nails’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: ضعيف على المشهور - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (22/387)

text: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Abu Abdullah, from his father, from the one who mentioned it, from Ayoub Bin Al Hurr, from Abu Hama, (It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘But rather, clip the nails because these are a resting-place for the Satan<sup>la</sup>, and from it happens the forgetfulness’.

citation.chapter: The Book of Outfits and the Beautification and the Magnanimity (al-Kafi, vol 6), 8:38
citation.arabic_text: إِنَّمَا قُصَّ الْأَظْفَارُ لِأَنَّهَا مَقِيلُ الشَّيْطَانِ وَ مِنْهُ يَكُونُ النِّسْيَانُ .
citation.translation: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Abu Abdullah, from his father, from the one who mentioned it, from Ayoub Bin Al Hurr, from Abu Hama, (It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘But rather, clip the nails because these are a resting-place for the Satan<sup>la</sup>, and from it happens the forgetfulness’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: مرسل - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (22/387)

text: From him, from Muhammad Bin Ali, from Al Hakam Bin Miskeyn, from Huzayfa Bin Mansour, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘The most veiled and most concealed (place) from where the Satan<sup>la</sup> overcomes a son of Adam<sup>as</sup> is that he<sup>la</sup> settles underneath the nails’.

citation.chapter: The Book of Outfits and the Beautification and the Magnanimity (al-Kafi, vol 6), 8:38
citation.arabic_text: إِنَّ أَسْتَرَ وَ أَخْفَى مَا يُسَلِّطُ الشَّيْطَانَ مِنِ ابْنِ آدَمَ أَنْ صَارَ أَنْ يَسْكُنَ تَحْتَ الْأَظَافِيرِ .
citation.translation: From him, from Muhammad Bin Ali, from Al Hakam Bin Miskeyn, from Huzayfa Bin Mansour, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘The most veiled and most concealed (place) from where the Satan<sup>la</sup> overcomes a son of Adam<sup>as</sup> is that he<sup>la</sup> settles underneath the nails’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: ضعيف - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (22/388)

text: From him, from Muhammad Bin Ali, from Ali Al Hannat, from Ali Bin Abu Hamza, from Al Husayn Bin Abu Al A’ala, from Abu Baseer, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, said, ‘I said to him<sup>asws</sup>, ‘What is a Reward for the one who takes (trims) from his moustache, and trims his nails during every Friday?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘He would not cease to be clean up to the other Friday’.

citation.chapter: The Book of Outfits and the Beautification and the Magnanimity (al-Kafi, vol 6), 8:38
citation.arabic_text: قُلْتُ لَهُ مَا ثَوَابُ مَنْ أَخَذَ مِنْ شَارِبِهِ وَ قَلَّمَ أَظْفَارَهُ فِي كُلِّ جُمُعَةٍ قَالَ لَا يَزَالُ مُطَهَّراً إِلَى الْجُمُعَةِ الْأُخْرَى .
citation.translation: From him, from Muhammad Bin Ali, from Ali Al Hannat, from Ali Bin Abu Hamza, from Al Husayn Bin Abu Al A’ala, from Abu Baseer, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, said, ‘I said to him<sup>asws</sup>, ‘What is a Reward for the one who takes (trims) from his moustache, and trims his nails during every Friday?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘He would not cease to be clean up to the other Friday’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: ضعيف على المشهور - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (2/388)

text: From him, from Ibn Fazzal, from Abu Hafs Al Jarjany, from Abu Al Khazeyb Al Rabie Bin Bakr Al Azdy, from Abdul Rahim al Qaseyr who said, ‘Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The one who takes from his nails and his moustache, every Friday, and says when he takes, ‘In the Name of Allah<sup>azwj</sup> and with Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, and upon Sunnah of Muhammad<sup>saww</sup>, Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup>’, there will not fall off from him, nether a clipping nor a trimming except that Allah<sup>azwj</sup> would Write for him, due to it, an emancipation of a person, and he would not fall sick except for the sickness in which he would be dying’.

citation.chapter: The Book of Outfits and the Beautification and the Magnanimity (al-Kafi, vol 6), 8:38
citation.arabic_text: قَالَ أَبُو جَعْفَرٍ ( عليه السلام ) مَنْ أَخَذَ مِنْ أَظْفَارِهِ وَ شَارِبِهِ كُلَّ جُمُعَةٍ وَ قَالَ حِينَ يَأْخُذُ بِسْمِ اللَّهِ وَ بِاللَّهِ وَ عَلَى سُنَّةِ مُحَمَّدٍ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ ( صلى الله عليه وآله ) لَمْ يَسْقُطْ مِنْهُ قُلَامَةٌ وَ لَا جُزَازَةٌ إِلَّا كَتَبَ اللَّهُ لَهُ بِهَا عِتْقَ نَسَمَةٍ وَ لَا يَمْرَضُ إِلَّا مَرَضَهُ الَّذِي يَمُوتُ فِيهِ .
citation.translation: From him, from Ibn Fazzal, from Abu Hafs Al Jarjany, from Abu Al Khazeyb Al Rabie Bin Bakr Al Azdy, from Abdul Rahim al Qaseyr who said, ‘Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The one who takes from his nails and his moustache, every Friday, and says when he takes, ‘In the Name of Allah<sup>azwj</sup> and with Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, and upon Sunnah of Muhammad<sup>saww</sup>, Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup>’, there will not fall off from him, nether a clipping nor a trimming except that Allah<sup>azwj</sup> would Write for him, due to it, an emancipation of a person, and he would not fall sick except for the sickness in which he would be dying’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: مجهول - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (22/388)

text: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Muhammad Bin Talha who said, ‘Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Trimming of the nails and clipping of the moustache, and washing of the head with the hibiscus (plant) every Friday negates the poverty and increase in the livelihood’.

citation.chapter: The Book of Outfits and the Beautification and the Magnanimity (al-Kafi, vol 6), 8:38
citation.arabic_text: قَالَ أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) تَقْلِيمُ الْأَظْفَارِ وَ قَصُّ الشَّارِبِ وَ غَسْلُ الرَّأْسِ بِالْخِطْمِيِّ كُلَّ جُمُعَةٍ يَنْفِي الْفَقْرَ وَ يَزِيدُ فِي الرِّزْقِ .
citation.translation: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Muhammad Bin Talha who said, ‘Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Trimming of the nails and clipping of the moustache, and washing of the head with the hibiscus (plant) every Friday negates the poverty and increase in the livelihood’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: مجهول - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (2/388)

text: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Al Hassan Bin Ali Bin Uqba, from Abu Kahmas who said, ‘A man said to Abdullah Bin Al-Hassan, ‘Teach me something regarding the sustenance’. So he said, ‘Necessitate upon yourself to stay in your Prayer mat when you have Prayed Al-Fajr, up to the emergence of the sun, for it is more beneficial in the seeking of the livelihood than the going about in the land, for I informed Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> with that, so he<sup>asws</sup> said, ‘Shall I<sup>asws</sup> teach you regarding the livelihood what is more beneficial than that?’ I said, ‘Yes’. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Take from your moustache and your nails, every Friday’.

citation.chapter: The Book of Outfits and the Beautification and the Magnanimity (al-Kafi, vol 6), 8:38
citation.arabic_text: قَالَ رَجُلٌ لِعَبْدِ اللَّهِ بْنِ الْحَسَنِ عَلِّمْنِي شَيْئاً فِي الرِّزْقِ فَقَالَ الْزَمْ مُصَلَّاكَ إِذَا صَلَّيْتَ الْفَجْرَ إِلَى طُلُوعِ الشَّمْسِ فَإِنَّهُ أَنْجَعُ فِي طَلَبِ الرِّزْقِ مِنَ الضَّرْبِ فِي الْأَرْضِ فَأَخْبَرْتُ بِذَلِكَ أَبَا عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) فَقَالَ أَ لَا أُعَلِّمُكَ فِي الرِّزْقِ مَا هُوَ أَنْفَعُ مِنْ ذَلِكَ قَالَ قُلْتُ بَلَى قَالَ خُذْ مِنْ شَارِبِكَ وَ أَظْفَارِكَ كُلَّ جُمُعَةٍ .
citation.translation: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Al Hassan Bin Ali Bin Uqba, from Abu Kahmas who said, ‘A man said to Abdullah Bin Al-Hassan, ‘Teach me something regarding the sustenance’. So he said, ‘Necessitate upon yourself to stay in your Prayer mat when you have Prayed Al-Fajr, up to the emergence of the sun, for it is more beneficial in the seeking of the livelihood than the going about in the land, for I informed Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> with that, so he<sup>asws</sup> said, ‘Shall I<sup>asws</sup> teach you regarding the livelihood what is more beneficial than that?’ I said, ‘Yes’. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Take from your moustache and your nails, every Friday’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: مجهول - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (2/389)

text: From him, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ali Bin Uqba, from his father who said, ‘I went over to Abdullah Bin Al-Hassan (Al-Basry), so I said, ‘Teach me a supplication regarding the livelihood. So he said, ‘Say, ‘O Allah<sup>azwj</sup>! You<sup>azwj</sup> Handle my matters and do not let anyone other than You<sup>azwj</sup> handle my matters’. So I presented it to Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, so he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Shall I<sup>asws</sup> point you upon what is more beneficial than this regarding the livelihood? Clip your nails and your moustache during every Friday, even though it be by filing it’.

citation.chapter: The Book of Outfits and the Beautification and the Magnanimity (al-Kafi, vol 6), 8:38
citation.arabic_text: أَتَيْتُ عَبْدَ اللَّهِ بْنَ الْحَسَنِ فَقُلْتُ عَلِّمْنِي دُعَاءً فِي الرِّزْقِ فَقَالَ قُلِ اللَّهُمَّ تَوَلَّ أَمْرِي وَ لَا تُوَلِّ أَمْرِي غَيْرَكَ فَعَرَضْتُهُ عَلَى أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) فَقَالَ أَ لَا أَدُلُّكَ عَلَى مَا هُوَ أَنْفَعُ مِنْ هَذَا فِي الرِّزْقِ تَقُصُّ أَظَافِيرَكَ وَ شَارِبَكَ فِي كُلِّ جُمُعَةٍ وَ لَوْ بِحَكِّهَا .
citation.translation: From him, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ali Bin Uqba, from his father who said, ‘I went over to Abdullah Bin Al-Hassan (Al-Basry), so I said, ‘Teach me a supplication regarding the livelihood. So he said, ‘Say, ‘O Allah<sup>azwj</sup>! You<sup>azwj</sup> Handle my matters and do not let anyone other than You<sup>azwj</sup> handle my matters’. So I presented it to Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, so he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Shall I<sup>asws</sup> point you upon what is more beneficial than this regarding the livelihood? Clip your nails and your moustache during every Friday, even though it be by filing it’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: حسن أو موثق - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (22/389)

text: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Abu Abdullah, from Ali Bin Asbaat, from Khalaf who said, ‘Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> saw me at Khurasan and I complained about my eyes. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Shall I<sup>asws</sup> point you upon something that if you were to do it, you would not complain of your eyes?’ So I said, ‘Yes’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Take from your nails during every Thursday’. So I did it, and I did not complain about my eyes up to the day that I am informing you’.

citation.chapter: The Book of Outfits and the Beautification and the Magnanimity (al-Kafi, vol 6), 8:38
citation.arabic_text: رَآنِي أَبُو الْحَسَنِ ( عليه السلام ) بِخُرَاسَانَ وَ أَنَا أَشْتَكِي عَيْنِي فَقَالَ أَ لَا أَدُلُّكَ عَلَى شَيْ‏ءٍ إِنْ فَعَلْتَهُ لَمْ تَشْتَكِ عَيْنَكَ فَقُلْتُ بَلَى فَقَالَ خُذْ مِنْ أَظْفَارِكَ فِي كُلِّ خَمِيسٍ قَالَ فَفَعَلْتُ فَمَا اشْتَكَيْتُ عَيْنِي إِلَى يَوْمَ أَخْبَرْتُكَ .
citation.translation: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Abu Abdullah, from Ali Bin Asbaat, from Khalaf who said, ‘Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> saw me at Khurasan and I complained about my eyes. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Shall I<sup>asws</sup> point you upon something that if you were to do it, you would not complain of your eyes?’ So I said, ‘Yes’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Take from your nails during every Thursday’. So I did it, and I did not complain about my eyes up to the day that I am informing you’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: مجهول - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (2/389)

text: From him, from his father, from Abu Abdullah Bin Al Fazl Al Nowfaly, from his father, and his uncle, altogether, (It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘The one who is habitual in taking his nails during every Thursday, would not have conjunctivitis of his eye’.

citation.chapter: The Book of Outfits and the Beautification and the Magnanimity (al-Kafi, vol 6), 8:38
citation.arabic_text: مَنْ أَدْمَنَ أَخْذَ أَظْفَارِهِ كُلَّ خَمِيسٍ لَمْ تَرْمَدْ عَيْنُهُ .
citation.translation: From him, from his father, from Abu Abdullah Bin Al Fazl Al Nowfaly, from his father, and his uncle, altogether, (It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘The one who is habitual in taking his nails during every Thursday, would not have conjunctivitis of his eye’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: مجهول - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (22/389)

text: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Al Nowfaly, from Al Sakuny who said, ‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said to the men: ‘Clip your nails’, and (said) to the women: ‘Leave them for it is an adornment for you’.

citation.chapter: The Book of Outfits and the Beautification and the Magnanimity (al-Kafi, vol 6), 8:38
citation.arabic_text: قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ ( صلى الله عليه وآله ) لِلرِّجَالِ قُصُّوا أَظَافِيرَكُمْ وَ لِلنِّسَاءِ اتْرُكْنَ فَإِنَّهُ أَزْيَنُ لَكُنَّ .
citation.translation: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Al Nowfaly, from Al Sakuny who said, ‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said to the men: ‘Clip your nails’, and (said) to the women: ‘Leave them for it is an adornment for you’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: ضعيف على المشهور - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (2/389)

text: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, raising it, ‘(He<sup>asws</sup> said): ‘With regards to clipping the nails, begin with the little finger of the left hand, then end with the little finger of the right hand’.

citation.chapter: The Book of Outfits and the Beautification and the Magnanimity (al-Kafi, vol 6), 8:38
citation.arabic_text: قَصِّ الْأَظْفَارِ تَبْدَأُ بِخِنْصِرِ الْأَيْسَرِ ثُمَّ تَخْتِمُ بِالْيَمِينِ .
citation.translation: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, raising it, ‘(He<sup>asws</sup> said): ‘With regards to clipping the nails, begin with the little finger of the left hand, then end with the little finger of the right hand’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: موقوف - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (22/390)

text: Al Husayn Bin Muhammad, from Moala Bin Muhammad, from Ja’far Bin Muhammad Al Ashary, from Ibn Al Qaddah, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘The Revelation was Withheld from the Prophet<sup>saww</sup>, so it was said to him<sup>saww</sup>, ‘The Revelation has been Withheld from you<sup>saww</sup>’. So he<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘And why should it not be Withheld and you all are not cutting your nails and are not cleaning your hands?’

citation.chapter: The Book of Outfits and the Beautification and the Magnanimity (al-Kafi, vol 6), 8:38
citation.arabic_text: احْتَبَسَ الْوَحْيُ عَنِ النَّبِيِّ ( صلى الله عليه وآله ) فَقِيلَ لَهُ احْتَبَسَ الْوَحْيُ عَنْكَ فَقَالَ ( صلى الله عليه وآله ) وَ كَيْفَ لَا يَحْتَبِسُ وَ أَنْتُمْ لَا تُقَلِّمُونَ أَظْفَارَكُمْ وَ لَا تُنَقُّونَ رَوَاجِبَكُمْ .
citation.translation: Al Husayn Bin Muhammad, from Moala Bin Muhammad, from Ja’far Bin Muhammad Al Ashary, from Ibn Al Qaddah, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘The Revelation was Withheld from the Prophet<sup>saww</sup>, so it was said to him<sup>saww</sup>, ‘The Revelation has been Withheld from you<sup>saww</sup>’. So he<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘And why should it not be Withheld and you all are not cutting your nails and are not cleaning your hands?’
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: ضعيف على المشهور - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (22/390)

text: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Al Hassan Bin Ali Al Washa, from Abdullah Bin Sinan, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘There is no problem with cutting the grey hair and plucking it, and cutting it is more beloved to me than plucking it’.

citation.chapter: The Book of Outfits and the Beautification and the Magnanimity (al-Kafi, vol 6), 8:39
citation.arabic_text: لَا بَأْسَ بِجَزِّ الشَّمَطِ وَ نَتْفِهِ وَ جَزُّهُ أَحَبُّ إِلَيَّ مِنْ نَتْفِهِ .
citation.translation: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Al Hassan Bin Ali Al Washa, from Abdullah Bin Sinan, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘There is no problem with cutting the grey hair and plucking it, and cutting it is more beloved to me than plucking it’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: صحيح - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (22/390)

text: From him, from Ibn Fazzal, from the one who mentioned it, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘There is no problem with cutting the grey hair and plucking it from the beard’.

citation.chapter: The Book of Outfits and the Beautification and the Magnanimity (al-Kafi, vol 6), 8:39
citation.arabic_text: لَا بَأْسَ بِجَزِّ الشَّمَطِ وَ نَتْفِهِ مِنَ اللِّحْيَةِ .
citation.translation: From him, from Ibn Fazzal, from the one who mentioned it, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘There is no problem with cutting the grey hair and plucking it from the beard’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: مرسل - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (2/390)

text: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Al Nowfaly, from Al Sakuny, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> that Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> did not view the cutting of the grey hairs as a problem, and disliked plucking it’.

citation.chapter: The Book of Outfits and the Beautification and the Magnanimity (al-Kafi, vol 6), 8:39
citation.arabic_text: أَنَّ أَمِيرَ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ ( عليه السلام ) كَانَ لَا يَرَى بِجَزِّ الشَّيْبِ بَأْساً وَ يَكْرَهُ نَتْفَهُ .
citation.translation: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Al Nowfaly, from Al Sakuny, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> that Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> did not view the cutting of the grey hairs as a problem, and disliked plucking it’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: ضعيف على المشهور - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (22/391)

text: And by this chain, ‘He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The first one to be grey-haired was Ibrahim<sup>as</sup>. He<sup>as</sup> said: ‘O Lord<sup>azwj</sup>! What is this?’ So He<sup>azwj</sup> Said: “A radiance and a reverence”. He<sup>as</sup> said: ‘Lord<sup>azwj</sup>! Increase for me<sup>as</sup>, from it’.

citation.chapter: The Book of Outfits and the Beautification and the Magnanimity (al-Kafi, vol 6), 8:39
citation.arabic_text: وَ بِهَذَا الْإِسْنَادِ قَالَ ( عليه السلام ) أَوَّلُ مَنْ شَابَ إِبْرَاهِيمُ ( عليه السلام ) فَقَالَ يَا رَبِّ مَا هَذَا فَقَالَ نُورٌ وَ تَوْقِيرٌ قَالَ رَبِّ زِدْنِي مِنْهُ .
citation.translation: And by this chain, ‘He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The first one to be grey-haired was Ibrahim<sup>as</sup>. He<sup>as</sup> said: ‘O Lord<sup>azwj</sup>! What is this?’ So He<sup>azwj</sup> Said: “A radiance and a reverence”. He<sup>as</sup> said: ‘Lord<sup>azwj</sup>! Increase for me<sup>as</sup>, from it’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: ضعيف على المشهور - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (2/391)

text: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hafs Bin Al Bakhtary, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘The people were not becoming grey-haired. So Ibrahim<sup>as</sup> saw something in his<sup>as</sup> beard, so he<sup>as</sup> said: ‘O Lord<sup>azwj</sup>! What is this?’ So He<sup>azwj</sup> Said: “This is a reverence”. So he<sup>as</sup> said: ‘O Lord<sup>azwj</sup>! Increase the reverence for me<sup>as</sup>’’.

citation.chapter: The Book of Outfits and the Beautification and the Magnanimity (al-Kafi, vol 6), 8:39
citation.arabic_text: كَانَ النَّاسُ لَا يَشِيبُونَ فَأَبْصَرَ إِبْرَاهِيمُ ( عليه السلام ) شَيْباً فِي لِحْيَتِهِ فَقَالَ يَا رَبِّ مَا هَذَا فَقَالَ هَذَا وَقَارٌ فَقَالَ يَا رَبِّ زِدْنِي وَقَاراً .
citation.translation: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hafs Bin Al Bakhtary, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘The people were not becoming grey-haired. So Ibrahim<sup>as</sup> saw something in his<sup>as</sup> beard, so he<sup>as</sup> said: ‘O Lord<sup>azwj</sup>! What is this?’ So He<sup>azwj</sup> Said: “This is a reverence”. So he<sup>as</sup> said: ‘O Lord<sup>azwj</sup>! Increase the reverence for me<sup>as</sup>’’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: حسن - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (22/391)

text: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Abu Abdullah, from Abu Ayoub Al Madainy, from Suleyman Al Ja’fary, (It has been narrated) from Al-Reza<sup>asws</sup>, from his<sup>asws</sup> forefathers<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘The grey hair in the front part of the head is a Blessing, and in the two sides is generosity, and in the top is courage, and in the back is inauspiciousness’.

citation.chapter: The Book of Outfits and the Beautification and the Magnanimity (al-Kafi, vol 6), 8:39
citation.arabic_text: الشَّيْبُ فِي مُقَدَّمِ الرَّأْسِ يُمْنٌ وَ فِي الْعَارِضَيْنِ سَخَاءٌ وَ فِي الذَّوَائِبِ شَجَاعَةٌ وَ فِي الْقَفَا شُؤْمٌ .
citation.translation: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Abu Abdullah, from Abu Ayoub Al Madainy, from Suleyman Al Ja’fary, (It has been narrated) from Al-Reza<sup>asws</sup>, from his<sup>asws</sup> forefathers<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘The grey hair in the front part of the head is a Blessing, and in the two sides is generosity, and in the top is courage, and in the back is inauspiciousness’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: مجهول - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (22/391)

text: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Ibn Fazzal, from one of his companions, from Abu Kahmas, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws regarding the Words of Allahazwj Mighty and Majestic [77:25] Have We not made the earth as a place [77:26] For the living and the dead. Heasws said: Burying of the hair and the nails’.

citation.chapter: The Book of Outfits and the Beautification and the Magnanimity (al-Kafi, vol 6), 8:40
citation.arabic_text: اللَّهِ عَزَّ وَ جَلَّ أَ لَمْ نَجْعَلِ الْأَرْضَ كِفاتاً أَحْياءً وَ أَمْواتاً قَالَ دَفْنُ الشَّعْرِ وَ الظُّفُرِ .
citation.translation: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Ibn Fazzal, from one of his companions, from Abu Kahmas, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws regarding the Words of Allahazwj Mighty and Majestic [77:25] Have We not made the earth as a place [77:26] For the living and the dead. Heasws said: Burying of the hair and the nails’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: ضعيف على المشهور - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (22/391)

text: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father and Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Suleym Al Farra’a, from a man, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> used to apply kohl with antimony (white powder) whenever he<sup>saww</sup> went to his<sup>saww</sup> bed, once, once (in each eye)’.

citation.chapter: The Book of Outfits and the Beautification and the Magnanimity (al-Kafi, vol 6), 8:41
citation.arabic_text: كَانَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ ( صلى الله عليه وآله ) يَكْتَحِلُ بِالْإِثْمِدِ إِذَا أَوَى إِلَى فِرَاشِهِ وَتْراً وَتْراً .
citation.translation: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father and Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Suleym Al Farra’a, from a man, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> used to apply kohl with antimony (white powder) whenever he<sup>saww</sup> went to his<sup>saww</sup> bed, once, once (in each eye)’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: مرسل - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (22/392)

text: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Al Hassan Bin Al Jaham who said, ‘Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> showed me an iron needle (applicator) and Kohl container (made out of) bone, so he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘It used to be for Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> to apply it, so I<sup>asws</sup> apply it’.

citation.chapter: The Book of Outfits and the Beautification and the Magnanimity (al-Kafi, vol 6), 8:41
citation.arabic_text: أَرَانِي أَبُو الْحَسَنِ ( عليه السلام ) مِيلًا مِنْ حَدِيدٍ وَ مُكْحُلَةً مِنْ عِظَامٍ فَقَالَ هَذَا كَانَ لِأَبِي الْحَسَنِ فَاكْتَحِلْ بِهِ فَاكْتَحَلْتُ .
citation.translation: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Al Hassan Bin Al Jaham who said, ‘Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> showed me an iron needle (applicator) and Kohl container (made out of) bone, so he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘It used to be for Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> to apply it, so I<sup>asws</sup> apply it’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: موثق كالصحيح - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (22/392)

text: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Abu Abdullah, from Musa Bin Al Qasim, from Safwan, from Zurara, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘The (application of) the Kohl at night benefits the eyes, and it is an adornment by the day’.

citation.chapter: The Book of Outfits and the Beautification and the Magnanimity (al-Kafi, vol 6), 8:41
citation.arabic_text: الْكُحْلُ بِاللَّيْلِ يَنْفَعُ الْعَيْنَ وَ هُوَ بِالنَّهَارِ زِينَةٌ .
citation.translation: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Abu Abdullah, from Musa Bin Al Qasim, from Safwan, from Zurara, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘The (application of) the Kohl at night benefits the eyes, and it is an adornment by the day’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: صحيح - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (2/393)

text: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Abdullah Bin Al Fal Al Hashimy, from his father and his uncle who both said, ‘Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Application of Kohl with antimony (white eye-powder) aromatises the breath and strengthens the edges of the eyes’.

citation.chapter: The Book of Outfits and the Beautification and the Magnanimity (al-Kafi, vol 6), 8:41
citation.arabic_text: ا قَالَ أَبُو جَعْفَرٍ ( عليه السلام ) الِاكْتِحَالُ بِالْإِثْمِدِ يُطَيِّبُ النَّكْهَةَ وَ يَشُدُّ أَشْفَارَ الْعَيْنِ .
citation.translation: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Abdullah Bin Al Fal Al Hashimy, from his father and his uncle who both said, ‘Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Application of Kohl with antimony (white eye-powder) aromatises the breath and strengthens the edges of the eyes’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: مجهول - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (2/393)

text: From him, from Ibn Fazzal, from Hammad Bin Isa, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘The Kohl freshens the mouth’.

citation.chapter: The Book of Outfits and the Beautification and the Magnanimity (al-Kafi, vol 6), 8:41
citation.arabic_text: الْكُحْلُ يُعْذِبُ الْفَمَ .
citation.translation: From him, from Ibn Fazzal, from Hammad Bin Isa, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘The Kohl freshens the mouth’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: موثق كالصحيح - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (22/393)

text: From him, from his father, from Khalaf Bin Hammad, from the one who mentioned, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘The Kohl grows the hair and sharpens the vision and assists upon the prolonged Prostrations’.

citation.chapter: The Book of Outfits and the Beautification and the Magnanimity (al-Kafi, vol 6), 8:41
citation.arabic_text: الْكُحْلُ يُنْبِتُ الشَّعْرَ وَ يُحِدُّ الْبَصَرَ وَ يُعِينُ عَلَى طُولِ السُّجُودِ .
citation.translation: From him, from his father, from Khalaf Bin Hammad, from the one who mentioned, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘The Kohl grows the hair and sharpens the vision and assists upon the prolonged Prostrations’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: مرسل - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (22/393)

text: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ali Bin Uqba, (It has been narrated) from a man from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘The antimony clears the vision, and grows the hair, and removes the tears’.

citation.chapter: The Book of Outfits and the Beautification and the Magnanimity (al-Kafi, vol 6), 8:41
citation.arabic_text: الْإِثْمِدُ يَجْلُو الْبَصَرَ وَ يُنْبِتُ الشَّعْرَ وَ يَذْهَبُ بِالدَّمْعَةِ .
citation.translation: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ali Bin Uqba, (It has been narrated) from a man from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘The antimony clears the vision, and grows the hair, and removes the tears’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: مرسل - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (22/393)

text: Ibn Fazzal, from one of our companions, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:’ The Kohl increased in the copulation’.

citation.chapter: The Book of Outfits and the Beautification and the Magnanimity (al-Kafi, vol 6), 8:41
citation.arabic_text: الْكُحْلُ يَزِيدُ فِي الْمُبَاضَعَةِ .
citation.translation: Ibn Fazzal, from one of our companions, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:’ The Kohl increased in the copulation’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: مرسل - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (2/393)

text: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Abu Abdullah, form Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Abu Nasr, from Ahmad Bin Al Mubarak, from Al Husayn Bin Al Hassan Bin Aasim, from his father, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘The one who sleeps upon antimony (white eye powder) without putting musk in it would be safe from the black water (blackness in the eyes) for ever for as long as he sleeps upon it’.

citation.chapter: The Book of Outfits and the Beautification and the Magnanimity (al-Kafi, vol 6), 8:41
citation.arabic_text: مَنْ نَامَ عَلَى إِثْمِدٍ غَيْرِ مُمَسَّكٍ أَمِنَ مِنَ الْمَاءِ الْأَسْوَدِ أَبَداً مَا دَامَ يَنَامُ عَلَيْهِ .
citation.translation: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Abu Abdullah, form Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Abu Nasr, from Ahmad Bin Al Mubarak, from Al Husayn Bin Al Hassan Bin Aasim, from his father, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘The one who sleeps upon antimony (white eye powder) without putting musk in it would be safe from the black water (blackness in the eyes) for ever for as long as he sleeps upon it’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: مجهول - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (22/393)

text: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Muhammad Bin Sinan, from Hammad Bin Usman, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘The application of Kohl grows the hair, and removes the tears, and freshens the saliva, and clears the vision’.

citation.chapter: The Book of Outfits and the Beautification and the Magnanimity (al-Kafi, vol 6), 8:41
citation.arabic_text: الْكُحْلُ يُنْبِتُ الشَّعْرَ وَ يُجَفِّفُ الدَّمْعَةَ وَ وَ يُعْذِبُ الرِّيقَ وَ يَجْلُو الْبَصَرَ .
citation.translation: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Muhammad Bin Sinan, from Hammad Bin Usman, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘The application of Kohl grows the hair, and removes the tears, and freshens the saliva, and clears the vision’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: ضعيف على المشهور - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (22/394)

text: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Abu Abdullah, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ibn Al Qaddah, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The one who applies Kohl so let him do it once, and the one who does it so he has done good, and the one who does not do it, so there is no problem’.

citation.chapter: The Book of Outfits and the Beautification and the Magnanimity (al-Kafi, vol 6), 8:41
citation.arabic_text: قَالَ أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ ( صلوات الله عليه ) مَنِ اكْتَحَلَ فَلْيُوتِرْ وَ مَنْ فَعَلَ فَقَدْ أَحْسَنَ وَ مَنْ لَمْ يَفْعَلْ فَلَا بَأْسَ .
citation.translation: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Abu Abdullah, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ibn Al Qaddah, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The one who applies Kohl so let him do it once, and the one who does it so he has done good, and the one who does not do it, so there is no problem’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: موثق - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (22/394)

text: From him, from Musa Bin Al Qasim, from Safwan, from Zurara, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> used to apply Kohl before he<sup>saww</sup> slept – four (times) in the right, and three (times) in the left’.

citation.chapter: The Book of Outfits and the Beautification and the Magnanimity (al-Kafi, vol 6), 8:41
citation.arabic_text: إِنَّ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ ( صلى الله عليه وآله ) كَانَ يَكْتَحِلُ قَبْلَ أَنْ يَنَامَ أَرْبَعاً فِي الْيُمْنَى وَ ثَلَاثاً فِي الْيُسْرَى .
citation.translation: From him, from Musa Bin Al Qasim, from Safwan, from Zurara, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> used to apply Kohl before he<sup>saww</sup> slept – four (times) in the right, and three (times) in the left’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: صحيح - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (22/394)

text: Ali Bin Ibrahim, form his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Is’haq Bin Ammar who said, ‘Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘From the mannerisms of the Prophets<sup>as</sup> is the brushing of teeth’.

citation.chapter: The Book of Outfits and the Beautification and the Magnanimity (al-Kafi, vol 6), 8:42
citation.arabic_text: قَالَ أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) مِنْ أَخْلَاقِ الْأَنْبِيَاءِ ( عليهم السلام ) السِّوَاكُ .
citation.translation: Ali Bin Ibrahim, form his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Is’haq Bin Ammar who said, ‘Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘From the mannerisms of the Prophets<sup>as</sup> is the brushing of teeth’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: حسن أو موثق - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (2/394)

text: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Muhammad Bin Khalid, and Al Husayn Bin Saeed altogether from Al Qasim Bin Urwat, from Is’haq Bin Ammar, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws having said: ‘Brushing of the teeth is from the Sunnah of the Mursil Prophetsas’.

citation.chapter: The Book of Outfits and the Beautification and the Magnanimity (al-Kafi, vol 6), 8:42
citation.arabic_text: السِّوَاكُ مِنْ سُنَنِ الْمُرْسَلِينَ .
citation.translation: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Muhammad Bin Khalid, and Al Husayn Bin Saeed altogether from Al Qasim Bin Urwat, from Is’haq Bin Ammar, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws having said: ‘Brushing of the teeth is from the Sunnah of the Mursil Prophetsas’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: مجهول - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (2/395)

text: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Ja’far Bin Muhammad Al Ashary, from Ibn Al Qaddah, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘Jibraeel<sup>as</sup> did not cease to advise me<sup>saww</sup> with brushing of the teeth to the extent that I<sup>saww</sup> feared being toothless and with thin teeth’.

citation.chapter: The Book of Outfits and the Beautification and the Magnanimity (al-Kafi, vol 6), 8:42
citation.arabic_text: قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ ( صلى الله عليه وآله ) مَا زَالَ جَبْرَئِيلُ ( عليه السلام ) يُوصِينِي بِالسِّوَاكِ حَتَّى خَشِيتُ أَنْ أَدْرَدَ وَ أُحْفِيَ .
citation.translation: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Ja’far Bin Muhammad Al Ashary, from Ibn Al Qaddah, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘Jibraeel<sup>as</sup> did not cease to advise me<sup>saww</sup> with brushing of the teeth to the extent that I<sup>saww</sup> feared being toothless and with thin teeth’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: ضعيف على المشهور - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (2/395)

text: And by this chain – ‘He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The brushing of the teeth is a cleansing for the mouth and a Pleasure of the Lord<sup>azwj</sup>’.

citation.chapter: The Book of Outfits and the Beautification and the Magnanimity (al-Kafi, vol 6), 8:42
citation.arabic_text: وَ بِهَذَا الْإِسْنَادِ قَالَ قَالَ أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ ( عليه السلام ) السِّوَاكُ مَطْهَرَةٌ لِلْفَمِ وَ مَرْضَاةٌ لِلرَّبِّ .
citation.translation: And by this chain – ‘He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The brushing of the teeth is a cleansing for the mouth and a Pleasure of the Lord<sup>azwj</sup>’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: ضعيف على المشهور - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (2/395)

text: Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Muhammad Bin Isa, from Al Hassan Bin Bahr, from Mihzam Al Asady who said, ‘I heard Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> saying: ‘In brushing of the teeth are ten qualities – Cleansing for the mouth, and a Pleasure of the Lord<sup>azwj</sup>, and a happiness for the Angels, and it is from the Sunnah, and it strengthens the gums, and polishes the vision, and it removes the phlegm, and removes the cavities’.

citation.chapter: The Book of Outfits and the Beautification and the Magnanimity (al-Kafi, vol 6), 8:42
citation.arabic_text: سَمِعْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) يَقُولُ فِي السِّوَاكِ عَشَرَةُ خِصَالٍ مَطْهَرَةٌ لِلْفَمِ وَ مَرْضَاةٌ لِلرَّبِّ وَ مَفْرَحَةٌ لِلْمَلَائِكَةِ وَ هُوَ مِنَ السُّنَّةِ وَ يَشُدُّ اللِّثَةَ وَ يَجْلُو الْبَصَرَ وَ يَذْهَبُ بِالْبَلْغَمِ وَ يَذْهَبُ بِالْحَفْرِ .
citation.translation: Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Muhammad Bin Isa, from Al Hassan Bin Bahr, from Mihzam Al Asady who said, ‘I heard Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> saying: ‘In brushing of the teeth are ten qualities – Cleansing for the mouth, and a Pleasure of the Lord<sup>azwj</sup>, and a happiness for the Angels, and it is from the Sunnah, and it strengthens the gums, and polishes the vision, and it removes the phlegm, and removes the cavities’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: ضعيف على المشهور - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (22/395)

text: From him, from Muhammad Bin Isa, from Ubeydullah Al Dahqan, from Dorost, from Ibn Sinan, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘In brushing of the teeth are twelve qualities – It is from the Sunnah, and a cleansing for the mouth, and a polishing for the vision, and a Pleasure of the Lord<sup>azwj</sup>, and it removes the phlegm, and increases in the memorisation, and it whitens the teeth, and it amplifies the Rewards, and removes the cavities, and strengthens the gums, and it makes one desirous of the food, and the Angels are happy with it’.

citation.chapter: The Book of Outfits and the Beautification and the Magnanimity (al-Kafi, vol 6), 8:42
citation.arabic_text: فِي السِّوَاكِ اثْنَتَا عَشَرَ خَصْلَةً هُوَ مِنَ السُّنَّةِ وَ مَطْهَرَةٌ لِلْفَمِ وَ مَجْلَاةٌ لِلْبَصَرِ وَ يُرْضِي الرَّبَّ وَ يَذْهَبُ بِالْبَلْغَمِ وَ يَزِيدُ فِي الْحِفْظِ وَ يُبَيِّضُ الْأَسْنَانَ وَ يُضَاعِفُ الْحَسَنَاتِ وَ يَذْهَبُ بِالْحَفْرِ وَ يَشُدُّ اللِّثَةَ وَ يُشَهِّي الطَّعَامَ وَ تَفْرَحُ بِهِ الْمَلَائِكَةُ .

citation.chapter: The Book of Outfits and the Beautification and the Magnanimity (al-Kafi, vol 6), 8:42
citation.arabic_text: وَصِيَّةِ النَّبِيِّ ( صلى الله عليه وآله ) لِأَمِيرِ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ ( صلوات الله عليه ) عَلَيْكَ بِالسِّوَاكِ لِكُلِّ صَلَاةٍ .

text: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Khalid, from his father, or someone else from Muhammad Bin Aslam Al Jably, raising it, said, ‘Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The best of the houses is the bathhouse. citation.chapter: The Book of Outfits and the Beautification and the Magnanimity (al-Kafi, vol 6), 8:43

text: From him, from Ali Bin Al Hakam and Ali Bin Hassan, from Suleyman Al Ja’fary, (It has been narrated) from Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Bathing a day, and not a day (alternatively) does not increase the flesh, and being habitual of it during every day removes the fat of the kidneys’.

citation.chapter: The Book of Outfits and the Beautification and the Magnanimity (al-Kafi, vol 6), 8:43

citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: صحيح - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (22/397)

text: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Rafa’at Bin Musa, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘The one who was a believer in Allah<sup>azwj</sup> and the Last Day, so he should not enter the bathhouse except with a loincloth’.

text: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Abdullah Bin Muhammad Al Hajjal, from Suleyman Al Ja’fary who said, ‘I was sick to the extent that my flesh went away. So I went over to Al-Reza<sup>asws</sup>, so he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Would you be joyful if I<sup>asws</sup> were to return your flesh to you?’ I said, ‘Yes’. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Necessitate the bathing intermittently so it would return back to you your flesh, and beware of being habitual of it, for being habitual in it inherits the tuberculosis’.

citation.chapter: The Book of Outfits and the Beautification and the Magnanimity (al-Kafi, vol 6), 8:43
citation.arabic_text: مَرِضْتُ حَتَّى ذَهَبَ لَحْمِي فَدَخَلْتُ عَلَى الرِّضَا ( صلوات الله عليه ) فَقَالَ أَ يَسُرُّكَ أَنْ يَعُودَ إِلَيْكَ لَحْمُكَ قُلْتُ بَلَى قَالَ الْزَمِ الْحَمَّامَ غِبّاً فَإِنَّهُ يَعُودُ إِلَيْكَ لَحْمُكَ وَ إِيَّاكَ أَنْ تُدْمِنَهُ فَإِنَّ إِدْمَانَهُ يُورِثُ السِّلَّ .

citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: صحيح - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (2/397)

text: Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Al Hakam, from Al Musna Bin Al Waleed Al Hannat, from Abu Baseer, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Do not enter the bathhouse except in your inside is something to cool down the heat of your stomach with, and it is more strengthening for your body, and do not enter it and you are filled up from the food’.

text: Ali Bin Al Hakam, from Rafa’at Bin Musa, from the one who informed it, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> that whenever he<sup>asws</sup> wanted to enter the bathhouse, he<sup>asws</sup> took something, so he<sup>asws</sup> ate it. I said to him<sup>asws</sup>, ‘The people with us are saying that it is much better upon the empty stomach as can be’. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘No, but eating something before it cools the gallbladder and settles the heat of the interior’.

citation.chapter: The Book of Outfits and the Beautification and the Magnanimity (al-Kafi, vol 6), 8:43
citation.arabic_text: قُلْتُ لَهُ إِنَّ النَّاسَ عِنْدَنَا يَقُولُونَ إِنَّهُ عَلَى الرِّيقِ أَجْوَدُ مَا يَكُونُ قَالَ لَا بَلْ يُؤْكَلُ شَيْ‏ءٌ قَبْلَهُ يُطْفِئُ الْمَرَارَةَ وَ يُسَكِّنُ حَرَارَةَ الْجَوْفِ .

citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: مرسل - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (22/397)

text: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Muhammad Bin Ismail Bin Bazie, altogether from Hanan Bin sadeyr, from his father who said, ‘I and my father, and my grandfather, and my uncle went over to a bathhouse at Al-Medina, so there was a man<sup>asws</sup> in the dressing room. So he said to us, ‘From whom are the people?’ So we said, ‘From the people of Al-Iraq’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said, ‘And from where in Al-Iraq?’ We said, ‘Kufians (from Kufa)’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said, ‘Welcome to you all, of people of Al-Kufa. You all are wearing clothes and are without a towel’. Then he<sup>asws</sup> said, ‘What is preventing you from the loincloth, for Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘The nakedness of the Believer upon the Believer is Prohibited’. He (the narrator) said, ‘He<sup>asws</sup> sent a cloth to my father, so he tore it into four pieces, and each one of us took one from it. Then we entered into it. So when we were in the hot house, he<sup>asws</sup> turned towards my grandfather, so he<sup>asws</sup> said, ‘O elderly, what prevents you from the dyeing?’ So my grandfather said to him, ‘I was with someone who was better than me and you<sup>asws</sup>, who did not dye’. So he<sup>asws</sup> got so angered due to that to the extent that we recognised his<sup>asws</sup> anger in the bathhouse. He<sup>asws</sup> said, ‘And who is that who is better than me<sup>asws</sup>?’ So he said, ‘I was with Ali<sup>asws</sup> Bin Abu Talib<sup>asws</sup> and he<sup>asws</sup> did not dye’. He (the narrator) said, ‘So he<sup>asws</sup> bowed his head and perspired, so he<sup>asws</sup> said, ‘You speak the truth, and are justified’. Then he said, ‘O elderly, you should dye, for Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> had dyed, and he<sup>saww</sup> was better than Ali<sup>asws</sup>, and if you leave it, so for you is a Sunnah with Ali<sup>asws</sup>’. So when we went out from the bathhouse, we asked about the man, so it was Ali<sup>asws</sup> Bin Al-Husayn<sup>asws</sup> and with him<sup>asws</sup> was his<sup>asws</sup> son<sup>asws</sup> Muhammad<sup>asws</sup> Bin Ali<sup>asws</sup>’.

citation.chapter: The Book of Outfits and the Beautification and the Magnanimity (al-Kafi, vol 6), 8:43
citation.arabic_text: دَخَلْتُ أَنَا وَ أَبِي وَ جَدِّي وَ عَمِّي حَمَّاماً بِالْمَدِينَةِ فَإِذَا رَجُلٌ فِي بَيْتِ الْمَسْلَخِ فَقَالَ لَنَا مِمَّنِ الْقَوْمُ فَقُلْنَا مِنْ أَهْلِ الْعِرَاقِ فَقَالَ وَ أَيُّ الْعِرَاقِ قُلْنَا كُوفِيُّونَ فَقَالَ مَرْحَباً بِكُمْ يَا أَهْلَ الْكُوفَةِ أَنْتُمُ الشِّعَارُ دُونَ الدِّثَارِ ثُمَّ قَالَ مَا يَمْنَعُكُمْ مِنَ الْأُزُرِ فَإِنَّ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ ( صلى الله عليه وآله ) قَالَ عَوْرَةُ الْمُؤْمِنِ عَلَى الْمُؤْمِنِ حَرَامٌ قَالَ فَبَعَثَ إِلَى أَبِي كِرْبَاسَةً فَشَقَّهَا بِأَرْبَعَةٍ ثُمَّ أَخَذَ كُلُّ وَاحِدٍ مِنَّا وَاحِداً ثُمَّ دَخَلْنَا فِيهَا فَلَمَّا كُنَّا فِي الْبَيْتِ الْحَارِّ صَمَدَ لِجَدِّي فَقَالَ يَا كَهْلُ مَا يَمْنَعُكَ مِنَ الْخِضَابِ فَقَالَ لَهُ جَدِّي أَدْرَكْتُ مَنْ هُوَ خَيْرٌ مِنِّي وَ مِنْكَ لَا يَخْتَضِبُ قَالَ فَغَضِبَ لِذَلِكَ حَتَّى عَرَفْنَا غَضَبَهُ فِي الْحَمَّامِ قَالَ وَ مَنْ ذَلِكَ الَّذِي هُوَ خَيْرٌ مِنِّي فَقَالَ أَدْرَكْتُ عَلِيَّ بْنَ أَبِي طَالِبٍ ( عليه السلام ) وَ هُوَ لَا يَخْتَضِبُ قَالَ فَنَكَسَ رَأْسَهُ وَ تَصَابَّ عَرَقاً فَقَالَ صَدَقْتَ وَ بَرِرْتَ ثُمَّ قَالَ يَا كَهْلُ إِنْ تَخْتَضِبْ فَإِنَّ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ ( صلى الله عليه وآله ) قَدْ خَضَبَ وَ هُوَ خَيْرٌ مِنْ عَلِيٍّ ( عليه السلام ) وَ إِنْ تَتْرُكْ فَلَكَ بِعَلِيٍّ سُنَّةٌ قَالَ فَلَمَّا خَرَجْنَا مِنَ الْحَمَّامِ سَأَلْنَا عَنِ الرَّجُلِ فَإِذَا هُوَ عَلِيُّ بْنُ الْحُسَيْنِ ( عليه السلام ) وَ مَعَهُ ابْنُهُ مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ عَلِيٍّ ( عليه السلام ) .

So he said to us, ‘From whom are the people?’ So we said, ‘From the people of Al-Iraq’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said, ‘And from where in Al-Iraq?’ We said, ‘Kufians (from Kufa)’. Then he<sup>asws</sup> said, ‘What is preventing you from the loincloth, for Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘The nakedness of the Believer upon the Believer is Prohibited’. He (the narrator) said, ‘He<sup>asws</sup> sent a cloth to my father, so he tore it into four pieces, and each one of us took one from it. Then we entered into it. So when we were in the hot house, he<sup>asws</sup> turned towards my grandfather, so he<sup>asws</sup> said, ‘O elderly, what prevents you from the dyeing?’ So my grandfather said to him, ‘I was with someone who was better than me and you<sup>asws</sup>, who did not dye’. So he<sup>asws</sup> got so angered due to that to the extent that we recognised his<sup>asws</sup> anger in the bathhouse. He<sup>asws</sup> said, ‘And who is that who is better than me<sup>asws</sup>?’ So he said, ‘I was with Ali<sup>asws</sup> Bin Abu Talib<sup>asws</sup> and he<sup>asws</sup> did not dye’. He (the narrator) said, ‘So he<sup>asws</sup> bowed his head and perspired, so he<sup>asws</sup> said, ‘You speak the truth, and are justified’. Then he said, ‘O elderly, you should dye, for Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> had dyed, and he<sup>saww</sup> was better than Ali<sup>asws</sup>, and if you leave it, so for you is a Sunnah with Ali<sup>asws</sup>’. So when we went out from the bathhouse, we asked about the man, so it was Ali<sup>asws</sup> Bin Al-Husayn<sup>asws</sup> and with him<sup>asws</sup> was his<sup>asws</sup> son<sup>asws</sup> Muhammad<sup>asws</sup> Bin Ali<sup>asws</sup>’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: ضعيف على المشهور - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (22/398)

text: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Ali Bin Al Hakam, from Ali Bin Abu Hamza who said, ‘I entered the bathhouse along with Abu Baseer, so we looked at Abu Abdullahasws had waxed, and heasws had waxed hisasws underarms with Al-Noura. So I informed Abu Baseer, so he said, ‘Guide me to himasws to ask himasws about it’. So I said, ‘I have seen himasws’. So he said, ‘You have seen himasws, and I cannot see himasws’, (as he was blind). Guide me to himasws’. So I guided him to himasws, so he said to himasws, ‘May I be sacrificed for youasws! text: Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Al Hakam, (It has been narrated) from a man from the Clan of Hashimas who said, ‘I went over to a group from the Clan of Hashimas, so I greeted them in a dark room. So one of them said, ‘Greet Abu Al Hassanasws, for heasws is in the centre’. So I greeted himasws and sat in front of himasws, and I said to himasws, ‘I desired to meet youasws for a while to ask youasws about certain things’. So heasws said: ‘Ask, whatever comes to you’. I said, ‘What are youasws saying regarding the bathhouse’. Heasws said: ‘Do not enter the bathhouse except with a loincloth, and lowering your eyes, and do not wash from the used water of the bathhouse for there has washed in it the adulterer, and the son of the adulterer, and the Hostile one (Nasibi) towards usasws, the Peopleasws of the Household, and he is the most evil of them’.

citation.chapter: The Book of Outfits and the Beautification and the Magnanimity (al-Kafi, vol 6), 8:43
citation.arabic_text: دَخَلْتُ عَلَى جَمَاعَةٍ مِنْ بَنِي هَاشِمٍ فَسَلَّمْتُ عَلَيْهِمْ فِي بَيْتٍ مُظْلِمٍ فَقَالَ بَعْضُهُمْ سَلِّمْ عَلَى أَبِي الْحَسَنِ ( عليه السلام ) فَإِنَّهُ فِي الصَّدْرِ قَالَ فَسَلَّمْتُ عَلَيْهِ وَ جَلَسْتُ بَيْنَ يَدَيْهِ فَقُلْتُ لَهُ قَدْ أَحْبَبْتُ أَنْ أَلْقَاكَ مُنْذُ حِينٍ لِأَسْأَلَكَ عَنْ أَشْيَاءَ فَقَالَ سَلْ مَا بَدَا لَكَ قُلْتُ مَا تَقُولُ فِي الْحَمَّامِ قَالَ لَا تَدْخُلِ الْحَمَّامَ إِلَّا بِمِئْزَرٍ وَ غُضَّ بَصَرَكَ وَ لَا تَغْتَسِلْ مِنْ غُسَالَةِ مَاءِ الْحَمَّامِ فَإِنَّهُ يُغْتَسَلُ فِيهِ مِنَ الزِّنَا وَ يَغْتَسِلُ فِيهِ وَلَدُ الزِّنَا وَ النَّاصِبُ لَنَا أَهْلَ الْبَيْتِ وَ هُوَ شَرُّهُمْ .

text: Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Ahmad Bin Asheym, from Suleyman Al Ja’fary, (He<sup>asws</sup>) having said: ‘The one who wants to carry flesh (to gain weight) so let him enter the bathhouse one day, and be absent from it one day, and the one who intends slimming and he was of a lot of flesh, so let him enter the bathhouse every day’.

citation.chapter: The Book of Outfits and the Beautification and the Magnanimity (al-Kafi, vol 6), 8:43
citation.arabic_text: مَنْ أَرَادَ أَنْ يَحْمِلَ لَحْماً فَلْيَدْخُلِ الْحَمَّامَ يَوْماً وَ يَغِبُّ يَوْماً وَ مَنْ أَرَادَ أَنْ يَضْمُرَ وَ كَانَ كَثِيرَ اللَّحْمِ فَلْيَدْخُلِ الْحَمَّامَ كُلَّ يَوْمٍ .

text: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Abdul Rahman Bin Al Hajjaj who said, ‘I asked Abu Abdullahasws about the man who waxes with Al-Noura, so he makes a container for himself of the flour with the oil to paste with it, so he touches with it upon himself after Al-Noura in order to cut-off its smell from himself’. Heasws said: ‘There is no problem’.

citation.chapter: The Book of Outfits and the Beautification and the Magnanimity (al-Kafi, vol 6), 8:43
citation.arabic_text: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) عَنِ الرَّجُلِ يَطَّلِي بِالنُّورَةِ فَيَجْعَلُ لَهُ الدَّقِيقَ بِالزَّيْتِ يَلُتُّ بِهِ فَيَمْسَحُ بِهِ بَعْدَ النُّورَةِ لِيَقْطَعَ رِيحَهَا عَنْهُ قَالَ لَا بَأْسَ .

text: And in another Hadeeth of Abdul Rahman, he said, ‘I saw Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> and he had massaged with flour mixed with oil. So I said to him<sup>asws</sup>, ‘The people are disliking that’. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘There is no problem with it’.

citation.chapter: The Book of Outfits and the Beautification and the Magnanimity (al-Kafi, vol 6), 8:43
citation.arabic_text: وَ فِي حَدِيثٍ آخَرَ لِعَبْدِ الرَّحْمَنِ قَالَ رَأَيْتُ أَبَا الْحَسَنِ ( عليه السلام ) وَ قَدْ تَدَلَّكَ بِدَقِيقٍ مَلْتُوتٍ بِالزَّيْتِ فَقُلْتُ لَهُ إِنَّ النَّاسَ يَكْرَهُونَ ذَلِكَ قَالَ لَا بَأْسَ بِهِ .

text: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Khalid, from Usman Bin Isa, from Is’haq Bin Abdul Aziz who said, ‘Abu Abdullahasws was asked about the massaging with the flour (mixed with oil) after Al-Noura, so heasws said: ‘There is no problem’. I said, ‘They (people) are alleging that it is an extravagance’. So heasws said: ‘There is no extravagance in the correction (well-being) of the body. Sometimes I order with the pure (flour), so it is mixed for measws with the oil, so I massage with it. But rather, the extravagance is in what is destruction of the wealth and harmful for the body’.

citation.chapter: The Book of Outfits and the Beautification and the Magnanimity (al-Kafi, vol 6), 8:43
citation.arabic_text: سُئِلَ أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) عَنِ التَّدَلُّكِ بِالدَّقِيقِ بَعْدَ النُّورَةِ فَقَالَ لَا بَأْسَ قُلْتُ يَزْعُمُونَ أَنَّهُ إِسْرَافٌ فَقَالَ لَيْسَ فِيمَا أَصْلَحَ الْبَدَنَ إِسْرَافٌ إِنِّي رُبَّمَا أَمَرْتُ بِالنَّقِيِّ فَيُلَتُّ لِي بِالزَّيْتِ فَأَتَدَلَّكُ بِهِ إِنَّمَا الْإِسْرَافُ فِيمَا أَتْلَفَ الْمَالَ وَ أَضَرَّ بِالْبَدَنِ .

text: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ali Bin Al Hassan Al Taymi, from Muhammad Bin Abu Hamza, from Umar Bin Yazeed, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> was saying: ‘Indeed! citation.arabic_text: كَانَ أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ ( صلوات الله عليه ) يَقُولُ أَلَا لَا يَسْتَلْقِيَنَّ أَحَدُكُمْ فِي الْحَمَّامِ فَإِنَّهُ يُذِيبُ شَحْمَ الْكُلْيَتَيْنِ وَ لَا يَدْلُكَنَّ رِجْلَيْهِ بِالْخَزَفِ فَإِنَّهُ يُورِثُ الْجُذَامَ .
citation.translation: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ali Bin Al Hassan Al Taymi, from Muhammad Bin Abu Hamza, from Umar Bin Yazeed, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> was saying: ‘Indeed! Not one of you should lie down in the bathhouse, for it melts the fat of the kidneys, and he should not massage his leg with the clay for it inherits the leprosy’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: حسن - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (22/402)

text: Muhammad Bin Yahya, raising it, from Abdullah Bin Muskan who said, ‘We were a group of our companions, and we entered the bathhouse. So when we went out, we met Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, so he<sup>asws</sup> said to us: ‘Where are you coming back from?’ So we said to him<sup>asws</sup>, ‘From the bathhouse’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘May Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Purify your bathing’. So we said to him<sup>asws</sup>, ‘May we be sacrificed for you<sup>asws</sup>’. And we went with him<sup>asws</sup> until he<sup>asws</sup> entered the bathhouse. So we sat around (waiting) for him<sup>asws</sup> until he<sup>asws</sup> came out. So we said to him<sup>asws</sup>, ‘May Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Purify your<sup>asws</sup> bathing’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘May Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Clean you all’.

citation.chapter: The Book of Outfits and the Beautification and the Magnanimity (al-Kafi, vol 6), 8:43
citation.arabic_text: كُنَّا جَمَاعَةً مِنْ أَصْحَابِنَا دَخَلْنَا الْحَمَّامَ فَلَمَّا خَرَجْنَا لَقِيَنَا أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) فَقَالَ لَنَا مِنْ أَيْنَ أَقْبَلْتُمْ فَقُلْنَا لَهُ مِنَ الْحَمَّامِ فَقَالَ أَنْقَى اللَّهُ غَسْلَكُمْ فَقُلْنَا لَهُ جُعِلْنَا فِدَاكَ وَ إِنَّا جِئْنَا مَعَهُ حَتَّى دَخَلَ الْحَمَّامَ فَجَلَسْنَا لَهُ حَتَّى خَرَجَ فَقُلْنَا لَهُ أَنْقَى اللَّهُ غَسْلَكَ فَقَالَ طَهَّرَكُمُ اللَّهُ .

citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: موثق - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (22/402)

text: Muhammad Bin Al Hassan, and Ali Bin Muhammad Bin Bundar, from Ibrahim Bin Is’haq Al Nahawandy, from Abdul Rahman Bin Hammad, from Abu Maryam Al Ansary, raising it, said, ‘Al-Hassanasws Bin Aliasws went out from the bathhouse, a person came across himasws, so he said, ‘May yourasws Istihmamuk be good’. So heasws said: ‘O dimwit, and are you doing with utilising the ‘ist’ over here (in the word)?’ So he said, ‘May your Hameemuk be good’. So heasws said: ‘But do you not know that Al-Hameem is the perspiration?’ He said, ‘May your Hamaamuk be good’. Heasws said: ‘And when myasws bathing is good, so which thing is for measws, but say, ‘May it be purified what is good from youasws, and may it be good what is purified from youasws’.

citation.chapter: The Book of Outfits and the Beautification and the Magnanimity (al-Kafi, vol 6), 8:43
citation.arabic_text: إِنَّ الْحَسَنَ بْنَ عَلِيٍّ ( عليه السلام ) خَرَجَ مِنَ الْحَمَّامِ فَلَقِيَهُ إِنْسَانٌ فَقَالَ طَابَ اسْتِحْمَامُكَ فَقَالَ يَا لُكَعُ وَ مَا تَصْنَعُ بِالِاسْتِ هَاهُنَا فَقَالَ طَابَ حَمِيمُكَ فَقَالَ أَ مَا تَعْلَمُ أَنَّ الْحَمِيمَ الْعَرَقُ قَالَ فَطَابَ حَمَّامُكَ قَالَ وَ إِذَا طَابَ حَمَّامِي فَأَيُّ شَيْ‏ءٍ لِي وَ لَكِنْ قُلْ طَهُرَ مَا طَابَ مِنْكَ وَ طَابَ مَا طَهُرَ مِنْكَ .

text: A number of our companons, from sahl Bin Ziyad, from Muhammad Bin Isa, from Ismail Bin Yasaar, from Usman Bin Affan Al Sadousy, from Basheer Al Nabaal who said, ‘I asked Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> the bathhouse, so he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Do you want to bathing?’ So I said, ‘Yes’. He (the narrator) said, ‘So he<sup>asws</sup> ordered with the warming of the bath, then he<sup>asws</sup> entered it, and he<sup>asws</sup> was wearing a trouser, and his<sup>asws</sup> knees were covered, as well as his<sup>asws</sup> navel. Then he<sup>asws</sup> ordered the one in charge of the bathhouse, so he<sup>asws</sup> anointed what was outside from the trouser. Then he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘go away from me<sup>asws</sup>’. Then he<sup>asws</sup> anointed what was underneath it by his<sup>asws</sup> own hands, then said: ‘This is how, so do it’.

citation.chapter: The Book of Outfits and the Beautification and the Magnanimity (al-Kafi, vol 6), 8:43
citation.arabic_text: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا جَعْفَرٍ ( عليه السلام ) عَنِ الْحَمَّامِ فَقَالَ تُرِيدُ الْحَمَّامَ فَقُلْتُ نَعَمْ قَالَ فَأَمَرَ بِإِسْخَانِ الْحَمَّامِ ثُمَّ دَخَلَ فَاتَّزَرَ بِإِزَارٍ وَ غَطَّى رُكْبَتَيْهِ وَ سُرَّتَهُ ثُمَّ أَمَرَ صَاحِبَ الْحَمَّامِ فَطَلَى مَا كَانَ خَارِجاً مِنَ الْإِزَارِ ثُمَّ قَالَ اخْرُجْ عَنِّي ثُمَّ طَلَى هُوَ مَا تَحْتَهُ بِيَدِهِ ثُمَّ قَالَ هَكَذَا فَافْعَلْ .
