text: Sahl, raising it, said, ‘Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The man should not enter the bathhouse along with his son, so that he would look at his nakedness’.

citation.chapter: The Book of Outfits and the Beautification and the Magnanimity (al-Kafi, vol 6), 8:43
citation.arabic_text: قَالَ أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) لَا يَدْخُلِ الرَّجُلُ مَعَ ابْنِهِ الْحَمَّامَ فَيَنْظُرَ إِلَى عَوْرَتِهِ .
citation.translation: Sahl, raising it, said, ‘Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The man should not enter the bathhouse along with his son, so that he would look at his nakedness’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: ضعيف على المشهور - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (22/403)

text: Ali Bin Muhammad Bin Bundar, from Ibrahim Bin Is’haq, from Yusuf Bin Al Sukht, raising it, said, ‘Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Do not lean (reclining posture) in the bathhouse, for it melts the fat of the kidneys; and do not comb in the bathhouse, for it thins the hair; and do not wash your head with the clay, for it removed the self-esteem; and do not massage with the clay for it inherits the vitiligo; and do not wipe your face with the trouser for it removes the water of the face’.

citation.chapter: The Book of Outfits and the Beautification and the Magnanimity (al-Kafi, vol 6), 8:43
citation.arabic_text: قَالَ أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) لَا تَتَّكِ فِي الْحَمَّامِ فَإِنَّهُ يُذِيبُ شَحْمَ الْكُلْيَتَيْنِ وَ لَا تُسَرِّحْ فِي الْحَمَّامِ فَإِنَّهُ يُرَقِّقُ الشَّعْرَ وَ لَا تَغْسِلْ رَأْسَكَ بِالطِّينِ فَإِنَّهُ يَذْهَبُ بِالْغَيْرَةِ وَ لَا تَتَدَلَّكْ بِالْخَزَفِ فَإِنَّهُ يُورِثُ الْبَرَصَ وَ لَا تَمْسَحْ وَجْهَكَ بِالْإِزَارِ فَإِنَّهُ يَذْهَبُ بِمَاءِ الْوَجْهِ .
citation.translation: Ali Bin Muhammad Bin Bundar, from Ibrahim Bin Is’haq, from Yusuf Bin Al Sukht, raising it, said, ‘Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Do not lean (reclining posture) in the bathhouse, for it melts the fat of the kidneys; and do not comb in the bathhouse, for it thins the hair; and do not wash your head with the clay, for it removed the self-esteem; and do not massage with the clay for it inherits the vitiligo; and do not wipe your face with the trouser for it removes the water of the face’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: ضعيف على المشهور - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (2/403)

text: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ali Bin Asbaat, (It has been narrated) from Abu Al-Hassan Al-Reza<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘Do not wash your heads with Egyptian clay, for it removes the self-esteem and in inherits the despicability’.

citation.chapter: The Book of Outfits and the Beautification and the Magnanimity (al-Kafi, vol 6), 8:43
citation.arabic_text: قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ ( صلى الله عليه وآله ) لَا تَغْسِلُوا رُءُوسَكُمْ بِطِينِ مِصْرَ فَإِنَّهُ يَذْهَبُ بِالْغَيْرَةِ وَ يُورِثُ الدِّيَاثَةَ .
citation.translation: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ali Bin Asbaat, (It has been narrated) from Abu Al-Hassan Al-Reza<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘Do not wash your heads with Egyptian clay, for it removes the self-esteem and in inherits the despicability’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: ضعيف - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (2/403)

text: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Abu Yahya Al Wasity, from one of our companions, (It has been narrated) from Abu Al-Hassan Al-Maazy<sup>asws</sup> (7<sup>th</sup> Imam<sup>asws</sup>) having said: ‘The private parts are of two types, the front and the back. So as for the back, it is veiled by the two buttocks. So when the manhood and the two organs (under it) are veiled, so the private parts have been veiled’. And he<sup>asws</sup> said in another report: ‘And as for the back, so the two buttocks have veiled it, and as for the front, so veil it with your hands’.

citation.chapter: The Book of Outfits and the Beautification and the Magnanimity (al-Kafi, vol 6), 8:43
citation.arabic_text: الْعَوْرَةُ عَوْرَتَانِ الْقُبُلُ وَ الدُّبُرُ فَأَمَّا الدُّبُرُ مَسْتُورٌ بِالْأَلْيَتَيْنِ فَإِذَا سَتَرْتَ الْقَضِيبَ وَ الْبَيْضَتَيْنِ فَقَدْ سَتَرْتَ الْعَوْرَةَ وَ قَالَ فِي رِوَايَةٍ أُخْرَى وَ أَمَّا الدُّبُرُ فَقَدْ سَتَرَتْهُ الْأَلْيَتَانِ وَ أَمَّا الْقُبُلُ فَاسْتُرْهُ بِيَدِكَ .
citation.translation: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Abu Yahya Al Wasity, from one of our companions, (It has been narrated) from Abu Al-Hassan Al-Maazy<sup>asws</sup> (7<sup>th</sup> Imam<sup>asws</sup>) having said: ‘The private parts are of two types, the front and the back. So as for the back, it is veiled by the two buttocks. So when the manhood and the two organs (under it) are veiled, so the private parts have been veiled’. And he<sup>asws</sup> said in another report: ‘And as for the back, so the two buttocks have veiled it, and as for the front, so veil it with your hands’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: حسن أو موثق - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (22/404)

text: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from someone else, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘The looking at a private part of the one who is not a Muslim is like looking at the private parts of the donkey’.

citation.chapter: The Book of Outfits and the Beautification and the Magnanimity (al-Kafi, vol 6), 8:43
citation.arabic_text: النَّظَرُ إِلَى عَوْرَةِ مَنْ لَيْسَ بِمُسْلِمٍ مِثْلُ نَظَرِكَ إِلَى عَوْرَةِ الْحِمَارِ .
citation.translation: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from someone else, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘The looking at a private part of the one who is not a Muslim is like looking at the private parts of the donkey’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: مرسل - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (22/404)

text: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Al Hakam, from Aban Bin Usman, from Ibn Abu Yafour who said, ‘I asked Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, ‘Can the man be bare during the pouring of the water to see his own private parts, or the water is poured over him, or he see the private parts of the people?’ So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘My<sup>asws</sup> father<sup>asws</sup> disliked that from every one’.

citation.chapter: The Book of Outfits and the Beautification and the Magnanimity (al-Kafi, vol 6), 8:43
citation.arabic_text: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) أَ يَتَجَرَّدُ الرَّجُلُ عِنْدَ صَبِّ الْمَاءِ تُرَى عَوْرَتُهُ أَوْ يُصَبُّ عَلَيْهِ الْمَاءُ أَوْ يَرَى هُوَ عَوْرَةَ النَّاسِ فَقَالَ كَانَ أَبِي يَكْرَهُ ذَلِكَ مِنْ كُلِّ أَحَدٍ .
citation.translation: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Al Hakam, from Aban Bin Usman, from Ibn Abu Yafour who said, ‘I asked Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, ‘Can the man be bare during the pouring of the water to see his own private parts, or the water is poured over him, or he see the private parts of the people?’ So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘My<sup>asws</sup> father<sup>asws</sup> disliked that from every one’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: حسن - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (2/404)

text: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Rafa’at, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘The one who was a believer in Allah<sup>azwj</sup> and the Last Day, so he should not let his wife go to the bathhouse’.

citation.chapter: The Book of Outfits and the Beautification and the Magnanimity (al-Kafi, vol 6), 8:43
citation.arabic_text: مَنْ كَانَ يُؤْمِنُ بِاللَّهِ وَ الْيَوْمِ الْآخِرِ فَلَا يُدْخِلْ حَلِيلَتَهُ الْحَمَّامَ .
citation.translation: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Rafa’at, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘The one who was a believer in Allah<sup>azwj</sup> and the Last Day, so he should not let his wife go to the bathhouse’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: موثق كالصحيح - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (2/404)

text: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Khalid, from Usman Bin Isa, from Sama’at, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘The one who was a believer in Allah<sup>azwj</sup> and the Last Day, so he should not send his wife to the bathhouse’.

citation.chapter: The Book of Outfits and the Beautification and the Magnanimity (al-Kafi, vol 6), 8:43

text: From him, from Ismail Bin Mihran, from Muhammad Bin Abu Hamza, from Ali Bin Yaqteen who said, ‘I said to Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup>, ‘Reciting the Quran in the bathhouse and the copulation?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘There is no problem’.

citation.chapter: The Book of Outfits and the Beautification and the Magnanimity (al-Kafi, vol 6), 8:43
citation.arabic_text: قُلْتُ لِأَبِي الْحَسَنِ ( عليه السلام ) أَقْرَأُ الْقُرْآنَ فِي الْحَمَّامِ وَ أَنْكِحُ قَالَ لَا بَأْسَ .
citation.translation: From him, from Ismail Bin Mihran, from Muhammad Bin Abu Hamza, from Ali Bin Yaqteen who said, ‘I said to Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup>, ‘Reciting the Quran in the bathhouse and the copulation?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘There is no problem’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: موثق - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (2/405)

text: Ali Bin Ibrahim, form his father, from Hammad Bin Isa, from Rabi’e Bin Abdullah, from Muhammad Bin Muslim who said, ‘I asked Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup>, ‘Was Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> forbidding from reciting the Quran in the bathhouse?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘No, but rather he<sup>asws</sup> had forbidden that the man should be reciting whilst he is naked. text: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Muhammad Bin Ahmad, from Umar Bin Ali Bin Umar Bin Yazeed, from his uncle Muhammad Bin Umar, from one who narrated it that, ‘Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> was saying: ‘The one who was a believer in Allah<sup>azwj</sup> and the Last Day, so he should not enter the bathhouse except with a loin cloth’. Al Husayn Bin Muhammad, from Moala Bin Muhammad, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Abdullah, from Muhammad Bin Ja’far, from one of his men, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘The man should not enter the bathhouse along with his son, so he would look at his nakedness’. And he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘It is not for the parent that they should look at the private part of the children, and it is not the children that they should look at the nakedness of the parents’. And he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> cursed the onlooker and the one looked at in the bathhouse, without a trouser’.

text: Al Husayn Bin Muhammad, and Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ali Bin Muhammad Bin Sa’ad, from Muhammad Bin salim, from Musa Bin Abdullah Bin Musa, ‘Muhammad Bin Ali, son of Ja’farasws narrated to us from Abu Al-Hassan Al-Rezaasws having said: ‘The one who takes clay from the bathhouse and he rubs his body with it, so the vitiligo hits him, so he should not blame anyone except for himself; and the one who washed from the water which had been bathed in, and the leprosy hits him, so he should not blame anyone except for himself’. Muhammad Bin Ali (the narrator) said, ‘So I said to Abu Al-Hassanasws that the people of Al-Medina are saying that there is a healing in it from the (evil) eyes’. So heasws said: ‘They are lying! There bathe in it the ones who have sexual impurities from the Prohibition (adultery), and the adulterer, and the Hostile one (Nasibi) who is the most evil of them, and every creature from the creatures of Allahazwj, then there would be a healing in it? But rather, a healing from the (evil) eye is recitation of Al-Hamd (Chapter 1), and Al-Mawazatayn (Chapter 113 & 114), and the Verse of the Chair [2:255], and the vapour of the incense with Al-Qust (saussurea), and Al-Murr (myrhh), and Al-Loban (frankincense)’.

text: Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Al Qasim Bin Yahya, from his grandfather Al Hassan Bin Rashid, from Abu Baseer, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Washing the head with the hibiscus removes the dirt and the filth’.

citation.arabic_text: قَالَ أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ ( عليه السلام ) غَسْلُ الرَّأْسِ بِالْخِطْمِيِّ يَذْهَبُ بِالدَّرَنِ وَ يَنْفِي الْأَقْذَاءَ .
citation.translation: Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Al Qasim Bin Yahya, from his grandfather Al Hassan Bin Rashid, from Abu Baseer, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Washing the head with the hibiscus removes the dirt and the filth’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: ضعيف - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (22/407)

text: Muhammad Bin Yahya, form Muhammad Bin Al Husayn Bin Musa Bin Sa’adan, from Abdullah Bin Sinan, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘The one who takes from his moustache, and clips his nails, and washes his head with the hibiscus on the day of Friday would be like the one who emancipated a person’.

citation.chapter: The Book of Outfits and the Beautification and the Magnanimity (al-Kafi, vol 6), 8:44
citation.arabic_text: مَنْ أَخَذَ مِنْ شَارِبِهِ وَ قَلَّمَ أَظْفَارَهُ وَ غَسَلَ رَأْسَهُ بِالْخِطْمِيِّ يَوْمَ الْجُمُعَةِ كَانَ كَمَنْ أَعْتَقَ نَسَمَةً .
citation.translation: Muhammad Bin Yahya, form Muhammad Bin Al Husayn Bin Musa Bin Sa’adan, from Abdullah Bin Sinan, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘The one who takes from his moustache, and clips his nails, and washes his head with the hibiscus on the day of Friday would be like the one who emancipated a person’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: ضعيف - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (22/407)

text: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Abu Abdullah, from Muhammad Bin Ali, from Al Hassan Bin Muhammad Al Sayrafi, from Ismail Bin Abdul Khaliq, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Washing the head with the hibiscus is an advertisement (of beauty)’.

citation.chapter: The Book of Outfits and the Beautification and the Magnanimity (al-Kafi, vol 6), 8:44
citation.arabic_text: غَسْلُ الرَّأْسِ بِالْخِطْمِيِّ نُشْرَةٌ .
citation.translation: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Abu Abdullah, from Muhammad Bin Ali, from Al Hassan Bin Muhammad Al Sayrafi, from Ismail Bin Abdul Khaliq, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Washing the head with the hibiscus is an advertisement (of beauty)’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: ضعيف - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (2/407)

text: From him, form Muhammad Bin Ismail, from Mansour Bin Buzraj who said, ‘I heard Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> saying: ‘Washing the head with the lotus bring the livelihood with a (strong) bringing’.

citation.chapter: The Book of Outfits and the Beautification and the Magnanimity (al-Kafi, vol 6), 8:44
citation.arabic_text: سَمِعْتُ أَبَا الْحَسَنِ ( عليه السلام ) يَقُولُ غَسْلُ الرَّأْسِ بِالسِّدْرِ يَجْلِبُ الرِّزْقَ جَلْباً .
citation.translation: From him, form Muhammad Bin Ismail, from Mansour Bin Buzraj who said, ‘I heard Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> saying: ‘Washing the head with the lotus bring the livelihood with a (strong) bringing’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: موثق - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (22/408)

text: From him, form Muhammad Bin Ali, from Ubeyd Bin yahya Al Sowr Al Attar, from Muhammad Bin Al Husayn Al Alawy, from his father, from his grandfather, (It has been narrated) from Aliasws having said: ‘When Allahazwj Mighty and Majestic Commanded Hisazwj Rasoolsaww with the manifestation of Al-Islam and the Revelation appeared, hesaww saw the scarcity of the Muslims and abundance of the Polytheists. So Rasool-Allahsaww was aggrieved by an intense grief. So Allahazwj Sent Jibraeelas to himsaww with a lotus from the Lotus Tree (Al-Sidrat Al-Muntaha). So hesaww washed hissaww head with it, and hissaww grief was removed by it’.

citation.chapter: The Book of Outfits and the Beautification and the Magnanimity (al-Kafi, vol 6), 8:44
citation.arabic_text: لَمَّا أَمَرَ اللَّهُ عَزَّ وَ جَلَّ رَسُولَهُ ( صلى الله عليه وآله ) بِإِظْهَارِ الْإِسْلَامِ وَ ظَهَرَ الْوَحْيُ رَأَى قِلَّةً مِنَ الْمُسْلِمِينَ وَ كَثْرَةً مِنَ الْمُشْرِكِينَ فَاهْتَمَّ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ ( صلى الله عليه وآله ) هَمّاً شَدِيداً فَبَعَثَ اللَّهُ عَزَّ وَ جَلَّ إِلَيْهِ جَبْرَئِيلَ ( عليه السلام ) بِسِدْرٍ مِنْ سِدْرَةِ الْمُنْتَهَى فَغَسَلَ بِهِ رَأْسَهُ فَجَلَا بِهِ هَمَّهُ .
citation.translation: From him, form Muhammad Bin Ali, from Ubeyd Bin yahya Al Sowr Al Attar, from Muhammad Bin Al Husayn Al Alawy, from his father, from his grandfather, (It has been narrated) from Aliasws having said: ‘When Allahazwj Mighty and Majestic Commanded Hisazwj Rasoolsaww with the manifestation of Al-Islam and the Revelation appeared, hesaww saw the scarcity of the Muslims and abundance of the Polytheists. So Rasool-Allahsaww was aggrieved by an intense grief. So Allahazwj Sent Jibraeelas to himsaww with a lotus from the Lotus Tree (Al-Sidrat Al-Muntaha). So hesaww washed hissaww head with it, and hissaww grief was removed by it’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: ضعيف - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (2/408)

text: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, form Suleym Al Fara’a who said, ‘Amir Al-Momineenasws said: ‘Al-Noura is a cleanser’.

citation.chapter: The Book of Outfits and the Beautification and the Magnanimity (al-Kafi, vol 6), 8:45
citation.arabic_text: قَالَ أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ ( عليه السلام ) النُّورَةُ طَهُورٌ .
citation.translation: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, form Suleym Al Fara’a who said, ‘Amir Al-Momineenasws said: ‘Al-Noura is a cleanser’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: حسن - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (22/408)

text: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, form Al Hajjal, from Hammad Bin Usman, (It has been narrated) from Abdul Rahman Bin Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘I entered the bathhouse along with Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, so he<sup>asws</sup> said to me: ‘O Abdul Rahman! Get waxing done’. So I said, ‘But rather I waxed a few days ago’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Get waxing done for it is a cleansing’.

citation.chapter: The Book of Outfits and the Beautification and the Magnanimity (al-Kafi, vol 6), 8:45
citation.arabic_text: دَخَلْتُ مَعَ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) الْحَمَّامَ فَقَالَ لِي يَا عَبْدَ الرَّحْمَنِ اطَّلِ فَقُلْتُ إِنَّمَا اطَّلَيْتُ مُنْذُ أَيَّامٍ فَقَالَ اطَّلِ فَإِنَّهَا طَهُورٌ .
citation.translation: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, form Al Hajjal, from Hammad Bin Usman, (It has been narrated) from Abdul Rahman Bin Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘I entered the bathhouse along with Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, so he<sup>asws</sup> said to me: ‘O Abdul Rahman! Get waxing done’. So I said, ‘But rather I waxed a few days ago’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Get waxing done for it is a cleansing’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: صحيح - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (22/408)

text: Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ali Bin Uqba, from Abu Kahmas, from Muhammad Bin Abdullah Bin Ali Bin Al Husayn who said, ‘Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> entered the bathhouse and I wanted to exit from it. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘O Muhammad! Did you not get waxing done?’ So I said, ‘I did apply with it a few days ago’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘But do you not know that it is a cleansing?’

citation.chapter: The Book of Outfits and the Beautification and the Magnanimity (al-Kafi, vol 6), 8:45
citation.arabic_text: دَخَلَ أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) الْحَمَّامَ وَ أَنَا أُرِيدُ أَنْ أَخْرُجَ مِنْهُ فَقَالَ يَا مُحَمَّدُ أَ لَا تَطَّلِي فَقُلْتُ عَهْدِي بِهِ مُنْذُ أَيَّامٍ فَقَالَ أَ مَا عَلِمْتَ أَنَّهَا طَهُورٌ .
citation.translation: Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ali Bin Uqba, from Abu Kahmas, from Muhammad Bin Abdullah Bin Ali Bin Al Husayn who said, ‘Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> entered the bathhouse and I wanted to exit from it. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘O Muhammad! Did you not get waxing done?’ So I said, ‘I did apply with it a few days ago’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘But do you not know that it is a cleansing?’
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: مجهول - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (2/409)

text: A number of our companions, form Ahmad Bin Abu Abdullah, from his father, from Khalaf Bin Hammad, from the one who reported it who said, ‘Abu Abdullahasws send a son of hisasws brother regarding a need, so he came and Abu Abdullahasws waxed with Al-Noura. So Abu Abdullahasws said: ‘Get waxing done’. So he said, ‘But rather, I had waxing done three (days) ago’. So Abu Abdullahasws said: ‘Al-Noura is a cleanser’.

citation.chapter: The Book of Outfits and the Beautification and the Magnanimity (al-Kafi, vol 6), 8:45
citation.arabic_text: بَعَثَ أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) ابْنَ أَخِيهِ فِي حَاجَةٍ فَجَاءَ وَ أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) قَدِ اطَّلَى بِالنُّورَةِ فَقَالَ لَهُ أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) اطَّلِ فَقَالَ إِنَّمَا عَهْدِي بِالنُّورَةِ مُنْذُ ثَلَاثٍ فَقَالَ أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) إِنَّ النُّورَةَ طَهُورٌ .
citation.translation: A number of our companions, form Ahmad Bin Abu Abdullah, from his father, from Khalaf Bin Hammad, from the one who reported it who said, ‘Abu Abdullahasws send a son of hisasws brother regarding a need, so he came and Abu Abdullahasws waxed with Al-Noura. So Abu Abdullahasws said: ‘Get waxing done’. So he said, ‘But rather, I had waxing done three (days) ago’. So Abu Abdullahasws said: ‘Al-Noura is a cleanser’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: مرسل - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (22/409)

text: From him, from Abdullah Bin Muhammad Al Naheyki, from Ibrahim Bin Abdul Hameed who said, ‘I heard Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> saying: ‘Cast off the hair from yourselves for it beautifies’.

citation.chapter: The Book of Outfits and the Beautification and the Magnanimity (al-Kafi, vol 6), 8:45
citation.arabic_text: سَمِعْتُ أَبَا الْحَسَنِ ( عليه السلام ) يَقُولُ أَلْقُوا عَنْكُمُ الشَّعْرَ فَإِنَّهُ يُحَسِّنُ .
citation.translation: From him, from Abdullah Bin Muhammad Al Naheyki, from Ibrahim Bin Abdul Hameed who said, ‘I heard Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> saying: ‘Cast off the hair from yourselves for it beautifies’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: موثق - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (2/409)

text: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from one of his companions, from Ali Bin Abu Hamza, from Abu Baseer who said, ‘I (Abu Hamza) was with him (Abu Baseer) guiding him (as he was blind), so I entered the bathhouse, and I saw Abu Abdullahasws applying Noura. So Abu Baseer went near him and greeted himasws, so heasws said: ‘O Abu Baseer! Apply Noura’. So he said, ‘But rather, I had applied Noura first thing yesterday, and the third day’. So heasws said: ‘But do you not know that is it a cleanser? Therefore you should apply Noura’.

citation.chapter: The Book of Outfits and the Beautification and the Magnanimity (al-Kafi, vol 6), 8:45
citation.arabic_text: كُنْتُ مَعَهُ أَقُودُهُ فَأَدْخَلْتُهُ الْحَمَّامَ فَرَأَيْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) يَتَنَوَّرُ فَدَنَا مِنْهُ أَبُو بَصِيرٍ فَسَلَّمَ عَلَيْهِ فَقَالَ يَا أَبَا بَصِيرٍ تَنَوَّرْ فَقَالَ إِنَّمَا تَنَوَّرْتُ أَوَّلَ مِنْ أَمْسِ وَ الْيَوْمَ الثَّالِثَ فَقَالَ أَ مَا عَلِمْتَ أَنَّهَا طَهُورٌ فَتَنَوَّرْ .
citation.translation: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from one of his companions, from Ali Bin Abu Hamza, from Abu Baseer who said, ‘I (Abu Hamza) was with him (Abu Baseer) guiding him (as he was blind), so I entered the bathhouse, and I saw Abu Abdullahasws applying Noura. So Abu Baseer went near him and greeted himasws, so heasws said: ‘O Abu Baseer! Apply Noura’. So he said, ‘But rather, I had applied Noura first thing yesterday, and the third day’. So heasws said: ‘But do you not know that is it a cleanser? Therefore you should apply Noura’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: ضعيف على المشهور - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (2/409)

text: Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Al Qasim Bin Yahya, from his grandfather Al Hassan Bin Rashid, from Abu Baseer, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws having said: ‘Amir Al-Momineenasws said: ‘Al-Noura is an advertisement (of beauty) and a cleanser for the body’.

citation.chapter: The Book of Outfits and the Beautification and the Magnanimity (al-Kafi, vol 6), 8:45
citation.arabic_text: قَالَ أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ ( عليه السلام ) النُّورَةُ نُشْرَةٌ وَ طَهُورٌ لِلْجَسَدِ .
citation.translation: Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Al Qasim Bin Yahya, from his grandfather Al Hassan Bin Rashid, from Abu Baseer, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws having said: ‘Amir Al-Momineenasws said: ‘Al-Noura is an advertisement (of beauty) and a cleanser for the body’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: ضعيف - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (2/409)

text: Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Al Qasim Bin Yahya, from his grandfather Al Hassan Bin Rashid, from Muhammad Bin Muslim, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘I<sup>asws</sup> would love it for the Believer if he were to wax (to remove unwanted hair) during every fifteen days’.

citation.chapter: The Book of Outfits and the Beautification and the Magnanimity (al-Kafi, vol 6), 8:45
citation.arabic_text: قَالَ أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ ( عليه السلام ) أُحِبُّ لِلْمُؤْمِنِ أَنْ يَطَّلِيَ فِي كُلِّ خَمْسَةَ عَشَرَ يَوْماً .
citation.translation: Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Al Qasim Bin Yahya, from his grandfather Al Hassan Bin Rashid, from Muhammad Bin Muslim, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘I<sup>asws</sup> would love it for the Believer if he were to wax (to remove unwanted hair) during every fifteen days’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: ضعيف - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (2/409)

text: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad and Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, altogether from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Abu Nasr, from Ahmad Bin Al Mubarak, from Al Husayn Bin Ahmad Bin Al Minqary, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws having said: ‘The Sunnah regarding Al-Noura is every fifteen days, so if twenty days were to come to you and it is not in your possession, so borrow upon Allahazwj’.

citation.chapter: The Book of Outfits and the Beautification and the Magnanimity (al-Kafi, vol 6), 8:45
citation.arabic_text: السُّنَّةُ فِي النُّورَةِ فِي كُلِّ خَمْسَةَ عَشَرَ يَوْماً فَإِنْ أَتَتْ عَلَيْكَ عِشْرُونَ يَوْماً وَ لَيْسَ عِنْدَكَ فَاسْتَقْرِضْ عَلَى اللَّهِ .
citation.translation: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad and Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, altogether from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Abu Nasr, from Ahmad Bin Al Mubarak, from Al Husayn Bin Ahmad Bin Al Minqary, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws having said: ‘The Sunnah regarding Al-Noura is every fifteen days, so if twenty days were to come to you and it is not in your possession, so borrow upon Allahazwj’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: ضعيف على المشهور - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (22/410)

text: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from Ahmad Bin Abu Abdullah, (It has been narrated) raising it to Abu Abdullahasws, said, ‘It was said to himasws, ‘Some of the people are alleging that Al-Noura is disliked on the day of Friday’. So heasws said: ‘It is not where you are going. Which cleanser is more purifying than Al-Noura on the day of Friday?’

citation.chapter: The Book of Outfits and the Beautification and the Magnanimity (al-Kafi, vol 6), 8:45
citation.arabic_text: قِيلَ لَهُ يَزْعُمُ بَعْضُ النَّاسِ أَنَّ النُّورَةَ يَوْمَ الْجُمُعَةِ مَكْرُوهَةٌ فَقَالَ لَيْسَ حَيْثُ ذَهَبْتَ أَيُّ طَهُورٍ أَطْهَرُ مِنَ النُّورَةِ يَوْمَ الْجُمُعَةِ .
citation.translation: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from Ahmad Bin Abu Abdullah, (It has been narrated) raising it to Abu Abdullahasws, said, ‘It was said to himasws, ‘Some of the people are alleging that Al-Noura is disliked on the day of Friday’. So heasws said: ‘It is not where you are going. Which cleanser is more purifying than Al-Noura on the day of Friday?’
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: مرفوع - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (2/410)

text: Ali Bin Ibrhim, form his father, from Al Nowfaly, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘The one who was a believer in Allah<sup>azwj</sup> and the Last Day, so he should not leave his pubic hair for more than forty days, nor is it Permissible for a woman who believes in Allah<sup>azwj</sup> and the Last Day that she should leave that from her for more than twenty days’.

citation.chapter: The Book of Outfits and the Beautification and the Magnanimity (al-Kafi, vol 6), 8:45
citation.arabic_text: قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ ( صلى الله عليه وآله ) مَنْ كَانَ يُؤْمِنُ بِاللَّهِ وَ الْيَوْمِ الْآخِرِ فَلَا يَتْرُكْ عَانَتَهُ فَوْقَ أَرْبَعِينَ يَوْماً وَ لَا يَحِلُّ لِامْرَأَةٍ تُؤْمِنُ بِاللَّهِ وَ الْيَوْمِ الْآخِرِ أَنْ تَدَعَ ذَلِكَ مِنْهَا فَوْقَ عِشْرِينَ يَوْماً .
citation.translation: Ali Bin Ibrhim, form his father, from Al Nowfaly, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘The one who was a believer in Allah<sup>azwj</sup> and the Last Day, so he should not leave his pubic hair for more than forty days, nor is it Permissible for a woman who believes in Allah<sup>azwj</sup> and the Last Day that she should leave that from her for more than twenty days’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: ضعيف على المشهور - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (2/410)

text: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Al Hasan Bin Ali Al Washa, from Ahmad Bin Sa’aba, from Ammar Al Sabaty who said, ‘Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Waxing in the summer is better than ten in the winter’.

citation.chapter: The Book of Outfits and the Beautification and the Magnanimity (al-Kafi, vol 6), 8:45
citation.arabic_text: قَالَ أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) طَلْيَةٌ فِي الصَّيْفِ خَيْرٌ مِنْ عَشْرٍ فِي الشِّتَاءِ .
citation.translation: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Al Hasan Bin Ali Al Washa, from Ahmad Bin Sa’aba, from Ammar Al Sabaty who said, ‘Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Waxing in the summer is better than ten in the winter’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: مجهول - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (22/410)

text: Ali Bin Muhammad Bin Bundar, form Al Sayyari, raising it, said, ‘Abu Abdullahasws said: ‘The one who wants the waxing with Al-Nouran, so he should take from Al-Noura with his fingers, and paste it upon the sides of his nose and say, ‘May Allahazwj Send Blessings upon Suleymanas Bin Dawoodas just as heas ordered us with Al-Noura’, would not be burnt by Al-Noura’.

citation.arabic_text: قَالَ أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) مَنْ أَرَادَ الِاطِّلَاءَ بِالنُّورَةِ فَأَخَذَ مِنَ النُّورَةِ بِإِصْبَعِهِ فَشَمَّهُ وَ جَعَلَ عَلَى طَرَفِ أَنْفِهِ وَ قَالَ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَى سُلَيْمَانَ بْنِ دَاوُدَ كَمَا أَمَرَنَا بِالنُّورَةِ لَمْ تُحْرِقْهُ النُّورَةُ .

text: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Khalid, from his father, from Zureyq Bin Al Zubeyr, (It has been narrated) from Sadeyr who heard Aliasws Bin Al-Husaynasws saying: ‘The one who says, whenever he waxes with Al-Noura, ‘O Allahazwj! Make good what is clean from me, and Purify what is good from me, and replace for me with clean hair which would not disobey Youazwj. O Allahazwj! I have cleaned seeking a Sunnah of the Mursil Prophetsas, and seeking Youazwj Pleasure, and Yourazwj Forgiveness, therefore Prohibit my hair and my person upon the Fire, and Purify my creation (body) and Make good my manners, and Purify my deeds, and Make me to be from the ones who would be meeting Youazwj upon the upright, the tolerant Religion of Ibrahimas, Yourazwj Friend, and the Religion of Muhammadsaww, Yourazwj Beloved, and Yourazwj Rasoolsaww, having abided by Yourazwj Laws, a follower of the Sunnah of Yourazwj Prophetsaww, having taken by it an education with the best of Yourazwj Education, and education of Yourazwj Rasoolsaww, and the education of Yourazwj Guardiansasws whom Youazwj Sustained with Yourazwj Education, and Cultivated the Wisdom in theirasws chests, and Made them the educators of Yourazwj Knowledge, may Blessing be upon themasws’. The one who says that, Allahazwj would Purify him from the filth in the world, and from the sins, and Replace for him with hair which would not disobey Allahazwj, and Allahazwj would Created for every hair from his body, an Angel who would Glorify for him up to the Establishment of the Hour, and that a Glorification from its Glorifications equates with one thousand Glorifications from the Glorifications of the people of the earth’.

citation.chapter: The Book of Outfits and the Beautification and the Magnanimity (al-Kafi, vol 6), 8:45
citation.arabic_text: مَنْ قَالَ إِذَا اطَّلَى بِالنُّورَةِ اللَّهُمَّ طَيِّبْ مَا طَهُرَ مِنِّي وَ طَهِّرْ مَا طَابَ مِنِّي وَ أَبْدِلْنِي شَعْراً طَاهِراً لَا يَعْصِيكَ اللَّهُمَّ إِنِّي تَطَهَّرْتُ ابْتِغَاءَ سُنَّةِ الْمُرْسَلِينَ وَ ابْتِغَاءَ رِضْوَانِكَ وَ مَغْفِرَتِكَ فَحَرِّمْ شَعْرِي وَ بَشَرِي عَلَى النَّارِ وَ طَهِّرْ خَلْقِي وَ طَيِّبْ خُلُقِي وَ زَكِّ عَمَلِي وَ اجْعَلْنِي مِمَّنْ يَلْقَاكَ عَلَى الْحَنِيفِيَّةِ السَّمْحَةِ مِلَّةِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ خَلِيلِكَ وَ دِينِ مُحَمَّدٍ ( صلى الله عليه وآله ) حَبِيبِكَ وَ رَسُولِكَ عَامِلًا بِشَرَائِعِكَ تَابِعاً لِسُنَّةِ نَبِيِّكَ ( صلى الله عليه وآله ) آخِذاً بِهِ مُتَأَدِّباً بِحُسْنِ تَأْدِيبِكَ وَ تَأْدِيبِ رَسُولِكَ وَ تَأْدِيبِ أَوْلِيَائِكَ الَّذِينَ غَذَوْتَهُمْ بِأَدَبِكَ وَ زَرَعْتَ الْحِكْمَةَ فِي صُدُورِهِمْ وَ جَعَلْتَهُمْ مَعَادِنَ لِعِلْمِكَ صَلَوَاتُكَ عَلَيْهِمْ مَنْ قَالَ ذَلِكَ طَهَّرَهُ اللَّهُ مِنَ الْأَدْنَاسِ فِي الدُّنْيَا وَ مِنَ الذُّنُوبِ وَ أَبْدَلَهُ شَعْراً لَا يَعْصِي اللَّهَ وَ خَلَقَ اللَّهُ بِكُلِّ شَعْرَةٍ مِنْ جَسَدِهِ مَلَكاً يُسَبِّحُ لَهُ إِلَى أَنْ تَقُومَ السَّاعَةُ وَ إِنَّ تَسْبِيحَةً مِنْ تَسْبِيحِهِمْ تَعْدِلُ بِأَلْفِ تَسْبِيحَةٍ مِنْ تَسْبِيحِ أَهْلِ الْأَرْضِ .

text: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Abu Abdullah, from Muhammad Bin Ali, from Sa’dan who said, ‘I was with Abu Baseer in the bathhouse, so I saw Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> waxing his<sup>asws</sup> armpits, so I informed Abu Baseer of that, so he said to him<sup>asws</sup>, ‘May I be sacrificed for you<sup>asws</sup>! Which is preferable, plucking the armpit or shaving it?’ So he<sup>asws</sup>said: ‘O Abu Muhammad! Plucking the armpit frails or weakens (the shoulders). Shave it’.

citation.chapter: The Book of Outfits and the Beautification and the Magnanimity (al-Kafi, vol 6), 8:46
citation.arabic_text: كُنْتُ مَعَ أَبِي بَصِيرٍ فِي الْحَمَّامِ فَرَأَيْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) يَطْلِي إِبْطَهُ فَأَخْبَرْتُ بِذَلِكَ أَبَا بَصِيرٍ فَقَالَ لَهُ جُعِلْتُ فِدَاكَ أَيُّمَا أَفْضَلُ نَتْفُ الْإِبْطِ أَوْ حَلْقُهُ فَقَالَ يَا أَبَا مُحَمَّدٍ إِنَّ نَتْفَ الْإِبْطِ يُوهِي أَوْ يُضْعِفُ احْلِقْهُ .
citation.translation: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Abu Abdullah, from Muhammad Bin Ali, from Sa’dan who said, ‘I was with Abu Baseer in the bathhouse, so I saw Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> waxing his<sup>asws</sup> armpits, so I informed Abu Baseer of that, so he said to him<sup>asws</sup>, ‘May I be sacrificed for you<sup>asws</sup>! Which is preferable, plucking the armpit or shaving it?’ So he<sup>asws</sup>said: ‘O Abu Muhammad! Plucking the armpit frails or weakens (the shoulders). Shave it’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: ضعيف - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (2/412)

text: One of our companions, from Ibn Jamhour, from Muhammad Bin Al Qasim, and Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Muhammad Bin Ahmad, from yusuf Bin Al Sukht Al Basry, from Muhammad Bin Suleyman, from Ibrahim Bin Yahya Bin Abu Al Balaad, from Al Hassan Bin Ali Bin Mihran, altogether from Abdullah Bin Abu Yafour who said, ‘We were at Al-Medina, so Zurara disputed with me regarding plucking the armpit and shaving it. So I said, ‘Shaving it is preferable’, and Zurara said, ‘Plucking it is preferable’. So we both sought permission to (see) Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, so he<sup>asws</sup> permitted for us and he<sup>asws</sup> was in the bathhouse waxing, having waxed his<sup>asws</sup> armpits. So I said to Zurara, ‘Do it suffice for you?’ He said, ‘No, perhaps he<sup>asws</sup> has done this and it is not allowed for me that I do it’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘In what (discussion) are you?’ So I said, ‘Zurara disputed with me regarding plucking of the armpit and the shaving of it’. So I said that shaving is preferable, and he said plucking is preferable’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘You have hit the Sunnah and Zurara has erred. Shaving it is preferable than plucking it, and waxing it is preferable than shaving it’. Then he<sup>asws</sup> said to us both: ‘Get waxing done’. So we both said, ‘We did that three (days) ago’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Repeat it, for waxing is a cleanser’.

citation.chapter: The Book of Outfits and the Beautification and the Magnanimity (al-Kafi, vol 6), 8:46
citation.arabic_text: كُنَّا بِالْمَدِينَةِ فَلَاحَانِي زُرَارَةُ فِي نَتْفِ الْإِبْطِ وَ حَلْقِهِ فَقُلْتُ حَلْقُهُ أَفْضَلُ وَ قَالَ زُرَارَةُ نَتْفُهُ أَفْضَلُ فَاسْتَأْذَنَّا عَلَى أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) فَأَذِنَ لَنَا وَ هُوَ فِي الْحَمَّامِ يَطَّلِي قَدِ اطَّلَى إِبْطَيْهِ فَقُلْتُ لِزُرَارَةَ يَكْفِيكَ قَالَ لَا لَعَلَّهُ فَعَلَ هَذَا لِمَا لَا يَجُوزُ لِي أَنْ أَفْعَلَهُ فَقَالَ فِيمَ أَنْتُمْ فَقُلْتُ لَاحَانِي زُرَارَةُ فِي نَتْفِ الْإِبْطِ وَ حَلْقِهِ فَقُلْتُ حَلْقُهُ أَفْضَلُ وَ قَالَ نَتْفُهُ أَفْضَلُ فَقَالَ أَصَبْتَ السُّنَّةَ وَ أَخْطَأَهَا زُرَارَةُ حَلْقُهُ أَفْضَلُ مِنْ نَتْفِهِ وَ طَلْيُهُ أَفْضَلُ مِنْ حَلْقِهِ ثُمَّ قَالَ لَنَا اطَّلِيَا فَقُلْنَا فَعَلْنَا ذَلِكَ مُنْذُ ثَلَاثٍ فَقَالَ أَعِيدَا فَإِنَّ الِاطِّلَاءَ طَهُورٌ.

text: Ali Bin Muhammad Bin Bundar and Muhammad Bin Al Hassan, altogether from Ibrahim Bin Is’haq Al Ahmar, (It has been narrated) from Al-Husayn son of Musaasws who said, ‘My fatherasws Musaasws Bin Ja’farasws, whenever heasws wanted to enter the bathhouse, ordered that it should be ignited for him with three (people) being over it, and heasws would not enter it until the slaves enter it and they would be laying down the matting for him. So when heasws entered it, (into the bath) heasws would be seated for a while, and standing for a while. So one day heasws came out from the bathhouse, and a man from the progeny of Al-Zubeyr called Kuneyd met himasws, and in hisasws hands were the traces of henna. So he said, ‘What are these traces in yourasws hands?’ So heasws said: ‘Traces of henna. Woe be unto you O Kuneyd! Myasws fatherasws narrated to me, and heasws was the most knowledgeable of the people of hisasws time, from hisasws fatherasws, from hisasws grandfatherasws having said: ‘Rasool-Allahsaww said: ‘The one who enters the bathhouse, so he waxes, then follows it up with the henna from his head to his feet, it would be a safety for him from the insanity, and the leprosy, and the vitiligo, and the corrosion to such like, from the Noura’.

citation.chapter: The Book of Outfits and the Beautification and the Magnanimity (al-Kafi, vol 6), 8:47
citation.arabic_text: كَانَ أَبِي مُوسَى بْنُ جَعْفَرٍ ( عليه السلام ) إِذَا أَرَادَ دُخُولَ الْحَمَّامِ أَمَرَ أَنْ يُوقَدَ لَهُ عَلَيْهِ ثَلَاثاً وَ كَانَ لَا يُمْكِنُهُ دُخُولُهُ حَتَّى يَدْخُلَهُ السُّودَانُ فَيُلْقُونَ لَهُ اللُّبُودَ فَإِذَا دَخَلَهُ فَمَرَّةً قَاعِدٌ وَ مَرَّةً قَائِمٌ فَخَرَجَ يَوْماً مِنَ الْحَمَّامِ فَاسْتَقْبَلَهُ رَجُلٌ مِنْ آلِ الزُّبَيْرِ يُقَالُ لَهُ كُنَيْدٌ وَ بِيَدِهِ أَثَرُ حِنَّاءٍ فَقَالَ مَا هَذَا الْأَثَرُ بِيَدِكَ فَقَالَ أَثَرُ حِنَّاءٍ فَقَالَ وَيْلَكَ يَا كُنَيْدُ حَدَّثَنِي أَبِي وَ كَانَ أَعْلَمَ أَهْلِ زَمَانِهِ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ جَدِّهِ قَالَ قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ ( صلى الله عليه وآله ) مَنْ دَخَلَ الْحَمَّامَ فَاطَّلَى ثُمَّ أَتْبَعَهُ بِالْحِنَّاءِ مِنْ قَرْنِهِ إِلَى قَدَمِهِ كَانَ أَمَاناً لَهُ مِنَ الْجُنُونِ وَ الْجُذَامِ وَ الْبَرَصِ وَ الْآكِلَةِ إِلَى مِثْلِهِ مِنَ النُّورَةِ.
citation.translation: Ali Bin Muhammad Bin Bundar and Muhammad Bin Al Hassan, altogether from Ibrahim Bin Is’haq Al Ahmar, (It has been narrated) from Al-Husayn son of Musaasws who said, ‘My fatherasws Musaasws Bin Ja’farasws, whenever heasws wanted to enter the bathhouse, ordered that it should be ignited for him with three (people) being over it, and heasws would not enter it until the slaves enter it and they would be laying down the matting for him. So when heasws entered it, (into the bath) heasws would be seated for a while, and standing for a while. So one day heasws came out from the bathhouse, and a man from the progeny of Al-Zubeyr called Kuneyd met himasws, and in hisasws hands were the traces of henna. So he said, ‘What are these traces in yourasws hands?’ So heasws said: ‘Traces of henna. Woe be unto you O Kuneyd! Myasws fatherasws narrated to me, and heasws was the most knowledgeable of the people of hisasws time, from hisasws fatherasws, from hisasws grandfatherasws having said: ‘Rasool-Allahsaww said: ‘The one who enters the bathhouse, so he waxes, then follows it up with the henna from his head to his feet, it would be a safety for him from the insanity, and the leprosy, and the vitiligo, and the corrosion to such like, from the Noura’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: ضعيف - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (22/413)

text: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Ali Bin Al Hakam, from Muawiya Bin Maysara, from Al Hakam Bin Uteyba who said, ‘I saw Abu Ja’farasws and heasws had taken the henna and made it to be upon hisasws nails, so heasws said: ‘O Hakam! What are you saying regarding this?’ So I said, ‘What can I say and youasws have done it, and among us it is the youth who do it’. So heasws said: ‘O Hakam! When the nails are hit by the Noura, it changes them until they resemble the nails of the dead, therefore change it back by the henna’.

citation.chapter: The Book of Outfits and the Beautification and the Magnanimity (al-Kafi, vol 6), 8:47
citation.arabic_text: رَأَيْتُ أَبَا جَعْفَرٍ ( عليه السلام ) وَ قَدْ أَخَذَ الْحِنَّاءَ وَ جَعَلَهُ عَلَى أَظَافِيرِهِ فَقَالَ يَا حَكَمُ مَا تَقُولُ فِي هَذَا فَقُلْتُ مَا عَسَيْتُ أَنْ أَقُولَ فِيهِ وَ أَنْتَ تَفْعَلُهُ وَ إِنَّ عِنْدَنَا يَفْعَلُهُ الشُّبَّانُ فَقَالَ يَا حَكَمُ إِنَّ الْأَظَافِيرَ إِذَا أَصَابَتْهَا النُّورَةُ غَيَّرَتْهَا حَتَّى تُشْبِهَ أَظَافِيرَ الْمَوْتَى فَغَيِّرْهَا بِالْحِنَّاءِ .
citation.translation: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Ali Bin Al Hakam, from Muawiya Bin Maysara, from Al Hakam Bin Uteyba who said, ‘I saw Abu Ja’farasws and heasws had taken the henna and made it to be upon hisasws nails, so heasws said: ‘O Hakam! What are you saying regarding this?’ So I said, ‘What can I say and youasws have done it, and among us it is the youth who do it’. So heasws said: ‘O Hakam! When the nails are hit by the Noura, it changes them until they resemble the nails of the dead, therefore change it back by the henna’.

text: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Abu Abdullah, from one of our companions, raising it, ‘He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The one who waxes and massages with the henna from his head to his feet, the poverty is negated from him’.

citation.chapter: The Book of Outfits and the Beautification and the Magnanimity (al-Kafi, vol 6), 8:47
citation.arabic_text: مَنِ اطَّلَى فَتَدَلَّكَ بِالْحِنَّاءِ مِنْ قَرْنِهِ إِلَى قَدَمِهِ نُفِيَ عَنْهُ الْفَقْرُ .

text: Ali Bin Muhammad, form Salih Bin Abu Hammad, from Ibrahim Bin Uqba, from Al Husayn Bin Musa who said, ‘Abu Al-Hassanasws was with a man in the presence of the grave of Rasool-Allahsaww, so he looked at himasws and heasws had applied henna upon hisasws hands. So one of the people of Al-Medina said, ‘Are you not looking at this one how heasws has applied the henna upon hisasws hands?’ So heasws turned towards him and said to him: ‘In it is what you are informed of and what you are not informed of’. Then heasws turned towards me, so heasws said: ‘The one who takes from the henna after him having been freed from the waxing of the Noura, from his head to his feet, is safe from three illnesses – the insanity, and the leprosy, and the vitiligo’.

citation.chapter: The Book of Outfits and the Beautification and the Magnanimity (al-Kafi, vol 6), 8:47
citation.arabic_text: كَانَ أَبُو الْحَسَنِ ( عليه السلام ) مَعَ رَجُلٍ عِنْدَ قَبْرِ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ ( صلى الله عليه وآله ) فَنَظَرَ إِلَيْهِ وَ قَدْ أَخَذَ الْحِنَّاءَ مِنْ يَدَيْهِ فَقَالَ بَعْضُ أَهْلِ الْمَدِينَةِ أَ مَا تَرَوْنَ إِلَى هَذَا كَيْفَ أَخَذَ الْحِنَّاءَ مِنْ يَدَيْهِ فَالْتَفَتَ إِلَيْهِ فَقَالَ لَهُ فِيهِ مَا تَخْبُرُهُ وَ مَا لَا تَخْبُرُهُ ثُمَّ الْتَفَتَ إِلَيَّ فَقَالَ إِنَّهُ مَنْ أَخَذَ مِنَ الْحِنَّاءِ بَعْدَ فَرَاغِهِ مِنِ اطِّلَاءِ النُّورَةِ مِنْ قَرْنِهِ إِلَى قَدَمِهِ أَمِنَ مِنَ الْأَدْوَاءِ الثَّلَاثَةِ الْجُنُونِ وَ الْجُذَامِ وَ الْبَرَصِ .

So one of the people of Al-Medina said, ‘Are you not looking at this one how heasws has applied the henna upon hisasws hands?’ So heasws turned towards him and said to him: ‘In it is what you are informed of and what you are not informed of’. text: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Abu Nasr, (It has been narrated) from Abu Al-Hassan Al-Reza<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘The perfume is from the etiquettes of the Prophets<sup>as</sup>’.

citation.arabic_text: الْعِطْرُ مِنْ سُنَنِ الْمُرْسَلِينَ .

text: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Ali Bin Ra’ib who said, ‘I was in the presence of Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> and I was with Abu Baseer, so I heard Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> and he<sup>asws</sup> was saying: ‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘The fragrance of the perfume strengthens the heart and increases in the copulation’.

citation.arabic_text: كُنْتُ عِنْدَ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) وَ أَنَا مَعَ أَبِي بَصِيرٍ فَسَمِعْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) وَ هُوَ يَقُولُ قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ ( صلى الله عليه وآله ) إِنَّ الرِّيحَ الطَّيِّبَةَ تَشُدُّ الْقَلْبَ وَ تَزِيدُ فِي الْجِمَاعِ .

text: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Moamar Bin Khallad, (It has been narrated) from Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘It is not befitting for the man that he should leave the perfume during each day, so if he is not able over it, so a day and a day (alternate days), so if he is not able, so during every Friday, and he should not leave it’.

citation.chapter: The Book of Outfits and the Beautification and the Magnanimity (al-Kafi, vol 6), 8:48
citation.arabic_text: لَا يَنْبَغِي لِلرَّجُلِ أَنْ يَدَعَ الطِّيبَ فِي كُلِّ يَوْمٍ فَإِنْ لَمْ يَقْدِرْ عَلَيْهِ فَيَوْمٌ وَ يَوْمٌ لَا فَإِنْ لَمْ يَقْدِرْ فَفِي كُلِّ جُمُعَةٍ وَ لَا يَدَعْ .
citation.translation: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Moamar Bin Khallad, (It has been narrated) from Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘It is not befitting for the man that he should leave the perfume during each day, so if he is not able over it, so a day and a day (alternate days), so if he is not able, so during every Friday, and he should not leave it’.

citation.arabic_text: مَنْ تَطَيَّبَ أَوَّلَ النَّهَارِ لَمْ يَزَلْ عَقْلُهُ مَعَهُ إِلَى اللَّيْلِ وَ قَالَ قَالَ أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) صَلَاةُ مُتَطَيِّبٍ أَفْضَلُ مِنْ سَبْعِينَ صَلَاةً بِغَيْرِ طِيبٍ .

citation.arabic_text: سَمِعْتُ أَبِي يَقُولُ الْعِطْرُ مِنْ سُنَنِ الْمُرْسَلِينَ .
citation.translation: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Abu Abdullah, from Muhammad Bin Ali, (It has been narrated) from Al-Abbas son of Musaasws who said, ‘I heard my fatherasws saying: ‘The perfume is from the Sunnah of the Mursil Prophetsas’.

text: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Talha Bin Zayd, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Three (things) are which the Prophets<sup>as</sup> came to – the perfume, and the wives, and the brushing of teeth’.

citation.chapter: The Book of Outfits and the Beautification and the Magnanimity (al-Kafi, vol 6), 8:48
citation.arabic_text: ثَلَاثٌ أُعْطِيَهُنَّ الْأَنْبِيَاءُ ( عليهم السلام ) الْعِطْرُ وَ الْأَزْوَاجُ وَ السِّوَاكُ .
citation.translation: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Talha Bin Zayd, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Three (things) are which the Prophets<sup>as</sup> came to – the perfume, and the wives, and the brushing of teeth’.

text: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Abu Abdullah, from Muhamad Bin Musa Bin Al Furat, from Ali Bin Matar, form Al Sakan Al Khazzaz who said, ‘I heard Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> saying: ‘It is a right upon every adolescent male during every Friday that he takes from his moustache, and his nails, and touches himself with something from the perfume; and Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup>, whenever it was the day of Friday, and there did not happen to be a perfume with him<sup>saww</sup>, would call for a scarf of one of his<sup>saww</sup> wives, so he<sup>saww</sup> would moisten it with the water, then place it upon his<sup>saww</sup> face’.

citation.chapter: The Book of Outfits and the Beautification and the Magnanimity (al-Kafi, vol 6), 8:48
citation.arabic_text: سَمِعْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) يَقُولُ حَقٌّ عَلَى كُلِّ مُحْتَلِمٍ فِي كُلِّ جُمُعَةٍ أَخْذُ شَارِبِهِ وَ أَظْفَارِهِ وَ مَسُّ شَيْ‏ءٍ مِنَ الطِّيبِ وَ كَانَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ ( صلى الله عليه وآله ) إِذَا كَانَ يَوْمُ الْجُمُعَةِ وَ لَمْ يَكُنْ عِنْدَهُ طِيبٌ دَعَا بِبَعْضِ خُمُرِ نِسَائِهِ فَبَلَّهَا بِالْمَاءِ ثُمَّ وَضَعَهَا عَلَى وَجْهِهِ .
citation.translation: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Abu Abdullah, from Muhamad Bin Musa Bin Al Furat, from Ali Bin Matar, form Al Sakan Al Khazzaz who said, ‘I heard Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> saying: ‘It is a right upon every adolescent male during every Friday that he takes from his moustache, and his nails, and touches himself with something from the perfume; and Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup>, whenever it was the day of Friday, and there did not happen to be a perfume with him<sup>saww</sup>, would call for a scarf of one of his<sup>saww</sup> wives, so he<sup>saww</sup> would moisten it with the water, then place it upon his<sup>saww</sup> face’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: ضعيف - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (22/416)

text: Al Husayn Bin Muhammad, form Moala Bin Muhammad, and a number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, altogether from Al Hassan Bin Ali, (It has been narrated) from Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘One could recognise the place of Prostration of Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> by the aromatic smell of it’.

citation.chapter: The Book of Outfits and the Beautification and the Magnanimity (al-Kafi, vol 6), 8:48
citation.arabic_text: كَانَ يُعْرَفُ مَوْضِعُ سُجُودِ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) بِطِيبِ رِيحِهِ .
citation.translation: Al Husayn Bin Muhammad, form Moala Bin Muhammad, and a number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, altogether from Al Hassan Bin Ali, (It has been narrated) from Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘One could recognise the place of Prostration of Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> by the aromatic smell of it’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: ضعيف على المشهور - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (22/416)

text: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Yasser, (It has been narrated) from Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said to me: ‘My<sup>saww</sup> beloved Jibraeel<sup>as</sup> said to me: ‘Apply perfume one day, and one day don’t, and the day of Friday is inevitable from it, and do not neglect it’.

citation.chapter: The Book of Outfits and the Beautification and the Magnanimity (al-Kafi, vol 6), 8:48
citation.arabic_text: قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ ( صلى الله عليه وآله ) قَالَ لِي حَبِيبِي جَبْرَئِيلُ ( عليه السلام ) تَطَيَّبْ يَوْماً وَ يَوْماً لَا وَ يَوْمَ الْجُمُعَةِ لَا بُدَّ مِنْهُ وَ لَا تَتْرُكْ لَهُ .
citation.translation: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Yasser, (It has been narrated) from Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said to me: ‘My<sup>saww</sup> beloved Jibraeel<sup>as</sup> said to me: ‘Apply perfume one day, and one day don’t, and the day of Friday is inevitable from it, and do not neglect it’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: مجهول كالحسن - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (2/417)

text: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Al Nowfaly, from Al Sakuny, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘Let each one of you apply perfume on the day of Friday, even if it is from a flask of his wife’.

citation.chapter: The Book of Outfits and the Beautification and the Magnanimity (al-Kafi, vol 6), 8:48
citation.arabic_text: قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ ( صلى الله عليه وآله ) لِيَتَطَيَّبْ أَحَدُكُمْ يَوْمَ الْجُمُعَةِ وَ لَوْ مِنْ قَارُورَةِ امْرَأَتِهِ .
citation.translation: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Al Nowfaly, from Al Sakuny, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘Let each one of you apply perfume on the day of Friday, even if it is from a flask of his wife’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: ضعيف على المشهور - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (22/417)

text: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Abu Abdullah, from Yaqoub Bin Yazeed, raising it, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Usman Bin Mazoun said to Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup>, ‘I have intended to leave the perfume and certain things’, and he mentioned these. So Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘Do not leave the perfume, for the Angels desire the aromatic fragrances from the Believer, therefore do not leave the perfume during every Friday’.

citation.chapter: The Book of Outfits and the Beautification and the Magnanimity (al-Kafi, vol 6), 8:48
citation.arabic_text: قَالَ عُثْمَانُ بْنُ مَظْعُونٍ لِرَسُولِ اللَّهِ ( صلى الله عليه وآله ) قَدْ أَرَدْتُ أَنْ أَدَعَ الطِّيبَ وَ أَشْيَاءَ ذَكَرَهَا فَقَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ ( صلى الله عليه وآله ) لَا تَدَعِ الطِّيبَ فَإِنَّ الْمَلَائِكَةَ تَسْتَنْشِقُ رِيحَ الطِّيبِ مِنَ الْمُؤْمِنِ فَلَا تَدَعِ الطِّيبَ فِي كُلِّ جُمُعَةٍ .
citation.translation: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Abu Abdullah, from Yaqoub Bin Yazeed, raising it, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Usman Bin Mazoun said to Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup>, ‘I have intended to leave the perfume and certain things’, and he mentioned these. So Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘Do not leave the perfume, for the Angels desire the aromatic fragrances from the Believer, therefore do not leave the perfume during every Friday’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: مرفوع - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (22/417)

text: A number of our companions, from sahl Bin Ziyad, from Muhammad Bin Isa, from Abdullah Bin Abdul Rahman, from Shuayb, from Abu Baseer, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘The perfume in the moustache is from the mannerism of the Prophets<sup>as</sup> and a prestige for the two Scribes (recording Angels)’.

citation.chapter: The Book of Outfits and the Beautification and the Magnanimity (al-Kafi, vol 6), 8:48
citation.arabic_text: الطِّيبُ فِي الشَّارِبِ مِنْ أَخْلَاقِ الْأَنْبِيَاءِ ( عليهم السلام ) وَ كَرَامَةٌ لِلْكَاتِبِينَ .
citation.translation: A number of our companions, from sahl Bin Ziyad, from Muhammad Bin Isa, from Abdullah Bin Abdul Rahman, from Shuayb, from Abu Baseer, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘The perfume in the moustache is from the mannerism of the Prophets<sup>as</sup> and a prestige for the two Scribes (recording Angels)’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: ضعيف على المشهور - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (22/417)

text: From him, from Muhammad Bin Isa, from Zakariyya Al Momin, raising it, ‘He<sup>asws</sup> said, ‘Whatever you spend regarding the perfume, so it is not an extravagance’.

citation.chapter: The Book of Outfits and the Beautification and the Magnanimity (al-Kafi, vol 6), 8:48
citation.arabic_text: مَا أَنْفَقْتَ فِي الطِّيبِ فَلَيْسَ بِسَرَفٍ .
citation.translation: From him, from Muhammad Bin Isa, from Zakariyya Al Momin, raising it, ‘He<sup>asws</sup> said, ‘Whatever you spend regarding the perfume, so it is not an extravagance’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: ضعيف - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (22/417)

text: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Al Nowfaly, from Al Sakuny, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘Perfume of the women is what displays its colour and hides its smell, and a perfume of the men is what manifests its smell and hides its colour’.

citation.chapter: The Book of Outfits and the Beautification and the Magnanimity (al-Kafi, vol 6), 8:48
citation.arabic_text: قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ ( صلى الله عليه وآله ) طِيبُ النِّسَاءِ مَا ظَهَرَ لَوْنُهُ وَ خَفِيَ رِيحُهُ وَ طِيبُ الرِّجَالِ مَا ظَهَرَ رِيحُهُ وَ خَفِيَ لَوْنُهُ .
citation.translation: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Al Nowfaly, from Al Sakuny, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘Perfume of the women is what displays its colour and hides its smell, and a perfume of the men is what manifests its smell and hides its colour’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: ضعيف على المشهور - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (22/417)

text: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Muhammad Bin Al Husayn, from Suleyman Bin Muhammad Al Khash’amy, from Ishaq Al Taweel Al Attar, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> used to spend regarding the perfume more than what he<sup>saww</sup> used to spend regarding the food’.

citation.chapter: The Book of Outfits and the Beautification and the Magnanimity (al-Kafi, vol 6), 8:48
citation.arabic_text: كَانَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ ( صلى الله عليه وآله ) يُنْفِقُ فِي الطِّيبِ أَكْثَرَ مِمَّا يُنْفِقُ فِي الطَّعَامِ .
citation.translation: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Muhammad Bin Al Husayn, from Suleyman Bin Muhammad Al Khash’amy, from Ishaq Al Taweel Al Attar, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> used to spend regarding the perfume more than what he<sup>saww</sup> used to spend regarding the food’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: مجهول - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (22/418)

text: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Khalid, from Usman Bin Isa, from Sama’at Bin Mihran, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, said, ‘I asked him<sup>asws</sup> about the man who rejects the perfume. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘It is not befitting that he rejects the prestige’.

citation.chapter: The Book of Outfits and the Beautification and the Magnanimity (al-Kafi, vol 6), 8:49
citation.arabic_text: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنِ الرَّجُلِ يَرُدُّ الطِّيبَ قَالَ لَا يَنْبَغِي لَهُ أَنْ يَرُدَّ الْكَرَامَةَ .
citation.translation: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Khalid, from Usman Bin Isa, from Sama’at Bin Mihran, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, said, ‘I asked him<sup>asws</sup> about the man who rejects the perfume. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘It is not befitting that he rejects the prestige’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: موثق - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (22/418)

text: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Ja’far Bin Muhammad Al Ashary, from Ibn Al Qaddah, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> was given anointing oil, and he<sup>asws</sup> used to anoint. So he<sup>asws</sup> anointed and said: ‘I<sup>asws</sup> do not reject the perfume’.

citation.chapter: The Book of Outfits and the Beautification and the Magnanimity (al-Kafi, vol 6), 8:49
citation.arabic_text: أُتِيَ أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ ( عليه السلام ) بِدُهْنٍ وَ قَدْ كَانَ ادَّهَنَ فَادَّهَنَ فَقَالَ إِنَّا لَا نَرُدُّ الطِّيبَ .
citation.translation: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Ja’far Bin Muhammad Al Ashary, from Ibn Al Qaddah, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> was given anointing oil, and he<sup>asws</sup> used to anoint. So he<sup>asws</sup> anointed and said: ‘I<sup>asws</sup> do not reject the perfume’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: ضعيف على المشهور - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (22/418)

text: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Al Hassan Bin Jahm who said, ‘I went over to Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup>, so he<sup>asws</sup> brought out to me a perfume box in which was musk, and said: ‘Take from this’. So I took something from it, and I applied with it. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘More, and make it to be in your chest from it’. So I took a little from it and made it to be in my chest. So he<sup>asws</sup> said to me: ‘More’. So I took from it again, and there remained something from it in my hand. So he<sup>asws</sup> said to me: ‘Make it to be in your chest’. So I did it. Then he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘No one refuses the prestige except for a donkey’. I said, ‘What is the meaning of that?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The perfume, and the pillow and a number of things’.

citation.chapter: The Book of Outfits and the Beautification and the Magnanimity (al-Kafi, vol 6), 8:49
citation.arabic_text: دَخَلْتُ عَلَى أَبِي الْحَسَنِ ( عليه السلام ) فَأَخْرَجَ إِلَيَّ مَخْزَنَةً فِيهَا مِسْكٌ وَ قَالَ خُذْ مِنْ هَذَا فَأَخَذْتُ مِنْهُ شَيْئاً فَتَمَسَّحْتُ بِهِ فَقَالَ أَصْلِحْ وَ اجْعَلْ فِي لَبَّتِكَ مِنْهُ قَالَ فَأَخَذْتُ مِنْهُ قَلِيلًا فَجَعَلْتُهُ فِي لَبَّتِي فَقَالَ لِي أَصْلِحْ فَأَخَذْتُ مِنْهُ أَيْضاً فَمَكَثَ فِي يَدِي مِنْهُ شَيْ‏ءٌ صَالِحٌ فَقَالَ لِي اجْعَلْ فِي لَبَّتِكَ فَفَعَلْتُ ثُمَّ قَالَ قَالَ أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ ( عليه السلام ) لَا يَأْبَى الْكَرَامَةَ إِلَّا حِمَارٌ قَالَ قُلْتُ مَا مَعْنَى ذَلِكَ قَالَ الطِّيبُ وَ الْوِسَادَةُ وَ عَدَّ أَشْيَاءَ.
citation.translation: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Al Hassan Bin Jahm who said, ‘I went over to Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup>, so he<sup>asws</sup> brought out to me a perfume box in which was musk, and said: ‘Take from this’. So I took something from it, and I applied with it. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘More, and make it to be in your chest from it’. So I took a little from it and made it to be in my chest. So he<sup>asws</sup> said to me: ‘More’. So I took from it again, and there remained something from it in my hand. So he<sup>asws</sup> said to me: ‘Make it to be in your chest’. So I did it. Then he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘No one refuses the prestige except for a donkey’. I said, ‘What is the meaning of that?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The perfume, and the pillow and a number of things’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: موثق - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (22/418)

text: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Muhammad Bin Ahmad, from Ahmad Bin Hilal, from Isa Bin Abdullah, from his father, from his grandfather, (It has been narrated) from Ali<sup>asws</sup> that: ‘The Prophet<sup>saww</sup> never used to reject the perfume and the sweets’.

citation.chapter: The Book of Outfits and the Beautification and the Magnanimity (al-Kafi, vol 6), 8:49
citation.arabic_text: أَنَّ النَّبِيَّ ( صلى الله عليه وآله ) كَانَ لَا يَرُدُّ الطِّيبَ وَ الْحَلْوَاءَ .
citation.translation: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Muhammad Bin Ahmad, from Ahmad Bin Hilal, from Isa Bin Abdullah, from his father, from his grandfather, (It has been narrated) from Ali<sup>asws</sup> that: ‘The Prophet<sup>saww</sup> never used to reject the perfume and the sweets’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: ضعيف - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (22/419)

text: Muhammad Bin Ja’far, from Muhammad Bin Khalid, from Sayf Bin Umeyra, from Abdul Ghaffar who said, ‘I heard Abu Abdullahasws saying: ‘The perfume is the musk, and the Amber, and the saffron, and the Oud (Aloe wood)’.

citation.chapter: The Book of Outfits and the Beautification and the Magnanimity (al-Kafi, vol 6), 8:50
citation.arabic_text: سَمِعْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) يَقُولُ الطِّيبُ الْمِسْكُ وَ الْعَنْبَرُ وَ الزَّعْفَرَانُ وَ الْعُودُ .
citation.translation: Muhammad Bin Ja’far, from Muhammad Bin Khalid, from Sayf Bin Umeyra, from Abdul Ghaffar who said, ‘I heard Abu Abdullahasws saying: ‘The perfume is the musk, and the Amber, and the saffron, and the Oud (Aloe wood)’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: مجهول - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (22/419)

text: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Ali Bin Hassan, from Musa Bin Bakr, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws having said: ‘When Adamas descended from the Paradise upon Al-Safa and Hawwaas upon the Marwa, and sheas used to comb in the Paradise with a perfume from the perfumes of the Paradise. So when sheas came to be in the earth, sheas said: ‘How hopeful Ias am from the combing and Ias am loathsome of myas hair’. So sheas loosened heras braids, so there scattered from her combing which sheas used to comb with in the Paradise, and the wind carried it and cast most of it in India. Thus, it is due to that, came to be the perfume in India’. A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Abu Adullah, from Ali Bin Hassan – similar to it. He (the narrator) said, ‘And in another Hadeeth - : ‘Sheas loosened her braids, so Allahazwj Sent upon what was therein, from that perfume, a wind, so it descended in the eat and the west. Thus, the origination of the perfume is from that’.

citation.chapter: The Book of Outfits and the Beautification and the Magnanimity (al-Kafi, vol 6), 8:51
citation.arabic_text: لَمَّا أُهْبِطَ آدَمُ ( عليه السلام ) مِنَ الْجَنَّةِ عَلَى الصَّفَا وَ حَوَّاءُ عَلَى الْمَرْوَةِ وَ قَدْ كَانَتِ امْتَشَطَتْ فِي الْجَنَّةِ بِطِيبٍ مِنْ طِيبِ الْجَنَّةِ فَلَمَّا صَارَتْ فِي الْأَرْضِ قَالَتْ مَا أَرْجُو مِنَ الْمَشْطِ وَ أَنَا مَسْخُوطٌ عَلَيَّ فَحَلَّتْ عَقِيصَتَهَا فَانْتَثَرَ مِنْ مُشْطَتِهَا الَّتِي كَانَتِ امْتَشَطَتْ بِهَا فِي الْجَنَّةِ فَطَارَتْ بِهِ الرِّيحُ فَأَلْقَتْ أَكْثَرَهُ بِالْهِنْدِ فَلِذَلِكَ صَارَ الْعِطْرُ بِالْهِنْدِ . عِدَّةٌ مِنْ أَصْحَابِنَا عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ حَسَّانَ مِثْلَهُ . قَالَ وَ فِي حَدِيثٍ آخَرَ فَحَلَّتْ عَقِيصَتَهَا فَأَرْسَلَ اللَّهُ عَلَى مَا كَانَ فِيهَا مِنْ ذَلِكَ الطِّيبِ رِيحاً فَهَبَّتْ فِي الْمَشْرِقِ وَ الْمَغْرِبِ فَأَصْلُ الطِّيبِ مِنْ ذَلِكَ .
citation.translation: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Ali Bin Hassan, from Musa Bin Bakr, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws having said: ‘When Adamas descended from the Paradise upon Al-Safa and Hawwaas upon the Marwa, and sheas used to comb in the Paradise with a perfume from the perfumes of the Paradise. So when sheas came to be in the earth, sheas said: ‘How hopeful Ias am from the combing and Ias am loathsome of myas hair’. So sheas loosened heras braids, so there scattered from her combing which sheas used to comb with in the Paradise, and the wind carried it and cast most of it in India. Thus, it is due to that, came to be the perfume in India’. A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Abu Adullah, from Ali Bin Hassan – similar to it. He (the narrator) said, ‘And in another Hadeeth - : ‘Sheas loosened her braids, so Allahazwj Sent upon what was therein, from that perfume, a wind, so it descended in the eat and the west. Thus, the origination of the perfume is from that’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: ضعيف على المشهور - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (22/419)

text: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ja’far Bin Yahya, from Ali Al Qaseyr, from a man, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, said, ‘I asked Him<sup>asws</sup> about the origination of the perfume, from which thing is it?’ So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Which thing are the people saying?’ I said, ‘They are alleging that Adam<sup>as</sup> descended from the Paradise and upon his<sup>as</sup> head was a crown’. text: Ali Bin Muhammad, from Salih Bin Abu Hammad, from Al Husayn Bin Yazeed, from Al Hassan Bin Ali Bin Abu Hamza, (It has been narrated) from Ibrahim, from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘When Allah<sup>azwj</sup> the Exalted Caused Adam<sup>as</sup> to descend from the Paradise, he<sup>as</sup> started covering himself<sup>as</sup> from a leaf of the Paradise, and his<sup>as</sup> clothes flew away from him<sup>as</sup>, which used to be upon him<sup>as</sup> from the garments of the Paradise. So he<sup>as</sup> cut off a leaf and veiled his<sup>as</sup> nakedness with it. So when he<sup>as</sup> descended, the aroma of that leaf remained at India with the vegetation. So the perfume came to be in the earth from the cause of that leaf upon which remained the aroma of the Paradise. Thus, from here on the perfume is at India, because upon the leaf fell the south wind, so its aroma led to the west because it carried the aroma of the leaf in the atmosphere. So when the wind stagnated at India, it remained in its trees, and its vegetation. So the first animal which grazed the musk from that leaf was a deer. Thus, from over there the musk came to be in the navel of the deer flowing the aroma of the vegetation in its body, and in its blood, gathering in the navel of the deer’.

citation.arabic_text: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنِ الْمِسْكِ فِي الدُّهْنِ أَ يَصْلُحُ قَالَ إِنِّي لَأَصْنَعُهُ فِي الدُّهْنِ وَ لَا بَأْسَ . وَ رُوِيَ أَنَّهُ لَا بَأْسَ بِصُنْعِ الْمِسْكِ فِي الطَّعَامِ .
citation.translation: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Al Amraky Bin Ali, (It has been narrated) from Ali son of Ja’far<sup>asws</sup>, from his brother<sup>asws</sup> Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup>, said, ‘I asked him<sup>asws</sup> about the musk in the anointing (oiling/massaging) is it correct?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘I<sup>asws</sup> apply it in the anointing and there is no problem’. And it is reported that there is no problem with making the musk to be in the food.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: صحيح - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (22/422)

text: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Usman Bin Isa, from Is’haq Bin Ammar, said, ‘I said to Abu Abdullahasws, ‘I work with the business people, so I make myself pleasant for the people not liking that they should see me as a destitute, so I take Al-Ghaliya’. So heasws said: ‘O Is’haq! A little from Al-Ghaliya suffices and a lot of it is the same. The one who takes a little Ghaliya all the time, that would suffice for him’. I’shaq said, ‘And I bought from it during the year with ten Dirhams, so I sufficed myself with it, and its aroma was affirmed for a long duration’.

citation.chapter: The Book of Outfits and the Beautification and the Magnanimity (al-Kafi, vol 6), 8:53
citation.arabic_text: قُلْتُ لِأَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) إِنِّي أُعَامِلُ التُّجَّارَ فَأَتَهَيَّأُ لِلنَّاسِ كَرَاهَةَ أَنْ يَرَوْا بِي خَصَاصَةً فَأَتَّخِذُ الْغَالِيَةَ فَقَالَ يَا إِسْحَاقُ إِنَّ الْقَلِيلَ مِنَ الْغَالِيَةِ يُجْزِئُ وَ كَثِيرَهَا سَوَاءً مَنِ اتَّخَذَ مِنَ الْغَالِيَةِ قَلِيلًا دَائِماً أَجْزَأَهُ ذَلِكَ قَالَ إِسْحَاقُ وَ أَنَا أَشْتَرِي مِنْهَا فِي السَّنَةِ بِعَشَرَةِ دَرَاهِمَ فَأَكْتَفِي بِهَا وَ رِيحُهَا ثَابِتٌ طُولَ الدَّهْرِ .

text: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Moamar Bin Khallad who said, ‘Abu Al-Hassan Al-Rezaasws ordered me, so I made a flask for himasws in which was musk, and Amber. So heasws ordered me that I should write down in a paper the Verse of the Chair [2:255], and the Mother of the Book (Surah Al-Fatiha), and Al-Mawazatain (Chapters 113 & 114), and certain Verses from the Quran, and make these to be in between the covering and the flask. So I did it, then I came over to himasws with it, and heasws placed it in a covering, and I was looking at himasws’.

citation.chapter: The Book of Outfits and the Beautification and the Magnanimity (al-Kafi, vol 6), 8:53
citation.arabic_text: أَمَرَنِي أَبُو الْحَسَنِ الرِّضَا ( عليه السلام ) فَعَمِلْتُ لَهُ دُهْناً فِيهِ مِسْكٌ وَ عَنْبَرٌ فَأَمَرَنِي أَنْ أَكْتُبَ فِي قِرْطَاسٍ آيَةَ الْكُرْسِيِّ وَ أُمَّ الْكِتَابِ وَ الْمُعَوِّذَتَيْنِ وَ قَوَارِعَ مِنَ الْقُرْآنِ وَ أَجْعَلَهُ بَيْنَ الْغِلَافِ وَ الْقَارُورَةِ فَفَعَلْتُ ثُمَّ أَتَيْتُهُ بِهِ فَتَغَلَّفَ بِهِ وَ أَنَا أَنْظُرُ إِلَيْهِ .

So I did it, then I came over to himasws with it, and heasws placed it in a covering, and I was looking at himasws’.

text: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Abu Abdullah, from Muhammad Bin Ali, from a slave of the Clan of hashimas, from Muhammad Bin Ja’far Bin Muhammad who said, ‘Aliasws Bin Al-Husaynasws came out one night and upon himasws was a robe of khazz and a cloak of khazz, and heasws had covered hisasws beard with Al-Ghaliya. So they (people) said, ‘At this time and in this beard?’ So heasws said: ‘I wanted to address the Maiden Hourie to Allahazwj Mighty and Majestic during this night’. Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Ali Bin Asbaat, from a slave of the Clan of Hashimas, from Muhammad Bin Ja’far – similar to it.

citation.chapter: The Book of Outfits and the Beautification and the Magnanimity (al-Kafi, vol 6), 8:53
citation.arabic_text: خَرَجَ عَلِيُّ بْنُ الْحُسَيْنِ ( عليه السلام ) لَيْلَةً وَ عَلَيْهِ جُبَّةُ خَزٍّ وَ كِسَاءُ خَزٍّ قَدْ غَلَفَ لِحْيَتَهُ بِالْغَالِيَةِ فَقَالُوا فِي هَذِهِ السَّاعَةِ فِي هَذِهِ الْهَيْئَةِ فَقَالَ إِنِّي أُرِيدُ أَنْ أَخْطُبَ الْحُورَ الْعِينَ إِلَى اللَّهِ عَزَّ وَ جَلَّ فِي هَذِهِ اللَّيْلَةِ . سَهْلُ بْنُ زِيَادٍ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ أَسْبَاطٍ عَنْ مَوْلًى لِبَنِي هَاشِمٍ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ جَعْفَرٍ مِثْلَهُ .
citation.translation: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Abu Abdullah, from Muhammad Bin Ali, from a slave of the Clan of hashimas, from Muhammad Bin Ja’far Bin Muhammad who said, ‘Aliasws Bin Al-Husaynasws came out one night and upon himasws was a robe of khazz and a cloak of khazz, and heasws had covered hisasws beard with Al-Ghaliya. So they (people) said, ‘At this time and in this beard?’ So heasws said: ‘I wanted to address the Maiden Hourie to Allahazwj Mighty and Majestic during this night’. Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Ali Bin Asbaat, from a slave of the Clan of Hashimas, from Muhammad Bin Ja’far – similar to it.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: ضعيف - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (2/423)

text: From him, from Abu Al Qasim Al Kufy, from the one who narrated it, from Muhammad Bin Al Waleed Al Kirmany who said, ‘I said to Abu Ja’farasws the 2nd, ‘What are youasws saying regarding the musk?’ So heasws said: ‘Myasws fatherasws ordered for musk to be made for himasws in a container, for seven hundred Dirhams. So Al-Fazl Bin Sahl wrote to himasws, informing himasws that the people are refusing that. So heasws wrote to him: ‘O Fazl! But do you not know that Yusufas, and heas was a Prophetas, used to wear the brocade buttoned with the gold, and would sit upon a chair of gold, and that did not reduce anything from hisas wisdom?’ He (the narrator) said, ‘So I made Ghaliya for himas for four thousand Dirhams’.

citation.chapter: The Book of Outfits and the Beautification and the Magnanimity (al-Kafi, vol 6), 8:53
citation.arabic_text: قُلْتُ لِأَبِي جَعْفَرٍ الثَّانِي ( عليه السلام ) مَا تَقُولُ فِي الْمِسْكِ فَقَالَ إِنَّ أَبِي أَمَرَ فَعُمِلَ لَهُ مِسْكٌ فِي بَانٍ بِسَبْعِمِائَةِ دِرْهَمٍ فَكَتَبَ إِلَيْهِ الْفَضْلُ بْنُ سَهْلٍ يُخْبِرُهُ أَنَّ النَّاسَ يَعِيبُونَ ذَلِكَ فَكَتَبَ إِلَيْهِ يَا فَضْلُ أَ مَا عَلِمْتَ أَنَّ يُوسُفَ ( عليه السلام ) وَ هُوَ نَبِيٌّ كَانَ يَلْبَسُ الدِّيبَاجَ مُزَرَّراً بِالذَّهَبِ وَ يَجْلِسُ عَلَى كَرَاسِيِّ الذَّهَبِ وَ لَمْ يَنْقُصْ ذَلِكَ مِنْ حِكْمَتِهِ شَيْئاً قَالَ ثُمَّ أَمَرَ فَعُمِلَتْ لَهُ غَالِيَةٌ بِأَرْبَعَةِ آلَافِ دِرْهَمٍ .
citation.translation: From him, from Abu Al Qasim Al Kufy, from the one who narrated it, from Muhammad Bin Al Waleed Al Kirmany who said, ‘I said to Abu Ja’farasws the 2nd, ‘What are youasws saying regarding the musk?’ So heasws said: ‘Myasws fatherasws ordered for musk to be made for himasws in a container, for seven hundred Dirhams. So Al-Fazl Bin Sahl wrote to himasws, informing himasws that the people are refusing that. So heasws wrote to him: ‘O Fazl! But do you not know that Yusufas, and heas was a Prophetas, used to wear the brocade buttoned with the gold, and would sit upon a chair of gold, and that did not reduce anything from hisas wisdom?’ He (the narrator) said, ‘So I made Ghaliya for himas for four thousand Dirhams’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: ضعيف - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (2/423)

text: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Al Husayn Bin Yazeed, from one of his companions, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws having said: ‘Aliasws Bin Al-Husaynasws met a slave of hisasws on a cold night and upon himasws was a rod of khazz, a gown of khazz, and a turban of khazz, and heasws had applied Al-Ghaliya. So he said to himasws, ‘May I be sacrificed for youasws! In a time like this, upon this beard, where to (are youasws going)?’ So heasws said: ‘To the Masjid of myasws grandfathersaww Rasool-Allahsaww, to address the Maiden Hourie to Allahazwj Mighty and Majestic’.

citation.chapter: The Book of Outfits and the Beautification and the Magnanimity (al-Kafi, vol 6), 8:53
citation.arabic_text: إِنَّ عَلِيَّ بْنَ الْحُسَيْنِ ( عليه السلام ) اسْتَقْبَلَهُ مَوْلًى لَهُ فِي لَيْلَةٍ بَارِدَةٍ وَ عَلَيْهِ جُبَّةُ خَزٍّ وَ مِطْرَفُ خَزٍّ وَ عِمَامَةُ خَزٍّ وَ هُوَ مُتَغَلِّفٌ بِالْغَالِيَةِ فَقَالَ لَهُ جُعِلْتُ فِدَاكَ فِي مِثْلِ هَذِهِ السَّاعَةِ عَلَى هَذِهِ الْهَيْئَةِ إِلَى أَيْنَ قَالَ فَقَالَ إِلَى مَسْجِدِ جَدِّي رَسُولِ اللَّهِ ( صلى الله عليه وآله ) أَخْطُبُ الْحُورَ الْعِينَ إِلَى اللَّهِ عَزَّ وَ جَلَّ .
citation.translation: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Al Husayn Bin Yazeed, from one of his companions, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws having said: ‘Aliasws Bin Al-Husaynasws met a slave of hisasws on a cold night and upon himasws was a rod of khazz, a gown of khazz, and a turban of khazz, and heasws had applied Al-Ghaliya. So he said to himasws, ‘May I be sacrificed for youasws!
