citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: مجهول - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (22/424)

text: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, form Ibn Fazzal, from Ibn Bukeyr, from Zurara who said, ‘I asked Abu Ja’farasws about Al-Khalouq, taking from it’. Heasws said: ‘There is no problem with it, but Iasws do not like it that you are perpetually upon it’.

citation.chapter: The Book of Outfits and the Beautification and the Magnanimity (al-Kafi, vol 6), 8:54
citation.arabic_text: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا جَعْفَرٍ ( عليه السلام ) عَنِ الْخَلُوقِ آخُذُ مِنْهُ قَالَ لَا بَأْسَ وَ لَكِنْ لَا أُحِبُّ أَنْ تَدُومَ عَلَيْهِ .
citation.translation: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, form Ibn Fazzal, from Ibn Bukeyr, from Zurara who said, ‘I asked Abu Ja’farasws about Al-Khalouq, taking from it’. Heasws said: ‘There is no problem with it, but Iasws do not like it that you are perpetually upon it’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: موثق - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (22/424)

text: Abu Ali Al Ashary, from one of his companions, from Ibn Abu Najran, from Abdullah Bin Sinan, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws having said: ‘There is no problem if you wipe Al-Khalouq in the bathhouse, or wipe your hands with it from the cracks (dry hands) to cure by it, and Iasws do not like making a habit of it’. And heasws said: ‘There is no problem that the man applies Al-Khalouq, but he should not sleep overnight having applied it’.

citation.chapter: The Book of Outfits and the Beautification and the Magnanimity (al-Kafi, vol 6), 8:54
citation.arabic_text: لَا بَأْسَ أَنْ تَمَسَّ الْخَلُوقَ فِي الْحَمَّامِ أَوْ تَمَسَّ بِهِ يَدَيْكَ مِنَ الشُّقَاقِ تُدَاوِيهِمَا بِهِ وَ لَا أُحِبُّ إِدْمَانَهُ وَ قَالَ لَا بَأْسَ أَنْ يَتَخَلَّقَ الرَّجُلُ وَ لَكِنْ لَا يَبِيتُ مُتَخَلِّقاً .
citation.translation: Abu Ali Al Ashary, from one of his companions, from Ibn Abu Najran, from Abdullah Bin Sinan, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws having said: ‘There is no problem if you wipe Al-Khalouq in the bathhouse, or wipe your hands with it from the cracks (dry hands) to cure by it, and Iasws do not like making a habit of it’. And heasws said: ‘There is no problem that the man applies Al-Khalouq, but he should not sleep overnight having applied it’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: مرسل - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (22/424)

text: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Abdullah Bin Sinan, ‘Heasws said: ‘There is no problem if you wipe Al-Khalouq in the bathhouse, or wipe your hands with it to cure by it (dryness of hands), and Iasws do not like being habitual of it’.

citation.arabic_text: لَا بَأْسَ أَنْ تَمَسَّ الْخَلُوقَ فِي الْحَمَّامِ أَوْ تَمْسَحَ بِهِ يَدَكَ تُدَاوِي بِهِ وَ لَا أُحِبُّ إِدْمَانَهُ .
citation.translation: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Abdullah Bin Sinan, ‘Heasws said: ‘There is no problem if you wipe Al-Khalouq in the bathhouse, or wipe your hands with it to cure by it (dryness of hands), and Iasws do not like being habitual of it’.

text: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Muhammad Bin Isa, from a man, from Muhammad Bin Al Fayz who said, ‘I heard Abu Abdullahasws saying: ‘Iasws love Al-Khalouq’.

citation.chapter: The Book of Outfits and the Beautification and the Magnanimity (al-Kafi, vol 6), 8:54
citation.arabic_text: سَمِعْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) يَقُولُ إِنَّهُ لَيُعْجِبُنِي الْخَلُوقُ .
citation.translation: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Muhammad Bin Isa, from a man, from Muhammad Bin Al Fayz who said, ‘I heard Abu Abdullahasws saying: ‘Iasws love Al-Khalouq’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: ضعيف على المشهور - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (22/425)

text: Humey Bin Ziyad, from Al Hassan Bin Muhammad Bin Sama’at, from Ja’far Bin Sama’at, from Aban, from a man who had affirmed it, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws havign said: ‘There is no problem if the man were to apply Al-Khalouq for his wife, but he should not sleep overnight having applied Al-Khalouq’.

citation.chapter: The Book of Outfits and the Beautification and the Magnanimity (al-Kafi, vol 6), 8:54
citation.arabic_text: لَا بَأْسَ أَنْ يَتَخَلَّقَ الرَّجُلُ لِامْرَأَتِهِ وَ لَكِنْ لَا يَبِيتُ مُتَخَلِّقاً .
citation.translation: Humey Bin Ziyad, from Al Hassan Bin Muhammad Bin Sama’at, from Ja’far Bin Sama’at, from Aban, from a man who had affirmed it, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws havign said: ‘There is no problem if the man were to apply Al-Khalouq for his wife, but he should not sleep overnight having applied Al-Khalouq’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: مرسل - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (22/425)

text: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from Salih Bin Al Sandy, from Ja’far Bin Basheer, from Aban, from Al Fazeyl, from a man, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abu Ja’farasws having said: ‘There is no problem if the man were to apply Al-Khalouq, but he should not sleep overnight having applied Al-Khalouq’.

citation.chapter: The Book of Outfits and the Beautification and the Magnanimity (al-Kafi, vol 6), 8:54
citation.arabic_text: لَا بَأْسَ بِأَنْ يَتَخَلَّقَ الرَّجُلُ وَ لَكِنْ لَا يَبِيتُ مُتَخَلِّقاً .
citation.translation: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from Salih Bin Al Sandy, from Ja’far Bin Basheer, from Aban, from Al Fazeyl, from a man, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abu Ja’farasws having said: ‘There is no problem if the man were to apply Al-Khalouq, but he should not sleep overnight having applied Al-Khalouq’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: مجهول - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (22/425)

text: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ali Bin Ibrahim Al ja’fary, from one of his companions, raising it, said, ‘Abu Abdullahasws said: ‘The aroma of Al-Oud which is in the body remains for forty days, and the aroma of Oud in the perfumes remains for twenty days’.

citation.chapter: The Book of Outfits and the Beautification and the Magnanimity (al-Kafi, vol 6), 8:55
citation.arabic_text: قَالَ أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) يَبْقَى رِيحُ الْعُودِ الَّتِي فِي الْبَدَنِ أَرْبَعِينَ يَوْماً وَ يَبْقَى رِيحُ عُودِ الْمُطَرَّاةِ عِشْرِينَ يَوْماً .
citation.translation: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ali Bin Ibrahim Al ja’fary, from one of his companions, raising it, said, ‘Abu Abdullahasws said: ‘The aroma of Al-Oud which is in the body remains for forty days, and the aroma of Oud in the perfumes remains for twenty days’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: مجهول مرفوع - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (2/425)

text: Al Husayn Bin Muhammad, from Moala Bin Muhammad, from al Washa, from Abdullah Bin Sinan, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘It is befitting for the man that he does incense whenever he is able to’.

citation.chapter: The Book of Outfits and the Beautification and the Magnanimity (al-Kafi, vol 6), 8:55
citation.arabic_text: يَنْبَغِي لِلرَّجُلِ أَنْ يُدَخِّنَ ثِيَابَهُ إِذَا كَانَ يَقْدِرُ .
citation.translation: Al Husayn Bin Muhammad, from Moala Bin Muhammad, from al Washa, from Abdullah Bin Sinan, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘It is befitting for the man that he does incense whenever he is able to’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: ضعيف على المشهور - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (22/425)

text: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Abu Abdullah, from Musa Bin Al Qasim, from Ali Bin Asbaat, from Al Hassan Bin Jahm who said, ‘Abu Al-Hassanasws came out to me, so I found from himasws an aroma of Al-Tajmeer (incense)’.

citation.chapter: The Book of Outfits and the Beautification and the Magnanimity (al-Kafi, vol 6), 8:55
citation.arabic_text: خَرَجَ إِلَيَّ أَبُو الْحَسَنِ ( عليه السلام ) فَوَجَدْتُ مِنْهُ رَائِحَةَ التَّجْمِيرِ .
citation.translation: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Abu Abdullah, from Musa Bin Al Qasim, from Ali Bin Asbaat, from Al Hassan Bin Jahm who said, ‘Abu Al-Hassanasws came out to me, so I found from himasws an aroma of Al-Tajmeer (incense)’.

text: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Murazam who said, ‘I entered the bathhouse along with Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup>. So when we came to the dressing room, he<sup>asws</sup> called for the incense burner so he<sup>asws</sup> applied the incense vapour with it, then said: ‘Apply the incense O Murazam! I said, ‘The one who want that he takes his share, can he take it?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Yes’.

citation.chapter: The Book of Outfits and the Beautification and the Magnanimity (al-Kafi, vol 6), 8:55
citation.arabic_text: دَخَلْتُ مَعَ أَبِي الْحَسَنِ ( عليه السلام ) الْحَمَّامَ فَلَمَّا خَرَجَ إِلَى الْمَسْلَخِ دَعَا بِمِجْمَرَةٍ فَتَجَمَّرَ بِهَا ثُمَّ قَالَ جَمِّرُوا مُرَازِمُ قَالَ قُلْتُ مَنْ أَرَادَ أَنْ يَأْخُذَ نَصِيبَهُ يَأْخُذُ قَالَ نَعَمْ .

text: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Muhammad Bin Ahmad, from Ali Bin Al Rayyan, (It has been narrated) from Ahmad Bin Abu Khalaf, a slave of Abu Al-Hassanasws, and heasws had bought his father, and his mother, and his brother, so heasws had freed them, and heasws had contracted Ahmad and made him hisasws butler. So Ahmad said, ‘When the wives of Abu Al-Hassanasws incensed, they took a type from a type of Al-Saykhani date, unrefined dates, and the peels, so they would cast these upon the fire before the incense. So when the dates smoked a little smoke, they threw the dates and burnt the incense from afterwards, and it tended to hand and be more remaining, and more aromatic for the vapour, and they used to instruct with these’.

citation.chapter: The Book of Outfits and the Beautification and the Magnanimity (al-Kafi, vol 6), 8:55
citation.arabic_text: أَحْمَدُ كَانَ نِسَاءُ أَبِي الْحَسَنِ ( عليه السلام ) إِذَا تَبَخَّرْنَ أَخَذْنَ نَوَاةً مِنْ نَوَى الصَّيْحَانِيِّ مَمْسُوحَةً مِنَ التَّمْرِ مُنْقَاةَ التَّمْرِ وَ الْقُشَارَةِ فَأَلْقَيْنَهَا عَلَى النَّارِ قَبْلَ الْبَخُورِ فَإِذَا دَخَنَتِ النَّوَاةُ أَدْنَى الدُّخَانِ رَمَيْنَ النَّوَاةَ وَ تَبَخَّرْنَ مِنْ بَعْدُ وَ كُنَّ يَقُلْنَ هُوَ أَعْبَقُ وَ أَطْيَبُ لِلْبَخُورِ وَ كُنَّ يَأْمُرْنَ بِذَلِكَ .

text: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from al Qasim Bin Yahya, from his grandfather Al Hassan Bin Rashid, from Abu Baseer, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The oiling (massaging) smoothens the person (skin) and increases in the brain, and eases the flow of the water (urination), and removes the scaling (dryness of the skin), and shines the complexion’.

citation.chapter: The Book of Outfits and the Beautification and the Magnanimity (al-Kafi, vol 6), 8:56
citation.arabic_text: قَالَ أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ ( عليه السلام ) الدُّهْنُ يُلَيِّنُ الْبَشَرَةَ وَ يَزِيدُ فِي الدِّمَاغِ وَ يُسَهِّلُ مَجَارِيَ الْمَاءِ وَ يُذْهِبُ الْقَشَفَ وَ يُسْفِرُ اللَّوْنَ .

citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: ضعيف - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (2/426)

text: From him, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Al hakam, from Abdullah Bin Jundab, from Sufyan Bin Al Samt, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘The oiling (massaging) removes the evil’.

citation.chapter: The Book of Outfits and the Beautification and the Magnanimity (al-Kafi, vol 6), 8:56
citation.arabic_text: الدُّهْنُ يَذْهَبُ بِالسُّوءِ .
citation.translation: From him, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Al hakam, from Abdullah Bin Jundab, from Sufyan Bin Al Samt, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘The oiling (massaging) removes the evil’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: مجهول - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (22/427)

text: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Al Nowfaly, from Al Sakuny, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘The oiling manifests the riches’.

citation.chapter: The Book of Outfits and the Beautification and the Magnanimity (al-Kafi, vol 6), 8:56
citation.arabic_text: الدُّهْنُ يُظْهِرُ الْغِنَى .

citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: ضعيف على المشهور - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (22/427)

text: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Muhammad Bin Isa, from Abdullah Bin Abdul Rahman, from Shuayb, from Abu Baseer, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The oiling (massaging) smoothens the person (skin), and increases in the brain power, and eases the flow of the water (urination), and it removes the scaling (dryness of the skin) and improves the complexion’.

citation.chapter: The Book of Outfits and the Beautification and the Magnanimity (al-Kafi, vol 6), 8:56

text: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Ibn Mahboub, from Abdullah Bin Sinan, from Abu Hamza, (It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘The oiling (massaging) at night flows in the veins and it irrigates the person (skin), and whitens the face’.

citation.chapter: The Book of Outfits and the Beautification and the Magnanimity (al-Kafi, vol 6), 8:56
citation.arabic_text: دُهْنُ اللَّيْلِ يَجْرِي فِي الْعُرُوقِ وَ يُرَوِّي الْبَشَرَةَ وَ يُبَيِّضُ الْوَجْهَ .
citation.translation: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Ibn Mahboub, from Abdullah Bin Sinan, from Abu Hamza, (It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘The oiling (massaging) at night flows in the veins and it irrigates the person (skin), and whitens the face’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: صحيح - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (22/427)

text: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Khalid, from his father, from Al Hassan Bin Bahr, from Mihzam Al Asady, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Whenever you take the oil upon your convenience, so say, ‘O Allah<sup>azwj</sup>! I ask You<sup>azwj</sup> for the grace and the beauty and the love, and I seek Refuge with You<sup>azwj</sup> from the disgrace, and the ugliness and the detestation’.

citation.chapter: The Book of Outfits and the Beautification and the Magnanimity (al-Kafi, vol 6), 8:56
citation.arabic_text: إِذَا أَخَذْتَ الدُّهْنَ عَلَى رَاحَتِكَ فَقُلِ اللَّهُمَّ إِنِّي أَسْأَلُكَ الزَّيْنَ وَ الزِّينَةَ وَ الْمَحَبَّةَ وَ أَعُوذُ بِكَ مِنَ الشَّيْنِ وَ الشَّنَآنِ وَ الْمَقْتِ ثُمَّ اجْعَلْهُ عَلَى يَأْفُوخِكَ ابْدَأْ بِمَا بَدَأَ اللَّهُ بِهِ .
citation.translation: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Khalid, from his father, from Al Hassan Bin Bahr, from Mihzam Al Asady, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Whenever you take the oil upon your convenience, so say, ‘O Allah<sup>azwj</sup>! I ask You<sup>azwj</sup> for the grace and the beauty and the love, and I seek Refuge with You<sup>azwj</sup> from the disgrace, and the ugliness and the detestation’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: مجهول - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (2/427)

text: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Muhammad Bin Ahmad Al Daqqan, from Muhammad Bin Ismail, from Salih Bin Uqba, from Bashir the masseur, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘The one who oils (massages) a Believer, Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Writes for him with every hair, a radiance on the Day of Judgement’.

citation.chapter: The Book of Outfits and the Beautification and the Magnanimity (al-Kafi, vol 6), 8:56
citation.arabic_text: مَنْ دَهَنَ مُؤْمِناً كَتَبَ اللَّهُ لَهُ بِكُلِّ شَعْرَةٍ نُوراً يَوْمَ الْقِيَامَةِ .
citation.translation: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Muhammad Bin Ahmad Al Daqqan, from Muhammad Bin Ismail, from Salih Bin Uqba, from Bashir the masseur, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘The one who oils (massages) a Believer, Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Writes for him with every hair, a radiance on the Day of Judgement’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: ضعيف على المشهور - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (22/428)

text: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Muhammad Bin Al Husayn, from Abdul Rahman Bin Abu Hashim, from Abu Khadeeja, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘The man should not oil (massage) every day. The man should look shaggier and he should not look smooth like a woman’.

citation.chapter: The Book of Outfits and the Beautification and the Magnanimity (al-Kafi, vol 6), 8:57
citation.arabic_text: لَا يَدَّهِنُ الرَّجُلُ كُلَّ يَوْمٍ يُرَى الرَّجُلُ شَعِثاً لَا يُرَى مُتَزَلِّقاً كَأَنَّهُ امْرَأَةٌ .
citation.translation: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Muhammad Bin Al Husayn, from Abdul Rahman Bin Abu Hashim, from Abu Khadeeja, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘The man should not oil (massage) every day. The man should look shaggier and he should not look smooth like a woman’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: مجهول - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (2/428)

text: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Muhammad Bin Sinan, from Is’haq Bin Ammar who said, ‘I said to Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, ‘I intermingle with the manly from the people and I have sufficed from the oil by the little bit, so I wipe with it every day’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘I<sup>asws</sup> do not like that for you’. So I said, ‘A day and not a day (alternatively)?’ So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘I<sup>asws</sup> do not like that for you’. I said, ‘One day, and not for two days?’ So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The Friday to the Friday, one day or two days’.

citation.chapter: The Book of Outfits and the Beautification and the Magnanimity (al-Kafi, vol 6), 8:57
citation.arabic_text: قُلْتُ لِأَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) أُخَالِطُ أَهْلَ الْمُرُوءَةِ مِنَ النَّاسِ وَ قَدْ أَكْتَفِي مِنَ الدُّهْنِ بِالْيَسِيرِ فَأَتَمَسَّحُ بِهِ كُلَّ يَوْمٍ فَقَالَ مَا أُحِبُّ لَكَ ذَلِكَ فَقُلْتُ يَوْمٌ وَ يَوْمٌ لَا فَقَالَ وَ مَا أُحِبُّ لَكَ ذَلِكَ قُلْتُ يَوْمٌ وَ يَوْمَيْنِ لَا فَقَالَ الْجُمُعَةُ إِلَى الْجُمُعَةِ يَوْمٌ وَ يَوْمَيْنِ .
citation.translation: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Muhammad Bin Sinan, from Is’haq Bin Ammar who said, ‘I said to Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, ‘I intermingle with the manly from the people and I have sufficed from the oil by the little bit, so I wipe with it every day’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘I<sup>asws</sup> do not like that for you’. So I said, ‘A day and not a day (alternatively)?’ So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘I<sup>asws</sup> do not like that for you’. I said, ‘One day, and not for two days?’ So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The Friday to the Friday, one day or two days’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: ضعيف على المشهور - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (22/428)

text: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Abu Abdullah, from Usman Bin Isa, from Is’haq Bin Jareer who said, ‘I said to Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, ‘How much shall I oil (massage)?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Once during every year’. So I said, ‘Then the people would look at me as a destitute’. So I did not cease bargaining with him<sup>asws</sup>, so he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘So in every month, once’, and he<sup>asws</sup> did not increase over it’.

citation.chapter: The Book of Outfits and the Beautification and the Magnanimity (al-Kafi, vol 6), 8:57
citation.arabic_text: قُلْتُ لِأَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) فِي كَمْ أَدَّهِنُ قَالَ فِي كُلِّ سَنَةٍ مَرَّةً فَقُلْتُ إِذَنْ يَرَى النَّاسُ بِي خَصَاصَةً فَلَمْ أَزَلْ أُمَاكِسُهُ فَقَالَ فَفِي كُلِّ شَهْرٍ مَرَّةً لَمْ يَزِدْنِي عَلَيْهَا .
citation.translation: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Abu Abdullah, from Usman Bin Isa, from Is’haq Bin Jareer who said, ‘I said to Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, ‘How much shall I oil (massage)?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Once during every year’. So I said, ‘Then the people would look at me as a destitute’. So I did not cease bargaining with him<sup>asws</sup>, so he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘So in every month, once’, and he<sup>asws</sup> did not increase over it’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: موثق - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (2/429)

text: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hisham Bin Al Hakam, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘The violet (oil) is the chief of your (massaging) oils’.

citation.chapter: The Book of Outfits and the Beautification and the Magnanimity (al-Kafi, vol 6), 8:58
citation.arabic_text: قَالَ الْبَنَفْسَجُ سَيِّدُ أَدْهَانِكُمْ .
citation.translation: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hisham Bin Al Hakam, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘The violet (oil) is the chief of your (massaging) oils’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: حسن - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (2/429)

text: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Ja’far Bin Muhammad Bin Abu Zayd Al Razy, from his father, from Salih Bin Uqba, from his father who said, ‘I gifted a mule to Abu Abdullahasws, so it dislodged the rider which I had sent along with it. So we went over to himasws and we entered Al-Medina. So we informed Abu Abdullahasws and heasws said: ‘Why don’t you make it sniff the violet (oil)?’ So I made it to sniff violet (oil) and it was cured. Then heasws said: ‘O Uqba! The violet (oil) is cold in the summer and hot in the winter, soft upon ourasws Shias, dry upon ourasws enemies. Had the people known what was in the violet (oil), they would have evaluated one Owqiya (a unit of measurement) of it, for one Dinar’.

citation.chapter: The Book of Outfits and the Beautification and the Magnanimity (al-Kafi, vol 6), 8:58
