citation.translation: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Abdullah Bin Ja’far, from Al Sayyari, raising it, said, ‘The Prophet<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘There is nothing better for the body than the lily oil, meaning the Jasmine flower’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: ضعيف - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (22/433)

text: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Al Abbas Bin Marouf, from Al Yaqouby, from Isa Bin Abdullah, (It has been narrated) from Ali son of Ja’farasws who said, ‘Abu Al-Hassan Musaasws used to sniff Al-Shaleysa (a perfume), and the lily in intense heat, (until it) dropped (drops from hisasws nose), and Al-Rezaasws as well sniffed with it’. So I said to Ali son of Ja’farasws, ‘Why is that?’ So Ali said, ‘I mentioned that to one of the physicians, so he mentioned that it is very good for the copulation’.

citation.chapter: The Book of Outfits and the Beautification and the Magnanimity (al-Kafi, vol 6), 8:61
citation.arabic_text: كَانَ أَبُو الْحَسَنِ مُوسَى ( عليه السلام ) يَسْتَعِطُ بِالشَّلِيثَا وَ بِالزَّنْبَقِ الشَّدِيدِ الْحَرِّ خَسْفَيْهِ قَالَ وَ كَانَ الرِّضَا ( عليه السلام ) أَيْضاً يَسْتَعِطُ بِهِ فَقُلْتُ لِعَلِيِّ بْنِ جَعْفَرٍ لِمَ ذَلِكَ فَقَالَ عَلِيٌّ ذَكَرْتُ ذَلِكَ لِبَعْضِ الْمُتَطَبِّبِينَ فَذَكَرَ أَنَّهُ جَيِّدٌ لِلْجِمَاعِ .
citation.translation: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Al Abbas Bin Marouf, from Al Yaqouby, from Isa Bin Abdullah, (It has been narrated) from Ali son of Ja’farasws who said, ‘Abu Al-Hassan Musaasws used to sniff Al-Shaleysa (a perfume), and the lily in intense heat, (until it) dropped (drops from hisasws nose), and Al-Rezaasws as well sniffed with it’. So I said to Ali son of Ja’farasws, ‘Why is that?’ So Ali said, ‘I mentioned that to one of the physicians, so he mentioned that it is very good for the copulation’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: مجهول - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (22/433)

text: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from someone else, from Al Khashaab, from Giyas Bin Kulyeb, from Is’haq Bin Ammar, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws that whenever Rasool-Allahsaww complained of his head (ache), would sniff the Al-Juljulaan oil, and it is the sesame’.

citation.chapter: The Book of Outfits and the Beautification and the Magnanimity (al-Kafi, vol 6), 8:62
citation.arabic_text: أَنَّ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ ( صلى الله عليه وآله ) كَانَ إِذَا اشْتَكَى رَأْسَهُ اسْتَعَطَ بِدُهْنِ الْجُلْجُلَانِ وَ هُوَ السِّمْسِمُ .
citation.translation: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from someone else, from Al Khashaab, from Giyas Bin Kulyeb, from Is’haq Bin Ammar, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws that whenever Rasool-Allahsaww complained of his head (ache), would sniff the Al-Juljulaan oil, and it is the sesame’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: حسن كالموثق - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (22/434)

text: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Abu Abdullah, from one of his companions, from a cousin of Al Wazaie, from Mas’ada Bin Al Yas’a, from Qays Al Bahily, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> that the Prophet<sup>saww</sup> used to love smelling the sesame oil’.

citation.chapter: The Book of Outfits and the Beautification and the Magnanimity (al-Kafi, vol 6), 8:62
citation.arabic_text: أَنَّ النَّبِيَّ ( صلى الله عليه وآله ) كَانَ يُحِبُّ أَنْ يَسْتَعِطَ بِدُهْنِ السِّمْسِمِ .
citation.translation: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Abu Abdullah, from one of his companions, from a cousin of Al Wazaie, from Mas’ada Bin Al Yas’a, from Qays Al Bahily, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> that the Prophet<sup>saww</sup> used to love smelling the sesame oil’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: مجهول مرسل - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (2/434)

text: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, and Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Khalid, altogether from Ibn Mahboub, from Ibrahim Bin Mihzam, from Talha Bin Zayd, from the one who raised it, said, ‘The Prophet<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘Whenever one of you is brought the basil, so let him smell it and place it upon his eyes, for it is from the Paradise, and whenever one of you is brought it, so let him not reject it’.

citation.chapter: The Book of Outfits and the Beautification and the Magnanimity (al-Kafi, vol 6), 8:63
citation.arabic_text: قَالَ النَّبِيُّ ( صلى الله عليه وآله ) إِذَا أُتِيَ أَحَدُكُمْ بِرَيْحَانٍ فَلْيَشَمَّهُ وَ لْيَضَعْهُ عَلَى عَيْنَيْهِ فَإِنَّهُ مِنَ الْجَنَّةِ وَ إِذَا أُتِيَ أَحَدُكُمْ بِهِ فَلَا يَرُدَّهُ .
citation.translation: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, and Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Khalid, altogether from Ibn Mahboub, from Ibrahim Bin Mihzam, from Talha Bin Zayd, from the one who raised it, said, ‘The Prophet<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘Whenever one of you is brought the basil, so let him smell it and place it upon his eyes, for it is from the Paradise, and whenever one of you is brought it, so let him not reject it’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: مرفوع - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (22/435)

text: Ibn Mahboub, from Abdullah Bin Sinan who said, ‘Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Whenever one of you is brought the basil, so let him smell it, and let him place it upon his eyes, for it is from the Paradise’.

citation.chapter: The Book of Outfits and the Beautification and the Magnanimity (al-Kafi, vol 6), 8:63
citation.arabic_text: قَالَ أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) إِذَا أُتِيَ أَحَدُكُمْ بِالرَّيْحَانِ فَلْيَشَمَّهُ وَ لْيَضَعْهُ عَلَى عَيْنَيْهِ فَإِنَّهُ مِنَ الْجَنَّةِ .
citation.translation: Ibn Mahboub, from Abdullah Bin Sinan who said, ‘Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Whenever one of you is brought the basil, so let him smell it, and let him place it upon his eyes, for it is from the Paradise’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: صحيح - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (22/435)

text: Muhammad Bin Yahya, raising it, said, ‘Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The basil is of twenty one types, the chief of it is the myrtle’.

citation.chapter: The Book of Outfits and the Beautification and the Magnanimity (al-Kafi, vol 6), 8:63
citation.arabic_text: قَالَ أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) الرَّيْحَانُ وَاحِدٌ وَ عِشْرُونَ نَوْعاً سَيِّدُهَا الْآسُ .
citation.translation: Muhammad Bin Yahya, raising it, said, ‘Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The basil is of twenty one types, the chief of it is the myrtle’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: مرفوع - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (2/435)

text: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Abu Abdullah, from Al Hassan Bin Ali Bin Yaqteen, from Yunus Bin Yaqoub who said, ‘I went over to Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> and in his<sup>asws</sup> hand was a dyeing-box wherein was basil’.

citation.chapter: The Book of Outfits and the Beautification and the Magnanimity (al-Kafi, vol 6), 8:63
citation.arabic_text: دَخَلْتُ عَلَى أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) وَ فِي يَدِهِ مِخْضَبَةٌ فِيهَا رَيْحَانٌ .
citation.translation: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Abu Abdullah, from Al Hassan Bin Ali Bin Yaqteen, from Yunus Bin Yaqoub who said, ‘I went over to Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> and in his<sup>asws</sup> hand was a dyeing-box wherein was basil’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: موثق - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (2/435)

text: Ali Bin Muhammad, from one of his companions, form Abu Hashim Al Ja’fary who said, ‘I went over to Abu Al Hassanasws the owner of the army (Saahib Al-Askarasws), so there came a child from hisasws children and gave him a rose. So heasws kissed it and placed it upon hisasws eyes, then gave it to me and said: ‘O Abu Hashim! The one who grabs a rose or basil should kiss it and place it upon his eyes, then send Blessings upon Muhammadsaww and the Progenyasws of Muhammadsaww, the Imamsasws, Allahazwj would Write for him the rewards similar to the sands of the wilderness, and delete the sins from him similar to that’.

citation.chapter: The Book of Outfits and the Beautification and the Magnanimity (al-Kafi, vol 6), 8:63
citation.arabic_text: دَخَلْتُ عَلَى أَبِي الْحَسَنِ صَاحِبِ الْعَسْكَرِ ( عليه السلام ) فَجَاءَ صَبِيٌّ مِنْ صِبْيَانِهِ فَنَاوَلَهُ وَرْدَةً فَقَبَّلَهَا وَ وَضَعَهَا عَلَى عَيْنَيْهِ ثُمَّ نَاوَلَنِيهَا وَ قَالَ يَا أَبَا هَاشِمٍ مَنْ تَنَاوَلَ وَرْدَةً أَوْ رَيْحَانَةً فَقَبَّلَهَا وَ وَضَعَهَا عَلَى عَيْنَيْهِ ثُمَّ صَلَّى عَلَى مُحَمَّدٍ وَ آلِ مُحَمَّدٍ الْأَئِمَّةِ كَتَبَ اللَّهُ لَهُ الْحَسَنَاتِ مِثْلَ رَمْلِ عَالِجٍ وَ مَحَا عَنْهُ مِنَ السَّيِّئَاتِ مِثْلَ ذَلِكَ .
citation.translation: Ali Bin Muhammad, from one of his companions, form Abu Hashim Al Ja’fary who said, ‘I went over to Abu Al Hassanasws the owner of the army (Saahib Al-Askarasws), so there came a child from hisasws children and gave him a rose. So heasws kissed it and placed it upon hisasws eyes, then gave it to me and said: ‘O Abu Hashim! The one who grabs a rose or basil should kiss it and place it upon his eyes, then send Blessings upon Muhammadsaww and the Progenyasws of Muhammadsaww, the Imamsasws, Allahazwj would Write for him the rewards similar to the sands of the wilderness, and delete the sins from him similar to that’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: مرسل - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (22/435)

text: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad Bin Ismail, from Al Fazl Bin Shazaan, altogether, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hisham Bin Al Hakam, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘From the happiness is the spaciousness of the home’.

citation.chapter: The Book of Outfits and the Beautification and the Magnanimity (al-Kafi, vol 6), 8:64
citation.arabic_text: مِنَ السَّعَادَةِ سَعَةُ الْمَنْزِلِ .
citation.translation: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad Bin Ismail, from Al Fazl Bin Shazaan, altogether, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hisham Bin Al Hakam, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘From the happiness is the spaciousness of the home’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: حسن كالصحيح - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (2/436)

text: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Moamar Bin Khallad who said, ‘Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> bought a house and ordered a slave of his<sup>asws</sup> that he transfers to it and said: ‘Your home is narrow’. So he said, ‘My father had built the house’. So Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘If your father was stupid is it befitting that you become similar to him?’

citation.chapter: The Book of Outfits and the Beautification and the Magnanimity (al-Kafi, vol 6), 8:64
citation.arabic_text: إِنَّ أَبَا الْحَسَنِ ( عليه السلام ) اشْتَرَى دَاراً وَ أَمَرَ مَوْلًى لَهُ أَنْ يَتَحَوَّلَ إِلَيْهَا وَ قَالَ إِنَّ مَنْزِلَكَ ضَيِّقٌ فَقَالَ قَدْ أَحْدَثَ هَذِهِ الدَّارَ أَبِي فَقَالَ أَبُو الْحَسَنِ ( عليه السلام ) إِنْ كَانَ أَبُوكَ أَحْمَقَ يَنْبَغِي أَنْ تَكُونَ مِثْلَهُ .
citation.translation: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Moamar Bin Khallad who said, ‘Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> bought a house and ordered a slave of his<sup>asws</sup> that he transfers to it and said: ‘Your home is narrow’. So he said, ‘My father had built the house’. So Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘If your father was stupid is it befitting that you become similar to him?’
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: صحيح - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (2/436)

text: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad and Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, altogether from Saeed Bin Janah, from Mutarraf, a slave of Ma’an, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘There are three (things) which are a best for the Believer – a spacious house to cover his nakedness and his evil state with from the people, and a righteous woman supporting him upon the affairs of the world and the Hereafter, and a daughter or a sister exiting her from his home either when he dies or by getting her married off’.

citation.chapter: The Book of Outfits and the Beautification and the Magnanimity (al-Kafi, vol 6), 8:64
citation.arabic_text: ثَلَاثَةٌ لِلْمُؤْمِنِ فِيهَا رَاحَةٌ دَارٌ وَاسِعَةٌ تُوَارِي عَوْرَتَهُ وَ سُوءَ حَالِهِ مِنَ النَّاسِ وَ امْرَأَةٌ صَالِحَةٌ تُعِينُهُ عَلَى أَمْرِ الدُّنْيَا وَ الْآخِرَةِ وَ ابْنَةٌ أَوْ أُخْتٌ يُخْرِجُهَا مِنْ مَنْزِلِهِ إِمَّا بِمَوْتٍ أَوْ بِتَزَوُّجٍ .
citation.translation: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad and Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, altogether from Saeed Bin Janah, from Mutarraf, a slave of Ma’an, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘There are three (things) which are a best for the Believer – a spacious house to cover his nakedness and his evil state with from the people, and a righteous woman supporting him upon the affairs of the world and the Hereafter, and a daughter or a sister exiting her from his home either when he dies or by getting her married off’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: مجهول - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (2/436)

text: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Abu Abdullah, from Nuh Bin Shuayb, from Suleyman Bin Rusheyd, from his father, from Bashir who said, ‘I heard Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> saying: ‘The good life is in the spaciousness of the home, and the graciousness regarding the servants’.

citation.chapter: The Book of Outfits and the Beautification and the Magnanimity (al-Kafi, vol 6), 8:64
citation.arabic_text: سَمِعْتُ أَبَا الْحَسَنِ ( عليه السلام ) يَقُولُ الْعَيْشُ السَّعَةُ فِي الْمَنَازِلِ وَ الْفَضْلُ فِي الْخَدَمِ .
citation.translation: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Abu Abdullah, from Nuh Bin Shuayb, from Suleyman Bin Rusheyd, from his father, from Bashir who said, ‘I heard Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> saying: ‘The good life is in the spaciousness of the home, and the graciousness regarding the servants’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: مجهول - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (22/437)

text: From him, from Mansour Bin Al Abbas, from Saeed, from someone else, ‘Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> was asked about the gracious living of the world. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Spaciousness of the home and the abundance of those that love you’.

citation.chapter: The Book of Outfits and the Beautification and the Magnanimity (al-Kafi, vol 6), 8:64
citation.arabic_text: سَعَةُ الْمَنْزِلِ وَ كَثْرَةُ الْمُحِبِّينَ .
citation.translation: From him, from Mansour Bin Al Abbas, from Saeed, from someone else, ‘Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> was asked about the gracious living of the world. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Spaciousness of the home and the abundance of those that love you’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: ضعيف - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (2/437)

text: Abu Ali Al Ashary, from Muhammad Bin Abdul Jabbar, from Muhammad Bin Ismail, from Ibrahim Bin Abu Al Balaad, from Ali Bin Abu Al Mugheira, (It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘From a miserable living, is a narrow home’.

citation.chapter: The Book of Outfits and the Beautification and the Magnanimity (al-Kafi, vol 6), 8:64
citation.arabic_text: مِنْ شَقَاءِ الْعَيْشِ ضِيقُ الْمَنْزِلِ .
citation.translation: Abu Ali Al Ashary, from Muhammad Bin Abdul Jabbar, from Muhammad Bin Ismail, from Ibrahim Bin Abu Al Balaad, from Ali Bin Abu Al Mugheira, (It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘From a miserable living, is a narrow home’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: كالصحيح - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (22/437)

text: Ali Bin Ibrahim, form his father, from Al Nowfaly, from Al Sakuny, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘From happiness of the Muslim person is the spacious dwelling’.

citation.chapter: The Book of Outfits and the Beautification and the Magnanimity (al-Kafi, vol 6), 8:64
citation.arabic_text: قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ ( صلى الله عليه وآله ) مِنْ سَعَادَةِ الْمَرْءِ الْمُسْلِمِ الْمَسْكَنُ الْوَاسِعُ .
citation.translation: Ali Bin Ibrahim, form his father, from Al Nowfaly, from Al Sakuny, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘From happiness of the Muslim person is the spacious dwelling’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: ضعيف على المشهور - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (2/437)

text: And by this chain, said, ‘A man from the helpers complained to Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> that the houses had congested him. So the Prophet<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘Raise your voice as much as you can and ask Allah<sup>azwj</sup> that He<sup>azwj</sup> Makes it spacious for you’.

citation.chapter: The Book of Outfits and the Beautification and the Magnanimity (al-Kafi, vol 6), 8:64
citation.arabic_text: وَ بِهَذَا الْإِسْنَادِ قَالَ شَكَا رَجُلٌ مِنَ الْأَنْصَارِ إِلَى رَسُولِ اللَّهِ ( صلى الله عليه وآله ) أَنَّ الدُّورَ قَدِ اكْتَنَفَتْهُ فَقَالَ النَّبِيُّ ( صلى الله عليه وآله ) ارْفَعْ صَوْتَكَ مَا اسْتَطَعْتَ وَ سَلِ اللَّهَ أَنْ يُوَسِّعَ عَلَيْكَ .
citation.translation: And by this chain, said, ‘A man from the helpers complained to Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> that the houses had congested him. So the Prophet<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘Raise your voice as much as you can and ask Allah<sup>azwj</sup> that He<sup>azwj</sup> Makes it spacious for you’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: ضعيف على المشهور - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (2/437)

text: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Muhammad Bin Khalid and Al Husayn Bin Saeed, from Al Qasim Bin Muhammad Al Jowhary, from Ali Bin Abu Hamza, from Abu Baseer, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘Jibraeel<sup>as</sup> came unto me<sup>saww</sup> and said: ‘O Muhammad<sup>saww</sup>! Your<sup>saww</sup> Lord<sup>azwj</sup> Conveys the Greetings and Forbids from decorating the houses’. Abu Baseer said, ‘So I said, ‘What is the decoration of the houses?’ So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Pictures and the statues’.

citation.chapter: The Book of Outfits and the Beautification and the Magnanimity (al-Kafi, vol 6), 8:65
citation.arabic_text: قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ ( صلى الله عليه وآله ) أَتَانِي جَبْرَئِيلُ وَ قَالَ يَا مُحَمَّدُ إِنَّ رَبَّكَ يُقْرِئُكَ السَّلَامَ وَ يَنْهَى عَنْ تَزْوِيقِ الْبُيُوتِ قَالَ أَبُو بَصِيرٍ فَقُلْتُ مَا تَزْوِيقُ الْبُيُوتِ فَقَالَ تَصَاوِيرُ التَّمَاثِيلِ .
citation.translation: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Muhammad Bin Khalid and Al Husayn Bin Saeed, from Al Qasim Bin Muhammad Al Jowhary, from Ali Bin Abu Hamza, from Abu Baseer, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘Jibraeel<sup>as</sup> came unto me<sup>saww</sup> and said: ‘O Muhammad<sup>saww</sup>! Your<sup>saww</sup> Lord<sup>azwj</sup> Conveys the Greetings and Forbids from decorating the houses’. Abu Baseer said, ‘So I said, ‘What is the decoration of the houses?’ So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Pictures and the statues’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: ضعيف - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (22/437)

text: Abu Ali Al Ashary, from Muhammad Bin Abdul Jabbar, from Safwan Bin yahya, from Ibn Muskan, from Muhammad Bin Marwan, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘Jibraeel<sup>as</sup> came unto me<sup>saww</sup>, so he<sup>as</sup> said: ‘We, the group of Angels neither enter a house in which is a dog, nor any statue of a body, nor a utensil in which is urine’.

citation.chapter: The Book of Outfits and the Beautification and the Magnanimity (al-Kafi, vol 6), 8:65
citation.arabic_text: قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ ( صلى الله عليه وآله ) إِنَّ جَبْرَئِيلَ ( عليه السلام ) أَتَانِي فَقَالَ إِنَّا مَعَاشِرَ الْمَلَائِكَةِ لَا نَدْخُلُ بَيْتاً فِيهِ كَلْبٌ وَ لَا تِمْثَالُ جَسَدٍ وَ لَا إِنَاءٌ يُبَالُ فِيهِ .
citation.translation: Abu Ali Al Ashary, from Muhammad Bin Abdul Jabbar, from Safwan Bin yahya, from Ibn Muskan, from Muhammad Bin Marwan, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘Jibraeel<sup>as</sup> came unto me<sup>saww</sup>, so he<sup>as</sup> said: ‘We, the group of Angels neither enter a house in which is a dog, nor any statue of a body, nor a utensil in which is urine’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: مجهول - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (2/438)

text: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Abdullah Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Ali Bin Al Hakam, from Aban Bin Usman, from Abu Baseer, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Jibraeel<sup>as</sup> said: ‘We (the Angels) neither enter a house in which there is a picture, nor a dog, meaning pictures of the humans, nor a house wherein are statues’.

citation.chapter: The Book of Outfits and the Beautification and the Magnanimity (al-Kafi, vol 6), 8:65
citation.arabic_text: إِنَّ جَبْرَئِيلَ ( عليه السلام ) قَالَ إِنَّا لَا نَدْخُلُ بَيْتاً فِيهِ صُورَةٌ وَ لَا كَلْبٌ يَعْنِي صُورَةَ الْإِنْسَانِ وَ لَا بَيْتاً فِيهِ تَمَاثِيلُ .
citation.translation: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Abdullah Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Ali Bin Al Hakam, from Aban Bin Usman, from Abu Baseer, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Jibraeel<sup>as</sup> said: ‘We (the Angels) neither enter a house in which there is a picture, nor a dog, meaning pictures of the humans, nor a house wherein are statues’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: مجهول - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (22/438)

text: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from a man, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘The one who carves a statue would be brought on the Day of Judgement (in front of the carving) and he (the carver will be asked to) blow the spirit into it (to bring it to life)’.

citation.chapter: The Book of Outfits and the Beautification and the Magnanimity (al-Kafi, vol 6), 8:65
citation.arabic_text: مَنْ مَثَّلَ تِمْثَالًا كُلِّفَ يَوْمَ الْقِيَامَةِ أَنْ يَنْفُخَ فِيهِ الرُّوحَ .
citation.translation: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from a man, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘The one who carves a statue would be brought on the Day of Judgement (in front of the carving) and he (the carver will be asked to) blow the spirit into it (to bring it to life)’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: حسن - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (22/438)

text: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Al Musna, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said that Ali<sup>asws</sup> disliked the pictures in the houses’.

citation.chapter: The Book of Outfits and the Beautification and the Magnanimity (al-Kafi, vol 6), 8:65
citation.arabic_text: إِنَّ عَلِيّاً ( عليه السلام ) كَرِهَ الصُّورَةَ فِي الْبُيُوتِ .
citation.translation: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Al Musna, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said that Ali<sup>asws</sup> disliked the pictures in the houses’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: حسن - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (22/438)

text: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Khalid, from Usman Bin Isa, from Sama’at, from Abu Baseer, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, said, ‘I asked him<sup>asws</sup> about the pillows and the rugs wherein happen to be the resemblances. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘There is no problem with it if it happens to be in the house’. I said, ‘The resemblances?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Everything which is trampled, so there is no problem with it’.

citation.chapter: The Book of Outfits and the Beautification and the Magnanimity (al-Kafi, vol 6), 8:65
citation.arabic_text: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنِ الْوِسَادَةِ وَ الْبِسَاطِ يَكُونُ فِيهِ التَّمَاثِيلُ فَقَالَ لَا بَأْسَ بِهِ يَكُونُ فِي الْبَيْتِ قُلْتُ التَّمَاثِيلُ فَقَالَ كُلُّ شَيْ‏ءٍ يُوطَأُ فَلَا بَأْسَ بِهِ .
citation.translation: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Khalid, from Usman Bin Isa, from Sama’at, from Abu Baseer, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, said, ‘I asked him<sup>asws</sup> about the pillows and the rugs wherein happen to be the resemblances. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘There is no problem with it if it happens to be in the house’. I said, ‘The resemblances?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Everything which is trampled, so there is no problem with it’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: موثق - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (22/439)

text: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad and Abdullah, two sons of Muhammad Bin Isa, from Ali Bin Al Hakam, from Aban Bin Usman, from Abu Al Abbas, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws regarding the Words of Allahazwj Mighty and Majestic [34:13] They made for him whatsoever he desired of Prayer Niches, and images. So heasws said: ‘By Allahazwj! These were not images of the men and the women, but these were the trees and the likes of it’.

citation.chapter: The Book of Outfits and the Beautification and the Magnanimity (al-Kafi, vol 6), 8:65
citation.arabic_text: اللَّهِ عَزَّ وَ جَلَّ يَعْمَلُونَ لَهُ ما يَشاءُ مِنْ مَحارِيبَ وَ تَماثِيلَ فَقَالَ وَ اللَّهِ مَا هِيَ تَمَاثِيلَ الرِّجَالِ وَ النِّسَاءِ وَ لَكِنَّهَا الشَّجَرُ وَ شِبْهُهُ .
citation.translation: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad and Abdullah, two sons of Muhammad Bin Isa, from Ali Bin Al Hakam, from Aban Bin Usman, from Abu Al Abbas, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws regarding the Words of Allahazwj Mighty and Majestic [34:13] They made for him whatsoever he desired of Prayer Niches, and images. So heasws said: ‘By Allahazwj! These were not images of the men and the women, but these were the trees and the likes of it’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: موثق كالصحيح - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (2/439)

text: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Jameel Bin Darraj, from Zurara Bin Ayn, (It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘There is no problem if there happen to be the resemblances in the houses when its heads are changed from it and it is left, what is besides that’.

citation.chapter: The Book of Outfits and the Beautification and the Magnanimity (al-Kafi, vol 6), 8:65
citation.arabic_text: لَا بَأْسَ بِأَنْ يَكُونَ التَّمَاثِيلُ فِي الْبُيُوتِ إِذَا غُيِّرَتْ رُءُوسُهَا مِنْهَا وَ تُرِكَ مَا سِوَى ذَلِكَ .
citation.translation: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Jameel Bin Darraj, from Zurara Bin Ayn, (It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘There is no problem if there happen to be the resemblances in the houses when its heads are changed from it and it is left, what is besides that’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: حسن - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (2/439)

text: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Al Amraky Bin Ali, (It has been narrated) from Ali son of Ja’far<sup>asws</sup>, from Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup>, said, ‘I asked him<sup>asws</sup> about the house and the chamber wherein are the resemblances, can one Pray in it?’ So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Do not Pray in it and therein is something facing you, except if it is inevitable then you can cut-off its heads, or else do not Pray in it’.

citation.chapter: The Book of Outfits and the Beautification and the Magnanimity (al-Kafi, vol 6), 8:65
citation.arabic_text: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنِ الدَّارِ وَ الْحُجْرَةِ فِيهَا التَّمَاثِيلُ أَ يُصَلَّى فِيهَا فَقَالَ لَا تُصَلِّ فِيهَا وَ فِيهَا شَيْ‏ءٌ يَسْتَقْبِلُكَ إِلَّا أَنْ لَا تَجِدَ بُدّاً فَتَقْطَعَ رُءُوسَهَا وَ إِلَّا فَلَا تُصَلِّ فِيهَا .
citation.translation: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Al Amraky Bin Ali, (It has been narrated) from Ali son of Ja’far<sup>asws</sup>, from Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup>, said, ‘I asked him<sup>asws</sup> about the house and the chamber wherein are the resemblances, can one Pray in it?’ So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Do not Pray in it and therein is something facing you, except if it is inevitable then you can cut-off its heads, or else do not Pray in it’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: صحيح - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (2/440)

text: Abu Ali Al Ashary, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, and Humeyd Bin Ziyad, from Al Hassan Bin Muhammad Bin Sama’at, altogether from Ahmad Bin Al Hassan Al Maysmi, from Aban Bin Usman, from Al Husayn Bin Al Munzar who said, ‘Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Three would be Punished on the Day of Judgement – a man who lied regarding his dream, he would be Encumbered to tie a knot between two grains, and he would not be able to tie a knot between the two; and a man who images resemblances, he would be Encumbered that he blows (a spirit) into it, and he would not be able to blow into it’. (P.s. – the description of the third is missing).

citation.chapter: The Book of Outfits and the Beautification and the Magnanimity (al-Kafi, vol 6), 8:65
citation.arabic_text: قَالَ أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) ثَلَاثَةٌ مُعَذَّبُونَ يَوْمَ الْقِيَامَةِ رَجُلٌ كَذَبَ فِي رُؤْيَاهُ يُكَلَّفُ أَنْ يَعْقِدَ بَيْنَ شَعِيرَتَيْنِ وَ لَيْسَ بِعَاقِدٍ بَيْنَهُمَا وَ رَجُلٌ صَوَّرَ تَمَاثِيلَ يُكَلَّفُ أَنْ يَنْفُخَ فِيهَا وَ لَيْسَ بِنَافِخٍ .
citation.translation: Abu Ali Al Ashary, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, and Humeyd Bin Ziyad, from Al Hassan Bin Muhammad Bin Sama’at, altogether from Ahmad Bin Al Hassan Al Maysmi, from Aban Bin Usman, from Al Husayn Bin Al Munzar who said, ‘Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Three would be Punished on the Day of Judgement – a man who lied regarding his dream, he would be Encumbered to tie a knot between two grains, and he would not be able to tie a knot between the two; and a man who images resemblances, he would be Encumbered that he blows (a spirit) into it, and he would not be able to blow into it’. (P.s. – the description of the third is missing).
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: حسن أو موثق - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (2/440)

text: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Ja’far Bin Muhammad Al Ashary, from Ibn Al Qaddah, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> sent me<sup>asws</sup> regarding the demolishing of the graves and breaking of the pictures’.

citation.chapter: The Book of Outfits and the Beautification and the Magnanimity (al-Kafi, vol 6), 8:65
citation.arabic_text: قَالَ أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ ( عليه السلام ) بَعَثَنِي رَسُولُ اللَّهِ ( صلى الله عليه وآله ) فِي هَدْمِ الْقُبُورِ وَ كَسْرِ الصُّوَرِ .
citation.translation: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Ja’far Bin Muhammad Al Ashary, from Ibn Al Qaddah, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> sent me<sup>asws</sup> regarding the demolishing of the graves and breaking of the pictures’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: ضعيف على المشهور - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (2/440)

text: Humeyd Bin Ziyad, from Al Hassan Bin Muhammad Bin Sama’at, from someone else, from Aban Bin Usman, from Amro Bin Khalid, (It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Jibraeel<sup>as</sup> said: ‘O Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup>! We (Angels) neither enter a house wherein is a picture of a human, nor a house which has been urinated in, nor a house in which is a dog’.

citation.chapter: The Book of Outfits and the Beautification and the Magnanimity (al-Kafi, vol 6), 8:65
citation.arabic_text: قَالَ جَبْرَئِيلُ ( عليه السلام ) يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ إِنَّا لَا نَدْخُلُ بَيْتاً فِيهِ صُورَةُ إِنْسَانٍ وَ لَا بَيْتاً يُبَالُ فِيهِ وَ لَا بَيْتاً فِيهِ كَلْبٌ .
citation.translation: Humeyd Bin Ziyad, from Al Hassan Bin Muhammad Bin Sama’at, from someone else, from Aban Bin Usman, from Amro Bin Khalid, (It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Jibraeel<sup>as</sup> said: ‘O Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup>! We (Angels) neither enter a house wherein is a picture of a human, nor a house which has been urinated in, nor a house in which is a dog’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: ضعيف - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (22/440)

text: Abu Ali Al Ashary, from Muhammad Bin Salim, from Ahmad Bin Al Nazar, from Amro Bin Shimr, from Jabir, from Abdullah Bin Yahya Al Kindy, (It has been narrated) from his father, and he was in charge of providing water for the ablution for Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup>, said, ‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘Jibraeel<sup>as</sup> said: ‘We (Angels) neither enter a house wherein are resemblances not trampled’. The Hadeeth is shortened.

citation.chapter: The Book of Outfits and the Beautification and the Magnanimity (al-Kafi, vol 6), 8:65
citation.arabic_text: قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ ( صلى الله عليه وآله ) قَالَ جَبْرَئِيلُ ( عليه السلام ) إِنَّا لَا نَدْخُلُ بَيْتاً فِيهِ تِمْثَالٌ لَا يُوطَأُ . الْحَدِيثُ مُخْتَصَرٌ .
citation.translation: Abu Ali Al Ashary, from Muhammad Bin Salim, from Ahmad Bin Al Nazar, from Amro Bin Shimr, from Jabir, from Abdullah Bin Yahya Al Kindy, (It has been narrated) from his father, and he was in charge of providing water for the ablution for Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup>, said, ‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘Jibraeel<sup>as</sup> said: ‘We (Angels) neither enter a house wherein are resemblances not trampled’. The Hadeeth is shortened.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: ضعيف - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (2/441)

text: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Al Nowfaly, from Al Sakuny, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> sent me<sup>asws</sup> to Al-Medina, so he<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘Neither leave any picture except delete it, nor any grave except even it, nor a dog except kill it’.

citation.chapter: The Book of Outfits and the Beautification and the Magnanimity (al-Kafi, vol 6), 8:65
citation.arabic_text: قَالَ أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ ( عليه السلام ) بَعَثَنِي رَسُولُ اللَّهِ ( صلى الله عليه وآله ) إِلَى الْمَدِينَةِ فَقَالَ لَا تَدَعْ صُورَةً إِلَّا مَحَوْتَهَا وَ لَا قَبْراً إِلَّا سَوَّيْتَهُ وَ لَا كَلْباً إِلَّا قَتَلْتَهُ .
citation.translation: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Al Nowfaly, from Al Sakuny, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> sent me<sup>asws</sup> to Al-Medina, so he<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘Neither leave any picture except delete it, nor any grave except even it, nor a dog except kill it’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: ضعيف على المشهور - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (2/441)

text: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Khalid, from his father, from Abdullah Bin Al Fazl Al Nowfaly, from Ziyad Bin Amro Al Ju’fy, from the one who narrated it, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic has Allocated an Angel with the construction, saying to the one who raises a roof above eighty cubits: ‘Where are you intending (to go to), O wicked one?’

citation.chapter: The Book of Outfits and the Beautification and the Magnanimity (al-Kafi, vol 6), 8:66
citation.arabic_text: إِنَّ اللَّهَ عَزَّ وَ جَلَّ وَكَّلَ مَلَكاً بِالْبِنَاءِ يَقُولُ لِمَنْ رَفَعَ سَقْفاً فَوْقَ ثَمَانِيَةِ أَذْرُعٍ أَيْنَ تُرِيدُ يَا فَاسِقُ .
citation.translation: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Khalid, from his father, from Abdullah Bin Al Fazl Al Nowfaly, from Ziyad Bin Amro Al Ju’fy, from the one who narrated it, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic has Allocated an Angel with the construction, saying to the one who raises a roof above eighty cubits: ‘Where are you intending (to go to), O wicked one?’
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: مجهول مرسل - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (22/441)

text: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hisham Bin Al Hakam, and someone else, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘When the ceiling of the room is above seven cubits’, or said: ‘eight cubits, what is above the seven and the eight cubits is a meeting place’, and some of them said, ‘He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘A dwelling (for Satan<sup>la</sup>)’’.

citation.chapter: The Book of Outfits and the Beautification and the Magnanimity (al-Kafi, vol 6), 8:66
citation.arabic_text: إِذَا كَانَ سَمْكُ الْبَيْتِ فَوْقَ سَبْعَةِ أَذْرُعٍ أَوْ قَالَ ثَمَانِيَةِ أَذْرُعٍ فَكَانَ مَا فَوْقَ السَّبْعِ وَ الثَّمَانِ الْأَذْرُعِ مُحْتَضَراً وَ قَالَ بَعْضُهُمْ مَسْكُوناً .
citation.translation: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hisham Bin Al Hakam, and someone else, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘When the ceiling of the room is above seven cubits’, or said: ‘eight cubits, what is above the seven and the eight cubits is a meeting place’, and some of them said, ‘He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘A dwelling (for Satan<sup>la</sup>)’’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: حسن - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (22/441)

text: Ali Bin Ibrahim, and a number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Abu Abdullah, and Sahl Bin Ziyad, altogether, from Muhammad Bin Isa, from Abu Muhammad Al Ansary, from Aban Bin Usman, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws having said: ‘A man complained to himasws of the bad treatment of the people of the land with his family and his children. So heasws said: ‘How much (height) is the ceiling of your house’. So heasws said: ‘Ten cubits’. So heasws said : ‘Measure out eight cubits, then write the Verse of the Chair [2:255] in what is between the eight to the ten, just as you go around. So in each of the rooms, it its ceiling is higher than eight cubits, so it is a meeting place, the Jinn being present in it, and in it would become its dwelling’.

citation.chapter: The Book of Outfits and the Beautification and the Magnanimity (al-Kafi, vol 6), 8:66
citation.arabic_text: شَكَا إِلَيْهِ رَجُلٌ عَبَثَ أَهْلِ الْأَرْضِ بِأَهْلِ بَيْتِهِ وَ بِعِيَالِهِ فَقَالَ كَمْ سَقْفُ بَيْتِكَ فَقَالَ عَشَرَةُ أَذْرُعٍ فَقَالَ اذْرَعْ ثَمَانِيَةَ أَذْرُعٍ ثُمَّ اكْتُبْ آيَةَ الْكُرْسِيِّ فِيمَا بَيْنَ الثَّمَانِيَةِ إِلَى الْعَشَرَةِ كَمَا تَدُورُ فَإِنَّ كُلَّ بَيْتٍ سَمْكُهُ أَكْثَرُ مِنْ ثَمَانِيَةِ أَذْرُعٍ فَهُوَ مُحْتَضَرٌ تَحْضُرُهُ الْجِنُّ يَكُونُ فِيهِ مَسْكَنُهُ .
citation.translation: Ali Bin Ibrahim, and a number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Abu Abdullah, and Sahl Bin Ziyad, altogether, from Muhammad Bin Isa, from Abu Muhammad Al Ansary, from Aban Bin Usman, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws having said: ‘A man complained to himasws of the bad treatment of the people of the land with his family and his children. So heasws said: ‘How much (height) is the ceiling of your house’. So heasws said: ‘Ten cubits’. So heasws said : ‘Measure out eight cubits, then write the Verse of the Chair [2:255] in what is between the eight to the ten, just as you go around. So in each of the rooms, it its ceiling is higher than eight cubits, so it is a meeting place, the Jinn being present in it, and in it would become its dwelling’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: حسن - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (22/442)

text: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ismail Bin Marrar, and Ahmad Bin Abu Abdullah, from his father, altogether from Yunus, from the one who mentioned it, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws having said regarding a ceiling of the house when it is raised to eight cubits, it would be a dwelling. So when it exceeds eight, so let him write at the top of the eight, the Verse of the Chair [2:255]’.

citation.chapter: The Book of Outfits and the Beautification and the Magnanimity (al-Kafi, vol 6), 8:66
citation.arabic_text: فِي سَمْكِ الْبَيْتِ إِذَا رُفِعَ ثَمَانِيَةَ أَذْرُعٍ كَانَ مَسْكُوناً فَإِذَا زَادَ عَلَى ثَمَانِيَةٍ فَلْيُكْتَبْ عَلَى رَأْسِ الثَّمَانِ آيَةُ الْكُرْسِيِّ .
citation.translation: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ismail Bin Marrar, and Ahmad Bin Abu Abdullah, from his father, altogether from Yunus, from the one who mentioned it, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws having said regarding a ceiling of the house when it is raised to eight cubits, it would be a dwelling. So when it exceeds eight, so let him write at the top of the eight, the Verse of the Chair [2:255]’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: مرسل - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (2/442)

text: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Abu Abdullah, from Muhammad Bin Ali, from Muhammad Bin Sinan, from Hamza Bin Humran who said, ‘A man complained to Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> and said: ‘The Jinn have made us to exit our house’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Make the ceilings of our houses of seven cubits, and make the bathroom in the fringes of the house’. The man said, ‘So we did that and we did not see anything we disliked after that’.

citation.chapter: The Book of Outfits and the Beautification and the Magnanimity (al-Kafi, vol 6), 8:66
citation.arabic_text: شَكَا رَجُلٌ إِلَى أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ ( عليه السلام ) وَ قَالَ أَخْرَجَتْنَا الْجِنُّ عَنْ مَنَازِلِنَا فَقَالَ اجْعَلُوا سُقُوفَ بُيُوتِكُمْ سَبْعَةَ أَذْرُعٍ وَ اجْعَلُوا الْحَمَامَ فِي أَكْنَافِ الدَّارِ قَالَ الرَّجُلُ فَفَعَلْنَا ذَلِكَ فَمَا رَأَيْنَا شَيْئاً نَكْرَهُهُ بَعْدَ ذَلِكَ .
citation.translation: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Abu Abdullah, from Muhammad Bin Ali, from Muhammad Bin Sinan, from Hamza Bin Humran who said, ‘A man complained to Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> and said: ‘The Jinn have made us to exit our house’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Make the ceilings of our houses of seven cubits, and make the bathroom in the fringes of the house’. The man said, ‘So we did that and we did not see anything we disliked after that’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: ضعيف على المشهور - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (2/442)

text: A number of our companions, from sahl Bin Ziyad, from Ja’far Bin Bashir, from Al Husayn Bin Zurara, from Muhammad Bin Muslim who said, ‘Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Build your house up to seven cubits, so whatever is above that, the Satans<sup>la</sup> would dwell in it. The Satans<sup>la</sup> are neither in the sky nor in the ground, but rather they dwell in the atmosphere’.

citation.chapter: The Book of Outfits and the Beautification and the Magnanimity (al-Kafi, vol 6), 8:66
citation.arabic_text: قَالَ أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) ابْنِ بَيْتَكَ سَبْعَةَ أَذْرُعٍ فَمَا كَانَ فَوْقَ ذَلِكَ سَكَنَهُ الشَّيَاطِينُ إِنَّ الشَّيَاطِينَ لَيْسَتْ فِي السَّمَاءِ وَ لَا فِي الْأَرْضِ وَ إِنَّمَا تَسْكُنُ الْهَوَاءَ .
citation.translation: A number of our companions, from sahl Bin Ziyad, from Ja’far Bin Bashir, from Al Husayn Bin Zurara, from Muhammad Bin Muslim who said, ‘Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Build your house up to seven cubits, so whatever is above that, the Satans<sup>la</sup> would dwell in it. The Satans<sup>la</sup> are neither in the sky nor in the ground, but rather they dwell in the atmosphere’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: ضعيف على المشهور - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (22/442)

text: From him, from Ali Bin Al Hakam, and Muhsan Bin Ahmad, from Aban Bin Usman, form Muhammad Bin Ismail, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws having said: ‘When the house is above eight cubits, so write in its upper part the Verse of the Chair [2:255]’.

citation.chapter: The Book of Outfits and the Beautification and the Magnanimity (al-Kafi, vol 6), 8:66
citation.arabic_text: إِذَا كَانَ الْبَيْتُ فَوْقَ ثَمَانِيَةِ أَذْرُعٍ فَاكْتُبْ فِي أَعْلَاهُ آيَةَ الْكُرْسِيِّ .
citation.translation: From him, from Ali Bin Al Hakam, and Muhsan Bin Ahmad, from Aban Bin Usman, form Muhammad Bin Ismail, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws having said: ‘When the house is above eight cubits, so write in its upper part the Verse of the Chair [2:255]’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: ضعيف على المشهور - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (22/443)

text: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hisham Bin Al Hakam, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> forbade to sleep upon the roof other than in an enclosure (boundary wall)’.

citation.chapter: The Book of Outfits and the Beautification and the Magnanimity (al-Kafi, vol 6), 8:67
citation.arabic_text: نَهَى رَسُولُ اللَّهِ ( صلى الله عليه وآله ) أَنْ يُبَاتَ عَلَى سَطْحٍ غَيْرِ مُحَجَّرٍ .
citation.translation: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hisham Bin Al Hakam, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> forbade to sleep upon the roof other than in an enclosure (boundary wall)’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: حسن - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (22/443)

text: Abu Ali Al Ashary, from Muhammad Bin Abdul Jabbar, from Ali Bin Is’haq, from Sahl Bin Al Yas’a, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘The one who sleeps upon a roof without an enclosure (boundary wall), so something hits him, so he should not blame any except for himself’.

citation.chapter: The Book of Outfits and the Beautification and the Magnanimity (al-Kafi, vol 6), 8:67
citation.arabic_text: قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ ( صلى الله عليه وآله ) مَنْ بَاتَ عَلَى سَطْحٍ غَيْرِ مُحَجَّرٍ فَأَصَابَهُ شَيْ‏ءٌ فَلَا يَلُومَنَّ إِلَّا نَفْسَهُ .
citation.translation: Abu Ali Al Ashary, from Muhammad Bin Abdul Jabbar, from Ali Bin Is’haq, from Sahl Bin Al Yas’a, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘The one who sleeps upon a roof without an enclosure (boundary wall), so something hits him, so he should not blame any except for himself’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: صحيح - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (2/443)

text: From him, from Al Hajjal, from Abdullah Bin Bukeyr, from Muhammad Bin Muslim, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having dislike that the man should sleep upon a roof and there is not enclosure upon it, and the man and the woman with regards to that, are the same’.

citation.chapter: The Book of Outfits and the Beautification and the Magnanimity (al-Kafi, vol 6), 8:67
citation.arabic_text: ذَلِكَ سَوَاءٌ .
citation.translation: From him, from Al Hajjal, from Abdullah Bin Bukeyr, from Muhammad Bin Muslim, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having dislike that the man should sleep upon a roof and there is not enclosure upon it, and the man and the woman with regards to that, are the same’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: موثق كالصحيح - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (22/443)

text: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ibn Bukeyr, from Muhammad Bin Muslim, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having disliked for the man to spend the night alone upon a roof, or upon a rood with no enclosure upon it, and the man and the woman with regards to it are at the same status’.

citation.chapter: The Book of Outfits and the Beautification and the Magnanimity (al-Kafi, vol 6), 8:67
citation.arabic_text: هِ بِمَنْزِلَةٍ .
citation.translation: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ibn Bukeyr, from Muhammad Bin Muslim, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having disliked for the man to spend the night alone upon a roof, or upon a rood with no enclosure upon it, and the man and the woman with regards to it are at the same status’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: موثق كالصحيح - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (22/443)

text: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Muhammad Bin Abu Hamza and someone else, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> regarding the roof one sleeps upon and he is not enclosed (by the boundary wall), he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘It would suffice for him if there happened to be a wall of a height of the measurement of two cubits’.

citation.chapter: The Book of Outfits and the Beautification and the Magnanimity (al-Kafi, vol 6), 8:67
citation.arabic_text: السَّطْحِ يُبَاتُ عَلَيْهِ وَ هُوَ غَيْرُ مُحَجَّرٍ قَالَ يُجْزِيهِ أَنْ يَكُونَ مِقْدَارُ ارْتِفَاعِ الْحَائِطِ ذِرَاعَيْنِ .
citation.translation: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Muhammad Bin Abu Hamza and someone else, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> regarding the roof one sleeps upon and he is not enclosed (by the boundary wall), he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘It would suffice for him if there happened to be a wall of a height of the measurement of two cubits’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: حسن - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (2/444)

text: From him, from his father, from Safwan Bin yahya, from Ays Bin Al Qasim who said, ‘I asked Abu Abdullahasws about the roof, can one sleep upon it without an enclosure?’ Heasws said: ‘Rasool-Allahsaww forbade from that’. So I asked himasws about three walls, so heasws said: ‘No, unless it is four’. I said, ‘How much should the height of the walls be?’ Heasws said: ‘The shortest of it is one cubit and one open-palms width (Shibr)’.

citation.chapter: The Book of Outfits and the Beautification and the Magnanimity (al-Kafi, vol 6), 8:67
citation.arabic_text: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) عَنِ السَّطْحِ يُنَامُ عَلَيْهِ بِغَيْرِ حُجْرَةٍ قَالَ نَهَى رَسُولُ اللَّهِ ( صلى الله عليه وآله ) عَنْ ذَلِكَ فَسَأَلْتُهُ عَنْ ثَلَاثَةِ حِيطَانٍ فَقَالَ لَا إِلَّا أَرْبَعَةً قُلْتُ كَمْ طُولُ الْحَائِطِ قَالَ أَقْصَرُهُ ذِرَاعٌ وَ شِبْرٌ .
citation.translation: From him, from his father, from Safwan Bin yahya, from Ays Bin Al Qasim who said, ‘I asked Abu Abdullahasws about the roof, can one sleep upon it without an enclosure?’ Heasws said: ‘Rasool-Allahsaww forbade from that’. So I asked himasws about three walls, so heasws said: ‘No, unless it is four’. I said, ‘How much should the height of the walls be?’ Heasws said: ‘The shortest of it is one cubit and one open-palms width (Shibr)’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: حسن - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (22/444)

text: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Al Sayyari, from a sheykh from his companions, from the one who mentioned it, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘From the bitterness of the living is the transferring from a house to a house and eating the bitter bread’.

citation.chapter: The Book of Outfits and the Beautification and the Magnanimity (al-Kafi, vol 6), 8:68
citation.arabic_text: حَدَّثَنِي شَيْخٌ مِنْ أَصْحَابِنَا عَمَّنْ ذَكَرَهُ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) قَالَ مِنْ مُرِّ الْعَيْشِ النُّقْلَةُ مِنْ دَارٍ إِلَى دَارٍ وَ أَكْلُ خُبْزِ الشِّرَى .
citation.translation: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Al Sayyari, from a sheykh from his companions, from the one who mentioned it, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘From the bitterness of the living is the transferring from a house to a house and eating the bitter bread’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: ضعيف على المشهور - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (22/444)

text: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hisham Bin Al Hakam, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘The one who gathers wealth from other than Permissible means, Allah<sup>azwj</sup> would Cause him to be overcome by the construction, and the water, and the clay’.

citation.chapter: The Book of Outfits and the Beautification and the Magnanimity (al-Kafi, vol 6), 8:68
citation.arabic_text: مَنْ كَسَبَ مَالًا مِنْ غَيْرِ حِلِّهِ سَلَّطَ اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ الْبِنَاءَ وَ الْمَاءَ وَ الطِّينَ .
citation.translation: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hisham Bin Al Hakam, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘The one who gathers wealth from other than Permissible means, Allah<sup>azwj</sup> would Cause him to be overcome by the construction, and the water, and the clay’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: حسن - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (22/444)

text: Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Husayn Bin Usman who said, ‘I saw Abu Al-Hassan Musa<sup>asws</sup> and he<sup>asws</sup> had built a construction at Mina, then demolished it’.

citation.chapter: The Book of Outfits and the Beautification and the Magnanimity (al-Kafi, vol 6), 8:68
citation.arabic_text: رَأَيْتُ أَبَا الْحَسَنِ مُوسَى ( عليه السلام ) وَ قَدْ بَنَى بِمِنًى بِنَاءً ثُمَّ هَدَمَهُ .
citation.translation: Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Husayn Bin Usman who said, ‘I saw Abu Al-Hassan Musa<sup>asws</sup> and he<sup>asws</sup> had built a construction at Mina, then demolished it’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: حسن - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (2/444)

text: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Ali Bin Asbat, from Dawood Al Raqy, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws, said, ‘I asked himasws about the Words of Allahazwj Mighty and Majestic [17:44] and there is not a single thing but it Glorifies Him with His praise, but you do not understand their Glorification. Heasws said: ‘The cracking of the wall is its Glorification’.

citation.chapter: The Book of Outfits and the Beautification and the Magnanimity (al-Kafi, vol 6), 8:68
citation.arabic_text: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنْ قَوْلِ اللَّهِ عَزَّ وَ جَلَّ وَ إِنْ مِنْ شَيْ‏ءٍ إِلَّا يُسَبِّحُ بِحَمْدِهِ وَ لكِنْ لا تَفْقَهُونَ تَسْبِيحَهُمْ قَالَ تَنَقُّضُ الْجُدُرِ تَسْبِيحُهَا .
citation.translation: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Ali Bin Asbat, from Dawood Al Raqy, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws, said, ‘I asked himasws about the Words of Allahazwj Mighty and Majestic [17:44] and there is not a single thing but it Glorifies Him with His praise, but you do not understand their Glorification. Heasws said: ‘The cracking of the wall is its Glorification’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: ضعيف على المشهور - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (22/445)

text: Al Husayn Bin Muhammad, from Ahmad Bin Is’haq, from Sa’dan Bin Muslim, from Is’haq Bin Ammar who said, ‘Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Sweep your courtyards and do not resemble the Jews’.

citation.chapter: The Book of Outfits and the Beautification and the Magnanimity (al-Kafi, vol 6), 8:68
citation.arabic_text: قَالَ أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) اكْنُسُوا أَفْنِيَتَكُمْ وَ لَا تَشَبَّهُوا بِالْيَهُودِ .
citation.translation: Al Husayn Bin Muhammad, from Ahmad Bin Is’haq, from Sa’dan Bin Muslim, from Is’haq Bin Ammar who said, ‘Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Sweep your courtyards and do not resemble the Jews’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: مجهول - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (22/445)

text: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Ali Bin Asbaat, from his uncle Yaqoub Bin Salim, raising it, said, ‘Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Do not accumulate the dust behind the door, for it is a shelter of the Satans<sup>la</sup>’.

citation.chapter: The Book of Outfits and the Beautification and the Magnanimity (al-Kafi, vol 6), 8:68
citation.arabic_text: قَالَ أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ ( عليه السلام ) لَا تُؤْوُوا التُّرَابَ خَلْفَ الْبَابِ فَإِنَّهُ مَأْوَى الشَّيَاطِينِ .
citation.translation: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Ali Bin Asbaat, from his uncle Yaqoub Bin Salim, raising it, said, ‘Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Do not accumulate the dust behind the door, for it is a shelter of the Satans<sup>la</sup>’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: ضعيف على المشهور - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (2/445)

text: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Abu Abdullah, from Safwan Bin Yahya, from Abu Jameela, from Humeyd Al Sayrafi, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Every construction without a boundary, so it would have bad consequences for its owner on the Day of Judgement’.

citation.chapter: The Book of Outfits and the Beautification and the Magnanimity (al-Kafi, vol 6), 8:68
citation.arabic_text: كُلُّ بِنَاءٍ لَيْسَ بِكَفَافٍ فَهُوَ وَبَالٌ عَلَى صَاحِبِهِ يَوْمَ الْقِيَامَةِ .
citation.translation: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Abu Abdullah, from Safwan Bin Yahya, from Abu Jameela, from Humeyd Al Sayrafi, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Every construction without a boundary, so it would have bad consequences for its owner on the Day of Judgement’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: ضعيف - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (22/446)

text: From him, from one of his companions, (It has been narrated) raising it to Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Sweeping the house negates the poverty’.

citation.chapter: The Book of Outfits and the Beautification and the Magnanimity (al-Kafi, vol 6), 8:68
citation.arabic_text: كَنْسُ الْبَيْتِ يَنْفِي الْفَقْرَ .

citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: مرفوع - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (2/446)

text: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Al Nowfaly, from Al Sakuny, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah having said: ‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> forbade from entering a dark house except with a lantern’.

citation.chapter: The Book of Outfits and the Beautification and the Magnanimity (al-Kafi, vol 6), 8:68
citation.arabic_text: نَهَى رَسُولُ اللَّهِ ( صلى الله عليه وآله ) أَنْ يَدْخُلَ بَيْتاً مُظْلِماً إِلَّا بِمِصْبَاحٍ .
citation.translation: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Al Nowfaly, from Al Sakuny, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah having said: ‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> forbade from entering a dark house except with a lantern’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: ضعيف على المشهور - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (22/446)

text: From him, from Ibrahim Bin Muhammad Al Saqafy, from Ali Bin Al Moala, from Ibrahim Bin Al Khataab, (It has been narrated) raising it to Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘The bottom part of the wall complained to Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic from the weight of its upper part. So Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic Revealed unto it bear each other’s weight’.

citation.chapter: The Book of Outfits and the Beautification and the Magnanimity (al-Kafi, vol 6), 8:68
citation.arabic_text: شَكَتْ أَسَافِلُ الْحِيطَانِ إِلَى اللَّهِ عَزَّ وَ جَلَّ مِنْ ثِقْلِ أَعَالِيهَا فَأَوْحَى اللَّهُ عَزَّ وَ جَلَّ إِلَيْهَا يَحْمِلُ بَعْضُكُمْ بَعْضاً .
citation.translation: From him, from Ibrahim Bin Muhammad Al Saqafy, from Ali Bin Al Moala, from Ibrahim Bin Al Khataab, (It has been narrated) raising it to Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘The bottom part of the wall complained to Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic from the weight of its upper part. citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: مجهول - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (22/446)

text: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Salma Bin Al Khataab, from Ibrahim Bin Maymoun, from Isa Bin Abdullah, from his grandfather who said, ‘Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘The house of Satans<sup>la</sup> from your houses is the house of the spider (cobweb)’.

citation.chapter: The Book of Outfits and the Beautification and the Magnanimity (al-Kafi, vol 6), 8:68
citation.arabic_text: قَالَ أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ ( عليه السلام ) قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ ( صلى الله عليه وآله ) بَيْتُ الشَّيَاطِينِ مِنْ بُيُوتِكُمْ بَيْتُ الْعَنْكَبُوتِ .
citation.translation: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Salma Bin Al Khataab, from Ibrahim Bin Maymoun, from Isa Bin Abdullah, from his grandfather who said, ‘Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘The house of Satans<sup>la</sup> from your houses is the house of the spider (cobweb)’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: ضعيف - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (22/446)

text: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Usman Bin Isa, from Sama’at who said, ‘I asked Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> about closing the doors, and covering the utensils, and extinguishing the lantern, so he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Close your door for the Satan<sup>la</sup> does not open a door, and extinguish your lantern from the rats, and it is the mouse which would not (be able to) burn down your house and overturn your utensils’. And it is reported that, ‘(He<sup>asws</sup> said): ‘The Satan<sup>la</sup> does not uncover a lid, meaning a covering’.

citation.chapter: The Book of Outfits and the Beautification and the Magnanimity (al-Kafi, vol 6), 8:68
citation.arabic_text: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) عَنْ إِغْلَاقِ الْأَبْوَابِ وَ إِيكَاءِ الْأَوَانِي وَ إِطْفَاءِ السِّرَاجِ فَقَالَ أَغْلِقْ بَابَكَ فَإِنَّ الشَّيْطَانَ لَا يَفْتَحُ بَاباً وَ أَطْفِ السِّرَاجَ مِنَ الْفُوَيْسِقَةِ وَ هِيَ الْفَأْرَةُ لَا تُحْرِقْ بَيْتَكَ وَ أَوْكِ الْإِنَاءَ . وَ رُوِيَ أَنَّ الشَّيْطَانَ لَا يَكْشِفُ مُخَمَّراً يَعْنِي مُغَطًّى .
citation.translation: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Usman Bin Isa, from Sama’at who said, ‘I asked Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> about closing the doors, and covering the utensils, and extinguishing the lantern, so he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Close your door for the Satan<sup>la</sup> does not open a door, and extinguish your lantern from the rats, and it is the mouse which would not (be able to) burn down your house and overturn your utensils’. And it is reported that, ‘(He<sup>asws</sup> said): ‘The Satan<sup>la</sup> does not uncover a lid, meaning a covering’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: موثق وآخره مرسل - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (2/446)

text: Abu Ali Al Ashary, raising it, said, ‘Al-Reza<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Igniting the lantern before the sun sets negates the poverty’.

citation.chapter: The Book of Outfits and the Beautification and the Magnanimity (al-Kafi, vol 6), 8:68
citation.arabic_text: أَبُو عَلِيٍّ الْأَشْعَرِيُّ رَفَعَهُ قَالَ قَالَ الرِّضَا ( عليه السلام ) إِسْرَاجُ السِّرَاجِ قَبْلَ أَنْ تَغِيبَ الشَّمْسُ يَنْفِي الْفَقْرَ .
citation.translation: Abu Ali Al Ashary, raising it, said, ‘Al-Reza<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Igniting the lantern before the sun sets negates the poverty’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: مرفوع - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (22/447)

text: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Al Nowfaly, from Al Sakuny, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Whenever the Prophet<sup>saww</sup> went out in the summer, went out on the day of Thursday, and whenever he<sup>saww</sup> wanted to enter in the winter from the cold, entered on the day of Friday’. And it has been reported as well that his<sup>saww</sup> entry and his<sup>saww</sup> exit was on the night of Friday.

citation.chapter: The Book of Outfits and the Beautification and the Magnanimity (al-Kafi, vol 6), 8:68
citation.arabic_text: كَانَ النَّبِيُّ ( صلى الله عليه وآله ) إِذَا خَرَجَ فِي الصَّيْفِ مِنَ الْبَيْتِ خَرَجَ يَوْمَ الْخَمِيسِ وَ إِذَا أَرَادَ أَنْ يَدْخُلَ فِي الشِّتَاءِ مِنَ الْبَرْدِ دَخَلَ يَوْمَ الْجُمُعَةِ وَ رُوِيَ أَيْضاً كَانَ دُخُولُهُ وَ خُرُوجُهُ لَيْلَةَ الْجُمُعَةِ .
citation.translation: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Al Nowfaly, from Al Sakuny, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Whenever the Prophet<sup>saww</sup> went out in the summer, went out on the day of Thursday, and whenever he<sup>saww</sup> wanted to enter in the winter from the cold, entered on the day of Friday’. And it has been reported as well that his<sup>saww</sup> entry and his<sup>saww</sup> exit was on the night of Friday.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: ضعيف على المشهور - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (2/447)

text: Al Husayn Bin Muhammad, from Moala Bin Muhammad, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Abdullah who said, ‘Abu Hisham Al-Ja’fary reported from Abu Al-Hassanasws the 3rd having said: ‘Allahazwj Mighty and Majestic Made from Hisazwj earth a spot called Al-Marhoumaat. Iasws would love it to supplicate therein for it would be Answered; and that Allahazwj Mighty and Majestic Made from Hisazwj earth a spot called Al-Muntaqimaat, so whenever the man amasses wealth from other than Permissible means, Allahazwj Causes a spot from it to overcome him, so its gets spent therein’.

citation.chapter: The Book of Outfits and the Beautification and the Magnanimity (al-Kafi, vol 6), 8:68
citation.arabic_text: رَوَى أَبُو هَاشِمٍ الْجَعْفَرِيُّ عَنْ أَبِي الْحَسَنِ الثَّالِثِ ( عليه السلام ) قَالَ إِنَّ اللَّهَ عَزَّ وَ جَلَّ جَعَلَ مِنْ أَرْضِهِ بِقَاعاً تُسَمَّى الْمَرْحُومَاتِ أَحَبَّ أَنْ يُدْعَى فِيهَا فَيُجِيبَ وَ إِنَّ اللَّهَ عَزَّ وَ جَلَّ جَعَلَ مِنْ أَرْضِهِ بِقَاعاً تُسَمَّى الْمُنْتَقِمَاتِ فَإِذَا كَسَبَ الرَّجُلُ مَالًا مِنْ غَيْرِ حِلِّهِ سَلَّطَ اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ بُقْعَةً مِنْهَا فَأَنْفَقَهُ فِيهَا .
citation.translation: Al Husayn Bin Muhammad, from Moala Bin Muhammad, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Abdullah who said, ‘Abu Hisham Al-Ja’fary reported from Abu Al-Hassanasws the 3rd having said: ‘Allahazwj Mighty and Majestic Made from Hisazwj earth a spot called Al-Marhoumaat. Iasws would love it to supplicate therein for it would be Answered; and that Allahazwj Mighty and Majestic Made from Hisazwj earth a spot called Al-Muntaqimaat, so whenever the man amasses wealth from other than Permissible means, Allahazwj Causes a spot from it to overcome him, so its gets spent therein’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: ضعيف على المشهور - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (22/447)

text: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ibn Qaddah, from his father who said, ‘I lodged at Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup>, so he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘O Maymoun! Who would slumber along with you at night, is there a slave with you?’ I said, ‘No’. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘So do not sleep alone, for the most audacious that the Satan<sup>la</sup> can become, does so upon the human being when he was alone’.

citation.chapter: The Book of Outfits and the Beautification and the Magnanimity (al-Kafi, vol 6), 8:69
citation.arabic_text: نَزَلْتُ عَلَى أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ ( عليه السلام ) فَقَالَ يَا مَيْمُونُ مَنْ يَرْقُدُ مَعَكَ بِاللَّيْلِ أَ مَعَكَ غُلَامٌ قُلْتُ لَا قَالَ فَلَا تَنَمْ وَحْدَكَ فَإِنَّ أَجْرَأَ مَا يَكُونُ الشَّيْطَانُ عَلَى الْإِنْسَانِ إِذَا كَانَ وَحْدَهُ .
citation.translation: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ibn Qaddah, from his father who said, ‘I lodged at Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup>, so he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘O Maymoun! Who would slumber along with you at night, is there a slave with you?’ I said, ‘No’. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘So do not sleep alone, for the most audacious that the Satan<sup>la</sup> can become, does so upon the human being when he was alone’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: مجهول - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (22/448)

text: Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Al A’ala Bin Razeyn, from Muhammad Bin Muslim, (It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘The one who defecates upon a grave or urinates standing, or urinates in water standing, or walks in one shoe, or drinks standing, or isolates himself alone in a house, and sleeps upon dripping hands (from food stains), so something from the Satan<sup>la</sup> hits him, it would not leave him except if Allah<sup>azwj</sup> so Desires it, and the quickest of what the Satan<sup>la</sup> comes upon the human being is when he is upon one of these states. Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> went out in a military brigade, so he<sup>saww</sup> came to a valley of the Jinn. So he<sup>saww</sup> called out to his<sup>saww</sup> companions: ‘Let each man from you grab the hand of his companions, and no man should enter alone, nor should a man go past it alone’. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘So a man went forward alone and ended up to it, and he had epileptic fits. So Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> was informed with that, so he<sup>saww</sup> grabbed with his thumb and touched him, then said: ‘In the Name of Allah<sup>azwj</sup>! Get out, Wicked one, I<sup>saww</sup> am Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup>!’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘So he stood up’.

citation.chapter: The Book of Outfits and the Beautification and the Magnanimity (al-Kafi, vol 6), 8:69
citation.arabic_text: مَنْ تَخَلَّى عَلَى قَبْرٍ أَوْ بَالَ قَائِماً أَوْ بَالَ فِي مَاءٍ قَائِماً أَوْ مَشَى فِي حِذَاءٍ وَاحِدٍ أَوْ شَرِبَ قَائِماً أَوْ خَلَا فِي بَيْتٍ وَحْدَهُ وَ بَاتَ عَلَى غَمَرٍ فَأَصَابَهُ شَيْ‏ءٌ مِنَ الشَّيْطَانِ لَمْ يَدَعْهُ إِلَّا أَنْ يَشَاءَ اللَّهُ وَ أَسْرَعُ مَا يَكُونُ الشَّيْطَانُ إِلَى الْإِنْسَانِ وَ هُوَ عَلَى بَعْضِ هَذِهِ الْحَالَاتِ فَإِنَّ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ ( صلى الله عليه وآله ) خَرَجَ فِي سَرِيَّةٍ فَأَتَى وَادِيَ مَجَنَّةٍ فَنَادَى أَصْحَابَهُ أَلَا لِيَأْخُذْ كُلُّ رَجُلٍ مِنْكُمْ بِيَدِ صَاحِبِهِ وَ لَا يَدْخُلَنَّ رَجُلٌ وَحْدَهُ وَ لَا يَمْضِي رَجُلٌ وَحْدَهُ قَالَ فَتَقَدَّمَ رَجُلٌ وَحْدَهُ فَانْتَهَى إِلَيْهِ وَ قَدْ صُرِعَ فَأُخْبِرَ بِذَلِكَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ ( صلى الله عليه وآله ) فَأَخَذَ بِإِبْهَامِهِ فَغَمَزَهَا ثُمَّ قَالَ بِسْمِ اللَّهِ اخْرُجْ خَبِيثُ أَنَا رَسُولُ اللَّهِ قَالَ فَقَامَ .

text: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Abdullah Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Al Hakam, from Aban Al Ahmar, from Muhammad Bin Muslim, (It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘The Satan<sup>la</sup> is the most troublesome with the human being when he happens to be alone, isolated. I<sup>asws</sup> should not see him sleeping alone’.

citation.chapter: The Book of Outfits and the Beautification and the Magnanimity (al-Kafi, vol 6), 8:69
citation.arabic_text: قَالَ إِنَّ الشَّيْطَانَ أَشَدَّ مَا يَهُمُّ بِالْإِنْسَانِ حِينَ يَكُونُ وَحْدَهُ خَالِياً لَا أَرَى أَنْ يَرْقُدَ وَحْدَهُ .
citation.translation: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Abdullah Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Al Hakam, from Aban Al Ahmar, from Muhammad Bin Muslim, (It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘The Satan<sup>la</sup> is the most troublesome with the human being when he happens to be alone, isolated. I<sup>asws</sup> should not see him sleeping alone’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: مجهول - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (22/448)

text: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Khalid, from Usman Bin Isa, from Sama’at Bin Mihran who said, ‘I asked Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> about the man who sleeps alone in a house, so he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘I<sup>asws</sup> dislke that, and if he is desperate to that, so there is no problem, but he should frequent in the mentioning of Allah<sup>azwj</sup> during his sleep for as long as he can’.

citation.chapter: The Book of Outfits and the Beautification and the Magnanimity (al-Kafi, vol 6), 8:69
citation.arabic_text: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) عَنِ الرَّجُلِ يَبِيتُ فِي بَيْتٍ وَحْدَهُ فَقَالَ إِنِّي لَأَكْرَهُ ذَلِكَ وَ إِنِ اضْطُرَّ إِلَى ذَلِكَ فَلَا بَأْسَ وَ لَكِنْ يُكْثِرُ ذِكْرَ اللَّهِ فِي مَنَامِهِ مَا اسْتَطَاعَ .

text: From him, from his father, from Abdullah Bin Al Mugheira, and Muhammad Bin Sinan, from Talha Bin Zayd, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having disliked that one should sleep in a house in which there is no door, nor a veil’.

citation.chapter: The Book of Outfits and the Beautification and the Magnanimity (al-Kafi, vol 6), 8:69
citation.arabic_text: بَيْتٍ لَيْسَ عَلَيْهِ بَابٌ وَ لَا سِتْرٌ .

text: And by his chain, ‘He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> disliked entering a dark house except with a lantern’.

citation.chapter: The Book of Outfits and the Beautification and the Magnanimity (al-Kafi, vol 6), 8:69
citation.arabic_text: وَ بِإِسْنَادِهِ قَالَ إِنَّ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ ( صلى الله عليه وآله ) كَرِهَ أَنْ يَدْخُلَ بَيْتاً مُظْلِماً إِلَّا بِسِرَاجٍ .
citation.translation: And by his chain, ‘He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> disliked entering a dark house except with a lantern’.

text: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Ja’far Bin Muhammad Al Ashary, from Ibn Al Qadah, from his father Maymoun, (It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having said to Muhammad Bin Suleyman: ‘Where have you lodged?’ He said, ‘In such a such place’. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Is there anyone with you?’ He said, ‘No’. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Do not be alone, transfer from it, O Maymoun, for the Satan<sup>la</sup> would be the most audacious upon the human being when he was alone’.

citation.chapter: The Book of Outfits and the Beautification and the Magnanimity (al-Kafi, vol 6), 8:69
citation.arabic_text: لِمُحَمَّدِ بْنِ سُلَيْمَانَ أَيْنَ نَزَلْتَ قَالَ فِي مَكَانِ كَذَا وَ كَذَا قَالَ مَعَكَ أَحَدٌ قَالَ لَا قَالَ لَا تَكُنْ وَحْدَكَ تَحَوَّلْ عَنْهُ يَا مَيْمُونُ فَإِنَّ الشَّيْطَانَ أَجْرَأَ مَا يَكُونُ عَلَى الْإِنْسَانِ إِذَا كَانَ وَحْدَهُ .

text: Sahl, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Abu Nasr, from Safwan, from Al A’ala, from Muhammad Bin Muslim, (It has been narrated) from one of the two (5<sup>th</sup> or 6<sup>th</sup> Imam<sup>asws</sup>) having said: ‘Do not drink while you are standing, nor urinate in stagnant water, nor spit by a grave, nor be isolated in a house alone, nor walk in one shoe, for the Satan<sup>la</sup> is quickest as he<sup>asws</sup> can be to the servant when he was upon one of these states’. And he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘If anything were to hit anyone upon these states so it would not separate from him except if Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic so Desires it’.

citation.chapter: The Book of Outfits and the Beautification and the Magnanimity (al-Kafi, vol 6), 8:69
citation.arabic_text: لَا تَشْرَبْ وَ أَنْتَ قَائِمٌ وَ لَا تَبُلْ فِي مَاءٍ نَقِيعٍ وَ لَا تَطُفْ بِقَبْرٍ وَ لَا تَخْلُ فِي بَيْتٍ وَحْدَكَ وَ لَا تَمْشِ فِي نَعْلٍ وَاحِدٍ فَإِنَّ الشَّيْطَانَ أَسْرَعَ مَا يَكُونُ إِلَى الْعَبْدِ إِذَا كَانَ عَلَى بَعْضِ هَذِهِ الْأَحْوَالِ وَ قَالَ إِنَّهُ مَا أَصَابَ أَحَداً شَيْ‏ءٌ عَلَى هَذِهِ الْحَالِ فَكَادَ أَنْ يُفَارِقَهُ إِلَّا أَنْ يَشَاءَ اللَّهُ عَزَّ وَ جَلَّ .

text: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from hammad, from Al Halby, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘The Satan<sup>la</sup> is the most troublesome with the human being when he was alone, therefore do not sleep alone, nor travel alone’.

citation.chapter: The Book of Outfits and the Beautification and the Magnanimity (al-Kafi, vol 6), 8:69
citation.arabic_text: إِنَّ الشَّيْطَانَ أَشَدَّ مَا يَهُمُّ بِالْإِنْسَانِ إِذَا كَانَ وَحْدَهُ فَلَا تَبِيتَنَّ وَحْدَكَ وَ لَا تُسَافِرَنَّ وَحْدَكَ .

citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: حسن - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (2/450)

text: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, and Ali Bin Ibrahim, altogether from Muhammad Bin Isa, from Al Dahqaan, from Dorost, from Ibrahim Bin Abdul Hameed, (It has been narrated) from Abu Al-Hassan Musa<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Three (things) are from which the insanity is feared – the one who defecates between the graves, and the walking in one shoe, and the man who sleeps alone; and these are the things, rather disliked due to this reason, and it is not Prohibited’.

citation.chapter: The Book of Outfits and the Beautification and the Magnanimity (al-Kafi, vol 6), 8:69
citation.arabic_text: ثَلَاثَةٌ يُتَخَوَّفُ مِنْهَا الْجُنُونُ التَّغَوُّطُ بَيْنَ الْقُبُورِ وَ الْمَشْيُ فِي خُفٍّ وَاحِدٍ وَ الرَّجُلُ يَنَامُ وَحْدَهُ وَ هَذِهِ الْأَشْيَاءُ إِنَّمَا كُرِهَتْ لِهَذِهِ الْعِلَّةِ وَ لَيْسَتْ هِيَ بِحَرَامٍ.

text: Al Husayn Bin Muhammad, from Moala Bin Muhammad, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from the one who informed him, from Ibn Tayfour Al Mutatabab who said, ‘Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> asked me: ‘Which thing do you ride?’ I said, ‘A donkey’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘With how much did you buy it?’ I said, ‘With thirteen Dinars’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘This is an extravagance if you were to buy a donkey with thirteen Dinars and neglect a work-horse’. I said, ‘My Master<sup>asws</sup>! The provision (feed) for the work-horse is more than a provision of the donkey’. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The One Who<sup>azwj</sup> Provides (feed) for the donkey would Provide for the work-horse. Do you not know that the one who associates with an animal in expectation of our<sup>asws</sup> matter (Rising of Al-Qaim<sup>asws</sup>), and annoys our<sup>asws</sup> enemies by it, and it is linked to us<sup>asws</sup>, Allah<sup>azwj</sup> would Manage his livelihood, and Open his chest, and successfully conclude his work, and it would be an aid upon his needs’.

citation.chapter: THE BOOK OF DOMESTIC ANIMALS (al-Kafi, vol 6), 9:1
citation.arabic_text: سَأَلَنِي أَبُو الْحَسَنِ ( عليه السلام ) أَيَّ شَيْ‏ءٍ تَرْكَبُ قُلْتُ حِمَاراً فَقَالَ بِكَمِ ابْتَعْتَهُ قُلْتُ بِثَلَاثَةَ عَشَرَ دِينَاراً فَقَالَ إِنَّ هَذَا هُوَ السَّرَفُ أَنْ تَشْتَرِيَ حِمَاراً بِثَلَاثَةَ عَشَرَ دِينَاراً وَ تَدَعَ بِرْذَوْناً قُلْتُ يَا سَيِّدِي إِنَّ مَئُونَةَ الْبِرْذَوْنِ أَكْثَرُ مِنْ مَئُونَةِ الْحِمَارِ قَالَ فَقَالَ إِنَّ الَّذِي يَمُونُ الْحِمَارَ يَمُونُ الْبِرْذَوْنَ أَ مَا عَلِمْتَ أَنَّ مَنِ ارْتَبَطَ دَابَّةً مُتَوَقِّعاً بِهِ أَمْرَنَا وَ يَغِيظُ بِهِ عَدُوَّنَا وَ هُوَ مَنْسُوبٌ إِلَيْنَا أَدَرَّ اللَّهُ رِزْقَهُ وَ شَرَحَ صَدْرَهُ وَ بَلَّغَهُ أَمَلَهُ وَ كَانَ عَوْناً عَلَى حَوَائِجِهِ .
citation.translation: Al Husayn Bin Muhammad, from Moala Bin Muhammad, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from the one who informed him, from Ibn Tayfour Al Mutatabab who said, ‘Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> asked me: ‘Which thing do you ride?’ I said, ‘A donkey’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘With how much did you buy it?’ I said, ‘With thirteen Dinars’. text: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Muhammad Bin Al Husayn, from Muhammad Bin Sinan, from Abdullah Bin Jundab, from a man from his companions, Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> has said: ‘Nine-tenths of the livelihood is with the owner of the animal’.

citation.chapter: THE BOOK OF DOMESTIC ANIMALS (al-Kafi, vol 6), 9:1
citation.arabic_text: حَدَّثَنِي رَجُلٌ مِنْ أَصْحَابِنَا عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) قَالَ تِسْعَةُ أَعْشَارِ الرِّزْقِ مَعَ صَاحِبِ الدَّابَّةِ .
citation.translation: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Muhammad Bin Al Husayn, from Muhammad Bin Sinan, from Abdullah Bin Jundab, from a man from his companions, Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> has said: ‘Nine-tenths of the livelihood is with the owner of the animal’.
