text: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, and Ahmad Bin Muhammad, altogether from Bakr Bin Salih, from Suleyman Al Ja’fary, (It has been narrated) from Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup>, ‘I heard him<sup>asws</sup> saying: ‘Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> gifted to Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup>, four horses from Al-Yemen. So he<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘Name these for me<sup>saww</sup>’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘These are of different types’. He<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘So is there a spotted one?’ So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Yes, there is a blonde one with spots’. He<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘So keep it for me<sup>saww</sup>’. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘And among these are two yellow ones with spots’. So he<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘Give these two to your<sup>asws</sup> two sons<sup>asws</sup>’. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘And the fourth one is plain and with no spots on it’. He<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘Sell it and keep its price for (the expenses of) your<sup>asws</sup> family. But rather, good fortune of the cavalry horse is in the one with the spots’. He (the narrator) said, ‘And I heard Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> saying: ‘We<sup>asws</sup> dislike the plain ones from the animals, all of these, except for the donkey, and the mule, and dislike the spots in the donkey and the mule being of different colours, and I<sup>asws</sup> dislike the bright-hooves in the mule except it happens to be expanded, nor do I<sup>asws</sup> desire it upon that state’.

citation.chapter: THE BOOK OF DOMESTIC ANIMALS (al-Kafi, vol 6), 9:1
citation.arabic_text: سَمِعْتُهُ يَقُولُ أَهْدَى أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ ( عليه السلام ) إِلَى رَسُولِ اللَّهِ ( صلى الله عليه وآله ) أَرْبَعَةَ أَفْرَاسٍ مِنَ الْيَمَنِ فَقَالَ سَمِّهَا لِي فَقَالَ هِيَ أَلْوَانٌ مُخْتَلِفَةٌ قَالَ فَفِيهَا وَضَحٌ فَقَالَ نَعَمْ فِيهَا أَشْقَرُ بِهِ وَضَحٌ قَالَ فَأَمْسِكْهُ عَلَيَّ قَالَ وَ فِيهَا كُمَيْتَانِ أَوْضَحَانِ فَقَالَ أَعْطِهِمَا ابْنَيْكَ قَالَ وَ الرَّابِعُ أَدْهَمُ بَهِيمٌ قَالَ بِعْهُ وَ اسْتَخْلِفْ بِهِ نَفَقَةً لِعِيَالِكَ إِنَّمَا يُمْنُ الْخَيْلِ فِي ذَوَاتِ الْأَوْضَاحِ قَالَ وَ سَمِعْتُ أَبَا الْحَسَنِ ( عليه السلام ) يَقُولُ كَرِهْنَا الْبَهِيمَ مِنَ الدَّوَابِّ كُلِّهَا إِلَّا الْحِمَارَ وَ الْبَغْلَ وَ كَرِهْتُ شِيَةَ الْأَوْضَاحِ فِي الْحِمَارِ وَ الْبَغْلِ الْأَلْوَنِ وَ كَرِهْتُ الْقُرْحَ فِي الْبَغْلِ إِلَّا أَنْ يَكُونَ بِهِ غُرَّةٌ سَائِلَةٌ وَ لَا أَشْتَهِيهَا عَلَى حَالٍ .

text: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Ali Bin Raib who said, ‘Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Buy an animal, for its benefit would be for you and its sustenance would be upon Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic’.

citation.chapter: THE BOOK OF DOMESTIC ANIMALS (al-Kafi, vol 6), 9:1
citation.arabic_text: قَالَ أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) اشْتَرِ دَابَّةً فَإِنَّ مَنْفَعَتَهَا لَكَ وَ رِزْقَهَا عَلَى اللَّهِ عَزَّ وَ جَلَّ .
citation.translation: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Ali Bin Raib who said, ‘Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Buy an animal, for its benefit would be for you and its sustenance would be upon Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: حسن - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (22/452)

text: A number of our companions, from sahl Bin Ziyad, from Muhammad Bin Al Husayn, from Ja’far Bin bashir, from Dawood Al Raqy who said, ‘Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The one who buys an animal, its back (for riding) would be for him, and upon Allah<sup>azwj</sup> would be its sustenance’.

citation.chapter: THE BOOK OF DOMESTIC ANIMALS (al-Kafi, vol 6), 9:1
citation.arabic_text: قَالَ أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) مَنِ اشْتَرَى دَابَّةً كَانَ لَهُ ظَهْرُهَا وَ عَلَى اللَّهِ رِزْقُهَا .
citation.translation: A number of our companions, from sahl Bin Ziyad, from Muhammad Bin Al Husayn, from Ja’far Bin bashir, from Dawood Al Raqy who said, ‘Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The one who buys an animal, its back (for riding) would be for him, and upon Allah<sup>azwj</sup> would be its sustenance’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: ضعيف على المشهور - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (2/453)

text: Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Muhammad Bin Al Waleed, from Yunus Bin Yaqoub who said, ‘Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said to me: ‘Take a donkey who would carry your belongings, for its sustenance would be upon Allah<sup>azwj</sup>’. He (the narrator) said, ‘So I took a donkey, and I and my brother Yusuf, when the year was completed, accounted for our expenditure, and we knew of its measurement. So we counted our expenditure after the buying of the donkey, so it was as it used to be beforehand, during every year, nothing had increased (from the expenses due to the feed of the donkey)’.

citation.chapter: THE BOOK OF DOMESTIC ANIMALS (al-Kafi, vol 6), 9:1
citation.arabic_text: قَالَ لِي أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) اتَّخِذْ حِمَاراً يَحْمِلْ رَحْلَكَ فَإِنَّ رِزْقَهُ عَلَى اللَّهِ قَالَ فَاتَّخَذْتُ حِمَاراً وَ كُنْتُ أَنَا وَ يُوسُفُ أَخِي إِذَا تَمَّتِ السَّنَةُ حَسَبْنَا نَفَقَاتِنَا فَنَعْلَمُ مِقْدَارَهَا فَحَسَبْنَا بَعْدَ شِرَاءِ الْحِمَارِ نَفَقَاتِنَا فَإِذَا هِيَ كَمَا كَانَتْ فِي كُلِّ عَامٍ لَمْ تَزِدْ شَيْئاً .

So we counted our expenditure after the buying of the donkey, so it was as it used to be beforehand, during every year, nothing had increased (from the expenses due to the feed of the donkey)’.

text: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Al Nowfaly, from Al Sakuny, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘For the animal, upon its owner, are six rights – he would not burden it above its strength, nor would he take its back as a seat for having discussions upon it, and he would begin by feeding it when he descends, and he would not brand it, and he would not harm it in its face for it Glorifies (Allah<sup>azwj</sup>), and he would present the water to it whenever he passes by it’.

citation.chapter: THE BOOK OF DOMESTIC ANIMALS (al-Kafi, vol 6), 9:2
citation.arabic_text: لِلدَّابَّةِ عَلَى صَاحِبِهَا سِتَّةُ حُقُوقٍ لَا يُحَمِّلُهَا فَوْقَ طَاقَتِهَا وَ لَا يَتَّخِذُ ظَهْرَهَا مَجَالِسَ يَتَحَدَّثُ عَلَيْهَا وَ يَبْدَأُ بِعَلْفِهَا إِذَا نَزَلَ وَ لَا يَسِمُهَا وَ لَا يَضْرِبُهَا فِي وَجْهِهَا فَإِنَّهَا تُسَبِّحُ وَ يَعْرِضُ عَلَيْهَا الْمَاءَ إِذَا مَرَّ بِهِ .

citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: ضعيف على المشهور - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (22/454)

text: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Abu Al Magra, from Suleyman Bin Khalid who said regarding what I think is, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Abu Zarr<sup>ra</sup> was seen watering a donkey at Al-Rabza, so one of the people said to him<sup>ra</sup>, ‘Is there not for you<sup>as</sup>, O Abu Zarr<sup>ra</sup>, one who would water the donkey for you<sup>as</sup>?’ So he<sup>as</sup> said: ‘I<sup>ra</sup> heard Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> saying: ‘There is none from the animals except that it asks Allah<sup>azwj</sup> every morning, ‘O Allah<sup>azwj</sup>! Grant me a righteous owner who would satiate me from the feed, and would quench me from the water, and would not encumber me above my strength’. Therefore I<sup>ra</sup> love to water it myself<sup>ra</sup>’.

citation.chapter: THE BOOK OF DOMESTIC ANIMALS (al-Kafi, vol 6), 9:2
citation.arabic_text: فِيمَا أَظُنُّ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) قَالَ رُئِيَ أَبُو ذَرٍّ رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ يَسْقِي حِمَاراً بِالرَّبَذَةِ فَقَالَ لَهُ بَعْضُ النَّاسِ أَ مَا لَكَ يَا أَبَا ذَرٍّ مَنْ يَكْفِيكَ سَقْيَ الْحِمَارِ فَقَالَ سَمِعْتُ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ ( صلى الله عليه وآله ) يَقُولُ مَا مِنْ دَابَّةٍ إِلَّا وَ هِيَ تَسْأَلُ اللَّهَ كُلَّ صَبَاحٍ اللَّهُمَّ ارْزُقْنِي مَلِيكاً صَالِحاً يُشْبِعُنِي مِنَ الْعَلَفِ وَ يُرْوِينِي مِنَ الْمَاءِ وَ لَا يُكَلِّفُنِي فَوْقَ طَاقَتِي فَأَنَا أُحِبُّ أَنْ أَسْقِيَهُ بِنَفْسِي .

text: Al Husayn Bin Muhammad, from Moala Bin Muhammad, from Al Washa, from Tarkhan Al Nakhas who said, ‘I passed by Abu Abdullahasws and heasws had lodged at Al-Hira, so heasws said to me: ‘What is your occupation?’ I said, ‘Animal trader’. So heasws said: ‘Find a Fazaah mule for me’. I said, ‘May I be sacrificed for youasws! And what is Al-Fazaah?’ Heasws said: ‘Plain, of white belly, white thighs, white mouth’. I said, ‘By Allahazwj! I have not seen the likes of this description’. So I returned from hisasws presence, so after a while I entered the ditch, and there was a slave who had sat upon a mule of this description. So I asked the slave, ‘For whom is this mule?’ So he said, ‘For my master’. I said, ‘Would he sell it’. He said, ‘I do not know’. So I followed him until I came up to his master. So I bought it from him, and I came over with it to himasws(the Imamasws). So heasws said: ‘This is the description which Iasws wanted’. I said, ‘May I be sacrificed for youasws! Supplicate to Allahazwj for me’. So heasws said: ‘May Allahazwj Amplify your wealth and your children’. He (the narrator) said, ‘So I became to be of the most abundant of the people of Al-Kufa in wealth and children’.

citation.chapter: THE BOOK OF DOMESTIC ANIMALS (al-Kafi, vol 6), 9:2
citation.arabic_text: مَرَرْتُ بِأَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) وَ قَدْ نَزَلَ الْحِيرَةَ فَقَالَ لِي مَا عِلَاجُكَ قُلْتُ نَخَّاسٌ فَقَالَ أَصِبْ لِي بَغْلَةً فَضْحَاءَ قُلْتُ جُعِلْتُ فِدَاكَ وَ مَا الْفَضْحَاءُ قَالَ دَهْمَاءُ بَيْضَاءُ الْبَطْنِ بَيْضَاءُ الْأَفْحَاجِ بَيْضَاءُ الْجَحْفَلَةِ قَالَ فَقُلْتُ وَ اللَّهِ مَا رَأَيْتُ مِثْلَ هَذِهِ الصِّفَةِ فَرَجَعْتُ مِنْ عِنْدِهِ فَسَاعَةً دَخَلْتُ الْخَنْدَقَ إِذَا أَنَا غُلَامٌ قَدْ أَشْفَى عَلَى بَغْلَةٍ عَلَى هَذَا الصِّفَةِ فَسَأَلْتُ الْغُلَامَ لِمَنْ هَذِهِ الْبَغْلَةُ فَقَالَ لِمَوْلَايَ قُلْتُ يَبِيعُهَا قَالَ لَا أَدْرِي فَتَبِعْتُهُ حَتَّى أَتَيْتُ مَوْلَاهُ فَاشْتَرَيْتُهَا مِنْهُ وَ أَتَيْتُهُ بِهَا فَقَالَ هَذِهِ الصِّفَةُ الَّتِي أَرَدْتُهَا قُلْتُ جُعِلْتُ فِدَاكَ ادْعُ اللَّهَ لِي فَقَالَ أَكْثَرَ اللَّهُ مَالَكَ وَ وَلَدَكَ قَالَ فَصِرْتُ أَكْثَرَ أَهْلِ الْكُوفَةِ مَالًا وَ وَلَداً .

text: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Al Qasim Bin Yahya, from his grandfather Al Hassan Bin Rashid, from Muhammad Bin Muslim, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘Do not strike the animals upon their faces, for they Glorify with the Praise of Allah<sup>azwj</sup>’. He<sup>asws</sup> (the Imam<sup>asws</sup>) said in another Hadeeth: ‘Do not brand them (curse them and hit) in their faces’.

citation.chapter: THE BOOK OF DOMESTIC ANIMALS (al-Kafi, vol 6), 9:2
citation.arabic_text: قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ ( صلى الله عليه وآله ) لَا تَضْرِبُوا الدَّوَابَّ عَلَى وُجُوهِهَا فَإِنَّهَا تُسَبِّحُ بِحَمْدِ اللَّهِ . قَالَ وَ فِي حَدِيثٍ آخَرَ لَا تَسِمُوهَا فِي وُجُوهِهَا .
citation.translation: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Al Qasim Bin Yahya, from his grandfather Al Hassan Bin Rashid, from Muhammad Bin Muslim, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘Do not strike the animals upon their faces, for they Glorify with the Praise of Allah<sup>azwj</sup>’. He<sup>asws</sup> (the Imam<sup>asws</sup>) said in another Hadeeth: ‘Do not brand them (curse them and hit) in their faces’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: ضعيف وآخره مرسل - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (22/455)

text: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Ja’far Bin Muhammad Bin Yasaar, from Ubeydullah Al Dahqan, from Dorost, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘When the animal stumbles beneath the man, so he (the man) says to it, ‘May you be ruined’. It (the animal) says, ‘May the one (who is) disobedient to the Lord<sup>azwj</sup> be ruined’.

citation.chapter: THE BOOK OF DOMESTIC ANIMALS (al-Kafi, vol 6), 9:2
citation.arabic_text: قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ ( صلى الله عليه وآله ) إِذَا عَثَرَتِ الدَّابَّةُ تَحْتَ الرَّجُلِ فَقَالَ لَهَا تَعَسْتِ تَقُولُ تَعَسَ أَعْصَانَا لِلرَّبِّ.
citation.translation: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Ja’far Bin Muhammad Bin Yasaar, from Ubeydullah Al Dahqan, from Dorost, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘When the animal stumbles beneath the man, so he (the man) says to it, ‘May you be ruined’. It (the animal) says, ‘May the one (who is) disobedient to the Lord<sup>azwj</sup> be ruined’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: ضعيف على المشهور - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (2/456)

text: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ali Bin Ibrahim Al Ja’fary, raising it, said, ‘I asked Al-Sadiq<sup>asws</sup>, ‘When can I strike my animal under me?’ So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘When it does not walk under you like it walks to its feeding place’.

citation.chapter: THE BOOK OF DOMESTIC ANIMALS (al-Kafi, vol 6), 9:2
citation.arabic_text: سَأَلْتُ الصَّادِقَ ( عليه السلام ) مَتَى أَضْرِبُ دَابَّتِي تَحْتِي فَقَالَ إِذَا لَمْ تَمْشِ تَحْتَكَ كَمَشْيَتِهَا إِلَى مِذْوَدِهَا .
citation.translation: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ali Bin Ibrahim Al Ja’fary, raising it, said, ‘I asked Al-Sadiq<sup>asws</sup>, ‘When can I strike my animal under me?’ So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘When it does not walk under you like it walks to its feeding place’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: مرفوع وآخره مرسل - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (22/456)

text: And it is reported, (It has been narrated) from the Prophet<sup>saww</sup> having said: ‘Strike it (animal) upon the fleeing, and do not strike it upon the stumbling’.

citation.chapter: THE BOOK OF DOMESTIC ANIMALS (al-Kafi, vol 6), 9:2
citation.arabic_text: اضْرِبُوهَا عَلَى النِّفَارِ وَ لَا تَضْرِبُوهَا عَلَى الْعِثَارِ .
citation.translation: And it is reported, (It has been narrated) from the Prophet<sup>saww</sup> having said: ‘Strike it (animal) upon the fleeing, and do not strike it upon the stumbling’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: ضعيف على المشهور - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (22/456)

text: Humeyd Bin Ziyad, from Al Khashab, from Ibn Baqah, from Moaz Al Jowhary, from Amro Bin Jumie, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘Do not sit upon the animal with both feet hanging on one side, and do not take its back for a meeting place (to hold discussions while sitting upon it)’.

citation.chapter: THE BOOK OF DOMESTIC ANIMALS (al-Kafi, vol 6), 9:2
citation.arabic_text: قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ ( صلى الله عليه وآله ) لَا تَتَوَرَّكُوا عَلَى الدَّوَابِّ وَ لَا تَتَّخِذُوا ظُهُورَهَا مَجَالِسَ .
citation.translation: Humeyd Bin Ziyad, from Al Khashab, from Ibn Baqah, from Moaz Al Jowhary, from Amro Bin Jumie, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘Do not sit upon the animal with both feet hanging on one side, and do not take its back for a meeting place (to hold discussions while sitting upon it)’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: ضعيف على المشهور - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (22/457)

text: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Ibn Raib, from Abu Hamza who said, ‘Ali<sup>asws</sup> Bin Al-Husayn<sup>asws</sup> was saying: ‘Whatever the dullness of the animals may be, but it is not dull from four (matters) – its recognition of the Lord<sup>azwj</sup>, and its recognition with the death, and its recognition with the female and the male, and its recognition with the pasture from the cultivated’.

citation.chapter: THE BOOK OF DOMESTIC ANIMALS (al-Kafi, vol 6), 9:2
citation.arabic_text: كَانَ عَلِيُّ بْنُ الْحُسَيْنِ ( عليه السلام ) يَقُولُ مَا بَهِمَتِ الْبَهَائِمُ فَلَمْ تُبْهَمْ عَنْ أَرْبَعَةٍ مَعْرِفَتِهَا بِالرَّبِّ وَ مَعْرِفَتِهَا بِالْمَوْتِ وَ مَعْرِفَتِهَا بِالْأُنْثَى مِنَ الذَّكَرِ وَ مَعْرِفَتِهَا بِالْمَرْعَى عَنِ الْخِصْبِ .
citation.translation: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Ibn Raib, from Abu Hamza who said, ‘Ali<sup>asws</sup> Bin Al-Husayn<sup>asws</sup> was saying: ‘Whatever the dullness of the animals may be, but it is not dull from four (matters) – its recognition of the Lord<sup>azwj</sup>, and its recognition with the death, and its recognition with the female and the male, and its recognition with the pasture from the cultivated’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: ضعيف على المشهور - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (22/457)

text: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Al Nowfaly, from Al Sakuny, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘For everything is a sanctity, and a sanctity of the animals is in their faces’.

citation.chapter: THE BOOK OF DOMESTIC ANIMALS (al-Kafi, vol 6), 9:2
citation.arabic_text: لِكُلِّ شَيْ‏ءٍ حُرْمَةٌ وَ حُرْمَةُ الْبَهَائِمِ فِي وُجُوهِهَا .
citation.translation: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Al Nowfaly, from Al Sakuny, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘For everything is a sanctity, and a sanctity of the animals is in their faces’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: مجهول مرسل - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (22/457)

text: Abu Ali Al Ashary, from Muhammad Bin Abdul Jabbar, from Al Hajjal and Ibn Fazzal, from Yaqoub Bin Salim, from a man, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Whatever dullness of the animals may be from something, but it would not be dull upon four qualities – Recognising that there is a Creator for it, and recognising seeking of the sustenance, and recognising the male from the female, and fear of the death’.

citation.chapter: THE BOOK OF DOMESTIC ANIMALS (al-Kafi, vol 6), 9:2
citation.arabic_text: مَهْمَا أُبْهِمَ عَلَى الْبَهَائِمِ مِنْ شَيْ‏ءٍ فَلَا يُبْهَمُ عَلَيْهَا أَرْبَعَةُ خِصَالٍ مَعْرِفَةُ أَنَّ لَهَا خَالِقاً وَ مَعْرِفَةُ طَلَبِ الرِّزْقِ وَ مَعْرِفَةُ الذَّكَرِ مِنَ الْأُنْثَى وَ مَخَافَةُ الْمَوْتِ .
citation.translation: Abu Ali Al Ashary, from Muhammad Bin Abdul Jabbar, from Al Hajjal and Ibn Fazzal, from Yaqoub Bin Salim, from a man, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Whatever dullness of the animals may be from something, but it would not be dull upon four qualities – Recognising that there is a Creator for it, and recognising seeking of the sustenance, and recognising the male from the female, and fear of the death’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: ضعيف على المشهور - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (2/457)

text: Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Muhammad Bin Al Hassan Bin Shamoun, from Al Asam, from Misma’a Bin Abdul Malik, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘Strike it upon the fleeing but do not strike it upon the stumbling’.

citation.chapter: THE BOOK OF DOMESTIC ANIMALS (al-Kafi, vol 6), 9:2
citation.arabic_text: قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ ( صلى الله عليه وآله ) اضْرِبُوهَا عَلَى النِّفَارِ وَ لَا تَضْرِبُوهَا عَلَى الْعِثَارِ .
citation.translation: Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Muhammad Bin Al Hassan Bin Shamoun, from Al Asam, from Misma’a Bin Abdul Malik, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘Strike it upon the fleeing but do not strike it upon the stumbling’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: ضعيف - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (22/457)

text: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Al Qasim Bin Yahya, from his grandfather Al Hassan Bin Rashid, from Yaqoub Bin Ja’far who said, ‘I heard Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> saying: ‘Upon each nostril of the animal is a Satan<sup>la</sup>. So whenever one of you to bridle it, so he should Name Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic’.

citation.chapter: THE BOOK OF DOMESTIC ANIMALS (al-Kafi, vol 6), 9:2
citation.arabic_text: سَمِعْتُ أَبَا الْحَسَنِ ( عليه السلام ) يَقُولُ عَلَى كُلِّ مَنْخِرٍ مِنَ الدَّوَابِّ شَيْطَانٌ فَإِذَا أَرَادَ أَحَدُكُمْ أَنْ يُلْجِمَهَا فَلْيُسَمِّ اللَّهَ عَزَّ وَ جَلَّ .
citation.translation: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Al Qasim Bin Yahya, from his grandfather Al Hassan Bin Rashid, from Yaqoub Bin Ja’far who said, ‘I heard Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> saying: ‘Upon each nostril of the animal is a Satan<sup>la</sup>. So whenever one of you to bridle it, so he should Name Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: صحيح - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (22/457)

text: Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Ibn Raib, from Abu Ubeyda, (It has been narrated) from one of the two (5th or 6th Imamasws) having said: ‘Whichever animal disobeys its owner from bridling and flees, so let him recite in its ears, or upon it - [3:83] Is it other than Allah's Religion that they seek (to follow), and to Him submits whoever is in the skies and the earth, willingly or unwillingly, and to Him shall they be returning’.

citation.chapter: THE BOOK OF DOMESTIC ANIMALS (al-Kafi, vol 6), 9:2
citation.arabic_text: أَيُّمَا دَابَّةٍ اسْتَصْعَبَتْ عَلَى صَاحِبِهَا مِنْ لِجَامٍ وَ نِفَارٍ فَلْيَقْرَأْ فِي أُذُنِهَا أَوْ عَلَيْهَا أَ فَغَيْرَ دِينِ اللَّهِ يَبْغُونَ وَ لَهُ أَسْلَمَ مَنْ فِي السَّماواتِ وَ الْأَرْضِ طَوْعاً وَ كَرْهاً وَ إِلَيْهِ يُرْجَعُونَ .
citation.translation: Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Ibn Raib, from Abu Ubeyda, (It has been narrated) from one of the two (5th or 6th Imamasws) having said: ‘Whichever animal disobeys its owner from bridling and flees, so let him recite in its ears, or upon it - [3:83] Is it other than Allah's Religion that they seek (to follow), and to Him submits whoever is in the skies and the earth, willingly or unwillingly, and to Him shall they be returning’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: حسن - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (22/458)

text: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hisham Bin Salim who said, ‘Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘It is from the right that the rider says to the walker, ‘The road’ (Make way)’. And in another copy – ‘(He<sup>asws</sup> said): ‘It is from the inequity that the rider should be saying to the walker, ‘The road’ (Make way)’.

citation.chapter: THE BOOK OF DOMESTIC ANIMALS (al-Kafi, vol 6), 9:2
citation.arabic_text: قَالَ أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( صلوات الله عليه ) إِنَّ مِنَ الْحَقِّ أَنْ يَقُولَ الرَّاكِبُ لِلْمَاشِي الطَّرِيقَ . وَ فِي نُسْخَةٍ أُخْرَى إِنَّ مِنَ الْجَوْرِ أَنْ يَقُولَ الرَّاكِبُ لِلْمَاشِي الطَّرِيقَ .
citation.translation: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hisham Bin Salim who said, ‘Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘It is from the right that the rider says to the walker, ‘The road’ (Make way)’. And in another copy – ‘(He<sup>asws</sup> said): ‘It is from the inequity that the rider should be saying to the walker, ‘The road’ (Make way)’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: ضعيف - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (22/458)

text: And by his chain, said, ‘Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> went out and he<sup>asws</sup> was riding, so they (people) walked along with him<sup>asws</sup>. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Is there any need for you (to be fulfilled)?’ They said, ‘No, but we love it that we should be walking along with you<sup>asws</sup>’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Disperse, for the walking of the walker with the rider is a spoiler for the rider, and a humiliation for the walker’.

citation.chapter: THE BOOK OF DOMESTIC ANIMALS (al-Kafi, vol 6), 9:2
citation.arabic_text: وَ بِإِسْنَادِهِ قَالَ خَرَجَ أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ ( عليه السلام ) وَ هُوَ رَاكِبٌ فَمَشَوْا مَعَهُ فَقَالَ أَ لَكُمْ حَاجَةٌ قَالُوا لَا وَ لَكِنَّا نُحِبُّ أَنْ نَمْشِيَ مَعَكَ فَقَالَ لَهُمُ انْصَرِفُوا فَإِنَّ مَشْيَ الْمَاشِي مَعَ الرَّاكِبِ مَفْسَدَةٌ لِلرَّاكِبِ وَ مَذَلَّةٌ لِلْمَاشِي .
citation.translation: And by his chain, said, ‘Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> went out and he<sup>asws</sup> was riding, so they (people) walked along with him<sup>asws</sup>. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Is there any need for you (to be fulfilled)?’ They said, ‘No, but we love it that we should be walking along with you<sup>asws</sup>’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Disperse, for the walking of the walker with the rider is a spoiler for the rider, and a humiliation for the walker’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: مرفوع - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (2/459)

text: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from Muhammad Bin Isa, from Al Dahqan, from Dorost, from Ibrahim Bin Abdul Hameed, (It has been narrated) from Abu Al-Hassanasws having said: ‘Rasool-Allahsaww said: ‘When the man rides the animal, so he Names (Bismillah) and Angel rides behind him, protecting him until he descends; and when he rides and does not Name (Bismillah), a Satanla rides behind him, so hela is saying to him, ‘Sing!’ So if he says to himla, ‘I am not good at it’, hela says to him, ‘Wish for it’. So he does not cease wishing until he descends’. And heasws said: ‘The one who says whenever he rides the animal, ‘In the Name of Allahazwj, there is no Might or Strength except with Allahazwj, [7:43] All Praise is due to Allah Who Guided us to this, and we would not have found the Way had it not been that Allah had Guided us, [43:13] Glory be to Him Who Made this subservient to us and we were not able to do it’, Allahazwj would Protect for him his self, and his animal until he descends’.

citation.chapter: THE BOOK OF DOMESTIC ANIMALS (al-Kafi, vol 6), 9:2
citation.arabic_text: قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ ( صلى الله عليه وآله ) إِذَا رَكِبَ الرَّجُلُ الدَّابَّةَ فَسَمَّى رَدِفَهُ مَلَكٌ يَحْفَظُهُ حَتَّى يَنْزِلَ وَ إِذَا رَكِبَ وَ لَمْ يُسَمِّ رَدِفَهُ شَيْطَانٌ فَيَقُولُ لَهُ تَغَنَّ فَإِنْ قَالَ لَهُ لَا أُحْسِنُ قَالَ لَهُ تَمَنَّ فَلَا يَزَالُ يَتَمَنَّى حَتَّى يَنْزِلَ وَ قَالَ مَنْ قَالَ إِذَا رَكِبَ الدَّابَّةَ بِسْمِ اللَّهِ لَا حَوْلَ وَ لَا قُوَّةَ إِلَّا بِاللَّهِ الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ الَّذِي هَدانا لِهذا الْآيَةَ وَ سُبْحانَ الَّذِي سَخَّرَ لَنا هذا وَ ما كُنَّا لَهُ مُقْرِنِينَ حُفِظَتْ لَهُ نَفْسُهُ وَ دَابَّتُهُ حَتَّى يَنْزِلَ .
citation.translation: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from Muhammad Bin Isa, from Al Dahqan, from Dorost, from Ibrahim Bin Abdul Hameed, (It has been narrated) from Abu Al-Hassanasws having said: ‘Rasool-Allahsaww said: ‘When the man rides the animal, so he Names (Bismillah) and Angel rides behind him, protecting him until he descends; and when he rides and does not Name (Bismillah), a Satanla rides behind him, so hela is saying to him, ‘Sing!’ So if he says to himla, ‘I am not good at it’, hela says to him, ‘Wish for it’. So he does not cease wishing until he descends’. And heasws said: ‘The one who says whenever he rides the animal, ‘In the Name of Allahazwj, there is no Might or Strength except with Allahazwj, [7:43] All Praise is due to Allah Who Guided us to this, and we would not have found the Way had it not been that Allah had Guided us, [43:13] Glory be to Him Who Made this subservient to us and we were not able to do it’, Allahazwj would Protect for him his self, and his animal until he descends’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: مرفوع - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (2/459)

text: Ali Bin Ibrahim, or someone else, raising it, said, ‘Abdul Samam Bin Ali went out and with him was a group of people, so he saw Abu Al Hassan Musa Bin Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> riding a mule towards him. So he said to the ones who were with him, ‘Stay in your places until I make you laugh from Musa<sup>asws</sup> Bin Ja’far<sup>asws</sup>’. So when he approached him<sup>asws</sup>, said to him<sup>asws</sup>, ‘What is this animal upon which neither can the vengeance be realised nor is it correct for the battleground’. So Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> said to him: ‘I<sup>asws</sup> have come down from the elevation of the cavalry horse and have exceeded the lowliness of the wild ass, and the best of the affairs is in its middle’. So Abdul Samad was speechless and could not responded with an answer’.

citation.chapter: THE BOOK OF DOMESTIC ANIMALS (al-Kafi, vol 6), 9:2
citation.arabic_text: خَرَجَ عَبْدُ الصَّمَدِ بْنُ عَلِيٍّ وَ مَعَهُ جَمَاعَةٌ فَبَصُرَ بِأَبِي الْحَسَنِ مُوسَى بْنِ جَعْفَرٍ ( عليه السلام ) مُقْبِلًا رَاكِباً بَغْلًا فَقَالَ لِمَنْ مَعَهُ مَكَانَكُمْ حَتَّى أُضْحِكَكُمْ مِنْ مُوسَى بْنِ جَعْفَرٍ فَلَمَّا دَنَا مِنْهُ قَالَ لَهُ مَا هَذِهِ الدَّابَّةُ الَّتِي لَا تُدْرِكُ عَلَيْهَا الثَّأْرَ وَ لَا تَصْلُحُ عِنْدَ النِّزَالِ فَقَالَ لَهُ أَبُو الْحَسَنِ ( عليه السلام ) تَطَأْطَأَتْ عَنْ سُمُوِّ الْخَيْلِ وَ تَجَاوَزَتْ قُمُوءَ الْعَيْرِ وَ خَيْرُ الْأُمُورِ أَوْسَطُهَا فَأُفْحِمَ عَبْدُ الصَّمَدِ فَمَا أَحَارَ جَوَاباً .
citation.translation: Ali Bin Ibrahim, or someone else, raising it, said, ‘Abdul Samam Bin Ali went out and with him was a group of people, so he saw Abu Al Hassan Musa Bin Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> riding a mule towards him. So he said to the ones who were with him, ‘Stay in your places until I make you laugh from Musa<sup>asws</sup> Bin Ja’far<sup>asws</sup>’. So when he approached him<sup>asws</sup>, said to him<sup>asws</sup>, ‘What is this animal upon which neither can the vengeance be realised nor is it correct for the battleground’. So Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> said to him: ‘I<sup>asws</sup> have come down from the elevation of the cavalry horse and have exceeded the lowliness of the wild ass, and the best of the affairs is in its middle’. So Abdul Samad was speechless and could not responded with an answer’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: سكت عنه - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (2/457)

text: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Abu Abdullah, from a number of our companions, from Ali Bin Asbaat, from his uncle Yaqoub Bin Salim, raising it, said, ‘Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘Three must not ride upon one animal, for one of them would be an Accursed’.

citation.chapter: THE BOOK OF DOMESTIC ANIMALS (al-Kafi, vol 6), 9:2
citation.arabic_text: قَالَ أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ ( صلوات الله عليه ) قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ ( صلى الله عليه وآله ) لَا يَرْتَدِفْ ثَلَاثَةٌ عَلَى دَابَّةٍ فَإِنَّ أَحَدَهُمْ مَلْعُونٌ .
citation.translation: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Abu Abdullah, from a number of our companions, from Ali Bin Asbaat, from his uncle Yaqoub Bin Salim, raising it, said, ‘Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘Three must not ride upon one animal, for one of them would be an Accursed’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: سكت عنه - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (2/459)

text: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from one of his companions, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘The saddle riding is detestable for the women’.

citation.chapter: THE BOOK OF DOMESTIC ANIMALS (al-Kafi, vol 6), 9:3
citation.arabic_text: السَّرْجُ مَرْكَبٌ مَلْعُونٌ لِلنِّسَاءِ.
citation.translation: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from one of his companions, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘The saddle riding is detestable for the women’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: حسن - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (22/459)

text: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Khalid, from Usman Bin Isa, from Sama’at who said, ‘Abu Abdullahasws was asked about skins of the predatory animals, so heasws said: ‘Ride in them but do not wear anything from these while offering Salaat (Praying in them)’.

citation.chapter: THE BOOK OF DOMESTIC ANIMALS (al-Kafi, vol 6), 9:3
citation.arabic_text: سُئِلَ أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) عَنْ جُلُودِ السِّبَاعِ فَقَالَ ارْكَبُوهَا وَ لَا تَلْبَسُوا شَيْئاً مِنْهَا تُصَلُّونَ فِيهِ .
citation.translation: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Khalid, from Usman Bin Isa, from Sama’at who said, ‘Abu Abdullahasws was asked about skins of the predatory animals, so heasws said: ‘Ride in them but do not wear anything from these while offering Salaat (Praying in them)’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: موثق - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (22/460)

text: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Al Amraky Bin Ali, (It has been narrated) from Ali<sup>asws</sup> son of Ja’far<sup>asws</sup>, from his brother<sup>asws</sup> Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup>, said, ‘I asked him<sup>asws</sup> about the saddle and the reins where is the silver, can one ride with it?’ So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘If it is coated on and you are not able to remove it, so there is no problem, otherwise do not ride with it’.

citation.chapter: THE BOOK OF DOMESTIC ANIMALS (al-Kafi, vol 6), 9:3
citation.arabic_text: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنِ السَّرْجِ وَ اللِّجَامِ فِيهِ الْفِضَّةُ أَ يُرْكَبُ بِهِ فَقَالَ إِنْ كَانَ مُمَوَّهاً لَا يُقْدَرُ عَلَى نَزْعِهِ فَلَا بَأْسَ وَ إِلَّا فَلَا تَرْكَبْ بِهِ .
citation.translation: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Al Amraky Bin Ali, (It has been narrated) from Ali<sup>asws</sup> son of Ja’far<sup>asws</sup>, from his brother<sup>asws</sup> Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup>, said, ‘I asked him<sup>asws</sup> about the saddle and the reins where is the silver, can one ride with it?’ So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘If it is coated on and you are not able to remove it, so there is no problem, otherwise do not ride with it’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: صحيح - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (22/460)

text: Abu Ali Al Ashary, from Muhammad Bin Abdul Jabbar, from Al Hajjal, from Safwan Al Jamaal who said, ‘Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Had the people known the true nature of the carriers as Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Made (Bearing the load) for the weak, they would not consider the animals as expensive’.

citation.chapter: THE BOOK OF DOMESTIC ANIMALS (al-Kafi, vol 6), 9:4
citation.arabic_text: قَالَ أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) لَوْ يَعْلَمُ النَّاسُ كُنْهَ حُمْلَانِ اللَّهِ لِلضَّعِيفِ مَا غَالَوْا بِبَهِيمَةٍ .
citation.translation: Abu Ali Al Ashary, from Muhammad Bin Abdul Jabbar, from Al Hajjal, from Safwan Al Jamaal who said, ‘Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Had the people known the true nature of the carriers as Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Made (Bearing the load) for the weak, they would not consider the animals as expensive’.

text: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Giyas Bin Ibrahim, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said; ‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘At the highest point of every camel is a Satan<sup>la</sup>, therefore degrade him and humiliate him to yourselves, and mention the Name of Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, for rather the carrier is (a Gift from) Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic’.

citation.chapter: THE BOOK OF DOMESTIC ANIMALS (al-Kafi, vol 6), 9:4
citation.arabic_text: قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ ( صلى الله عليه وآله ) إِنَّ عَلَى ذِرْوَةِ كُلِّ بَعِيرٍ شَيْطَاناً فَامْتَهِنُوهَا لِأَنْفُسِكُمْ وَ ذَلِّلُوهَا وَ اذْكُرُوا اسْمَ اللَّهِ فَإِنَّمَا يَحْمِلُ اللَّهُ عَزَّ وَ جَلَّ .
citation.translation: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Giyas Bin Ibrahim, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said; ‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘At the highest point of every camel is a Satan<sup>la</sup>, therefore degrade him and humiliate him to yourselves, and mention the Name of Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, for rather the carrier is (a Gift from) Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: موثق - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (22/462)

text: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hisham Bin Al Hakam, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Had the Pilgrim known what is for him from the carriers, no one would consider the camel to be expensive’.

citation.chapter: THE BOOK OF DOMESTIC ANIMALS (al-Kafi, vol 6), 9:4
citation.arabic_text: لَوْ يَعْلَمُ الْحَاجُّ مَا لَهُ مِنَ الْحُمْلَانِ مَا غَالَ أَحَدٌ بِبَعِيرٍ .

citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: حسن - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (22/462)

text: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Abu Abdullah, from his father, from Muhamad Bin Amro, from Suleyman Al Rahhal, from Abdullah Bin Abu Yafour who said, ‘I passed by Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> and I was walking in the presence of my she-camel, so he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘What is the matter you are not riding? ‘ So I said, ‘My camel has weakened, so I wanted to lighten from it’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘May Allah<sup>azwj</sup> have Mercy on you! Ride, for Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Carries from the weak and the strong’.

citation.chapter: THE BOOK OF DOMESTIC ANIMALS (al-Kafi, vol 6), 9:4
citation.arabic_text: مَرَّ بِي أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) وَ أَنَا أَمْشِي عَرْضَ نَاقَتِي فَقَالَ مَا لَكَ لَا تَرْكَبُ فَقُلْتُ ضَعُفَتْ نَاقَتِي فَأَرَدْتُ أَنْ أُخَفِّفَ عَنْهَا فَقَالَ رَحِمَكَ اللَّهُ ارْكَبْ فَإِنَّ اللَّهَ يَحْمِلُ عَنِ الضَّعِيفِ وَ الْقَوِيِّ .
citation.translation: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Abu Abdullah, from his father, from Muhamad Bin Amro, from Suleyman Al Rahhal, from Abdullah Bin Abu Yafour who said, ‘I passed by Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> and I was walking in the presence of my she-camel, so he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘What is the matter you are not riding? ‘ So I said, ‘My camel has weakened, so I wanted to lighten from it’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘May Allah<sup>azwj</sup> have Mercy on you! Ride, for Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Carries from the weak and the strong’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: مجهول - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (2/462)

text: From him, from his father, from the one who mentioned it, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> forbade cross the line (of the camels). So it was said, ‘O Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup>! And why?’ He<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘There is none from the line except and what is between the camel to the camel is a Satan<sup>la</sup>’.

citation.chapter: THE BOOK OF DOMESTIC ANIMALS (al-Kafi, vol 6), 9:4
citation.arabic_text: نَهَى رَسُولُ اللَّهِ ( صلى الله عليه وآله ) أَنْ يُتَخَطَّى الْقِطَارُ قِيلَ يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ وَ لِمَ قَالَ إِنَّهُ لَيْسَ مِنْ قِطَارٍ إِلَّا وَ مَا بَيْنَ الْبَعِيرِ إِلَى الْبَعِيرِ شَيْطَانٌ .
citation.translation: From him, from his father, from the one who mentioned it, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> forbade cross the line (of the camels). citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: مرسل - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (2/462)

text: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Husayn Bin Umar Bin Yazeed, from his father who said, ‘I bought a camel and I was staying at Al-Medina, so it fascinated me with an intense fascination. So I went over to Abu Al-Hassanasws and mentioned it to himasws. So heasws said: ‘What is it to you and the camel? But, do you not know that it is with a lot of difficulties?’ He (the narrator) said, ‘So, from my fascination with it, I hired it out and sent two slaves of mine with it to Al-Kufa. So all of it was fruitless. So I went over to himasws and informed himasws, so heasws said: ‘[24:63] therefore let those beware who go against his order lest a trial afflict them or there befalls upon them a painful Punishment’.

text: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Khalid, from Al Hajjal, form Safwan Al Jammal who said, ‘Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘O Safwan! Buy a camel for me<sup>asws</sup> and take it as deformed, for it is something which is of longer life-span’. So I bought a camel for him<sup>asws</sup> with eighty Dirhams, and went over to him<sup>asws</sup> with it’. And in another Hadeeth - ‘He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Buy the black, the ugly, for it is something with a longer life-span’.

citation.chapter: THE BOOK OF DOMESTIC ANIMALS (al-Kafi, vol 6), 9:4
citation.arabic_text: قَالَ أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) يَا صَفْوَانُ اشْتَرِ لِي جَمَلًا وَ خُذْهُ أَشْوَهَ فَإِنَّهُ أَطْوَلُ شَيْ‏ءٍ أَعْمَاراً فَاشْتَرَيْتُ لَهُ جَمَلًا بِثَمَانِينَ دِرْهَماً فَأَتَيْتُهُ بِهِ . وَ فِي حَدِيثٍ آخَرَ قَالَ اشْتَرِ السُّودَ الْقِبَاحَ فَإِنَّهَا أَطْوَلُ شَيْ‏ءٍ أَعْمَاراً .
citation.translation: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Khalid, from Al Hajjal, form Safwan Al Jammal who said, ‘Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘O Safwan! Buy a camel for me<sup>asws</sup> and take it as deformed, for it is something which is of longer life-span’. So I bought a camel for him<sup>asws</sup> with eighty Dirhams, and went over to him<sup>asws</sup> with it’. And in another Hadeeth - ‘He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Buy the black, the ugly, for it is something with a longer life-span’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: صحيح - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (22/462)

text: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Ja’far Bin Muhammad, (It has been narrated) from Ibn Al-Qaddah, from Abu Abdullahasws, and from his father Maymoun who said, ‘We went out with Abu Ja’farasws to the land of Tayba and with himasws was Amro Bin Dinar, and a group of hisasws companions. So we stayed at Tayba for as long as Allahazwj so Deisred, and Abu Ja’farasws rode upon a difficult camel. So Amro Bin Dinar said to himasws, ‘How difficult is yourasws camel’. So heasws said: ‘Or do you not know that Rasool-Allahsaww said: ‘Upon the peak of every camel is a Satanla, therefore disgrace it and humiliated it, and mention the Name of Allahazwj upon it, for rather it is (the Strength of) Allahazwj Who Carries’. Then heasws entered Makkah and we entered with himasws without Ihraam’.

text: And by this chain, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘When the family takes a sheep, Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Grant them its sustenance and increases in their sustenance, and the poverty departs from them with a departing. So if they were to take two sheep, Allah<sup>azwj</sup> would Grant them sustenance for both of them and increase in their sustenance, and the poverty would depart from them with departing twice. So if they were to take three, Allah<sup>azwj</sup> would Grant the their sustenance, and the poverty would depart from them at the onset’.

citation.chapter: THE BOOK OF DOMESTIC ANIMALS (al-Kafi, vol 6), 9:5
citation.arabic_text: إِذَا اتَّخَذَ أَهْلُ بَيْتٍ شَاةً أَتَاهُمُ اللَّهُ بِرِزْقِهَا وَ زَادَ فِي أَرْزَاقِهِمْ وَ ارْتَحَلَ الْفَقْرُ عَنْهُمْ مَرْحَلَةً فَإِنِ اتَّخَذَ شَاتَيْنِ أَتَاهُمُ اللَّهُ بِأَرْزَاقِهِمَا وَ زَادَ فِي أَرْزَاقِهِمْ وَ ارْتَحَلَ الْفَقْرُ عَنْهُمْ مَرْحَلَتَيْنِ فَإِنِ اتَّخَذُوا ثَلَاثَةً أَتَاهُمُ اللَّهُ بِأَرْزَاقِهِمْ وَ ارْتَحَلَ الْفَقْرُ عَنْهُمْ رَأْساً .

So if they were to take two sheep, Allah<sup>azwj</sup> would Grant them sustenance for both of them and increase in their sustenance, and the poverty would depart from them with departing twice. So if they were to take three, Allah<sup>azwj</sup> would Grant the their sustenance, and the poverty would depart from them at the onset’.

text: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Abdullah Bin Sinan, from Muhammad Bin Ajlan who said, ‘I heard Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> saying: ‘There is none from a family which happens to have a sheep with them for milking except it is sanctified twice every day’. I said, ‘And how is it said to them?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘It is said to them: ‘You are Blessed! You are Blessed!’

citation.chapter: THE BOOK OF DOMESTIC ANIMALS (al-Kafi, vol 6), 9:5
citation.arabic_text: سَمِعْتُ أَبَا جَعْفَرٍ ( عليه السلام ) يَقُولُ مَا مِنْ أَهْلِ بَيْتٍ يَكُونُ عِنْدَهُمْ شَاةٌ لَبُونٌ إِلَّا قُدِّسُوا فِي كُلِّ يَوْمٍ مَرَّتَيْنِ قُلْتُ وَ كَيْفَ يُقَالُ لَهُمْ قَالَ يُقَالُ لَهُمْ بُورِكْتُمْ بُورِكْتُمْ .
citation.translation: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Abdullah Bin Sinan, from Muhammad Bin Ajlan who said, ‘I heard Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> saying: ‘There is none from a family which happens to have a sheep with them for milking except it is sanctified twice every day’. citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: حسن - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (22/464)

text: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Ibn Mahboub, from Muhammad Bin Marad who said, ‘I heard Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> saying: ‘There is none from a Believer what happens to have a dairy goat in his home, except the inhabitants of that home are sanctified and Blessings are upon them. So if there were to be two, so they are sanctified and Blessings are upon them twice every day’. So one of our companions said, ‘And how are they sanctified?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘An Angels pauses over them during every morning, so he is saying to them: ‘You are sanctified, and Blessings are upon you, and you are (made to be) good, and your sauce is (made to be) good’. I said to him<sup>asws</sup>, ‘And what is the meaning of ‘You are sanctified’?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘You are purified (from sins)’.

citation.chapter: THE BOOK OF DOMESTIC ANIMALS (al-Kafi, vol 6), 9:5
citation.arabic_text: سَمِعْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) يَقُولُ مَا مِنْ مُؤْمِنٍ يَكُونُ فِي مَنْزِلِهِ عَنْزٌ حَلُوبٌ إِلَّا قُدِّسَ أَهْلُ ذَلِكَ الْمَنْزِلِ وَ بُورِكَ عَلَيْهِمْ فَإِنْ كَانَتَا اثْنَتَيْنِ قُدِّسُوا وَ بُورِكَ عَلَيْهِمْ فِي كُلِّ يَوْمٍ مَرَّتَيْنِ قَالَ فَقَالَ بَعْضُ أَصْحَابِنَا وَ كَيْفَ يُقَدَّسُونَ قَالَ يَقِفُ عَلَيْهِمْ مَلَكٌ فِي كُلِّ صَبَاحٍ فَيَقُولُ لَهُمْ قُدِّسْتُمْ وَ بُورِكَ عَلَيْكُمْ وَ طِبْتُمْ وَ طَابَ إِدَامُكُمْ قَالَ قُلْتُ لَهُ وَ مَا مَعْنَى قُدِّسْتُمْ قَالَ طُهِّرْتُمْ .

So one of our companions said, ‘And how are they sanctified?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘An Angels pauses over them during every morning, so he is saying to them: ‘You are sanctified, and Blessings are upon you, and you are (made to be) good, and your sauce is (made to be) good’. text: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Khalid, form Ibn Abu Najran, from Abu Jameela, from Jabir, (It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said to his<sup>saww</sup> paternal aunt: ‘What prevents you from taking Blessings to be in your house?’ She said, ‘O Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup>! citation.chapter: THE BOOK OF DOMESTIC ANIMALS (al-Kafi, vol 6), 9:5
citation.arabic_text: قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ ( صلى الله عليه وآله ) لِعَمَّتِهِ مَا يَمْنَعُكِ أَنْ تَتَّخِذِي فِي بَيْتِكِ بَرَكَةً قَالَتْ يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ وَ مَا الْبَرَكَةُ قَالَ شَاةٌ تُحْلَبُ فَإِنَّهُ مَنْ كَانَ فِي دَارِهِ شَاةٌ تُحْلَبُ أَوْ نَعْجَةٌ أَوْ بَقَرَةٌ تُحْلَبُ فَبَرَكَاتٌ كُلُّهُنَّ .

text: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, form Hammad, from Hareyz, from Abu Al Jaroud, (It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> went over to Umm Salma<sup>as</sup>, so he<sup>saww</sup> said to her<sup>as</sup>: ‘I<sup>saww</sup> do not see the blessing in your<sup>as</sup> room’. text: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Abu Abdullah, from his father, from Suleyman Al Ja’fary, (It has been narrated) raising it to Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘There is none from a family to whom thirty sheep unwind, except that the Angels do not cease to enclose them until the morning’.

citation.chapter: THE BOOK OF DOMESTIC ANIMALS (al-Kafi, vol 6), 9:5
citation.arabic_text: مَا مِنْ أَهْلِ بَيْتٍ تَرُوحُ عَلَيْهِمْ ثَلَاثُونَ شَاةً إِلَّا لَمْ تَزَلِ الْمَلَائِكَةُ تَحْرُسُهُمْ حَتَّى يُصْبِحُوا .

text: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Yunus Bin Yaqoub who said, ‘I said to Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, ‘Can I brand the sheep in their faces?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Brand them in their ears’.

citation.arabic_text: قُلْتُ لِأَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) أَسِمُ الْغَنَمَ فِي وُجُوهِهَا قَالَ سِمْهَا فِي آذَانِهَا .
citation.translation: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Yunus Bin Yaqoub who said, ‘I said to Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, ‘Can I brand the sheep in their faces?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Brand them in their ears’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: موثق - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (22/466)

text: Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Abdullah Bin Sinan who said, ‘I asked Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> about branding the livestock, so he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘There is no problem with it except in their faces’.

citation.chapter: THE BOOK OF DOMESTIC ANIMALS (al-Kafi, vol 6), 9:6
citation.arabic_text: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) عَنْ سِمَةِ الْمَوَاشِي فَقَالَ لَا بَأْسَ بِهَا إِلَّا فِي الْوُجُوهِ .
citation.translation: Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Abdullah Bin Sinan who said, ‘I asked Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> about branding the livestock, so he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘There is no problem with it except in their faces’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: صحيح - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (22/466)

text: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Al Hakam, and Ibn Mahboub, from Muawiya Bin Wahab who said, ‘The pigeon is from the birds of the Prophets<sup>as</sup>’.

citation.chapter: THE BOOK OF DOMESTIC ANIMALS (al-Kafi, vol 6), 9:7
citation.arabic_text: الْحَمَامُ مِنْ طُيُورِ الْأَنْبِيَاءِ ( عليهم السلام ) .
citation.translation: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Al Hakam, and Ibn Mahboub, from Muawiya Bin Wahab who said, ‘The pigeon is from the birds of the Prophets<sup>as</sup>’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: صحيح - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (22/467)

text: Al Husayn Bin Muhammad, from Moala Bin Muhammad, from Al Washa, from Hammad Bin usman, form Abdul A’ala, a slave of the progeny of Sam who sai, ‘I heard Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> saying that: ‘The first pigeon which was at Makkah was a pigeon of Ismail<sup>as</sup>’.

citation.chapter: THE BOOK OF DOMESTIC ANIMALS (al-Kafi, vol 6), 9:7
citation.arabic_text: سَمِعْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) يَقُولُ إِنَّ أَوَّلَ حَمَامٍ كَانَ بِمَكَّةَ حَمَامٌ لِإِسْمَاعِيلَ ( عليه السلام ) .
citation.translation: Al Husayn Bin Muhammad, from Moala Bin Muhammad, from Al Washa, from Hammad Bin usman, form Abdul A’ala, a slave of the progeny of Sam who sai, ‘I heard Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> saying that: ‘The first pigeon which was at Makkah was a pigeon of Ismail<sup>as</sup>’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: ضعيف على المشهور - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (2/467)

text: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, form Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hafs Bin Al Bakhtary, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘The original pigeon of the Sanctuary of the rest of the pigeons was for Ismail<sup>as</sup> Bin Ibrahim<sup>as</sup>. citation.arabic_text: إِنَّ أَصْلَ حَمَامِ الْحَرَمِ بَقِيَّةُ حَمَامٍ كَانَ لِإِسْمَاعِيلَ بْنِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ ( عليه السلام ) اتَّخَذَهَا كَانَ يَأْنَسُ بِهَا فَقَالَ أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) يُسْتَحَبُّ أَنْ تَتَّخِذَ طَيْراً مَقْصُوصاً تَأْنَسُ بِهِ مَخَافَةَ الْهَوَامِّ .

He<sup>as</sup> took it as he<sup>as</sup> was comfortable with it’. So Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘It is recommended for you to take a clipped bird to be comfortable with it, if fear of the vermin’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: حسن - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (2/467)

text: Ali Bin Muhammad, from Salih Bin Abu Hammad, from Al Washa, from Ahmad Bin A’aiz, from Abu Khadeeja who said, ‘I heard Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> saying: ‘This pigeon here, pigeon of the Sanctuary, it is from the lineage of a pigeon of Ismail<sup>as</sup> Bin Ibrahim<sup>as</sup> which was for him<sup>as</sup>’.

text: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from Muhammad Bin Isa, from Ubeydullah Al Dahqan, from Dorost, from Abdullah Bin Sinan, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘A man complained to Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> of loneliness, so he<sup>saww</sup> ordered him to take in his house, a pair of pigeons’.

text: A number of our companions, form Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Abu Abdullah Al Jamourany, from Al Hassan Bin Ali Bin Abu Hamza, from his father, from Sandal, from Zayd Al Shahaam who said, ‘I mentioned the pigeon in the presence of Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, so he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Take these to be in your houses, for these are beloved. The supplication of Noah<sup>as</sup> has been attached to it, and it is a comforting thing in the house’.

citation.chapter: THE BOOK OF DOMESTIC ANIMALS (al-Kafi, vol 6), 9:7
citation.arabic_text: ذُكِرَتِ الْحَمَامُ عِنْدَ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) فَقَالَ اتَّخِذُوهَا فِي مَنَازِلِكُمْ فَإِنَّهَا مَحْبُوبَةٌ لَحِقَتْهَا دَعْوَةُ نُوحٍ ( عليه السلام ) وَ هِيَ آنَسُ شَيْ‏ءٍ فِي الْبُيُوتِ .
citation.translation: A number of our companions, form Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Abu Abdullah Al Jamourany, from Al Hassan Bin Ali Bin Abu Hamza, from his father, from Sandal, from Zayd Al Shahaam who said, ‘I mentioned the pigeon in the presence of Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, so he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Take these to be in your houses, for these are beloved. text: Al Husayn Bin Muhammad, from Moala Bin Muhammad, from Al Washa, from a man, from Umar Bin Yazeed, from Abu Salma who said, ‘Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The pigeon is a bird from the birds of the Prophets<sup>as</sup> which they<sup>as</sup> were keeping in their<sup>as</sup> houses, and there is none from a house wherein is a pigeon, except that its inhabitants would not be hit by an affliction from the Jinn. The foolish ones from the Jinn are tampering in the house, so they would be tampering with the pigeons instead and leave the people’. He (the narrator) said, ‘So I saw in the rooms of Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, a pigeon for his<sup>asws</sup> son Ismail’.

citation.chapter: THE BOOK OF DOMESTIC ANIMALS (al-Kafi, vol 6), 9:7
citation.arabic_text: قَالَ أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) الْحَمَامُ طَيْرٌ مِنْ طُيُورِ الْأَنْبِيَاءِ ( عليهم السلام ) الَّتِي كَانُوا يُمْسِكُونَ فِي بُيُوتِهِمْ وَ لَيْسَ مِنْ بَيْتٍ فِيهِ حَمَامٌ إِلَّا لَمْ تُصِبْ أَهْلَ ذَلِكَ الْبَيْتِ آفَةٌ مِنَ الْجِنِّ إِنَّ سُفَهَاءَ الْجِنِّ يَعْبَثُونَ فِي الْبَيْتِ فَيَعْبَثُونَ بِالْحَمَامِ وَ يَدَعُونَ النَّاسَ قَالَ فَرَأَيْتُ فِي بُيُوتِ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) حَمَاماً لِابْنِهِ إِسْمَاعِيلَ .
citation.translation: Al Husayn Bin Muhammad, from Moala Bin Muhammad, from Al Washa, from a man, from Umar Bin Yazeed, from Abu Salma who said, ‘Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The pigeon is a bird from the birds of the Prophets<sup>as</sup> which they<sup>as</sup> were keeping in their<sup>as</sup> houses, and there is none from a house wherein is a pigeon, except that its inhabitants would not be hit by an affliction from the Jinn. The foolish ones from the Jinn are tampering in the house, so they would be tampering with the pigeons instead and leave the people’. He (the narrator) said, ‘So I saw in the rooms of Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, a pigeon for his<sup>asws</sup> son Ismail’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: ضعيف على المشهور - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (22/468)

text: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Al Qasim Bin Yahya, from his grandfather Al Hassan Bin Rashid, from Yaqoub Bin Ja’far who said, ‘Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> said, and he<sup>asws</sup> looked at the pigeons in his<sup>asws</sup> house: ‘There is none from a twitching which it twitches by, except Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Repel by it the ones who enter the house from the determined ones (with evil intentions) of the people of the earth’.

citation.chapter: THE BOOK OF DOMESTIC ANIMALS (al-Kafi, vol 6), 9:7
citation.arabic_text: قَالَ أَبُو الْحَسَنِ ( عليه السلام ) وَ نَظَرَ إِلَى حَمَامٍ فِي بَيْتِهِ مَا مِنِ انْتِفَاضٍ يَنْتَفِضُ بِهَا إِلَّا نَفَّرَ اللَّهُ بِهَا مَنْ دَخَلَ الْبَيْتَ مِنْ عُزْمَةِ أَهْلِ الْأَرْضِ .
citation.translation: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Al Qasim Bin Yahya, from his grandfather Al Hassan Bin Rashid, from Yaqoub Bin Ja’far who said, ‘Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> said, and he<sup>asws</sup> looked at the pigeons in his<sup>asws</sup> house: ‘There is none from a twitching which it twitches by, except Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Repel by it the ones who enter the house from the determined ones (with evil intentions) of the people of the earth’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: ضعيف على المشهور - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (22/468)

text: From him, from Al Jamourany, form Ibn Abu Hamza, from Sandal, from Dawood Bin Farqad who said, ‘I was seated in the house of Abu Abdullahasws, so I looked at an Al-Ra’aiby pigeon cooing for a long time. So Abu Abdullahasws looked at me, so heasws said: ‘O Dawood! Do you know what this bird is saying?’ I said, ‘No, by Allahazwj, may I be sacrificed for youasws’. Heasws said: ‘It is supplicating against the killers of Al-Husaynasws, therefore take it to be in your houses’.

citation.chapter: THE BOOK OF DOMESTIC ANIMALS (al-Kafi, vol 6), 9:7
citation.arabic_text: كُنْتُ جَالِساً فِي بَيْتِ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) فَنَظَرْتُ إِلَى حَمَامٍ رَاعِبِيٍّ يُقَرْقِرُ طَوِيلًا فَنَظَرَ إِلَيَّ أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) فَقَالَ يَا دَاوُدُ تَدْرِي مَا يَقُولُ هَذَا الطَّيْرُ قُلْتُ لَا وَ اللَّهِ جُعِلْتُ فِدَاكَ قَالَ يَدْعُو عَلَى قَتَلَةِ الْحُسَيْنِ ( عليه السلام ) فَاتَّخِذُوا فِي مَنَازِلِكُمْ .
citation.translation: From him, from Al Jamourany, form Ibn Abu Hamza, from Sandal, from Dawood Bin Farqad who said, ‘I was seated in the house of Abu Abdullahasws, so I looked at an Al-Ra’aiby pigeon cooing for a long time. citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: ضعيف - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (2/469)

text: From him, from Muhammad Bin Ali, from a man, from Yahya Al Azraq who said, ‘I heard Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> saying: ‘The swishing of the wings of the pigeons expels the satans<sup>la</sup>’.

citation.chapter: THE BOOK OF DOMESTIC ANIMALS (al-Kafi, vol 6), 9:7
citation.arabic_text: سَمِعْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) يَقُولُ إِنَّ حَفِيفَ أَجْنِحَةِ الْحَمَامِ لَتَطْرُدُ الشَّيَاطِينَ .
citation.translation: From him, from Muhammad Bin Ali, from a man, from Yahya Al Azraq who said, ‘I heard Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> saying: ‘The swishing of the wings of the pigeons expels the satans<sup>la</sup>’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: ضعيف - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (22/469)

text: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, raising it, said, ‘Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic Defends, by the pigeons, the house from crumbling down’.

citation.chapter: THE BOOK OF DOMESTIC ANIMALS (al-Kafi, vol 6), 9:7
citation.arabic_text: قَالَ أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) إِنَّ اللَّهَ عَزَّ وَ جَلَّ يَدْفَعُ بِالْحَمَامِ عَنْ هَدَّةِ الدَّارِ .
citation.translation: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, raising it, said, ‘Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic Defends, by the pigeons, the house from crumbling down’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: ضعيف على المشهور - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (22/469)

text: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Al Nowfaly, from Al Sakuny, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws having said: ‘Take Al-Ra’aiby pigeons to be in your houses, for these curse the killers of Al-Husaynasws Bin Aliasws, and Allahazwj Curses hisasws killers’.

citation.chapter: THE BOOK OF DOMESTIC ANIMALS (al-Kafi, vol 6), 9:7
citation.arabic_text: اتَّخِذُوا الْحَمَامَ الرَّاعِبِيَّةَ فِي بُيُوتِكُمْ فَإِنَّهَا تَلْعَنُ قَتَلَةَ الْحُسَيْنِ بْنِ عَلِيٍّ ( عليه السلام ) وَ لَعَنَ اللَّهُ قَاتِلَهُ .
citation.translation: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Al Nowfaly, from Al Sakuny, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws having said: ‘Take Al-Ra’aiby pigeons to be in your houses, for these curse the killers of Al-Husaynasws Bin Aliasws, and Allahazwj Curses hisasws killers’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: ضعيف على المشهور - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (2/469)

text: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Bakr Bin Salih, from Muhammad Bin Abu Hamza, from Usman Al Asbahany who said, ‘Ismail son of Abu Abdullahasws gifted (something) to me, so I gifted to him a Raiby bird (pigeon). So I went to Abu Abdullahasws and heasws said: ‘Make this Raiby bird to be with measws in the house, for it comforts measws’. He (the narrator) said, ‘And Usman said, ‘I went over to Abu Abdullahasws and in front of himasws was a pigeon. Heasws was breaking bread for it’.

citation.chapter: THE BOOK OF DOMESTIC ANIMALS (al-Kafi, vol 6), 9:7
citation.arabic_text: اسْتَهْدَانِي إِسْمَاعِيلُ بْنُ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) فَأَهْدَيْتُ لَهُ طَيْراً رَاعِبِيّاً فَدَخَلَ أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) فَقَالَ اجْعَلُوا هَذَا الطَّيْرَ الرَّاعِبِيَّ مَعِي فِي الْبَيْتِ يُؤْنِسُنِي قَالَ وَ قَالَ عُثْمَانُ دَخَلْتُ عَلَى أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) وَ بَيْنَ يَدَيْهِ حَمَامٌ يَفُتُّ لَهُنَّ خُبْزاً .
citation.translation: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Bakr Bin Salih, from Muhammad Bin Abu Hamza, from Usman Al Asbahany who said, ‘Ismail son of Abu Abdullahasws gifted (something) to me, so I gifted to him a Raiby bird (pigeon). So I went to Abu Abdullahasws and heasws said: ‘Make this Raiby bird to be with measws in the house, for it comforts measws’. He (the narrator) said, ‘And Usman said, ‘I went over to Abu Abdullahasws and in front of himasws was a pigeon. Heasws was breaking bread for it’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: ضعيف على المشهور - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (22/469)

text: From him, from Bakr Bin Salih, from Ash’as Bin Muhammad Al Barqy, from Abdul Kareem Bin Salih who said, ‘I went over to Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, so I saw three green pigeons upon his<sup>asws</sup> mattress, and they had made droppings upon the mattress. So I said, ‘May I be sacrificed for you<sup>asws</sup>! These pigeons have dirties the mattress’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘No, it is recommended that they dwell in the house’.

citation.chapter: THE BOOK OF DOMESTIC ANIMALS (al-Kafi, vol 6), 9:7
citation.arabic_text: دَخَلْتُ عَلَى أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) فَرَأَيْتُ عَلَى فِرَاشِهِ ثَلَاثَ حَمَامَاتٍ خُضْرٍ قَدْ ذَرَقْنَ عَلَى الْفِرَاشِ فَقُلْتُ جُعِلْتُ فِدَاكَ هَؤُلَاءِ الْحَمَامُ تَقْذَرُ الْفِرَاشَ فَقَالَ لَا إِنَّهُ يُسْتَحَبُّ أَنْ تُسْكَنَ فِي الْبَيْتِ .
citation.translation: From him, from Bakr Bin Salih, from Ash’as Bin Muhammad Al Barqy, from Abdul Kareem Bin Salih who said, ‘I went over to Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, so I saw three green pigeons upon his<sup>asws</sup> mattress, and they had made droppings upon the mattress. So I said, ‘May I be sacrificed for you<sup>asws</sup>! These pigeons have dirties the mattress’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘No, it is recommended that they dwell in the house’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: ضعيف - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (22/469)

text: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from one of his companions, from Aban, from a man, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘There was in the house of Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup>, a pair of red pigeons’.

citation.chapter: THE BOOK OF DOMESTIC ANIMALS (al-Kafi, vol 6), 9:7
citation.arabic_text: كَانَ فِي مَنْزِلِ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ ( صلى الله عليه وآله ) زَوْجُ حَمَامٍ أَحْمَرُ .
citation.translation: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from one of his companions, from Aban, from a man, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘There was in the house of Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup>, a pair of red pigeons’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: مرسل - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (2/470)

text: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Najran, from Muhammad Bin Amro, from Ibrahim Al Sandy, from Yahya Al Azraq who said, ‘Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said: Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> dug a well, so they (people) threw (things) in it. Then Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘A swishing of their wings is a repellent for the satans<sup>la</sup>’.
