citation.arabic_text: قَالَ أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) احْتَفَرَ أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ ( عليه السلام ) بِئْراً فَرَمَوْا فِيهَا فَأُخْبِرَ بِذَلِكَ فَجَاءَ حَتَّى وَقَفَ عَلَيْهَا فَقَالَ لَتَكُفَّنَّ أَوْ لَأُسْكِنَنَّهَا الْحَمَامَ ثُمَّ قَالَ أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) إِنَّ حَفِيفَ أَجْنِحَتِهَا تَطْرُدُ الشَّيَاطِينَ .
citation.translation: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Najran, from Muhammad Bin Amro, from Ibrahim Al Sandy, from Yahya Al Azraq who said, ‘Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said: Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> dug a well, so they (people) threw (things) in it. So he<sup>asws</sup> was informed with that, so he<sup>asws</sup> came over until he<sup>asws</sup> paused over it and said: ‘You should refrain or else I<sup>asws</sup> will dwell the pigeons in it’. Then Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘A swishing of their wings is a repellent for the satans<sup>la</sup>’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: مجهول - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (2/470)

text: From him, from his father, from one of our companions who said, ‘The pigeons were mentioned in the presence of Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, so a man said to him<sup>asws</sup>, ‘It has reached me that Umar saw a pigeon flying by and a man was running under it, so Umar said, ‘A satan<sup>la</sup> underneath a satan<sup>la</sup>’. So Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘What was Ismail<sup>as</sup> among you all?’ So it was said, ‘A truthful one’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The remaining pigeons of the Sanctuary are from a pigeon of Ismail<sup>as</sup>’.

citation.chapter: THE BOOK OF DOMESTIC ANIMALS (al-Kafi, vol 6), 9:7
citation.arabic_text: ذُكِرَ الْحَمَامُ عِنْدَ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) فَقَالَ لَهُ رَجُلٌ إِنَّهُ بَلَغَنِي أَنَّ عُمَرَ رَأَى حَمَاماً يَطِيرُ وَ رَجُلٌ تَحْتَهُ يَعْدُو فَقَالَ عُمَرُ شَيْطَانٌ يَعْدُو تَحْتَهُ شَيْطَانٌ فَقَالَ أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) مَا كَانَ إِسْمَاعِيلُ عِنْدَكُمْ فَقِيلَ صِدِّيقٌ فَقَالَ إِنَّ بَقِيَّةَ حَمَامِ الْحَرَمِ مِنْ حَمَامِ إِسْمَاعِيلَ .
citation.translation: From him, from his father, from one of our companions who said, ‘The pigeons were mentioned in the presence of Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, so a man said to him<sup>asws</sup>, ‘It has reached me that Umar saw a pigeon flying by and a man was running under it, so Umar said, ‘A satan<sup>la</sup> underneath a satan<sup>la</sup>’. So Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘What was Ismail<sup>as</sup> among you all?’ So it was said, ‘A truthful one’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The remaining pigeons of the Sanctuary are from a pigeon of Ismail<sup>as</sup>’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: مرسل - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (22/470)

text: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, and Ahmad Bin Muhammad, altogether from Ibn Abu Nasr who said, ‘A man asked Al-Reza<sup>asws</sup> about the pair of pigeons with him who had incubated, ‘Can the bird marry its mother, and its daughter?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘There is no problem with what was from between the beasts’.

citation.chapter: THE BOOK OF DOMESTIC ANIMALS (al-Kafi, vol 6), 9:7
citation.arabic_text: سَأَلَ رَجُلٌ الرِّضَا ( عليه السلام ) عَنِ الزَّوْجِ مِنَ الْحَمَامِ يُفْرِخُ عِنْدَهُ يَتَزَوَّجُ الطَّيْرُ أُمَّهُ وَ ابْنَتَهُ قَالَ لَا بَأْسَ بِمَا كَانَ بَيْنَ الْبَهَائِمِ .
citation.translation: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, and Ahmad Bin Muhammad, altogether from Ibn Abu Nasr who said, ‘A man asked Al-Reza<sup>asws</sup> about the pair of pigeons with him who had incubated, ‘Can the bird marry its mother, and its daughter?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘There is no problem with what was from between the beasts’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: صحيح - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (2/470)

text: A number of our companions, form Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Khalid, from Muhammad Bin Ismail, from Muhammad Bin Uzafar who said, ‘I asked Abu Abdullahasws about the bird sent with a message from the remote city which it had never seen at all, so it comes’. So heasws said: ‘O Ibn Uzafar! It would come to the house of its own from thirty Farsakhs (about 120 kilometers) upon its recognition and its reckoning. So when it exceeds upon thirty Farsakhs, it goes to its nourishes with its sustenance’.

citation.chapter: THE BOOK OF DOMESTIC ANIMALS (al-Kafi, vol 6), 9:8
citation.arabic_text: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) عَنِ الطَّيْرِ يُرْسَلُ مِنَ الْبَلَدِ الْبَعِيدِ الَّذِي لَمْ يَرَهُ قَطُّ فَيَأْتِي فَقَالَ يَا ابْنَ عُذَافِرٍ هُوَ يَأْتِي مَنْزِلَ صَاحِبِهِ مِنْ ثَلَاثِينَ فَرْسَخاً عَلَى مَعْرِفَتِهِ وَ حَسَبِهِ فَإِذَا زَادَتْ عَلَى ثَلَاثِينَ فَرْسَخاً جَاءَتْ إِلَى أَرْبَابِهَا بِأَرْزَاقِهَا .
citation.translation: A number of our companions, form Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Khalid, from Muhammad Bin Ismail, from Muhammad Bin Uzafar who said, ‘I asked Abu Abdullahasws about the bird sent with a message from the remote city which it had never seen at all, so it comes’. So heasws said: ‘O Ibn Uzafar! It would come to the house of its own from thirty Farsakhs (about 120 kilometers) upon its recognition and its reckoning. So when it exceeds upon thirty Farsakhs, it goes to its nourishes with its sustenance’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: صحيح - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (2/471)

text: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, raising it, said, ‘Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘What (bird) comes to you from thirty Farsakhs (120 kilometers), so it is by guidance, and what was more than that, so it is by eating’.

citation.chapter: THE BOOK OF DOMESTIC ANIMALS (al-Kafi, vol 6), 9:8
citation.arabic_text: قَالَ أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) مَا أَتَى مِنْ ثَلَاثِينَ فَرْسَخاً فَبِالْهِدَايَةِ وَ مَا كَانَ أَكْثَرَ مِنْ ذَلِكَ فَبِالْأُكُلِ .
citation.translation: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, raising it, said, ‘Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘What (bird) comes to you from thirty Farsakhs (120 kilometers), so it is by guidance, and what was more than that, so it is by eating’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: ضعيف على المشهور - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (2/471)

text: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Al Hakam, from Sayf Bin Umeyra, from Is’haq Bin Ammar who said, ‘I said to Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, ‘The bird which comes from the remote place’. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘But rather, it comes to its sustenance'.

citation.chapter: THE BOOK OF DOMESTIC ANIMALS (al-Kafi, vol 6), 9:8
citation.arabic_text: قُلْتُ لِأَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) الطَّيْرُ يَجِي‏ءُ مِنَ الْمَكَانِ الْبَعِيدِ قَالَ إِنَّمَا يَجِي‏ءُ لِرِزْقِهِ .
citation.translation: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Al Hakam, from Sayf Bin Umeyra, from Is’haq Bin Ammar who said, ‘I said to Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, ‘The bird which comes from the remote place’. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘But rather, it comes to its sustenance'.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: موثق - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (2/471)

text: Al Husayn Bin Muhammad, from Moala Bin Muhammad, from Muhammad Bin Jamhour, from Ali Bin Dawood Al Haddad, from Hareyz, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, said, ‘I said, ‘The pigeons which are sent with a message from the remote places, so they come, and they are sent from the nearby places so they don’t come’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘When its feed is cut-off, so they don’t come’.

citation.chapter: THE BOOK OF DOMESTIC ANIMALS (al-Kafi, vol 6), 9:8
citation.arabic_text: قُلْتُ الْحَمَامُ يُرْسَلْنَ مِنَ الْمَوَاضِعِ الْبَعِيدَةِ فَيَأْتِي وَ يُرْسَلْنَ مِنَ الْمَكَانِ الْقَرِيبِ فَلَا يَأْتِي فَقَالَ إِذَا انْقَطَعَ أُكُلُهُ فَلَا يَأْتِي .
citation.translation: Al Husayn Bin Muhammad, from Moala Bin Muhammad, from Muhammad Bin Jamhour, from Ali Bin Dawood Al Haddad, from Hareyz, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, said, ‘I said, ‘The pigeons which are sent with a message from the remote places, so they come, and they are sent from the nearby places so they don’t come’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘When its feed is cut-off, so they don’t come’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: ضعيف على المشهور - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (22/471)

text: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Khalid, from Muhammad Bin Ali, from Abu Jameela, from Jabir, (It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘A white frightening rooster protects a house of its inhabitants, and seven other houses around it’.

citation.chapter: THE BOOK OF DOMESTIC ANIMALS (al-Kafi, vol 6), 9:9
citation.arabic_text: قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ ( صلى الله عليه وآله ) دِيكٌ أَبْيَضُ أَفْرَقُ يَحْرُسُ دُوَيْرَةَ أَهْلِهِ وَ سَبْعَ دُوَيْرَاتٍ حَوْلَهُ .
citation.translation: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Khalid, from Muhammad Bin Ali, from Abu Jameela, from Jabir, (It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘A white frightening rooster protects a house of its inhabitants, and seven other houses around it’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: ضعيف - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (22/472)

text: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, form Ali Bin Suleyman Bin Rusheyd, from Al Qasim Bin Abdul Rahman Al Hashimy, from Muhammad Bin Makhlad Al Ahwazy, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘A white frightening rooster protects its house and seven houses around it, and a swishing (of the wings) from a speckled pigeon is superior than seven white frightening roosters’.

citation.chapter: THE BOOK OF DOMESTIC ANIMALS (al-Kafi, vol 6), 9:9
citation.arabic_text: دِيكٌ أَبْيَضُ أَفْرَقُ يَحْرُسُ دُوَيْرَتَهُ وَ سَبْعَ دُوَيْرَاتٍ حَوْلَهُ وَ لَنَفْضَةٌ مِنْ حَمَامٍ مُنَمَّرَةٍ أَفْضَلُ مِنْ سَبْعِ دُيُوكٍ فُرْقٍ بِيضٍ .
citation.translation: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, form Ali Bin Suleyman Bin Rusheyd, from Al Qasim Bin Abdul Rahman Al Hashimy, from Muhammad Bin Makhlad Al Ahwazy, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘A white frightening rooster protects its house and seven houses around it, and a swishing (of the wings) from a speckled pigeon is superior than seven white frightening roosters’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: ضعيف على المشهور - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (22/472)

text: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Khalid, from Al Qasim Bin Yahya, from his grandfather Al Hassan Bin Rashid, from Yaqoub Bin Ja’far Bin Ibrahim Al Ja’fary who said, ‘The beauty of peacoks were mentioned in the presence of Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup>, so he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘It would not increase you anything upon the beauty of the white rooster’. He (the narrator) said, ‘And I heard him<sup>asws</sup> saying, ‘The rooster is of better voice than the peacock, and it is greater in Blessings. It alerts you during the timings of the Prayers, rather the peacock bewails due to the error which it indulged in’.

citation.chapter: THE BOOK OF DOMESTIC ANIMALS (al-Kafi, vol 6), 9:9
citation.arabic_text: ذُكِرَ عِنْدَ أَبِي الْحَسَنِ ( عليه السلام ) حُسْنُ الطَّاوُسِ فَقَالَ لَا يَزِيدُكَ عَلَى حُسْنِ الدِّيكِ الْأَبْيَضِ شَيْ‏ءٌ قَالَ وَ سَمِعْتُهُ يَقُولُ الدِّيكُ أَحْسَنُ صَوْتاً مِنَ الطَّاوُسِ وَ هُوَ أَعْظَمُ بَرَكَةً يُنَبِّهُكَ فِي مَوَاقِيتِ الصَّلَاةِ وَ إِنَّمَا يَدْعُو الطَّاوُسُ بِالْوَيْلِ لِخَطِيئَةِ الَّتِي ابْتُلِيَ بِهَا .
citation.translation: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Khalid, from Al Qasim Bin Yahya, from his grandfather Al Hassan Bin Rashid, from Yaqoub Bin Ja’far Bin Ibrahim Al Ja’fary who said, ‘The beauty of peacoks were mentioned in the presence of Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup>, so he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘It would not increase you anything upon the beauty of the white rooster’. He (the narrator) said, ‘And I heard him<sup>asws</sup> saying, ‘The rooster is of better voice than the peacock, and it is greater in Blessings. It alerts you during the timings of the Prayers, rather the peacock bewails due to the error which it indulged in’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: ضعيف - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (2/472)

text: From him, form one of his companions, raising it, said, ‘Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The white rooster is my<sup>asws</sup> friend and a friend of every Believer’.

citation.chapter: THE BOOK OF DOMESTIC ANIMALS (al-Kafi, vol 6), 9:9
citation.arabic_text: قَالَ أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) الدِّيكُ الْأَبْيَضُ صَدِيقِي وَ صَدِيقُ كُلِّ مُؤْمِنٍ .
citation.translation: From him, form one of his companions, raising it, said, ‘Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The white rooster is my<sup>asws</sup> friend and a friend of every Believer’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: مرسل - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (2/473)

text: From him, from one of his companions, from Abu Shuayb Al Mahamily, (It has been narrated) from Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘The rooster has five characteristics from the characteristics of the Prophets<sup>as</sup> – The generosity, and the bravery, and the contentment, and the recognition of the timings of the Prayers, and the frequency of mating, and the self-esteem’.

citation.chapter: THE BOOK OF DOMESTIC ANIMALS (al-Kafi, vol 6), 9:9
citation.arabic_text: قَالَ فِي الدِّيكِ خَمْسُ خِصَالٍ مِنْ خِصَالِ الْأَنْبِيَاءِ السَّخَاءُ وَ الشَّجَاعَةُ وَ الْقَنَاعَةُ وَ الْمَعْرِفَةُ بِأَوْقَاتِ الصَّلَوَاتِ وَ كَثْرَةُ الطَّرُوقَةِ وَ الْغَيْرَةِ .
citation.translation: From him, from one of his companions, from Abu Shuayb Al Mahamily, (It has been narrated) from Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘The rooster has five characteristics from the characteristics of the Prophets<sup>as</sup> – The generosity, and the bravery, and the contentment, and the recognition of the timings of the Prayers, and the frequency of mating, and the self-esteem’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: مرسل - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (22/473)

text: From him, from a number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, altogether, from Ja’far Bin Muhammad Al Ashary, from Ibn Al Qaddah, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The shrieking of the rooster is its Prayer, and the flapping of its wings are its bowings and its prostrations’.

citation.chapter: THE BOOK OF DOMESTIC ANIMALS (al-Kafi, vol 6), 9:9
citation.arabic_text: قَالَ أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ ( صلوات الله عليه ) صِيَاحُ الدِّيكِ صَلَاتُهُ وَ ضَرْبُهُ بِجَنَاحِهِ رُكُوعُهُ وَ سُجُودُهُ .
citation.translation: From him, from a number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, altogether, from Ja’far Bin Muhammad Al Ashary, from Ibn Al Qaddah, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The shrieking of the rooster is its Prayer, and the flapping of its wings are its bowings and its prostrations’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: مجهول - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (22/473)

text: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Khalid, from Ismail Bin Mihran, from Sayf Bin Ameyra, from Abu Bakr Al hazramy, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws having said: ‘The one who takes a bird to be in his house, so let him take a Al-Warshaan for it is a thing which frequents in the mentioning of Allahazwj Mighty and Majestic, and frequents in Glorification, and it is a bird beloved to usasws the Peopleasws of the Household’.

citation.chapter: THE BOOK OF DOMESTIC ANIMALS (al-Kafi, vol 6), 9:10
citation.arabic_text: مَنِ اتَّخَذَ فِي بَيْتِهِ طَيْراً فَلْيَتَّخِذْ وَرَشَاناً فَإِنَّهُ أَكْثَرُ شَيْئاً لِذِكْرِ اللَّهِ عَزَّ وَ جَلَّ وَ أَكْثَرُ تَسْبِيحاً وَ هُوَ طَيْرٌ يُحِبُّنَا أَهْلَ الْبَيْتِ .
citation.translation: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Khalid, from Ismail Bin Mihran, from Sayf Bin Ameyra, from Abu Bakr Al hazramy, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws having said: ‘The one who takes a bird to be in his house, so let him take a Al-Warshaan for it is a thing which frequents in the mentioning of Allahazwj Mighty and Majestic, and frequents in Glorification, and it is a bird beloved to usasws the Peopleasws of the Household’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: حسن أو صحيح - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (22/474)

text: From him, from Bakr Bin Salih, from Muhammad Bin Abu Hamza, from Usman Al Asbahany who said, ‘Ismail son of Abu Abdullahasws gifted me a bird from the birds of Al-Iraq, so I gifted to him Al-Warshaan. So Abu Abdullahasws came covered and heasws saw it, so heasws said: ‘The Warshaan is saying, ‘Blessing be upon you, Blessings be upon you!’, therefore keep it’.

citation.chapter: THE BOOK OF DOMESTIC ANIMALS (al-Kafi, vol 6), 9:10
citation.arabic_text: اسْتَهْدَانِي إِسْمَاعِيلُ بْنُ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) طَيْراً مِنْ طُيُورِ الْعِرَاقِ فَأَهْدَيْتُ وَرَشَاناً فَدَخَلَ أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) فَرَآهُ فَقَالَ إِنَّ الْوَرَشَانَ يَقُولُ بُورِكْتُمْ بُورِكْتُمْ فَأَمْسِكُوهُ .
citation.translation: From him, from Bakr Bin Salih, from Muhammad Bin Abu Hamza, from Usman Al Asbahany who said, ‘Ismail son of Abu Abdullahasws gifted me a bird from the birds of Al-Iraq, so I gifted to him Al-Warshaan. So Abu Abdullahasws came covered and heasws saw it, so heasws said: ‘The Warshaan is saying, ‘Blessing be upon you, Blessings be upon you!’, therefore keep it’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: ضعيف - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (22/474)

text: From him, from Al Jamourany, from Ibn Abu Hamza, from sayf, from Is’haq Bin Ammar, from Abu Baseer, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws that heasws forbade hisasws son Ismail from taking the ring-dove (Fakhta), and said: ‘If it was inevitable that you take, so take Al-Warshaan, for it frequents in the mentioning of Allahazwj Blessed and High’.

citation.chapter: THE BOOK OF DOMESTIC ANIMALS (al-Kafi, vol 6), 9:10
citation.arabic_text: إِنْ كُنْتَ لَا بُدَّ مُتَّخِذاً فَاتَّخِذْ وَرَشَاناً فَإِنَّهُ كَثِيرُ الذِّكْرِ لِلَّهِ تَبَارَكَ وَ تَعَالَى .
citation.translation: From him, from Al Jamourany, from Ibn Abu Hamza, from sayf, from Is’haq Bin Ammar, from Abu Baseer, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws that heasws forbade hisasws son Ismail from taking the ring-dove (Fakhta), and said: ‘If it was inevitable that you take, so take Al-Warshaan, for it frequents in the mentioning of Allahazwj Blessed and High’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: ضعيف - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (22/474)

text: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, form Hafs Bin Al Bakhtary, from a man, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws having said: ‘There used to be in the house of Abu Ja’farasws, a Fakhta, so heasws heard it one days and it was shrieking. So heasws said to them: ‘Do you all know what it this Fakhta is saying?’ They said, ‘No’. Heasws said: ‘It is saying, ‘You are all lost, you are all lost!’ Then heasws said: ‘Weasws will lose it before it loses usasws’. Then heasws ordered for it to be slaughtered’.

citation.chapter: THE BOOK OF DOMESTIC ANIMALS (al-Kafi, vol 6), 9:11
citation.arabic_text: كَانَتْ فِي دَارِ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ ( عليه السلام ) فَاخِتَةٌ فَسَمِعَهَا يَوْماً وَ هِيَ تَصِيحُ فَقَالَ لَهُمْ أَ تَدْرُونَ مَا تَقُولُ هَذِهِ الْفَاخِتَةُ قَالُوا لَا قَالَ تَقُولُ فَقَدْتُكُمْ فَقَدْتُكُمْ ثُمَّ قَالَ لَنَفْقِدَنَّهَا قَبْلَ أَنْ تَفْقِدَنَا ثُمَّ أَمَرَ بِهَا فَذُبِحَتْ .
citation.translation: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, form Hafs Bin Al Bakhtary, from a man, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws having said: ‘There used to be in the house of Abu Ja’farasws, a Fakhta, so heasws heard it one days and it was shrieking. So heasws said to them: ‘Do you all know what it this Fakhta is saying?’ They said, ‘No’. Heasws said: ‘It is saying, ‘You are all lost, you are all lost!’ Then heasws said: ‘Weasws will lose it before it loses usasws’. Then heasws ordered for it to be slaughtered’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: مرسل أو حسن - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (22/474)

text: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Khalid, from Bakr Bin Salih, from Muhammad Bin Ab Hamza, from Usman Al Asbahany who said, ‘I gifted a Sulsula to Ismail, son of Abu Abdullahasws. text: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al Halby, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘It is abhorrent that there would happen to be the dog in the house of the man’.

citation.chapter: THE BOOK OF DOMESTIC ANIMALS (al-Kafi, vol 6), 9:12
citation.arabic_text: يُكْرَهُ أَنْ يَكُونَ فِي دَارِ الرَّجُلِ الْمُسْلِمِ الْكَلْبُ .
citation.translation: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al Halby, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘It is abhorrent that there would happen to be the dog in the house of the man’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: حسن - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (22/475)

text: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ibn Bukeyr, from Zurara, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘There is no one who would take a dog except that one carat (unit of measurement) would be reduced from his deeds every day’.

citation.chapter: THE BOOK OF DOMESTIC ANIMALS (al-Kafi, vol 6), 9:12
citation.arabic_text: مَا مِنْ أَحَدٍ يَتَّخِذُ كَلْباً إِلَّا نَقَصَ فِي كُلِّ يَوْمٍ مِنْ عَمَلِ صَاحِبِهِ قِيرَاطٌ .
citation.translation: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ibn Bukeyr, from Zurara, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘There is no one who would take a dog except that one carat (unit of measurement) would be reduced from his deeds every day’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: موثق - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (22/475)

text: From him, from Usman, from Sama’at who said, ‘I asked about the dog, ‘Can we keep it in the house?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘No’.

citation.chapter: THE BOOK OF DOMESTIC ANIMALS (al-Kafi, vol 6), 9:12
citation.arabic_text: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنِ الْكَلْبِ نُمْسِكُهُ فِي الدَّارِ قَالَ لَا .
citation.translation: From him, from Usman, from Sama’at who said, ‘I asked about the dog, ‘Can we keep it in the house?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘No’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: موثق - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (22/476)

text: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Yusuf Bin Aqeel, from Muhammad Bin Qays, (It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘There is no goodness in the dogs except for the hunting dog, or a walking dog’.

citation.chapter: THE BOOK OF DOMESTIC ANIMALS (al-Kafi, vol 6), 9:12
citation.arabic_text: قَالَ أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ ( صلوات الله عليه ) لَا خَيْرَ فِي الْكِلَابِ إِلَّا كَلْبَ صَيْدٍ أَوْ كَلْبَ مَاشِيَةٍ .
citation.translation: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Yusuf Bin Aqeel, from Muhammad Bin Qays, (It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘There is no goodness in the dogs except for the hunting dog, or a walking dog’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: صحيح - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (22/476)

text: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Khalif, from his father, from Al Nazar Bin Suweyd, from Al Qasim Bin Suleyman, from Jarrah Al Madainy, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Do not keep a hunting dog in the house except if there happens to be a door between you and it’.

citation.chapter: THE BOOK OF DOMESTIC ANIMALS (al-Kafi, vol 6), 9:12
citation.arabic_text: لَا تُمْسِكْ كَلْبَ الصَّيْدِ فِي الدَّارِ إِلَّا أَنْ يَكُونَ بَيْنَكَ وَ بَيْنَهُ بَابٌ .
citation.translation: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Khalif, from his father, from Al Nazar Bin Suweyd, from Al Qasim Bin Suleyman, from Jarrah Al Madainy, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Do not keep a hunting dog in the house except if there happens to be a door between you and it’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: مجهول - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (2/476)

text: From him, from Usman Bin Isa, from Sama’at who said, ‘I asked about a hunting dog, to be kept in the house’. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘If there was door which could be locked on it, so there is no problem’.

citation.chapter: THE BOOK OF DOMESTIC ANIMALS (al-Kafi, vol 6), 9:12
citation.arabic_text: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنْ كَلْبِ الصَّيْدِ يُمْسَكُ فِي الدَّارِ قَالَ إِذَا كَانَ يُغْلَقُ دُونَهُ الْبَابُ فَلَا بَأْسَ .
citation.translation: From him, from Usman Bin Isa, from Sama’at who said, ‘I asked about a hunting dog, to be kept in the house’. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘If there was door which could be locked on it, so there is no problem’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: موثق - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (2/476)

text: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, and Muhammad Bin yahya, from Abdullah Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Al Hakam, from Aban, from Zurara, (It has been narrated) from one of the two (5<sup>th</sup> or 6<sup>th</sup> Imam<sup>asws</sup>) having said: ‘The dogs, entirely black, are from the Jinn’.

citation.chapter: THE BOOK OF DOMESTIC ANIMALS (al-Kafi, vol 6), 9:12
citation.arabic_text: الْكِلَابُ السُّودُ الْبَهِيمُ مِنَ الْجِنِّ .
citation.translation: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, and Muhammad Bin yahya, from Abdullah Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Al Hakam, from Aban, from Zurara, (It has been narrated) from one of the two (5<sup>th</sup> or 6<sup>th</sup> Imam<sup>asws</sup>) having said: ‘The dogs, entirely black, are from the Jinn’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: موثق - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (22/476)

text: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Muhammad Bin Al Husayn, from Muhammad Bin Ismail, from Ali Bin Al Hakam, from Maalik Bin Atiyya, from Abu Hamza Al Sumaly who said, ‘I was with Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> in what is between Makkah and Al-Medina, when he<sup>asws</sup> turned to his<sup>asws</sup> left, so there was an entirely black dog. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘What is the matter with you? Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Made you ugly, how fiercely you rush! and it was the resemblance of a bird’. So I said, ‘What is this? May I be sacrificed for you<sup>asws</sup>’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘This is Gusaym, a postman of the Jinn. Hisham died at this time, and he (turned himself into) a bird notifying it in every city’.

citation.chapter: THE BOOK OF DOMESTIC ANIMALS (al-Kafi, vol 6), 9:12
citation.arabic_text: كُنْتُ مَعَ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) فِيمَا بَيْنَ مَكَّةَ وَ الْمَدِينَةِ إِذَا الْتَفَتَ عَنْ يَسَارِهِ فَإِذَا كَلْبٌ أَسْوَدُ بَهِيمٌ فَقَالَ مَا لَكَ قَبَّحَكَ اللَّهُ مَا أَشَدَّ مُسَارَعَتَكَ وَ إِذَا هُوَ شَبِيهٌ بِالطَّائِرِ فَقُلْتُ مَا هَذَا جُعِلْتُ فِدَاكَ فَقَالَ هَذَا غُثَيْمٌ بَرِيدُ الْجِنِّ مَاتَ هِشَامٌ السَّاعَةَ وَ هُوَ يَطِيرُ يَنْعَاهُ فِي كُلِّ بَلْدَةٍ .
citation.translation: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Muhammad Bin Al Husayn, from Muhammad Bin Ismail, from Ali Bin Al Hakam, from Maalik Bin Atiyya, from Abu Hamza Al Sumaly who said, ‘I was with Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> in what is between Makkah and Al-Medina, when he<sup>asws</sup> turned to his<sup>asws</sup> left, so there was an entirely black dog. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘What is the matter with you? Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Made you ugly, how fiercely you rush! and it was the resemblance of a bird’. So I said, ‘What is this? May I be sacrificed for you<sup>asws</sup>’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘This is Gusaym, a postman of the Jinn. Hisham died at this time, and he (turned himself into) a bird notifying it in every city’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: صحيح - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (22/476)

text: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Muhammad Bin Al Hassan Bin Shamoun, from Abdullah Bin Abdul Rahman, from Misma’a, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘The dogs are from the weak ones of the Jinn. So when one of you is eating the meal, and there is something from it in front of him, so let him feed it or let him repel it, for it has an evil self for it’.

citation.chapter: THE BOOK OF DOMESTIC ANIMALS (al-Kafi, vol 6), 9:12
citation.arabic_text: قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ ( صلى الله عليه وآله ) الْكِلَابُ مِنْ ضَعَفَةِ الْجِنِّ فَإِذَا أَكَلَ أَحَدُكُمُ الطَّعَامَ وَ شَيْ‏ءٌ مِنْهَا بَيْنَ يَدَيْهِ فَلْيُطْعِمْهُ أَوْ لِيَطْرُدْهُ فَإِنَّ لَهَا أَنْفُسَ سَوْءٍ .
citation.translation: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Muhammad Bin Al Hassan Bin Shamoun, from Abdullah Bin Abdul Rahman, from Misma’a, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘The dogs are from the weak ones of the Jinn. So when one of you is eating the meal, and there is something from it in front of him, so let him feed it or let him repel it, for it has an evil self for it’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: ضعيف على المشهور - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (2/477)

text: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Muhammad Bin Al Husayn, from Abdul Rahman Bin Abu Hashim, from Salim Bin Abu Salma, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, said, ‘He<sup>asws</sup> was asked about the dogs, so he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Every entirely black one, and every entirely red one, and every entirely white one, so that is a creature from the dogs from the Jinn, and whatever was speckled, so it is one morphed from the Jinn and the humans’.

citation.chapter: THE BOOK OF DOMESTIC ANIMALS (al-Kafi, vol 6), 9:12
citation.arabic_text: سُئِلَ عَنِ الْكِلَابِ فَقَالَ كُلُّ أَسْوَدَ بَهِيمٌ وَ كُلُّ أَحْمَرَ بَهِيمٌ وَ كُلُّ أَبْيَضَ بَهِيمٌ فَذَلِكَ خَلْقٌ مِنَ الْكِلَابِ مِنَ الْجِنِّ وَ مَا كَانَ أَبْلَقَ فَهُوَ مَسْخٌ مِنَ الْجِنِّ وَ الْإِنْسِ .
citation.translation: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Muhammad Bin Al Husayn, from Abdul Rahman Bin Abu Hashim, from Salim Bin Abu Salma, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, said, ‘He<sup>asws</sup> was asked about the dogs, so he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Every entirely black one, and every entirely red one, and every entirely white one, so that is a creature from the dogs from the Jinn, and whatever was speckled, so it is one morphed from the Jinn and the humans’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: مختلف فيه - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (22/477)

text: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Al Nowfaly, from Al Sakuny, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> that Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> allowed for the people of the countryside to take dogs’.

citation.chapter: THE BOOK OF DOMESTIC ANIMALS (al-Kafi, vol 6), 9:12
citation.arabic_text: كَلْبٍ يَتَّخِذُونَهُ .
citation.translation: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Al Nowfaly, from Al Sakuny, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> that Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> allowed for the people of the countryside to take dogs’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: ضعيف على المشهور - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (22/477)

text: From him, from his father, from Ibn Mahboub, from Al A’ala Bin Razeyn, from Muhammad Bin Muslim who said, ‘I asked Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> about the greyhound dog. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘When you touch it, so wash your hand’.

citation.chapter: THE BOOK OF DOMESTIC ANIMALS (al-Kafi, vol 6), 9:12
citation.arabic_text: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) عَنِ الْكَلْبِ السَّلُوقِيِّ قَالَ إِذَا مَسِسْتَهُ فَاغْسِلْ يَدَكَ .
citation.translation: From him, from his father, from Ibn Mahboub, from Al A’ala Bin Razeyn, from Muhammad Bin Muslim who said, ‘I asked Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> about the greyhound dog. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘When you touch it, so wash your hand’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: حسن - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (22/477)

citation.arabic_text: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنِ التَّحْرِيشِ بَيْنَ الْبَهَائِمِ فَقَالَ كُلُّهُ مَكْرُوهٌ إِلَّا الْكَلْبَ .
citation.translation: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Al Hakam, from Aban Bin Usman, from Abu Al Abbas, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, said, ‘I asked him<sup>asws</sup> about the instigation between the animals, so he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘All of it is abhorred, except for the dog’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: موثق كالصحيح - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (22/477)

text: From him, from Ali Bin Al Hakam, from Aban, from Misma’a who said, ‘I asked Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> about the instigation between the animals. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘I<sup>asws</sup> dislike that, except for the dogs’.

citation.arabic_text: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) عَنِ التَّحْرِيشِ بَيْنَ الْبَهَائِمِ فَقَالَ أَكْرَهُ ذَلِكَ إِلَّا الْكِلَابَ .
citation.translation: From him, from Ali Bin Al Hakam, from Aban, from Misma’a who said, ‘I asked Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> about the instigation between the animals. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘I<sup>asws</sup> dislike that, except for the dogs’.
